As I worked on this writing over the years, Adie and JJ Mitchell charted their own lives, along with Chloe and Jesse, while also sharing the journey of this book. Our numerous adventures together, on waters charted and uncharted, epitomise all the challenges and joys of that shared life. Lila Abu-Lughod shared every moment of these years. Her counsel, her intellect, and her love have been indispensable to the writing of the book and to every part our life together. Finally, my five siblings have always provided for every undertaking the proper mix of scepticism, humour, and support. The book is dedicated to them.<a id="page-xii-en"></a>〔原书第xii页〕


# 导论：优步外卖——资本主义如何消费未来

<a id="introduction-0001"></a>

<a id="page-1"></a>〔原书第1页〕

<a id="page-1-en"></a>〔原书第1页〕

<a id="introduction-0002"></a>

## 导论：优步外卖——资本主义如何消费未来

## Introduction Uber Eats – How Capitalism Consumes the Future

<a id="introduction-0003"></a>

我们生活在一个非凡财富似乎来自深不可测之源的时代。2019 年美国公司优步（Uber）上市时，股市对其估值达 820 亿美元；对一家成立十年、不拥有任何车辆、从未盈利的叫车服务公司来说，这是一个天文数字。为解释这类事件，新闻媒体常借用气象学隐喻，把投资者的收益形容为“高入平流层”。例如，高盛 2011 年向优步投资的 500 万美元，如今价值已超过 5 亿美元，八年回报率超过 1,000%，除此之外还能怎样解释？更具批判性的评论者则说，这家公司的价值是从“稀薄的空气”中变出来的东西。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-001"></a>[1](#note-int-001)

We live in an age in which extraordinary wealth seems to arrive from unfathomable sources. When the US firm Uber went public in 2019, the stock market set its value at $82 billion, an immense figure for a ten-year-old car service company that owned no cars and had never made a profit. To explain such events, the news media often turn to metaphors from meteorology, describing the investors’ gains as ‘stratospheric’. What other way to explain, for example, how the $5 million that Goldman Sachs had invested in Uber in 2011 was now worth over half a billion dollars, a return in eight years of more than 1,000 per cent? More critical commentators called the firm’s value something conjured out of ‘thin air’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-001"></a>[1](#note-int-001)

<a id="introduction-0004"></a>

这类意外之财的来源与气象无关。要理解这种赚钱方式，我们必须回到地面。优步是一个极端案例，但它获取非劳动财富的方式却司空见惯。这种方式是我们当代生活形式的一个决定性特征，是理解我们称之为资本主义的致富与致贫方法如何以及为何产生的关键，也是理解我们如今为何面临气候崩溃灾难的线索。这家公司通过建造一种消费未来的实用手段，创造了自己的价值。

The source of such windfalls is nothing meteorological. To understand this way of making money we need to come down to earth. While Uber is an extreme case, its mode of acquiring unearned wealth is commonplace. The mode is a defining feature of our contemporary form of life, a key to understanding how and why the methods of enrichment and impoverishment we call capitalism came into being, and a clue to grasping why we now face the catastrophe of climate collapse. The company created its value by constructing a practical means of consuming the future.

<a id="introduction-0005"></a>

本书旨在追问：我们如何开始以未来贫困化为原则来组织集体生活；在河流的毁灭、领土的殖民、城市的扩张、基础设施的建设和碳的燃烧中，这一原则如何发展；今天的生计如何因偿还早先的抽取<a id="page-2"></a>〔原书第2页〕而背上负担；以及这种使多数人贫乏、少数人富足的机制如何与气候危机相连。本书还旨在考察那些为描述和安排这些生活形式而发展起来的政治与经济语言——资本主义、技术、金融、经济及其增长等术语——并追问它们是否足以解释这种贫乏化如何运作，以及我们为何在气候崩溃面前无力行动。

The aim of this book is to ask how we came to organise collective life on the principle of the impoverishment of the future; explore the development of this principle in the destruction of rivers, the colonising of territories, the expansion of cities, the building of infrastructure, and the burning of carbon; see how lives today are encumbered by the <a id="page-2-en"></a>〔原书第2页〕repayment of earlier extractions; and connect this mode of impoverishing the many and enriching the few to the climate crisis. Its aim is also to examine the political and economic language that developed to describe and order these forms of life – terms like capitalism, technology, finance, the economy and its growth – and ask whether they are adequate for making sense of how the impoverishment operates and of our inability to act in the face of climate breakdown.

<a id="introduction-0006"></a>

从未来抽取收入的方法早已存在。优步所使用的工具——股份公司——以目前的形式已存在一百五十多年。现代投资者所有的企业最早于十九世纪在西方大量涌现，用于建造铁路以及其他绵延的、改造大地的、碳密集的、往往带有帝国主义性质的结构。这些结构规模庞大、经久耐用，通常以巨大的生态和人力代价建成，却向股东许诺了从未来获取非劳动财富的通道。股份公司的历史还要更早，正如我们将看到的，可追溯到欧洲商人在比十九世纪早约三百年的时期开始创建的武装贸易公司；这些公司旨在征服世界贸易，使欧洲人得以殖民土地，并征服或消灭世界各地的人民。

Methods of extracting income from the future have been around for a long time. The device that Uber used, the joint-stock company, has existed in its current form for more than 150 years. Modern investor-owned firms first proliferated in the West in the nineteenth century to construct railways and other extended, terraforming, carbon-intensive, often imperial structures whose scale and durability, usually built at great ecological and human cost, promised their shareholders access to unearned wealth from the future. The history of joint-stock companies goes back even further, as we will see, to the armed trading corporations that European merchants began creating some three centuries earlier to conquer world trade, enabling them to colonise lands and subjugate or eliminate peoples across the Earth.

<a id="introduction-0007"></a>

在过去，这类致富方法通常是例外。股份公司只能通过皇家特许状或议会法案设立，特许状通常在有限的若干年后失效。早期的殖民公司引发了投机泡沫和帝国战争的负担，也容易遭到政治反对、被关闭、获公共救助或崩溃。欧洲殖民试图篡夺的亚洲和非洲更古老的商人网络，尤其是印度—伊斯兰世界的网络，曾对使用商业契约获取未指定、不可见的未来货物加以限制，理由是这类投机安排允许一方从另一方榨取非劳动利润。即便如此，横跨那个世界的长途贸易仍通常以信用进行——距离造成支付延迟，而延迟又为更高价格提供了理由；于是距离和延迟本身成了利润的来源。伊斯兰法律实践也承认一些安排，允许商人通过投机性购买未来资产获利，例如广泛使用远期合约，从那些急需筹钱纳税的人手中提前低价购得农作物。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-002"></a>[2](#note-int-002)但从中所抽取剩余的未来，受作物周期长度或跨地区贸易路线范围的限制。随着西方的殖民扩张，尤其是从十九世纪末的帝国时代<a id="page-3"></a>〔原书第3页〕起，投资者所有的公司成了一种手段，用来控制跨越各大洲的未来，并在巨大尺度上重组生计与景观。

In the past, such methods of enrichment were usually the exception. Joint-stock companies could be established only by royal charter or act of parliament, the charter typically expiring after a limited number of years. The early colonising corporations led to speculative bubbles and the burdens of imperial war, and were liable to political opposition, closure, public rescue, or collapse. The older merchant networks of Asia and Africa that European colonisation sought to usurp, in particular those of the Indo-Islamic world, had placed limits on the use of business contracts for acquiring unspecified, unseen future goods, on the grounds that such speculative schemes allowed one party to extract unearned profit from another. Even so, long-distance trade across that world was routinely conducted on credit, the distance creating a delay in payment that justified a higher price – distance and delay thus operating as the very source of profit. Islamic legal practice also recognised arrangements that allowed merchants to profit from the speculative purchase of future assets, such as the widespread use of forward contracts to acquire agricultural crops cheaply in advance, from those compelled to find funds to pay taxes.<a id="ref-en-note-int-002"></a>[2](#note-int-002) But the futures from which surplus was extracted were limited by the length of the crop cycle or the extent of a trans-regional trade route. With the colonial expansion of the West, and especially from the imperial age of the late nineteenth <a id="page-3-en"></a>〔原书第3页〕century, the investor-owned corporation became a means of controlling futures across continents and reorganising livelihoods and landscapes on an immense scale.

<a id="introduction-0008"></a>

今天，像优步这样的公司采用的方法有所不同，但其扩张野心同样巨大。2019 年上市后，该公司借款 30 亿美元收购总部位于迪拜的 Careem，力图垄断中东和北非的叫车服务业务——这是其主导各大洲交通服务计划的一部分。这类公司无论过去还是现在，其地理扩张既构成了投资者财富的来源，又同时掩盖了这一来源。它们试图控制的，是从未来获取收入。

Today, a firm like Uber works through somewhat different methods but has a similarly expansive ambition. Following its stock market launch in 2019, the company borrowed $3 billion to purchase the Dubai-based firm Careem, in an effort to monopolise the car service business across the Middle East and North Africa – part of a plan to dominate transportation services on every continent. The geographical expansion of such firms, both past and present, serves as, and at the same time conceals, the source of their investors’ wealth. What they seek to control is the acquisition of revenue from the future.

<a id="introduction-0009"></a>

我们有一套日常语言来描述我们与未来的经济关系，例如股价、利率、技术进步和经济增长。但这些术语都不能解释非劳动所得的来源，也不能说明后来者如何为此买单。它们也无法解释，当下的生活如何因先前对未来的抽取而背负负担；也无法解释，这种私有化的未来关系——明天的生活形式在当下成为可买卖的资产——如何促成一个可存续的集体未来的毁灭。事实上，金融的语言使我们看不清这一关系，它让我们相信，未来人类的生计不是收益的来源，而是受益者。

We have an everyday language for describing our economic relation to the future, using terms like stock price, interest rate, the advance of technology, and economic growth. But none of these terms explains the source of unearned income, to show how those coming later pay the bill. Nor do they explain how lives in the present are encumbered by previous extractions from the future, or how such privatised relations to the future, in which tomorrow’s forms of life become assets bought and sold in the present, contribute to the destruction of a viable collective future. In fact, the language of finance blinds us to this relationship, persuading us that future human livelihoods are not the source of the gains, but our beneficiaries.

<a id="introduction-0010"></a>

面对气候危机以及其他人为因素对地球系统平衡的扰乱，包括河流流域的破坏、栖息地的崩溃、物种灭绝的加速，以及合成塑料和农业杀生物剂对土地、海洋、空气和人体造成的毒害——并且认识到不同人类群体对这些扰乱的脆弱性极不平等——我们需要理解这种盲目是如何产生的。人类对地球的改造已经超出了安全且公正的限度，而我们随处可见一种迟来的承认：地球未来的可居住性今天必须被纳入考量。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-003"></a>[3](#note-int-003)于是，我们同时以两种相互矛盾的方式在当下把握未来：一种是末日式的，从当前的灾难和扰乱中认出即将到来的灾祸的直接征兆；另一种则是一套使我们盲目、并已将这场灾难带到我们身上的机制：它把未来安排成可计算的巨额财富来源，通过把债务强加给绝大多数人，让最富有者在当下致富。各国政府似乎无法正视这一矛盾，而它们的行动<a id="page-4"></a>〔原书第4页〕面对那些寻求进一步控制未来资产的势力时，往往显得无能为力，或者像是在为这些人服务。即使有可能克服这些困难，后果似乎仍然难以承受。资本主义无论代价如何，都声称给了我们增长。如果未来不再由经济扩张原则界定，我们还能在另一种时间性下生存吗？

In the face of the climate crisis and other anthropogenic disruptions to the balance of Earth systems, including the destruction of river basins, the collapse of habitats, the accelerating extinction of species, and the poisoning of land, sea, air, and human bodies with synthetic plastics and agricultural biocides – and aware of the very unequal vulnerability of different human communities to these disruptions – we need to understand how this blindness is produced. Having already exceeded safe and just limits to the human modification of the Earth, we are seeing everywhere a belated acknowledgement that the future liveability of the planet must today be taken into account.<a id="ref-en-note-int-003"></a>[3](#note-int-003) So we coexist with two contradictory ways of grasping the future in the present: one apocalyptic, recognising in current disasters and disruptions the immediate signs of a catastrophe to come; the other a mechanism of blindness that has brought the calamity upon us, by arranging the future as a calculable source of extraordinary wealth, enriching the wealthiest in the present by imposing debts on the vast majority. Governments appear unable to take account of this contradiction, while their actions <a id="page-4-en"></a>〔原书第4页〕often seem to be powerless against the agents seeking the further control of future assets, or to be working on their behalf. Even if it were possible to overcome these difficulties, the consequences would still seem unworkable. Capitalism, whatever its costs, claims to have given us growth. How could we survive under a different temporality, in which the future was not defined by a principle of economic expansion?

<a id="introduction-0011"></a>

自从我们开始围绕经济增长原则组织集体生活以来，就一直有人努力指出它的限度：增长不可持续、衡量有误，或者社会与生态代价过高。这些批评都很重要，但还有另一种看待我们与未来关系的方式。增长不是资本主义现代性的逻辑，而是它的托词。

For as long as we have organised collective life around the principle of economic growth, there have been efforts to point out its limits: that growth is unsustainable, is mismeasured, or comes at too great a social and ecological cost. Those are important criticisms, but there is another way to see our relation to the future. Growth is not the logic of capitalist modernity, but its alibi.

<a id="introduction-0012"></a>

过去，我们常以物理扩张来谈论现代性。历史学家把资本主义描述为一个始于欧洲、逐渐扩张至全世界的过程。如今我们知道，这只是对从未孤立于一地的变化的一种片面叙述。贸易与信用格局的重组、对劳动力和土地剥削的加剧，以及人口和生态系统的毁灭，始终在跨大陆尺度上发生。把这一切描述为西方的空间“扩张”，确实反映了这一重组过程的某些方面。但正如大量后殖民研究所示，这种描述本身就是某种分析变化方式的产物：它衡量那些被假定起源于欧洲、向外越过被动地理空间的运动，在报告的同时也遮蔽了同样多的东西。

In the past, we often spoke of modernity in terms of physical expansion. Historians described capitalism as a process that began in Europe and gradually expanded to encompass the world. We now see this as a partial account of changes that were never isolated in one place. The reworking of patterns of trade and credit, the intensifying exploitation of labour and the soil, and the destruction of populations and ecosystems were always occurring on a transcontinental scale. To describe this as the spatial ‘expansion’ of the West reflected some aspects of the reworking. But as so much postcolonial scholarship has shown, it was a product of ways of analysing change that, in measuring movements assumed to originate in Europe and move outwards across a passive geographical space, obscured as much as they reported.

<a id="introduction-0013"></a>

是否有一种类似的方式，可以修正我们对时间的理解？不仅仅像批判“地理即扩张”的观念那样批判“历史即增长”的观念，而且可以说，发展出一种类似的后殖民视角？不仅纳入那些土地和生计被殖民者的视角，也纳入那些未来被夺走者的视角？要做到这一点，我们需要理解在增长的托词之下运作的、各式各样的未来抽取机制。

Is there a similar way to revise our understanding of time? Not just to be as critical towards conceptions of history-as-growth as we are towards geography-as-expansion, but, as it were, to develop a similar kind of postcolonial perspective? To include the perspective, not only of those whose lands and livelihoods have been colonised, but of those whose future has been taken from them? To achieve this, we need to understand the diverse mechanisms of extraction from the future that have operated under the alibi of growth.

<a id="introduction-0014"></a>

### 价值高于一切

### Value Over All

<a id="introduction-0015"></a>

资本不是从过去积攒下来的东西。正如其他人已经表明、本书将进一步探讨的那样，资本是对未来的攫取。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-004"></a>[4](#note-int-004)我们可以从现代股东所有的公司如何获得其<a id="page-5"></a>〔原书第5页〕价值这一简单案例入手，来思考这种与未来的关系。当一家公司在股票市场上市时，出售的股份代表着对公司未来利润所有权的索取。由于收入不能立即到手，每年预期收入的价值都被向下调整，即“折现”，以补偿时间延迟。把未来各年利润的“折现现值”加总，就得出公司的估值。

Capital is not something saved up from the past. As others have shown and this book will further explore, it is a capture from the future.<a id="ref-en-note-int-004"></a>[4](#note-int-004) We can start thinking about this relation to the future through the straightforward case of the way a modern shareholder-owned firm acquires its <a id="page-5-en"></a>〔原书第5页〕value. When a company is floated on the stock market, the shares offered for sale represent a claim on the ownership of its future profits. Since the revenue is not available immediately, the value of each year’s prospective income is adjusted downwards, or ‘discounted’, to compensate for the delay in time until it arrives. Adding up the ‘present discounted value’, as it is called, of the years of future profits, produces the firm’s valuation.

<a id="introduction-0016"></a>

让我们回到优步的例子。尽管本书大部分内容关注更长的历史、更广的案例，以及与美国当代科技公司不同的土地，但优步这个案例在此可用于说明有关资本以及我们如何理解资本的一些更广泛问题。由于优步除欧洲和北美外，还扩张到全球南方许多城市，本书大多数读者都会熟悉它。

Let us return to the example of Uber. Although most of this book is concerned with longer histories, wider cases, and other lands than those of a contemporary US tech firm, the case of Uber can serve here to illustrate some of the broader issues about capital and how we understand it. Thanks to its expansion across many of the cities of the Global South, in addition to Europe and North America, Uber will be familiar to most of the readers of this book.

<a id="introduction-0017"></a>

公司上市时，优步尚未盈利。公司一直把叫车服务价格定在低于实际成本的水平，以把竞争者赶出市场。这些补贴运营每年亏损数十亿美元。为了给公司估值，金融分析师假定优步会继续扩张，直至取得“市场支配地位”。通过消灭替代选择，优步及其唯一的美国竞争对手 Lyft 可以继续从司机赚取的每一笔车费中抽取一部分，平均抽成 20%，同时利用日益增强的支配地位限制付给司机的部分，并提高乘客支付的费用。这些假设意味着，优步将在上市六年后停止亏损，并在十年内实现每年近 50 亿美元的利润。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-005"></a>[5](#note-int-005)

At the time the firm went public, Uber had not yet made a profit. The company had been setting the price of car service rides below their actual cost, to drive competitors out of business. These subsidised operations were losing billions of dollars every year. To value the firm, financial analysts assumed that Uber would continue to expand until it achieved ‘market dominance’. By eliminating alternatives, Uber and its one US rival, Lyft, could continue to claim a portion of every fare their drivers earned, taking on average a 20 per cent share, while using their growing dominance to limit the part paid to drivers and increase the cost to passengers. These assumptions suggested that Uber would stop losing money six years after turning public, and, within ten years, would be earning annual profits of almost $5 billion.<a id="ref-en-note-int-005"></a>[5](#note-int-005)

<a id="introduction-0018"></a>

投资者所有的公司提供的不只是对未来利润的索取权。它还是在当下取得那笔被许诺收入的机制。当公司在股票市场出售股份时，拥有公司的投资者出售的是一种财产：今天对从未来获得的资产的所有权。这就是所谓“资本化”未来收入的过程。发起人从出售中获得的意外之财并非凭空而来，而是来自资本化的政治稳固性——一种把对未来的私人索取权货币化并加以出售的方法。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-006"></a>[6](#note-int-006)这里的“政治稳固性”指的是使未来索取权具有非凡价值所依赖的一切权威、法律、警务、经济推理，以及对社会正义或地球未来之诉求的漠视。

An investor-owned company provides not just a claim on future profits. It is a mechanism for acquiring that promised income in the present. In offering shares for sale on the stock market, the investors who own a firm are selling a form of property, the ownership today of assets acquired from the future. This is the process known as ‘capitalising’ a future revenue. The windfalls the promoters earn from the sale come not from thin air, but from the political robustness of capitalisation – the method of monetising and marketing a private claim to the future.<a id="ref-en-note-int-006"></a>[6](#note-int-006) The term ‘political robustness’ here refers to all the forms of authority, law, policing, economic reasoning, and disregard of claims for social justice or planetary futures on which the extraordinary value of a future claim depends.

<a id="introduction-0019"></a>

这笔意外之财代表的是强加给公司未来客户和劳动者、以及他们所属社区和<a id="page-6"></a>〔原书第6页〕生态的负担的价值。公司的利润乃至股东的分红，都取决于维持并确实增加这一负担。股份的价值以及它所依赖的分红，优先于劳动者要求更公平工资、客户要求更低价格、社区要求保护公共物品的任何诉求——这种优先性反映了公司相对于劳动者、客户和社区更强大的力量。这种力量正是“市场支配地位”这一误导性狭窄术语所指的权力。这项负担并非经营企业的必要成本，而是公司支配地位使其能够强加的一项附加费。优步 820 亿美元的估值，代表了这样一种权力安排的现值。公司的司机和乘客，以及因其对公共交通和其他集体物品的影响而受到波及的更广泛人群，将在一段时间内自掏腰包偿还这一价值。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-007"></a>[7](#note-int-007)

The windfall represents the value of an encumbrance imposed on the firm’s future customers and workers and on the communities and <a id="page-6-en"></a>〔原书第6页〕ecologies to which they belong. The company’s profits, and thus its shareholders’ dividends, depend on maintaining and indeed increasing this burden. The value of the share, and the dividend on which it depends, takes priority over any demand from workers for fairer wages, from customers for lower prices, or from communities for the protection of common goods – a priority that reflects the greater strength of the company compared to its workers, customers, and communities. This strength is the power indicated by the misleadingly narrow term ‘market dominance’. The encumbrance is not a necessary cost of running a business, but a surcharge that the dominant position of the company allows it to impose. The $82-billion valuation of Uber represented the present value of such a power arrangement. The firm’s drivers and passengers, and the wider populations affected by its impact on public transport and other collective goods, would repay this value, over time, from their pockets.<a id="ref-en-note-int-007"></a>[7](#note-int-007)

<a id="introduction-0020"></a>

因此，股东公司是一套殖民时间的装置。它提供了一种手段，通过向未来数千万用户施加额外收费，在当下让一群企业家和金融家致富。那些设立控制机制、安排信贷额度从而搭建这套装置的人今天获得的意外之财，将由数月、数年或数十年后生活的人——事实上，是攫取装置所能延伸到的最远的未来——用收入来支付。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-008"></a>[8](#note-int-008)除了让创始人致富，企业股份还可以为购买和交易股份的散户投资者与投资基金、为收取交易费用的人、为从股价涨跌中投机的人提供收益来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-009"></a>[9](#note-int-009)事实上，随着强加给未来收入的抽取不断加重，即使中等富裕者也转向这些攫取方式，依靠私人退休基金、房地产投资和其他增值资产来保护自己的生活水平。这进一步加重了未来、特别是那些日益无力购买住房或其他资产的人所承受的负担。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-010"></a>[10](#note-int-010)

The shareholder corporation is thus an apparatus for colonising time. It provides a means of enriching a group of entrepreneurs and financiers in the present by imposing an additional charge on tens of millions of users in the future. The windfall acquired today by those who set up the control mechanisms and arrange the credit lines out of which the apparatus is built will be paid from the incomes of those living months, years, or decades from now – in fact, as far into the future as the apparatus of capture can be extended.<a id="ref-en-note-int-008"></a>[8](#note-int-008) Besides enriching its founders, the shares in a business firm can also provide a source of gain to the retail investors and investment funds that purchase and trade them, to those who charge fees for such trades, and to those who speculate in the rise and fall of their price.<a id="ref-en-note-int-009"></a>[9](#note-int-009) Indeed, as the extractions imposed on future incomes increase, even the moderately well off turn to these modes of capture, relying on private retirement funds, property investments, and other appreciating assets to protect their standard of living. This compounds the imposition of costs on the future, in particular upon those increasingly unable to purchase housing or other assets.<a id="ref-en-note-int-010"></a>[10](#note-int-010)

<a id="introduction-0021"></a>

这种对未来攫取并不是科技公司、风险投资和资产管理公司时代的独特现象。在现代企业兴起之前的数百年里，就有让民众陷入债务的手段，通常是通过商人向遭遇突然困境或背负纳税义务的人提供信贷。但商人的利润更多来自利用地理空间上的价格差异，而不是资本化所依赖的时间推迟。使未来背负负担的<a id="page-7"></a>〔原书第7页〕规模是较晚近的事。在过去一个半世纪中，随着现代企业攫取收入的方法出现，股东公司迅速成为伟大的挪威裔美国经济学家托斯丹·凡勃伦 1923 年所称的“文明生活的主导制度”。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-011"></a>[11](#note-int-011)

Nothing about this capture of the future is unique to the contemporary era of tech firms, venture capital, and asset-management companies. For centuries before the rise of modern business firms, there were means of placing populations in debt, typically through merchants providing credit to those experiencing sudden hardship or burdened with tax obligations. But merchants’ profits arose more often from taking advantage of differences in price across geographical space than from the temporal postponement on which capitalisation depends. The <a id="page-7-en"></a>〔原书第7页〕scale of encumbering the future is more recent. When the modern corporate method of capturing revenues emerged over the last century and a half, the shareholder corporation quickly became what the great Norwegian American economist Thorstein Veblen called in 1923 ‘the master institution of civilised life’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-011"></a>[11](#note-int-011)

<a id="introduction-0022"></a>

还有其他从未来抽取支付、承受以往负担之重的生活方式，本书将探讨其中几种。当殖民公司开始引发殖民战争时，给予它们特许状的君主们向同一批大商人借款以支付战争费用，制造了毁灭性的公共债务。战争费用不是像过去统治者那样用当期收入偿还，而是通过抵押未来年份的税收来偿还，由此形成了所谓的国债——并在这一过程中发明了现代“国家”（nation），作为承担这一负担的主体。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-012"></a>[12](#note-int-012)政府债券和其他形式的公共债务成为最大的信用创造工具，把征税权变成一套不断扩张的未来抽取装置。军国主义在许多国家仍然是迫使民众陷入长期债务的主要手段，压缩了可用于维持医疗、教育和其他公共福利的公共资源份额。在全球南方许多地区，因依赖国际债权人而膨胀的国债——无论近来还是殖民时期——一再把整个国家变成债务机器，让组织信贷供给的人致富。

There are other methods of extracting payments from the future, and of living under the weight of past encumbrances, several of which this book will explore. When colonising corporations began to provoke colonial warfare, the monarchs who chartered them drew on credit from the same large merchants to fund the costs of war, creating ruinous public debts. The cost of war was repaid not from current revenue, as rulers had done in the past, but by pledging the tax revenue of future years, creating what became known as the national debt – inventing, in the process, the modern ‘nation’ as the body accountable for this imposition.<a id="ref-en-note-int-012"></a>[12](#note-int-012) Government bonds and other kinds of public debt became the largest instruments of credit creation, turning the power of taxation into an expanding apparatus for extraction from the future. Militarism continues to be a principal means in many countries of forcing populations into long-term debt, shrinking the share of public resources available to maintain healthcare, education, and other common benefits. In many parts of the Global South, the forms of national debt, swollen by dependence on international creditors, both recently and in the colonial past, have repeatedly turned countries as a whole into debt machines, enriching those who organise the supply of credit.

<a id="introduction-0023"></a>

军费债务、外国贷款和公司股票市场把成本强加给一般民众，而另有许多工具在特定个人和家庭身上制造负担。凡勃伦论述股东公司约十年后，第二种“主导制度”出现，用于在当下实现未来收入：抵押贷款银行和住房市场。1930 年代以前，住房抵押贷款在美国、英国或其他地方都很少使用，但它把住房变成另一种广泛使用的资本化方式。在南方许多国家，这种贷款至今仍使用有限；然而奇怪的是，近几十年来，把土地和住房变成金融资产一直被吹捧为解决全球贫困的灵丹妙药。住房的投机性开发有更长的历史，尤其是在英格兰这样的国家，城市扩张用地常被大型私人地产垄断。但新住房通常用于出租，建筑物的租金与土地的租金分开计算，且仅以<a id="page-8"></a>〔原书第8页〕建造成本为基础。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-013"></a>[13](#note-int-013)住房抵押贷款（以房产作担保的贷款）并未广泛使用，通常不到房屋价值的一半，且常常在几年后一次性还清。西方在第二次世界大战前后发明了长期抵押贷款，由政府担保补贴，按月分期偿还、为期数十年，把住房变成一套扩展的未来支付攫取装置。投机建筑商现在出售房屋时，价格不再基于实体建造成本，而是基于居住三十年以上所折算的资本化价值。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-014"></a>[14](#note-int-014)20 世纪下半叶，随着住房成为北大西洋世界遥遥领先的最大资产化和债务载体，住房价格上涨的 75% 到 90% 以上，都不能归于建造成本，而应归于这种资本化方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-015"></a>[15](#note-int-015)

While military debt, foreign loans, and corporate stock markets impose costs on a population in general, there are numerous devices for creating encumbrances on specific individuals and households. About a decade after Veblen wrote about the shareholder corporation, a second ‘master institution’ emerged for realising future revenue in the present: the mortgage bank and the housing market. Little used in the United States, Britain, or elsewhere before the 1930s, home mortgages converted housing into another widely used mode of capitalisation. In many countries of the South, they are still used sparingly today, although strangely, turning land and housing into financial assets has been touted in recent decades as a magical solution to global poverty. The speculative development of housing has a much longer history, especially in countries like England where the land for urban expansion was often monopolised by large private estates. But new housing was typically leased or rented, with the lease of the building calculated separately from the lease of the land, and based simply on the cost of <a id="page-8-en"></a>〔原书第8页〕construction.<a id="ref-en-note-int-013"></a>[13](#note-int-013) Housing mortgages (loans secured by the property) were not widely used, typically covered less than half the value of the home, and were usually paid off in a lump sum after a handful of years. The invention of long-term mortgages in the West, in the years before and after the Second World War, subsidised with government guarantees and repaid in monthly instalments over decades, transformed housing into an expanded apparatus for the capture of payments from the future. Speculative builders could now sell homes not at the cost of their material construction, but at the capitalised value of occupying a residence over thirty or more years.<a id="ref-en-note-int-014"></a>[14](#note-int-014) In the second half of the twentieth century, as housing became by far the largest vehicle of assetisation and debt across the North Atlantic world, between 75 and more than 90 per cent of the increased price of housing was attributable not to the cost of construction but to this mode of capitalisation.<a id="ref-en-note-int-015"></a>[15](#note-int-015)

<a id="introduction-0024"></a>

随着住房价格开始大幅超过建造成本，房地产和抵押贷款行业成长为足以与股份公司匹敌的装置，用来使未来负债，并在当下攫取预期收入。这种不劳而获的增值使一位纽约建筑师把一座新建筑描述为“一台让土地付钱的机器”。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-016"></a>[16](#note-int-016)土地付费的观念反映出，住房成本的上升表现为开发土地价值的提高，尽管这一价值并非来自土地性质的任何变化，而是来自更强大的机制，能够确保未来数十年的租金和抵押贷款支付，包括分区规划、种族隔离和止赎等机器。即使是一处多年前已付清购地和建造成本的旧房产，也要收取这笔费用。付款并非来自土地，而是来自需要居住或工作场所的人。银行和房地产公司的利润，由此给普通人的收入增添了非凡的财务负担。在后来的几十年里，汽车贷款、信用卡、大学教育、医疗账单以及许多其他工具相继出现，把人生历程转化为还款时间表。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-017"></a>[17](#note-int-017)

As the price of housing began exceeding the cost of construction by a large factor, the real estate and mortgage industries grew to rival the joint-stock corporation as apparatuses for indebting the future and capturing a prospective revenue in the present. This unearned increment led a New York architect to describe a new building as ‘a machine that makes the land pay’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-016"></a>[16](#note-int-016) The idea of a payment for land reflected the fact that the increased cost of housing appeared as the higher value of development land, even though the value came not from any change in the nature of land but from the enhanced mechanisms for securing decades of prospective rent and mortgage payments, including the machinery of zoning, racial segregation, and foreclosure. The cost was charged even for a used property whose land purchase and production expense were paid off many years before. The payments came not from the land but from those needing a place to live or work. The profits of banks and property firms thus added an extraordinary financial burden on the incomes of ordinary people. In later decades, the automobile loan, the credit card, the college education, the medical bill, and many other devices emerged for converting the course of human lives into repayment schedules.<a id="ref-en-note-int-017"></a>[17](#note-int-017)

<a id="introduction-0025"></a>

今天，几乎所有预期支付的安排都可以资本化。任何可靠地施加于未来的负担，都会变成一种资产，可以在当下一并打包、推销并折价购得：从公司股票和债券到信用卡债务，从住房租金到基础设施收费，从水电供应到数据流，从交易平台和云服务到音乐和写作版税。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-018"></a>[18](#note-int-018)这些支付流以折价卖给<a id="page-9"></a>〔原书第9页〕投资者，并常常在二级市场交易；此后，它便承担着按全价偿还这笔预付款的负担，产生一种投资者作为“利息”享有的不劳而获的增值。资本化的负担并不只是加在资本成本或资产价值上的一笔费用。资本本身正是通过这一过程产生的——不是像我们通常想象的那样，作为从过去积攒下来的资产，而是作为这些从未来抽取的机制。

Today, almost any arrangement of prospective payment can be capitalised. Any encumbrance reliably placed on the future becomes an asset that is open to being bundled, marketed, and acquired in the present at a discount, from corporate shares and bonds to credit card debt, from housing rents to infrastructure fees, from water and electricity supplies to data streams, from trading platforms and cloud services to musical and writing royalties.<a id="ref-en-note-int-018"></a>[18](#note-int-018) Sold at a discounted price to <a id="page-9-en"></a>〔原书第9页〕investors and often traded in secondary markets, the payment stream then carries the burden of repaying this advance at full price, creating an unearned increment that the investor enjoys as ‘interest’. The burden of capitalisation is not simply a charge added to the cost of capital or to the value of an asset. Capital itself comes into being through this process – not as an asset saved up from the past, as we usually imagine, but as these mechanisms of extraction from the future.

<a id="introduction-0026"></a>

### 驱动利润

### Driving Profits

<a id="introduction-0027"></a>

我们与未来关系令人惊讶之处在于，我们对自身如何使未来贫乏如此盲目，与此同时却在当下承受先前强加的负担。一个世纪前，像凡勃伦这样的经济学家非常清楚这种他称为“蓄意破坏”的方法如何运作。他解释说，企业获利不是通过创新或效率，而是通过扰乱和阻碍的力量。他的年轻同代人中更著名的约瑟夫·熊彼特，我们将在[第一章](#ch01-0001)中第一次见到他——当时他还是开罗的一位年轻经济学家，帮助拯救了一家糖业公司，并发展了一小片甘蔗种植园——他对资本持有一种不同但相关的看法，认为资本具有破坏性，并理解资本依赖于对未来的支配。在本书中，我们将始终关注这种破坏、施加负担、支配和扰乱的历史。今天，经济学家有另一套语言可用。他们把这种靠后来者偿还债务来生活的方法，转换为所谓的“增长”。

The surprising thing about our relationship to the future is that we have become so blind to the way in which we impoverish it, living in the present under the burden of previous impositions. A century ago, it was quite clear to an economist like Thorstein Veblen how this method of sabotage, as he called it, operated. Business made its profits, he explained, not through innovation or efficiency, but through powers of disruption and obstruction. His younger and better-known contemporary, Joseph Schumpeter, whom we will first meet in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001) as a youthful economist in Cairo, where he helped rescue a sugar company and develop a small sugar plantation, had a different but related view of capital as disruptive and an understanding of its dependence on a command of the future. Throughout this book, we will pay attention to histories of such sabotage, encumbrance, command, and disruption. Today, economists have available a different language. They transpose the method of living at the expense of those who will repay the debt into what is called ‘growth’.

<a id="introduction-0028"></a>

把施加负担描绘成增长，用了两种手法。就企业而言，第一种是把企业价值的增长归因于技术进步，而不是其从未来抽取的力量以及所依赖的“支配地位”。第二种是把当下获得的意外之财和未来用来偿还这笔意外之财的收费，都衡量为对更大善——即我们所称的“经济”的增长——的同等贡献。虽然这些论点常被用来解释企业价值增长的来源，但它们反映了一种更广泛的思考方式，涉及资本主义的发展和非劳动收益的来源。

Two moves are made to portray the imposition of encumbrances as growth. In the case of a business firm, the first is to attribute the increasing value of the business not to its power of extraction from the future and the ‘dominance’ on which this depends but to an improvement in technology. The second is to measure both the windfall gained in the present and the charges through which it will be repaid in the future as equivalent contributions to a larger good – the growth of what we call the economy. While these arguments are routinely offered to explain the source of an increase in the value of a business, they reflect a wider way of thinking about the development of capitalism and the sources of unearned gain.

<a id="introduction-0029"></a>

第一种手法把收益归因于技术。成功企业的高估值，不正是由带来效率提升的创新所致吗？投资者享有的意外之财，不正是他们扶持创新的回报吗？企业未来的<a id="page-10"></a>〔原书第10页〕员工和客户，不正是这些效率和成本节约的受益者吗？技术进步不正是支配各经济体增长以及全球富国与穷国差距的更广泛原则吗？

The first move ascribes the gain to technology. Is not the high valuation of successful companies due to innovation, which produces increased efficiencies? Are not the windfalls enjoyed by investors simply their reward for fostering innovation? Will not a firm’s future <a id="page-10-en"></a>〔原书第10页〕employees and customers be the beneficiaries of these efficiencies and cost savings? Is not the progress of technology a wider principle governing the growth of economies and the difference on a global level between rich nations and poor?

<a id="introduction-0030"></a>

让我们再次回到优步这个简单而有用的例子。正如休伯特·霍兰所解释的，它的成功不能归因于任何技术突破。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-019"></a>[19](#note-int-019)它的商业模式——用私家车取代公司自有的出租车或豪华轿车车队，让司机承担燃料、所有权、保险和维修成本——是从对手公司那里借来的。它的智能手机应用，是由外部承包商“拼凑”出来的简单程序。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-020"></a>[20](#note-int-020)优步没有发明智能手机、锂离子电池、互联网、GPS、蜂窝网络、电子支付，也没有发明汽车客运服务公司使用的任何其他技术。事实上，这些系统的关键组成部分是由公共资金提供的，包括全球定位卫星（由美国空军维护）、互联网协议（由科学家和业余程序员的同行群体作为共同资源开发），以及支付自动清算所（由联邦储备银行和其他国家的银行服务机构提供）。运行这些系统大部分功能的微型元件——硅基半导体——由埃及裔美国机械工程师穆罕默德·阿塔拉及其同事在 1950 年代发明，据说是历史上制造量最大的器件，而它源自美国军方对足够轻、可用于火箭的部件的需求。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-021"></a>[21](#note-int-021)到优步创立时，智能手机、蜂窝网络、GPS、电子支付等系统的协同使用，正扩散到城市生活的几乎每个领域，从点餐、购物到乘坐公交车。它们在私人交通中的使用由优步从更早的初创企业借来，很快又被大多数汽车客运服务公司和出汽车客运服务公司采用。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-022"></a>[22](#note-int-022)优步的创新——如果有的话——在于把使用这些设备的成本转嫁给个体司机，并让大量空车在街上巡游等单，使竞争企业难以生存。优步自己也承认，其业务的主要威胁不是新技术的到来，而是每个国家都有以更优惠价格提供同样服务的对手公司。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-023"></a>[23](#note-int-023)

Let us return once more to the simple but useful example of Uber. Its success, as Hubert Horan explains, cannot be attributed to any technological breakthrough.<a id="ref-en-note-int-019"></a>[19](#note-int-019) Its business model, replacing company-owned taxi or limousine fleets with private cars whose drivers now carried the costs of fuel, ownership, insurance, and repair, was borrowed from rival companies. Its smartphone app was a rudimentary program ‘hacked together’ by outside contractors.<a id="ref-en-note-int-020"></a>[20](#note-int-020) Uber did not invent the smartphone, the lithium-ion battery, the internet, GPS, cellular networks, electronic payments, or any other technology used by car firms. In fact, vital components of these systems were provided through public funding, including global positioning satellites (maintained by the United States Air Force), internet protocols (developed as a common resource by peer groups of scientist and amateur programmers), and automated clearing houses for payments, provided by the Federal Reserve Banks and other national banking services. The miniature element running most of these systems, the silicon-based semiconductor – invented in the 1950s by an Egyptian American mechanical engineer, Mohamed Atalla, and his colleagues, and said to be the most widely manufactured device in history – emerged from the need of the US military for components light enough to use in rocketry.<a id="ref-en-note-int-021"></a>[21](#note-int-021) By the time Uber was founded, the coordinated use of smartphones, cellular networks, GPS, electronic payments, and other systems was spreading in almost every area of urban life, from ordering food to shopping to catching a city bus. Their use in private transportation, borrowed by Uber from earlier start-ups, was soon adopted by most car service companies and taxi firms.<a id="ref-en-note-int-022"></a>[22](#note-int-022) Uber’s innovation, if any, lay in transferring the cost of using these devices onto individual drivers, and in crowding the streets with so many empty vehicles cruising for rides that competing firms would struggle to survive. Uber itself acknowledged that a main threat to its business was not the arrival of new technologies but the presence of rival companies in every country offering the same service at better prices.<a id="ref-en-note-int-023"></a>[23](#note-int-023)

校注：原文在这里笼统使用“硅基半导体”。与所述研究相关的Dawon Kahng专利US3102230A描述的是一种以硅片、氧化物绝缘层和电场控制构成的特定半导体器件，不宜将此段理解为硅基半导体这一整类器件均由一人发明。正文保留原作措辞。 https://patents.google.com/patent/US3102230A/en

<a id="introduction-0031"></a>

正如大型企业长期历史中常见的那样，优步的扩张并非基于技术创新，而主要基于掠夺性定价和对政治支持的操纵，意在瓦解市政监管，迫使对手和本地公司出局。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-024"></a>[24](#note-int-024)它的风险投资者为它<a id="page-11"></a>〔原书第11页〕提供了 130 亿美元资金，其中包括来自沙特阿拉伯主权财富基金的 35 亿美元，公司用这些钱把车费定得远低于每单成本。最初，公司每赚到 1 美元车费，就要付出 1.50 美元成本。后来它减少了亏损，但只是靠提高每笔车费中的抽成、压低司机收入，把平均“抽成率”从 20% 提高到接近 30%。在某些情况下，优步抽走的车费比例可达 50% 以上。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-025"></a>[25](#note-int-025)

As so often in the long history of large business firms, Uber’s expansion was based not on technological innovation but largely on its predatory pricing and the manipulation of political support, intended to break down municipal regulation and to force rival firms and local companies out of business.<a id="ref-en-note-int-024"></a>[24](#note-int-024) Its venture capitalist investors equipped it <a id="page-11-en"></a>〔原书第11页〕with a fund of $13 billion, including $3.5 billion from the Saudi Arabian sovereign wealth fund, which it used to set the price of fares well below the cost of each ride. Initially, the firm was paying $1.50 in costs for every dollar it earned carrying passengers. Later it reduced the loss, but only by increasing the share it claimed from each fare and forcing down the income of its drivers, increasing its average ‘take rate’ from 20 to almost 30 per cent. In some cases, the portion of the fare that Uber took could be 50 per cent or more.<a id="ref-en-note-int-025"></a>[25](#note-int-025)

<a id="introduction-0032"></a>

这不是新技术，而是“旧事物的冲击”。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-026"></a>[26](#note-int-026)正如经常发生的那样，新业务的核心是某种出人意料地并不新颖的东西：已有百年历史的私家车机器。在建造二十世纪那些不可持续的世界方面，没有哪种机器比私家汽车更重要。汽车使石油生产成为世界最大产业，对碳排放增长和气候崩溃威胁的贡献超过任何其他装置。私家车对人们的生活方式也产生了类似影响：城市中多达 50% 的土地用于道路和停车，促成了郊区及其碳密集的住房、土地利用和私有化交通方式。而个人拥有汽车——汽车是多数家庭可能购买的物品中远为昂贵的一项——催生了最早、规模最大的企业消费金融形式。汽车工业开创了广泛的个人债务，使日常生活和劳动成为向银行支付费用和利息的不断扩张的系统。

Rather than a new technology, this was the ‘shock of the old’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-026"></a>[26](#note-int-026) As often happens, the core of the new business was something surprisingly unoriginal, the century-old machinery of the private car. No machine was more important than the private automobile for building the unsustainable worlds of the twentieth century. The motorcar made the production of petroleum the world’s largest industry, contributing more than any other device to the growth of carbon emissions and the threat of climate collapse. Private cars had a parallel effect on how people lived, accounting for up to 50 per cent of land use in cities for roads and parking and enabling the creation of suburbia, with its carbon-intensive modes of housing, land use, and privatised transportation. And the individual ownership of cars, by far the most expensive item that most households might purchase, generated the first and largest forms of corporate consumer finance. The car industry pioneered the creation of widespread personal debt, through which everyday lives and labour became an expanding system for funding the payment of fees and interest to banks.

<a id="introduction-0033"></a>

新的交通公司没有开发新技术，而是找到另一种从私人车辆使用中获取收入的方式，与石油公司、房地产开发商、汽车制造商、以石油为基础的主权财富基金和银行业并立。少数全球叫车服务公司如今能够许诺这样一个未来：从每一次车辆出行中抽取垄断租金。

Instead of developing a novel technology, the new transportation firms had found a different way to earn payments from the use of private vehicles, slotting in alongside oil companies, property developers, motorcar manufacturers, petroleum-based sovereign wealth funds, and the banking industry. A handful of global car service corporations could now promise a future in which they would extract monopoly rents from every vehicle journey.

<a id="introduction-0034"></a>

数十年来，经济学家和经济史家一直诉诸“技术”观念来解释巨大财富的创造。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-027"></a>[27](#note-int-027)这种解释方式不仅用于说明特定企业或企业家的利润，也用于说明集体生活组织中的巨大转变，例子很多。从欧洲对非欧洲世界的殖民，到英国工业革命；从通过河流治理、筑坝和土地清理对生态进行重新工程化，到铁路、电网、石油<a id="page-12"></a>〔原书第12页〕管道、数据中心以及其他交通、储存、通信和电力大型基础设施的建设：一次又一次，技术进步的观念为资本扩张的力量提供了解释。几乎同样长久以来，技术史家一直在质疑归于抽象技术力量的那种威力。问题不在于许多装置是否改善了人类境况——尽管未必总是惠及所有人，也并非没有代价，尤其并非没有威胁到一个适宜人类繁荣的星球能否继续存续这一前景。毋宁说，正如优步的案例所示，技术发展即使让生活更宜居，也往往是用旧部件临时拼装而成，而且通常很快被共享。

For many decades, economists and economic historians have been appealing to the idea of ‘technology’ to explain the creation of great wealth.<a id="ref-en-note-int-027"></a>[27](#note-int-027) There are many examples of this way of accounting not just for the profits of particular firms or entrepreneurs but for large transformations in the organisation of collective life. From Europe’s colonisation of the non-European world, to the British industrial revolution; to the re-engineering of ecologies through river control, dam building, and land clearing; to the construction of railways, electrical grids, oil <a id="page-12-en"></a>〔原书第12页〕pipelines, data centres, and other large infrastructures of transportation, storage, communication, and power: again and again, the idea of technological advance offers the explanation for the power of capital to expand. For almost as long, historians of technology have been questioning the power attributed to the abstract force of technology. The question is not whether many devices have improved the human condition – although not always for everyone, and not without costs, not least to the very prospect of the continued viability of a planet hospitable to human flourishing. Rather, as the case of Uber shows, technical developments, even where they make life more liveable, are often jury-rigged from older components and are usually quickly shared.

<a id="introduction-0035"></a>

### 经济学家希望经济长什么样

### What Economists Would Like the Economy to Look Like

<a id="introduction-0036"></a>

技术创新难以解释非劳动的财富增长。把这些意外之财——以及它们所依赖的负担——归因于技术，构成了我所谓资本托词的一个方面：使未来背负负担的阻碍与控制关系，在此被误认或忽视。在这种忽视中，经济学扮演着特殊角色。它是一门没有研究技术物与政治关系如何共同生产的传统的知识领域；更值得注意的是，它不研究技术、政治或经济之间的边界如何不断被协商，也不研究这种协商如何同时确立权力关系和概念含义。相反，经济思想依赖一种简单的技术观念，不仅用来理解当前时代——被“科技”这一意象本身所捕捉——而且用来解释资本主义本身。这一托词没有把资本看作与未来的关系，而是代之以一种旧的资本观：资本是从过去积攒起来、借给企业家的资金，通常用于投资机器或技术以赚取更多钱。在通俗想象和许多经济学家的模型中，这种技术设备成了资本本身的代表。于是，投资者和企业家积累的意外之财与利息支付，可以被描述为对那些表面上的“储蓄”被用于增长更多财富者的回报——而不是投资基金和金融机构凭借国家担保的特权与保护、组织对未来支付的支配而强加的费用。

Technical innovation does not easily account for unearned increases in wealth. Attributing these windfalls – and the encumbrances on which they rely – to technology operates as an aspect of what I call the alibi of capital, in which the relations of obstruction and control that allow the future to be encumbered are misidentified or overlooked. In this overlooking, economics plays a special role. It operates as a field of knowledge with no tradition of studying how technical objects and political relations are coproduced; or, more significantly, how the boundary between what is technical and what is political or economic is continually negotiated; or how this negotiation helps to establish both relations of power and the meanings of concepts. Instead, economic thought depends on a simple idea of technology, not only to understand the current era – captured by the very image of ‘tech’ – but to explain capitalism itself. Rather than seeing capital as a relation to the future, the alibi substitutes an old view of capital as funds that have been saved up from the past, to be loaned to entrepreneurs, typically to invest in the machines or technology required to make more money. In the popular imagination, and many economists’ models, this technical equipment comes to stand for capital itself. The windfalls and interest payments accrued by investors and entrepreneurs can then be described as the reward given to those whose apparent ‘savings’ have been used to grow more wealth – rather than the charge imposed by investment funds and financial institutions that, thanks to their state-guaranteed privileges and protections, organise the command of payments from the future.

<a id="introduction-0037"></a>

<a id="page-13"></a>〔原书第13页〕在本书其他章节中，我们将引入若干术语，以理解经济学在促成和掩盖未来攫取这两方面所占据的位置。这些术语包括“技术政治”，指一种研究政治和政治经济学的方法，它不把技术和物质过程仅仅当作政治经济分析的对象，而是把它们视为我们的政治得以成形的安排；“资本化”和“经济化”，指商品和活动被攫取并变得可计算的方式；“经济全景装置”（EconoCon），指“经济”的生产，类比米歇尔·福柯对杰里米·边沁全景敞视监狱的解读，把它视为一种安排欲望、管理未来的装置；以及“经济义论”（oikodicy），类比“神义论”这一神学概念，用来理解经济学在辩护人类苦难方面所起的作用。借用宗教研究术语，并非暗示经济学已取代宗教的角色，而是像我们将看到的，提请注意“宗教”与“经济”作为现代概念并行出现，作为相互关联的辩护实践。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-028"></a>[28](#note-int-028)

<a id="page-13-en"></a>〔原书第13页〕In other chapters of this book, we will introduce a number of terms for understanding the place of economics in both facilitating and obfuscating the capture of the future. These include the idea of ‘technopolitics’, meaning an approach to studying politics and political economy that treats technical and material processes not merely as the object of political and economic analysis but as the arrangements through which our politics takes shape; ‘capitalisation’ and ‘economisation’, referring to the ways in which goods and activities are captured and made calculable; the ‘EconoCon’, referring to the production of ‘the economy’, by analogy with Michel Foucault’s reading of Jeremy Bentham’s Panopticon, as a device for ordering desire and managing the future; and ‘oikodicy’, by analogy with the theological concept of ‘theodicy’, for understanding the role of economics in the justification of human suffering. Adopting a term from the study of religion is intended not to suggest that economics has come to replace the role of religion, but to draw attention, as we will see, to the parallel emergence of ‘religion’ and ‘economy’ as modern concepts, working as connected practices of justification.<a id="ref-en-note-int-028"></a>[28](#note-int-028)

<a id="introduction-0038"></a>

不过，现在让我们暂且停留在优步这个较简单的想法上。尽管有相反证据，经济学家仍把对未来租金的抽取归因于所谓的技术进步。就优步而言，公司雇用自己的经济学家，把对剩余日益增强的支配描述为客户福利。公司的垄断地位提供了提出这类主张所需的私有数据。在设定乘客车费和司机工资时，优步受益于对每次行程所收集信息的排他性控制。这使公司能够根据算法调整收费，算计司机工资能压多低、乘客车费能提多高，以便每一刻都最大化自己的份额。这种被称为“动态加价”的做法规避了车费监管和最低工资支付，却被宣传为新价值的技术来源。数百万私人付费乘客的专有数据被用来构建这一论点。

For now, however, let us stay with the simpler idea of Uber. Despite the evidence to the contrary, economists continue to attribute the extracting of future rents to supposed improvements in technology. In the case of Uber, the firm employed its own economists to describe the increasing command of surplus as a customer benefit. The company’s monopoly provided the private data through which such claims could be made. In setting passenger fares and drivers’ wages, Uber benefited from exclusive control of the information gathered from every ride taken. This enabled the firm to adjust charges according to an algorithm that calculated how low drivers’ wages could be pushed, or how high passenger fares increased, to maximise its own share at every moment. Known as ‘surge pricing’, this evasion of fare regulation and minimum wage payments was promoted as the technological source of new value. The proprietary data from millions of private fare payers was used to construct the argument.

<a id="introduction-0039"></a>

优步的经济学家在 2016 年发表了一篇学术论文，估算这种福利的价值。他们声称，在优步车费上每支付 1 美元，就产生 1.60 美元的价值，由此创造出他们富有想象力地称为“消费者剩余”的每年 68 亿美元。这个数字是优步实际收取的车费与乘客可能愿意支付的最高车费之间的差额，后者根据乘客对动态加价的反应估算。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-029"></a>[29](#note-int-029)换句话说，优步未能充分运用其动态加价<a id="page-14"></a>〔原书第14页〕算法、未能每时每刻都榨取最高价格，反而成了依赖其叫车服务者的福利。商业媒体和经济学家博客宣传这些发现，作为优步技术正在创造新价值形式的证据。优步向大学经济学家支付高达 10 万美元的报酬，请他们撰写学术文章，支持公司关于其车费计算和司机报酬方法对双方都有利的主张。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-030"></a>[30](#note-int-030)

Economists at Uber published an academic paper in 2016 estimating the value of the benefit. Every dollar paid for Uber rides, they claimed, produced $1.60 in value, generating what they labelled imaginatively as a ‘consumer surplus’ of $6.8 billion a year. This figure was the difference between the fare Uber charged and the highest fare passengers might have been willing to pay, estimated from their responses to surge pricing.<a id="ref-en-note-int-029"></a>[29](#note-int-029) In other words, Uber’s failure to fully deploy its surge-pricing <a id="page-14-en"></a>〔原书第14页〕algorithm and extract the highest possible price at every instant became a benefit to those dependent on its car services. The business press and the blogs of economists promoted these findings as evidence of the novel forms of value that Uber’s technology was creating. Uber paid university economists fees as high as $100,000 to author academic articles favourable to the company’s claim that its method of calculating fares for riders and payments for drivers produced benefits for both.<a id="ref-en-note-int-030"></a>[30](#note-int-030)

<a id="introduction-0040"></a>

许多经济学家努力使经济体现他们观念中的真理，包括这样一种观念：一种更高效或更具强制性的定价方法可以创造价值。他们的写作常常体现了“傲慢技术”——运用操作上娴熟但概念上狭隘的分析形式，来确认并颂扬某种技术改进。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-031"></a>[31](#note-int-031)芝加哥大学一位著名经济学家是那篇关于动态加价的优步论文的合著者，他把这家公司描述为“经济学家心目中经济应有的样子的化身”。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-032"></a>[32](#note-int-032)

Many economists work hard to make the economy embody the truth of their ideas, including the idea that a more efficient or coercive pricing method can create value. Their writing often exemplifies the ‘technologies of hubris’ that deploy mechanically proficient but conceptually narrow forms of analysis to confirm and celebrate some technical improvement.<a id="ref-en-note-int-031"></a>[31](#note-int-031) A prominent University of Chicago economist, who co-authored the Uber paper on surge pricing, described the firm as ‘the embodiment of what the economists would like the economy to look like’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-032"></a>[32](#note-int-032)

<a id="introduction-0041"></a>

看似技术突破的东西，反而可能成为新成本和无效率的来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-033"></a>[33](#note-int-033)优步和 Lyft 与本地汽车客运服务公司有一个重要区别：新公司不拥有车辆。要求司机使用自己的车辆，使车辆的拥有和管理更昂贵，因为车主无法享受批量购车和投保折扣，也无法享受受到监督的维护计划。这些公司设定司机工资和工作条件，却拒绝把他们归类为雇员，使其无法享有最低工资或就业福利。不拥有车辆，使新公司得以规避城市监管汽车客运服务业的法律。市政监管无论多么不完善，至少能够筛查和许可司机，并制定保障公共利益的规则，例如要求接受前往较贫困社区的乘客、容纳残障乘客，以及确保司机最低工资的车费。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-034"></a>[34](#note-int-034)

What appears as a technological breakthrough can instead be the source of new costs and inefficiencies.<a id="ref-en-note-int-033"></a>[33](#note-int-033) Uber and Lyft differed from local car service firms in one important way: the new companies did not own the vehicles. Requiring drivers to use their own cars made the vehicles more expensive to own and manage, as owners could not benefit from fleet discounts for buying and insuring them or from supervised maintenance programmes. The companies set drivers’ wages and terms of work but refused to class them as employees, with rights to a minimum wage or employment benefits. Owning no cars allowed the new firms to evade the laws with which cities regulated the car service industry. Municipal regulation, however imperfect, had allowed for the screening and licensing of drivers and for rules ensuring public goods, such as the requirement to accept riders travelling to poorer neighbourhoods or to accommodate those with disabilities, and for fares that assured drivers a minimum wage.<a id="ref-en-note-int-034"></a>[34](#note-int-034)

<a id="introduction-0042"></a>

这种对市政府的削弱带来了更广泛的成本，抵消了任何可能的技术改进的好处。优步的长期目标不只是摧毁城市汽车客运服务公司，还包括摧毁公共交通。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-035"></a>[35](#note-int-035)为美国国家科学院所做的一项研究发现，这些公司补贴的车程把乘客从公共交通吸引走，使公共服务失去收入。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-036"></a>[36](#note-int-036)该报告的一位作者在另一项研究中发现，在人口稠密的大城市，如果没有新的叫车服务公司，60% 的叫车服务使用者“本会乘坐公共交通、步行、骑车或干脆不出行”，由此使城市街道上的驾驶量<a id="page-15"></a>〔原书第15页〕增加 160%。为了建立垄断，新公司宣传车辆的即时可用性；这依赖过剩司机在街上巡游等单，让汽车堵塞道路，损害行人和骑行者，并增加空气污染和化石燃料燃烧。报告把影响总结为“更多车流，更少公交，更少公平与环境可持续性”。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-037"></a>[37](#note-int-037)另一项研究表明，美国城市引入网约车服务还提高了机动车事故和死亡率，包括行人死亡，帮助逆转了美国交通事故死亡率的长期下降趋势。用美国交通部所称的统计生命价值（VSL）计算，与网约车相关的死亡增加每年造成约 94.8 亿美元成本——这一成本未被计入公司利润或技术改进，对数万名受伤或丧生者而言，则是对其未来的急剧截断。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-038"></a>[38](#note-int-038)

There were wider costs to this undermining of municipal government, which offset the benefit of any possible technical improvements. Uber’s long-term goal was to destroy not only urban car service companies but also public transportation.<a id="ref-en-note-int-035"></a>[35](#note-int-035) A study for the National Academy of Sciences found that the companies’ subsidised rides drew passengers away from mass transit, depriving public services of income.<a id="ref-en-note-int-036"></a>[36](#note-int-036) One of the authors of that report found in another study that 60 per cent of car service users in large, dense cities ‘would have taken public transportation, walked, biked or not made the trip’ if the new car service companies had not been available, causing a 160 per cent increase in driving <a id="page-15-en"></a>〔原书第15页〕on city streets. To build their monopoly, the new firms promoted the instant availability of vehicles, which relied on surplus drivers cruising the streets waiting for rides, clogging roadways with cars at the expense of pedestrians and cyclists and increasing air pollution and the burning of fossil fuels. The report summed up the impact as ‘more traffic, less transit, and less equity and environmental sustainability’.<a id="ref-en-note-int-037"></a>[37](#note-int-037) A further study showed that the introduction of ride-sharing services in American cities also increased the rate of vehicle accidents and fatalities, including pedestrian deaths, helping to reverse the long-term decline in American traffic fatalities. Using what the US Department of Transportation calls the Value of a Statistical Life (VSL), the annual cost of the increase in fatalities associated with ride sharing was estimated at $9.48 billion per year – a cost included nowhere in the calculation of company profits or technological improvement and a dramatic curtailing of futures for the tens of thousands who were injured or lost their lives.<a id="ref-en-note-int-038"></a>[38](#note-int-038)

<a id="introduction-0043"></a>

新公司的未来利润并非来自技术效率或集体福利的改善，而是来自建立垄断权力的机会以及保护这种权力的政治运动。优步试图把垄断扩展到一般交通服务，2015 年推出名为“优步外卖”（Uber Eats）的送餐服务。但送餐比载人更难垄断，五年之内，公司便在埃及、海湾和印度等许多市场放弃这项服务。扩张既没有带来技术创新，也没有提供把亏损公司变成未来利润机器的手段，除非公司的政治权力使它能够从未来的司机和顾客身上抽取租金。优步吃掉的，是未来。

The future profits of the new companies would arise not from technical efficiencies or improvements in collective welfare but from the opportunities for building monopoly power and from political campaigns to protect it. Uber attempted to expand its monopoly into general transportation services, launching a food delivery service in 2015 called Uber Eats. But delivering food was harder to monopolise than delivering people, and, within five years, the company was abandoning the service in many markets, including Egypt, the Gulf, and India. Expansion offered no technical innovation and no means of turning a loss-making company into a machine of future profits, except where the firm’s political power enabled it to extract a rent payment from future drivers and customers. What Uber eats is the future.

<a id="introduction-0044"></a>

### 增长

### Growth

<a id="introduction-0045"></a>

第二种误解我们以未来为代价的生活模式的手法呢：把我们与未来的关系描述为增长？在当下攫取预期收入，反映的是对日后利润的期待。随着企业成长，它将创造“经济增长”。收入或许来自未来，但那必定是一个更大、更繁荣的未来。这种观点解释说，当下的意外之财是对企业家的回报，因为他们设计增长，为所有人创造了更大繁荣。

What about the second move for misapprehending our mode of living at the expense of the future: describing our relationship to the future as growth? The capture of prospective revenue in the present reflects the expectation of later profits. As business grows, it will create ‘economic growth’. The income may come from the future, but it is a future that will surely be larger and more prosperous. The windfall in the present is a reward, this view explains, for the entrepreneurs who engineer growth and create greater prosperity for all.

<a id="introduction-0046"></a>

与技术改进一样，经济增长是资本的托词，是一种<a id="page-16"></a>〔原书第16页〕误认我们与未来关系的方式。我们可以区分这种托词的两个方面：单个企业的成长，以及表面上的人类社会整体增长。我们已习惯用前者来估算后者，把人类集体当作一群企业来计量。我们给这家集体企业起的奇特名字，正如本书后文将探讨的，就是“经济”。

Like technical improvement, economic growth is an alibi of capital, a <a id="page-16-en"></a>〔原书第16页〕mode in which our relation to the future is misrecognised. We can distinguish two aspects of the alibi: the growth of the individual business firm, and what appears as the growth of human society as a whole. We have come to reckon the second in terms of the first, measuring the human collective as if it were a collection of business firms. The unusual name we give this collective firm, as we will explore later in this book, is ‘the economy’.

<a id="introduction-0047"></a>

托词的第一个方面是单个企业及其投资者。最初的创业者把股份卖给其他投资者，后者取得公司未来收入的所有权。他们不太可能享有创始投资者获得的横财，而且如果股市认定创始人对未来收益的估计被夸大了，他们就有亏钱的风险。但为了吸引他们购买，未来租金会以折价提供。

The first aspect of the alibi is the individual firm and its investors. The original entrepreneurs sell shares to other investors, who acquire ownership of the company’s future revenue. They are unlikely to enjoy the windfall gained by the founding investors, and risk losing money if the stock market decides the founders’ estimates of future earnings have been exaggerated. But, to attract them as buyers, they are offered the future rents at a discount.

<a id="introduction-0048"></a>

折价的计算，考虑了股票买家如果购买另一家企业的股份本可赚到多少。按照惯例，这种放弃的收益被假定为银行向企业提供信贷所收取的金额——利率。“利息”概念是描述所谓货币时间价值的一种现代方式，而这种价值如今被我们视为货币的自然属性。正如本书将表明的，它更适合被理解为现代安排的产物：一方面是可靠地推迟收入支付的安排，如股份公司；另一方面是把未来支付打包成当下可用信用货币的银行业。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-039"></a>[39](#note-int-039)没有这种可靠推迟和聚合的机制，就不会有货币的时间价值。事实上，鉴于今天大多数货币是通过银行提供信贷创造出来的，若没有这些机制，几乎就不会有货币。

The discount is calculated by considering what the buyers of stock might have earned by purchasing shares in another business. By convention, the value of that foregone earning is assumed to be the amount that banks would charge for extending credit to a firm – the rate of interest. The concept of ‘interest’ is a modern way of describing the so-called time value of money, a value that we now take to be a natural property of money. As this book will show, it is better understood as a product of modern arrangements, such as the joint-stock company, that reliably postpone income payments and a banking industry that bundles the future payments into credit money available in the present.<a id="ref-en-note-int-039"></a>[39](#note-int-039) Without such mechanisms of reliable postponement and aggregation there would be no time value of money. In fact, given the way most money is created today – through the supply of credit by banks – there would be virtually no money.

<a id="introduction-0049"></a>

对未来进行折现，是一种政治技术。它有着悠久的历史，我们将在[第三章](#ch03-0001)再谈。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-040"></a>[40](#note-int-040)贬低并购买未来收入的方法，通常被反过来描述。普通投资者不把它理解为折价购买货币，而理解为当下的一种“投资”，其价值不知何故随时间“增长”。“增长”一词暗示某种物质扩张。但这种增长的发生，并不需要任何东西在物理尺寸或复杂度上增加。恰恰相反，它需要某种东西缩水：未来收入仅以其价值的一小部分被购得。这种缩水是通过组织推迟的力量产生的。货币并非天生具有折价购买未来收入的能力。这种能力来自时间可以被控制这一事实——通过建造一套可靠地<a id="page-17"></a>〔原书第17页〕攫取和殖民未来的政治装置。我们已经生活在一个越来越受这类安排支配的世界。我们通过发展在当下廉价获取未来的机制来贬低未来的价值，然后把通往那个被窃取的未来的道路体验为“增长”。

The practice of discounting the future is a political technology. It has a long history, to which we will return in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001).<a id="ref-en-note-int-040"></a>[40](#note-int-040) The method of devaluing and purchasing a future revenue is usually described in reverse. The ordinary investor understands it not as the purchase of money at a discounted price, but as an ‘investment’ in the present that somehow ‘grows’ in value over time. The term growth suggests some kind of material expansion. But nothing is required to increase in physical size or complexity for such growth to occur. If anything, it requires something to shrink: the future revenue is acquired at a fraction of its value. This shrinkage is produced by organising the power of postponement. Money does not possess this ability to purchase future income at a discount by nature. The ability is derived from the fact that time can be controlled – by the construction of a political apparatus that will reliably <a id="page-17-en"></a>〔原书第17页〕capture and colonise the future. We have come to inhabit a world governed more and more by such arrangements. We diminish the value of the future by developing mechanisms to acquire it cheaply in the present, then experience the path to that purloined future as ‘growth’.

<a id="introduction-0050"></a>

增长观念的另一个问题在于，它不仅被视为单个企业的特征，也被视为社会的集体轨迹。为了管理对时间的控制，一个更大的政治框架被建造出来，帮助稳定企业有时不稳的时间性。这套支撑结构仅于二十世纪中叶被发明，被称为“经济”。我们通常从空间角度理解经济，把它视为特定地理疆域内一切货币交易的总和。但经济也是一台时间机器，一种安排我们与未来关系的方式——实际上是生产未来，把它作为管理我们生活的框架。与企业价值一样，经济的本性就是显得在“增长”——逐年扩张。与企业一样，这种增长掩盖了一个事实：越来越多的未来收入是以折价获得的。随后按全价偿还，又把一种消费未来的方式变成表面上的规模增长。

The other problem with the idea of growth is that it is seen not just as a feature of individual business firms, but as the collective trajectory of society. To manage the control of time, a larger political frame has been constructed that helps stabilise the sometimes unsteady temporality of the business firm. Invented only in the mid-twentieth century, this supporting armature is called ‘the economy’. We usually think of the economy in spatial terms, as the sum of all monetary transactions within a given geographical territory. But the economy is also a kind of time machine, a way of arranging our relation to the future – indeed of producing the future, as a frame inside which our lives are to be managed. Like the value of a business firm, the nature of the economy is to appear to ‘grow’ – to expand year-on-year. As with the firm, such growth hides the fact that more and more future income has been acquired at a discount. Its subsequent repayment, at full price, turns a mode of consuming the future into what appears as an increase in size.

<a id="introduction-0051"></a>

家庭购买和消费物质商品时，这种消费被计为经济的一部分。但当他们支付垄断企业强加的负担、银行和抵押贷款公司收取的利息、为教育和医疗背负的债务，以及为日益私有化和垄断化的服务支付的其他一切费用和收费时，这些不断上升的支付全都被计入“增长”的衡量。事实上，在美国和许多其他国家，所谓增长的相当一部分来自这类租金、费用和附加费，它们如今在商品生产或服务提供成本中占越来越大比重。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-041"></a>[41](#note-int-041)

When households purchase and consume material goods, this consumption is measured as part of the economy. But when they pay the encumbrances imposed by monopolistic firms, the interest payments charged by banks and mortgage companies, the debts incurred for education and healthcare, and every other expense and fee imposed for increasingly privatised and monopolised services, those escalating payments all count towards the measurement of ‘growth’. In fact, in the United States and many other countries, a significant part of so-called growth is accounted for by rents, fees, and surcharges of this kind, which are now an increasing part of the cost of creating goods or providing services.<a id="ref-en-note-int-041"></a>[41](#note-int-041)

<a id="introduction-0052"></a>

我们生活的世界，被组织成让未来负债：收入折价给债权人，日后由背负负担或债务的人全额偿还。最初折价与随后全额偿还之间的差额，被计为经济增长，并被误认为集体福祉的改善。

We live in a world organised to place the future in debt, with the income discounted to the creditor and later repaid in full by those encumbered or indebted. The difference between the initial discount and the subsequent full repayment is measured as a growth in the economy and mistaken for an improvement in collective well-being.

<a id="introduction-0053"></a>

这些当代金融和债务形式有时被描述为“金融化”，这个术语把这些成本与“实体”经济的需求和生产性——即实际商品和服务的生产——对立起来。我们在此不使用金融化概念，原因有二。第一，信用货币和债务从不是凭空<a id="page-18"></a>〔原书第18页〕变出的；它们需要建造一套真实的未来支付攫取装置，对它的控制是一切信用货币的来源。优步试图通过对数百万人在城市中物理移动方式的物质性控制来产生金融利润，在这一点上并无特别之处。第二，金融与实体之间的对立，恰恰是我们必须理解其生产过程的误导性区分。一项重要的金融化研究将其定义为“经济中的盈利越来越多地通过金融渠道而非生产活动实现的趋势”，并补充说“生产性”一词指涉及“商品生产或交易”的活动。例如，福特和其他汽车制造商如今从其提供购车贷款的金融部门获得的利润，超过制造汽车所得，这表明我们可以把贷款上实现的利润与出售汽车获得的利润区分开来。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-042"></a>[42](#note-int-042)然而，尽管金融与生产之间的区分是真实的区分，却并非新近才有。正如本书将表明的，资本家一直通过为未来生活形式融资和生产这些形式来获取利润，而他们的产品依赖于这些未来生活形式。在一种未来生活形式与需要它的“产品”之间制造区分，并由此在“产品”与“金融”、实物与单纯的货币之间制造区分，对于殖民非欧洲世界、碳动力工业化或现代股份公司的兴起来说，与对更晚近的发展同样重要。事实上，正如[第三章](#ch03-0001)所提出的，我们所谓的工业革命可以被视为一段绕道。它作为信用创造机制的一次中断而发生，尽管这次中断和绕道把所谓的金融化推上了新的轨道。信用装置总是由真实的生活形式建造而成——包括我们很快将看到的、河流系统重组之类工程，或其他帝国的大地改造与生态破坏工程。

These contemporary forms of finance and debt are sometimes described as ‘financialisation’, a term that contrasts such costs with the needs and productivity of the ‘real’ economy – the production of actual goods and services. The idea of financialisation is not a term we will use here, for two reasons. First, credit money and debt are never conjured <a id="page-18-en"></a>〔原书第18页〕‘out of thin air’; they require building a real apparatus for the capture of future payments, the control of which is the source of all credit money. Uber’s attempt to generate financial profits through a material control over the way millions of people move physically around cities is nothing unusual in this respect. Second, this opposition between the financial and the real is precisely the misleading distinction whose production we have to understand. An important study of financialisation defines it as ‘the tendency for profit-making in the economy to occur increasingly through financial channels rather than through productive activities’, adding that the term productive refers to activities that involve ‘the production or trade of commodities’. As an example, the fact that Ford and other car makers were now making more profit from their financial arms, providing loans for the purchase of vehicles, than from manufacturing them, suggests that we can distinguish profits realised on the loan from profits made on the sale of the vehicle.<a id="ref-en-note-int-042"></a>[42](#note-int-042) However, although the distinction between finance and production is a real distinction, it is nothing new. As this book will show, capitalists have always derived their profits from financing and producing the future forms of life on which their products depend. Creating the distinction between a future form of life and the ‘product’ that requires it, and hence between ‘product’ and ‘finance’, between real things and mere money, was as important to, say, the colonising of the non-European world, carbon-powered industrialisation, or the rise of the modern joint-stock company as it has been to more recent developments. In fact, as [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) proposes, what we call the industrial revolution can be seen as a detour. It happened as a disruption to the mechanisms of credit creation, albeit a disruption and detour that tipped so-called financialisation onto a new trajectory. Credit apparatuses are always constructed out of real forms of life – including, as we will shortly see, such projects as the reorganisation of a river system or other imperial projects of terraforming and ecological destruction.

<a id="introduction-0054"></a>

增长在我们看来是人类轨迹在时间中的展开，由现代化力量驱动。我们用资本主义或全球化之类的术语，来命名推动我们前进的力量。这些术语能让增长观念显得自然且不可避免，也让人难以超越这种增长观念去思考。我们以天真的历史时间感行事，把未来视为过去和现在的向前展开，于是无法把未来理解为一个政治与物质框架——这个框架不是由自然的时间增量构成，而是由<a id="page-19"></a>〔原书第19页〕攫取技术和计算技术构成，我们正是依靠它、以未来为代价而生活。要摆脱增长问题，似乎需要逆转历史运动本身。

Growth appears to us as the unfolding of a human trajectory through time, driven by the forces of modernisation. We use terms like capitalism or globalisation to name the power of what propels us forwards. These terms can make the idea of growth seem like something natural and inevitable. They also make it difficult to see beyond. Operating with a naive sense of historical time, in which the future is no more than the unfolding forwards of the past and the present, we fail to understand the future as a political and material framework – a framework constructed not from natural increments of time but from the <a id="page-19-en"></a>〔原书第19页〕techniques of capture and technologies of calculation through which we live at its expense. Escaping the problem of growth seems to require reversing the very movement of history.

<a id="introduction-0055"></a>

许多关于气候问题的论述——其起源我们将在[第一章](#ch01-0001)考察，并将在本书接近结尾时再谈——把我们的困境归咎于增长现象。它们正确地指出，大多数旨在减少化石燃料燃烧及其他破坏生物圈行为的努力，都远远不够。但我们常常把这些失败归因于一种与未来的总体关系，并通过资本的托词，错误地把这种关系认定为我们历史的根本逻辑。

Many accounts of the climate question, whose origins we will consider in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001) and to which we will return towards the end of the book, blame our predicament on the phenomenon of growth. They point out, correctly, the inadequacy of most efforts to reduce the burning of fossil fuels and other actions destructive of the biosphere. But we often attribute these failures to a general relationship to the future that we identify, misleadingly, through the alibi of capital, as the very logic of our history.

<a id="introduction-0056"></a>

不可否认，某些过程以加速的速率展开，例如煤炭和石油的开采。但我们也知道，其他东西在减少，例如雨林面积或多数人的闲暇时间。也许现在该以更有限的方式使用“增长”这样的词，只捕捉某些变化而非全部变化，从而不再把它当作描述我们与未来关系的总称。

There is no denying that some processes have unfolded at accelerating rates, such as the extraction of coal and oil. But we also know that other things decrease, such as the extent of rainforests or the amount of most people’s leisure time. Perhaps it is time to use a word like growth in more limited ways, to capture some changes and not others, and therefore not as a general term for our relationship to the future.

<a id="introduction-0057"></a>

如此一来我们就会发现，增长观念在当代政治中最广泛的用法源自金融和经济学，它指的不是社会的集体运动，而是企业会计的晦涩惯例。这些惯例描述的是一种以未来为代价的生活方式。通过托词的转移注意力和错误指向，它们让我们看不见未来被削弱的方式。

In doing so, we would discover that the most widespread use of the idea of growth in contemporary politics, derived from finance and economics, denotes not the collective movement of society but the obscure conventions of business accounting. Those conventions describe a mode of living at the expense of the future. Through the distraction and misdirection of an alibi, they blind us to the way that future is diminished.

<a id="introduction-0058"></a>

资本不是货币或财富，尽管通俗说法常把它描绘成这些；也不是经济学家通常描述的可用于生产财富的资产或机器。资本是使未来背负负担的权力。“资本的托词”指那些转移注意力、引开视线或掩盖这种负担的施加的观念和装置。其中包括本导论探讨的增长和技术改进观念，也包括货币、利息、经济以及本书将考察的其他若干观念。托词是一种（错误的）指向。字面上，它是“别处”，是“在另一个地方”，可以同时具有时间与空间两个方面。正如我们将看到的，这些方面包括对我们如何相对于当下来生产未来的误解，也包括“西方”在地理上的引开视线。无论我们如何把资本的历史全球化，或如何试图把欧洲在这一历史中的位置地方化，这段历史总会重新以欧美世界为中心。<a id="ref-zh-note-int-043"></a>[43](#note-int-043)在本书各处，我们将在不同场合考察<a id="page-20"></a>〔原书第20页〕这个“别处”，包括在关键时刻考察印度—伊斯兰世界的历史。事实上，本书半数以上章节将借助埃及的经验；在那里，资本化过程及其托词的历史可以被鲜明地辨识出来。最后，“资本的托词”也正是这个意思：资本本身就是托词。我们往往不是去把握一个不确定的支配过程——对未来的资本化——而是代之以一个结构：“资本主义”。我们不把资本视为支配未来的各种方式，而把它视为一件东西、一项资产、一种价值。资本使我们无法理解它得以产生的多重方式，从而成了自己的托词。

Capital is not money or wealth, despite the way that popular accounts often portray it, nor is it the assets or machinery that can be deployed to produce wealth, as economists usually describe it. Capital is the power to encumber the future. The term ‘alibi of capital’ refers to ideas and devices that distract, divert attention from, or disguise the encumbering. These include the concepts of growth and technical improvement, explored in this introduction, but also money, interest, economy, and several more that this book will examine. An alibi is a (mis)direction. Literally an ‘elsewhere’, an ‘in another place’, it can have both a temporal and a spatial aspect. These include, as we will see, a misunderstanding of how we produce the future in relation to the present, but also the geographical distraction of ‘the West’. However much we globalise the history of capital or try to provincialise the place of Europe in that history, this history recentres itself in the Euro-American world.<a id="ref-en-note-int-043"></a>[43](#note-int-043) Throughout this book, at different instances, we will consider <a id="page-20-en"></a>〔原书第20页〕this ‘elsewhere’, including at key moments histories of the Indo-Islamic world. In fact, more than half the chapters will draw on the experience of Egypt, a place where histories of the capitalising process and its alibis can be vividly discerned. The ‘alibi of capital’, finally, is also just that: capital itself as an alibi. Instead of grasping an uncertain process of domination, the capitalising of the future, too often we substitute a structure, ‘capitalism’. We treat capital not as the modes of commanding the future, but as a thing, an asset, a value. In distracting us from understanding the multiple ways it comes into being, capital has become its own alibi.


# 第一章　破土

<a id="ch01-0001"></a>

<a id="page-21"></a>〔原书第21页〕

<a id="page-21-en"></a>〔原书第21页〕

<a id="ch01-0002"></a>

## 第一章　破土

## 1 Groundbreaking

<a id="ch01-0003"></a>

在不久前的某个时刻，北大西洋世界的人们失去了时间感。他们开始把未来想象为一种无限资源，并以牺牲后来者为代价组织集体生活。奇怪的是，他们似乎始终意识到自己与未来的关系有缺陷。上个世纪的每一个十年都带来新的警告：资源枯竭、经济增长不可持续、地球遭受不可修复的损害。但他们主要把问题说成是计算失误。他们说，经济制度未能把自然考虑在内。在计算成本与收益时，它大体上排除了对自身之外的客体——自然世界——所造成的损害。如果他们确实在以未来为代价生活，那么这种占有似乎只是对地球的一种无意抽取。

Somewhere in the recent past, the people of the North Atlantic world lost their sense of time. They began to imagine the future as an infinite resource, and to organise collective life at the expense of those who would come later. Strangely, they always seemed aware that their relationship to the future was flawed. Every decade of the last century brought new warnings about the exhaustion of resources, unsustainable rates of economic growth, and irreparable damage to the Earth. But they framed the problem mainly as one of miscalculation. The economic system, they said, failed to take account of nature. In calculating costs and benefits, it largely excluded the damage done to an object outside themselves, the natural world. If they were living at the expense of the future, the appropriation seemed to happen as an inadvertent extraction from the Earth.

<a id="ch01-0004"></a>

还有另一种方式，可以理解未来的生命和生活方式如何被弄得贫乏。未来的丧失并非计算失败的结果。我们生活在一套安排之中，这套安排被组织起来计算未来、确立其价值，并让某些人抽取和享有这种价值——不是在未来的某个时候，而是在当下。我们的生活方式并非忽视未来，而是朝向未来。但我们是以一种特定方式、通过特定的接触条件朝向它。同样，我们并不忽视物理和生物世界，而是通过具体的实践和理解与之发生关系。我们用自然、技术、经济、增长等术语来表达这种关系。这些词主要在二十世纪获得了当前的用法和含义，却使我们看不清自己如何以他人为代价生活。

There is a different way of understanding how future lives and ways of living are impoverished. The loss of the future is not the result of a failure to calculate. We live within a set of arrangements organised to calculate the future, establish its value, and allow some to extract and enjoy that value – not in a time to come, but in the present. Rather than neglecting the future, our mode of life is oriented towards it. But we are oriented in a particular manner, through specific terms of engagement. In the same way, we do not ignore the physical and biological world. But we relate to it through concrete practices and understandings. We express our relationship using terms like nature, technology, economy, and growth. Those words, which acquired their current use and meaning largely in the twentieth century, blind us to the way we live at the expense of others.

<a id="ch01-0005"></a>

<a id="page-22"></a>〔原书第22页〕我们如何变得无法理解自己正以何种方式使地球变得不适合人类繁荣？我们如何发展出一些安排，使我们误认自己与未来的关系？要寻找答案，可以从回望二十世纪初开始。尽管关于自然世界、技术过程和经济力量的思考方式有更长的历史，但在上个世纪之交，新的政治和技术生活形式赋予这些观念不同的形态。这些生活形式产生于欧洲帝国扩张的顶点。正是在帝国的事件中，人们最清楚地看到它们出现。

<a id="page-22-en"></a>〔原书第22页〕How did we become uncomprehending of the ways in which we are rendering the Earth inhospitable to human flourishing? How did we develop arrangements that cause us to misrecognise our relationship to the future? To find answers, we can start by looking back to the beginning of the twentieth century. While ways of thinking about the natural world, technical processes, and economic forces have much longer histories, at the turn of the last century new forms of political and technical life gave such ideas a different shape. Those forms of life were produced at the high-water mark of European imperial expansion. It is in the events of empire that one can most clearly see them appear.

<a id="ch01-0006"></a>

### 文明必须有其牺牲品

### Civilisation Must Have Its Victims

<a id="ch01-0007"></a>

1902 年，英国在埃及的水利工程师完成了毁灭尼罗河的第一阶段工程。埃及当时才被英国入侵和占领二十年。工程师们监督在开罗以南 500 英里的阿斯旺修建一座大坝，意在拦蓄河流夏季的大部分洪水。他们声称，目标是取代一种古老的灌溉方式：在围堤田块中蓄留洪水，每年只能种一季作物；代之以全年蓄水，实现常年灌溉，一年最多种植三季作物。把水蓄在大坝之后，可以消除异常洪水的威胁——洪水小时会导致作物歉收，极大时又会摧毁田地。调节河流不均衡的水流，也会减少因耕作面积不可预测而造成的财务不确定性。再加上把边缘土地纳入生产的新运河，扩大的耕作将能够养活不断增长的人口，同时让国家满足甘蔗和棉花等经济作物的需求。即使在今天，关于尼罗河的史书和埃及现代发展的叙述，仍在重复水利工程师带来的必要改良这一套说法。

In 1902, British hydraulic engineers in Egypt, a country Britain had invaded and occupied only two decades earlier, completed the first stage of the destruction of the River Nile. They supervised the building of a dam at Aswan, 500 miles south of Cairo, intended to hold back most of the river’s summer floodwaters. The aim, the engineers said, was to replace an ancient mode of irrigation based on capturing the flood in field basins, which allowed only a single crop each year, with year-round water storage that would allow perennial irrigation and the growing of up to three crops a year. Storing the water behind the dam would remove the threat of exceptional floods, which caused crops to fail when floods were low and devastated the fields when extremely high. Regulating the uneven flow of the river would also reduce the financial uncertainty caused by the unpredictable extent of cultivation. Combined with new canals bringing marginal lands into productive use, the expanded cultivation would enable the feeding of a growing population, while allowing the country to meet the demand for industrial crops like sugar cane and cotton. Even today, histories of the Nile and accounts of the country’s modern development repeat this narrative of necessary improvement introduced by the hydraulic engineers.

<a id="ch01-0008"></a>

就像许多关于殖民现代性带来益处的叙述一样，这个故事几乎每一个要素都带有误导性或纯属错误。全年灌溉并没有用多季种植取代一年一季的作物，而几乎做了相反的事：用单一作物的大面积种植取代三季农业。灾难性干旱和洪水的风险，并不是新工程解决了的古老问题，而主要是灌溉工程<a id="page-23"></a>〔原书第23页〕加剧的现代威胁。财务不确定性不是有待消除的不均衡，而是一种有待工程化制造的效果，以创造在当下从未来抽取支付的可能性。新工程没有把不毛之地纳入耕作，反而改变了边缘土地的使用方式，并使全国每一块田越来越不丰产，因为洪水、土壤形成、作物轮作、大型土壤动物和微生物生命之间的共生关系被扰乱和摧毁。大多数作物产量不升反降，因为洪水带来的淤泥不再肥田；只有一种植物例外，那就是水葫芦。这种原产亚马逊、能形成密集浮垫的水生杂草，由殖民时期的欧洲人作为观赏植物引入，它利用大坝造成的异常静水，逐渐用密集的草垫堵塞开罗以北的每条小运河和水道。洪水被消除后，人类本身变成了宿主，哺育不断扩张的寄生虫群体，包括携带钩虫病、疟疾和血吸虫病的寄生虫，而不是为不断增长的人口提供食物——随着粮食作物让位给棉花，人们的饮食已经恶化。但最具误导性的说法是那个主要说法：筑坝拦河通过全年蓄水消除了生态风险。英国人在阿斯旺建造的大坝和水库并未开创尼罗河水的储存。它们以不同方式储水，削弱并最终摧毁了一种规模更大、更为多样、却更不显眼的储水方式，以及管理气候、降雨和洪水不确定性的方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-001"></a>[1](#note-ch1-001)

Like so many accounts of the benefits brought by colonial modernity, almost every element of that story is misleading or wrong. Year-round irrigation did not replace the growing of a single annual crop with multiple cropping, but accomplished almost the reverse, replacing three-season agriculture with the widespread cultivation of a single crop. The risk of catastrophic droughts and floods was not an ancient problem solved by new engineering but mainly a modern threat <a id="page-23-en"></a>〔原书第23页〕exacerbated by irrigation works. Financial uncertainty was not an unevenness to be removed but an effect to be engineered, to create the possibility of extracting in the present payments from the future. Rather than bringing unproductive lands into cultivation, the new works altered the way marginal lands were used and rendered every field in the country less and less productive, as the symbiosis of flood, soil formation, crop rotation, macrofauna, and microbial life was disrupted and destroyed.
