As the American economist Irving <a id="page-44-en"></a>〔原书第44页〕Fisher explained in *The Rate of Interest* (1908), the work that established the new understanding of capital, the power of money to earn interest had nothing to do with the transformations in the technosphere and the expansion of imperial power that had made possible the capture of revenue from the future on an unprecedented scale. It was simply a consequence of human impatience.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-070"></a>[70](#note-ch1-070)

校注：本章正文记《利息率》为1908年，原注70记为1907年。1908年《Economic Journal》的同期书评明确列出版年份为1907。本章随后“1911年，问世三年后”的说法沿用正文年代；译文均保留底本。 https://academic.oup.com/ej/article-abstract/18/69/66/5291306

<a id="ch01-0066"></a>

起初，这种从货币的作用力转向人类偏好的变化有其批评者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-071"></a>[71](#note-ch1-071)资本和利息理论怎能完全不关注生产过程？资本赚取收入的能力，必定与其投入的技术过程有关。对这一反对意见的答案很快找到了，办法是引入另一个人物，以及一个更可靠的托词来源：企业家的形象。

At first, this shift from the agency of money to the preferences of humans had its critics.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-071"></a>[71](#note-ch1-071) How could the theory of capital and interest pay no attention to the productive process? Surely the earning power of capital must have something to do with the technical processes into which it was put. An answer to this objection was soon found, by introducing another human agent, and a more reliable source of alibi: the figure of the entrepreneur.

<a id="ch01-0067"></a>

### 企业家

### The Entrepreneur

<a id="ch01-0068"></a>

在较早的古典经济学家中，也发生过类似的转向。事实上，正是让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊引入了“企业家”一词，来解释财富的生产——以及利息的赚取——如何依赖这一关键人物。萨伊《概论》1803 年的第一版对此谈得很少。但在接下来的十年里，萨伊因拿破仑·波拿巴夺取政权而被迫退出公共生活，便尝试亲自组织一个生产过程。他利用一位富有的姑姨辈亲属和其他投资者的资金，并在弟弟路易的协助下，把法国东北部奥希村上游的一条小河改造成运河，建立了一座水磨坊，把棉纤维纺成纱线。这家企业面临一个反复出现的技术难题：木制机器中把动力从*moteur hydraulique*（水力驱动装置）传送到缠绕纱线的锭子上的部件，不断断裂。用熟铁部件替换木制部件未能消除断裂，再用更坚固但更脆的铸铁部件替换也失败了。与许多想成为工业家的人一样，萨伊发现引入机械化的尝试过于困难。生产中受损材料的浪费——占原棉的 25%——加剧了困难。由于无法从水力机器中获利，萨伊于 1812 年解散了这家企业，成为食利者，投资于若干其他事业。他尤其帮助弟弟接管了一家炼糖企业。炼糖厂比纺织厂更不容易发生故障，因为煮沸和提纯原糖<a id="page-45"></a>〔原书第45页〕比把棉纤维纺成细纱的过程更简单。路易·萨伊炼糖公司后来成为法国最成功的制糖企业，也是该国最大的工业企业之一——尽管正如该公司的经理以自己手指的代价所发现的那样，即使在炼糖过程中，工业事故也可能造成后果。

Among the earlier, classical economists, a similar move had been made. In fact, it was Jean-Baptiste Say who introduced the term *entrepreneur* to explain how the production of wealth – and the earning of interest – depends on this pivotal figure. The first edition of Say’s *Treatise*, in 1803, said little on the subject. But, over the following decade, forced out of public life by Napoleon Bonaparte’s seizure of power, Say tried his own hand at organising a productive process. With funds from a wealthy aunt and other investors, and the assistance of his younger brother Louis, he canalised a small river above the village of Auchy in northeast France and set up a water mill for spinning cotton fibre into yarn. The venture faced a recurrent technical difficulty: the parts of the wooden machine that transferred motion from the *moteur hydraulique* to the spindles on which the yarn was wound repeatedly broke. Replacing the wooden parts with wrought iron failed to end the breakages, and replacing those with parts of cast iron, which is stronger but more brittle, also failed. Like many would-be industrialists, Say found the attempt to introduce mechanisation too much of a challenge. The wastage of material damaged in production, which amounted to 25 per cent of the raw cotton, added to the difficulties. Unable to make a profit from his hydraulic machine, Say dissolved the business in 1812 and became a rentier, investing in a number of other ventures. In particular, he helped his brother take over a sugar-refining business. A refinery was less prone to breakdowns than a textile mill, as boiling and purifying raw sugar <a id="page-45-en"></a>〔原书第45页〕was a simpler process than spinning cotton fibres into fine yarns. The Louis Say Refining Company went on to become the most successful sugar business in France and one of the country’s largest industrial enterprises – although, as the firm’s manager was to discover with the fingers of his own hand, even in the refining of sugar industrial accidents could have their consequences.

<a id="ch01-0069"></a>

与此同时，让-巴蒂斯特重新转向政治经济学；1814 年，随着拿破仑战败，他得以出版《概论》的修订版。新版与亚当·斯密和大卫·李嘉图的观点决裂——他们认为商品价值主要由生产它所需的劳动量决定——强调一个新人物企业家的同等重要贡献。这个人协调劳动和机器的使用，改进工作组织，供应或引入资本，而且最重要的是，利用他对供需原理的理解来调节生产的速度和方向——例如，决定生产棉花还是糖更有利可图。换言之，资本的“生产性作用力”之所以有效，是因为企业家身上结合了技术诀窍和经济科学。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-072"></a>[72](#note-ch1-072)

Meanwhile, Jean-Baptiste turned back to political economy, and in 1814, with the defeat of Napoleon, he was able to publish a revised edition of the *Treatise*. The new version broke with the view of Adam Smith and David Ricardo that the value of a good is determined principally by the amount of labour required for its production, emphasising the equally important contribution of a new figure, the entrepreneur. This person coordinates the use of labour and machines, improves the organisation of work, supplies or draws in capital, and, above all, uses his understanding of the principles of supply and demand to regulate the pace and direction of production – including, for example, deciding whether it is more profitable to produce cotton or sugar. In other words, the ‘productive agency’ of capital is effective thanks to the combining of technical know-how and economic science in the person of the entrepreneur.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-072"></a>[72](#note-ch1-072)

<a id="ch01-0070"></a>

一个世纪后，在二十世纪的最初几年，企业家的形象再次出现。这个人物将再一次提供托词，为资本和利息理论提供一种解释货币生钱能力的方式。随着经济学把关注点收窄为一门价格机制的科学，它发现了一种方式，可以通过企业家这个人物构成的薄弱联系，把赋予货币繁殖力的其他一切机器和生产过程重新纳入对货币本质的解释。然而，这个人物的角色被重新定义了。他不再是一位至关重要的协调者，而是被想象为偶尔的扰乱者——事实上，是一位破土者。

A century later, in the opening years of the twentieth century, the figure of the entrepreneur reappeared. Once again, this character would provide an alibi, offering the theory of capital and interest a way to explain the ability of money to make money. As economics narrowed its focus to become a science of the price mechanism, it would find a means to readmit into the explanation of the nature of money every other piece of machinery and process of production that gave money its reproductive power, via the tenuous human link of the entrepreneur. The role of this figure, however, was redefined. Rather than a vital coordinator, the entrepreneur was now imagined as an occasional disruptor – in fact, as a groundbreaker.

<a id="ch01-0071"></a>

1911 年，在欧文·费雪的《利息率》问世三年后，一位年轻奥地利学者出版了他最重要的著作；此人后来迁往哈佛大学，并逐渐与费雪争夺二十世纪上半叶最有影响美国经济学家的头衔。约瑟夫·熊彼特的《经济发展理论》提出了一种关于资本和利息的论述，其中货币赚取货币的能力在决定性程度上依赖于企业家的角色。然而，对熊彼特而言，企业家不是协调者，而是失序的推动者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-073"></a>[73](#note-ch1-073)企业家启动了创新、动荡和技术重组的过程，<a id="page-46"></a>〔原书第46页〕他后来称之为“创造性破坏”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-074"></a>[74](#note-ch1-074)一个多世纪后的今天，熊彼特式论述——把资本主义视为由一种独特的破坏性创新力量所驱动的过程——或许仍是对于界定资本主义现代性的那种时间经验最具说服力的解释，无论对资本权力的批评者还是捍卫者都是如此。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-075"></a>[75](#note-ch1-075)

In 1911, three years after the appearance of Irving Fisher’s *Rate of Interest*, a young Austrian scholar, who would later move to Harvard University and come to rival Fisher for the title of the most influential American economist of the first half of the twentieth century, published his most important work. Joseph Schumpeter’s *Theory of Economic Development* proposed an account of capital and interest in which the very ability of money to earn money turned decisively on the role of the entrepreneur. For Schumpeter, however, the entrepreneur was not a coordinator but an agent of disorder.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-073"></a>[73](#note-ch1-073) The entrepreneur set in motion the processes of innovation, upheaval, and technical reorganisation that <a id="page-46-en"></a>〔原书第46页〕he later termed ‘creative destruction’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-074"></a>[74](#note-ch1-074) Today, more than a century later, the Schumpeterian account of capitalism as a process driven by a unique force of disruptive innovation remains, among critics of the power of capital as much as its defenders, perhaps the most persuasive explanation for the very experience of temporality that defines capitalist modernity.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-075"></a>[75](#note-ch1-075)

<a id="ch01-0072"></a>

尽管熊彼特在若干处提到让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊的著作，但把企业家角色置于货币新论述中心这一做法的动力，并非来自萨伊的《概论》，也不是来自他在维也纳求学时读到的其他文本。它来自他完成学业后的第一份工作。那份工作是在开罗。

While Schumpeter referred in places to the writing of Jean-Baptiste Say, the impetus for placing the role of the entrepreneur at the centre of the new account of money did not come from Say’s *Treatise*, nor from other texts he encountered as a student in Vienna. It arose from his first job after completing his education. That employment was in Cairo.

<a id="ch01-0073"></a>

熊彼特的思想是在埃及形成的，但不是通过萨伊的著作，而是通过他在那里接触到的、由让-巴蒂斯特的弟弟创建的实力雄厚的制糖企业——路易·萨伊炼糖公司。正是该公司在埃及靠糖发财的计划破产，塑造了二十世纪关于货币如何生钱的最有影响的论述。

Schumpeter’s ideas were formed in Egypt not by Say’s writings but in his encounter there with the powerful sugar business created by Jean-Baptiste’s brother, the Louis Say Refining Company. It was the collapse of the Company’s scheme to make a fortune from sugar in Egypt that shaped the most influential twentieth-century account of how money is made from money.

<a id="ch01-0074"></a>

没有什么比欧洲人称之为埃及的地方，更能体现二十世纪之交“资本主义”的含义——货币生钱的权力。开罗及其乡村在 1860 年代经历了第一轮金融繁荣。政府修建铁路线，扩大棉花种植园，建立甘蔗种植园，利用美国南方奴隶种植的棉花和糖供应中断的机会，欧洲金融家推动了信用扩张，创造了“尼罗河上的克朗代克”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-076"></a>[76](#note-ch1-076)然而，在美国蓄奴州战败、美国棉花出口恢复之后，棉花价格暴跌。1873 年的国际金融危机造成了进一步压力，导致埃及政府拖欠债务，落入欧洲金融控制之下。随后的一场人民起义被 1882 年英国军事占领镇压。占领为棉花和糖生产的新投资奠定了基础，到世纪之交，又创造了第二轮信用繁荣。土地本身成为投机资产，令当地观察者惊讶的是，其价值随棉花和糖价格的涨落而波动。

Nowhere better exemplified the sense of capitalism at the turn of the twentieth century – the power of money to make money – than the place that Europeans called Egypt. Cairo and its countryside had seen a first financial boom in the 1860s. As the government constructed railway lines, expanded cotton plantations, and established sugar cane estates, taking advantage of the interruption to the supply of slave-grown cotton and sugar from the American South, European financiers drove an expansion of credit that created a ‘Klondike on the Nile’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-076"></a>[76](#note-ch1-076) However, after the defeat of the American slave states and the resumption of US cotton exports, the price paid for cotton collapsed. The international financial crisis of 1873 created further pressure and led the Egyptian government to default on its debt payments and fall under European financial control. A popular uprising that followed was ended by the British military occupation of 1882. The occupation laid the groundwork for renewed investment in cotton and sugar production, which by the turn of the century created a second credit boom. Land itself became a speculative asset, its value fluctuating, to the astonishment of local observers, with the rise and fall of the price of cotton and sugar.

<a id="ch01-0075"></a>

到 1905 年，这个围绕棉花、糖、股票和土地投机组织起来的不断扩张的信用世界，已成为开罗政界持续辩论的话题。那年，一位主要作家雅各布·萨鲁夫在他主编的月刊<a id="page-47"></a>〔原书第47页〕《穆克塔塔夫》的文学副刊上连载了一部小说。伊丽莎白·霍尔特认为，故事从一期到下一期的悬念，复制了这样一个世界的不确定性：在那里，富人仅仅是“从他人损失中获利的人”，“没人确知自己的明天”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-077"></a>[77](#note-ch1-077)新攫取模式的物质性——其建筑、交易机制和信息系统——在印刷文化和想象生活的新形式中被复制和折射。“在欧洲各国首都，都有一座巨大的建筑，上面写着‘证券交易所’，”埃及统治精英中的一位成员 1905 年对一位法裔美国访客说，并抱怨投机者的“瘟疫”正在消耗这个国家的生命。“在这里，整个国家就是一座巨大的证券交易所。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-078"></a>[78](#note-ch1-078)同年，这场繁荣的崩溃触发了 1907 年大崩盘。

By 1905, this expanding world of credit organised around speculation in cotton, sugar, stocks, and land became a topic of continuous debate in political circles in Cairo. A leading writer, Ya‘qub Sarruf, serialised a novel that year in a literary supplement to the monthly journal <a id="page-47-en"></a>〔原书第47页〕he edited, *al-Muqtataf*. The suspense from the appearance of one instalment of the story to the next replicated, Elizabeth Holt suggests, the uncertainty of a world in which the wealthy were simply ‘those who win from the loss of another’ and where ‘no one is sure of his tomorrow’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-077"></a>[77](#note-ch1-077) The materiality of the new modes of capture – its buildings, exchange mechanisms, and information systems – were duplicated and refracted in new forms of print culture and imaginative life. ‘In all the capitals of Europe there is a huge building on which is written “Stock Exchange”,’ a member of Egypt’s ruling elite remarked to a French American visitor in 1905, complaining about the ‘plague’ of speculators sapping the country’s life. ‘Here the whole country is one vast Stock Exchange.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-078"></a>[78](#note-ch1-078) The collapse of the boom that same year was to trigger the Great Crash of 1907.

<a id="ch01-0076"></a>

约瑟夫·熊彼特在那场崩盘之后来到开罗，而促成此行的一连串事件，起于1905年巴黎的一起自杀。

The events that took Joseph Schumpeter to Cairo, in the wake of that crash, were set in motion by a suicide in Paris in 1905.

<a id="ch01-0077"></a>

### 熊彼特的糖厂

### Schumpeter’s Sugar Mill

<a id="ch01-0078"></a>

1905 年 8 月欧内斯特·克罗尼耶之死，似乎集中体现了那些日子的金融脆弱性。一名仆人发现他的尸体躺在卧室地板上。在相邻浴室进行的尸检表明，克罗尼耶曾试图用氰化钾自杀。由于无法把毒药留在胃里，他随后朝自己的心脏开枪。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-079"></a>[79](#note-ch1-079)奇怪的是，他扣动扳机的那只手有两根假指，这是十二年前在他的炼糖厂检查机器维修时发生事故的结果。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-080"></a>[80](#note-ch1-080)那些维修，以及那些失去的手指，提供了一条我们稍后将回到的线索。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-081"></a>[81](#note-ch1-081)克罗尼耶被称为糖王，*le roi du sucre*，他把所控制的王国——路易·萨伊炼糖公司——建成足以垄断法国食糖市场的大型企业。他最初受聘担任工程师和经理，在路易的孙子亨利·萨伊于 1899 年去世后，接管了这家由让-巴蒂斯特及其弟弟创办的公司。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-082"></a>[82](#note-ch1-082)但克罗尼耶在糖期货上进行的一笔大规模投机投资失败了。接着，一封从开罗寄到巴黎的信暗示，他在那里对所控制的制糖业的欺诈性经营——曾为投机提供资金——已被发现。几天之内，他结束了自己的生命。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-083"></a>[83](#note-ch1-083)1905 年 8 月 27 日他去世的消息传出后，公司股价暴跌。巴黎股市下挫，造成巨额损失，随后的几天，伦敦、纽约和汉堡交易所的交易商也感受到了这场<a id="page-48"></a>〔原书第48页〕冲击。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-084"></a>[84](#note-ch1-084)

The death of Ernest Cronier in August 1905 seemed to epitomise the financial fragility of those days. A servant found his body on the bedroom floor. The autopsy, carried out in the adjoining bathroom, revealed that Cronier had tried to poison himself with potassium cyanide. Unable to keep the poison down, he then shot himself in the heart.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-079"></a>[79](#note-ch1-079) Curiously, the hand with which he pulled the trigger had two prosthetic fingers, the consequence of an accident twelve years earlier inspecting repairs to machinery at his sugar refinery.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-080"></a>[80](#note-ch1-080) Those repairs, and the missing fingers, provide a clue to which we will return.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-081"></a>[81](#note-ch1-081) Known as the sugar king, *le roi du sucre*, Cronier had built the kingdom he controlled, the Louis Say Refining Company, into a business large enough to corner the French sugar market. Hired first as an engineer and manager, he had taken control of the firm – founded by Jean-Baptiste and his brother Louis – following the death of Louis’s grandson, Henri Say, in 1899.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-082"></a>[82](#note-ch1-082) But a large speculative investment Cronier had made in sugar futures had failed. Then a letter reached him in Paris from Cairo suggesting that his fraudulent management of the sugar industry he controlled there, which had funded the speculation, had been uncovered. Within days, he took his life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-083"></a>[83](#note-ch1-083) On the news of his death, on 27 August 1905, the value of the Company’s shares collapsed. The Paris stock market fell, causing huge losses, and traders felt the <a id="page-48-en"></a>〔原书第48页〕shock over the following days in the exchanges of London, New York, and Hamburg.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-084"></a>[84](#note-ch1-084)

<a id="ch01-0079"></a>

在亚历山大和开罗——当时那里的货币市场属于世界上最活跃之列——冲击更大。路易·萨伊炼糖公司不久前才与当地投资者以及我们先前遇到的英国金融家欧内斯特·卡塞尔爵士合伙，控制了埃及制糖业，创建了这个国家最大的工业企业。该公司前景一度未卜。世纪之交阿斯旺大坝的完工，导致农民出人意料地减少而非扩大甘蔗种植。这家公司没有从加工甘蔗中获利，反而成了一家生产债务的企业。它的董事们靠发行没有真实销售基础的虚构汇票而兴旺，创造出为克罗尼耶在巴黎进行糖期货投机提供资金的信用货币。经理的自杀迫使这家埃及公司暂停交易其暴跌的股票并进行重组，关闭一半炼糖厂，出售甘蔗种植园和农业铁路。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-085"></a>[85](#note-ch1-085)

In Alexandria and Cairo, where the money markets were among the most active in the world at that time, the shock was even greater. The Louis Say Refining Company had only recently taken control of the Egyptian sugar industry, in partnership with local investors and Sir Ernest Cassel, the British financier we met earlier, creating the country’s largest industrial enterprise. The firm had faced an uncertain future. The completion of the Aswan Dam at the turn of the century had led farmers unexpectedly to decrease rather than expand the growing of sugar cane. Instead of profiting from processing the cane, the firm had become a business for producing debt. Its directors had prospered by issuing fictitious bills of exchange, with no underlying sale, creating the credit money that funded Cronier’s speculations in sugar futures in Paris. The manager’s suicide forced the Egyptian company to suspend dealing in its collapsing shares and reorganise, closing half its refineries and selling off its sugar estates and agricultural railways.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-085"></a>[85](#note-ch1-085)

<a id="ch01-0080"></a>

反常的是，这场抛售助长了埃及殖民未来的新一轮投机，制造了一场繁荣；十八个月后，即 1907 年 4 月，这场繁荣的崩溃震动了全世界。在这十八个月里，买家抬高农业土地开发公司的价格，房地产公司在开罗和亚历山大推动了一股建设狂热，组织债务创造的银行和抵押贷款公司也是如此。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-086"></a>[86](#note-ch1-086)“人们显然疯了，”后来提交给埃及国民银行股东的一份报告说，这家金融机构正是卡塞尔帮助创建的。“他们似乎认为，每一家新成立的公司，甚至在开始营业之前，价值就已经翻倍。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-087"></a>[87](#note-ch1-087)

Perversely, the sell-off fuelled a new round of speculation in Egypt’s colonial future, creating a boom whose collapse eighteen months later, in April 1907, was to reverberate around the world. Over those eighteen months, buyers bid up the price of agrarian land development companies, and property firms promoted a frenzy of construction in Cairo and Alexandria, as did the banks and mortgage companies organising the creation of debt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-086"></a>[86](#note-ch1-086) ‘People were apparently mad,’ according to a later report to the shareholders of the National Bank of Egypt, the financial firm that Cassel had helped create. ‘They seemed to think that every company that came out was worth double its value even before it had started business.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-087"></a>[87](#note-ch1-087)

<a id="ch01-0081"></a>

然而突然间，英国对埃及殖民占领的长期未来——一个与阿斯旺大坝一起造就了那些股票和抵押贷款价值的政治未来——似乎不那么确定了。1906 年夏天，反对英国占领的抗议加剧；此前在开罗以北四十五英里的三角洲村庄丁沙瓦伊，村民反抗英国士兵为取乐射杀他们的家鸽（家鸽养在鸽舍里，用于收集鸽粪作肥料；在新的灌溉方案对土壤肥力造成有害影响后，这些养分变得日益重要），随后四人被绞死，其他人被监禁和鞭打，公众对此予以谴责。为了减少政治反对，次年 4 月，伦敦政府接受了其驻开罗总督<a id="page-49"></a>〔原书第49页〕克罗默勋爵的辞呈；克罗默自 1883 年起管理殖民政府。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-088"></a>[88](#note-ch1-088)

Suddenly, however, the long-term future of Britain’s colonial occupation of Egypt, a political future that had, along with the dam, produced the value of those shares and mortgages, seemed less certain. In the summer of 1906, protests against the British occupation intensified, in public condemnation of the hanging of four men and the imprisonment and flogging of others in the Delta village of Dinshawai, forty-five miles north of Cairo, after they resisted British soldiers shooting their domestic pigeons for sport (housed in dovecotes, pigeons were raised for their droppings, which were used as fertiliser, providing nutrients of increasing importance following the deleterious effect of the new irrigation schemes on soil fertility). Anxious to reduce political opposition, the following April the government in London accepted the resignation <a id="page-49-en"></a>〔原书第49页〕of its proconsul in Cairo, Lord Cromer, who had administered the colonial government since 1883.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-088"></a>[88](#note-ch1-088)

<a id="ch01-0082"></a>

随后，一场自 1 月起威胁就已显而易见的金融危机爆发了。从伦敦紧急运送的 60 万英镑黄金未能阻止银行挤兑。“埃及最先倒下，”当时对 1907 年全球金融危机最具说服力的记述报道说。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-089"></a>[89](#note-ch1-089)恐慌蔓延到日本、德国和智利，然后在 10 月蔓延到纽约；华尔街的崩溃引发了一场金融收缩，其严重程度在此后一个世纪中只有大萧条超过。

A financial crisis, the threat of which had been clear since January, then broke. An emergency shipment of £600,000 in gold from London failed to stop the run on the banks. ‘Egypt went first’, the most persuasive contemporary account of the worldwide financial crisis of 1907 reported.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-089"></a>[89](#note-ch1-089) The panic spread to Japan, Germany, and Chile, and then by October to New York, where the collapse on Wall Street triggered a financial contraction, whose severity was surpassed over the next century only by the Great Depression.

<a id="ch01-0083"></a>

与此同时，埃及法院任命了一组专家来重组这家糖业公司。他们的计划是扩大当地甘蔗的加工，而不是试图从加工进口的受补贴奥地利甜菜糖中获利。为协助重组，负责人聘请了一位年轻的奥地利律师——未来的哈佛经济学家约瑟夫·熊彼特。熊彼特受过经济学训练（当时欧洲大学仍把经济学作为法律的一个分支教授），1908 年大部分时间都在开罗度过，并在业余时间发展了那本书的构思；回到欧洲后不久，他便完成了写作。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-090"></a>[90](#note-ch1-090)

Meanwhile, the Egyptian courts had appointed a group of experts to reorganise the sugar company. Their plan was to expand the refining of local sugar cane, rather than trying to profit from processing imports of subsidised Austrian beet sugar. To assist in the reorganisation, those in charge hired a young Austrian lawyer – the future Harvard economist Joseph Schumpeter. Trained in economics (still taught as a branch of law in European universities at that time), Schumpeter spent most of 1908 in Cairo, and in his spare time developed the ideas for the book that he completed writing soon after his return to Europe.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-090"></a>[90](#note-ch1-090)

<a id="ch01-0084"></a>

熊彼特的《经济发展理论》探讨了如何解释这个不断扩张的货币生钱世界。这个问题再次被提为资本如何赚取利息的问题。他希望理解他所说的“抽吸装置”；这种装置使资本家——即信用的提供者——能够从利润中抽出“源源不断的商品流”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-091"></a>[91](#note-ch1-091)为解释这套装置，这本书吸收了他重组糖业企业时获得的洞见。他的传记作者指出，在开罗，熊彼特“获得了实际的商业经验，以及商业和贸易在现实世界中如何运作的第一手知识”，他帮助重组糖业公司，实施不同的生产方法。“他对这项创新的参与给熊彼特留下了不可磨灭的印象。他亲眼见证了创新过程及其后果。这后来成为他理论的核心。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-092"></a>[92](#note-ch1-092)正如现代证券交易所为上一代经济学家提供了一个简化场所，使他们得以从中推导价格机制的抽象模型，一次对殖民埃及制糖业的短暂接触，也为熊彼特提供了实验室，让他以企业家的形象生成一整套资本理论。

Schumpeter’s *Theory of Economic Development* addressed the question of how to explain this expanding world of money that makes money. The question was posed, once again, as the issue of how capital earns interest. He wished to understand what he called ‘the suction apparatus’ that enabled the capitalist, meaning the supplier of credit, to draw ‘a permanent stream of goods from profits’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-091"></a>[91](#note-ch1-091) To explain the apparatus, the book drew on insights he obtained while reorganising the sugar business. In Cairo, his biographer notes, Schumpeter ‘acquired practical business experience and firsthand knowledge of how business and commerce worked in the real world’, in helping to reorganise the sugar company and implement different methods of production. ‘His participation in this innovation made an indelible impression on Schumpeter. He had witnessed firsthand the innovation process and its consequences. It would later become a centrepiece for his theory.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-092"></a>[92](#note-ch1-092) Just as the modern stock exchange had provided a previous generation of economists with a simplified site from which to derive an abstract model of the price mechanism, a brief encounter with the business of sugar production in colonial Egypt provided Schumpeter with the laboratory in which to generate, in the figure of the entrepreneur, an entire theory of capital.

<a id="ch01-0085"></a>

这本书具有广泛影响的论点是，货币扩张<a id="page-50"></a>〔原书第50页〕的力量——换言之，资本家通过创造信用赚取利息的能力——并非来自货币的属性，也非来自提供货币的资本家的权力，而是来自另一个不同人物——企业家——的独特角色。企业家的作用不是像萨伊所主张的那样协调商业，而是扰乱商业。

The widely influential argument of the book was that the power of <a id="page-50-en"></a>〔原书第50页〕money to expand – the ability, in other words, of the capitalist to earn interest from the creation of credit – arose not from the properties of money, nor from the powers of the capitalist who supplied it, but from the distinctive role of a different figure, the entrepreneur. The role of the entrepreneur was not to coordinate business, as Say had argued, but to disrupt it.

<a id="ch01-0086"></a>

### 利息作为对扰乱的回报

### Interest as a Reward for Disruption

<a id="ch01-0087"></a>

瓦尔拉斯和费雪等人设计的经济生活模型基于均衡原理，假定市场价格机制会不断在商品需求与供给之间产生平衡；这些模型没有给蓄意扰乱留出位置。因此，这些经济学家无法解释货币的赚钱能力，除非假定一种普遍的“时间偏好”，即偏好当下商品甚于未来商品。他们推测，这种偏好使那些向急需某种商品的借款人提供信用货币的人，能够索取一笔溢价（利息收费），迫使那些不愿等待的人支付超过商品价值的费用。正如熊彼特所指出的，这种普遍偏好没有证据。大多数企业通过留存利润为其持续或扩张活动提供资金，无需为使用货币支付费用（正如今天，股票市场在为企业提供资本方面作用极小）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-093"></a>[93](#note-ch1-093)只有那些陷入困境的人，例如面临财产被剥夺的债务人或面临意外危机的企业，才被迫以利息借入货币。要解释货币利息支付近来已成为普遍特征这一事实，就必须理解企业家的角色。

The models of economic life that men like Walras and Fisher devised, based on the principle of equilibrium, where the mechanism of a market price is assumed to continually produce a balance between the demand for goods and their supply, had no place for deliberate disruption. These economists were therefore unable to account for the earning power of money, except by positing a universal ‘time preference’ for present over future goods. This preference, they surmised, allowed those supplying credit money to a borrower seeking a good immediately to exact a premium (an interest charge), forcing those unwilling to wait for a good to pay more than its value. As Schumpeter pointed out, there was no evidence for this universal preference. Most businesses funded their continuing or expanding activities through retained profits, with no need to pay a fee for the use of money (just as today, stock markets played very little role in providing capital for business firms).<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-093"></a>[93](#note-ch1-093) Only those in distress, such as a debtor facing dispossession or a business facing an unexpected crisis, were forced to borrow money at interest. To explain the fact that the payment of interest on money had recently become a general feature, one had to understand the role of the entrepreneur.

<a id="ch01-0088"></a>

熊彼特写道，企业家是引入“新组合”的人，这些组合重组了现有的生产过程。重新安排使一家企业短暂地比竞争对手更有利可图。这种持续的重组在整个工业生活中反复进行，使经济生活的均衡论述所设想的、生产与消费之间的商品循环流动反复受到扰乱。扰乱产生了动态运动。与趋于均衡的经济过程这一形象相对照，熊彼特把这种扰乱性运动称为经济“发展”。他的论述不仅仅是对资本主义制度运作的社会学解释。它是对资本赚取利息、货币累积货币之力量这一解释难题的一种<a id="page-51"></a>〔原书第51页〕解答。企业家区别于普通企业经营者之处在于，作为创新者，企业家是唯一无法从留存收益或预期收益中为经营提供资金的行动者。看重当下资金之获取甚于未来货币，并不是普遍的人类特征；它源于企业家的特殊需要，企业家必须作为债务人运作。这种需要确立了一个货币市场，其价格就是利率。不同领域企业家对货币的需求，被市场转化为适用于一切资本的普遍利率。

Entrepreneurs are those who introduce ‘new combinations’, Schumpeter wrote, which reorganise an existing productive process. The rearrangement makes a business briefly more profitable than its rivals. Carried out repeatedly across the whole of industrial life, this continual rearranging causes the circular flow of goods between production and consumption, as envisioned in the equilibrium account of economic life, to be repeatedly disrupted. The disruption gives rise to a dynamic movement. As a contrast with the image of economic processes tending towards an equilibrium, Schumpeter termed this disruptive movement economic ‘development’. His account was not just a sociological explanation for the working of a capitalist system. It was a <a id="page-51-en"></a>〔原书第51页〕solution to the problem of explaining the power of capital to earn interest, of money to accumulate money. What distinguished the entrepreneur from the ordinary operator of a business was that, as an innovator, the entrepreneur was the only agent unable to fund operations out of retained or expected earnings. Valuing the access to present funds over future money was not a general human trait; it arose from the special needs of the entrepreneur, who was required to operate as a debtor. This need established a market for money, for which the price was the rate of interest. The demand for money among entrepreneurs in different fields was transformed by the market into the general rate of interest for all capital.

<a id="ch01-0089"></a>

对熊彼特而言，利息不是货币的内在属性，也不是对耐心的回报。它只是企业家赚取的一种特殊利润，作为重组生产过程的临时回报。重新安排使一家企业短暂地比竞争对手更有利可图。一旦其他企业采用同样的方法，竞争就会压低商品价格，企业家的利润也就终结。为说明这个过程，他举了一个直接来自开罗经验的例子。“让我们假设一位先前种植甘蔗的种植者改种棉花，而棉花直到不久前还比现在更有利可图。这是一种新组合；此人因此成为企业家并赚取利润。”接着，竞争压低收入，例如通过增加地租——“正如实际发生的那样”，他写道——到那时，“这个人的企业家职能便消失了”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-094"></a>[94](#note-ch1-094)

For Schumpeter, interest was not an intrinsic property of money, nor a reward for patience. Rather, it was simply the special kind of profit earned by an entrepreneur, as a temporary reward for reorganising a process of production. The rearrangement briefly makes an enterprise more profitable than its rivals. As soon as other businesses adopt the same methods, competition forces down the prices of goods and the entrepreneur’s profit comes to an end. To illustrate this process, he gave an example drawn directly from his own experience in Cairo. ‘Let us assume that a planter who has previously cultivated sugar cane changes over to cotton-growing, which until recently was more lucrative than it is now. This is a new combination; the man thereby becomes an entrepreneur and makes a profit.’ Then, competition forces down receipts, for example through an increase in the rent of the land – ‘as has actually happened’, he notes – and at that point ‘the entrepreneurial function of this man disappears’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-094"></a>[94](#note-ch1-094)

<a id="ch01-0090"></a>

让-巴蒂斯特·萨伊曾尝试棉花制造，失败后与弟弟合作实施一项更简单的炼糖计划，从而偶然发现了企业家的重要性。熊彼特也通过描述一位种植者把种植从棉花转向甘蔗，以同样的材料获得了类似的启示。而且他是在拯救同一家法国糖业公司时做到这一点的。

Jean-Baptiste Say had chanced upon the importance of the entrepreneur by trying his hand at cotton manufacturing, failing, and then collaborating with his brother on a simpler scheme for refining sugar. Schumpeter had had a similar revelation, with the same materials, by describing a plantation owner who shifts their cultivation from cotton to sugar cane. And he did it while rescuing the same French sugar company.

校注：上一段所引熊彼特例子是从甘蔗改种棉花，本段原文却写从棉花改种甘蔗，改种方向前后不一。译文保留原作差异。 

<a id="ch01-0091"></a>

在开罗期间，熊彼特可能亲身经历了种植甘蔗还是改种棉花这一选择。除了拯救糖业公司，他还参与组织了一座新的农业庄园，它属于埃及统治家族的一位公主。资料没有告诉我们这个人的名字。然而，这很可能是与赫迪夫分居的妻子；她像熊彼特一样是奥地利人，最近在开罗北郊获得了自己的宫殿和庄园。她通过<a id="page-52"></a>〔原书第52页〕她的兄弟结识了赫迪夫；她的兄弟曾是赫迪夫在维也纳特蕾西亚学院的同班同学，哈布斯堡帝国的政治精英在那里接受教育，几位奥斯曼—埃及王子也被送到那里学习。熊彼特是同一所学校的毕业生。熊彼特喜欢回忆商业成功之外的其他成就，并习惯于“凭魅力与年轻女性亲近”；他后来吹嘘自己与这位公主有染。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-095"></a>[95](#note-ch1-095)与任何私人关系相比，有趣却从未被提及的是熊彼特所参与的那家企业的性质。这座庄园位于开罗北郊的穆斯塔鲁德（今天是埃及最大炼油厂的所在地），对于当时在那里涌现的企业家形式而言，既典型又不寻常。它建在五年前阿斯旺大坝完工后才得以开放、可进行夏季棉花种植的土地上。它属于赫迪夫最近购置的一组示范农场，包括邻近的一座他自己的庄园，用于试验扩大棉花种植。一位英国作家刚在一本书中详细描述了这一模式，该书旨在鼓励“有意在这个受眷顾的国度从事商业生涯”的英国定居者迁往埃及，购地开发为棉花种植园。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-096"></a>[96](#note-ch1-096)

While in Cairo, Schumpeter may have experienced exactly this choice between planting sugar cane or switching to the cultivation of cotton. Besides rescuing the sugar company, he also had a hand in the organisation of a new agricultural estate, belonging to a princess of the Egyptian ruling family. The sources do not tell us the name of the person. However, this was likely the estranged wife of the Khedive, an Austrian like Schumpeter, who had recently acquired her own palace and estate on the northern outskirts of Cairo. She had met the Khedive <a id="page-52-en"></a>〔原书第52页〕through her brother, who had been his classmate at the Theresianum in Vienna, where the political elite of the Habsburg Empire was educated and where several Ottoman-Egyptian princes were sent to study. Schumpeter was a graduate of the same school. Fond of recalling other achievements besides his business success, and in the habit of ‘charm[ing] his way into intimacies with young women’, Schumpeter later boasted of having an affair with the princess.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-095"></a>[95](#note-ch1-095) Rather than any personal liaison, what is interesting but never mentioned is the nature of the enterprise in which Schumpeter had a hand. Located at Mostorod, on the northern outskirts of Cairo (today the site of Egypt’s largest oil refinery), the estate was both typical and unusual for the forms of entrepreneurship emerging there at that moment. It was built on lands made open to the summer cultivation of cotton by the completion five years earlier of the Aswan Dam. It formed part of a group of model farms that the Khedive had recently acquired, including a neighbouring estate of his own, to experiment in the expansion of cotton cultivation. An English writer had just described the model in detail, in a book aimed at encouraging English settlers ‘disposed to enter upon a business career in this favoured country’ to move to Egypt and buy up land to develop as cotton plantations.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-096"></a>[96](#note-ch1-096)

<a id="ch01-0092"></a>

在繁荣的开罗城短暂而多事的逗留期间，熊彼特相信，他通过自己对企业家的短暂体验，发现了资本主义与未来独特关系的秘密。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-097"></a>[97](#note-ch1-097)然而，企业家在此出现，并不是作为资本主义的动力之钥，而是作为帮助召唤出其托词的人。

In his short and eventful stay in the booming city of Cairo, Schumpeter believed he had discovered, through his own brief experience of the role of the entrepreneur, the secret of capitalism’s distinctive relationship to the future.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-097"></a>[97](#note-ch1-097) The entrepreneur makes his appearance here, however, not as the key to the dynamic of capitalism, but as the one who helps to conjure into being its alibi.

<a id="ch01-0093"></a>

资本的托词出现在这种既显得具有开创性、又显得是增长来源的组合之中。如果资本获得了它那种神秘的扩张能力，使货币能够生钱，那么就要在一种被误认为创新的破坏性力量中提供解释。为了命名他对资本主义的理解——一个以这种新的货币力量为特征的体系——熊彼特在书名中提出了一个新词：“经济发展”（*wirtschaftliche Entwicklung*）。发展，即引入新组合，是由企业家触发的过程。把所谓新古典经济理论所研究的静态循环交换过程，与动态的商业过程、或货币具有扩张性赚钱能力的资本主义体系区分开来，正取决于这个新出现的“发展”概念。

The alibi of capital emerges in this combination of what appears as both groundbreaking and the source of growth. If capital has acquired its mysterious ability to expand, enabling money to make money, an explanation is to be offered in the disruptive force misrecognised as innovation. To name his understanding of capitalism, as a system characterised by this new power of money, Schumpeter presented in the title of his book a novel term: ‘economic development’ (*wirtschaftliche Entwicklung*). Development, or the introduction of new combinations, was the process triggered by the entrepreneur. Distinguishing the static, circular process of exchange studied by so-called neoclassical economic theory from the dynamic process of business, or the capitalist system in which money had an expanding power to make money, depended on this emergent concept of development.

<a id="ch01-0094"></a>

熊彼特书名中的“经济发展”一词，尚未<a id="page-53"></a>〔原书第53页〕具有它在此后几十年将获得的更广泛含义。到二十世纪中叶，正如我们将在[第五章](#ch05-0001)看到的，经济的发明——一个以其“增长”来构想和衡量的对象——将改变发展的含义。在世纪之交的开罗，英国殖民政权还没有经济发展的概念。这不是他们使用的术语。他们专注于发展，但他们使用这个词时有更早、更具体的含义——它不指经济的发展，甚至也不指更含糊的经济发展（他们不使用这个术语），而是指“土地开发”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-098"></a>[98](#note-ch1-098)它描述了当时英国政策的重点：尼罗河的重组、灌溉工程的扩张，以及把农业转变为大规模私人和公司债务创造的领域。这正是熊彼特从中抽象出其资本理论的过程：把土地转为更有利可图的用途，或者说，由于灌溉方案以及棉花和甘蔗等工业作物的传播，转为更容易被资本化的用途。土地被重塑为一台更强大的装置，用于从未来“抽吸”收入。

The term ‘economic development’ in Schumpeter’s title did not yet <a id="page-53-en"></a>〔原书第53页〕have the wider meaning it would acquire in subsequent decades. By the mid-twentieth century, as we will see in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001), the invention of the economy, an object conceived and measured in terms of its ‘growth’, would transform the meaning of development. In turn-of-the-century Cairo, the British colonial regime had as yet no conception of economic development. It was not a term they used. They were preoccupied with development, but their use of the word had an earlier and more specific sense – it referred not to the development of an economy, nor even to a vaguer economic development, a term they did not use, but to ‘land development’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-098"></a>[98](#note-ch1-098) It described the focus of British policy at that time, the reorganisation of the Nile, the expansion of irrigation works, and the transformation of agriculture into a field of extensive private and corporate debt creation. This was precisely the process from which Schumpeter abstracted his theory of capital: converting land to more profitable purposes, or rather to purposes more easily capitalised, thanks to irrigation schemes and the spread of industrial crops such as cotton and sugar cane. Land was remade as a more powerful apparatus for the ‘suction’ of income from the future.

<a id="ch01-0095"></a>

种植棉花或甘蔗，以及决定从一种改种另一种，并没有什么创新之处。正如我们很快将会看到，两者在尼罗河谷的种植都已超过一千年。它们与增长也没有任何简单关系，因为这两种作物的产量都将下降。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch1-099"></a>[99](#note-ch1-099)我们在此引入这些农业计划，是为了追问它们所设计的新未来关系，同时避免暗示这代表了“改良”，或“增长”或“发展”的普遍过程。要把握对资本主义条件下未来工程的一种不同理解，出发点是用以下问题取代把历史构想为经济发展的做法：对未来收入的控制是如何被工程化的，未来本身又是如何通过组织耐久性与流动性的组合，被生产为集体生活的框架的。

There was nothing innovative about the cultivating of cotton or sugar cane, or the decision to switch from one to another. Both had been cultivated in the Nile Valley, as we shall shortly see, for more than a millennium. Nor did they have any simple relationship to growth, since the yields of both crops were set to decline.<a id="ref-en-note-ch1-099"></a>[99](#note-ch1-099) In introducing here these agricultural schemes, our aim has been to ask about the new relationship to the future that they engineered, while avoiding the implication that this represented ‘improvement’ or a general process of ‘growth’ or ‘development’. To grasp a different understanding of the engineering of the future under capitalism, the starting point is to replace a history conceived as economic development with the question of how the control of future revenues is engineered, and how the future itself is produced as a frame of collective life, through organising combinations of the durable and the liquid.

<a id="ch01-0096"></a>

熊彼特的埃及糖厂使我们能够把本书已开始追问的几个问题连接起来。在帝国时代——大致指第一次世界大战之前帝国迅速扩张的五十年——同时发生了两件事：技术圈的迅速扩张加速了对大地的破坏；经济学家和其他人用来解释非凡财富攫取——这种攫取<a id="page-54"></a>〔原书第54页〕伴随着这场对大地的攻击——的观点和思想，也同时呈现出轻盈或转瞬即逝的性质。破土活动在尘世间的物质破坏性，似乎与企业家的非物质性、观念性、想象性工作截然相反——尽管在实践中两者不可分割。破土使大规模从未来抽取成为可能，并在此过程中产生了不稳定性和不确定性；这些不稳定性和不确定性集中体现在新人物“破土者”——即“资本家”——身上。

Schumpeter’s Egyptian sugar mill allows us to connect together several questions that this book has begun to ask. In the age of empire, meaning roughly the five decades of rapid imperial expansion prior to the First World War, there occurred both an accelerated breaking of the Earth, in the rapid expansion of the technosphere, and a simultaneous lightness or evanescence of the arguments and ideas with which economists and others tried to explain the extraordinary capture of wealth that <a id="page-54-en"></a>〔原书第54页〕accompanied this ground assault. The earthly, material destructiveness of the groundbreaking appeared as the very opposite of the immaterial, ideational, imaginative work of the entrepreneur – although in practice the two were inseparable. Groundbreaking made it possible to extract from the future on a large scale, and in the process to generate instabilities and uncertainties personified in the new figure of the ground-breaker, the ‘capitalist’.

<a id="ch01-0097"></a>

熊彼特和妻子在开罗都染上了一种严重的发热病，导致他们在不到一年后便缩短了在该国的逗留。下一章，我们将在埃及多停留一段时间。离开糖厂大门和示范农场之后，是时候展开更广泛的问题：资本主义与未来的关系，以及现代货币的力量，是如何被组织起来的。我们将看到，种植棉花还是甘蔗的选择，并不仅仅是企业家的进取决定。为了产生企业家及其决定，整个国家必须被重塑，其生态必须被重新工程化，其人民必须被贫困化，其河流必须被毁灭。

Schumpeter and his wife both contracted a serious fever while in Cairo, causing them to cut short their stay in the country after less than a year. In the next chapter, we will linger in Egypt a little longer. Leaving the gates of the sugar factory and the model farm, it is time to open up wider questions about how the capitalist relationship to the future, and the modern power of money, were organised. As we will see, the choice between growing cotton and sugar cane was not simply the enterprising decision of an entrepreneur. To produce the entrepreneur and his decision, an entire country had to be remade, its ecology re-engineered, its people impoverished, and its river destroyed.


# 第二章　论弑河

<a id="ch02-0001"></a>

<a id="page-55"></a>〔原书第55页〕

<a id="page-55-en"></a>〔原书第55页〕

<a id="ch02-0002"></a>

## 第二章　论弑河

## 2 On Rivercide

<a id="ch02-0003"></a>

十九世纪的埃及为了信用货币的生产和偿还，经历了一场地理与生态的灾难性重排。这场灾难使我们得以更仔细地考察殖民占领、生态破坏与对未来进行资本化攫取之间的联系。埃及或许比世界上任何其他地方都更能体现货币生钱的力量。约瑟夫·熊彼特利用他在开罗的短暂经历，发展出把资本主义解释为“创造性破坏”的理论；这种对资本主义现代性的理解至今仍塑造着人们的想象方式。熊彼特为这种破坏性创造力提供的少数具体例子之一，就来自他对埃及农业转型的短暂参与。但那场破坏究竟包括什么？需要怎样重排技术圈？它又建立在怎样的未来生产、过去重想、技术诀窍重组、托词安排和无知扩张之上？

Egypt in the nineteenth century endured a catastrophic reordering of its geography and ecology in the service of the production and repayment of credit. The catastrophe allows us to look more closely at the connection between colonial occupation, ecological destruction, and the capitalising capture of the future. Egypt became a place, perhaps more than any other site in the world, that exemplified the power of money to make money. Joseph Schumpeter used his brief experience in Cairo to develop an explanation of capitalism as ‘creative destruction’, an understanding of capitalist modernity that still shapes the way it is imagined today. One of the few concrete examples that Schumpeter offered of this destructive creativity was drawn from his brief involvement in the agricultural transformation of Egypt. But what exactly did that destruction involve? What reordering of the technosphere was required? And on what producing of the future, reimagining of the past, reorganisation of know-how, arranging of alibis, and expansion of ignorance would it be based?

<a id="ch02-0004"></a>

“每位水利工程师都自认为是金融家，”威廉·威尔科克斯在回顾自己在埃及的职业生涯时写道，“而每位金融家都自认为是水利工程师。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-001"></a>[1](#note-ch2-001)威尔科克斯制定了阿斯旺大坝——建于 1899—1902 年——的第一批设计方案，后来管理了建坝出资人——英国资本家和企业家欧内斯特·卡塞尔爵士——的糖业地产。正如我们所见，正是卡塞尔糖业投资的崩溃把熊彼特带到了开罗。在埃及，水利工程是一种新金融秩序的基础，而这一秩序又得益于新程度的创造性破坏。信用创造、从未来<a id="page-56"></a>〔原书第56页〕抽吸支付的装置，不仅由欧内斯特·卡塞尔及其合伙人欧内斯特·克罗尼耶这样的企业家建造，也由运河、水闸、大坝、拦河堰和蒸汽泵构成。从未来获取，反过来又需要重写过去。

‘Every hydraulic engineer considered himself a financier’, wrote William Willcocks, reflecting on his career in Egypt, ‘and every financier considered himself a hydraulic engineer.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-001"></a>[1](#note-ch2-001) Willcocks produced the first designs for the Aswan Dam, built in 1899–1902, and later managed the sugar estates of the man who financed it, the English capitalist and entrepreneur Sir Ernest Cassel. It was the collapse of Cassel’s sugar investments, as we saw, that had brought Schumpeter to Cairo. In Egypt, hydraulic engineering was the basis of a new financial order, enabled by a new degree of creative destruction. The apparatus of credit creation, of <a id="page-56-en"></a>〔原书第56页〕the suction of payments from the future, was being built not just by entrepreneurs like Ernest Cassel and his partner Ernest Cronier, but out of canals, sluices, dams, barrages, and steam pumps. The acquisition from the future would require, in turn, a rewriting of the past.

<a id="ch02-0005"></a>

1882 年，英国为应对一场政治—金融危机而占领埃及。欧洲银行家运用其扩张的信用创造工具，相继发行政府贷款，每一笔贷款都确立了对不同未来收入来源的控制。各省税收、国家铁路、盐税、关税，以及最终统治者私人种植园，依次被抵押给银行家。每笔新贷款中越来越大的部分，用于偿还先前债务的利息和费用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-002"></a>[2](#note-ch2-002)每一笔贷款都把未来收入流的耐久性，与把那些预期收入之控制权转化为当下信用支付的安排的流动性结合起来。1873 年的国际金融危机由欧洲和美国铁路股票投机崩溃引发，并导致全球性萧条；加上再没有公共收入可供抵押，埃及政府被迫破产。一场反对政权及其债权人的民众起义导致了民族主义政府的建立，并使该国最大的地主和金融家寻求外部支持以恢复旧秩序，从而促成了英国的军事占领。1884 年，另一场民众起义的成功——马赫迪派推翻苏丹的埃及统治——以及开罗的又一轮金融危机，说服英国把临时的“干预”变成一种不设期限的帝国行政。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-003"></a>[3](#note-ch2-003)

The British had occupied Egypt in 1882 in response to a political-financial crisis. European bankers had deployed their expanded tools of credit creation to float successive government loans, each establishing a hold over a different source of future revenue. The taxes of individual provinces, the state railways, the salt tax, customs duties, and eventually the ruler’s private plantations were each mortgaged in turn to the bankers. An increasing part of every new loan was devoted to repaying interest and fees on the previous debts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-002"></a>[2](#note-ch2-002) Each loan combined the durability of a future flow of income with the liquidity of the arrangement that converted the control of those prospective revenues into a credit payment in the present. The international financial crisis of 1873, precipitated by the collapse of speculation in railway shares in Europe and the United States and leading to a worldwide depression, along with the lack of any further public revenues to mortgage, forced the Egyptian government into bankruptcy. A popular revolt against the regime and its creditors led to the creation of a nationalist government and caused the country’s largest landowners and financiers to seek external support to restore the old order, precipitating Britain’s military occupation. In 1884, the success of another popular revolt – the Mahdist overthrow of Egyptian rule in Sudan – and another round of financial crisis in Cairo persuaded Britain to turn its temporary ‘intervention’ into an open-ended imperial administration.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-003"></a>[3](#note-ch2-003)

<a id="ch02-0006"></a>

### 反复无常的自然

### A Volatile Nature

<a id="ch02-0007"></a>

随后是长达五十年、把一个国家改造成偿债机器的实验。建造这台机器既需要水利工程师调节世界最长河流的水流，也需要历史学家重写世界上有记载的最长历史之一。要理解这台机器的运作，必须重新考虑英国如何通过重新工程化尼罗河建立殖民政权的标准叙述。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-004"></a>[4](#note-ch2-004)

There followed a five-decade experiment in remaking a country as a repayment machine. The building of this machine required both the work of irrigation engineers to alter the flow of the world’s longest river and the work of historians to rewrite one of the world’s longest recorded histories. To understand the working of this machine, the standard account of how Britain built a colonial regime through the re-engineering of the Nile needs to be reconsidered.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-004"></a>[4](#note-ch2-004)

<a id="ch02-0008"></a>

这种标准叙述几乎立即开始被书写。1890 年，我们<a id="page-57"></a>〔原书第57页〕在上一章匆匆提到过的美国工程师戴维·埃姆斯·韦尔斯，出版了后来成为该时期美国最有影响的经济学文本的著作。他把埃及的转型置于他对 1870 年代以来技术创新所引发的革命性“扰动”的论述中心，预见了二十年后熊彼特的思想。他从苏伊士运河的例子开始，以英国工程师对尼罗河的改造结束。

The standard account began to be written almost immediately. In 1890 the American engineer David Ames Wells, whom we met in <a id="page-57-en"></a>〔原书第57页〕passing in the previous chapter, published what was to become the most influential US economic text of the period. He placed the transformation of Egypt at the centre of his account of the revolutionary ‘disturbances’ brought on by technical innovation since the 1870s, anticipating the ideas of Schumpeter two decades later. He started with the example of the Suez Canal and ended with the transformation of the Nile by the work of British engineers.

<a id="ch02-0009"></a>

> 1884 年，英国实际上占有了埃及；从那一刻起，在一群熟练工程师和实干者的管理下，这个国家赖以维持人民生命与繁荣的供水和灌溉系统开始了一场革新，并且已经带来了极其仁慈的结果。在下埃及，土地开垦正以每年五万英亩的速度进行，在尼罗河谷其他地区则达到这一数字的两倍；这为一个备受压迫、贫穷困苦的种族提供了数百年未有的更好机会，使他们能用自己的劳动养活自己。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-005"></a>[5](#note-ch2-005)

> In 1884 Britain virtually took possession of Egypt, and from that moment there was initiated, under the management of a body of skilled engineers and practical men, a renovation of the water-supply and irrigation system of the country upon which the life and prosperity of its people depend, and which has already been attended with results of extraordinary beneficence. In Lower Egypt land reclamation is going on at the rate of fifty thousand acres per annum, and in other sections of the Nile Valley at double that amount; giving to a down-trodden and impoverished race better opportunities than they have had for centuries of supporting themselves by their own labor.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-005"></a>[5](#note-ch2-005)

<a id="ch02-0010"></a>

按照传统叙述，英国最早采取的步骤之一，是废除旧农业制度所依赖的所谓“传统”强制劳动制度——*corvée*（徭役）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-006"></a>[6](#note-ch2-006)接着，占领当局处理埃及农业发展长期面临的问题——反复无常的自然力量。“埃及的历史就是人类利用尼罗河的故事，”后来成为现代埃及主要经济史著作的作者写道，“如果放任不管，这条河将是一位反复无常、变化多端的女主人，今年带来繁荣，明年带来饥荒。自从人类在尼罗河谷定居以来，就一直在以不同程度的成功努力驯服这条河，使它为自己服务。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-007"></a>[7](#note-ch2-007)我们将会发现，这段关于反复无常、不确定性和饥荒的历史是编造出来的。

One of Britain’s first steps, the conventional story goes, was to abolish the so-called ‘traditional’ system of forced labour, the *corvée*, on which the old agrarian system was based.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-006"></a>[6](#note-ch2-006) Next, the occupying authorities addressed the persistent problem facing the development of agriculture in Egypt – the volatile forces of nature. ‘The history of Egypt is the story of the use man has made of the Nile’, wrote the author of what became the leading economic history of modern Egypt. ‘Left to herself, the river would be a capricious and changeful mistress, bringing prosperity one year, famine the next. Ever since man settled down in the Nile Valley, he has endeavoured, with the varying degrees of success, to tame the river and turn it to his service.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-007"></a>[7](#note-ch2-007) This history of volatility, uncertainty, and famine, as we will discover, was a fabrication.

<a id="ch02-0011"></a>

一切耕作都依赖河流每年的泛滥，而历史学家声称，泛滥的范围无法预测。为了矫正这一点，英国人设计了一套他们称为“洪水控制”的新系统，以调节河流的水流。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-008"></a>[8](#note-ch2-008)首先，他们监督修复开罗以北的一座拦河堰，提高河流向尼罗河三角洲主要运河供水处的水位。随后，他们在南方的阿斯旺修建了一座大得多的水坝，并在前两者中间、艾斯尤特修建了第三座拦河堰。这些工程使尼罗河水能够储存在坝后水库中，调节<a id="page-58"></a>〔原书第58页〕夏季每年的泛滥，并把大部分灌溉系统从围堤田块改造为永久运河。据说，新的蓄水机制提高了农业生产力，办法是把全国大部分农业从每年一季、在洪水退去后的围堤田块播种的制度，转变为常年种植制度，同一块田每年可种两三季作物。尼罗河三角洲许多地区和中埃及的小块地区已经引入常年种植，通过畜力灌溉机械，以及日益增多的蒸汽泵，从河流或本世纪早些时候修建的深运河中提水。新的拦河堰运作方式不同：它们不是加深运河以便在河流水位低时输水，而是在全年提高河流和运河的水位，使该国四分之三以上的农田得以从围堤田块的季节性利用转变为全年种植。这反过来又使棉花和甘蔗这两种主要工业作物的生产大规模扩张。用于出口的棉花种植面积，在 1820 年代和 1830 年代有限水平的基础上，到 1860 年代和 1870 年代已增至十倍，1882 年后的二十年里又翻了一倍多。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-009"></a>[9](#note-ch2-009)据标准叙述，棉花种植成为该国经济增长的支柱，并把它整合进所谓的世界市场。

All cultivation depended on the annual inundation of the river, whose extent, historians claimed, was unpredictable. To remedy this, the British engineered a new system of what they termed ‘flood control’ to alter the flow of the river.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-008"></a>[8](#note-ch2-008) First, they supervised repairs to a barrage north of Cairo, raising the level of the river where it supplied the main canals of the Nile Delta. They then built the much larger dam in the south at Aswan, together with a third barrage midway between the other two, at Asyut. These made it possible to store the water of the Nile in the reservoir behind the dam, regulate the annual inundation in the <a id="page-58-en"></a>〔原书第58页〕summer, and convert most of the irrigation system from flood basins to permanent canals. The new storage mechanisms allowed an increase in agricultural productivity, it was said, by switching most of the country’s agriculture from a system based on a single annual crop, sown in the catch basins after the flood waters receded, to a system of perennial cultivation, in which two or three crops a year could be grown in the same field. Many parts of the Nile Delta and small areas of Middle Egypt had already introduced perennial cropping, lifting water from the river or deep-lying canals constructed earlier in the century, via animalpowered irrigation machines and, increasingly, steam pumps. The new barrages worked differently: rather than deepening the canals to carry water when the river was low, they raised the water level in the river and the canals throughout the year, allowing the conversion of more than three-quarters of the country’s fields from the seasonal use of flood basins to year-round cultivation. This in turn enabled a large expansion in the production of the two main industrial crops, cotton and sugar cane. The area devoted to growing cotton for export, which had already increased tenfold by the 1860s and 1870s from its modest levels in the 1820s and 1830s, more than doubled again in the two decades after 1882.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-009"></a>[9](#note-ch2-009) Its cultivation became the mainstay of the country’s economic growth, according to standard accounts, and integrated it into so-called world markets.

<a id="ch02-0012"></a>

因此，埃及的历史被讲述为与自然的遭遇，其形式是一条河流，而这条河流不可预测的洪水使她成为一位需要被“驯服”的“反复无常、变化多端的女主人”。负责驯服她的人掌握了调节和管理她反复无常的技术手段。关于如何管理未驯服的社会力量，也有一种平行的论述。*corvée*，连同*courbage*——用埃及河马的皮制成、用来强制执行强制劳动制度的鞭子（甚至当河马正被其皮所强制推行的灌溉工程逼向灭绝时也是如此）——集中体现了一个腐败专制的政府，而它将被改造为法治而人道的政府。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-010"></a>[10](#note-ch2-010)正如自然力量将被控制，东方天然的专制将被一种更理性、更人道的行政所取代。在这种叙述中，技术重组的作用是改善、推进、合理化并提高生产力。

Thus, the history of Egypt is told as the encounter with nature, in the form of a river whose unpredictable flood made her a ‘capricious and changeful mistress’ in need of being ‘tamed’. The men taking charge of her taming had mastered the technical means to regulate and manage her capriciousness. A parallel argument was made about the administering of untamed social forces. The *corvée*, together with the *courbage*, the whip made from the hide of the Egyptian hippo and used to enforce the compulsory labour regime (even as the hippo was being driven extinct by the very irrigation works its hide enforced), epitomised a corrupt and despotic government that was to be rendered juridical and humane.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-010"></a>[10](#note-ch2-010) Just as the forces of nature were to be controlled, the natural despotism of the East was to be replaced with a more rational, more humane, administration. The role of technical reorganisation, in this account, was to improve, to advance, to rationalise, and to make more productive.

<a id="ch02-0013"></a>

当焦点不在于从未驯服的自然（无论是物理的还是人类的）中安排、改良和榨取剩余的问题，而在于如何通过灌溉工程<a id="page-59"></a>〔原书第59页〕建造技术圈，把它变成攫取未来的新装置时，这段历史就呈现为不同的样子。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-011"></a>[11](#note-ch2-011)我们不应假定技术变化就是改良，而应追问问题是怎样被定义的，解决方案又服务于什么。十九世纪埃及农民面临的主要威胁，不是尼罗河洪水过高或过低的问题。那种“风险”很容易被夸大，而工程本身又使它更加严重。农民面临一种不同的、反复出现的生态威胁，它正是近来毁灭性作物歉收和经济灾难的原因。它还可能增加了过度泛滥的概率。这种新威胁影响了现有的安排：把多余的尼罗河水储存起来，供泛滥退去、洪泛平原排干之后使用；这种安排使耕作者能够应对洪水过高过低的问题，但如今却要被摧毁。

This history appears differently when the focus is placed not on the problems of ordering, improving, and extracting a surplus from an untamed nature (whether physical or human), but on how the making <a id="page-59-en"></a>〔原书第59页〕of a technosphere built out of irrigation works a new apparatus for the capture of the future.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-011"></a>[11](#note-ch2-011) We should not assume that technical changes were improvements, but ask how the problems were defined and for what the solutions were useful. The main threat faced by Egyptian farmers in the nineteenth century was not the problem of high and low Nile floods. That ‘risk’ was easily exaggerated and the engineering works themselves made it worse. Farmers faced a different, recurrent ecological threat, one that was the cause of recent, devastating crop failures and economic calamity. It may also have increased the likelihood of excessive inundation. The new threat affected an existing arrangement for storing surplus Nile waters for use after the inundation and draining of the floodplain, an arrangement that allowed cultivators to manage the problem of high and low floods, but which was now to be destroyed.

<a id="ch02-0014"></a>

与本世纪早些时候进行的灌溉工程不同，英国建造的蓄水系统没有承认现有机制，没有考虑其长处，也没有处理这些其他脆弱性。新安排处理的不是那些问题，而是资本化问题：如何把田地从产生和储存财富、只允许有限形式信用创造的安排，转变为一种从未来产生预期收入流的装置，这些收入流可以在当下变现，成为那些在空间和时间上都与田地分离者的非劳动所得。这一切都不是由对棉花或糖等原料的特定*需要*所驱动，也不是由欧洲“剩余”资本的流动所驱动，也不是由把埃及在空间上整合进世界市场的需求所驱动。那些都是常见的故事。它也不代表十九世纪晚期金融化的新阶段，因为至少从本世纪中叶起，创造信用并从信用建设中获利，一直是欧洲参与灌溉和农业计划的目的，而在此前很久，参与贸易计划也是如此。

Unlike the irrigation works carried out earlier in the century, the storage system built by the British did not recognise the existing mechanism, did not consider its strengths, and did not deal with these other vulnerabilities. The new arrangement addressed not those issues, but the problem of capitalisation: how to convert the fields from arrangements that produced and stored wealth, allowing only limited forms of credit creation, into an apparatus producing flows of prospective revenue from the future, which could be realised in the present and made into unearned income for those separated from the fields in both space and time. None of this was driven by a particular *need* for raw materials, such as cotton or sugar, nor by a flow of ‘surplus’ capital from Europe, nor by a demand to integrate Egypt spatially into a world market. Those are the usual stories. Nor did it represent a new, late-nineteenth-century stage of financialisation, for the creating and profiting from credit construction had been the purpose of European involvement in irrigation and agricultural schemes since at least the middle of the century, and in trading schemes long before that.

<a id="ch02-0015"></a>

### 水车会吱呀作响吗？

### Can the Waterwheel Squeak?

<a id="ch02-0016"></a>

1990 年代及其后二十年，我曾多次在埃及南部一个村庄生活，了解人们如何耕种土地、维持生计。我们住的房子旁边，靠着一堵畜棚的土坯墙，立着一台拆散的木质灌溉机械——一个巨大的带齿木轮，属于<a id="page-60"></a>〔原书第60页〕*saqiya*，即畜力水车。我得知，这台机器曾被用来从一口井里提水，灌溉周围的田地；那口井就挖在我们现在房子所在地的旁边。与我同龄的男人记得年轻时在 1960 年代末阿斯旺高坝完工之前帮忙操作水车。我从年长的男人那里了解到一件不同寻常的事。在大坝建成前的旧日里，每年洪水退去后，这样的水车会被架设在田野各处，每一台都安放在一个砖砌的大型地下蓄水池或水井上。这些水井和水车构成了一个广泛的蓄水和灌溉农业系统，而我从未读到过。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-012"></a>[12](#note-ch2-012)甚至三十年后，这种蓄水方式以及它所组织的世界，仍从未被描述过。

During the 1990s and over the following two decades, I lived for several periods in a village in the south of Egypt, learning how people farmed the land and made their livelihoods. Next to the house where we lived, against the mudbrick wall of an animal shelter, stood the disassembled parts of a wooden irrigation machine – the large, toothed wheel of a <a id="page-60-en"></a>〔原书第60页〕*saqiya*, or animal-driven waterwheel. The machine, I learned, was once used to raise water from a well that had been dug adjacent to where our house now stood, to irrigate the surrounding field. The men of my age remembered helping with the wheel in their youth, before the completion of the High Dam at Aswan in the late 1960s. From older men I learned something remarkable. In the old days before the dam, once the flood waters receded each year, waterwheels like this would be assembled across the fields, each one placed over a large, brick-built underground cistern or well. The wells and waterwheels constituted an extensive system of water storage and irrigated farming about which I had never read.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-012"></a>[12](#note-ch2-012) Even today, thirty years later, this method of storage, and the world it organised, has never been described.

<a id="ch02-0017"></a>

储存问题对我们思考资本主义的方式很重要。在许多论述中，前现代国家通过控制储存来治理。开罗等城市的大型粮仓可以充当政府税收支付的接收者、信用机制和价格控制工具。它还可以在短缺时期供应粮食，以防混乱。据说，在资本主义下，储存被转变为一种组织流动和人口控制的不同方法。大多数商品可以通过市场交换按需获得，因此现在只有某些战略物品被储存，主要是那些具有液态或流动形式的东西——水、石油，尤其是货币。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-013"></a>[13](#note-ch2-013)其中最大的货币资本，被想象为从过去积累起来的储备，但储存起来就会贬值。它必须被迅速投入运转并分散开来，以补充储备，实际上扩大储备。因此，大多数关于资本主义的论述实际上保留了一种简单的储存模式：从过去堆积起来的东西支配未来。我们在此探索一种不同的理解：资本是攫取或资产化未来的装置，使少数人能够在当下享用那种未来收入，并把随后偿还的负担强加给多数人。从未来获取不仅通过金融工程运作，也通过工业生活、人类生计和生态系统的工程运作。埃及的蓄水和水利工程史可以提供一种关于资本主义现代性的不同叙述。储存既没有消失，也没有增加。它被重组到新的手中，转移到新的地点，在运作上被大幅简化。这场改变地球的转型，摧毁了河流本身的生命，其目的不是储存储备，而是构造对未来的新支配。

The question of storage is important to how we think about capitalism. In many accounts, pre-modern states governed through the control of storage. A large grain store in a city such as Cairo could serve as the recipient of government tax payments, a machinery of credit, and an instrument of price control. It could also be used to prevent disorder, by supplying grain in periods of shortage. Under capitalism, it is said, storage was transformed into a different method of organising the control of flows and populations. Most goods could be acquired on demand through market exchange, so now only certain strategic items were stored, mainly those available in liquid form – water, petroleum, and above all money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-013"></a>[13](#note-ch2-013) The largest of these, money capital, is imagined as a reserve accumulated from the past, but one that loses value if stored. It must be quickly put in motion and dispersed, to replenish the store and indeed expand it. So, most accounts of capitalism in fact retain a simple storage model: what is piled up from the past governs the future. Here we are exploring a different understanding: capital as apparatuses that capture, or assetise, the future, allowing a few to enjoy that future income in the present and imposing on the majority the burden of its subsequent repayment. The acquisition from the future operates not only through financial engineering, but through the engineering of industrial life, human livelihoods, and ecological systems. The history of water storage and hydraulic engineering in Egypt can offer a different account of capitalist modernity. Storage neither disappeared nor increased. It was reorganised into new hands, relocated in new locations, and vastly simplified in operation. This terraforming transformation, in which the very life of the river was destroyed, was to serve not the storing up of a reserve but the constructing of a new command of the future.

<a id="ch02-0018"></a>

<a id="page-61"></a>〔原书第61页〕对英国人而言，灌溉工程处理的是可见、可测量之物。它忽视无法直接看到和计算的东西。殖民工程师运用水文学——即关于地表水流的科学——来处理尼罗河。他们很少关注后来所谓的水文地质学，即处理不可见、不可测量的地下水。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-014"></a>[14](#note-ch2-014)这种忽视源于无知的制造（agnotology），而非单纯的不知情。他们知道地下水存在，而且正如我们将看到的，它被广泛使用，但他们选择忽视它。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-015"></a>[15](#note-ch2-015)通过估算可见、易于测量和控制的东西——河流或运河横截面的面积及其水流速度——他们能够计算流量，即单位时间内的水量。流量使他们能够估算“单位供水的灌溉面积”（duty of water）；这个术语源于英国用水力驱动机器进行工业生产的用法，后来被印度和埃及的灌溉工程师采用，用以计算给定地表水供应可灌溉的作物面积。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-016"></a>[16](#note-ch2-016)目标是让“尼罗河供水……发挥其能提供的最大功效”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-017"></a>[17](#note-ch2-017)

<a id="page-61-en"></a>〔原书第61页〕For the British, irrigation engineering dealt with what was visible and measurable. It ignored what could not be directly seen and calculated. Colonial engineers addressed the Nile using the science of hydrology: in terms of the flow of surface water. They paid little attention to what would later be known as hydrogeology, dealing with water that was not visible or measurable, stored beneath the surface.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-014"></a>[14](#note-ch2-014) This inattention was the product of agnotology, not ignorance. They knew that water was present beneath the ground and, as we will see, widely used, but chose to ignore it.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-015"></a>[15](#note-ch2-015) By estimating what could be seen and easily measured and controlled – the area of a cross-section of a river channel or canal and the velocity at which its water moved – they were able to calculate the flow rate, or the volume per unit of time. The flow rate allowed them to estimate the ‘duty of water’, a term coined in the use of water power to run industrial machinery in Britain but taken up by irrigation engineers in India and then Egypt to calculate the area of each crop that a given supply of surface water could irrigate.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-016"></a>[16](#note-ch2-016) The aim was to make ‘the Nile supply . . . do the maximum work that could be got out of it’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-017"></a>[17](#note-ch2-017)

<a id="ch02-0019"></a>

要理解发生的转变，我们需要以不同方式思考尼罗河，同时考虑可见和不可见的水，从而看到另一种生态。历史学家把先前的安排称为围堤蓄水灌溉，但只提到这个系统的一半。没有任何现代学术研究描述过农民如何把河流用作全年蓄水系统，支撑常年灌溉和多季作物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-018"></a>[18](#note-ch2-018)英国为拦蓄尼罗河水而修建的大坝，并未引入河水储存，也没有开创常年灌溉和全年农业。相反，它们以不同的、效率更低的方式，把水储存在地表的狭窄河道中。工程师们启动的不是常年灌溉，而是把水截留在地表，而此前水是分散储存于地下的。

To understand the transformation that occurred, we need to consider the Nile differently, in terms of both visible and invisible water, bringing into view a different ecology. Historians refer to the previous arrangement as basin irrigation but mention only one-half of the system. No modern scholarship has described how farmers used the river as a year-round storage system, supporting perennial irrigation and multiple crop seasons.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-018"></a>[18](#note-ch2-018) The dams built by the British to impound the Nile did not introduce the storing of its waters and did not initiate perennial irrigation and year-round agriculture. Rather, they stored the waters differently, and less effectively, in a narrow channel on the surface. The engineers instigated, not perennial irrigation, but a trapping of waters on the surface of the land, where they had previously been dispersed and stored beneath it.

<a id="ch02-0020"></a>

尼罗河谷呈下坡走向，既有纵向的（像所有河流一样），在这里是向北流向地中海，也有横向的：河流的洪泛平原在离河最近处最高，即紧邻主河道的天然堤上。几千年来，河流在夏末因埃塞俄比亚季风雨而上涨，溢出河岸，沉积一层淤泥，它先把最重的淤泥颗粒丢在离河道最近处，形成一道高于洪泛平原其余部分的河岸高台，如图一所示。天然堤之外，土地向外侧倾斜，直到可耕种河谷边缘，止于沙漠的石灰岩陡崖。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-019"></a>[19](#note-ch2-019)<a id="page-62"></a>〔原书第62页〕

The Nile Valley runs downhill, both longitudinally (like all rivers), in this case northwards towards the Mediterranean Sea, but also laterally: the floodplain of the river is highest at the point closest to the river, on the levees adjacent to the main channel. Over millennia, as the river, swollen in late summer by the monsoon rains of Ethiopia, overflowed its banks and deposited a layer of silt, it dropped the heaviest particles of silt first, closest to the channel, creating a berm higher than the rest of the floodplain, as shown in figure one. Beyond the levees the land slopes downwards towards the outer edges of the cultivable valley, which ends at the limestone escarpment of the desert.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-019"></a>[19](#note-ch2-019)<a id="page-62-en"></a>〔原书第62页〕

<a id="ch02-fig01"></a>



![一幅地质剖面图显示贝尼苏韦夫附近的尼罗河谷地层，自西向东标注，包含层状沉积物、高程标尺以及标明石灰岩、砂和泥的图例。](images/ufig_1.jpg)

图1　贝尼苏韦夫附近尼罗河谷横剖面。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-020"></a>[20](#note-ch2-020)

Figure 1. Cross-section across the Nile Valley at Beni Suef.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-020"></a>[20](#note-ch2-020)





<a id="ch02-0022"></a>

围堤蓄水灌溉方法已使用了数千年，经历了发展、废弃和恢复的时期。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-021"></a>[21](#note-ch2-021)在这种制度下，主要灌溉渠道穿过河岸高台，把夏季泛滥的水引到远处的田地。土堤把洪泛平原分成大型蓄水田区，每块一千到数万英亩，又由较小的坝分成便于管理的区块。水闸门或堤坝上的临时开口，使每个田区能够依次蓄水到一到三米深，把富含养分的洪水储存约四十五天，然后把多余的水排入下游较低的田区，最终回到河中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-022"></a>[22](#note-ch2-022)在 1805 年至 1848 年统治的穆罕默德·阿里治下，工程师改进了蓄水田区的布局，改进了较高与较低田区之间的依次衔接，并增建运河，从更上游引来洪水，供应靠近河流的河岸高地上的田地。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-023"></a>[23](#note-ch2-023)排干洪水后，随着地面开始干燥开裂，农民播种两种主要谷类作物：小麦供富裕者制作面包，大麦用于制作普通面包、喂养马匹和酿造啤酒（尼罗河洪水较弱时，人们更偏好大麦，因为它所需生长季更短、用水更少）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-024"></a>[24](#note-ch2-024)他们用同样的方法种植豆科作物，主要是喂养牛和水牛的三叶草，以及小扁豆、鹰嘴豆、葫芦巴、羽扇豆和蚕豆。与谷类作物不同，豆科作物为土壤增添更多养分，与<a id="page-63"></a>〔原书第63页〕根区吸收空气中氮气并将其转化为可用形态的细菌共生。水、空气、淤泥、土壤、细菌和人类劳动相互作用，生产出这些作物，既不需要人造肥料或额外灌溉，甚至不需要犁地、清除石块、防治害虫或除草的劳动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-025"></a>[25](#note-ch2-025)

The method of basin irrigation had been in use for millennia, through periods of development, disuse, and restoration.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-021"></a>[21](#note-ch2-021) Under this system, the main irrigation channels were cut through the berm to carry the summer inundation to the fields beyond. Earthen dykes divided the floodplain into large catch basins, each of a thousand to tens of thousands of acres, subdivided by smaller dams into manageable sections. Sluice gates or temporary openings in the dykes and dams made it possible to fill each basin in turn to a depth of one to three metres, store the nutrient-rich inundation for about forty-five days, and then release the surplus into a lower basin downstream and eventually back into the river.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-022"></a>[22](#note-ch2-022) Under Muhammad Ali, who ruled from 1805 to 1848, engineers had improved the arrangement of catch basins, enhancing the sequence of upper and lower basins and adding canals drawing flood water from further upstream to supply the elevated fields on the berm close to the river.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-023"></a>[23](#note-ch2-023) After draining the flood waters, as the ground began to dry and crack, farmers sowed the two main cereal crops, wheat for the bread of the well-to-do and barley to make ordinary bread and to feed horses and make beer (barley was preferred to wheat when the Nile flood was weak, as it required a shorter growing season and less water).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-024"></a>[24](#note-ch2-024) They used the same method for the leguminous crops, principally clover to feed cattle and water buffalo, alongside lentils, chickpeas, fenugreek, lupins, and broad beans. Unlike the cereal crops, the legumes added further nutrients to the soil, working symbiotically with bacteria in the <a id="page-63-en"></a>〔原书第63页〕root zone that absorb nitrogen from the air and process it into useable form. The interaction of water, air, silt, soil, bacteria, and human labour produced these crops without need for artificial fertiliser or further irrigation, nor even for the labour of ploughing, stone removal, pest control, or weeding.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-025"></a>[25](#note-ch2-025)

<a id="ch02-0023"></a>

每一部埃及农业史都描述这个系统。但还有第二种蓄水方法，用来在冬季主收成之后的初夏生产第二季作物——甚至在秋季生产第三季作物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-026"></a>[26](#note-ch2-026)穆罕默德·阿里治下引入的改良，部分就是为了加强这种安排。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-027"></a>[27](#note-ch2-027)水不是储存在围堤田块中，而是储存在它们之下的地层中。现代历史学家被殖民灌溉工程师说服，认为旧制度每年只允许种植一季主要作物，“一年其余时间因缺乏灌溉用水而休耕”，因此从未描述过十九世纪后期灌溉方案所摧毁的旧制度。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-028"></a>[28](#note-ch2-028)

Every account of Egypt’s agrarian history describes this system. But there was a second method for storing water, which was used to produce a second crop, in early summer, after the main winter harvest – and even a third crop, in the autumn.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-026"></a>[26](#note-ch2-026) The improvements introduced under Muhammad Ali were designed in part to enhance this arrangement.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-027"></a>[27](#note-ch2-027) The water was stored not in the field basins but in a substrate beneath them. Convinced by the colonial irrigation engineers that the old system allowed only one main crop a year, ‘the land lying fallow during the rest of the year for want of irrigation water’, modern historians have never described the old system that later-nineteenth-century irrigation schemes destroyed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-028"></a>[28](#note-ch2-028)

<a id="ch02-fig02"></a>



![一幅横剖面图显示扎加齐格附近尼罗河三角洲的地质层，标注尼罗河各支流、沉积层、高程标尺和地名。](images/ufig_2.jpg)

图2　扎加齐格附近尼罗河三角洲横剖面。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-029"></a>[29](#note-ch2-029)





该横剖面展示扎加齐格附近的尼罗河三角洲，深度从正 20 米标至负 30 米。图左标注尼罗河罗塞塔支流，中部附近标注达米埃塔支流，右侧标出扎加齐格。表层标注全新世淤泥。其下区域标注晚更新世砂层。更深处标注更新世砂砾层。图中显示不平整的沉积边界以及切穿各层的垂直河道，所有单元均清楚标注。





![A cross section shows geological layers across the Nile Delta at Zagazig, with labelled branches of the Nile, sediment layers, elevation scale, and place names.](images/ufig_2.jpg)

Figure 2. Cross-section across the Nile Delta at Zagazig.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-029"></a>[29](#note-ch2-029)





The cross section presents the Nile Delta at Zagazig with depth marked from plus 20 metres to negative 30 metres. Labels identify the Rosetta branch of the Nile on the left and the Damietta branch of the Nile near the centre, with Zagazig marked on the right. Surface layers are labelled Holocene mud. Beneath this, areas are labelled Late Pleistocene sands. Deeper layers are labelled Pleistocene sands and gravels. The diagram shows uneven sediment boundaries and vertical channels cutting through layers, with all units clearly named.



<a id="ch02-0025"></a>

尼罗河洪泛平原的土壤由两层组成，如[图二](#ch02-fig02)剖面所示：上层是冲积砂土和黏土，其相对不透水的物质构成围堤田区的底部，储存并缓慢吸收部分洪水；下层是砾石和砂的基质。这种更粗糙、颗粒状的物质可以蓄存大量<a id="page-64"></a>〔原书第64页〕水分，水被截留在上覆黏土层之下。当洪水通过堤坝和运河的开口淹没田地表层时，也补给了下方的砾石层，水向下渗过黏土，或在河流上涨时从河床两侧直接渗入，或通过淹没田间挖的灌溉坑而进入。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-030"></a>[30](#note-ch2-030)即使在今天，尽管上游地表水库造成地下水减少、下游因此发生海水入侵（全球海平面上升又加剧了这一点），这种地下储存仍是世界上最大的地下水储层之一。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-031"></a>[31](#note-ch2-031)

The soils of the Nile floodplain consist of two layers, as shown in crosssection in [figure 2](#ch02-fig02): an upper level of alluvial sands and clays, whose relatively impermeable material forms the basins that stored and slowly absorbed some of the flood waters; and a substrate of gravel and sand. This more coarse and granular material could hold large amounts of <a id="page-64-en"></a>〔原书第64页〕water trapped beneath the clayey soils above. As the flood waters inundated the surface of the fields via openings in the dykes and canals, they also recharged the gravel layer below, seeping down through the clays, or percolating directly from the sides of the riverbed as the river rose, or via the flooding of irrigation pits dug in the fields.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-030"></a>[30](#note-ch2-030) Even today, despite depletion by surface reservoirs upstream and consequent seawater intrusion downstream (exacerbated by rising global sea levels), this underground storage forms one of the largest groundwater reservoirs in the world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-031"></a>[31](#note-ch2-031)

<a id="ch02-fig03"></a>



![一幅侧视图显示萨基亚水车从井中提水，一头牲畜绕圈拉动水平横梁，横梁与装有提水容器的垂直链条相连。](images/ufig_3.jpg)

图3　*萨基亚*水车从井中提水。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-032"></a>[32](#note-ch2-032)





侧视图显示用于从井中提水的萨基亚装置。一头牲畜绕圈行走，拉动一根连接垂直旋转轴的水平横梁。旋转驱动一条装有等距容器的垂直链条，链条下行入井，从另一侧上升。装满的容器向上移动，在地面水槽处倒空。石墙勾勒出井筒及周围结构。底部标尺显示 0 至 5 英尺。





![A side view shows a saqiya lifting water from a well, with an animal turning a horizontal beam connected to a vertical chain of containers.](images/ufig_3.jpg)

Figure 3. *Saqiya* raising water from a well.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-032"></a>[32](#note-ch2-032)





The side view shows a saqiya mechanism used to raise water from a well. An animal walks in a circle, pulling a horizontal beam attached to a vertical rotating shaft. The rotation drives a vertical chain fitted with evenly spaced containers that descend into the well and rise on the opposite side. The filled containers move upward and empty into a trough at ground level. Stone walls outline the well shaft and surrounding structure. A scale at the bottom shows 0 to 5 feet.



<a id="ch02-0027"></a>

第二季作物用水来自这个地下储层，使用的是置于大型砖砌水井之上的*saqiya*，即畜力水车。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-033"></a>[33](#note-ch2-033)每一位埃及历史读者都熟悉*saqiya*，但通常假定它是从尼罗河或运河中提水。然而，在二十世纪之前，耕作者主要用它从井中提水。它由一个由牛驱动的水平轮组成，带动两个由轴连接的竖直轮（见[图三](#ch02-fig03)）。较大的竖直轮通过一长串水罐从井中提水。安置*saqiya*的那口井则不那么为人熟悉。它是一个大型腔体，通过挖一个直径约十米、深三米到十或十五米的坑建成，<a id="page-65"></a>〔原书第65页〕深度取决于地下水位。坑壁用黏土砖砌成圆形墙体，砖在工地制作并烧制，以获得强度和抗水性（见[图四](#ch02-fig04)）。正如一份中世纪文献所述，为下沉这口井，地面的砌砖工在由金合欢木制成的环形木基上砌筑一层层砖石，其他人则用桶从坑底挖出淤泥和水，在框架下方挖掘。

The second crop was irrigated from this subterranean reservoir, using *saqiyas*, or animal-driven waterwheels, placed over large, brick-built wells.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-033"></a>[33](#note-ch2-033) The *saqiya* is familiar to every reader of Egyptian history, but is usually assumed to have lifted water from the Nile or from a canal. Before the twentieth century, however, cultivators used it to raise water mainly from wells. It consisted of a horizontal wheel driven by an ox, turning two vertical wheels connected by an axle (see [figure 3](#ch02-fig03)). The larger of the vertical wheels lifted the water from the well in a chain of pots. The well over which the *saqiya* was placed is less familiar. It was a large chamber, constructed by excavating a pit about ten metres in diameter, to a depth ranging from three metres to ten or fifteen metres, <a id="page-65-en"></a>〔原书第65页〕depending on the level of the ground water. The sides were lined with a circular wall of clay bricks, produced on site and fired to impart strength and resistance to water (see [figure 4](#ch02-fig04)). To sink the well, as a medieval text relates, bricklayers at the surface laid courses of masonry on a ringshaped wooden base made of acacia, while other men used buckets to excavate silt and water from the bottom of the pit, digging beneath the frame.

<a id="ch02-0028"></a>

“随着它下面的土壤松动，”文献解释说，“又随着它自身的重量加上砌在其上的砖层而增加，它便沉入地下。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-034"></a>[34](#note-ch2-034)当井达到所需深度后，砖块向内砌成拱形，形成一个支撑上方机械的拱顶，屋顶中央留出一个矩形开口，让*saqiya*的竖直轮及其水桶链能够降入其中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-035"></a>[35](#note-ch2-035)这些砖砌水井是景观中的永久特征，尽管除了地表的开口外，大部分都看不见。水车通常每年秋天在洪水到来前拆开，到下一个季节再重新组装。

‘As the soil under it loosens’, the text explains, ‘and as its own weight increases with the brick courses laid upon it, it goes down into the ground.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-034"></a>[34](#note-ch2-034) When the well reached its required depth, the bricks were arched inwards to form a vault to support the machinery above, leaving a rectangular slot at the centre of the roof through which the vertical wheel of the *saqiya* and its chain of buckets could descend.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-035"></a>[35](#note-ch2-035) The brick-built wells were a permanent feature of the landscape, although except for the slot on the surface largely invisible. The waterwheels were typically disassembled each autumn before the flood waters arrived, then reassembled the following season.

<a id="ch02-fig04"></a>



![一幅横剖面图显示萨基亚井，有砖砌井壁、拱顶、环形木基座以及延伸至地面的矩形开口。](images/ufig_4.jpg)

图4　*萨基亚*井横剖面，显示环形木基座、砖墙、拱顶和矩形开口。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-036"></a>[36](#note-ch2-036)







![A cross section shows a saqiya well with brick lined walls, a vaulted roof, an annular wooden base, and a rectangular opening extending to the surface.](images/ufig_4.jpg)

Figure 4. Cross-section of a *saqiya* well, showing annular wooden base, brick walls, vaulted roof, and rectangular opening.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-036"></a>[36](#note-ch2-036)





<a id="ch02-0030"></a>

春夏两季，*saqiya*日夜转动，木制齿轮呻吟、吱呀作响。对任何访客来说，这都是乡村的一种独特声音。1845 年 3 月，按照<a id="page-66"></a>〔原书第66页〕穆罕默德·阿里帕夏的命令，埃及工程师约瑟夫·赫克基扬在一个村庄住了几夜，调查大麻种植。在“埃及村庄夜间最安静地段的噪音与不便”中——这些曾令他十分烦恼——他列出了“沉重水车的吱呀声”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-037"></a>[37](#note-ch2-037)外国访客通常乘船沿河旅行，很少在村庄和田野停留。他们通过乡村的声音景观来领会乡村生活，常常把埃及乡村夏季特有的声音描述为水车哀怨的吱呀声。“沿着这里，也就是阿斯旺下游七八英里的地方，从船上望去看不到任何植被，除了一片片生长茂盛的棕榈树，”最受欢迎的游记之一记载道，“但远处一定有土壤，因为萨基亚水车总在吱呀作响。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-038"></a>[38](#note-ch2-038)这种声音景观的大部分很快就消失了。

As the *saqiya* rotated, day and night through spring and summer, its wooden gear wheels groaned and squeaked. For any visitor, this was a distinctive sound of the countryside. In March 1845, at the order of <a id="page-66-en"></a>〔原书第66页〕Muhammad Ali Pasha, the Egyptian engineer Joseph Hekekyan spent several nights in a village, investigating hemp cultivation. Among ‘the noises and inconveniences of the quietest part of an Egyptian village night’, which had greatly annoyed him, he listed ‘the creaking of the heavy waterwheels’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-037"></a>[37](#note-ch2-037) Foreign visitors usually travelled through the country by boat on the river, seldom spending time in the villages and fields. They apprehended rural life through its soundscape, often describing the characteristic noise of the Egyptian countryside in summer as the doleful squeaking of the waterwheel. ‘Along here, seven or eight miles below Assouan, there is no vegetation in sight from the boat, except strips of thrifty palm-trees,’ recorded one of the most popular accounts, ‘but there must be soil beyond, for the sakiyas are always creaking.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-038"></a>[38](#note-ch2-038) Much of this soundscape was soon to disappear.

<a id="ch02-0031"></a>

根据中世纪农业历书——例如重印在马格里齐《赫塔特》中的那一部——在科普特历第五个月图巴月（1 月 9 日至 2 月 7 日），主要作物成熟时，农民会修复围堤田块中央的水井，然后取出并组装水车。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-039"></a>[39](#note-ch2-039)水井可能有数米深，但在许多情况下，砾石层在洪泛平原边缘——沿河床以及外缘——升得更高。边缘处抬高的地下水位所产生的压力，形成了人工水头，把水推向井口。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-040"></a>[40](#note-ch2-040)马格里齐告诉我们，每口井可灌溉四到六英亩；如果土地就在附近，伊本·马马提的历书具体指出，可多达十英亩。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-041"></a>[41](#note-ch2-041)根据这些历书，井中储水在生长季节逐渐减少，到阿比布月第十五天（7 月 9 日）达到最低水位，届时上涨的尼罗河会开始补给它们。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-042"></a>[42](#note-ch2-042)水井和水车对中世纪农业如此重要，尤其是对大型庄园上种植甘蔗和其他夏季作物而言，以至于文献常常把这类庄园称为“水车”（*sawaqi*）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-043"></a>[43](#note-ch2-043)

According to the medieval agrarian almanacs, such as the one reproduced in the *Khitat* of Maqrizi, in the month of Tuba (9 January to 7 February), the fifth month of the Coptic calendar, as the main crops were maturing, farmers would restore the wells in the middle of the field basins, then bring out and assemble the waterwheels.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-039"></a>[39](#note-ch2-039) While the wells might be several metres deep, in many cases the gravel layer rose higher at the edges of the floodplain, both along the riverbed and at the outer margin.
