The pressure of the raised water table at the edges created an artificial head, forcing the supply up towards the top of the well.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-040"></a>[40](#note-ch2-040) Each well, Maqrizi tells us, could irrigate four to six acres; or up to ten acres, the almanac of Ibn Mammati specifies, if the land was close by.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-041"></a>[41](#note-ch2-041) The wells were gradually depleted during the growing season, reaching their lowest level on the fifteenth day of Abib (9 July), according to the almanacs, at which point the rising Nile would begin to replenish them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-042"></a>[42](#note-ch2-042) The wells and waterwheels were so important to medieval agriculture, especially for producing sugar cane and other summer crops on large estates, that the sources often refer to such estates as ‘waterwheels’ (*sawaqi*).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-043"></a>[43](#note-ch2-043)

<a id="ch02-0032"></a>

二十世纪之交，当欧洲土地投机者发现这些水井时，他们以为压力必定来自深处的地下储层，于是成立了几家自流井公司，投资开发这种新资源。没有发现任何自流泉，这些公司都失败了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-044"></a>[44](#note-ch2-044)灌溉工程师后来承认，水井被洪水补给“令我们惊讶”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-045"></a>[45](#note-ch2-045)他们请来牛津培养的地质学家哈特利·特拉弗斯·费拉尔——斯科特船长首次南极探险的老队员——到埃及调查。他的报告记载，在上埃及卢克索以北约二十五英里的基夫特镇，“可以看到一股洪水<a id="page-67"></a>〔原书第67页〕流入一个萨基亚井坑，却没有抬高其中的水位”。他指出，围堤田块中估计仍有 40,600 台*saqiya*，并补充说，“如果每台在洪水期被淹没的萨基亚水车都发生这种情况，那么通过这种方式进入洪积层的水量必定非常巨大”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-046"></a>[46](#note-ch2-046)

When European land speculators discovered these wells around the turn of the twentieth century, they assumed the pressure must come from reservoirs deep below and set up several artesian water companies to invest in exploiting this new resource. No artesian springs were found and the companies failed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-044"></a>[44](#note-ch2-044) The recharging of the wells by the flood ‘came as a surprise to us’, the irrigation engineers later acknowledged.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-045"></a>[45](#note-ch2-045) They brought to Egypt an Oxford-trained geologist, Hartley Travers Ferrar, a veteran of Captain Scott’s first Antarctic expedition, to investigate. His report recorded that at Qift, a town in Upper Egypt about twenty-five miles north of Luxor, ‘a stream of flood water was seen <a id="page-67-en"></a>〔原书第67页〕flowing into a sakia-pit without raising the level of the water in it’. Noting that there were still an estimated 40,600 *saqiyas* in field basins, he added that ‘if this takes place at every sakia which is submerged during flood time, the quantity of water which passes into the diluvial beds by this means must be very great’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-046"></a>[46](#note-ch2-046)

<a id="ch02-0033"></a>

砾石层延伸到整个洪泛平原之下。然而在洪水较强的年份，这种地下储存还可以由另一种储备来补充：让水积聚在低洼地，包括洪泛平原外缘的土地，甚至周围沙漠中相邻的干谷。低洼、积水的土地排水最慢，因此被种上亚麻——一种偏好较湿土壤的贵重作物，加工成亚麻布后，正如我们将看到的，又提供了另一种储存选择。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-047"></a>[47](#note-ch2-047)或者，低地可以被挖深，形成池塘，储存来年春季和夏季的灌溉水。许多这样的*khaznas*，即蓄水池，在十九世纪仍在使用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-048"></a>[48](#note-ch2-048)事实上，在十九世纪灌溉工程之前，沿着尼罗河洪泛平原的大片地区，这类池塘沿沙漠边缘形成了第二条河道。它们由地下水和多余的洪水补给，并在主要蓄水田区排空时蓄满，这个地表网络补充了水井，成为储存水的来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-049"></a>[49](#note-ch2-049)（事实上，穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者修建的深层“夏季运河”，在某些方面是这一系统的延伸，因为它们不仅由上涨的尼罗河供水，也由地下水渗流供水。）<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-050"></a>[50](#note-ch2-050)在中埃及，一条古老的运河——优素福运河，像大多数古老运河一样，由这些河流次级河道之一形成——让多余的洪水排入一个更大的洼地，即位于开罗以北约五十英里的法尤姆盆地。在古代和中世纪，法尤姆成为该国最富生产力的农业区之一，也是其亚麻工业的中心。管理这些泄洪通道的使用，进一步降低了下游洪水过量的风险。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-051"></a>[51](#note-ch2-051)

The gravel beds extended beneath the entire area of the floodplain. However, in years of stronger floods, this underground storage could be supplemented with another reserve by allowing water to collect in low-lying ground, including land at the outer edges of the floodplain, or even adjacent wadis in the surrounding desert. Being the slowest to drain, low-lying, waterlogged lands were planted with flax, a valuable crop that prefers wetter soil and provides, when processed into linen, as we will see, another storage option.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-047"></a>[47](#note-ch2-047) Or the lowlands could be deepened by excavation to form pools that stored irrigation water for the following spring and summer. Numerous such *khaznas*, or storage ponds, were still in use in the nineteenth century.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-048"></a>[48](#note-ch2-048) In fact, along great stretches of the Nile floodplain, prior to the irrigation works of the nineteenth century, such pools formed a second river channel along the desert edge. Fed from ground water and surplus flood water, and filling as the main catch basins were emptying, this surface network supplemented the wells as a source of stored water.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-049"></a>[49](#note-ch2-049) (In fact, the deep ‘summer canals’ built by Muhammad Ali and his successors were, in some ways, an extension of this system, for they filled not only from the rising Nile but from the seepage of groundwater.)<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-050"></a>[50](#note-ch2-050) In Middle Egypt, an ancient canal, the Bahr Yusif – formed, like most older canals, from one of these secondary channels of the river – allowed surplus flood water to escape to a much larger depression, the Fayyum basin, lying about fifty miles north of Cairo. In the ancient and medieval periods, Fayyum became one of the country’s most productive agricultural regions and a centre of its linen industry. Managing the use of these escapes further reduced the risk of excess floods downstream.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-051"></a>[51](#note-ch2-051)

校注：底本此处写法尤姆位于开罗以北；埃及国家新闻署的法尤姆介绍列其位置为开罗西南。正文方位照录。 https://sis.gov.eg/en/egypt/system-of-government/executive-authority/fayyoum/

<a id="ch02-0034"></a>

水井灌溉的主要作物是*dhurra*，即高粱。这种夏季作物的种植如此广泛，以至于在围堤蓄水农业被消除之前，高粱一直是埃及的主食。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-052"></a>[52](#note-ch2-052)高粱原产于非洲半干旱地区，是一种适应供水不足或不稳定问题的谷物，这正是苏丹地带——尼罗河、尼日尔河和塞内加尔河——大型河流流域数千年来所实行的洪水退去后耕作制的典型特征。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-053"></a>[53](#note-ch2-053)与小麦等谷类相比，它的根要深得多，叶片能够在干旱期间暂停光合作用，<a id="page-68"></a>〔原书第68页〕进入一种类似休眠的状态。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-054"></a>[54](#note-ch2-054)高粱还能耐受积水土壤和洪水，部分原因是它具有中等耐盐性，能够承受过饱和土壤中较高的盐度。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-055"></a>[55](#note-ch2-055)它是一种多用途作物，叶片和茎秆可为牲畜提供饲料，为面包烤炉提供燃料，为住房提供茅草。在洪水小的年份，如果冬季收成不好，农民会利用额外的井灌扩大高粱的夏季种植。为了进一步弥补冬季收成不佳，在第三个生长季，即秋季，种植高粱的面积会“大幅增加”，使小农“能够重新装满谷仓”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-056"></a>[56](#note-ch2-056)穆罕默德·阿里治下对围堤蓄水系统的改良，促进了第三季高粱的种植。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-057"></a>[57](#note-ch2-057)因此，高粱既适应使用地下储水的挑战，也适应供水的变化。与此同时，它又是一种能够弥补这种变化所可能导致之短缺的资源。

The principal crop produced from the well irrigation was *dhurra*, or sorghum. The cultivation of this summer-season crop was so extensive that sorghum served as the staple food of Egypt prior to the elimination of flood-basin agriculture.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-052"></a>[52](#note-ch2-052) Native to the semi-arid regions of Africa, sorghum is a grain adapted to the problems of light or variable water supply, typical of the flood-recession farming practised for millennia in the large river basins of the Sudanic belt – the Nile, Niger, and Senegal rivers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-053"></a>[53](#note-ch2-053) Compared with cereals like wheat, it has much deeper roots, and its leaves are able to suspend photosynthesis during drought, <a id="page-68-en"></a>〔原书第68页〕entering a kind of hibernation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-054"></a>[54](#note-ch2-054) Sorghum also tolerates waterlogged soils and flooding, in part because it is moderately salt-tolerant, withstanding the higher salinity of over-saturated soils.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-055"></a>[55](#note-ch2-055) It is a multipurpose crop, its leaves and stalk supplying forage for livestock, fuel for bread ovens, and thatch for housing. In years of low floods, if the winter harvest was poor, farmers expanded the summer cultivation of sorghum using additional well irrigation. To further compensate for a poor winter harvest, in the third growing season, the autumn, the area planted with sorghum would be ‘very considerably increased’, enabling small farmers ‘to refill their granaries’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-056"></a>[56](#note-ch2-056) The improvements to the basin system under Muhammad Ali facilitated this cultivation of sorghum in the third season.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-057"></a>[57](#note-ch2-057) Thus sorghum was suited to the challenges of using stored subterranean water and to variations in water supply. At the same time, it was a resource that could remedy the shortages to which such variability might lead.

<a id="ch02-0035"></a>

水井还被用来种植小块果园水果和其他有价值的夏季作物，包括靛蓝作物、芝麻、棉花和甘蔗，以及种植富含养分的芋头（*qulqas*）。这是一种根茎类作物，在湿润土壤中生长旺盛，实际上浸在水中长得更好，因此可以留在地里一直到秋季下一季洪水开始上涨之时。芋头被该国奥斯曼—土耳其精英视为美味，每英亩收入是棉花或甘蔗的两倍，生长时间却只有一半。一份资料告诉我们，一个土地很少的大家庭可能靠一英亩芋头生活。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-058"></a>[58](#note-ch2-058)

The wells were also used to cultivate smaller areas of orchard fruits and other valuable summer crops, including indigo, sesame, cotton, and sugar cane, and to grow the nutrient-rich Colocasia (*qulqas*), or taro, a root crop that flourishes in moist soil and in fact grows better when submerged in water, allowing it to remain in the ground even into autumn when the next season’s flood began to rise. Prized as a delicacy by the country’s Ottoman-Turkish elite, taro produced twice the income per acre of cotton or sugar cane in half the growing time. A large household with little land, one source tells us, might live off an acre of taro.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-058"></a>[58](#note-ch2-058)

<a id="ch02-0036"></a>

### 公共储存

### Public Storage

<a id="ch02-0037"></a>

与英国人要用来取代它的河流拦河堰、永久地表水库和所谓常年灌溉系统相比，在地表之下储水有几个优势。第一，旧系统让田地得以被淹没，并沉积富含养分的淤泥。土壤既因淤泥中的硝酸盐、磷酸盐和微量金属而肥沃，也因淹没期间土地被迫休养而肥沃。新的拦河堰和水库将摧毁这一自行运转的泛滥与增肥过程，使全年从运河提水和机械施肥都需要繁重劳动和高昂费用。每一部历史叙述都顺带提到新系统的这一后果和旧系统的优势。更多的好处则很少被提及。

Storing water beneath the surface had several advantages compared to the system of river barrages, permanent surface reservoirs, and so-called perennial irrigation with which the British were to replace it. First, the old system allowed the inundation of the fields and depositing of nutrient-rich sediment. Soils were enriched both by the nitrates, phosphates, and trace metals in the sediment and by the enforced resting of the land during inundation. The new barrages and reservoirs were to destroy this self-moving process of flooding and fertilisation, creating a need for the heavy labour and expense of year-round water lifting from canals and mechanical fertilisation. Every historical account notes in passing this consequence of the new system and the advantage of the old. The further benefits are seldom noted.

<a id="ch02-0038"></a>

<a id="page-69"></a>〔原书第69页〕第二个优势是，这种自然发生的肥力补充在两个方向上横向流动：先是洪水，然后是退水。河流每年的扩张和收缩，使营养物质和生物在河道与洪泛平原之间双向交换，维持着陆地、鸟类和水生生命。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-059"></a>[59](#note-ch2-059)摧毁季节性的“洪水脉冲”——水文学家现在这样称呼它——消除了维系陆地与水中生命繁衍的相互作用，包括鸟类和水禽，以及大量鱼类及其食物来源，它们的筑巢、产卵和迁徙周期依赖于洪水周期及其提供的养分。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-060"></a>[60](#note-ch2-060)洪水退去时，把网放在把水送回河流的渠道口，就能获得丰收。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-061"></a>[61](#note-ch2-061)人们还在田里用手捉鱼，使用芦苇陷阱，或从水排入的水井中捕鱼——这使地下蓄水池发挥了第二种作用，即鱼塘。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-062"></a>[62](#note-ch2-062)据报道，可放在陶罐中储存数月之久的腌鱼，是普通人最常食用的动物性食物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-063"></a>[63](#note-ch2-063)幼鱼还捕食蚊幼虫，防止疟疾传播，而疟疾在更南方的尼罗河流域国家为地方性流行病。

<a id="page-69-en"></a>〔原书第69页〕The second advantage was that this self-moving enrichment flowed laterally in both directions, first the flood and then the ebb. The annual expansion and contraction of the stream allowed the two-way exchange of nutrients and biota between the river channel and the floodplain, sustaining terrestrial, avian, and aquatic life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-059"></a>[59](#note-ch2-059) Destroying the seasonal ‘flood pulse’, as hydrologists now call it, eliminated interactions that reproduced life on both land and water, including birds and waterfowl and an abundance of fish and their food sources, whose cycles of nesting, spawning, and migration depended on the flood cycle and the nutrients it supplied.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-060"></a>[60](#note-ch2-060) When the flood receded, fishing nets placed at the mouth of the channels that carried the waters back to the river yielded an abundant catch.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-061"></a>[61](#note-ch2-061) Fish were also caught by hand in the fields, using reed traps, or from the wells into which the waters drained – allowing the underground cisterns to serve a second role, as fish tanks.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-062"></a>[62](#note-ch2-062) Cured fish, which could be stored in earthenware pots for months, was reportedly the animal food that ordinary people consumed most often.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-063"></a>[63](#note-ch2-063) Young fish also preyed on mosquito larvae, preventing the spread of malaria, which was endemic in Nile Basin countries farther south.

<a id="ch02-0039"></a>

第三，采用底土储水时，储存的水很少因蒸发而损失。在常年灌溉下，大量水从新水库和扩大的河流表面积蒸发。与此同时，每年淹没田地，然后把洪水储存在地表之下，再随着河流回到最低水位而缓慢释放回河道，会自然地排干土地，把有害盐分冲洗到根区以下。河流的涨落还冲洗并晾干了往返田间的支渠，清除了杂草和害虫。使用拦河堰和大坝的常年灌溉把平均河流水位和地下水位抬高了几米，导致土壤积水和日益盐碱化、作物产量下降，并需要大量排水沟和泵。支渠变成了静止的永久沟渠，成了水葫芦的人造避风港——这种浮水植物由欧洲人作为观赏植物引入——它那为抵抗亚马逊河急流而演化出的纤维根垫，开始堵塞下埃及的水道和湖泊（在殖民地印度、美国南部以及后来整个尼罗河流域的主要河流中也是如此），使蒸发造成的水损失翻倍，并杀死其他生命形式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-064"></a>[64](#note-ch2-064)

Third, with subsoil storage, little of the stored water was lost by evaporation. Under perennial irrigation, large volumes of water evaporated from the new reservoirs and from the expanded surface area of the river. At the same time, inundating the fields each year, then storing the flood waters below the surface, from where they were slowly released back into the river channel as it returned to its minimum level, automatically drained the land and flushed harmful salts to below the root zone. The flood and ebb of the river also flushed and dried the branch canals that carried waters to and from the fields, cleaning them of weeds and pests. Perennial irrigation using barrages and dams raised the average river level and water table by several metres, leading to waterlogged and increasingly saline soils, declining crop yields, and the need for extensive drains and pumps. Transformed into still, permanent ditches, the branch canals became a manufactured haven for water hyacinth – the floating plant introduced as an ornamental by Europeans – whose fibrous root mats, developed to resist the fast-flowing rivers of Amazonia, began to clog the waterways and lakes of Lower Egypt (as it did the major rivers of colonial India, the southern United States, and later the entire Nile Basin), doubling the loss of water by evaporation and killing off other forms of life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-064"></a>[64](#note-ch2-064)

<a id="ch02-0040"></a>

第四，永久运河及其河岸也成为携带埃及血吸虫病和钩虫病的螺类和线虫的滋生地。正如珍妮弗·德尔所解释的，这两种<a id="page-70"></a>〔原书第70页〕使人衰弱的寄生虫感染成为埃及乡村的地方病，缓慢地殖民了相当一部分人口的身体。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-065"></a>[65](#note-ch2-065)在新灌溉制度下，这些身体还因日益严重的营养不良而衰弱，特别是糙皮病的传播。运河系统促进了棉花的广泛种植，这又鼓励人们改吃玉米（美洲玉米）；玉米夏季生长期短，与棉花的两年轮作相吻合，其秸秆还可在从南威尔士进口煤炭之外充当燃料，用于蒸汽灌溉泵的锅炉。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-066"></a>[66](#note-ch2-066)大量工人从上埃及种植高粱的地区转移到下三角洲劳动密集的棉花种植园，促成了饮食的这一变化。与其他谷物不同，玉米不提供烟酸（维生素 B3），除非在碱性溶液中煮沸，这正是其原产地墨西哥制作玉米饼粉的方法。糙皮病由缺乏烟酸引起，会造成皮肤和消化系统的疼痛性损伤，以及痴呆，有时甚至死亡。英国人对痴呆率上升感到惊恐。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-067"></a>[67](#note-ch2-067)洪水的消除以及棉花和甘蔗种植的指数级增长，还使其他感染、寄生虫和害虫得以大量繁殖。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-068"></a>[68](#note-ch2-068)老鼠被甘蔗汁吸引，而甘蔗高大的茎秆保护它们免受猛禽捕食，于是大量侵扰甘蔗田。它们啃咬甘蔗基部，可毁掉多达四分之一的收成。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-069"></a>[69](#note-ch2-069)最具破坏性的害虫是棉叶虫——一种蛾（*Spodoptera littoralis*），其幼虫因棉花种植扩大而大量繁殖。如果不逐片摘除受虫害的叶子，它们能毁掉整片棉花田。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-070"></a>[70](#note-ch2-070)

Fourth, the permanent canals and their banks also became breeding grounds for the snails and nematodes that carried bilharzia (schistosomiasis) and hookworm disease. As Jennifer Derr explains, these two <a id="page-70-en"></a>〔原书第70页〕debilitating parasitic infections became endemic to rural Egypt, slowly colonising the bodies of a significant part of the population.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-065"></a>[65](#note-ch2-065) Those bodies were also weakened under the new irrigation regime by increasing malnutrition, in particular the spread of pellagra. The canal system facilitated the widespread cultivation of cotton, which encouraged a switch to the consumption of maize (American corn), whose short summer growing season synchronised with the two-year rotation of cotton, and whose straw supplemented imports of coal from south Wales as fuel for the boilers of the steam-driven irrigation pumps.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-066"></a>[66](#note-ch2-066) A great transfer of workers from the sorghum-growing regions of Upper Egypt to the labour-intensive cotton plantations of the lower Delta contributed to this change in diet. Unlike other grains, maize does not supply niacin (vitamin B3), unless boiled in an alkaline solution, the method used in making tortilla flour in its native Mexico. Caused by lack of niacin, pellagra results in painful damage to the skin and digestive system, and in dementia and sometimes death. The British became alarmed at increasing rates of dementia.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-067"></a>[67](#note-ch2-067) The elimination of the flood and the exponential increase in cotton and cane cultivation also allowed other infections, parasites, and pests to flourish.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-068"></a>[68](#note-ch2-068) Rats, attracted to the juice of sugar cane, whose tall stalks protect them from birds of prey, infested cane fields. By gnawing the base of the canes, they could destroy up to a quarter of the crop.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-069"></a>[69](#note-ch2-069) The most destructive pest was the cotton worm, a moth (*Spodoptera littoralis*) whose larvae thrived on the increased cultivation of cotton. They could destroy entire fields of cotton if not checked by picking off the infected leaves one by one.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-070"></a>[70](#note-ch2-070)

<a id="ch02-0041"></a>

与水库和运河中的新储水方式相比，储存在土壤下的水还有一个优势。与地表水不同，它不受强大的种植园主——他们可能垄断新运河的使用权——以及为他们服务的灌溉工程师的控制。“在这里，我们看到围堤蓄水灌溉达到了最佳状态，”一份对索哈杰省的调查指出；这个南部地区尚未遭受邻省那种破坏性工程，尤其是更北边建立的大片甘蔗种植园。“土地肥沃，作物繁茂，人民富裕而独立，底土水得到充分利用。”这些农民享有显著的独立与繁荣：“没有任何工程师能够截断他们的洪水，而水位便于利用的充沛地下水则是他们自己的财产。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-071"></a>[71](#note-ch2-071)

Water stored beneath the soil had one further advantage over the new storage in reservoirs and canals. Unlike water held on the surface, it was beyond the control of powerful plantation owners, who might monopolise access to the new canals, and of the irrigation engineers who served their needs. ‘Here we see basin irrigation at its best’, noted a survey of the province of Sohaj, a region in the south that had not yet suffered the damaging engineering work of neighbouring provinces, in particular the extensive sugar plantations created further north. ‘The land is rich, the crops luxuriant, the people well off and independent, and the subsoil water well utilised.’ Farmers ‘whose flood waters no engineer can cut off, and whose plentiful subsoil water at a convenient level is their own property’, enjoyed a notable independence and prosperity.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-071"></a>[71](#note-ch2-071)

<a id="ch02-0042"></a>

水车本身是人、动物、土壤和作物之间复杂互动的焦点。它们通常由牛拉动，牛的饲料——主要是埃及三叶草——可以种在<a id="page-71"></a>〔原书第71页〕同一片田里，一次种植可收割三次以上，还能改善土壤。牛会繁殖自己的后代，从而延续这个国家的主要动力来源。正如在大多数农业社会（包括欧洲的农业社会）中一样，饲养它们是储存和增加家庭财富的主要手段（英语中 cattle 一词源自 chattel 或 capital，意为“存货”；其含义到十六世纪才收窄为*活*畜）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-072"></a>[72](#note-ch2-072)用牛作为灌溉劳力，使公犊有了价值；后来用机械泵取代它们，使公犊在很大程度上变得无用，迫使它们被宰杀作肉食，并导致以肉为基础的饮食增加。牛粪被做成扁饼，在阳光下晒干，储存在屋顶上，用作烘焙和烹饪的燃料。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-073"></a>[73](#note-ch2-073)水井对国家的丝绸生产也变得重要。埃及以前依赖进口丝线，在十九世纪之交发展了自己的养蚕业。到 1820 年代，提供蚕蛾幼虫食物的桑树数量估计达到三百万棵。蚕蛾是一种家养昆虫（事实上是除蜜蜂之外唯一被家养的昆虫），它产下的卵需要凉爽处孵化，因此被储存在灌溉井中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-074"></a>[74](#note-ch2-074)

The waterwheels themselves were the focus of a complex interaction among humans, animals, soils, and crops. They were usually turned by oxen, whose fodder – mostly Egyptian clover – could be grown in the <a id="page-71-en"></a>〔原书第71页〕same fields, supplying three or more cuttings from a single planting and improving the soil. Cattle produced their own young, thus reproducing the country’s main source of motive power. As in most agrarian societies, including those of Europe, rearing them was a principal means of storing and increasing household wealth (in English, the word cattle derives from chattel or capital, meaning stock; its sense narrowed to *live*stock only in the sixteenth century).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-072"></a>[72](#note-ch2-072) Using oxen as irrigation labour gave value to male calves; their replacement with mechanical pumps would later render the males largely useless, forcing their slaughter for meat and an increase in meat-based diets. Cattle dung, formed into flat cakes, dried in the sun, and stored on rooftops, provided fuel for baking and cooking.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-073"></a>[73](#note-ch2-073) The wells also became important to the country’s silk production. Previously reliant on imported thread, Egypt developed a domestic silkworm industry at the turn of the nineteenth century. By the 1820s, the number of mulberry trees, whose leaves provide the food for the larvae of the silk moth, reached an estimated three million. The silk moth, a domesticated insect (the only one, in fact, besides the honeybee), produces eggs that require a cool place to incubate; they were therefore stored in the irrigation wells.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-074"></a>[74](#note-ch2-074)

<a id="ch02-0043"></a>

建造一口井需要砖匠制作烧砖，也需要砌砖工施工。水井机械需要木匠制造水轮，并每季拆装，这维持了村庄中最大的非农业生计。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-075"></a>[75](#note-ch2-075)为了转动机械，最多有八头牛轮班工作，因此通常会有多户人家共用一台水轮，通过一个浅田沟网络把水分配给各个地块。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-076"></a>[76](#note-ch2-076)这种合作使水轮日夜转动，也包括挖掘和维护沟渠、种植供养人和动物的作物等劳动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-077"></a>[77](#note-ch2-077)合作并不意味着和谐或没有强制；与任何共同体一样，家庭内部和家庭之间的等级关系会塑造任务的分配。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-078"></a>[78](#note-ch2-078)二十世纪的记述把这种合作安排的残存实例称为“*saqiya*合作圈”。农民往往通过亲属关系联系在一起，每人提供自己的役畜，有时参加不止一个合作圈。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-079"></a>[79](#note-ch2-079)在苏丹北部和努比亚，上涨的尼罗河通常留在河道内，很少淹没更广阔的洪泛平原，因此使用*saqiya*如此普遍，以至于这个词被用来指村庄本身，即围绕水车合作形成的共同体。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-080"></a>[80](#note-ch2-080)在上埃及，主要的夏收节不是在收割高粱时庆祝，而是在<a id="page-72"></a>〔原书第72页〕*saqiya*完成对作物的第十次、也是最后一次灌溉时庆祝。人们把*kunafa*或其他甜食带到田里的水车旁分享，然后把吃空的盘子装满高粱穗送回；主人会再割下四穗，系在转动水轮的两头牛额头上，然后心怀感激与喜悦地把它们赶回家。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-081"></a>[81](#note-ch2-081)

Building a well required brickmakers to make fired bricks and bricklayers to construct it. The well machinery needed carpenters to fabricate the wheel and assemble and disassemble it each season, sustaining the largest non-farming livelihood in the villages.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-075"></a>[75](#note-ch2-075) To turn the machine, up to eight oxen worked in shifts, so a number of houses would typically share in each wheel, which distributed the water to individual plots via a network of shallow field ditches.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-076"></a>[76](#note-ch2-076) The collaboration kept the wheel turning day and night, and included the labour of those who dug and maintained the ditches and grew the crops that fed humans and animals alike.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-077"></a>[77](#note-ch2-077) Collaboration does not imply harmony or the absence of compulsion; as in any community, hierarchies within and among households would shape the allocation of tasks.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-078"></a>[78](#note-ch2-078) Twentieth-century accounts describe surviving instances of this cooperative arrangement as a ‘*saqiya* ring’. Often linked by kinship, the farmers each provided their own draft animal, sometimes participating in more than one ring.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-079"></a>[79](#note-ch2-079) In northern Sudan and Nubia, where the rising Nile usually remained within its channel and seldom inundated the wider floodplain, using the *saqiya* was so universal that the word came to refer to the village itself, a community formed through the collaboration around the wheel.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-080"></a>[80](#note-ch2-080) In Upper Egypt, the main summer harvest feast was celebrated not when the sorghum was cut but when the <a id="page-72-en"></a>〔原书第72页〕*saqiya* completed the tenth and final watering of the crop. After sharing *kunafa* or other sweetmeats brought out to the waterwheel in the field, then returning the empty plates piled with heads of sorghum, the owner would cut four more heads and fasten them to the foreheads of the two oxen that had turned the wheel, before driving them home in gratitude and celebration.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-081"></a>[81](#note-ch2-081)

<a id="ch02-0044"></a>

在那些由包税人或其他收入权利持有者索取一部分收成的土地上——这种安排在个人土地所有权于十九世纪后期重新出现之前，广泛用于马穆鲁克和奥斯曼时期——围绕水车的合作会包括所谓的“协助”（*‘auna*），即强制性劳动，为主张这些权利的人经营水井。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-082"></a>[82](#note-ch2-082)在前现代时期，萨基亚水车系统的周期性扩张可能与甘蔗种植园的发展有关，这些种植园需要在更大规模上使用人力和畜力的强制劳动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-083"></a>[83](#note-ch2-083)从 1820 年代起，随着开罗政权开始重新殖民该国南部，发给负责建立大型农业庄园的官员的首批命令就是取得牛只并“架设水车”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-084"></a>[84](#note-ch2-084)到该世纪后期，尤其在 1863—4 年大牛瘟之后，统治家族和其他大庄园主开始用英国制造的蒸汽泵取代*saqiyas*；这些泵最初太重，无法在年度泛滥前拆卸移走，但又足够坚固，能在“每次洪水时被完全淹没”后幸存。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-085"></a>[85](#note-ch2-085)工程师随后改装了*locomobile*——一种蒸汽动力犁——作为移动泵，在洪水退去后可以推到田间架在水井上。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-086"></a>[86](#note-ch2-086)与此同时，大多数农民继续依赖*saqiya*，不过在二十世纪，他们逐渐先用柴油泵、后用小型电动泵取代了它（如今可以用太阳能供电）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-087"></a>[87](#note-ch2-087)然而，这些提水装置的使用越来越局限于从新灌溉运河中提水。水如今被远程储存在上游拦河堰和大坝之后，尤其是在阿斯旺大坝于 1912 年和 1933 年两次加高、1937 年在喀土穆上游白尼罗河的杰贝勒奥利亚修建第二座大坝之后；1960 年代建成规模大得多的阿斯旺高坝，以及 2020 年埃塞俄比亚在青尼罗河上建成第二座巨型拦河坝——埃塞俄比亚复兴大坝之后，这种情况更加明显。随着尼罗河洪水及其益处被消除，灌溉水如今可以全年从运河抽水获得，地下蓄水系统在很大程度上被废弃了。

On lands where a share of the produce was claimed by a tax farmer or other holder of rights to revenue, an arrangement widely used in the Mamluk and Ottoman periods, prior to the re-emergence of individual proprietorship in the late nineteenth century, the collaboration around the waterwheel would include the ‘assistance’ (*‘auna*), meaning obligatory labour, required to run the wells of the person claiming those rights.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-082"></a>[82](#note-ch2-082) The periodic expansion of the *saqiya* system in pre-modern times may have been associated with the development of sugar plantations, requiring compulsory labour, both human and animal, on a larger scale.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-083"></a>[83](#note-ch2-083) From the 1820s, as the regime in Cairo began to recolonise the south of the country, the first orders to officials creating large agricultural estates were to secure cattle and ‘erect waterwheels’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-084"></a>[84](#note-ch2-084) Later in the century, especially after the great cattle plague of 1863–4, the ruling household and other owners of large estates began to replace *saqiyas* with British-built steam pumps, which initially were too heavy to disassemble and remove before the annual inundation but were robust enough to survive being ‘completely buried under water every flood’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-085"></a>[85](#note-ch2-085) Engineers then adapted the locomobile, a steam-powered plough, to serve as a mobile pump that could be wheeled into the fields and placed over wells when the flood receded.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-086"></a>[86](#note-ch2-086) Meanwhile, most farmers continued to rely on *saqiyas*, although, in the twentieth century, they gradually replaced them first with diesel pumps and later with small electric pumps (which today can be solar-powered).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-087"></a>[87](#note-ch2-087) However, their use was increasingly restricted to lifting water from the new irrigation canals. The water was now stored remotely, behind barrages and large dams upstream, especially after the height of the Aswan Dam was raised, in 1912 and again in 1933, and a second dam was built in 1937, at Gebel Aulia, on the White Nile just above Khartoum, and more so after the completion of a much larger structure, the Aswan High Dam, in the 1960s, and of a second giant barrage, the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia, in 2020. With the elimination of the Nile flood and its benefits and with irrigation water now available by pumping it year-round from canals, the subterranean storage system was largely abandoned.

校注：底本将埃塞俄比亚复兴大坝的建成与2020年相联系。美国地质调查局的卫星观测说明记载，2020年夏开始的是水库第一阶段蓄水；蓄水开始不等于大坝全面建成。正文保留原作年代及措辞。 https://eros.usgs.gov/earthshots/grand-ethiopian-renaissance-dam-ethiopia

<a id="ch02-0045"></a>

<a id="page-73"></a>〔原书第73页〕

<a id="page-73-en"></a>〔原书第73页〕

<a id="ch02-0046"></a>

### 让萨基亚水车沉默

### Silencing the Saqiya

<a id="ch02-0047"></a>

水车和水井已经消失。它们既从河流的使用方式中被消除，也从埃及殖民过程的描述中被消除。它们从河流历史中消失，可以为我们提供线索，说明它们为何从景观中被移除。随着它们一起从视野中消失的，是河流本身的生态、储存的经济，以及它们所促成的生活方式。这促使我们提出刚刚那个问题：水车会吱呀作响吗？如果我们永远无法充分还原殖民主义所沉默的庶民声音，那么还有其他沉默、其他声音和其他能动性——人类的与非人类的——同样难以恢复，但关于攫取装置的叙述仍然可以尝试承认它们。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-088"></a>[88](#note-ch2-088)

The waterwheel and the well have disappeared. They have been eliminated both from the way the river is used and the way the colonising of Egypt is described. Their elimination from the history of the river can offer us clues as to why they were removed from the landscape. With them have vanished from sight the very ecology of the river and the economy of storage and modes of life they enabled. This motivates the question we have just posed: Can the waterwheel squeak? If we can never adequately recapture the subaltern voices that colonialism silences, there are other silences, other sounds, and other agencies, human and nonhuman, that are equally difficult to recover, but that an account of apparatuses of capture can nevertheless try to acknowledge.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-088"></a>[88](#note-ch2-088)

<a id="ch02-0048"></a>

*saqiya*消失有三个原因。每一个原因都告诉我们一些关于剩余如何被攫取、以及这种攫取如何被重组的情况。第一，关于欧洲殖民之前尼罗河历史的最佳叙述，大多基于关注某种特定河流治理方式的资料。它们的焦点是实施权威和抽取收入的大型工程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-089"></a>[89](#note-ch2-089)一个主要来源是一份名为*al-Jusur al-sultaniyya*（苏丹堤堰登记册）的政府登记簿。奥斯曼人在十六世纪征服埃及后编纂了这份登记簿，它以更早的记录为基础，是一部描述管理河流流量的地表渠道的汇编。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-090"></a>[90](#note-ch2-090)*jusur*一词指堤岸或土堤，其维护确保洪水被妥善控制，既包括河岸，也包括把河水送往围堤田块和泄洪道的运河。这些登记簿在十九世纪后期仍然可用，当时它们似乎是该国灌溉网络最全面记述的来源，即阿里帕夏·穆巴拉克的《赫塔特》。穆巴拉克是一位主要工程师和公职人员，他把该著作的第 18、19 卷用于逐村描述灌溉基础设施。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-091"></a>[91](#note-ch2-091)

There are three reasons for the disappearance of the *saqiya*. Each tells us something about the way surplus was captured and how its capturing was to be reorganised. First, the best accounts of the history of the Nile prior to European colonisation are based largely upon sources that were concerned with a specific mode of governing the river. Their focus is the large-scale works through which authority was exercised and revenue extracted.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-089"></a>[89](#note-ch2-089) A principal source is a government register known as *al-Jusur al-sultaniyya*. Compiled by the Ottomans after they conquered Egypt in the sixteenth century, and based on older records, the register is a compendium describing the channels on the surface through which the flow of the river was managed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-090"></a>[90](#note-ch2-090) The term *jusur* refers to the embankments or dykes whose upkeep ensured that the flood waters were properly contained, encompassing both the banks of the river and the canals that carried its water to field basins and escapes. The registers were still available in the late nineteenth century, when they appear to have been a source for the most comprehensive account of the country’s irrigation network, Ali Pasha Mubarak’s *Khitat*. A leading engineer and public official, Mubarak devoted volumes 18 and 19 of that work to describing village by village the infrastructure of irrigation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-091"></a>[91](#note-ch2-091)

<a id="ch02-0049"></a>

直接或间接利用这些登记簿来描述灌溉系统的著作，只是偶尔提到水井和操作水井的*saqiyas*。人们可以为此提出一个直接的理由。作为大型基础设施，运河和堤岸要求并促成了更广泛的权威结构的发展，这反映在登记簿的维护上。而水车和水井是分散的本地设备，并未产生这种效果。水车是一种临时装置，<a id="page-74"></a>〔原书第74页〕每季组装和拆卸，由家庭拥有和维护，不为建立政府的权力或主张提供基础设施。因此，它们没有被“登记”。

Writings that draw on these registers, directly or indirectly, to describe the irrigation system make only occasional mention of wells and the *saqiyas* that worked them. One could suggest a straightforward reason for this. As large-scale infrastructures, the canals and embankments required and enabled the development of a wider structure of authority, reflected in the maintaining of registers. As discrete, local equipment, the waterwheels and wells did not. A temporary apparatus <a id="page-74-en"></a>〔原书第74页〕assembled and disassembled each season, owned and maintained by households, the waterwheel provided no infrastructure for building the powers or claims of government. They were not, therefore, ‘registered’.

<a id="ch02-0050"></a>

技术装置与权威行使之间的同样关系，也见于尼罗河历史的第二个主要来源——法律制度的记录。法庭处理的案件中，陌生人之间的纠纷占了不成比例的高份额；它们或许更关注同样的大型基础设施所产生的问题。运河以水车所没有的方式制造冲突，因为它们穿越多处地产和社区，容易受到阻断和争议。驱动水轮的牛可能在陌生人之间交易，或挣脱束缚损坏他人财产，因此，如果*saqiya*出现在文献中，往往与动物纠纷有关。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-092"></a>[92](#note-ch2-092)法律制度围绕这些问题扩展，而这些问题正是书写河流历史的主要题材。

The same relation between a technical apparatus and the exercise of authority is seen in a second major source for histories of the Nile, the records of the legal system. Court cases dealt disproportionately with disputes among strangers; they were perhaps more concerned with the problems produced by the same large-scale infrastructure. Canals created conflict in ways that waterwheels did not, for they traversed multiple properties and communities and were easily subject to interruption and dispute. The oxen that drove the wheels might be traded among strangers, or break loose and damage another property, so, if the *saqiya* appears in the sources, it is often in relation to disputes over animals.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-092"></a>[92](#note-ch2-092) The legal system expanded around such issues, and these were the main topics around which the history of the river could be written.

<a id="ch02-0051"></a>

相比之下，反映社区内部纠纷解决的资料，例如地方法学家（*muftis*，穆夫提）用来不诉诸法院而解决冲突的法律手册，可以更多地揭示*saqiya*的社会世界。“如果一个人借用他人的牛来配自己的*saqiya*使用，而牛掉进井里，”一部最广泛使用的手册解释说，“那么他应承担责任。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-093"></a>[93](#note-ch2-093)用运河和水库系统取代*saqiya*，与地方法学意见被法院系统和政府登记簿体系取代是同步发生的；扩展的基础设施促成并依赖后者。换言之，水轮在历史资料中的出现或缺失，可能不仅反映不同的灌溉手段，也反映正义与权力形式的扩张或消退。

By contrast, sources that reflect the resolution of disputes within the community, such as the legal manuals used by local jurists (*muftis*) to settle conflicts without resort to the court system, can reveal more about the social world of the *saqiya*. ‘If a person borrows another’s ox to use with his *saqiya* and it falls into the well’, one of the most widely used manuals explains, ‘then he is liable for it’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-093"></a>[93](#note-ch2-093) The replacement of the *saqiya* by a system of canals and reservoirs went hand in hand with the displacement of local juridical opinion by the system of courts and government registers that an expanded infrastructure enabled and depended upon. In other words, the presence or absence of the water-wheel in historical sources may reflect not just alternative means of irrigation but expanding or receding forms of justice and power.

<a id="ch02-0052"></a>

*saqiya*的消失，还因为许多现代论述依赖欧洲资料，尤其是那些在穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者治下帮助发展尼罗河灌溉工程的法国工程师。工程师的关注点——被后来历史学家复制——是那些工程。许多当代学者依赖罗杰·欧文的经典叙述，而欧文依赖让·马聚埃尔 1937 年的著作，马聚埃尔又借鉴利南·德·贝勒丰 1874 年的研究，据此提出下埃及只有大约八分之一的农田用于种植夏季作物，上埃及更少。这个数字是那个错误观念的主要来源：全国大部分土地每年只生产一季作物。但利南只提到由新夏季运河供水的面积。他指出，有权势的地主垄断了运河，而普通农民，<a id="page-75"></a>〔原书第75页〕“那些挖了运河的人，却不得不用井水供应夏季种植园，靠萨基亚水车提水”。他表示，*saqiyas*灌溉的面积要大得多——但没有记录在夏季种植面积的估算中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-094"></a>[94](#note-ch2-094)

The disappearance of the *saqiya* was further caused by the reliance of many modern accounts on European sources, especially the French engineers who helped develop Nile irrigation works under Muhammad Ali and his successors. The focus of the engineers, reproduced by more recent historians, was those schemes. Many contemporary scholars depend on the classic account by Roger Owen, who relies on Jean Mazuel’s work of 1937, who drew on Linant de Bellefonds’s 1874 study, to suggest that only about an eighth of the agricultural land in Lower Egypt was used to grow summer crops, and even less in Upper Egypt. This figure was a principal source for the erroneous idea that most of the country’s land produced only a single crop each year. But Linant was referring only to the area fed by the new summer canals. He noted that powerful proprietors monopolised the canals, while ordinary farmers, <a id="page-75-en"></a>〔原书第75页〕‘who have dug the canals, are obliged to supply their summer plantations with water from wells, raised by means of sakiehs’. The *saqiyas*, he indicated, irrigated a far larger area – but were not recorded in the estimates of land devoted to summer cultivation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-094"></a>[94](#note-ch2-094)

校注：底本正文记利南著作为1874年，原注94记1872—1873年；法国国家劳动世界档案馆书目列出版年为1872—1873。原注48的Louis与原注94的Maurice均为书目所列全名Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds的一部分。原文各处写法照录。 https://pmb.culture.fr/opac_anmt/index.php?id=19106&lvl=author_see

<a id="ch02-0053"></a>

然而，水井灌溉系统消失的主要原因是英国人努力消除它，既从河流的管理方式中，也从其历史的书写方式中消除。英国占领后被迫靠边的埃及工程师了解大型夏季运河的有害影响，尤其是 1870 年代为该国统治者赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔的甘蔗种植园而建的易卜拉希米亚运河；他们主张保留围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉系统。工程师阿里·穆巴拉克在赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔最后一届政府中担任公共工程大臣（1878—9），就在英国和法国施压奥斯曼苏丹解除赫迪夫职务之前。1879 年，穆巴拉克在离任期间出版了一本关于尼罗河管理的书，*Nukhbat al-fikr fi tadbir nil Misr*（《尼罗河治理精要》），提出了一系列建议，以改善现有的混合种植制度和以河谷为基础（而非完全以河流为基础）的蓄水：延长水在围堤田块中的储存时间，并更缓慢地排放；在侧谷和洼地建设额外储水；增加小型拦河堰，以提高三角洲部分地区的河流水位。他反对扩大棉花和甘蔗种植，部分原因是种植这些作物在犁地、播种、田间管理和收获，以及挖掘和清理夏季灌溉运河方面需要大量强制劳动。他编制数字表格，表明埃及在 1800 年围堤蓄水农业下种植的粮食和纤维作物组合，比 1860 年代广泛种植的棉花和甘蔗更有价值。他还主张，更丰富的作物多样性支持畜牧业，以及一系列以羊毛、亚麻和其他纤维加工为基础的本地工业。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-095"></a>[95](#note-ch2-095)

The main reason for the disappearance of the system of well irrigation, however, is that the British worked to eliminate it, both from how the river was managed and how its history was written. Egyptian engineers, forced aside after the British occupation, and aware of the deleterious effects of the large summer canals, especially the Ibrahimiya Canal built in the 1870s to serve the sugar plantations of Khedive Isma‘il, the country’s ruler, had argued in favour of retaining the system of catch basins and well irrigation. The engineer Ali Mubarak served as Minister of Public Works in Khedive Isma‘il’s final government in 1878–9, just before Britain and France pressured the Ottoman sultan to remove the Khedive from power. In 1879, while out of office, Mubarak published a book on the management of the Nile, *Nukhbat al-fikr fi tadbir nil Misr*, which made a series of proposals for improving the existing mixed-crop system and valley-based (rather than exclusively river-based) water storage: increasing the length of time water was stored in field basins, and releasing it more slowly; building additional storage in side valleys and depressions; and adding small barrages to raise the level of the river in parts of the Delta. He opposed the increased cultivation of cotton and sugar cane, in part because of the quantity of forced labour they required for ploughing, planting, tending, and harvesting and for digging and clearing the summer irrigation canals. He produced tables of figures to demonstrate that the mix of food and fibre crops Egypt cultivated under flood-basin farming in 1800 was more valuable than the extensively grown cotton and cane of the 1860s. He also argued that the greater diversity of crops supported animal husbandry and a range of local industries based on the processing of wool, flax, and other fibres.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-095"></a>[95](#note-ch2-095)

<a id="ch02-0054"></a>

英国官员不得不努力贬低这些观点，尤其因为这些观点起初得到最有见识的殖民灌溉专家威廉·威尔科克斯本人的支持。威尔科克斯后来成为埃及政府的蓄水系统主管和第一座阿斯旺大坝的设计者，也是《埃及灌溉》的作者；这部综合性研究在 1913 年出版、长达 900 页的第三版，是后来这一领域每一位历史学家所依赖的。然而，在该报告 1889 年出版、仅 350 页的第一版中，即英国<a id="page-76"></a>〔原书第76页〕占领仅七年之后，威尔科克斯主张保留甚至重新扩大围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉系统。他收集的数据表明，围堤蓄水系统比把土地改为运河灌溉更具生产力和利润，部分原因是“在围堤田区中种植一英亩作物的成本微不足道”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-096"></a>[96](#note-ch2-096)虽然三角洲拦河堰的完工使低洼土地能够通过永久运河灌溉，但即使在下埃及，“在 8 米等高线以上（海拔），水井被大量用于灌溉”，而在上埃及的围堤田区中，“到处都挖井进行夏季灌溉”，从而实现第二、第三个生长季。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-097"></a>[97](#note-ch2-097)英国占领后出版的其他记述也提出了类似论点。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-098"></a>[98](#note-ch2-098)与阿里·穆巴拉克一样，威尔科克斯和其他工程师更倾向于把多余的洪水储存在河谷一侧的泄水区，而不是在河流本身筑坝，并希望有一天，当人们对新运河系统和拦河堰的后果“感到绝望”时，三角洲能恢复整个南部仍在使用的泛滥过程，重新引入“旧的健康制度：土地每年由尼罗河本身冲洗、熟化和施钙，无需任何其他媒介”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-099"></a>[99](#note-ch2-099)

British officials had to work hard to discredit these views, especially when they were supported at first by the most knowledgeable of the colonial irrigation experts, William Willcocks himself. The man who would become director of reservoirs in the Egyptian government and the architect of the first Aswan Dam, Willcocks was the author of *Egyptian Irrigation*, a compendious study on whose third edition, published in 1913 and 900 pages long, every later historian in this area relies. In the first edition of that report, however, only 350 pages in length and published in 1889, just seven years after the British <a id="page-76-en"></a>〔原书第76页〕occupation, Willcocks argued for retaining and even re-expanding the system of catch basins and irrigation from wells. He compiled figures showing that the flood-basin system was more productive and profitable than converting land to canal irrigation, in part because ‘the cost of raising crops on an acre of land in the basins is insignificant’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-096"></a>[96](#note-ch2-096) While completing the Delta Barrage had allowed the irrigation of lower-lying lands by permanent canals, it was still the case even in Lower Egypt that ‘above an 8-meter contour [above sea level], wells are freely used for irrigation’, while in the basins of Upper Egypt ‘wells are dug everywhere for summer irrigation’, allowing a second and third growing season.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-097"></a>[97](#note-ch2-097) Other accounts published after the British occupation made similar arguments.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-098"></a>[98](#note-ch2-098) Like Ali Mubarak, Willcocks and other engineers preferred schemes for storing surplus flood waters in escapes at the side of the valley, rather than the damming of the river itself, and hoped that one day, when people were ‘in despair’ at the consequences of the new canal system and barrages, the Delta would be restored to the process of inundation still used throughout the south, reintroducing ‘the old healthy system, by which the land is washed, matured, and limed annually by the Nile itself without any other agency’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-099"></a>[99](#note-ch2-099)

<a id="ch02-0055"></a>

*Egyptian Irrigation*在伦敦和纽约两地出版，部分面向“有意投资土地开垦计划的人”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-100"></a>[100](#note-ch2-100)然而，威尔科克斯的上司贾斯廷·罗斯中校在第一版中加上了自己的导言，说作者支持围堤蓄水田区和水井灌溉的论点是错误的。罗斯是英国带到埃及的八名在印度受训的灌溉工程师之一（威尔科克斯也在其中），不久前被提升为灌溉总监，地位超过威尔科克斯。他上任后的最初行动之一，就是改写威尔科克斯的计算，声称水井灌溉只允许在 10% 的土地上种植夏季高粱。其余 90% 在夏季将闲置，“因为劳动力稀缺”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-101"></a>[101](#note-ch2-101)这一计算使旧制度显得生产力较低。且不说蒸汽泵可以取代人力和畜力在围堤蓄水田区提井水——这一发展已在进行中——劳动力稀缺有两个原因，其中之一我们将在下文讨论。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-102"></a>[102](#note-ch2-102)但正如威尔科克斯本人所解释的，直接原因是南部村庄的男丁被抽空，为北方提供劳动力，去挖掘和维护棉花种植如今所依赖的运河系统；他们要么被强制劳动驱使，要么按合同受雇，工资由公共资金支付。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-103"></a>[103](#note-ch2-103)换言之，<a id="page-77"></a>〔原书第77页〕使北方新运河系统如此昂贵的非凡劳动力需求，被反常地用来使*saqiya*系统显得不切实际。

*Egyptian Irrigation* was published in New York as well as London, intended in part for ‘persons desirous of investing money in land reclamation schemes’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-100"></a>[100](#note-ch2-100) However, Willcocks’s superior, Lieutenant Colonel Justin Ross, added his own introduction to the first edition, saying that the author’s argument in favour of flood basins and well irrigation was wrong. One of eight Indian-trained irrigation engineers, including Willcocks, whom the British had brought to Egypt, Ross had recently been promoted over him as inspector general of irrigation. In one of his first acts on becoming his supervisor, he reworked Willcocks’s calculations to claim that well irrigation allowed the summer sorghum crop to be grown on only 10 per cent of the land. The other 90 per cent would be unused in summer, ‘owing to the scarcity of labour’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-101"></a>[101](#note-ch2-101) This calculation made the old system appear less productive. Leaving aside the fact that steam pumps could replace human and animal labour to lift well water in flood basins, a development already under way, labour was scarce for two reasons, one of which we will come to below.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-102"></a>[102](#note-ch2-102) But the immediate cause, as Willcocks himself explained, was the emptying of men from villages in the south to provide labour in the north, to excavate and maintain the system of canals on which cotton cultivation now depended, driven there by the imposition of forced labour or hired on contracts paid from public funds.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-103"></a>[103](#note-ch2-103) In other words, the <a id="page-77-en"></a>〔原书第77页〕extraordinary need for labour that made the new canal system in the north so expensive was used perversely to make the *saqiya* system appear impractical.

<a id="ch02-0056"></a>

四年后，在苏格兰地理学会的一次演讲中，罗斯承认水井灌溉是合适的，但只适合小耕作者：“要引入甘蔗、棉花或水稻等夏季作物，”他承认，“我们首先只需挖井，用机器把水提上来。”然而他坚持认为，这种方法“适合拥有小块土地、以自给自足方式生活的耕作者。它不经济，也不能以最少劳动获得最大产量。”他或许是在暗指苏丹——如前所述，那里水车仍被广泛使用，马赫迪国家曾击败埃及占领——补充说：“对于半野蛮国家，容易因战争和半野蛮敌人的入侵而动荡，这种方法极好。”他甚至承认：“上埃及仍有许多地区以这种方式耕作，井水实际上取之不尽，因为即使在夏季，尼罗河水面距地表也从不超过 35 英尺。”然而，他认为，要大规模进行夏季种植，必须用由地表运河和蒸汽泵组成的系统取代地下水的使用。

Four years later, in a lecture to the Scottish Geographical Society, Ross conceded that irrigation using wells was suitable, but only for small cultivators: ‘To introduce summer crops, such as sugar, cotton, or rice,’ he acknowledged, ‘we have only, in the first instance, to dig wells and lift up the water by machines.’ He insisted, however, that this method ‘is suitable to cultivators who have small holdings, and who live in a self-supporting fashion. It is not economical, nor is there a maximum of produce for a minimum of labour expended.’ Alluding, perhaps, to Sudan, where waterwheels (as noted) were still widely used and the Mahdist state had defeated the Egyptian occupation, he added, ‘For semi-barbaric countries, liable to be upset by war and incursions of semi-savage enemies, it is excellent.’ He even admitted that ‘There are still many tracts of Upper Egypt cultivated thus, and the well-water is practically inexhaustible, as the Nile-water is never more than 35 feet below the surface even in summer.’ However, for summer cultivation on a large scale, he argued, the use of groundwater must be replaced by a system of surface canals and steam pumps.

<a id="ch02-0057"></a>

> 我们必须把尼罗河水引到地表，办法要么是修建运河，要么是在尼罗河上游很远的地方开凿一条坡度平缓的引水渠，要么用蒸汽动力把水抽到田地高度或抽入一条大运河，要么在尼罗河中筑坝，抬高其夏季水位，使开挖运河的成本不至于过高。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-104"></a>[104](#note-ch2-104)

> We must bring the water of the Nile to the surface, either by a canal or a low-grade slope taking off far up the Nile, or by pumping water by steam power up to the field level or into a large canal, or we must make a dam in the Nile to raise its summer level, so that the cost of excavating the canal may not be excessive.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-104"></a>[104](#note-ch2-104)

<a id="ch02-0058"></a>

《埃及灌溉》后来的版本降低了对*saqiya*系统的强调，把关于水井使用的论述主要限制在“埃及土壤”的初步观察中。当报告转入灌溉的详细讨论时，焦点是洪水控制以及运河和拦河堰的建设。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-105"></a>[105](#note-ch2-105)到 1908 年，福阿登和弗莱彻的《埃及农业教科书》——由教育部在国立大学创立之年在开罗出版——直截了当地指出：“在围堤蓄水制度下，只能种植冬季作物……在收获与洪水之间没有农活可做。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-106"></a>[106](#note-ch2-106)使用地下水的井灌系统被弄得不可见。埃及的农业史和经济史如今可以书写了，只是缺少了一半图景。

The later editions of *Egyptian Irrigation* reduced the emphasis on the *saqiya* system, confining remarks on the use of wells mainly to preliminary observations on ‘The Soil of Egypt’. When the report moved on to the detailed discussion of irrigation, the focus was on flood control and the construction of canals and barrages.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-105"></a>[105](#note-ch2-105) By 1908, Foaden and Fletcher’s *Text-Book of Egyptian Agriculture*, published in Cairo by the Ministry of Education in the year of the founding of a national university, stated flatly that ‘under the basin system, only winter crops can be grown . . . There is no agricultural work to be done between harvest and flood.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-106"></a>[106](#note-ch2-106) The system of well irrigation using subterranean water was rendered invisible. Egypt’s agrarian and economic history could now be written, with half the picture missing.

<a id="ch02-0059"></a>

<a id="page-78"></a>〔原书第78页〕

<a id="page-78-en"></a>〔原书第78页〕

<a id="ch02-0060"></a>

### 畜力

### Animal Power

<a id="ch02-0061"></a>

除了在政府登记簿中缺席以及英国人想消除它之外，历史叙述忽视这个系统的第三个原因，可能在于大多数欧洲作家只看到了它的残迹。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-107"></a>[107](#note-ch2-107)就像十六世纪登陆秘鲁的西班牙征服者，发现印加世界已因先期抵达的天花而陷入崩溃一样，穆罕默德·阿里治下的法国工程师以及后来取代他们的英国人，遇到的是一个遭受一系列流行病和大流行病袭击的国家，这些疾病在欧洲军队之前就已传到埃及。尽管没有可靠数字，1800 年埃及人口可能处于几个世纪以来的最低点，饱受周期性鼠疫爆发和新出现的霍乱威胁之苦。俄罗斯向北方的奥斯曼领土扩张，英国和法国在东地中海及南亚扩张军事势力，由此带来的战争增多，以及贸易和朝圣往来的日益频繁，都促使这两种疾病传播。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-108"></a>[108](#note-ch2-108)穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者在奥斯曼早先公共卫生政策的基础上，实行隔离和其他措施，使人口水平得以恢复，但霍乱和鼠疫在 1830 年代再次袭击，霍乱也频繁重现，包括 1881 年英国占领前夕。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-109"></a>[109](#note-ch2-109)欧洲人倾向于把鼠疫和其他疾病视为病态东方的自然特征，视为界定其与西方差异的一部分，而不是视为暴力、动荡和交换加剧的产物，尽管他们自己在其中扮演了主导角色。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-110"></a>[110](#note-ch2-110)因此，在他们看来使现有耕作方法无利可图的“劳动力稀缺”，不仅是由于劳动密集型的运河灌溉棉花生产增加，也是帝国扩张和战争的长期影响所致。

A third reason why historical accounts have ignored this system, besides its absence from government registers and the British desire to eliminate it, may be that most European writers saw only its vestiges.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-107"></a>[107](#note-ch2-107) Like the Spanish conquistadores landing in sixteenth-century Peru and finding an Inca world already collapsing from the smallpox that had reached there ahead of them, the French engineers under Muhammad Ali and the British who later replaced them encountered a country attacked by a series of epidemic and pandemic diseases that had travelled to Egypt in advance of the European forces. Although we have no reliable figures, in 1800 the population of Egypt may have been at its lowest point in centuries, afflicted by periodic outbreaks of plague and by the new threat of cholera. Both diseases spread with the increased warfare that came with Russian expansion into Ottoman lands to the north and British and French military expansion in the Eastern Mediterranean and South Asia, as well as the increasing movement of trade and pilgrimage traffic.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-108"></a>[108](#note-ch2-108) Building on earlier Ottoman public health policy, Muhammad Ali and his successors introduced quarantines and other measures that allowed population levels to recover, but epidemics of cholera and plague struck again in the 1830s, and cholera reappeared frequently, including in 1881, on the eve of the British occupation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-109"></a>[109](#note-ch2-109) Europeans tended to see plague and other diseases as a natural aspect of a sickly Orient, part of what defined its difference from the West, rather than as the product of forms of violence, upheaval, and intensification of exchange in which they themselves played a leading role.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-110"></a>[110](#note-ch2-110) So the ‘scarcity of labour’ that, in their view, rendered existing methods of cultivation unprofitable was caused not only by an increase in the more labour-intensive method of canal-irrigated cotton production, but by longer-term effects of imperial expansion and warfare.

校注：底本写1881年英国占领前夕霍乱再次出现，原注109所引论文题名则为1883年疫情。该注另引Kuhnke的Lives at Risk区分了1881年汉志霍乱及埃及检疫措施，与1883年埃及疫情。正文照录，不将两地与两年混同。 https://publishing.cdlib.org/ucpressebooks/public/book/lives-at-risk-public-health-in-nineteenth-century-egypt.html

<a id="ch02-0062"></a>

即使防治鼠疫和霍乱的措施降低了发病率，另一种疾病更直接地影响了使用*saqiyas*的井灌。它攻击这个系统的主要动力——该国的牛群。这就是牛瘟，一种针对消化道的传染病，引起发烧和大面积胃肠炎，产生“令人作呕的恶臭”，在多数情况下导致死亡。在最严重的形式中，它可以杀死所感染动物的 95% 以上。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-111"></a>[111](#note-ch2-111)

Even as measures to combat plague and cholera reduced their incidence, another disease affected more directly the employment of well irrigation using *saqiyas*. It attacked the main motor of the system, the country’s cattle population. This was rinderpest, the cattle plague, a contagious disease that targets the digestive tract causing fever and extensive gastroenteritis, producing a ‘loathsome stench’ and, in most cases, death. In its severest form, it can kill more than 95 per cent of the animals it afflicts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-111"></a>[111](#note-ch2-111)

<a id="ch02-0063"></a>

现代时期第一次大动物流行病暴发于 1784—5 年，使埃及南部的牲畜大批死亡。在接下来的四年里，它又三次袭击开罗和<a id="page-79"></a>〔原书第79页〕北方。政府敦促农民改用水牛而不是黄牛来转动水车。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-112"></a>[112](#note-ch2-112)在许多情况下，人们不得不代替死去的动物，用自己的身体转动水车。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-113"></a>[113](#note-ch2-113)1820 年代，政府组织从苏丹中部的科尔多凡进口黄牛，以应对持续的短缺。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-114"></a>[114](#note-ch2-114)没有动物，水井便被废弃。1826 年，穆罕默德·阿里帕夏向他负责尼罗河三角洲西部米努夫和阿什蒙两个区的官员抱怨，该区的“水井和水车结构失修”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-115"></a>[115](#note-ch2-115)1833 年，帕夏设立了一个政府办事处，从苏丹进口替换牲畜，在尼罗河畔的基纳修建大型牲口棚，牛只从南方运到那里。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-116"></a>[116](#note-ch2-116)病毒在 1841—2 年再次袭击，从俄罗斯草原经多瑙河和的里雅斯特传来，摧毁了该国多达 90% 的牛群。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-117"></a>[117](#note-ch2-117)1861 年和 1863—4 年，南方又爆发了疫情。当地报告说，一些地方每天损失三四百头牛，农民“因缺少牛而无法浇地”，社区虚弱得无法搬走和掩埋所有尸体，成千上万头死牛顺河漂流。人们再一次“用自己的身体转动萨基亚水车”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-118"></a>[118](#note-ch2-118)据记载，1872—6 年和 1881 年英国占领前夕又发生了疫情。最后，1889 年爆发了牛瘟大流行，它始于埃塞俄比亚，当时意大利军队正从厄立特里亚海岸扩大殖民占领。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-119"></a>[119](#note-ch2-119)这场瘟疫沿非洲大陆南北蔓延近十年，在埃及及其南方国家造成毁灭性后果。

The first major epizootic of the modern period struck in 1784–5, decimating the livestock of southern Egypt. It returned in Cairo and the <a id="page-79-en"></a>〔原书第79页〕north three times in the next four years. The government urged farmers to respond by using water buffalo instead of oxen to turn the water-wheels.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-112"></a>[112](#note-ch2-112) In many cases humans had to replace the dead animals, turning the waterwheels with their own bodies.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-113"></a>[113](#note-ch2-113) In the 1820s, the government organised the importing of oxen from Kordofan in central Sudan to deal with the continuing shortage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-114"></a>[114](#note-ch2-114) Without animals, the wells fell into disuse. In 1826, Muhammad Ali Pasha complained to his official in charge of Minuf and Ashmoun, two western districts of the Nile Delta, that the district’s ‘wells and waterwheel structures are in disrepair’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-115"></a>[115](#note-ch2-115) In 1833 the Pasha set up a government office for importing replacement cattle from Sudan, building large barns on the Nile at Qina, where the animals arrived from the south.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-116"></a>[116](#note-ch2-116) The virus struck again in 1841–2, arriving from the Russian steppes via the Danube and Trieste, and destroying as much as 90 per cent of the country’s herds.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-117"></a>[117](#note-ch2-117) In 1861 and 1863–4, there were outbreaks in the south. Local reports speak of some localities losing three or four hundred head of cattle a day, farmers ‘unable to water the land for want of oxen’, communities too weak to carry off and bury all the carcasses, and dead cattle flowing down the river in their thousands. Once again, ‘men [we]re turning the sakiahs’ with their own bodies.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-118"></a>[118](#note-ch2-118) Further outbreaks were recorded in 1872–6 and in 1881 on the eve of the British occupation. Finally, there arrived the great rinderpest panzootic of 1889, which started in Ethiopia as Italian forces expanded their colonial occupation from the coast of Eritrea.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-119"></a>[119](#note-ch2-119) The plague spread north and south along the length of the continent for almost a decade, with devastating consequences in Egypt and the countries to its south.

<a id="ch02-0064"></a>

在埃塞俄比亚，由此引发的饥荒——因连续三年厄尔尼诺相关干旱而加剧——是有记忆以来最严重的一次。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-120"></a>[120](#note-ch2-120)牛的损失消除了主要的热能来源——干牛粪，给本已稀少的木材供应带来压力。到该世纪最后十年，埃塞俄比亚高原的树木覆盖——已因农业扩张而减少，又因奥斯曼—埃及、英国和意大利军队的入侵而进一步受损——降至最低点。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-121"></a>[121](#note-ch2-121)土地失去树木，促成了降雨量、降雨强度以及河流径流的变化。径流成为尼罗河的洪水，而洪水又因此变得更加极端，时而过高，时而过低。因此，牛瘟可能在埃及产生了第二重影响：它不仅反复摧毁畜力系统，同时也使这些动物用水车提取的洪水变得更加多变和不可预测。

In Ethiopia, the resulting famine, exacerbated by three years of El Niño–related droughts, was the worst in memory.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-120"></a>[120](#note-ch2-120) The loss of cattle removed the main source of heat energy, dried cow dung, putting pressure on scarce supplies of timber. By the last decade of the century, tree cover across the Ethiopian highlands, already reduced by agricultural expansion and further damaged by the invasion of Ottoman-Egyptian, British, and Italian armies, was at its lowest.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-121"></a>[121](#note-ch2-121) Denuding the land of its trees contributed to changes in the level and intensity of rainfall and runoff into rivers. The runoff becomes the flood waters of the Nile, which, in turn, saw more extreme high and low floods. So, the cattle plague may have had a second impact in Egypt: as well as repeatedly destroying the system of animal power, it simultaneously made the flood waters that those animals lifted using waterwheels more variable and unpredictable.

<a id="ch02-0065"></a>

<a id="page-80"></a>〔原书第80页〕当英国工程师在 1880 年代和 1890 年代调查并记述他们所看到的灌溉系统时，以及此前几十年的法国工程师也是如此，他们目睹的是一套机制，其关键部件和主要能源已被反复攻击和摧毁。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-122"></a>[122](#note-ch2-122)

<a id="page-80-en"></a>〔原书第80页〕When British engineers surveyed and wrote about the irrigation system as they found it in the 1880s and 1890s, and French engineers in the decades before them, they were witnessing a mechanism whose vital parts and main source of energy had been repeatedly attacked and destroyed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-122"></a>[122](#note-ch2-122)

<a id="ch02-0066"></a>

### 所谓饥荒史

### The So-Called History of Famines

<a id="ch02-0067"></a>

英国当局急于为殖民重新工程化河流和对河流的生态破坏辩护，忽视了最近的流行病和动物流行病史——他们自己的帝国行动和其他欧洲强国的行动对这种历史负有责任——也忽视了地下蓄水系统，而这个系统曾调节供水，并创造了肥沃而适应性强的耕作制度。他们忽视了边缘土地作为泄水区的用途，那里可以储存多余的水，供洪水大的年份使用。他们排除了埃及主要工程师阿里·穆巴拉克的建议，即更多地利用这类水库，作为在河流筑坝的替代方案。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-123"></a>[123](#note-ch2-123)他们还拒绝了瓦迪拉扬计划——一位美国考古学家提出的项目，旨在恢复法尤姆附近一个古老湖泊，以储存多余的灌溉水，作为三角洲拦河堰的替代方案。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-124"></a>[124](#note-ch2-124)

Anxious to justify the colonial re-engineering and ecological destruction of the river, the British authorities overlooked the recent history of epidemics and epizootics to which their own imperial actions and those of other European powers had contributed and ignored the system of subterranean water storage that had regulated the supply of water and created a fertile and adaptable system of farming. They ignored the use of marginal lands as an escape, in which excess water could be stored and used in years of high floods. They ruled out the proposals of the leading Egyptian engineer, Ali Mubarak, to increase the use of such reservoirs as an alternative to the damming of the river.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-123"></a>[123](#note-ch2-123) They also rejected the Wadi Rayan scheme, the project of an American archaeologist to restore an ancient lake adjacent to Fayyum to store excess irrigation waters, as an alternative to the Delta Barrage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-124"></a>[124](#note-ch2-124)

<a id="ch02-0068"></a>

此外，随着殖民政权以永久运河和拦河堰为基础，巩固对河流更集中的控制，一个新的无知空间打开了。电报的使用使官员能够从开罗监测洪水威胁，开始害怕这种“风险”。以前在当地处理的计算与决策，如今要在远处作出。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-125"></a>[125](#note-ch2-125)过去在洪水高涨时，当上涨的尼罗河接近峰值，巡堤人会被部署在堤岸的脆弱地段，并由一群准备处理任何决口的人协助；河面上布满装载石头和木桩的小船，供修复之用，所有船上都挂着灯笼。灯光倒映在水中，“场景充满欢快与生气，”一位英国地区工程师在这样一个地点报道说，“陌生人会以为正在举行盛大的集市。”这位工程师赞赏处理任何威胁时“沉稳而务实的作风”，并“觉得几乎不可能发生决口，而开罗的官员坐在办公室里读着电报副本，总是紧张胆怯”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-126"></a>[126](#note-ch2-126)

In addition, as the colonial regime consolidated a more centralised control of the river, based on permanent canals and barrages, a new space of ignorance opened up. The use of the telegraph allowed officials to monitor the threat of flooding from Cairo, becoming fearful of the ‘risk’. Calculations and decisions that were previously handled locally were now to be made at a distance.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-125"></a>[125](#note-ch2-125) In the past, during high floods, when the rising Nile approached its peak, watchmen would be stationed along vulnerable stretches of the embankment, assisted by gangs of men ready to deal with any breach, while the river was covered with small boats laden with stones and stakes for making repairs, all carrying lanterns. With the lamps reflected in the water, ‘the scene is full of gaiety and animation’, reported a British district engineer at one such site. ‘A stranger might imagine a great fair was on.’ Admiring the ‘steady business-like manner’ in which any threat was addressed, the engineer ‘felt that it was almost impossible for a breach to occur, while the officials in Cairo, seated in their offices reading the duplicates of telegrams, were always nervous and timid’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-126"></a>[126](#note-ch2-126)

<a id="ch02-0069"></a>

所谓旧制度的脆弱性，部分正是消除它的措施所制造的无知的产物。从开罗的<a id="page-81"></a>〔原书第81页〕办公室，英国高级官员把过去几个世纪的尼罗河灌溉描绘成一个人类极不安全的系统，国家的生存始终面临河流不可预测性以及生态破坏和饥荒威胁的风险。官员们还把这种不可预测性归咎于对殖民统治的抵抗，包括 1881 年在马赫迪穆罕默德·艾哈迈德·本·阿卜杜拉领导下在苏丹建立独立国家。“德尔维希（苦行僧派）阻止对尼罗河流量的任何科学考察，”他们抱怨道。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-127"></a>[127](#note-ch2-127)河流控制将成为消除这种独立的论据。一条不驯之河的生态和政治“风险”，被一群不驯的民众放大，成为进一步摧毁这条河的理由。

The alleged vulnerability of the old system was partly a product of the very ignorance produced by the measures to eliminate it. From their <a id="page-81-en"></a>〔原书第81页〕offices in Cairo, senior British officials pictured Nile irrigation over the preceding centuries as a system of great human precarity, in which the very survival of the country was permanently at risk from the river’s unpredictability and the ever-present threat of ecological devastation and famine. The officials also blamed this unpredictability on resistance to colonial rule, including the establishing of an independent state in Sudan in 1881 under the Mahdi, Muhammad Ahmad bin Abd Allah. ‘The Dervishes’, they complained, ‘prevent any scientific examination’ of the flow of the Nile.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-127"></a>[127](#note-ch2-127) River control would become an argument for the elimination of such independence. The ecological and political ‘risk’ of an unruly river, magnified by an unruly population, was a further justification for the river’s destruction.

<a id="ch02-0070"></a>

这种关于不稳定的观点在大多数现代历史叙述中被复制，为弑河行为提供了托词。它又因对早期阿拉伯作家的误读而得到强化。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-128"></a>[128](#note-ch2-128)基于同时代资料的中世纪埃及史提供了不同的图景。由于尼罗河在赤道东非有众多源头，埃塞俄比亚季风又十分规律，它的洪水节律比世界上任何其他河流都更可预测、更可靠。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-129"></a>[129](#note-ch2-129)虽然洪水峰顶的高度和时间逐年变化，但一旦水位开始上涨，这种变化就可以预测——例如，记录洪峰之间的间隔以及尼罗河沿岸测量站冲积沉积物的密度。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-130"></a>[130](#note-ch2-130)根据这些预测，可以扩大或缩小耕种面积，还可以像前面提到的那样，把多余的水储存在泄水区，或通过井灌在第二季甚至第三季种植额外作物，以应对低水位洪水。如果到第三季水井水位下降，次年夏天上涨的尼罗河会补给它们。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-131"></a>[131](#note-ch2-131)有丰年也有荒年，但极端情况因以下能力而得到缓和：把谷物和豆类从一个季节储存到下一个季节，无论是存放在住宅内，还是储存在大商人和统治家族的粮仓中，后者可能拥有数千甚至数万吨粮食。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-132"></a>[132](#note-ch2-132)慈善基金会（阿拉伯语*awqaf*，单数*waqf*）拥有大片土地，这些土地发展成一种保护城乡财产免受政府征税要求的工具；它们利用粮食储备和厨房，在短缺时期支持弱势者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-133"></a>[133](#note-ch2-133)该国的纺织品生产——主要建立在种植亚麻、织成亚麻布的基础上，这一行业在中世纪繁荣，并在十七和<a id="page-82"></a>〔原书第82页〕十八世纪复兴——提供了又一种储存系统。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-134"></a>[134](#note-ch2-134)亚麻在低洼地带的湿润土壤中茁壮生长，使人们能够利用大洪水留下的多余土地，并把剩余物储存起来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-135"></a>[135](#note-ch2-135)亚麻工业的扩张可能部分出于这个目的，同时商人也从为其生产提供预付信贷中获利。把田地作物变成一匹匹布，提供了比谷物更安全、更有价值、更耐久、也更具可互换性的财富储存手段。事实上，成卷的布匹比粮仓更容易被用来隐匿财富以逃税，甚至可能被用来缴税。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-136"></a>[136](#note-ch2-136)由于能够储存谷物、豆类、织物和洪水，在中世纪埃及，洪水脉冲的波动从未导致饥荒。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-137"></a>[137](#note-ch2-137)

This view of precarity is reproduced in most modern historical accounts, providing an alibi for the act of rivercide. It has been reinforced by a misreading of earlier Arab writers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-128"></a>[128](#note-ch2-128) Histories of medieval Egypt, based on contemporaneous sources, offer a different picture. The flood regime of the Nile was more predictable and more dependable than that of any other world river, thanks to the multiplicity of its sources in equatorial East Africa and the regularity of the Ethiopian monsoon.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-129"></a>[129](#note-ch2-129) While the height and timing of the crest of the flood varied from year to year, the variation could be predicted once the water levels began to rise – for example, by recording the interval between surges and the density of the alluvium deposit at measuring stations along the Nile.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-130"></a>[130](#note-ch2-130) The area to be cultivated could be extended or restricted based on these predictions, with the further options, as mentioned, of storing excess water in escapes or dealing with low floods by planting additional crops using well-water irrigation in a second and even a third season. If by the third season the wells were running low, the rising Nile of the following summer replenished them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-131"></a>[131](#note-ch2-131) There were years of abundance and years of scarcity, but the extremes were moderated by the ability to store grains and pulses from one season to the next, whether within the domestic dwelling or in the granaries of large merchants and the ruling households, who might hold thousands or in some cases tens of thousands of tons.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-132"></a>[132](#note-ch2-132) Charitable foundations (in Arabic, *awqaf*, or *waqf*, singular), whose extensive landholdings developed as a means of shielding rural and urban property from the government’s revenue claims, used their food stores and kitchens to support the disadvantaged in periods of shortage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-133"></a>[133](#note-ch2-133) The country’s textile production, based mainly on growing flax to weave into linen, an industry that flourished in the medieval period and was revived again in the seventeenth and <a id="page-82-en"></a>〔原书第82页〕eighteenth centuries, provided a further storage system.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-134"></a>[134](#note-ch2-134) Thriving in the moist soil of low-lying tracts, flax allowed the utilisation of surplus land from a heavy flood, and the storing of the surplus.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-135"></a>[135](#note-ch2-135) The flax industry may have expanded partly for this purpose, alongside the profit that merchants made from advancing credit for its production. Transforming a field crop into bolts of cloth provided a means of storing wealth that was more secure, valuable, durable, and fungible even than grain. In fact, rolls of cloth could be used more easily than granaries to secrete wealth to avoid the payment of taxes, and may even have been used to pay those taxes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-136"></a>[136](#note-ch2-136) Thanks to the ability to store grain, pulses, fabrics, and flood water, in medieval Egypt the fluctuation in the flood pulse was never a cause of famine.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-137"></a>[137](#note-ch2-137)

<a id="ch02-0071"></a>

前现代时期生计的主要威胁不是河流的多变，而是偶尔发生的政治动荡，例如 1062—73 年的“大灾难”（*al-shidda al-‘uzma*），或十二世纪末和十三世纪末的政治危机。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-138"></a>[138](#note-ch2-138)更常见的是来自大商人的威胁，他们受诱在预期短缺时囤积粮食，以抬高价格。他们有时夸大洪水峰顶偏低的威胁，使民众恐慌购买，从而为其涨价提供理由。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-139"></a>[139](#note-ch2-139)马穆鲁克时期关于这些问题的主要史料是马格里齐约 1405 年写的*Ighathat al-umma bi-kashf al-ghumma*，它按时间顺序记载了此前几个世纪每一次已知的粮食短缺和困苦。它承认气候因素在洪水变化和粮食生产中的作用。它顺带提到两个世纪前一个离奇的记载：干旱极端严重，以至于富人开始食用儿童的血肉，并“对此习以为常”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-140"></a>[140](#note-ch2-140)但这本书主要论述政府当局和市场监督官（*muhtasib*）控制价格、惩罚欺诈的责任；马格里齐本人曾三次为开罗城担任这一职务。他把近期的匮乏归因于当局决定停止铸造银币，转而依靠账面信用（记账货币），辅以作为辅币的铜币；马格里齐指责这种做法贬低货币价值，使农民贫困。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-141"></a>[141](#note-ch2-141)

The main threat to livelihoods in the pre-modern period came not from the variability of the river but from occasional episodes of political strife, as with the ‘great calamity’ (*al-shidda al-‘uzma*) of 1062–73, or the political crises at the end of the twelfth century and again at the end of the thirteenth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-138"></a>[138](#note-ch2-138) More frequently, the threat came from large merchants, who were tempted to hoard supplies of grain in anticipation of shortages in order to drive up the price. They would sometimes exaggerate the threat of a low crest to the flood, to panic the population into purchases that would justify their raising of prices.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-139"></a>[139](#note-ch2-139) The principal historical source on these matters from the Mamluk period, Maqrizi’s *Ighathat al-umma bi-kashf al-ghumma*, written around 1405, chronicles every known episode over the preceding centuries of food shortage and distress. It acknowledges the role of climatic factors in the variation of the flood and grain production. It mentions in passing a fantastical account from two centuries earlier of a drought so extreme that the well-to-do began to consume the flesh of children, a taste ‘to which they became accustomed’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-140"></a>[140](#note-ch2-140) But the text addresses mainly the responsibility of government authorities and the market supervisor, or *muhtasib*, an office in which Maqrizi himself served for the city of Cairo on three occasions, to control prices and punish fraud. He attributes recent episodes of dearth to the decision of the authorities to cease coining money in silver and rely instead on book credit (money of account) supplemented with token copper coins, a practice Maqrizi blames for debasing the value of money and impoverishing the peasantry.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-141"></a>[141](#note-ch2-141)

<a id="ch02-0072"></a>

马格里齐这本书的押韵书名很难译成英文，但可以译为《考察困苦以救助民众》。最早注意到这部著作的法国东方学家给它起了另一个书名：*Le Traité des Famines*（《饥荒论》）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-142"></a>[142](#note-ch2-142)把这本书称为“关于<a id="page-83"></a>〔原书第83页〕饥荒的论著”，并未抓住马格里齐文本的含义及其对货币和信用的关切（这个主题我们将在下一章讨论），反而抓住了殖民者对农业危机的执念。所谓的饥荒“风险”确立了旧秩序的不足和脆弱，为有计划地摧毁河流提供了又一个托词。

The rhymed title of Maqrizi’s book is difficult to render in English but can be translated as ‘Aiding the Community by Examining Its Distress’. The French Orientalists who first noted the work’s existence gave it a different title: *Le Traité des Famines*.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-142"></a>[142](#note-ch2-142) Calling the book a ‘treatise on <a id="page-83-en"></a>〔原书第83页〕famines’ captured not the meaning of Maqrizi’s text and its concern with money and credit (a topic to which we turn in the next chapter) but the colonial preoccupation with agrarian crisis. The supposed ‘risk’ of famine established the inadequacy and precarity of the old order and provided a further alibi for the planned destruction of the river.

<a id="ch02-0073"></a>

### 资本化

### Capitalisation

<a id="ch02-0074"></a>

关注地表水而忽视灌溉水的储存和提取方法，还有另一个原因。建立在地表水和地下水储存基础上的旧方法——畜力、多季种植——对于农业如今要服务的新目的来说适应性过强、过于复杂。尼罗河的殖民化和资本化无法轻易与洪水退去后的农业制度共存，不是因为土地需要生产更多——正如我们将看到的，土地生产力即将迅速下降——而是因为它需要以不同方式生产，这种方式把泛滥从资源变成威胁。殖民主义如今将设计出一个“易受洪水侵害的景观”，其风险更适合于从未来抽取，而不是对自然的开发。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-143"></a>[143](#note-ch2-143)

Focusing on surface water and ignoring the methods of storing and lifting irrigation water had an additional reason. The old methods of animal-powered, multiple cropping, based on both surface and subterranean storage, were too adaptable and too complex for the novel purpose that agriculture was now to serve. The colonising and capitalising of the Nile could not easily coexist with the regime of flood-recession farming, not because the land needed to produce more – as we will see, the productivity of the land was set to rapidly decline – but because it needed to produce differently, in ways that turned inundation from a resource into a threat. Colonialism would now engineer a ‘flood-vulnerable landscape’, one whose risks were better suited, not to the exploitation of nature, but to extraction from the future.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-143"></a>[143](#note-ch2-143)

<a id="ch02-0075"></a>

在英国殖民主义下，尼罗河将作为从未来获利——通过征税——的手段运作。从未来抽取支付的机制本身并不新鲜。几个世纪以来，开罗的大商人依靠向耕作者提供信贷而兴旺，办法是签订预购作物合同，待交货时以更高价格出售。定期缴税的要求帮助迫使耕地者预售产品并负债。征税的当局和为缴税预付信贷的商人相互依赖，以充实自身。近几个世纪，在马穆鲁克和奥斯曼统治下，特定村庄及其土地税收份额的权利被作为薪饷分配给军官，后来又拍卖给包税人。这些收入权利演变为乡村庄园，使其持有者成为商人和耕作者之间抽取机制的中介。十九世纪初，穆罕默德·阿里用直接征税取代包税制，试图通过命令把作物直接运到政府仓库来排挤大商人，随后开始把未来收成、并逐渐把整个庄园<a id="page-84"></a>〔原书第84页〕作为信用支付分配给外国商人，作为对扩张中的军队和农村行政的军官和官员的补偿。控制这些庄园——其中许多从旧马穆鲁克统治家族手中没收——的人，被指定为“负责者”（*muta’ahhid*），负责向政府缴纳所欠税款，而政府逐渐提高并简化了税率。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-144"></a>[144](#note-ch2-144)

The Nile under British colonialism was to operate as a means of profiting from – by taxing – the future. Mechanisms for extracting payments from the future were not in themselves something new. For centuries, the large merchants of Cairo had prospered from the ability to extend credit to cultivators, through contracts for the advance purchase of crops that they could sell for a higher price when delivered. The requirement to pay taxes at regular intervals helped compel those who farmed the land to sell their produce in advance and become indebted. The authorities imposing taxes and the merchants advancing credit for their payment depended on one another for their own enrichment. In recent centuries, under Mamluk and Ottoman rule, the right to a share in the tax revenues of specific villages and their lands had been assigned as salaries to military officers and later auctioned to tax farmers. These rights to revenue evolved into rural estates, inserting the holders as middlemen between merchants and cultivators in the mechanism of extraction. In the early nineteenth century, Muhammad Ali replaced tax farming with direct taxation, tried to cut out the large merchants by commanding the delivery of crops directly to government warehouses, and then began allocating future harvests, and gradually entire estates, <a id="page-84-en"></a>〔原书第84页〕as credit payments to foreign merchants and as recompense for the military officers and officials of an expanding army and rural administration. Those controlling the estates, many of which were confiscated from the former Mamluk ruling households, were made ‘responsible’ (*muta’ahhid*) for the taxes owed to the government, which gradually raised and simplified the tax rate.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-144"></a>[144](#note-ch2-144)

<a id="ch02-0076"></a>

正如阿姆尔·海勒·艾哈迈德（Amr Khairy Ahmed）所解释的，在该世纪下半叶，两场危机帮助产生了新规模的资本化。第一，一波接一波的牛瘟消灭了驱动该国灌溉机械的畜力，为引入大量以赊购方式供应的蒸汽泵创造了机会。牛是通过合作安排或合伙关系饲养、喂养和繁殖的，这些安排很少提供抽取信用支付的机会；而蒸汽泵成本高得多、寿命长得多，使贷款得以激增，包括为购买进口煤炭而提供的贷款。第二，美国以奴隶制为基础的棉花生产的持续，引发了另一场危机：美国内战和 1861—5 年的全球棉花饥荒。它与埃及 1863—4 年的牛瘟同时发生，棉价的跳升为该国的欧洲和黎凡特金融家提供了以新规模创造信用的手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-145"></a>[145](#note-ch2-145)蒸汽动力轧棉机与灌溉泵一起，成为资本化的机器。当棉花饥荒突然结束时，赫迪夫·伊斯梅尔转向糖业生产；他从 1863 年统治到 1879 年在欧洲债权人及其政府的要求下被废黜。他下令开挖该国最长的运河——中埃及的易卜拉希米亚运河——为其配备大型蒸汽泵站以灌溉广阔的甘蔗种植园，并建造“由蒸汽驱动的大型制糖厂，在厂中碾磨甘蔗并完成煮沸和精炼”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-146"></a>[146](#note-ch2-146)机械、基础设施和种植园的规模，促成了甚至更大规模的信用创造。伊斯梅尔所借贷款的一半到四分之三，用于购买蒸汽泵并为新种植园建造工厂、轻便铁路、运河和其他基础设施。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-147"></a>[147](#note-ch2-147)伊斯梅尔日益独立于伊斯坦布尔，使金融家能够通过抵押政府收入，最终抵押整个政府和王室地产来获得信用保障。到 1870 年代末，这些国家和王室领地——如今已被宣布伊斯梅尔破产的欧洲债权人夺取和管理——占该国耕地面积的 10%。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-148"></a>[148](#note-ch2-148)种植园和机械、它们所设计的债务水平，以及它们促成的生态、<a id="page-85"></a>〔原书第85页〕金融和政治危机，触发了英国占领。伊斯梅尔及其债权人在该国糖业和棉花种植园中开创的做法，如今要在全国范围内尝试。

In the second half of the century, as Amr Khairy Ahmed explains, two crises helped generate a new scale of capitalisation. First, waves of cattle plague, wiping out the animal power that drove the country’s irrigation machinery, created the opportunity to introduce large numbers of steam-driven pumps, supplied on credit. While cattle were raised, nourished, and reproduced through collaborative arrangements or partnerships that seldom provided openings for extracting credit payments, the much greater cost and longevity of a steam pump allowed a proliferation of loans, including those provided to purchase imports of coal. Second, the perpetuation of slave-based cotton production in the United States triggered another crisis, the American Civil War and the worldwide cotton famine of 1861–5. Coinciding with the 1863–4 cattle plague in Egypt, the jump in cotton prices offered the country’s European and Levantine financiers the means to create credit on a new scale.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-145"></a>[145](#note-ch2-145) Steam-powered cotton gins joined the irrigation pumps as machineries of capitalisation. When the cotton famine abruptly ended, Khedive Isma‘il, who ruled from 1863 until his deposition at the behest of his European creditors and their governments in 1879, switched to sugar production. He commissioned the digging of the country’s longest canal, the Ibrahimiya Canal in Middle Egypt, equipped it with large steam-powered pumping stations to feed extensive cane plantations, and built ‘immense sugar manufactories worked by steam, in which the cane is ground and the boiling and refining done’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-146"></a>[146](#note-ch2-146) The size of the machinery, infrastructure, and plantations facilitated an even larger creation of credit. Between half and three-quarters of the loans that Isma‘il took on were used to purchase steam pumps and build factories, light railways, canals, and other infrastructure for the new plantations.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-147"></a>[147](#note-ch2-147) The increasing independence of Isma‘il from Istanbul allowed the financiers to secure the credit through mortgages on government revenues and eventually on entire government and royal estates. By the end of the 1870s these state and royal domains, now seized and administered by the European creditors who had declared Isma‘il bankrupt, occupied 10 per cent of the country’s cultivated area.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-148"></a>[148](#note-ch2-148) The plantations and machinery, the levels of debt they engineered, and the ecological, <a id="page-85-en"></a>〔原书第85页〕financial, and political crises to which they contributed triggered the British occupation. What Isma‘il and his creditors had pioneered on the country’s sugar and cotton plantations was now to be attempted across the country as a whole.

<a id="ch02-0077"></a>

要进一步扩大从未来抽取的系统，就需要以不同方式储水：不再使用围堤田块及其下方的地层，也不使用少数几条深挖的夏季运河（它们依赖同一地下水的渗流），而是把水储存在一个大型地表水库中、河流本身因水位抬高而增大的水体中，以及工业作物的纤维素壁中。

Expanding further the system of extraction from the future required water to be stored differently: rather than using field basins and the substrate beneath them, and the handful of deeply excavated summer canals, which depended on seepage from the same groundwater, storage was to be located in a large surface reservoir, in the raised volume of the river itself, and within the cellulose walls of industrial crops.

<a id="ch02-0078"></a>

为了以新规模使埃及农业资本化，把尼罗河本身变成一台信用和时间转移的机器，金融家力图扩大棉花和甘蔗这两种工业作物的种植，而这两者都不受小农欢迎。工业作物不在当地消费，也不能留待将来使用。农户和商人可以把谷物、豆类、稻米和当地加工的纺织纤维储存数年，却难以储存棉花或甘蔗。收获时，整批作物迅速离开本地人手中，运往糖厂或轧棉厂。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-149"></a>[149](#note-ch2-149)作物种植与其产品的加工、制造之间的分离，使种植者保留的作物价值份额更容易被削减。传统上保留大部分主食作物的农民，从经济作物中获得的收入可能不到其价值的一半。不归耕作者的那部分价值如今可以通过出售土地所有权提供给投资者，成为一种可被资本化的长期未来收入。

To capitalise Egyptian agriculture on a new scale, turning the Nile itself into a machine of credit and time transfer, financiers sought to expand the growing of the two industrial crops, cotton and sugar cane, neither of which was popular among small farmers. Industrial crops are not consumed locally and cannot be set aside for future use. While farming households and merchants can store cereal grains, pulses, rice, and locally processed textile fibres for years, they cannot easily store cotton or sugar cane. At harvest, the entire crop moves quickly out of local hands and is carried to sugar mills or cotton gins.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-149"></a>[149](#note-ch2-149) The interruption between the growing of the crop and the processing and manufacturing of its product made it easier to reduce the share of the crop’s value retained by the grower. Farmers who conventionally kept a large part of a staple food crop might receive less than half the value of crops grown for manufacturing.
