The non-farming share could now be made available to investors, via the sale of title to the land, becoming a longterm future income to be capitalised.

<a id="ch02-0079"></a>

由于与工业用途相关的种种原因，大规模种植的工业作物与现有的蓄水系统不相容，因而也与尼罗河的生命周期不相容。它们需要不同的种植期，基于获取灌溉水的不同时间表。大多数基本粮食作物生长很快——食物通常储存在果实或种子中，播种后几周内即可收获。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-150"></a>[150](#note-ch2-150)在全年日照和灌溉水（来自洪水和井水）的环境中，正如我们所见，这使一年种植多季作物成为可能。相比之下，这两种工业作物的价值不在于快速生长的果实或种子，而在于其支撑结构的纤维素组织——储存甘蔗汁液的茎秆，或容纳棉株棉纤维的棉铃。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-151"></a>[151](#note-ch2-151)这种纤维素储存容器的成熟需要长得多的时间。长绒棉占地九<a id="page-86"></a>〔原书第86页〕个月，甘蔗长达十二个月，还要加上犁地和整地所需的数周，因此每年只能种一季。旧的双层灌溉水储存系统要求在夏末让大部分田地被淹长达六周。工业作物需要长达一年时间来构建自己的储存系统，无法与洪水周期同步。

For reasons related to their industrial purpose, industrial crops grown on an extensive scale were incompatible with the existing system of water storage, and thus incompatible with the life cycle of the Nile. They required a different period of cultivation, based on a different timetable of access to irrigation water. Most basic food crops grow quickly – the food is typically stored in the fruit or seed, which can be ready to harvest within a few weeks of sowing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-150"></a>[150](#note-ch2-150) In an environment with year-round sunshine and irrigation water, from flood water and well water, this allowed, as we have seen, the growing of multiple crops in a year. The value of the two industrial crops, in contrast, lies not in a fast-growing fruit or seed, but in the cellulosic structure of its support – the stalk that stores the juices of the sugar cane or the boll that contains the lint of the cotton plant.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-151"></a>[151](#note-ch2-151) This cellulose storage vessel takes much longer to mature. Long-staple cotton occupies the ground for nine <a id="page-86-en"></a>〔原书第86页〕months and sugar cane for up to twelve, in addition to the weeks needed for ploughing and preparing the soil, allowing for only one crop per year. The old double-layered system for storing irrigation water required the flooding of most fields for up to six weeks in late summer. The industrial crops, needing up to a year to build their own storage system, could not be synchronised with the flood cycle.

<a id="ch02-0080"></a>

始终可以留出小块土地种植甘蔗和棉花，以及第三种夏季工业作物靛蓝植物，用水车从井中或上涨的河水中灌溉。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-152"></a>[152](#note-ch2-152)在中世纪和近代早期，对大商人来说，这些作物较长的生长期不是障碍，而是其利润的来源。棉花通常限于一英亩或一英亩半的小块地，而乡间的围堤田区延伸数百或数千英亩。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-153"></a>[153](#note-ch2-153)甘蔗的种植更为广泛。大约从十一世纪起，埃及利用水车灌溉小块土地，发展出重要的制糖业。糖被视为药物，早期榨糖厂的投资者往往是医生。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-154"></a>[154](#note-ch2-154)据内莉·汉纳所述，十七世纪对甘蔗种植有了新的投资，到该世纪末，糖的精炼和贸易已成为开罗最赚钱的生意之一。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-155"></a>[155](#note-ch2-155)对大商人来说，甘蔗的优势恰恰在于其生长季的长度。从种植到收获之间长达一年的延迟，迫使农民预售作物以借债，为缴税和其他需求提供资金。对于很大一部分利润来自提供信贷的商人来说（我们将在下一章进一步探讨），生长季越长，潜在利润就越大。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-156"></a>[156](#note-ch2-156)出于同样的原因，大多数农民避免种植甘蔗，因为“种植它需要预付资金”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-157"></a>[157](#note-ch2-157)

It was always feasible to reserve small sections of land for cane and cotton, along with the third industrial summer crop, indigo, to be irrigated from wells or from the rising river using waterwheels.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-152"></a>[152](#note-ch2-152) In the medieval and early modern period, for large merchants, the extended growing season of these crops was not a handicap but a source of their profitability. Cotton was generally restricted to small plots of an acre or an acre and a half, in a countryside where field basins extended for hundreds or thousands of acres.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-153"></a>[153](#note-ch2-153) Sugar cane was more extensively cultivated. From around the eleventh century, Egypt developed an important sugar industry using irrigation of small tracts by waterwheel. The sugar was valued as a medicine, and the investors in early cane-pressing factories were often physicians.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-154"></a>[154](#note-ch2-154) In the seventeenth century, according to Nelly Hanna, there was a renewed investment in sugar cultivation and, by the end of that century, the refining and trading of sugar was one of Cairo’s most profitable businesses.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-155"></a>[155](#note-ch2-155) For large merchants, the advantage of cane lay precisely in the length of its growing season. The year-long delay between planting and harvesting forced farmers to enter into debt by selling the crop in advance, to provide funds for tax payments and other needs. For merchants, a significant part of whose profit came from the supply of credit (as we will explore further in the next chapter), the longer the growing season, the greater the potential profit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-156"></a>[156](#note-ch2-156) For the same reason, most farmers avoided planting sugar, due to ‘the advances that its cultivation requires’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-157"></a>[157](#note-ch2-157)

<a id="ch02-0081"></a>

扩大棉花和甘蔗种植，与尼罗河洪水退去后的生态不相容。要扩大到 1820 年代三角洲部分地区首次尝试、1860—70 年代在三角洲和中埃及扩大、并被英国殖民行政官员以及欧内斯特·卡塞尔及其合伙人等金融家设想推广到全国的范围，河流的生命如今必须被摧毁。

Expanding the cultivation of cotton and sugar was inconsonant with the flood-recession ecology of the Nile. To extend their production on the scale first attempted in parts of the Delta in the 1820s, expanded in the Delta and Middle Egypt in the 1860s and 1870s, and envisioned for the entire country by the British colonial administrators, and by financiers like Ernest Cassel and his partners, the life of the river now had to be destroyed.

<a id="ch02-0082"></a>

事实上，从十九世纪早些时候起就在进行的工业作物扩张，已经开始扰乱河流的洪水脉冲。这些作物不仅与个别田地的淹没不相容，也与尼罗河整个涨落过程不相容。由于被改种棉花和甘蔗的田地<a id="page-87"></a>〔原书第87页〕不再能在夏季储存大量洪水，这些作物种植的扩大使可供应对多余洪水的围堤田区减少。越来越多的洪水不得不在危险状态下被限制在河岸和运河之内。这一变化增加了尼罗河洪峰高的年份发生灾难的风险。此外，在围堤田区中，水位上涨时土地通常处于休耕状态，因此意外的淹没对作物损害不大；而河岸高地的任何淹没，通常也会因多一层淤泥而使下一季产量增加作为补偿。但当强洪水或削弱的堤坝导致棉田或甘蔗田意外被淹时，耕作者会失去整整一年的收成。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-158"></a>[158](#note-ch2-158)反过来，与高粱不同，工业作物不适应缺水或干旱，因此尼罗河水位低造成损失的风险要大得多。尼罗河洪水水位的周期性极端变化，以及偶尔发生意外淹没的风险，成为一种无法驾驭的威胁。英国人力图克服的所谓自然不可预测性和饥荒风险，其实是放弃更复杂的蓄水系统、引入资本化所需的脆弱控制和耐久形式的产物。

In fact, the expansion of industrial crops, under way from earlier in the nineteenth century, had already begun to disrupt the river’s flood pulse. The crops were incompatible not just with the flooding of individual fields, but with the entire ebb and flow of the Nile. Since the fields <a id="page-87-en"></a>〔原书第87页〕that were being converted to cotton and cane were no longer able to store significant flood waters in the summer, the expanding cultivation of these crops left fewer basins available to cope with excess water. More and more of the flood had to be contained dangerously within the banks of the river and its canals. This change increased the risk of devastation in years of a high Nile crest. Moreover, with flood basins the land was usually lying fallow as the waters rose, so an unexpected inundation did little damage to crops, and any flooding of the berms was usually compensated by an increased yield in the following season thanks to the additional layer of silt. But when strong floods or weakened dykes led to the accidental flooding of a field of cotton or sugar cane, the cultivator lost an entire year’s production.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-158"></a>[158](#note-ch2-158) Conversely, unlike sorghum, the industrial crops were not adapted to deal with water scarcity or drought, so the risk of losses from a low Nile was much greater. The periodic extremes in the level of the Nile flood, and the occasional risk of accidental flooding, became an unmanageable threat. The apparent unpredictability of nature and risk of famine that the British sought to overcome was a product of abandoning a more complex system of water storage and of introducing the vulnerable form of control and durability required for capitalisation.

<a id="ch02-0083"></a>

工业作物的传播也是英国人力图解决的另一个问题的原因：*corvée*即强制劳动的广泛使用和日益苛刻。十九世纪后期的*corvée*并不是欧洲人常描绘的那种专制政府部署劳动力的古老方法。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-159"></a>[159](#note-ch2-159)长期以来一直存在要求集体劳动维护堤岸、运河和其他灌溉工程的做法，而在帝国扩张时期，会动员规模大得多的劳动力来修建新的围堤田区和运河（通常从河流废弃的河道挖成）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-160"></a>[160](#note-ch2-160)控制大庄园的包税人，以及穆罕默德·阿里治下取代他们的“税收担保人”，可以强迫他们所征税的人劳动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-161"></a>[161](#note-ch2-161)但在仲夏洪水上涨时维护河岸，让水依次流入田地，然后在冬季运河干涸时清理运河，与围绕棉田和甘蔗田保持堤岸完好、把运河当作长期水库并必须不惜一切代价防止其崩溃和淹没邻近田地的工作相比，是一项易于管理的任务。

The spread of industrial crops was also the cause of the other problem the British sought to solve: the widespread and increasingly exacting use of the *corvée* or forced labour. The *corvée* of the later nineteenth century was not an ancient method of deploying labour by a despotic government, as the Europeans often portrayed it.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-159"></a>[159](#note-ch2-159) There was a longstanding practice of requiring collective labour to maintain embankments, canals, and other irrigation works, and much larger workforces were mobilised in periods of imperial expansion to construct new basins and canals (usually dug from abandoned channels of the river).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-160"></a>[160](#note-ch2-160) Tax farmers who controlled large estates, and the ‘tax guarantors’ who replaced them under Muhammad Ali, could compel labour from those they taxed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-161"></a>[161](#note-ch2-161) But maintaining the banks as the flood water rose in midsummer and allowing it to flow into the fields in sequence, then cleaning the canals when dry in the winter, was a manageable task compared with the work of keeping the embankments intact around fields of cotton and sugar, using the canals as long-term reservoirs that had to be prevented at all costs from collapsing and flooding the adjacent fields.

<a id="ch02-0084"></a>

英国人在把大片土地改种棉花和甘蔗时遇到的更大问题是，随着拦河堰和永久运河的发展，过去由洪水<a id="page-88"></a>〔原书第88页〕携带并沉积在田地各处的肥沃淤泥——估计每年 1.25 亿吨——如今沉积在灌溉运河中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-162"></a>[162](#note-ch2-162)田地肥力的古老来源变成了一种废物。英国占领埃及时，此时大部分*corvée*劳动力都需要用于每年挖掘这种不受欢迎的淤泥（此外还在劳动密集的棉花收获季在大庄园从事无偿劳动）。由于不可能清除这么多淤泥，主要运河的河床升高，抬高了它们从河中取水的水位，使运河在洪水低的年份更难使用，从而大大增加了这些年份耕作的风险。

A larger problem that the British encountered with the conversion of large tracts to cotton and sugar cane was that with the development of barrages and permanent canals the fertilising silt that used to be carried <a id="page-88-en"></a>〔原书第88页〕by the flood waters and deposited across the fields – estimated at 125 million tons per year – was now deposited in the irrigation canals.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-162"></a>[162](#note-ch2-162) The ancient source of the fecundity of the fields had been transformed into a waste product. When the British occupied Egypt, the bulk of the *corvée* labour by that point was required for the annual excavation of this unwanted silt (and in addition as unpaid work on large estates in the labour-intensive cotton harvest). Since it was impossible to remove so much silt, the floor level of the main canals rose, raising the level at which they took water from the river and making it more difficult to use the canals in years of low floods and thus rendering the risks to cultivation in such years much greater.

<a id="ch02-0085"></a>

### 横跨尼罗河的水坝

### Dams Across the Nile

<a id="ch02-0086"></a>

解决“废物”问题的办法，是通过在阿斯旺修建大坝、在下游以及后来在阿斯旺上游修建更多拦河堰来阻断水流，从而完成对河流的摧毁。洪水脉冲被取代：在旧河床中工程化出一条全年有水的河道，它变成一条受调控的、渠道化的水流，其中大部分甚至从未到达海洋。虽然第一座阿斯旺大坝设计了底部泄水闸，以便夏季让一些含沙水流向下游，但大部分“废物”如今会被截留在坝后水库中。拦河堰会抬高河流水位，消除每年挖运河的大部分需要。河流及其运河取代了田地和地下水库，成为本地的蓄水场所。

The solution to the problem of ‘waste’ was to complete the destruction of the river by building the dam at Aswan and additional barrages downstream and later upstream of Aswan to block its flow. The flood pulse was replaced by engineering a year-round channel of water in the old riverbed, which became a regulated, canalised stream, most of it never even reaching the sea. Although the first Aswan Dam was designed with under-sluices to allow some of the silt-laden water to flow downstream in the summer, much of the ‘waste’ would now be trapped in the reservoirs behind the dams. The barrages would raise the level of the river, eliminating most of the annual need to dig out the canals. The river and its canals replaced the fields and underground reservoirs as local sites of water storage.

<a id="ch02-0087"></a>

这带来了始料未及的后果，其中几项已在描述旧地下蓄水系统优势时提到：全年抬高河流和运河水位造成盐碱化和渍水问题；常年有水的运河为寄生虫提供了栖息地，这些寄生虫引起地方性、使人衰弱的疾病；最重要的是，减少并最终消除洪水，摧毁了田地肥力和河流生物丰度所依赖的洪水脉冲。此外，在围堤田区播种的作物不需要犁地或耙地，而如今土地要接受大量机械处理——以棉花为例，至少犁三遍，把未耗尽养分的土壤翻到表面并清除杂草。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-163"></a>[163](#note-ch2-163)正如我们现在所知，犁地破坏土壤结构和微生物生命，逐渐降低其<a id="page-89"></a>〔原书第89页〕肥力（也会释放植物固存的大气碳）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-164"></a>[164](#note-ch2-164)所有这些因素都促成了 1900 年至 1920 年间农业产量下降 20%。农民被迫以越来越高的成本从其他来源补充流失的养分，主要是进口硝酸盐和后来的合成肥料，但未能遏止产量下降。

This had unforeseen consequences, several of which have already been mentioned in describing the advantages of the old system of underground water storage: raising the water level of the river and canals year-round caused problems of salination and water logging; perennial canals provided a home for parasites that caused endemic and debilitating diseases; and, above all, reducing and eventually eliminating the flood destroyed the flood pulse on which both the fertility of the fields and the richness of the river’s biota depended. In addition, while crops sown in flood basins required no ploughing or harrowing, the land now received extensive mechanical treatment – a minimum of three ploughings in the case of cotton, to bring unexhausted soil to the surface and eliminate weeds.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-163"></a>[163](#note-ch2-163) Ploughing, as we now know, destroys the structure and microbial life of the soil, gradually reducing its <a id="page-89-en"></a>〔原书第89页〕fertility (and also releases the atmospheric carbon sequestered by plants).<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-164"></a>[164](#note-ch2-164) All of these factors contributed to the 20 per cent decline in agricultural yields between 1900 and 1920. Farmers were forced to replace the lost nutrients from other sources, mainly imports of nitrates and later of synthetic fertiliser, at an increasing cost, but failed to stem the decline in yields.

<a id="ch02-0088"></a>

河流被毁的又一个代价——对资本化而言则是好处——是它的洪泛平原不仅变得更不肥沃，而且可以改作道路和住房用地。此前，人类定居主要局限于今河道及古代废弃河道两岸抬高的天然堤；河谷边缘未开垦的陡崖；以及众多高出洪泛平原的“土丘”（tell），即人类聚居形成的土墩，是在同一地点建造和重建数百年甚至数千年的结果。随着洪水被消除，富裕者如今可以把住房扩展到村镇下方的田地中，或在乡间建造豪华的*‘izbas*（庄园），包括约瑟夫·熊彼特参与规划的开罗以北那座庄园。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-165"></a>[165](#note-ch2-165)此外，在开罗和其他城市周围，土地开发公司开始把现有和潜在的农田改造成投机性住房项目，以及制砖厂和其他工业设施。因此，农田不仅变得更不肥沃，也变得更不可得，尽管有人许诺洪水控制会扩大耕种面积。相反，在大坝建成后的几年里，耕地面积实际上减少了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-166"></a>[166](#note-ch2-166)甚至 1960 年代规模大得多的阿斯旺高坝，在建成后的十年里也没有带来耕地面积的增加，主要原因是城市侵占。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-167"></a>[167](#note-ch2-167)然而，所有这些土地损失都无法与努比亚人所遭受的损失相比；努比亚是阿斯旺以南尼罗河瀑布群之间的地区。第一座阿斯旺大坝的修建淹没了他们土地的最北一百英里，而 1933 年大坝加高又淹没了整个上努比亚。后来的高坝形成了水库，把这个地区——田地和村庄——整个抹去了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-168"></a>[168](#note-ch2-168)

A further cost of the river’s destruction, and benefit for capitalisation, was that its floodplain was rendered not only less fertile, but available for conversion to roadways and housing. Human settlement had previously been confined mainly to the raised berms along the banks of the current river channel and of ancient, abandoned channels; to the uncultivated escarpment at the valley’s edge; and to the numerous ‘tells’ or human-formed settlement mounds rising above the floodplain, the result of building and rebuilding for centuries or millennia on the same site. With the elimination of the flood, the well-to-do could now expand their housing into the fields below the villages and towns, or build lavish *‘izbas*, or estates, in the countryside, including the estate that Joseph Schumpeter took a hand in planning, north of Cairo.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-165"></a>[165](#note-ch2-165) In addition, around Cairo and other cities, land development companies began converting both existing and potential farmland into speculative housing schemes, and into factories for brick-making and other industries. So agricultural land became not only less fertile but less available, despite the promise that flood control would extend the area of cultivation. Instead, the cultivated area actually decreased in the years after the building of the dam.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-166"></a>[166](#note-ch2-166) Even the much larger High Dam, in the 1960s, produced no increase in cultivated area in the decade after it was built, due largely to urban encroachment.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-167"></a>[167](#note-ch2-167) None of that loss of land, however, compared with the loss suffered by the people of Nubia, the country lying between the Nile cataracts south of Aswan. The building of the first Aswan Dam flooded the northernmost hundred miles of their land, while the raising of the dam in 1933 submerged all of Upper Nubia. The High Dam was later to form a reservoir that obliterated the entire country – fields and villages alike.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-168"></a>[168](#note-ch2-168)

校注：底本把1933年大坝加高的淹没区域写为“上努比亚”，并笼统称后来的水库抹去整个地区。密歇根大学凯尔西博物馆对阿斯旺坝及淹没遗址的介绍使用“下努比亚”。此处应注意上下努比亚及实际淹没范围的区别；正文保留原作表述。 https://exhibitions.kelsey.lsa.umich.edu/galleries/Exhibits/AncientNubia/PhotoIntro.html

<a id="ch02-0089"></a>

最后，终止洪水不仅终结了一种耕作制度，也终结了塑造埃及本身的地质过程。每年冲积物的沉积形成了三角洲——如今大多数埃及人在那里生活和耕作——并把海岸线作为宽阔的扇形向地中海延伸。几千年来，每年增加几毫米的尼罗河沉积物挡住了大海，并抵消了三角洲的逐渐下沉；这种下沉<a id="page-90"></a>〔原书第90页〕是由下方地层的压实造成的。失去洪水之后，土地继续下沉，而二十世纪后期以来的全球变暖又使海平面稳步上升，这一改造地球的过程被推向反面。到二十一世纪初，每年有数十米海岸线被大海夺去。混凝土海防设施可以限制部分地表损失，却无法阻止海水渗入下方地下水。三角洲北三分之一的地下水变成咸水，越来越无法支撑农业；中间三分之一的地下水变成半咸水，对大多数作物有害。尼罗河变成一个大半封闭的水库，只有不到 10% 的水到达地中海，大海如今正在使土地盐碱化。所有这一切，甚至发生在全球持续变暖将带来的更大海平面上升之前。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-169"></a>[169](#note-ch2-169)

Finally, ending the flood brought to an end not just a system of farming but the geological process through which Egypt itself had been formed. The annual deposit of alluvium had formed the Delta where the majority of Egyptians now lived and farmed, building out its shoreline as a wide fan into the Mediterranean. Over millennia, the annual increment of a few millimetres of Nile sediment had kept the sea at bay and counteracted the gradual sinking of the Delta, a phenomenon <a id="page-90-en"></a>〔原书第90页〕caused by the compaction of the strata beneath. Deprived of the flood, with the land continuing to sink, and with global warming from the late twentieth century causing the sea level steadily to rise, this terraforming process was pushed into reverse. By the early twenty-first century, dozens of metres of coastline were being lost to the sea each year. Concrete sea defences could limit some of the surface loss but could not prevent the sea’s infiltration of the groundwaters below. The groundwater of the northern third of the Delta turned saline, increasingly unable to support agriculture, and that of the middle third became brackish, rendering it harmful to most crops. With the Nile turned into a largely enclosed reservoir, less than 10 per cent of its water reaching the Mediterranean, the sea was now salting the earth. All this was occurring even before the much larger rise in sea levels that continued global warming would bring.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-169"></a>[169](#note-ch2-169)

<a id="ch02-0090"></a>

洪水脉冲的逐渐消除，伴随着产权和土地税的转变。在十九世纪重新工程化尼罗河之前，开罗政府征收农业税，每年根据哪些土地被淹、种植什么作物进行调整。在中世纪，种植小麦、亚麻等的土地有不同的税类，而前一年种植过这些作物或其他耗尽土壤肥力的作物的土地也有不同税类。这些土地会以不同方式评估，以允许休耕期，或种植能恢复土地肥力的作物。虽然税收不是按产量的百分比征收，但仍根据肥力、洪水脉冲和作物性质的变化进行校准。十九世纪，政府在包税制时期之后恢复直接征税时，取消了税收、作物与土壤肥力之间的这种关系。

The gradual elimination of the flood pulse was accompanied by a transformation in property rights and land taxes. Prior to the re-engineering of the Nile in the nineteenth century, governments in Cairo imposed taxes on agriculture that were adjusted each year according to variations in which lands were flooded and what crops were planted. In the medieval period, there were different tax categories for land planted with wheat, flax, and so on, but also for land planted the previous year with those or other crops that exhausted the soil. These would be assessed differently to allow periods of fallowing, or planting with crops that restored the land’s fertility. While the tax was not charged as a percentage of the yield, it was calibrated nevertheless to the variation in fertility, flood pulse, and the nature of the crop. In the nineteenth century, when the government restored direct taxation after the period of subcontracted tax farming, it eliminated this relation between tax payments, crops and soil fertility.

<a id="ch02-0091"></a>

与上一代人修建的苏伊士运河一样，大坝本身也是一个具有耐久性——延展的时间和工程尺度——的项目，这使它可供资本化。尺度之所以重要，不是因为它产生更高效或更有效的灌溉机制，而是因为它创造一台耐久的信用机器。它建造了信用创造所需的未来。

Like the Suez Canal a generation earlier, the dam itself was a project with a durability – an extended temporal and technical scale – that made it available to capitalisation. Scale matters, not because it produces a more efficient or effective irrigation mechanism, but because it creates a durable credit machine. It builds the future that the creation of credit requires.

<a id="ch02-0092"></a>

自 1876 年债务危机以来，埃及的公共财政一直处于一名英国和一名法国控制者的监督之下。代表私人欧洲债权人的机构公共债务基金（Caisse de la Dette publique）直接接收政府收入，包括关税、铁路和电报收入，以及其他指定用于偿债的来源。该基金实际上作为一家私人经营的国库运作。这一安排限制政府未经该基金批准<a id="page-91"></a>〔原书第91页〕借款。尤其是法国债券持有人，拒绝批准大规模新贷款，包括为修建主要灌溉工程提供资金的贷款。

Since the debt crisis in 1876, Egypt’s public finances were under the supervision of a British and French controller. An agency representing private European creditors, the Caisse de la Dette publique (Fund for the Public Debt), received government revenues directly, including customs duties and railway and telegraph revenues, and other sources allocated to debt service. The Caisse operated in effect as a privately run treasury. The arrangement restricted the government from borrowing <a id="page-91-en"></a>〔原书第91页〕funds without the approval of the Caisse. The French bondholders, in particular, refused to approve large new loans, including a loan to finance the building of major irrigation works.

<a id="ch02-0093"></a>

阿斯旺大坝的融资不是通过政府直接借款，而是通过在伦敦货币市场创造货币。英国金融家欧内斯特·卡塞尔设计了一个不同寻常的投资方案来支付大坝费用。这不仅是关于大坝如何获得融资、一项大型工程如何找到信用供给的问题，更是关于金融*本身如何被工程化*、大规模信用的创造如何找到一种使其得以产生的物质结构的问题。

The Aswan Dam was financed, not by direct government borrowing, but by creating money on the London money markets. Ernest Cassel, the British financier, created an unusual investment scheme to pay for the dam. This is not just a question of how the dam was financed, how a large engineering work found a supply of credit, but more, how finance *was engineered*, how the creation of large-scale credit found a material structure through which it could come into being.

<a id="ch02-0094"></a>

大坝施工合同授予一家英国工程公司。工程款不是以现金支付，而是以“灌溉凭证”支付。这是一种由卡塞尔及其合伙人创造的货币形式；他们在伦敦成立了灌溉投资公司，并通过英格兰银行发行这些凭证。投资者分期购买面值 100 英镑的凭证，从其银行账户开出支票，先支付 5 英镑的初始支票，再加上 3 英镑的费用，使凭证总成本达到 103 英镑。这一切都不涉及支付过去储蓄的资金：它由埃及农民未来的税款提供资金。购买股份的投资者的银行通过把每笔支票付款记作投资者的借方、并把相同金额记入英格兰银行贷方，创造出信用货币。后者反过来在施工各阶段完成后，用三年时间把资金记入承包商账户的贷方。与此同时，埃及政府本应对通过新蓄水系统获得灌溉水的土地增税；然而，如前所述，获得灌溉的土地面积——因而税收的增加——远低于大坝支持者的预期，而且土地产量开始急剧下降。三年后，埃及政府开始每半年从这些税收中向凭证持有人的银行账户付款，通过卡塞尔转交，并附加相当于约 6% 利率的额外金额。利息的三分之二归凭证持有人，三分之一归卡塞尔及其合伙人。为了组织一笔 270 万英镑的贷款——其中没有他本人的任何资本——作为项目企业家的卡塞尔赚取了估计 50 万至 100 万英镑的费用。大坝是一台攫取远不止灌溉水的机器。

The contract for the construction of the dam was awarded to a British engineering firm. The work was paid not in cash but in ‘irrigation certificates’. This was a form of money created by Cassel and his partners, who set up the Irrigation Investment Corporation in London and issued the certificates through the Bank of England. Investors purchased £100 certificates in instalments, by writing cheques on their bank accounts, starting with an initial cheque for £5, with a £3 fee bringing the total cost of the certificate to £103. None of this involved the payment of funds saved from the past: it was funded by the future tax payments of Egyptian farmers. The banks of the investors buying shares created credit money, by marking each cheque payment as a debit against the name of the investor and crediting the same amount to the Bank of England. The latter, in turn, credited the funds to the contractor’s account, over three years, as the stages of construction were completed. Meanwhile, the Egyptian government was supposed to increase the tax on lands that received irrigation waters via the new storage system, although, as noted, the areas of land irrigated, and thus the increase in taxes, were much less than the dam’s proponents had anticipated, and yields from the land began a sharp decline. After three years, the Egyptian government began making payments every six months from these tax revenues to bank accounts of the holders of the certificates, through Cassel, with an additional amount equivalent to an interest rate of about 6 per cent. Two-thirds of the interest went to the certificate holders, and one-third to Cassel and his partners. For organising a loan of £2.7 million, in which none of his own capital was involved, Cassel, the entrepreneur of the project, earned a fee estimated at £500,000 to £1 million. The dam was a machine for capturing much more than irrigation waters.

<a id="ch02-0095"></a>

这笔惊人的交易只是开始。卡塞尔及其合伙人在<a id="page-92"></a>〔原书第92页〕阿斯旺大坝下游不远的康翁波平原投资建立了甘蔗种植园。该方案吸引数百名小投资者和佃农，他们难以获得回报或维持生计。卡塞尔还成立了一个银行财团，命名为埃及国民银行，以向埃及政府提供更多信贷。在大坝修建宣布之前，卡塞尔设计了一套同样复杂的安排，以收购前赫迪夫的那些被称为达伊拉·萨尼亚（Daira Saniya）或王室领地的大片糖业种植园——拥有二十二座榨糖厂——以及棉花庄园，它们已被抵押给他的欧洲债权人。大坝的修建急剧提高了这些地产的价值。其中一些以巨额利润转手，而购买它们的初始信用同样是由相关金融家创造的。工业设备以及部分糖业地产由卡塞尔保留，他与欧内斯特·克罗尼耶和当地投资者合伙，创建了埃及糖业公司——正如我们在上一章所见，约瑟夫·熊彼特的企业家理论正是在那里诞生的。

This astounding deal was just the start. Cassel and his partners invested in the creation of a sugar plantation on the Plain of Kom Ombo, <a id="page-92-en"></a>〔原书第92页〕just downstream from the dam at Aswan. The scheme drew in hundreds of small investors and tenant farmers, who struggled to make a return or a living. Cassel also set up a banking consortium, which he named the National Bank of Egypt, to extend further credit to the Egyptian government. Before the building of the dam was announced, Cassel engineered an equally intricate arrangement to acquire the former Khedive’s sugar plantations, the vast landholdings known as the Daira Saniya, or royal domain, with twenty-two cane-pressing mills, and cotton estates, which had been mortgaged to his European creditors. The construction of the dam sharply increased the value of the estates. Some of these were turned over at large profit, again with the credit for their initial purchase created by the financiers involved. The industrial plant and some of the sugar estates were retained by Cassel, in partnership with Ernest Cronier and local investors, who created the Egyptian Sugar Company – the place, as we saw in the last chapter, where Joseph Schumpeter’s theory of the entrepreneur was born.

<a id="ch02-0096"></a>

此后，几十名、最终几百名企业家开始意识到糖业和棉花庄园的资本化机会。欧洲人有时与开罗当地合伙人一起，成立土地投资公司。这些公司会取得边缘土地的所有权，这些土地如今可以被平整、灌溉，并出租给耕作者。资本化按十四年计算：土地如今可以出售，但不是按过去地块易手的旧价格（与土地税水平相关），而是（如同给公司股份估值的新方法一样）按照一种新颖的计算机制：其价值基于预期未来收益，为年净利的十四倍。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-170"></a>[170](#note-ch2-170)地价和地租几乎一夜之间翻了一番。但为了得到这个价格，一半土地必须种上棉花。棉花需要三年轮作，以防土壤迅速枯竭。由于资本化建立在让一半而非三分之一的土地种棉花的基础上，土壤枯竭加速，产量开始急剧下降。

Following this, dozens and eventually hundreds of other entrepreneurs began to realise the opportunities for the capitalisation of sugar and cotton estates. Europeans, sometimes with local Cairo partners, set up land investment companies. These would acquire title to marginal lands that could now be levelled, irrigated, and leased to cultivators. Capitalisation was calculated over fourteen years: land could now be sold, not at the old rates at which parcels changed hand, related to levels of land tax, but (as with the new method of valuing company shares) according to a novel mechanism of calculation: its value was based on estimated future earnings, at fourteen times the annual net profit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-170"></a>[170](#note-ch2-170) Land prices and rents doubled almost overnight. But, to obtain this price, half the land had to be planted in cotton. Cotton requires a three-year rotation, to prevent rapid depletion of the soil. With capitalisation based on keeping half rather than one-third of the land in cotton, soil depletion accelerated and yields began their sharp decline.

<a id="ch02-0097"></a>

### 土地开发

### Land Development

<a id="ch02-0098"></a>

与此同时，更大规模的未来可以建立在尼罗河大坝所许诺的未来之上。这个结构不仅工程化了资本化农业的新可能性；它还第一次暗示，英国占领有着长期的未来，而正是这一占领批准并促成了大坝的建设。这个预期的政治未来，为<a id="page-93"></a>〔原书第93页〕其他长期结构提供了框架。随着房地产开发公司成立，在开罗建设新街区，以及像马阿迪和赫利奥波利斯这样的整个郊区——通常与给开发商的垄断特许权相结合，以经营电车和公用事业——出现了城市土地繁荣。“根据 1914 年的数字，在 2.1 亿埃及镑（埃及外国资本投资总额）中，1.663 亿镑，即 79%，属于非生产性投资（公共债务、抵押贷款和银行）；2,650 万镑，即 12.6%，属于运输和贸易；只有 1,050 万镑，即仅仅 5%，属于工业和建筑。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-171"></a>[171](#note-ch2-171)

Meanwhile, much larger futures could be built on the future promised by the dam. The structure engineered not just new possibilities for capitalised agriculture; it implied, for the first time, a long-term future for the British occupation that sanctioned and facilitated the dam’s construction. The projected political future provided the frame for <a id="page-93-en"></a>〔原书第93页〕other long-term structures. There was an urban land boom, as property development companies were formed to build new neighbourhoods in Cairo, and entire suburbs like Maadi and Heliopolis, typically built in association with monopoly concessions to developers to run tramways and utilities. ‘According to the figures given for 1914, out of £E210,000,000 (the total sum of foreign capital investments in Egypt), 166,300,000 or 79 per cent was accounted for by non-productive investments (public debt, mortgage and banks), 26,500,000, or 12.6 per cent, by transport and trade and only 10,500,000 or a mere 5 per cent by industry and construction.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-171"></a>[171](#note-ch2-171)

<a id="ch02-0099"></a>

请注意，资本化的权力不必掌握在私人手中。完全可以把未来支付的非凡意外之财转化为公共收入，用于社会目的。最初在某些情况下，事情就是这样发生的。例如，埃及干线铁路从 1850 年代开始由政府修建。统治政权拒绝把权利授予私人公司。到 1904 年，铁路占政府收入的 20%——尽管政府因 1870 年代的债务危机不得不把这些收入用于偿债。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch2-172"></a>[172](#note-ch2-172)

Note that the powers of capitalisation did not have to be placed in private hands. It would have been perfectly possible to convert the extraordinary windfalls from future payments into public revenue and use them for social ends. Initially, in some cases, this happened. For example, the mainline Egyptian railways, starting in the 1850s, were built by the government. The ruling regime refused to grant the rights to private companies. By 1904, the railways were responsible for 20 per cent of government revenue – although it had been forced by the 1870s debt crisis to commit those revenues to the repayment of debt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch2-172"></a>[172](#note-ch2-172)

<a id="ch02-0100"></a>

资本如何消费未来？我们又如何对此视而不见？对未来的消费看起来是投机性的、脆弱的、人造的。但事实上，它通过一套必须被工程化的攫取技术装置运作。这种工程化使资本家和殖民者——正如我们在埃及案例中所探讨的——能够把从未来攫取的收入描绘成技术进步的产物，而不是那些日后以自己的生活偿还这笔收入的人所创造的产物。我们已在运河、蓄水系统、动物和作物的层面上仔细研究了这种工程化，因为技术进步和经济进步的主张对我们的想象力有如此强大的控制力——强大到我们甚至不再听见水车曾经如何吱呀作响。这种工程化不一定带来财富或福祉的改善——事实上，它可能使两者恶化。它的设计主要是为了改善对未来的攫取。

How does capital consume the future? And how are we made blind to this? The consumption of the future appears speculative, flimsy, and artificial. But, in fact, it works through a technical apparatus of capture, which must be engineered. This engineering allows the capitalist, and the coloniser, as we have explored in the case of Egypt, to portray the revenue captured from the future as the product, not of those whose lives later on repay it, but of technical improvements. We have studied the engineering closely, at the level of canals, storage systems, animals, and crops, for the claim of technical improvement and economic progress has such a hold on our imagination – a hold so powerful that we no longer even hear how the waterwheel used to squeak. The engineering does not necessarily produce any improvement in wealth or well-being – in fact, it can make those worse. It was designed mainly to improve the capture of the future.


# 第三章　作为绕道的资本主义

<a id="ch03-0001"></a>

<a id="page-94"></a>〔原书第94页〕

<a id="page-94-en"></a>〔原书第94页〕

<a id="ch03-0002"></a>

## 第三章　作为绕道的资本主义

## 3 Capitalism as a Detour

<a id="ch03-0003"></a>

在新冠疫情的众多受害者中，有一个不太引人注意的意外伤亡。2020 年的大封锁把世界推入大萧条以来最严重的经济衰退。数百万人因新冠病毒丧生，与此同时，更广泛的人失去了生计和经济前途。然而，在这场苦难之中，世界各地的股市在经历一次急剧下挫后，却经历了非凡增长的一年。股市的扩张紧随主要央行决定创造数万亿美元的新资产、几乎使资产负债表规模翻倍之后；它们使用的是被称为量化宽松的创造货币的方法，这种方法最早在应对 2008 年全球金融危机时被广泛部署。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-001"></a>[1](#note-ch3-001)银行资产的倍增拯救了金融市场。而伤亡的，是任何仍然认为我们的常识或经济学教科书懂得货币如何运作的残留信念。

Among the many victims of the Covid-19 pandemic, there was a minor, unexpected casualty. The Great Lockdown of 2020 pushed the world into the worst economic recession since the Great Depression. The loss of millions of lives to the coronavirus was accompanied by an even wider loss of livelihoods and economic futures. Yet, amid this hardship, stock markets around the world, after a sharp setback, experienced a year of extraordinary growth. Their expansion followed the decision of leading central banks to create trillions of dollars of new assets, almost doubling the size of their balance sheets, using the method of manufacturing money known as quantitative easing, first widely deployed in response to the global financial crisis of 2008.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-001"></a>[1](#note-ch3-001) The multiplying of banking assets saved the financial markets. The casualty was any lingering claim that our common sense, or the textbooks of economics, understood how money works.

<a id="ch03-0004"></a>

为什么理解货币如此困难？这种困难又告诉了我们什么关于资本主义的事情？商业银行、利率、股票和债券交易、衍生品合约、量化宽松，以及创造信用和债务的各种机制的其他部分，似乎都处于我们日常理解和经济生活标准模型之外。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-002"></a>[2](#note-ch3-002)为什么金融业——它不知怎地制造了所有这些货币——比其他制造业分支更不透明？金融业更技术化、更抽象吗？货币工具的设计和生产，肯定不可能比微处理器或新冠疫苗的制造更复杂吧？答案不在于货币作为一个过程的<a id="page-95"></a>〔原书第95页〕复杂性，而在于这个过程与我们用来理解它的观念之间的关系。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-003"></a>[3](#note-ch3-003)

Why is it so hard to make sense of money? And what does this difficulty tell us about capitalism? The apparatus of commercial banking, interest rates, equity and bond trading, derivative contracts, quantitative easing, and other parts of the various mechanisms that create credit and debt seem to lie outside both our everyday comprehension and standard models of economic life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-002"></a>[2](#note-ch3-002) Why is the industry of finance, which somehow manufactures all this money, rendered so much more opaque than other branches of manufacturing? Is the financial industry more technical, or more abstract? Surely the design and production of monetary instruments cannot be more complex than the making of a microprocessor, say, or a Covid-19 vaccine? The answer lies not in the <a id="page-95-en"></a>〔原书第95页〕complexity of money as a process, but in the relation between the process and the ideas with which we make sense of it.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-003"></a>[3](#note-ch3-003)

<a id="ch03-0005"></a>

理解货币的困难，源于它的制造方式塑造了解释它的科学。像货币本身一样，经济学这门学科通过把其生产装置的大部分置于视野之外来运作。经济学是一种知识形式，它也像货币一样，通过假定一个极其简单的区分来运作：对象与其价格之间的差别，物质与货币之间的差别，金融与社会之间的差别，真实世界与其表象之间的差别。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-004"></a>[4](#note-ch3-004)这些问题不仅关乎理解货币。资本的托词正是通过这些看似自明的区分生产出来的。它们背后是我们对现代生活形式如何产生、如今又如何被治理的理解。要处理这些问题，除其他事项外，需要考察殖民和奴役在创造现代货币体系中的位置；所谓工业革命中进入制造业和雇佣劳动的*绕道*，这次绕道使货币显得仅仅是支付手段或价值的代表；以及十九世纪后期现代公司和现代银行作为新的货币创造机器的兴起。那些十九世纪后期的安排，部分正是在上一章埃及所探讨的那类帝国计划中出现的。这类计划既促成又掩盖了货币的制造，以及世界似乎被划分为金融与实体、虚构与物质——以及殖民者与被殖民者——这一更广泛效果的产生。

The difficulty in understanding money arises from the way its manufacturing has shaped the science that explains it. Like money itself, the discipline of economics works by placing out of sight much of the apparatus of its production. Economics is a form of knowledge that operates, again like money, by assuming a remarkably simple distinction: the difference between an object and its price, between the material and the monetary, between finance and society, and between the real world and its representation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-004"></a>[4](#note-ch3-004) These issues concern not just making sense of money. The alibi of capital is produced through these apparently self-evident distinctions. Behind them lies our understanding of how modern forms of life came into being, and how they are governed today. Addressing them requires, among other things, considering the place of colonisation and enslavement in creating modern systems of money, the *detour* into manufacturing and wage labour in the so-called industrial revolution that made money appear to be merely a means of payment or representation of value, and then the rise of the modern corporation and the modern bank in the later nineteenth century as new machines of money creation. Those late-nineteenth-century arrangements emerged in part in the kinds of imperial schemes explored in Egypt in the previous chapter. Such schemes facilitated and disguised both the making of money and the creating of the wider effect of a world that seemed divided into the financial and the real, the fictitious and the material – and the colonising and the colonised.

<a id="ch03-0006"></a>

### 货币不是实物

### Money Is No Object

<a id="ch03-0007"></a>

什么是货币？直到最近，答案似乎显而易见。我们把它视为一种物品，形状是纸币和硬币，是它在手中呈现的日常样貌。我们主要把它的生产与现代国家的权力联系起来，因为政府授权铸造和印刷货币，并确立缴税和其他债务必须使用的法定货币。经济学家传统上用三种功能来定义它的用途。它是交换媒介，使人们能够在不诉诸物物交换的情况下交易商品和服务；它是记账单位，使企业能够记录商品价格并计算利润；它还是储存财富的手段，形式便于囤积、取用和交换。这些关于货币<a id="page-96"></a>〔原书第96页〕创造和使用的描述，几乎仍见于每一本经济学教科书，与我们的日常经验相符。

What is money? The answer until recently seemed obvious. We thought of it as an object, in the shape of banknotes and coins, the everyday appearance it took in our hands. We associated its production largely with the powers of the modern state, since governments authorise the coining and printing of currency and establish the legal tender in which taxes and other debts must be paid. Economists conventionally defined its use in terms of three functions. It is a medium of exchange, enabling people to trade goods and services without resorting to barter; it is a unit of account, allowing business firms to record the prices of goods and calculate their profits; and it is a means of storing wealth, in a form that is easy to stockpile, retrieve, and exchange. These descriptions of <a id="page-96-en"></a>〔原书第96页〕the creation and use of money, still found in almost every textbook of economics, corresponded to our ordinary experience.

<a id="ch03-0008"></a>

然而今天，关于货币的正统和常识观点已被认为是不充分的。二十一世纪最初几十年的金融动荡，揭示出需要一种不同的理解。金融繁荣和房地产泡沫是由担保债务凭证和其他复杂货币产品的创造所推动的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-005"></a>[5](#note-ch3-005)这些产品在 2007—8 年崩溃后引发的银行业危机，需要通过量化宽松的做法前所未有地创造银行信用。2020 年 3 月新冠疫情引发的流动性危机，导致信用货币更大幅度的扩张。在这些事件中，货币不仅是为了促进贸易或记账而被创造。它以新颖的方式、在新的尺度上被工程化。货币是一种装置，在其制造过程中，非凡形式的财富、不稳定和负债被创造出来。

Today, however, the orthodox and common-sense view of money is recognised as inadequate. The financial turbulence of the opening decades of the twenty-first century revealed the need for a different understanding. Financial booms and real estate bubbles were driven by the creation of collateralised debt obligations and other complex monetary products.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-005"></a>[5](#note-ch3-005) The banking crisis that followed the collapse of those products in 2007–8 required an unprecedented creation of bank credit, through the practice of quantitative easing. The liquidity crisis triggered by the Covid-19 pandemic in March 2020 led to an even larger expansion of credit money. In these events, money was not just created to facilitate trade or accounting. It was engineered in novel ways on a new scale. Money was a device in whose manufacture extraordinary forms of wealth, instability, and indebtedness were being created.

<a id="ch03-0009"></a>

鉴于这些事件，一种对货币的不同理解出现了——或者更确切地说，被重新发现了。就其生产而言，政府创造的货币极少。尽管货币与国家货币和现代国家的权威相关联，但几乎所有货币的生产都不是政府财政部或中央银行的工作，而是公司利益集团的工作。在现代，商业银行获得了一种被经济学教科书大多忽视的巨大权力，可以大规模生产货币。就其用途而言，货币不仅是促进交换或提供财富储存手段的物品，而且是一种与未来的关系。它作为信用而产生，即对延期支付或未来商品的当下权利。无论其进一步用途如何，货币的起源和主要重要性在于索取未来收入，并且——这对我们所谓的资本主义至关重要——把这种未来索取权资本化，使其在当下以折价形式可得。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-006"></a>[6](#note-ch3-006)

In light of these events, a different understanding of money has emerged – or, rather, has been rediscovered. In terms of its production, very little money is created by the government. Despite its association with national currencies and the authority of modern states, the production of almost all money is the work not of government treasuries or central banks but of corporate interests. In modern times, commercial banks have acquired an immense power, largely ignored by the textbooks of economics, to mass produce money. In terms of its use, money is not just an object that facilitates exchange or provides a means of storing wealth, but a relation to the future. It comes into being as credit, or the present right to a deferred payment or good. Whatever its further uses, the origin and main importance of money lies in claiming a future income and, crucial to what we call capitalism, capitalising that future claim and making it available at a discount in the present.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-006"></a>[6](#note-ch3-006)

<a id="ch03-0010"></a>

然而，正如我们将看到的，银行并非单独行动创造货币。如果未来没有被组织成可靠的支付来源，对未来支付的索取权就不会有效。银行只有在更广泛的未来攫取机制中，才获得制造货币的权力。这些机制包括贸易、基础设施和制造业的形式，法律及其执行系统，以及衡量、预测和简化当下与未来关系的装置。金融常与未来的另一个方面相关，即其不确定性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-007"></a>[7](#note-ch3-007)然而，不确定性只有在作为从对未来的有效支配力内部产生并调节这种支配力的要素时，才具有重要意义。

As we will see, however, banks do not create money by acting alone. A claim on a future payment would be ineffective if that future was not organised as a reliable source of payment. Banks acquire the power to manufacture money only as part of wider mechanisms for the capture of the future. Those mechanisms include forms of trade, infrastructure, and manufacturing, systems of law and its enforcement, and devices that measure, forecast, and simplify the relation between the present and the future. Finance is often associated with a different aspect of the future, its uncertainty.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-007"></a>[7](#note-ch3-007) However, uncertainty is significant only as an element that arises from within, and modulates, an effective power over the future.

<a id="ch03-0011"></a>

<a id="page-97"></a>〔原书第97页〕尽管新近才可见，这种把货币理解为对未来商品或支付的有效索取权、因而是一种支配未来的权力关系的观点并不新鲜。我们可以回到一百多年前的二十世纪初，当时货币的现代权力首次被清晰阐述，并克服经济学中因遗忘这项工作而来的“失去的世纪”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-008"></a>[8](#note-ch3-008)被遗忘的关键文本之一，是 1913 年一篇题为“什么是货币？”的短文。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-009"></a>[9](#note-ch3-009)其作者阿尔弗雷德·米切尔—英尼斯最初不是在纽约或伦敦，而是在开罗了解现代金融的。他在英国占领时期于那里度过了职业生涯的形成期，担任埃及财政部副部长。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-010"></a>[10](#note-ch3-010)正如我们在前几章所见，那些年的埃及是新形式信用货币发展的重要场所。

<a id="page-97-en"></a>〔原书第97页〕Although newly visible, this understanding of money as an effective claim on future goods or payments, and thus a relation of power over the future, is not new. We can turn back more than a hundred years to the early twentieth century, when the modern powers of money were first clearly articulated, and overcome the ‘lost century’ in economics that followed the forgetting of this work.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-008"></a>[8](#note-ch3-008) One of the key forgotten texts is a short essay of 1913 entitled ‘What Is Money?’<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-009"></a>[9](#note-ch3-009) Its author, Alfred Mitchell-Innes, had first learned about modern finance not in New York or London, but in Cairo. He spent the formative years of his career there during the British occupation, serving as under-secretary at the Egyptian Ministry of Finance.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-010"></a>[10](#note-ch3-010) As we saw in the previous chapters, Egypt in those years was an important site for the development of new forms of credit money.

<a id="ch03-0012"></a>

1908 年，米切尔—英尼斯结束在开罗的任务后，被派往华盛顿。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-011"></a>[11](#note-ch3-011)五年后，他在《银行法杂志》上发表了“什么是货币？”。次年，在“许多经济学家和大学教授”反对他的观点后，该杂志编辑邀请他发表第二篇文章，更详细地阐述他所说的“货币信用理论”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-012"></a>[12](#note-ch3-012)约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯刚刚完成他自己第一项关于货币的研究《印度货币与财政》，他称赞米切尔—英尼斯的工作表明，传统的货币史“纯属神话”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-013"></a>[13](#note-ch3-013)约瑟夫·熊彼特——我们知道他也曾与米切尔—英尼斯在同一时期短暂在开罗工作——已于 1911 年用德文发表了自己版本的货币信用理论，尽管其英译本《经济发展理论》直到 1934 年才问世。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-014"></a>[14](#note-ch3-014)

After ending his assignment in Cairo, in 1908 Mitchell-Innes was posted to Washington.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-011"></a>[11](#note-ch3-011) He published ‘What Is Money?’ in *The Banking Law Journal* five years later. The following year, after ‘many economists and college professors’ objected to his views, the journal’s editor invited him to publish a second article, spelling out in more detail what he termed ‘The Credit Theory of Money’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-012"></a>[12](#note-ch3-012) John Maynard Keynes, who had just completed his own first study of money, *Indian Currency and Finance*, praised the work of Mitchell-Innes for showing that the conventional history of money ‘is quite mythical’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-013"></a>[13](#note-ch3-013) Joseph Schumpeter, who as we know had also worked briefly in Cairo in the same period as Mitchell-Innes, had published his own version of the credit theory of money in German in 1911, although its English translation, *The Theory of Economic Development*, did not appear until 1934.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-014"></a>[14](#note-ch3-014)

<a id="ch03-0013"></a>

“什么是货币？”揭示了两大谬误。第一种认为货币的价值来自黄金或白银。尽管纸币的使用远比硬币和金银条广泛，但据称货币所基于的黄金或白银“本位”被认为决定了它的价值，并使一种货币的数量能够用另一种货币来衡量。这种观念主导了十九世纪的经济思想，但在二十世纪中叶后基本被放弃。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-015"></a>[15](#note-ch3-015)第二种谬误常被错误地归于亚当·斯密，在米切尔—英尼斯揭穿它之后又盛行了百年，它把货币的起源和目的解释为提供促进交换的手段。早期社会通过物物交换交易商品。随着商业扩张，人们通过发展货币作为交换媒介，克服了用一种商品交换另一种商品的不便。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-016"></a>[16](#note-ch3-016)

‘What Is Money?’ exposed two fallacies. The first held that money derived its value from gold or silver. Even though paper notes were used far more widely than coins and bullion, the gold or silver ‘standard’ on which money was said to be based was thought to determine its worth, and to allow a quantity of one currency to be measured against another. This idea had governed economic thinking in the nineteenth century but was to be largely abandoned after the mid-twentieth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-015"></a>[15](#note-ch3-015) The second fallacy, often attributed falsely to Adam Smith and prevailing for another hundred years after Mitchell-Innes debunked it, explained the origin and purpose of money as providing a means to facilitate exchange. Early societies traded goods by barter. As commerce expanded, people overcame the inconvenience of bartering one good for another by developing the use of money as a medium of exchange.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-016"></a>[16](#note-ch3-016)

<a id="ch03-0014"></a>

<a id="page-98"></a>〔原书第98页〕米切尔—英尼斯表明，现有历史证据不支持这两种观点。第一，直到现代，人们从未试图用金属本位来定义“镑”“第纳尔”“美元”或任何其他货币的价值。这些名称表示记账单位。它们不是具有确定大小和重量的固定物体。统治者可能定期发行的金属硬币——通常用于支付士兵或其他服务，并作为税款收回——是其价值会变化的代币。金属货币在任何货币安排中都只占很小部分。它并不决定商人账目中记录的金额价值，而这些账目通常代表着最大、最稳定的货币体系。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-017"></a>[17](#note-ch3-017)

<a id="page-98-en"></a>〔原书第98页〕The available historical evidence, Mitchell-Innes showed, supported neither of these views. First, until modern times, no attempt was made to define the value of a ‘pound’, a ‘dinar’, a ‘dollar’, or any other money in terms of a metallic standard. These names denoted units of account. They were not fixed objects of a determined size and weight. The metal coins that rulers might periodically issue, typically to pay for soldiers or other services, and to reclaim as tax payments, were tokens whose worth varied. Metal-based money was a minor part of any monetary arrangement. It did not determine the value of the sums recorded in the accounts of merchants, which usually represented the largest and most stable system of money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-017"></a>[17](#note-ch3-017)

<a id="ch03-0015"></a>

第二，货币并非作为物物交换的便利替代品出现，而是作为信用机制出现。信用的使用见于最早文明的记录。在农业社会，信用与作物周期相关。商人和有权势的家庭向农民提供以田间作物为担保的信贷，收获后偿还。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-018"></a>[18](#note-ch3-018)每当商业关系和商人权力增强，信用就发挥更大的作用。在中世纪伊斯兰世界，商人使用*bay‘ bi-salam*（预购）的做法，以折扣价购买未来作物，或为应付政府的税款提供资金，作为创造信用货币并从中获利的手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-019"></a>[19](#note-ch3-019)同样，零售和批发业务通常也以信用进行。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-020"></a>[20](#note-ch3-020)“在大多数情况下，”一位十一世纪的主要穆斯林法学家写道，“只有赊销才能获得利润。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-021"></a>[21](#note-ch3-021)印度—伊斯兰世界的商人发展出为长途贸易延期支付的做法，广泛用于印度洋和阿拉伯地区的商业，后来传播到意大利，再传到欧洲其他地区。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-022"></a>[22](#note-ch3-022)这种方法通过一种在埃及和更广阔的阿拉伯世界被称为波斯术语*suftaja*的装置创造货币。它在英语中被称为汇票。

Second, money emerges not as a convenient substitute for exchange by barter but as a mechanism of credit. The use of credit is found in the records of the earliest civilisations. In agrarian societies it was associated with the crop cycle. Merchants and other powerful households extended credit to farmers against the crop in the field, to be repaid with the harvest.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-018"></a>[18](#note-ch3-018) Credit assumed a greater role whenever commercial relations and the power of merchants intensified. In the medieval Islamic world, merchants used the device of *bay*‘ *bi-salam* (forward buying) to purchase a future crop at a discount, or to cover a tax payment owed to the government, as a means of creating and profiting from credit money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-019"></a>[19](#note-ch3-019) Likewise, both retail and wholesale business were routinely conducted on credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-020"></a>[20](#note-ch3-020) ‘In most cases’, wrote a leading Muslim jurist of the eleventh century, ‘profit can only be achieved by selling for credit.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-021"></a>[21](#note-ch3-021) The practice of deferred payment for long-distance trade, developed by merchants of the Indo-Islamic world and widely used in the commerce of the Indian Ocean and the Arab lands, spread to Italy and then the rest of Europe.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-022"></a>[22](#note-ch3-022) The method allowed the creation of money through a device that in Egypt and the wider Arab world was known by the Persian term *suftaja*. It came to be known in English as a bill of exchange.

<a id="ch03-0016"></a>

就最简单形式而言，汇票的运作如下。货物供应商需要预先得到付款，以生产或获取商品并安排运输。购买货物的商人通过开具一张作为欠条的汇票来创造一种信用——这个过程被称为“开立汇票”。汇票是承诺在未来某个日期付款的票据，名义上是货物应交付的日期；按照惯例，这段期限是标准的天数、周数或月数，取决于货物类型和运输距离。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-023"></a>[23](#note-ch3-023)承诺的可靠性——即汇票的可靠性——取决于<a id="page-99"></a>〔原书第99页〕商人的声誉和实力。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-024"></a>[24](#note-ch3-024)这种实力通过诉诸法院和法律救济而延伸。在伊斯兰世界，法官及其法院在使商人能够发放信贷和收回欠款方面发挥了重要作用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-025"></a>[25](#note-ch3-025)在欧洲，诉诸法官和法律调解的机会可能更为有限，早期现代国家的形成可以追溯到对更强有力的收债机制的需求。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-026"></a>[26](#note-ch3-026)

In its simplest form, a bill of exchange works as follows. A supplier of goods requires to be paid in advance, to produce or acquire the merchandise and arrange its shipment. The merchant purchasing the goods creates a form of credit, by writing a bill of exchange as an IOU – the process known as ‘drawing a bill’. The bill is a promise to make the payment on a future date, nominally the date by which the goods are to be delivered and, by convention, a standard period of days, weeks, or months depending on the type of good and the distance it will travel.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-023"></a>[23](#note-ch3-023) The reliability of the promise – the soundness of the bill – rests on the <a id="page-99-en"></a>〔原书第99页〕reputation and strength of the merchant.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-024"></a>[24](#note-ch3-024) This strength was extended through access to courts and legal remedies. In the Islamic world, judges and their courts played an important role in enabling merchants to extend and reclaim debts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-025"></a>[25](#note-ch3-025) In Europe, where access to judges and the mediation of the law may have been more restricted, the formation of early modern states can be traced to the demand for stronger mechanisms for collecting debts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-026"></a>[26](#note-ch3-026)

<a id="ch03-0017"></a>

未来付款的承诺变成一种可以立即交易的金融工具。如果汇票的持票人急需资金来偿还先前债务或购买更多货物，他可以把汇票签给另一个商人，作为支付手段。一旦同一张汇票可以多次由商人签转或背书，它就发挥支付系统的作用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-027"></a>[27](#note-ch3-027)这种实践越是扩大——部分得益于索偿权的法律可执行性增强——它就变得越非个人化，越来越脱离特定的商人。这种脱离越深，支付装置的“货币性”就越强。尽管汇票与长途贸易有关，一种被称为“融通汇票”的变体提供了另一种创造信用的手段，其基础的商品销售是虚构的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-028"></a>[28](#note-ch3-028)

The promise of future payment becomes a financial instrument that can be immediately traded. A recipient of a bill who requires the funds right away, to settle an earlier debt or purchase further goods, can sign it over to another merchant as a means of payment. Once the same bill can be signed over, or endorsed, from merchant to merchant multiple times, it functions as a payment system.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-027"></a>[27](#note-ch3-027) The more the practice expands, thanks in part to the increasing legal enforceability of claims, the more impersonal it becomes, increasingly detached from specific merchants. The greater the detachment, the greater the ‘moneyness’ of the payment device. Although bills were associated with long-distance trade, a variant known as a ‘bill of accommodation’, where the underlying sale of goods was fictitious, provided a further means of creating credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-028"></a>[28](#note-ch3-028)

<a id="ch03-0018"></a>

并非所有信用都需要汇票。金融信用常常可能是非货币化信用和债务关系的延伸，在平常时期，这些关系构成了相互义务的结构，社会共同体正是通过它形成的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-029"></a>[29](#note-ch3-029)当地货物供应商通常只需把债务记录在商人账簿中，或通过口头协议，就向零售客户或其他企业提供信用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-030"></a>[30](#note-ch3-030)这种日常信用使用在欧洲资料中有广泛记载，在对中世纪和近代早期伊斯兰世界的研究中也同样明显。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-031"></a>[31](#note-ch3-031)与汇票不同，商人的账面信用不作为支付装置流通，也不总是与费用、折扣或利息支付相关。然而，信用余额可以通过开具本票来结清，本票作为信用货币在人们手中流转。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-032"></a>[32](#note-ch3-032)在欧洲，小企业也可能把账簿上的债务转换为汇票，尤其是那些长期未付的债务，或者它们也可能接受另一张汇票作为支付。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-033"></a>[33](#note-ch3-033)

Not all credit required bills. Financial credit may often have functioned as an extension of non-monetised relations of credit and debt, which, in ordinary times, created the fabric of reciprocal obligation through which social community was forged.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-029"></a>[29](#note-ch3-029) Local suppliers of goods would typically extend credit to retail customers or other businesses by simply recording a debt in the merchant’s books, or by oral agreement.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-030"></a>[30](#note-ch3-030) Widely documented in European sources, this everyday use of credit is equally evident in studies of the medieval and early modern Islamic world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-031"></a>[31](#note-ch3-031) Unlike bills of exchange, merchants’ book credit did not circulate as a payment device and was not always associated with a fee, discount, or interest payment. However, credit balances could be settled by writing promissory notes, which circulated from hand to hand as credit money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-032"></a>[32](#note-ch3-032) In Europe, small businesses might also convert the debts on their books into bills of exchange, especially those obligations that went unpaid for long periods, or they might accept another bill in payment.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-033"></a>[33](#note-ch3-033)

<a id="ch03-0019"></a>

商人会在彼此之间结清汇票，许多债务和债权相互抵消，任何未结余额都转换为本票。铸币很少使用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-034"></a>[34](#note-ch3-034)对于当地贸易，这种“结算”会偶尔进行，或者仅仅在账簿记满时进行。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-035"></a>[35](#note-ch3-035)历史上，定期集市<a id="page-100"></a>〔原书第100页〕为来自不同地区的商人结算账目提供了场合。在东地中海，这种做法延续到现代。“不多年前，在埃及的集市上，”米切尔—英尼斯评论道，人们仍能看到大型集市——通常与宗教节日相关——如何充当商人的票据交换所。除了活跃的零售贸易，大多数商人在集市上的主要业务——例如在埃及三角洲坦塔举行的与赛义德·巴达维节相关的集市——是“债务与债权的结算”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-036"></a>[36](#note-ch3-036)在近代早期欧洲，中世纪长途贸易的集市转变为“汇兑集市”，专门用于清算汇票。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-037"></a>[37](#note-ch3-037)据费尔南·布罗代尔所述，在最重要的集市、热那亚附近的皮亚琴察，每季度一次的票据交换和债务结算“支配了西方物质生活的节奏”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-038"></a>[38](#note-ch3-038)

Merchants would settle their bills among themselves, with many of the debts and credits cancelling one another out and any outstanding balance converted to a promissory note. Coinage was used only rarely.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-034"></a>[34](#note-ch3-034) For local trade, this ‘reckoning’ would happen on an occasional basis, or simply whenever an account book was full.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-035"></a>[35](#note-ch3-035) Historically, periodic fairs <a id="page-100-en"></a>〔原书第100页〕provided the occasion for the settling of accounts between merchants from different regions. In the Eastern Mediterranean, this practice continued into modern times. ‘Not many years ago at the fairs of Egypt,’ Mitchell-Innes remarked, one could still see how large fairs, often associated with religious festivals, served as clearing houses for merchants. Alongside a brisk retail trade, the main business for most merchants at the fair – such as that associated with the feast of Sayyid Badawi held at Tanta in the Egyptian Delta – was ‘the settlement of debts and credits’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-036"></a>[36](#note-ch3-036) In early modern Europe, the trade fairs of medieval long-distance trade were transformed into ‘exchange fairs’, dedicated to the clearing of bills.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-037"></a>[37](#note-ch3-037) According to Fernand Braudel, the quarterly exchange of paper and settling of debts at the most important of the fairs, at Piacenza, near Genoa, ‘dictated the rhythm of the material life of the West’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-038"></a>[38](#note-ch3-038)

<a id="ch03-0020"></a>

这里的“西方”指位于印度—伊斯兰世界伟大贸易路线和商业中心边缘的一组城邦和王国。这种边缘位置使欧洲商人，尤其是热那亚的汇兑银行家，与货币形成了一种不同寻常的关系，并获得了从其创造中获利的机会。与其他地方一样，商人银行家与王公们共存，后者试图通过垄断铸造金银币的权利来巩固对城市和领地的控制。尽管铸币在货币体系中通常只起很小作用，但从十六世纪起，拉丁欧洲的贵金属承担了不同角色。商人冒险家开始把黄金和白银不作为货币，而作为主要贸易品，这几乎是他们可以用来交换亚洲织物、香料和其他奢侈品的唯一商品。与此同时，争相控制这种贸易并武装其参与者的王公们，需要越来越多的金银币来支付官员和雇佣兵。票据汇兑的做法与贵金属贸易交织在一起，使控制汇兑集市的人能够从日益复杂的汇兑关系中获利——往往通过腐败手段。到十七世纪初，这种复杂性和腐败促成了热那亚体系的崩溃。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-039"></a>[39](#note-ch3-039)欧洲对亚洲贸易路线的武装篡夺，使信用创造走上了一条不同的道路。但它很快又会再次转变。

‘The West’ refers here to a collection of city-states and kingdoms located at the periphery of the great trade routes and commercial hubs of the Indo-Islamic world. The peripheral location gave European merchants, and especially the exchange bankers of Genoa, an unusual relation to money and the opportunities to profit from its creation. As elsewhere, merchant bankers coexisted with princes attempting to consolidate control over their cities and territories by monopolising the right to mint gold or silver coins. Although coinage typically played a small part in monetary systems, in Latin Europe from the sixteenth century, precious metals took on a different role. Merchant adventurers began to use gold and silver not as money but as a principal item of trade, almost the only commodity available to them to exchange for the fabrics, spices, and other luxury goods of Asia. At the same time, princes competing to control this trade and arm its protagonists required increasing access to gold and silver coinage, to pay their administrators and mercenaries. The practice of exchange by bills became entwined with trade in precious metals, allowing those who controlled the exchange fairs to profit – often corruptly – from the proliferating complexity of exchange relations. By the early seventeenth century, the complexity and the corruption helped bring about the collapse of the Genoese system.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-039"></a>[39](#note-ch3-039) Europe’s armed usurpation of Asian trade routes had set credit creation on a different path. But it would soon be transformed again.

<a id="ch03-0021"></a>

<a id="page-101"></a>〔原书第101页〕

<a id="page-101-en"></a>〔原书第101页〕

<a id="ch03-0022"></a>

### 货币成为折现的未来

### Money Becomes the Discounted Future

<a id="ch03-0023"></a>

随着欧洲长途贸易的主要路线及其日益增长的财富来源从地中海世界、黎凡特和红海转向大西洋和印度洋，欧洲货币创造的中心也从意大利转移到北方，先是十七和十八世纪的德国、安特卫普和阿姆斯特丹，然后到十九世纪的伦敦。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-040"></a>[40](#note-ch3-040)最大的英国商行——例如巴林家族，他们是来自英格兰西部的德国—荷兰裔棉花商人，以及罗斯柴尔德家族，他们先是在汉堡、后在曼彻斯特以布商身份发展业务——演变为商人银行家，专门交易和清算汇票，并承销和出售政府债务。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-041"></a>[41](#note-ch3-041)在十八和十九世纪，政府开始管制纸币发行，并指定一家国家银行或货币当局作为纸币的唯一发行者，把这些付款承诺转变为国家货币。英格兰作为该时期最成功的战争和殖民强国，开创了一种新颖的公私安排，由政府未来的税收收入保障纸币的价值。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-042"></a>[42](#note-ch3-042)然而，尽管集中印制的纸币成为一国法定货币的标志，它们在日常货币创造和供给中只起次要作用。随着私人银行从商人手中接管提供信用的主要角色，它们通过汇票、贷款和账簿余额创造货币——这些债务形式为购买未来商品和其他资产提供资金。这成为几乎所有货币的来源。

As the main routes of Europe’s long-distance trade and the source of its increasing wealth shifted from the Mediterranean world, the Levant, and the Red Sea to the Atlantic and Indian oceans, the hub of European money creation shifted from Italy to the north, first to Germany, Antwerp, and Amsterdam in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and then in the nineteenth century to London.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-040"></a>[40](#note-ch3-040) The largest English merchant houses – firms such as the Barings, who were cotton traders of German-Dutch origin from the English West Country, and the Rothschilds, who grew their business as cloth merchants first in Hamburg and then in Manchester – evolved into merchant bankers, specialising in trading and clearing bills of exchange and underwriting and selling government debt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-041"></a>[41](#note-ch3-041) In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, governments began to regulate the issuing of notes, and to designate a national bank or monetary authority as the sole issuer of banknotes, transforming these promises to pay into national currencies. England, emerging as the most successful war-making and colonising power of that period, had pioneered a novel public–private arrangement, in which the government’s future tax revenues secured the value of paper money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-042"></a>[42](#note-ch3-042) However, while centrally printed bank notes came to designate a country’s legal tender, they were to play only a minor role in the daily creation and supply of money. As private banks took over from merchants the main role in supplying credit, they created money through bills, loans, and ledger balances – forms of debt produced to fund the purchase of future goods and other assets. This became the source of almost all money.

<a id="ch03-0024"></a>

以英国为例，随着工厂雇佣劳动的发展，大部分货币仍采取私人创造的信用形式。大雇主很少用现金支付工资，况且现金也很难找到。正如我们将看到的，他们用代金券、商店赊账或其他实物工资形式支付工人，但也用越来越多的私人“乡村”或地方银行发行的信用票据支付。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-043"></a>[43](#note-ch3-043)当政府限制地方银行发行票据时，个人支票支付成为纸币的主要形式。直到 1913 年，约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯还评论说，在英国，支票是货币的主要形式，除了“某些自掏腰包的开支，例如铁路旅行，因为习俗要求现金支付”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-044"></a>[44](#note-ch3-044)但在十九世纪下半叶现代银行业巩固之前，英国——如同欧洲其他地方——的多数<a id="page-102"></a>〔原书第102页〕可即时使用的货币采取商店赊账、本票、地方私人银行票据和汇票的形式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-045"></a>[45](#note-ch3-045)

With the development of wage labour in factories, to remain with the case of Britain, most money continued to take the form of privately created credit. Large employers seldom paid wages in cash, which in any case was difficult to find. As we will see, they would pay workers in scrip, shop credit, or other forms of truck, but also with credit notes issued by the growing number of private ‘country’ or provincial banks.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-043"></a>[43](#note-ch3-043) When the government restricted the creation of notes by provincial banks, payment by personal cheque emerged as the main form of paper money. As late as 1913, John Maynard Keynes remarked that in Britain cheques were the principal form of money, except for ‘certain kinds of out-of-pocket expenditure, such as that on railway travelling, for which custom requires cash payment’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-044"></a>[44](#note-ch3-044) But, before the consolidation of modern banking in the second half of the nineteenth century, most <a id="page-102-en"></a>〔原书第102页〕ready money in Britain, as elsewhere in Europe, took the form of shop credit, promissory notes, local private bank notes, and bills of exchange.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-045"></a>[45](#note-ch3-045)

<a id="ch03-0025"></a>

理解货币作为信用而产生，不仅对金融史重要。信用货币是一种社会和技术关系，建立在当下确立并向前延伸的权力之上，以控制未来应偿还的债务。虽然货币体系也可以提供记账手段，但其主要目的源于创造一种以可靠的强制执行手段确保在未来偿付的债务。那个被强制执行的未来，是一个通过技术政治过程构建和控制的世界，它塑造生活方式和繁荣形式。货币不仅是代表价值或润滑某种更真实过程的物品。它是一种攫取的技术装置。然而，这种装置的力量部分在于它显得仅仅是一种抽象物，是更真实对象或过程的单纯符号或代表。

Understanding that money comes into being as credit matters not just for the history of finance. Credit money is a social and technical relation, built upon a power established in the present and extending forwards, to control a debt to be paid in the future. While a monetary system may also provide a means of keeping accounts, its main purpose derives from creating a debt that is paid forwards through a means of reliable enforcement. That enforced future is a world that is constructed and controlled through a technopolitical process, in ways that shape patterns of living and forms of prosperity. Money is not simply an object representing value or lubricating some more real process. It is a technical apparatus of capture. However, the strength of the apparatus rests in part on appearing as only an abstraction, the mere token or representation of a more real object or process.

<a id="ch03-0026"></a>

当这种跨时间关系规模化组织时，它成为债权人重要收入的来源。收益来自所谓的“贴现”实践。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-046"></a>[46](#note-ch3-046)货币是对未来资产或债务的当下索取权。由于获取该资产或债务支付的机会在未来，愿意接受汇票作为当前债务清偿的商人或金融商行，可以通过支付低于面值的价格来获得它。以较低价格购买汇票或未来付款承诺，被称为对汇票“贴现”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-047"></a>[47](#note-ch3-047)

When organised at scale, this relation across time becomes the source of significant income to the creditor. The gain arises from the practice known as ‘discounting’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-046"></a>[46](#note-ch3-046) Money is a present claim on a future asset or debt. Since access to that asset or debt payment lies in the future, the merchant or finance house willing to take a bill of exchange as settlement for a current debt can acquire it by offering less than its face value. The purchase of a bill, or promise of future payment, at a lower price is known as ‘discounting’ the bill.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-047"></a>[47](#note-ch3-047)

<a id="ch03-0027"></a>

其运作如下。一位商人接受一张承诺——比方说——六个月后支付 100 英镑的汇票时，可能会把其价值贴现 5%。当下的贴现值反映了延期付款发生前的时间延迟，以及这笔款项可能永远无法兑现的小风险。（那些后来被称为“贴现商行”的大型商人银行，可以通过持有庞大而多样化的票据组合，把接受汇票的风险降到最低。）持有 100 英镑汇票、急需用钱的人，只能从愿意接受汇票的商人那里得到 95 英镑。卖方满足了立即偿还先前债务或进行进一步采购的需要，代价是损失应得收入的 5%。此人以损失未来收入的形式付出代价。另一方面，以折扣价获得汇票的商人赚取了损失的那部分金额，用 95 英镑购买 100 英镑的收入。几乎不费力气，95 英镑的付款经过几个月就变成 100 英镑。汇票贴现大规模反复进行，成为重要且几乎无成本利润的来源。

This works as follows. A merchant accepting a bill that promises, say, a payment of £100 at a date six months in the future might discount its value by 5 per cent. The discounted value in the present reflects the delay in time until the deferred payment occurs, and the small risk that the payment might never materialise. (The large merchant banking houses, which came to be known as ‘discount houses’, could minimise the risk in accepting bills by maintaining a large and diverse portfolio.) The owner of the £100 bill who needs to spend the funds right away receives only £95 from the merchant willing to take it. The seller satisfies a need to pay off an earlier debt or make a further purchase immediately, at the cost of losing 5 per cent of the income due. That person pays a penalty in the form of a loss of future earnings. The merchant who acquires the bill at a discount, on the other hand, gains that lost amount, purchasing £100 of income for £95. For the expenditure of little or no effort, a payment of £95 is transformed by the passage of a few months into £100. Repeated on a wide scale, the discounting of bills became the source of significant and almost costless profits.

<a id="ch03-0028"></a>

<a id="page-103"></a>〔原书第103页〕正如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)所见，二十世纪的经济学家，尤其是美国的经济学家，逐渐把这种收益视为对“货币的时间价值”的回报，仿佛时间是货币的自然属性。但创造获利机会的推迟或延迟，并非简单的自然现象。延迟机制必须被工程化。

<a id="page-103-en"></a>〔原书第103页〕As we saw in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), economists in the twentieth century, especially in the United States, came to see this gain as a reward for ‘the time value of money’, as if time were a natural property of money. But the postponement or delay that creates the opportunity for gain is not a simple phenomenon of nature. The mechanism of delay had to be engineered.

<a id="ch03-0029"></a>

长途贸易的进行，为创造信用货币提供了不断扩大的机会。通过在购买与交货之间打开显著的时间缺口，异地交换产生了推迟或中断，汇票贴现者可以从中获利。随着延迟和贴现机会的激增，创造信用货币成为贸易的目的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-048"></a>[48](#note-ch3-048)大商人或商人银行的目标越来越不是获取商品并从异地的转售中获利，而是组织商品流动，以创造信用创造的机会，并从开立（创造）汇票与其付款之间的时间延迟中获利。距离和延迟迫使供应商接受汇票的折价，而商人或银行商行则从以折扣价获得未来付款中获利。大商人不是组织信用来促进贸易流动，而是组织贸易来促进信用创造。

The conduct of long-distance trade provided an expanding opportunity to create credit money. By opening a significant gap in time between a purchase and its delivery, non-local exchange generated the deferral or interruption from which a discounter of bills could make a gain. As the opportunities for delay and discounting proliferated, the creation of credit money became the purpose of trade.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-048"></a>[48](#note-ch3-048) The goal of the large merchant or merchant bank was increasingly not to acquire goods and profit from their resale in a different location. It was to organise the movement of goods in order to create opportunities for the creation of credit, and to profit from the delay in time between the drawing (creating) of a bill and its payment. The distance and delay forced the supplier to accept a discounted price for the bill, and the merchant or banking house profited from acquiring future payments at a discount. Rather than organising credit to facilitate the flow of trade, large merchants organised trade to facilitate the creation of credit.

<a id="ch03-0030"></a>

货币不仅仅是某种更真实事物的代表。它构成一种从未来获取收入的机制；在这个日益被组织起来——正如我们将看到的——以创造延迟和推迟形式的世界里，这些形式把未来设定为有利可图的抽取场所。

Money is not the mere representation of something more real. It forms a mechanism for acquiring income from the future, in a world increasingly organised, as we will see, to create forms of delay and postponement that set up the future as a place for profitable extraction.

<a id="ch03-0031"></a>

### 制造

### Fabrication

<a id="ch03-0032"></a>

正如前几章所示，我们不应把资本视为从过去积累起来的东西，而应视为从未来索取的东西。它代表的不是财富储备的积累，而是对预期付款的控制。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-049"></a>[49](#note-ch3-049)这种视角转变乍看意味着我们放弃了具体、物质关系的研究。它意味着把注意力从物质转向投机，从真实转向虚构。如果资本是一种与未来的关系，与尚未发生的事情的关系，那么它似乎建立在猜测和虚构之上，而不是建立在活生生的人类之间物质生活的实际生产之上。这种关于我们<a id="page-104"></a>〔原书第104页〕与时间关系的思想——未来是虚构的，只有过去是真实的——难以理解组织集体世界的当代方式。它反映了一种幼稚的历史思维模式：过去是已知事件和安排的事实序列，而未来主要作为预测存在——根据对过去的了解可能推测出的一系列“结果”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-050"></a>[50](#note-ch3-050)这种简单的历史主义不会让我们走得很远。我们已经知道，过去是被建构出来的——这里取fabrication一词积极的、制作与构建的含义。它是一组当下的指涉、记忆、报告、档案、遗产、痕迹和效果，我们试图组织、缓和并领会其力量。未来同样具有当下性。如果它是一种投射或建构，那它也是以具体方式被构建和投射的：人们在当下组织它、计算它、据此行动，并使它成为可供利用的东西。因此，目标不是放弃物质叙述——或者更好的说法，技术政治叙述——而是像关注过去的效果那样，关注未来被建构出来的效果。

We should think of capital, as previous chapters have shown, not as something accumulated from the past but as what is claimed from the future. It represents not the building up of a store of wealth, but the controlling of prospective payments.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-049"></a>[49](#note-ch3-049) This change in perspective suggests, at first, that we are abandoning the study of concrete, material relations. It implies refocusing attention from the material to the speculative, from the real to the fictitious. If capital is a relationship to the future, to something that has not yet happened, it seems to be built on conjectures and fabrications, rather than on the actual production of material life among living humans. Such thinking about our <a id="page-104-en"></a>〔原书第104页〕relationship to time, where the future is fictitious and only the past is real, has difficulty making sense of contemporary ways of organising the collective world. It reflects a naive historical mode of thought, in which the past is a factual sequence of known events and arrangements, while the future exists mainly as prognosis – the range of possible ‘outcomes’ that might be conjectured from a knowledge of the past.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-050"></a>[50](#note-ch3-050) This simple historicism will not get us far. We already know that the past is a fabrication, in the positive sense of that word. It is a present set of references, memories, reports, archives, legacies, traces, and effects whose force we attempt to organise, mitigate, and apprehend. The future is no less present. If it is a projection or fabrication, it is fabricated and projected in concrete ways that are organised, calculated, acted upon, and made available in the current moment. The aim, then, is not to abandon a material account – or better, a technopolitical one. It is to be as attentive to the fabricated effects of the future as we have been to the effects of the past.

<a id="ch03-0033"></a>

技术政治叙述可以区别于以物质生活生产为中心的历史叙述。理解资本的生产主义路径实际上也从未来开始，正如我们已经指出的，但那只是人类需求的未来。那些被假定的需求创造了一种需求，即提供维持人类生命所需之物的需求。物质需求通过组织生产过程得到满足。资本主义产生于这些生产过程的发展。在这种生产主义历史的核心，人们发现的不是通过在当下攫取预期收入而使未来负债的方法，而是改变当下生产物质商品以满足未来需求的方法。它的典型制度是生产商品的大型场所——现代工厂。它的典型支配形式是雇佣劳动，或由此产生的各种抽象。它的决定性事件是工业革命。

A technopolitical account can be distinguished from an account centred in the mere production of material life. The productivist approach to understanding capital actually starts in the future, as we already noted, but only a future of human needs. Those assumed needs create a demand, the demand to provide what is required to sustain human life. The material demand is met by organising processes of production. Capitalism arises from the development of those productive processes. At the centre of this productivist history, one finds not the methods of indebting the future by capturing prospective income in the present, but the transformation of present methods of producing material goods to meet the needs of the future. Its characteristic institution is the large-scale site of the production of goods, the modern factory. Its archetypal form of domination is wage labour, or the abstractions to which this gives rise. And its defining event is the industrial revolution.

<a id="ch03-0034"></a>

然而，如果我们把这一事件视为攫取未来方式的转变，它就具有不同的意义。这种转变使英国和欧洲在那些转型中的角色去中心化，有助于更好地理解殖民、战争和奴隶制在现代形成中的位置。它也使我们能够重新定位雇佣劳动——正如我们将看到的——不是作为支配借以发生的抽象之来源，而是作为另一种生产债务关系的装置，未来正是通过这些关系被施加负担，并在当下被攫取。

That event, however, takes on a different import if we approach it as a shift in modes of capturing the future. The shift decentres the role of Britain and Europe in those transformations, contributing to a better understanding of the place of colonisation, war-making, and slavery in the shaping of the modern era. And it allows us to resituate wage labour, as we will see, not as the source of the abstraction through which domination occurs, but as another apparatus for the production of debt relations through which the future is encumbered and captured in the present.

<a id="ch03-0035"></a>

<a id="page-105"></a>〔原书第105页〕英国工业革命的故事广为人知——其重要性也仍然常常被夸大。从 1780 年代到 1830 年的五十年间，英格兰西北部的纺织商人先重组了棉纱的纺制，最终重组了布匹的织造。他们摆脱了亚麻和羊毛行业以及加工来自奥斯曼帝国和印度的进口棉布时所使用的外放制，直接控制了大批工人，把他们聚集在水力“工厂”中（通常由其他用途改造而来），操作纺纱机和织布机，利用曼彻斯特周围山丘中湍急的溪流。乡村位置保证了低成本强制劳动力的供应，其中大多是儿童，由急于把贫民从账簿上划掉、把他们运往乡村教区的不断扩张的城市贫民习艺所提供。这些工厂生产的棉纱和后来的棉纺织品数量迅速增加。原棉没有一磅是当地种植的，成品布料也很少在本土消费，当地人仍偏好质量更好的羊毛和亚麻织物，或更精细的印度和波斯织物。较不耐用、质量较低的机器织棉布大多运往国外，最初是欧洲、西非以及加勒比和美国南方的奴隶种植园，后来是中东、南亚和世界其他地区。

<a id="page-105-en"></a>〔原书第105页〕The story of the industrial revolution in Britain is widely known – and its significance still often exaggerated. Within a span of fifty years, from the 1780s to 1830, textile merchants in northwest England reorganised first the spinning of cotton yarn and eventually the weaving of cloth. Moving away from the putting-out system used in the linen and woollen trades and in finishing imported cottons from the Ottoman Empire and India, they took direct control of large groups of workers, who were assembled in water-powered ‘mills’ (often repurposed from other uses) to operate spinners and looms that took advantage of fast-flowing streams in the hills around Manchester. The rural location guaranteed a supply of low-cost, forced labour, mostly children, provided by expanding urban poorhouses anxious to move paupers off their books by shipping them to rural parishes. The mills produced rapidly increasing quantities of cotton yarn and later cotton textiles. None of the raw cotton was grown locally, and little of the finished fabric was consumed at home, where the preference continued for better-quality woollens and linens, or the finer Indian and Persian fabrics. The less durable, low-quality machine-woven cotton fabric was mostly shipped abroad, initially to Europe, West Africa, and the slave plantations of the Caribbean and the American South, and later to the Middle East, South Asia, and the rest of the world.

<a id="ch03-0036"></a>

对这种不同寻常安排的传统叙述，关键在于技术的作用，而技术常常充当资本的托词。它们把工业化（在某些解释中，还有先行的农业革命）视为由迅速而持续的技术创新所驱动的转变。这些叙述的不同之处主要在于这种驱动力的原因。相互竞争的解释将它分别归于：剩余资本的积累；自由或无财产的劳动力的获得所引起的生产者竞争；主要由儿童和妇女组成的大量贫困劳动力；创造勤奋精神的新消费文化；执行产权的有效法律制度的兴起；人口增长和土地可用性限制造成的生态压力；以及对殖民地和奴隶种植园的特权性准入——这些地方既生产原棉，又消费制成品。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-051"></a>[51](#note-ch3-051)

Traditional accounts of this unusual arrangement turn on the role of technology, which functions so often as an alibi of capital. They see industrialisation (and, in some explanations, an antecedent agricultural revolution) as a transformation driven by rapid and continuous technical innovation. The accounts differ mainly in the reasons for this drive. Rival explanations attribute it variously to an accumulation of surplus capital, the competition among producers caused by access to free or propertyless labour, an abundant pauperised workforce of mainly children and women, a new culture of consumption creating a spirit of industriousness, the rise of an effective legal regime enforcing property rights, ecological pressures caused by a rising population and limits to the availability of land, and privileged access to colonies and slave plantations that both produced the raw cotton and consumed the manufactured textiles.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-051"></a>[51](#note-ch3-051)

<a id="ch03-0037"></a>

这些叙述把焦点放在棉纺厂及其机械上，并不令人意外。随着生产规模扩大，专门建造的工厂变成巨大而壮观的结构，成为景观中的新特征，其中一些甚至保留至今。曼彻斯特地区最著名的工厂之一，是<a id="page-106"></a>〔原书第106页〕柴郡威尔姆斯洛附近的奎里班克纱厂（Quarry Bank Mill），如今是英国最大保护组织英国国民信托拥有的工业遗产地。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-052"></a>[52](#note-ch3-052)它建于 1784 年，后来发展成为世界上最大的棉纺织厂之一。今天它是一座关于工业革命的博物馆和档案馆，甚至是一部阴郁的英国电视剧的场景，编剧根据该遗址档案中的文件发展了故事。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-053"></a>[53](#note-ch3-053)来自该档案馆的史料出现在几乎所有关于英国工业革命的学术史中。用于构建那段历史的其他广泛使用的史料，包括工厂检查员的报告和机械发明的专利，都把故事聚焦于技术创新和工厂生产组织。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-054"></a>[54](#note-ch3-054)像奎里班克纱厂这样的大型纱厂实际上并不代表制造业；制造业在大多数情况下是在较小的场所发展起来的，但这些大厂给访客留下了印象，并受益于“维多利亚时代把‘资本’的力量物化并放大的倾向”，也受益于恩格斯、马克思和桑巴特等德国作家“执迷于把*Grossbetreib*（大企业）与高度资本主义时代联系起来”的做法。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-055"></a>[55](#note-ch3-055)纱厂加工的原棉以及生产的纱线和布匹，为编写一部聚焦于物质商品生产转变的历史提供了更多有形的材料。棉花的故事把更广阔的世界带入这部物质史。加勒比、美国南方、印度和埃及被组织起来生产棉花，按照标准叙述的说法，被纳入一个以工业生产为中心的世界经济。

The focus of accounts on the cotton mill and its machinery is no surprise. As the scale of production expanded, the purpose-built mills became large, imposing structures, forming new features in the landscape, some of which survive even today. One of the most well known of the Manchester-area factories, Quarry Bank Mill near Wilmslow in <a id="page-106-en"></a>〔原书第106页〕Cheshire, is now an industrial heritage site owned by Britain’s biggest conservation organisation, the National Trust.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-052"></a>[52](#note-ch3-052) Built in 1784, it grew into one of the largest cotton-manufacturing plants in the world. Today it is a museum and archive of the industrial revolution, and even the setting of a grim British television drama series whose writers developed the story from documents in the site’s archive.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-053"></a>[53](#note-ch3-053) Sources from that archive figure in almost every scholarly history of the British industrial revolution.
