Other sources widely used to construct that history, including the reports of factory inspectors and patents for mechanical inventions, focus the story on technical innovation and the organisation of factory production.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-054"></a>[54](#note-ch3-054) Large mills like Quarry Bank were not actually representative of manufacturing, which, in most cases, developed in smaller establishments, but they made an impression on visitors, and benefited from ‘the Victorian disposition to reify and magnify the power of “capital”’, and from ‘the obsessive association of the *Grossbetreib*’, or large enterprise, with the age of high capitalism by German writers like Engels, Marx, and Sombart.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-055"></a>[55](#note-ch3-055) The raw cotton that the mill processed and the yarn and cloth it produced provide further tangible matter for composing a history focused on the transformation in the production of material goods. The story of cotton brings the wider world into this material history. The Caribbean, the southern United States, India, and Egypt were organised to produce the cotton, becoming incorporated, as the standard accounts put it, into a world-economy centred on industrial production.

校注：底本德语拼作Grossbetreib；《杜登》所列“大企业”一词为Großbetrieb，词尾应为betrieb而非betreib。正文底本拼写照录。 https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Groszbetrieb

<a id="ch03-0038"></a>

这种以机器为焦点、以生产为中心、以英国为基础的现代资本主义起源叙述，已经受到一段时间的质疑。它有几个弱点。棉花的故事指的是一个小飞地，即便在英国也不代表大多数工业的组织方式或工人受雇方式。即使在纺织业中，对于大多数织物而言，外放制在很长时间内仍更有利可图，非机械化生产也大幅增加；许多企业领域继续使用手工劳动而没有大规模机械化，包括造船、酿造、吹玻璃、造纸、皮革加工、建筑业，以及大多数煤矿和炼铁。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-056"></a>[56](#note-ch3-056)棉花生产在另一种意义上也是一个飞地。与这一时期大多数英国和欧洲工业不同，其原料和大部分成品都不是本地的。正如我们刚才指出的，英国不种植棉花，而多达四分之三的纱线和制成布料——在其生产国是一种“薄得无法单独穿着”的织物——被出口。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-057"></a>[57](#note-ch3-057)正如一家曼彻斯特商行所描述的，这个行业以这种反常方式作为世界<a id="page-107"></a>〔原书第107页〕商业的“怪胎”运作，与当地生活的其他领域联系薄弱，包括用当地羊毛和亚麻制成的更受欢迎、质量更好的织物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-058"></a>[58](#note-ch3-058)事实上，正如贝克特所指出的，棉花作为一种既在欧洲之外生产（作为原料）又在欧洲之外消费的商品，其反常性恰恰意味着它特别适合全球资本化过程；具体而言，正如我们将看到的，适合大规模制造信用所需的错位。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-059"></a>[59](#note-ch3-059)

This machine-focused, production-centred, British-based account of the genesis of modern capitalism has been questioned for some time. It has several weaknesses. The story of cotton refers to a small enclave, not representative, even in Britain, of how most industry was organised or workers were employed. Even in textiles, the putting-out system long remained more profitable for most fabrics, and non-mechanised production increased vastly; many areas of enterprise continued to use hand labour without large-scale mechanisation, including ship building, brewing, glass-blowing, paper making, leather work, the building trades, and most coal mining and iron smelting.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-056"></a>[56](#note-ch3-056) Cotton production was an enclave in another sense. Unlike most British and European industry in this period, the raw material and most of the final product were non-local. As we just noted, no cotton was grown in Britain, while up to three-quarters of the spun yarn and manufactured cloth, a fabric ‘too flimsy to be worn by itself’ in its country of fabrication, was exported.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-057"></a>[57](#note-ch3-057) Operating abnormally in this way as a ‘freak’ of world <a id="page-107-en"></a>〔原书第107页〕commerce, as a Manchester firm described it, the industry had weak linkages with other areas of local life, including the more popular and better-quality textiles made from local wool and linen.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-058"></a>[58](#note-ch3-058) Indeed, as Beckert notes, the very abnormality of cotton, as a commodity that was both produced (as raw material) and consumed outside Europe, meant it was suited uniquely to the global process of capitalisation; and specifically, as we will see, to the dislocation required for the large-scale manufacture of credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-059"></a>[59](#note-ch3-059)

<a id="ch03-0039"></a>

关于以技术进步解释资本主义的传统，人们还指出了许多其他问题。正如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)和[第二章](#ch02-0001)所见，这类叙述常常忽视资本化对废物生产的偏好。棉花就是一个例子。它所取代的当地织物更耐久、更易修补；尤其是羊毛，不需要那么频繁地洗涤，因为它能吸收而不是困住身体的水分，而且与棉花不同，它天然抗菌。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-060"></a>[60](#note-ch3-060)相比之下，棉花的单薄及其产品的一次性，有利于频繁更换，因而有利于资本化所依赖的收入耐久性。更一般地说，与所谓工业革命相关的生产和财富的迅速增长，大部分并不是技术转型的结果。事实上，其中大部分可以归因于人口增长。机械化并没有产生物质增长。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-061"></a>[61](#note-ch3-061)这一时期的一项关键转型——从水力工厂到燃煤蒸汽机——的驱动力不是寻求技术改良，正如安德烈亚斯·马尔姆所示，而是因为更具成本效益的水力需要一群协调一致的使用者共同开发公共资源，而煤炭供应可以由私人确保（并被资本化）。蒸汽机还使生产能够从乡村转移到城市，提供更大、更脆弱的劳动力池，而机器过程扩大了控制劳动力的机会；劳动力集中在工厂中，使其拥有越来越大的权力来扰乱生产，从而要求改善条件。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-062"></a>[62](#note-ch3-062)最后，其他地区——例如中国——面临类似的人口压力和改良机会，却走上了与生产机械化不同的道路。如果说有什么不同，欧洲的发展不是由物质或技术优势塑造的，而是由缺乏禀赋塑造的——只有对亚热带奴隶殖民地的占有除外，这些殖民地既提供了机械化所围绕的原料，也提供了相关产品的市场。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-063"></a>[63](#note-ch3-063)

Many other issues have been noted regarding the tradition of explaining capitalism in terms of technical progress. As we saw in [chapters 1](#ch01-0001) and [2](#ch02-0001), such accounts often overlook the preference of capitalisation for the production of waste. Cotton exemplifies this. The local fabrics it replaced were more durable and mendable; wool in particular required less frequent laundering, since it is able to absorb rather than trap moisture from the body, and unlike cotton it is naturally anti-bacterial.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-060"></a>[60](#note-ch3-060) In contrast, the flimsiness of cotton and the disposability of its products favoured frequent replacement and thus the durability of revenue on which capitalisation depends. More generally, the rapid increase in production and wealth associated with the so-called industrial revolution was for the most part not the result of technical transformation. Most of it, in fact, can be attributed to increases in population. Mechanisation did not produce material growth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-061"></a>[61](#note-ch3-061) A key transformation of the period, from water-powered mills to coal-powered steam engines, was driven not by a search for technical improvement, as Andreas Malm has shown, but by the fact that the more cost-effective water power required the shared development of a public resource among a coordinated group of users, whereas the supply of coal could be secured (and capitalised) privately. Steam engines also allowed production to move from rural to urban locations, providing a larger, more vulnerable pool of labour, while the machine process expanded the opportunities for control of a workforce whose concentration in factories had given it an increasing power to disrupt production and thus demand improved conditions.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-062"></a>[62](#note-ch3-062) Finally, other regions, such as China, faced similar demographic pressures and opportunities for improvement but took a different path from the mechanisation of production. If anything, developments in Europe were shaped not by material or technical advantages but by a lack of endowments – except for the possession of sub-tropical slave colonies, which provided both a source and a market for the material around which mechanisation was organised.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-063"></a>[63](#note-ch3-063)

<a id="ch03-0040"></a>

<a id="page-108"></a>〔原书第108页〕这些问题早已使一种较少欧洲中心主义的工业化叙述成为可能；这种叙述不从非凡的技术改良、英国人的独特勤奋或对日益增多商品的简单需求中寻找对已发生之事的解释，并且更意识到偶然性因素。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-064"></a>[64](#note-ch3-064)如今有一种强有力的反叙述，用更具全球性的术语解释工业革命，将其与更早的长途贸易、殖民和种植园奴隶制的发展联系起来。在这些解释中，有一场关于工业革命融资所需信用或资本来源的重要辩论，包括大西洋奴隶制与夺取莫卧儿帝国资源的相对重要性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-065"></a>[65](#note-ch3-065)然而，要恰当地使欧洲及其工业化去中心化，就需要改变这些辩论的术语。即使在最好的叙述中，商业或商人资本也仅仅为工业化铺路。它提供的金融仅仅“润滑”了向工业生产的过渡。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-066"></a>[66](#note-ch3-066)

<a id="page-108-en"></a>〔原书第108页〕These issues have already allowed for some time a less Eurocentric account of industrialisation, one that does not seek explanations for what happened in exceptional technical improvement, the peculiar industriousness of the British, or a simple demand for increasing numbers of goods, and one that is more aware of the element of contingency.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-064"></a>[64](#note-ch3-064) There is now a strong counter-narrative explaining the industrial revolution in more global terms, in relation to the earlier development of long-distance trade, colonisation, and plantation slavery. Within those explanations, there is an important debate on the sources of credit or capital for financing the industrial revolution, including the relative importance of Atlantic slavery versus the capture of resources of the Mughal Empire.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-065"></a>[65](#note-ch3-065) However, to properly decentre Europe and its industrialisation, the terms of those debates need to be altered. Even in the best accounts, commercial or mercantile capital merely prepares the way for industrialisation. The finance it supplies simply ‘lubricates’ the transition to industrial production.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-066"></a>[66](#note-ch3-066)

<a id="ch03-0041"></a>

应该使我们关切的问题，不是工业化如何获得融资。如果沿用这些术语，问题就会是*金融如何以及为何被工业化*。然而这些术语并不充分，因为它们似乎假定了“金融”与“工业”之间的区别，假定了仅仅是润滑剂的货币与它所润滑的真实“机器”之间的区别，因而假定了货币经济与“实体经济”之间的区别。在接下来两章中，我们将从“实体”一侧接近这些问题，考察经济的谱系。我们将通过我们称之为“经济化”的过程，考察先是“经济的”事物、然后是“经济”这一对象的出现。然而目前，从理解货币这一侧出发，我们将继续使用更具包容性的术语“资本化”，正是因为它不从金融与实体之间的对立出发，而是探讨这种区分如何被发明、部署和掩盖。

The question that should concern us is not how industrialisation was financed. If we were to keep with these terms, the question would be how and why *finance was industrialised*. These terms are inadequate, however, for they appear to assume the difference between ‘finance’ and ‘industry’, between money that is merely a lubricant and the real ‘machine’ that it lubricates, and thus between the monetary economy and the ‘real economy’. In the following two chapters we will approach these questions from the side of the ‘real’ and consider the genealogy of the economy. We will examine the emergence of first ‘the economic’ and then ‘the economy’ through processes we will identify as ‘economisation’. For now, however, working from the side of understanding money, we will continue with the more capacious term ‘capitalisation’, precisely because it does not start from an opposition between the financial and the real, but explores how that distinction has been invented, deployed, and disguised.

<a id="ch03-0042"></a>

因此，我们在此关注的不是商业和“商业资本主义”，而是资本化，商业只是资本化和攫取未来收入的一种方式。由此我们可以进一步提出两个论点。这两个论点将把工厂制度的发展不是置于早期商业发展的顶点，而是置于一次*绕道*的后果之中；这次绕道是一种扰动，打乱了更广泛、较少以欧洲为中心的当下获取未来付款的方式。绕道的观念不仅暗示一种偶然性因素——多种发展相结合产生一个结果——而且暗示一个较少<a id="page-109"></a>〔原书第109页〕线性的过程，其特征是延迟、中断和不连续。我们还将看到，工厂生产的一个显著特征如何使它出人意料地产生一种从未来抽取的新方式——一种更地方化的信用创造方法，它作为雇佣劳动运作，并被误认为雇佣劳动。在工资这一装置中，我们将发现，一种现代而极其简单的货币概念出现了。

By focusing here, then, not on commerce and ‘commercial capitalism’ but on capitalisation, where commerce is one mode of capitalising and capturing a future revenue, we can go on to propose two additional arguments. These will place the development of the factory system not as the culmination of earlier commercial developments but as the consequence of a *detour*, a disturbance that unsettled the wider, less-European-centred modes of acquiring future payments in the present. The idea of a detour suggests not just an element of contingency, in which multiple developments combine to create an outcome, but a less <a id="page-109-en"></a>〔原书第109页〕linear process characterised by delay, interruption, and discontinuity. And we will see how one notable feature of factory production allowed it to give rise, unexpectedly, to a new mode of extraction from the future – the more localised method of credit creation that operated and was misrecognised as wage labour. In the device of the wage, we will discover, there emerged a modern and very simple conception of money.

<a id="ch03-0043"></a>

### 工业革命作为一次绕道

### Industrial Revolution as a Detour

<a id="ch03-0044"></a>

首先是绕道。英国商人早已习惯于从资助殖民贸易、战争和动产奴隶制中获得巨额利润，他们为何会选择不同寻常而艰辛的道路，在离家很近的地方把工人大规模组织进工厂？通过新的制造业控制来提高剩余，与从未来攫取收入有何联系？与其诉诸“技术改良”或“需求”增加的论点，不如从 1770 年代到 1820 年代发生的一场全球性资本化过程危机中寻找另一种答案；这一过程依赖于军事化贸易垄断、殖民和奴役。转向棉纺织，是为了挽救被全球战争、殖民扩张、抵抗和革命打乱的信用制造体系而采取的一次绕道。这场危机的一部分——发生在欧洲内部的发展——广为人知，尽管人们较少把它与其所联系的更广泛事件联系起来。但让我们从那里开始。

First, the detour. Why did British merchants, long accustomed to the large profits from financing colonial trade, warfare, and chattel slavery, take the unusual and laborious path of organising workers close to home on a large scale into factories? How was the raising of surplus through a new control over manufacturing connected with the capture of revenue from the future? Instead of resorting to arguments about ‘technical improvement’ or increasing ‘demand’, an alternative answer can be found in the worldwide crisis in the processes of capitalisation, dependent on militarised trading monopolies, colonisation, and enslavement, that occurred in the period from the 1770s to the 1820s. Cotton manufacture was the diversion taken to salvage a system of credit manufacture disrupted by global warfare, colonial expansion, resistance, and revolution. One part of this crisis is well-known, the developments occurring within Europe, although it is less often associated with the wider events to which it was connected. But let us start there.

<a id="ch03-0045"></a>

1789 年凡尔赛三级会议召开后的几年里，革命席卷欧洲，伦敦的商人—金融家及其在欧洲的商业伙伴被迫把信用转用于纺织生产的扩张。这种转用既不能用消费者对更多布匹的突然需求来解释，也不能用寻找新投资的资本“剩余”来解释。它是商人金融发生错位的结果，需要一个新的过程来完成信用创造和获利所依赖的循环。

When revolution engulfed Europe in the years after the summoning of the Estates-General at Versailles in 1789, merchant-financiers in London and their business partners in Europe were forced to divert credit into the expansion of textile production. This diversion is explained neither by a sudden consumer demand for more cloth, nor by a ‘surplus’ of capital looking for new investments. It was the result of a dislocation of merchant finance, requiring a new process through which to complete the circulation that allowed the creation of and profit from credit.

<a id="ch03-0046"></a>

1790 年代，法国革命战争蔓延欧洲，伦敦的商人债权人资助了欧洲大陆的战争。英国政府为德国各邦统治者提供的雇佣兵付费，扩展了美国独立战争期间发展起来的雇佣兵制度。这些战争付款的规模<a id="page-110"></a>〔原书第110页〕前所未有。到拿破仑战争结束时，军费开支占英国政府收入的 58%。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-067"></a>[67](#note-ch3-067)政府以未来税收作抵押借款，付款不是用现金，而是通过以伦敦商人为付款人的信用证转移；这些商人在德国的代理或合伙人把资金用于招募和供应士兵。于是欧洲大陆的商人在伦敦积累了贷方余额。这些纸面财富只有通过找到把信用反向转移的办法才能变现，即用德国人在伦敦持有的票据购买英国货物，供应欧洲。（票据本身不移动：相反，为了平衡贷方和借方，并从其创造中获利，货物必须运回德国。）用于这种互补的信用流动和利润实现的主要载体，是纺织品的转移。虽然现有的英格兰毛织品和亚麻织品贸易可以提供部分信用转移机制，但疏通和扩大金融的主要手段，是让这些票据发挥作用，在英格兰发展另一种织物——棉布——的生产，而棉布此前主要从东方进口。用于资助欧洲大陆战争的伦敦票据，需要换上一身新衣才能回流。正如一位伦敦金融家 1811 年所言，被冻结的战时票据信用相当于“如此多的外国资本投资于英国工业”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-068"></a>[68](#note-ch3-068)

As the French revolutionary wars spread across Europe in the 1790s, London merchant creditors financed war on the continent. The British government paid for mercenaries supplied by the rulers of German states, extending a system of hired soldiery developed during the American Revolutionary War. The scale of these payments for warfare <a id="page-110-en"></a>〔原书第110页〕was unprecedented. By the end of the Napoleonic wars, military spending was accounting for 58 per cent of the British government’s revenue.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-067"></a>[67](#note-ch3-067) Borrowing against future tax revenues, the government transferred the payments not in cash but via letters of credit drawn on London merchants, whose agents or partners in Germany made the funds available to recruit and supply the soldiers. The merchants on the continent thus accumulated credits in London. These paper fortunes could be realised only by finding ways to move credit in the reverse direction, by using the German-owned bills in London to purchase British goods to supply to Europe. (The bills themselves did not move: rather, to balance the credits and debts, and to profit from their creation, goods had to move back to Germany.) The main vehicle used for this complementary movement of credit and the realisation of profit was the transfer of textiles. While the existing trade in English woollens and linens could provide some of the machinery of credit transfer, the principal means of unblocking and expanding finance was to put the bills to work in developing the production in England of a different fabric, cotton, which until then had been largely imported from the East. The London bills used to fund the war on the continent required a new clothing to return. As a London financier remarked in 1811, the blocked credit of wartime bills amounted to ‘so much foreign capital invested in British industry’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-068"></a>[68](#note-ch3-068)

<a id="ch03-0047"></a>

这一过程得益于商人从巴黎、阿姆斯特丹、汉堡和其他欧洲大陆贸易中心迁往伦敦。他们逃离革命势力，在其触及不到的地方建立商行，从资助货物运输的战时机会中获利。拿破仑在埃及战败后，法国实施大陆封锁体系，试图阻断与英国的贸易，这为有能力走私货物、突破封锁的人带来了额外利润。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-069"></a>[69](#note-ch3-069)据关于金融资本主义兴起的主要历史著作所述，这些由战争驱动的信用流动，以及创造和调动信用所需的货物流动，“简明地解释了”“英国工业革命为何发生在那个时期”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-070"></a>[70](#note-ch3-070)

The process was aided by the relocation of merchants from Paris, Amsterdam, Hamburg, and other trading centres on the continent to London. Fleeing the revolutionary forces and establishing trading houses outside their reach, the merchants profited from the wartime opportunities to finance the movement of goods. After Napoleon was defeated in Egypt, France imposed the Continental System in an attempt to block commerce with Britain, allowing additional profits for those with means to smuggle goods through the blockade.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-069"></a>[69](#note-ch3-069) These movements of credit driven by war, and of the goods required to create and mobilise credit, ‘explain succinctly’, according to the leading history of the rise of finance capitalism, ‘why the British industrial revolution took place during that period’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-070"></a>[70](#note-ch3-070)

<a id="ch03-0048"></a>

内森·罗斯柴尔德的职业生涯说明了这种借助机器的绕道如何运作；他是这些流离失所的布商和金融家中最著名的一位。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-071"></a>[71](#note-ch3-071)他的父亲是法兰克福一位成功的商人，曾担任黑森—卡塞尔统治者的金融代理人，后者是英国雇佣兵的主要供应者。父亲通过经营该统治者的英国汇票发家，后来又为向奥地利皇室<a id="page-111"></a>〔原书第111页〕供应战争物资提供融资。他的儿子内森在 1799 年左右被派往曼彻斯特，当时他二十出头，开始做棉布生意，把布匹运回法兰克福和欧洲其他城市。当时至少有八名德国商人定居曼彻斯特，他是其中之一，这个数字还在继续增加。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-072"></a>[72](#note-ch3-072)内森可以从处理他父亲票据生意英国一端的伦敦商行获得汇票——换言之，利用他父亲在伦敦积累的剩余欠条作为可即时使用的货币。这种获得充足信用货币的渠道，使他能够以低于其他曼彻斯特棉布商人的价格出售，后者通常用两到六个月到期的票据从当地织工那里购买布匹。内森通过“按即期票据条件”预付，可以找到“急需用钱”并愿意降价 15% 或 20% 的织工。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-073"></a>[73](#note-ch3-073)

The career of Nathan Rothschild, one of the best known of these displaced cloth traders and financiers, illustrates this machinic diversion at work.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-071"></a>[71](#note-ch3-071) His father was a successful Frankfurt merchant who served as a financial agent for the ruler of Hesse-Kassel, the main supplier of mercenary troops to the British. The father built a fortune dealing in the ruler’s English bills of exchange, and later in financing the <a id="page-111-en"></a>〔原书第111页〕supply of war matériel to the Austrian imperial court. His son Nathan was sent to Manchester around 1799, while still in his early twenties, to begin trading in cotton goods, shipping cloth back to Frankfurt and other cities in Europe. He was one of at least eight German traders to settle in Manchester around then, a number that continued to increase.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-072"></a>[72](#note-ch3-072) Nathan could obtain bills from the merchant houses in London that handled the British side of his father’s bill dealing – using, in other words, the surplus IOUs his father had built up in London as ready money. This access to plentiful credit money allowed him to undercut other Manchester cotton traders, who typically purchased cloth from local weavers with bills payable in two to six months. By paying upfront ‘on present bill terms’, Nathan could find weavers ‘in want of money’ and willing to lower their prices by 15 or 20 per cent.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-073"></a>[73](#note-ch3-073)

<a id="ch03-0049"></a>

罗斯柴尔德通过疏通需要伦敦对应票据的德国票据来采购布匹，这一成功意味着他很快就难以找到足够的供应。大约一年内，他与博尔顿—瓦特公司达成安排，购买一台绕纱机——一种木制装置，可以把供织机梭子使用的纱线同时卷绕到几根锭子上。通过向织工提供已经绕在锭子上的纱线，罗斯柴尔德提高了织工向他供应布匹的速度。绕纱机在充当加速布匹生产装置的同时，还有更多作用——它是一种改善信用货币流通的机制。积累在他位于法兰克福的父亲手中的汇票，如今可以投入使用了。

Rothschild’s success in buying via the unblocking of German bills in need of London counterparts meant he soon struggled to find sufficient supplies. Within about a year, he arranged with the firm of Boulton& Watt to purchase a copping machine, a wooden contraption that allowed the yarn for the weavers’ shuttles to be ‘copped’, or wound, onto several spindles at once. By supplying weavers with yarn already wound on the spindle, Rothschild increased the rate at which the weavers could supply him with cloth. While serving as a device to speed up the production of cloth, the copping machine was something more – a mechanism to improve the circulation of credit money. The bills of exchange accumulating in the hands of his father in Frankfurt could now be put to work.

<a id="ch03-0050"></a>

几年之内，内森·罗斯柴尔德搬到伦敦，专注于贸易融资、汇票贴现，以及充当统治者的投资经纪人。通往曼彻斯特的绕道在疏通了信用流动之后，如今可以留给别人。曼彻斯特成为商人—金融家的中心，他们与周围乡村的纺织厂合作并投资，但“最重要的是……为贸易融资，充当制造供应商的付款人，并向海外客户提供长期信贷”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-074"></a>[74](#note-ch3-074)在海外贸易中发挥主导作用的是定居曼彻斯特的外国人，尤其是德国商人，例如埃尔门—恩格斯公司；创始人之一的儿子弗里德里希·恩格斯在那里管理公司的商业交易、会计和情报收集。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-075"></a>[75](#note-ch3-075)这些情报有助于他朋友卡尔·马克思的写作，塑造了一种以曼彻斯特为中心的资本化过程论述。

Within a few years, Nathan Rothschild had moved to London, to focus on the financing of trade, the discounting of bills, and acting as investment broker to rulers. The detour to Manchester, having unblocked the flow of credit, could now be left to others. The city became the centre of merchant-financiers, who worked with and invested in the textile mills in the surrounding countryside but ‘above all . . . financed the trade, serving as paymasters to their manufacturing suppliers and extending long credits to their overseas customers’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-074"></a>[74](#note-ch3-074) A dominant role in the overseas trade was played by foreigners settled in Manchester, especially German merchants, such as the firm of Ermen& Engels, where Friedrich Engels, the son of one of the founders, managed the firm’s commercial dealing, accounting, and intelligence gathering.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-075"></a>[75](#note-ch3-075) This intelligence helped inform the writing of his friend Karl Marx, shaping a Manchester-centred account of the capitalisation process.

<a id="ch03-0051"></a>

随着德国商行的发展，来自奥斯曼世界的商人后来也日益增多——希腊人、<a id="page-112"></a>〔原书第112页〕亚美尼亚人、阿拉伯人和土耳其人，他们在英国都被称为“希腊人”，为与伊兹密尔、阿勒颇、开罗和亚历山大等城市的贸易融资，后来又为与西非和大多数其他地区的贸易融资。在许多情况下，他们在海外城市建立了自己的分号。例如，由来自伊斯坦布尔的希腊商人家庭创办的曼彻斯特卡瓦菲公司（Cavafy and Co.），于 1840 年代在亚历山大开设了一家分号，由创办人的儿子之一彼得罗斯经营。（彼得罗斯去世、1870 年代的金融危机迫使家族关闭亚历山大分号后，家族回到了曼彻斯特。一位孙子又搬回亚历山大，兼职做股票交易所经纪人来赚钱，但作为时代变迁的标志，他在英国统治下的灌溉部工作了三十年，以此谋生——这份任职倒也恰如其分。从这个希腊商人世界的角落，“与宇宙成一个微小的角度”站立，他成为著名诗人 C. P. 卡瓦菲。）<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-076"></a>[76](#note-ch3-076)来自奥斯曼世界的商人数量继续增长，到 1870 年，他们在主导曼彻斯特长途贸易的 400 名常驻外国商人中超过了德国人，成为最大的群体。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-077"></a>[77](#note-ch3-077)据一份当时的报道，曼彻斯特“被殖民化”了，殖民者正是这些外国商人。凭借他们的信用网络、贸易经验、对海外商法的理解以及多种语言知识，奥斯曼和其他商人群体是棉纺织业发展的“主要推动者”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-078"></a>[78](#note-ch3-078)

The growth of German merchant houses was later matched by the increasing number of traders from the Ottoman world – Greeks, <a id="page-112-en"></a>〔原书第112页〕Armenians, Arabs, and Turks, all referred to in Britain as ‘Greeks’, who financed trade with cities like Izmir, Aleppo, Cairo, and Alexandria, and later with West Africa and most other regions. In many cases, they established their own branches in overseas cities. The Manchester firm of Cavafy and Co., for example, founded by a Greek merchant family from Istanbul, opened an Alexandria office in the 1840s, run by one of the founder’s sons, Petros. (The family returned to Manchester after the death of Petros and the financial crisis of the 1870s had forced the family to close the Alexandria office. A grandson moved back to Alexandria and made money on the side as a broker on the stock exchange, but, as a sign of the changing times, supported himself under the British by working for thirty years, appropriately enough, at the Ministry of Irrigation. From this corner of the Greek merchant world, standing ‘at a slight angle to the universe’, he became the noted poet C. P. Cavafy.)<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-076"></a>[76](#note-ch3-076) The merchants from the Ottoman world continued to grow in number, and, by 1870, surpassed the Germans as the largest group among the 400 resident foreign merchants who dominated Manchester’s long-distance trade.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-077"></a>[77](#note-ch3-077) Manchester, according to a contemporary report, ‘came to be colonised’ by these foreign merchants. With their credit networks, trading experience, understanding of overseas commercial law, and knowledge of multiple languages, the Ottoman and other merchant communities were the ‘prime movers’ in the development of cotton manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-078"></a>[78](#note-ch3-078)

校注：底本称彼得罗斯去世后家族回到曼彻斯特。奥纳西斯卡瓦菲档案馆的传记记述，诗人的母亲在1870年丈夫去世后携子女赴英，1872—1877年先住利物浦、后住伦敦，随后返回亚历山大。正文地名照录。 https://cavafy.onassis.org/creator/cavafy-c-p/

<a id="ch03-0052"></a>

### 使曼彻斯特地方化

### Provincialising Manchester

<a id="ch03-0053"></a>

如果说曼彻斯特的外国商人为贸易提供融资，推动了向棉纺织业的绕道，那么其中的“希腊人”把这次绕道与奥斯曼世界，尤其是埃及和阿拉伯正在进行的转变联系起来。在离开欧洲—地中海世界之前，让我们简要追踪这一联系。拿破仑·波拿巴对埃及的短暂占领（1798—1801）本意是把该国变成法国殖民地，以弥补最近失去印度和北美殖民地，以及加勒比被奴役者起义可能带来进一步损失的威胁，尤其是法国最有价值的海外领地、也可能是世界上生产力最高的殖民地领土——圣多明各（海地）的糖业种植园殖民地。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-079"></a>[79](#note-ch3-079)马赛的法国航运利益集团<a id="page-113"></a>〔原书第113页〕热切支持埃及冒险。他们的利润在于为东地中海贸易融资，这种商业在十八世纪上半叶曾短暂被他们主导（尽管他们对更富裕的奥斯曼内部贸易仍处于边缘），但如今正输给希腊、亚美尼亚和其他奥斯曼商行。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-080"></a>[80](#note-ch3-080)然而结果却截然不同：法国在尼罗河上建立一个海地的计划失败了，埃及则作为一个有别于其他地区的权力中心得到加强，相对于伊斯坦布尔的奥斯曼当局获得了越来越大的自主性。

If the foreign merchants of Manchester financed the trade that helped drive the detour into cotton manufacturing, the ‘Greeks’ among them connected that detour to transformations under way in the Ottoman world, especially Egypt and Arabia. Before leaving the European-Mediterranean world, let us briefly follow this connection. Napoleon Bonaparte’s short-lived occupation of Egypt (1798–1801) had been intended to make the country into a French colony, to compensate for the recent loss of colonies in India and North America and the threat of further losses from uprisings by enslaved people in the Caribbean, notably in France’s most valuable overseas possession, and possibly the most productive colonial territory anywhere in the world, the sugar plantation colony of Saint-Domingue (Haiti).<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-079"></a>[79](#note-ch3-079) French shipping interests in Marseilles were <a id="page-113-en"></a>〔原书第113页〕keen to support the Egyptian venture. Their profits lay in financing trade with the Eastern Mediterranean, a commerce they had briefly dominated in the first half of the eighteenth century (although they remained peripheral to the richer internal Ottoman trade), but were now losing to the Greek, Armenian, and other Ottoman merchant houses.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-080"></a>[80](#note-ch3-080) The result, however, was something very different: the defeat of the French plan for a Haiti-on-the-Nile and the strengthening of Egypt as a distinct centre of power, increasingly autonomous from the Ottoman authorities in Istanbul.

<a id="ch03-0054"></a>

开罗的自主性在十八世纪后期已经增强，得益于奥斯曼日益分权化的治理政策。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-081"></a>[81](#note-ch3-081)像阿里贝伊·卡比尔这样的地方统治者开始压过对手执政家族，着手军事扩张，并鼓励商业增长、从中获利；埃及历史学家贾巴尔提注意到了这一发展，其标志是在布拉克——服务于开罗的河港——和坦塔等地建造大型商业综合体，后者盛大的季节性集市我们已经提到过。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-082"></a>[82](#note-ch3-082)对奥斯曼统治的另一个商业和政治挑战出现在阿拉伯半岛，穆罕默德·本·沙特治下的迪里耶酋长国与从事长途贸易的富有阿拉伯商人以及穆罕默德·伊本·阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜的宗教改革运动结盟，将其权力从波斯湾扩展到红海，横跨整个半岛，控制了圣城麦加；麦加每年的布匹集市是印度洋世界最大的商业活动之一。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-083"></a>[83](#note-ch3-083)在拿破仑的干预之后，开罗在 1805 年至 1848 年统治的穆罕默德·阿里帕夏治下继续扩张。他建立了一支庞大的陆军和海军，镇压了阿拉伯半岛的瓦哈比运动，并进一步扩大统治，先征服苏丹诸王国，然后进军巴勒斯坦和叙利亚。为了获得新帝国，他从欧洲寻求武器和海军舰艇，这给了英国、希腊和其他商人——他们从阿勒颇和其他奥斯曼贸易中心被吸引到亚历山大——为供应主要进口品提供融资的机会，即埃及不断增强的战争能力所需的“军需品、木材和其他商品”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-084"></a>[84](#note-ch3-084)

Cairo’s autonomy had already been growing in the later eighteenth century, benefiting from an Ottoman policy of increasingly decentralised governance.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-081"></a>[81](#note-ch3-081) Local rulers like Ali Bey al-Kabir began to dominate rival governing households, embark on military expansion, and encourage and profit from increasing commerce, a development noted by the Egyptian historian al-Jabarti and marked by the building of large commercial complexes at sites like Bulaq, the river port serving Cairo, and Tanta, whose great seasonal fair has already been mentioned.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-082"></a>[82](#note-ch3-082) Another commercial and political challenge to Ottoman rule emerged in Arabia, where the Emirate of Dir’iya, under Muhammad bin Sa’ud, in alliance with wealthy long-distance Arab merchants and with the reformist religious movement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, extended its power across the entire peninsula from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea, taking control of the holy city of Mecca, whose annual cloth fair was among the largest commercial events of the Indian Ocean world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-083"></a>[83](#note-ch3-083) After the interruption by Napoleon, Cairo continued its expansion under Muhammad Ali Pasha, who ruled from 1805 to 1848. He built a large army and navy, crushed the Wahhabi movement in Arabia, and further expanded his rule, first over the kingdoms of Sudan and then to Palestine and Syria. To acquire the new empire, he sought arms and naval vessels from Europe, giving British, Greek, and other merchants, drawn to Alexandria from Aleppo and other Ottoman trading centres, the opportunity to finance the supply of the main imports, namely ‘warlike stores, timber, and other commodities’ required for the expanding Egyptian powers of war-making.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-084"></a>[84](#note-ch3-084)

校注：本段将迪里耶政权的扩张合并叙述在穆罕默德·本·沙特治下。Saudipedia记其统治止于1765年，并将此后跨半岛扩张分别置于继任者阿卜杜勒阿齐兹及沙特治下，故此处不宜理解为所列扩张均由创立者在世时完成。正文保留原作概述。 https://saudipedia.com/en/first-saudi-state

<a id="ch03-0055"></a>

为一个尼罗河上的新强国扩张提供融资，又造就了另一股需要取道兰开夏棉纺厂的力量。穆罕默德·阿里以信用购买武器和其他战争物资，信用由这些商人垫付，尤其是英国布里格斯公司（Briggs & Co.）。为了获得信用，帕夏也以自己的信用支付，形式是未来<a id="page-114"></a>〔原书第114页〕交付作物的合同。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-085"></a>[85](#note-ch3-085)但哪些作物？为了从资助军需供应中获利，布里格斯和其他商人银行家需要一种可以运回欧洲的商品。起初，他们可以依赖埃及的主要出口作物小麦，拿破仑战争期间及之后，马耳他和伊比利亚半岛需要小麦供应英国军队。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-086"></a>[86](#note-ch3-086)然而到 1820 年代，他们需要一种不同的材料来维持商人金融的流动。备选品包括靛蓝、鸦片、丝绸、亚麻籽油（亚麻工业的副产品），以及从苏丹和更南地区运来的阿拉伯胶和象牙等物品。然而这些都不足以资助不断扩大的军火贸易。

Financing the expansion of a new power on the Nile created another force needing a diversion through the cotton mills of Lancashire. Muhammad Ali funded the purchase of arms and other warlike materials on credit, which was advanced by these merchants, especially the English firm of Briggs& Co. To obtain the credit, the Pasha offered credit payments of his own, in the form of contracts for the future <a id="page-114-en"></a>〔原书第114页〕delivery of crops.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-085"></a>[85](#note-ch3-085) But which crops? To profit from financing military supplies, Briggs and other merchant bankers needed a commodity they might ship back to Europe. At first, they could rely on Egypt’s main export crop, wheat, which was in demand in Malta and the Iberian Peninsula to supply British forces during and after the Napoleonic wars.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-086"></a>[86](#note-ch3-086) By the 1820s, however, they needed a different material through which to sustain the movement of merchant finance. Alternatives included indigo, opium, silk, linseed oil (a by-product of the linen industry), and items brought from Sudan and further south, such as gum arabic and ivory. None of these, however, was sufficient to finance the expanding trade in arms.

<a id="ch03-0056"></a>

解决办法由棉花提供。每一部关于埃及及其棉花业的历史都会重复一个故事：一位来自里昂的法国纺织工程师路易·朱梅尔在纽约逗留后抵达埃及，碰巧在开罗一位贵族的花园里“发现”了一种新的长绒棉（即纤维长度较长的棉种），随后说服穆罕默德·阿里广泛种植这种作物，发展出口产业，以满足欧洲纺织制造业的需要。这个故事几乎每一个要素都是神话，由十九世纪法国历史学家和美国外交官编造，他们急于把穆罕默德·阿里治下埃及转型的功劳归于法国或美国。朱梅尔不是里昂人，从未访问美国，受雇于埃及政府是为了发展毛纺厂，而不是棉花产业。他抵达后不到五年就在开罗病逝。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-087"></a>[87](#note-ch3-087)历史学家夸大了他的作用，却忽视了埃及试图从小麦出口国转向棉花出口国的更可能原因。这些原因在于奥斯曼—埃及的扩张，尤其是对苏丹的殖民。

The solution was provided by cotton. Every history of Egypt and its cotton industry repeats the story of a French textile engineer from Lyon, Louis Jumel, arriving in Egypt after a stay in New York, who happened to ‘discover’ a new strain of cotton with a long staple, or length of fibre, growing in the garden of a nobleman in Cairo, and who then persuaded Muhammad Ali to plant the crop widely and develop an export industry to serve the needs of European textile manufacturing. Almost every element of this story is a myth, elaborated by nineteenth-century French historians and American diplomats anxious to give France or the United States the credit for the transformation of Egypt under Muhammad Ali. Jumel was not from Lyon, had never visited the United States, and accepted employment from the Egyptian government to develop a woollen factory, not a cotton industry. He became ill and died in Cairo within five years of his arrival.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-087"></a>[87](#note-ch3-087) In exaggerating his role, the historians overlooked the more likely reasons for Egypt’s attempted transformation from an exporter of wheat to an exporter of cotton. Those reasons lay in Ottoman-Egyptian expansion, in particular the colonisation of Sudan.

<a id="ch03-0057"></a>

如果征服苏丹产生了对武器的需求，它也提供了支付武器的办法。在开罗附近“花园”里种植长绒棉的“贵族”——那无疑是城郊一处有围墙的果园；每个大城镇的富人都会在这样的地方用井水灌溉树木类作物，使其免受尼罗河洪水侵袭——是马胡贝伊·乌尔法利，一位库尔德马穆鲁克，他站在穆罕默德·阿里一边，帮助完成对苏丹的征服，在帕夏的军队中担任高级骑兵军官，后来担任苏丹北部柏柏尔省省长。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-088"></a>[88](#note-ch3-088)通过马胡贝伊，很可能是苏丹——而不是一个法国人——提供了在埃及发展这种作物的模式、动机和棉花品种。

If conquering Sudan was the source of a need for arms, it also offered a solution to pay for them. The ‘nobleman’ cultivating long-staple cotton in his ‘garden’ near Cairo – no doubt a walled orchard on the outskirts of the city, a place where the wealthy of every large town used irrigation from wells to grow tree crops protected from the Nile flood – was Mahu Bey al-Urfali, a Kurdish Mamluk who had sided with Muhammad Ali and helped carry out the conquest of Sudan, serving as a senior cavalry officer in the Pasha’s army and then as governor of Berber Province in northern Sudan.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-088"></a>[88](#note-ch3-088) Through Mahu Bey, it was quite probably Sudan, not a Frenchman, that provided the model, the motive, and the cotton variety for the development of the crop in Egypt.

<a id="ch03-0058"></a>

<a id="page-115"></a>〔原书第115页〕尼罗河地区发现两种棉花：一种多年生棉花长成小树，短纤维适合粗纱以及床垫和长沙发的填充物；另一种较小，长成灌木，每年用种子重新种植，长绒纤维可纺出用于奢华布料的细线。在埃及，棉花种植很少，因为作为夏季作物，正如我们在[第二章](#ch02-0001)所见，它与田地的夏季泛滥不相容。在南部，棉花仅种在尼罗河沿岸高地；在其他地方，则仅种在有围墙的果园里，那里的灌溉井在夏季供水。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-089"></a>[89](#note-ch3-089)另一方面，在苏丹，尤其是尼罗河的栋古拉和申迪河段，大多数田地高于洪水水位，用水车灌溉，夏季种植十分普遍。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-090"></a>[90](#note-ch3-090)该地区几个世纪以来专门生产棉花，既在河边使用水车，也——至少在近几十年包括破坏性的奥斯曼—埃及征服带来的灾难之前——在井上使用水车，获取由尼罗河补给的地下水。据报道，苏丹的棉纺织厂“为东北非大部分地区提供衣物”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-091"></a>[91](#note-ch3-091)水车，即萨基亚（*saqiya*），使用如此广泛，以至于政府收入以对水车的征税而非土地为基础；正如我们在[第二章](#ch02-0001)所指出的，*saqiya*一词不仅指水车，还指围绕维持每台水车运转所需的家庭、动物和田地组织起来的整个共同体。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-092"></a>[92](#note-ch3-092)

<a id="page-115-en"></a>〔原书第115页〕Two kinds of cotton were found on the Nile, a perennial grown as a small tree, whose short staple was suitable for coarse yarns and as stuffing for mattresses and divans, and a smaller variety, grown as a bush and replanted each year from seed, whose long-staple fibres produced fine threads for luxury cloths. In Egypt, cotton was only sparsely cultivated, since, as a summer crop, it was incompatible, as we saw in [chapter 2](#ch02-0001), with the summer inundation of the fields. In the south it was confined to Nile berms and elsewhere to walled orchards, where irrigation wells made water available in summer.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-089"></a>[89](#note-ch3-089) In Sudan, on the other hand, especially on the Dongola and Shendi reaches of the Nile, where most of the fields lay above the flood level and were irrigated with waterwheels, summer cultivation was widely practised.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-090"></a>[90](#note-ch3-090) The region had specialised in cotton production for centuries, using waterwheels both at the river’s edge and, at least before the devastation of recent decades including the destructive Ottoman-Egyptian conquest, on wells accessing groundwater replenished by the Nile. The cotton manufactories of Sudan, it was reported, ‘furnish the greater part of north-eastern Africa with articles of dress’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-091"></a>[91](#note-ch3-091) The water-wheel, or *saqiya*, was used so widely that government revenue was based on the taxation of wheels, not land, and the term *saqiya* referred not just to the wheel, as we noted in [chapter 2](#ch02-0001), but to the entire community organised around the households, animals, and fields required to keep each wheel running.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-092"></a>[92](#note-ch3-092)

<a id="ch03-0059"></a>

在殖民苏丹时，穆罕默德·阿里最初的目标是接管这些富裕的农业地区，利用奴隶劳动发展棉花、靛蓝和糖的生产——这种方法在美国南方正被证明是成功的。然而，1822 年苏丹北部的努比亚和阿拉伯语社群反抗占领，杀死了入侵部队的指挥官、穆罕默德·阿里的儿子伊斯梅尔帕夏。土耳其—埃及军队在试图控制上埃及时也遇到了类似的抵抗。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-093"></a>[93](#note-ch3-093)占领者最终镇压了抵抗，并努力发展棉花和靛蓝产业，但他们的主要精力转回了北方。在儿子死去的同一年，穆罕默德·阿里下令在开罗以北的尼罗河三角洲挖掘数千口井并建造水车，大概效仿苏丹模式，以便把种植从灌溉果园扩展到大型田地，实现广泛的夏季种植。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-094"></a>[94](#note-ch3-094)另一家当地商行——布里格斯公司的对手吉巴拉兄弟——为三角洲的新种植园提供信贷。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-095"></a>[95](#note-ch3-095)兰开夏<a id="page-116"></a>〔原书第116页〕机械化纺纱的引入，使英国纱厂依赖这些奢侈品种；这不是为了生产更精细的布料，而是因为用较长纤维纺出的纱线在机器过程的粗暴处理中不易被拉断。因此，在利物浦，长绒棉的价格远高于“黎凡特”棉或短绒棉。

In colonising Sudan, Muhammad Ali’s initial aim had been to take over these rich agricultural regions and develop cotton, indigo, and sugar production using slave labour – the method that was proving successful in the American South. However, in 1822 the Nubian and Arabic-speaking communities of northern Sudan rebelled against the occupation and killed the commander of the invading forces, Muhammad Ali’s son Isma‘il Pasha. The Turco-Egyptian forces encountered similar opposition to their attempts to control Upper Egypt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-093"></a>[93](#note-ch3-093) While the occupiers eventually suppressed the resistance and made efforts to develop a cotton and indigo industry, their main efforts moved back to the north. In the same year as the death of his son, Muhammad Ali ordered the digging of thousands of wells and the construction of waterwheels in the Nile Delta north of Cairo, presumably following the Sudanese model, in order to expand cultivation from irrigated gardens into large fields and allow widespread summer cultivation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-094"></a>[94](#note-ch3-094) Another local merchant firm, the Jibara brothers, rivals of Briggs& Co, supplied credit for a new plantation in the Delta.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-095"></a>[95](#note-ch3-095) The introduction of <a id="page-116-en"></a>〔原书第116页〕mechanised spinning in Lancashire had made British mills dependent on these luxury varieties, not to produce finer cloth but because threads spun from the longer fibres were less liable to pull apart in the rough handling of the machine process. For this reason, in Liverpool long-staple cotton achieved a much higher price than the ‘Levant’ or short-staple variety.

<a id="ch03-0060"></a>

棉花如今可以为向埃及供应武器提供资金。马胡贝伊把棉花用作获取“优质武器”的手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-096"></a>[96](#note-ch3-096)已经为埃及海军供应过船只的塞缪尔·布里格斯，代表穆罕默德·阿里派一艘护卫舰到英格兰，进行包铜处理并安装火炮和其他装备。当费用远远超过该船运去的亚麻籽油货物价值时，布里格斯赊购了工程和武器，然后向利物浦运送了 270 包长绒棉，作为偿还债务的第一期款项。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-097"></a>[97](#note-ch3-097)这批货开启了与兰开夏之间利润丰厚的埃及棉花贸易。在东地中海建造并武装一个强大的新国家，为亚历山大的商人银行家提供了通过曼彻斯特棉纺厂重新引导信用创造的新机会。

The cotton could now finance the supply weapons to Egypt. Mahu Bey used the cotton as a means of acquiring ‘weapons of superior quality’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-096"></a>[96](#note-ch3-096) Samuel Briggs, who had already supplied vessels for the Egyptian navy, sent a frigate to England on behalf of Muhammad Ali, to be coppered and fitted with guns and other equipment. When the expense far exceeded the value of the cargo of linseed oil the ship had carried there, Briggs had the work and the weaponry supplied on credit, then sent a shipment of 270 bales of long-staple cotton to Liverpool, as a first instalment of the repayment of the debt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-097"></a>[97](#note-ch3-097) This shipment inaugurated a lucrative trade in Egyptian cotton with Lancashire. Building and arming a powerful new state in the Eastern Mediterranean provided the merchant bankers of Alexandria with a new opportunity to reroute credit creation via the cotton mills of Manchester.

<a id="ch03-0061"></a>

### 包装贡赋

### Packaging Tribute

<a id="ch03-0062"></a>

欧洲的革命战争和奥斯曼帝国的转变，为信用创造突然转向艰难的工厂生产绕道提供了一种解释。这次绕道不是由对商品的简单需求驱动的，而是由对新的信用机制的需要驱动的：战争破坏了旧的商业路线，创造了转移金融票据的迫切需求。然而，欧洲经历的革命和战争——尽管其破坏性超过该大陆近期历史上的任何其他事件——以及尼罗河上新地区强国的建立，都只是更大范围内信用流动及依赖这种流动的利润遭到扰乱的一部分。更广泛的中断不是以欧洲和奥斯曼世界为中心，而是以亚洲殖民政权的转变和美洲以奴隶制为基础的生产体系为中心。

The revolutionary wars in Europe and the transformations in the Ottoman Empire offer one explanation for the sudden diversion of credit creation into the difficult detour of factory production. The detour was driven not by a simple demand for goods, but by the need for a new mechanism of credit, when warfare broke up old routes of commerce and created an urgent need for mechanisms to move financial paper. However, the European experience of revolution and war, although more disruptive than any other events in the continent’s recent past, and the building of a new regional power on the Nile were only part of a much wider interruption to the flow of credit, and the profits that depended on it. The broader interruption centred not on Europe and the Ottoman world, but on the transformation of colonial regimes in Asia and the system of slave-based production in the Americas.

<a id="ch03-0063"></a>

在印度，孟加拉强大商人和信用网络的兴起——这一发展与开罗正在发生的变化相似——削弱了莫卧儿统治，并把英国东印度公司的代理人吸引到从这些商业<a id="page-117"></a>〔原书第117页〕网络中获利、在权力斗争中选边站的机会中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-098"></a>[98](#note-ch3-098)结果，莫卧儿帝国把最富有的领土控制权丢给了公司。1765 年，它被迫授予公司对孟加拉及邻近省份税收的权利。公司从一家军事化贸易公司转变为领土强权。在接下来的几年里，它通过进一步击败欧洲和印度对手扩大了这种权力。因此，正如埃德蒙·伯克所报道的，“商业和统治领域都发生了一场非常重大的革命”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-099"></a>[99](#note-ch3-099)这一转变虽然确保了公司在印度的财富，却带来了如何把这些收入运回英国的新问题。作为一家贸易公司，其股东和公司职员曾通过为欧洲和印度之间的货物运输融资而致富：运往欧洲的主要是精细纺织品、香料和其他奢侈品。为了通过汇票贴现从贸易融资中获利，公司需要一些东西从欧洲运回印度。由于十七和十八世纪的欧洲几乎不生产任何值得运回亚洲的东西，这种贸易依赖于运送从另一个殖民统治地获取的商品——墨西哥和秘鲁矿山的白银。到 1750 年，白银变得稀缺，于是补充以军需品和海军物资，供针对亚洲和欧洲对手的日益扩大的殖民战争使用，此外还有数量不多的毛织品（通常免运费运输）以及铜和其他金属。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-100"></a>[100](#note-ch3-100)到 1780 年代，船只有时空载驶往印度，运回货物的目的不是互惠贸易，而是包装贡赋，尤其是公司职员作为私人财富获取的那部分。“以货物汇寄贡赋的想法自然使他们对其价格和质量漠不关心——货物本身似乎只是贡赋的一种包装，”伯克解释说，“作为贡赋取得或代替贡赋购买的货物，永远不可能在种类和价格上长期适合一个仅靠商业信誉支撑的市场。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-101"></a>[101](#note-ch3-101)这种单方面转移贡赋的结果是孟加拉的贫困。但它也导致了伦敦建立在早期互惠商业基础上的票据体系的崩溃。这里谈到的第二种、发生时间更早的中断，是转向制造业的又一个来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-102"></a>[102](#note-ch3-102)

In India, the rise of powerful merchants and credit networks in Bengal, a development similar to the changes under way in Cairo, had weakened Mughal rule and drawn agents of the British East India Company into the opportunities to profit from these commercial <a id="page-117-en"></a>〔原书第117页〕networks and to take sides in the power struggle.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-098"></a>[98](#note-ch3-098) As a result, the Mughal Empire lost control of its richest territories to the Company. In 1765, it had been forced to grant the Company the right to the tax revenues of Bengal and neighbouring provinces. The Company was transformed from a militarised trading corporation into a territorial power. It extended that power over the following years with further defeats of both European and Indian rivals. Consequently, as Edmund Burke reported, ‘a very great revolution took place in commerce as well as in dominion’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-099"></a>[99](#note-ch3-099) While the transformation secured the riches of the Company in India, it presented the novel problem of how to ship those revenues back to Britain. As a trading firm, its shareholders and company servants had grown rich from financing the movement of goods between Europe and India: mostly fine textiles, spices, and other luxuries to Europe. To profit from the financing of trade, through the discounting of bills of exchange, the Company needed something to ship in the other direction, from Europe back to India. Since Europe in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries produced almost nothing worth carrying back to Asia, the trade had depended on shipping a commodity sourced in another place of colonial rule, silver from the mines of Mexico and Peru. By 1750, silver was becoming scarce and was supplemented with the shipment of military and naval supplies for the expanding colonial warfare against both Asian and European rivals, along with modest supplies of woollen goods, usually shipped freight-free, and copper and other metals.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-100"></a>[100](#note-ch3-100) By the 1780s, ships were sometimes travelling empty to India, returning with goods whose purpose was not reciprocal trade but a means of packaging tribute, especially the part acquired as private wealth by company servants. ‘The idea of remitting tribute in goods naturally produced an indifference to their price and quality, – the goods themselves appearing little else than a sort of package to the tribute,’ Burke explained. ‘Merchandise taken as tribute, or bought in lieu of it, can never long be of a kind or of a price fitted to a market which stands solely on its commercial reputation.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-101"></a>[101](#note-ch3-101) The result of this one-way transfer of tribute was the impoverishment of Bengal. But it also caused the collapse of the paper system in London built on earlier reciprocal commerce. This second and earlier disruption was a further source of the detour into manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-102"></a>[102](#note-ch3-102)

<a id="ch03-0064"></a>

第三种扰乱的来源——可以说对信用创造转向制造业最为重要——是由 1775—83 年美国独立战争造成的奴隶贸易和奴隶种植园利润中断，以及大西洋奴隶战争和结束人口贸易的压力对这些<a id="page-118"></a>〔原书第118页〕利润构成的更广泛威胁。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-103"></a>[103](#note-ch3-103)美国革命的爆发部分受到印度事件的影响。英国政府曾试图通过授予东印度公司向其北美殖民地运输茶叶的垄断权，来解决印度贸易危机，导致波士顿茶叶商人发起叛乱。北美殖民者试图效仿英国商人移民在印度享有的自由，“强调帝国不同部分——尤其是孟加拉和十三个殖民地——之间的宪制相似性”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-104"></a>[104](#note-ch3-104)美国人甚至似乎仿用了东印度公司旗帜上的十三道红白条纹，作为新共和国的国旗。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-105"></a>[105](#note-ch3-105)

The third source of disruption, and, arguably, the most important for the diversion of credit creation into manufacturing, was the interruption to profits from slave trading and slave plantations, caused by the American Revolutionary War of 1775–83 and by wider threats to those <a id="page-118-en"></a>〔原书第118页〕profits from the Atlantic slave war and the pressures to end the trade in humans.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-103"></a>[103](#note-ch3-103) The outbreak of the American Revolution was partly influenced by events in India. The British government had tried to address the crisis in the India trade by awarding the East India Company a monopoly on shipping tea to its North American colonies, causing Boston tea merchants to initiate their rebellion. The North American colonists sought to emulate the freedom enjoyed by British merchant-settlers in India, ‘emphasizing constitutional similarities among the different parts of the empire, especially Bengal and the thirteen colonies’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-104"></a>[104](#note-ch3-104) The Americans even appear to have copied the thirteen red-and-white stripes of the East India Company ensign for the flag of the new republic.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-105"></a>[105](#note-ch3-105)

<a id="ch03-0065"></a>

但这场叛乱是一场更广泛危机的一部分。奴役非洲人在西印度群岛生产糖、在北美殖民地生产烟草，推动了一个庞大的信用循环。被奴役者在数年或数十年间为其所有者带来回报，因此对他们的奴役不仅产生了人口贸易，还产生了一个不断扩张的信用体系。一个奴隶的价格代表了那些未来劳动年限的资本化价值。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-106"></a>[106](#note-ch3-106)这笔钱通常不是在购买时以现金支付，而是作为债务在数年内偿还给利物浦商人和伦敦代理商人，他们以信用方式为被奴役劳动力的供应提供融资，“主要通过汇票贴现机制”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-107"></a>[107](#note-ch3-107)汇票贴现也是建立在奴役之上的更广泛三角贸易的主要利润来源。以非洲贸易为例，虽然可以通过商品销售产生收入，但对主导贸易的人来说，主要业务和利润来源是通过汇票贴现组织信用所产生的收入。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-108"></a>[108](#note-ch3-108)大西洋奴隶贸易对整个信用体系的重要性，使它处于“英国政治和经济生活的正中心”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-109"></a>[109](#note-ch3-109)

But this rebellion was part of a wider crisis. The enslavement of Africans to work in the production of sugar in the West Indies and tobacco in the North American colonies had given movement to a vast circulation of credit. Enslaved humans generated a return to their owners over years or decades, so their enslavement produced not just a trade in human lives but an expanding system of credit. The price of a slave represented the capitalised value of those prospective years of labour.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-106"></a>[106](#note-ch3-106) It was typically paid not in cash at the moment of purchase, but as a debt repaid over the years to the Liverpool merchants and London commission agents who financed the supply of enslaved labour on credit, ‘mostly through the mechanism of bill discounting’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-107"></a>[107](#note-ch3-107) The discounting of bills was also a main source of profit in the wider triangular trade built upon enslavement. In the case of the Africa trade, for example, while an income could be generated from merchandise sales, the primary business and source of profit for those who dominated the trade was the income generated from the organising of credit through the discounting of bills.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-108"></a>[108](#note-ch3-108) The importance of the Atlantic slave trade to the entire system of credit positioned it ‘at the very center of English political and economic life’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-109"></a>[109](#note-ch3-109)

<a id="ch03-0066"></a>

美国革命对这一奴隶金融体系的中断，刺激了棉纺织业的发展。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-110"></a>[110](#note-ch3-110)美国战争使四分之三的伦敦商行破产。在曼彻斯特，五分之四的制造商——其中大多数人既是制造商也是商人——在二十年的战争期间消失了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-111"></a>[111](#note-ch3-111)前文提到的最早大型棉纺厂之一奎里班克纱厂，就是在奴隶贸易受扰、北美贸易中断之后建立的，而拥有该厂的格雷格家族主要从事的正是这些贸易，他们拥有奴隶种植园和商船<a id="page-119"></a>〔原书第119页〕运输业务。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-112"></a>[112](#note-ch3-112)与受法国战争打乱的德国商人一样，活跃于大西洋贸易的人积累了大量汇票，以及通过赊售被奴役者、或从因战争被迫破产的所有者手中收购加勒比奴隶种植园而获得的债券。兰开夏与加勒比奴隶制的密切联系，使英格兰这个地区在货币意义上独一无二。作为大西洋体系的一部分，它是全国唯一一个汇票而非硬币、地方银行券或其他信用形式充当主要货币来源的地区。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-113"></a>[113](#note-ch3-113)大西洋体系形成了密集的信用货币网络，却被战时封锁和中断打乱。棉花生产提供了一种疏通这些流动的手段，尤其是因为它促进了“第二次奴隶制”的发展，即把被奴役者大规模重新部署到美国南方的新种植区，而种族灭绝和生态毁灭为扩张清除了道路。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-114"></a>[114](#note-ch3-114)作为另一个半球的收成，棉花受到长途运输不确定性和遥远气候不可预测性的影响，为投机性贸易和保险合同创造了更多获利机会。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-115"></a>[115](#note-ch3-115)棉花还具有一种不同寻常的商品特性：它可以双向运输，先作为原棉运往兰开夏，然后作为制成品返回美洲。在其他时候，原料生产者会避免这种迂回过程，把制造过程搬到棉花原本的产地——那里同时也是制成品后来的销售地。但在这个案例中，生产者是被奴役的，种植园主可以阻止他们自己织布，因为种植园主的利润需要这种运输绕道。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-116"></a>[116](#note-ch3-116)从汇票中获利，依赖于这种组织绕道、创造信用货币双向流动的能力。

The interruption to this system of slave finance from the American Revolution was a spur to the development of cotton manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-110"></a>[110](#note-ch3-110) The American war bankrupted three-quarters of the London merchant houses. In Manchester, four out of five manufacturers, most of them merchants as much as manufacturers, disappeared during the two decades of war.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-111"></a>[111](#note-ch3-111) Quarry Bank Mill, already mentioned as one of the first large cotton mills, was set up after disruptions to the slave trade and interruptions to the North American trade in which the proprietors, the Greg family, owners of slave plantations and merchant <a id="page-119-en"></a>〔原书第119页〕shipping, were mainly involved.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-112"></a>[112](#note-ch3-112) Like the German merchants disrupted by the French wars, those active in the Atlantic trade accumulated large numbers of bills of exchange, as well as the bonds acquired in the credit sale of enslaved people or in the acquisition of Caribbean slave plantations from owners forced into bankruptcy by the war. The close connections between Lancashire and Caribbean slavery made that region of England unique in monetary terms. As an element of the Atlantic system, it was the one part of the country in which bills of exchange, rather than specie, local banknotes, or other forms of credit, functioned as the main source of money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-113"></a>[113](#note-ch3-113) Forming a dense network of credit money, the Atlantic system was thrown into disarray by the wartime blockages and interruption. Cotton production provided a means to unblock these flows, not least because it facilitated the development of ‘the second slavery’, the vast redeployment of enslaved people to the new plantation zones of the American South, where genocide and ecocide cleared the path of expansion.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-114"></a>[114](#note-ch3-114) As the harvest of another hemisphere, cotton was subject to the uncertainty of longdistance shipping and the unpredictability of a distant climate, creating additional opportunities for profit from both speculative trading and insurance contracts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-115"></a>[115](#note-ch3-115) Cotton also had the unusual character of a commodity that could be shipped in both directions, first as raw cotton to Lancashire and then as manufactured products crossing back to the Americas. In other times, the producers of the raw material would have avoided this circuitous process by bringing the manufacturing process to where the cotton was first produced and later sold as a finished product. But, in this case, the producers, being enslaved, could be prevented from making their own cloth by the owners of the plantations, whose profit required the detour of shipping.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-116"></a>[116](#note-ch3-116) Profiting from bills of exchange depended on this ability to organise a detour, creating reciprocal movements of credit money.

<a id="ch03-0067"></a>

把现代工业生活的兴起视为一次历史绕道，有几个好处。第一，它有助于避开技术决定论问题——这一问题在殖民灌溉史、优步的故事以及许多其他领域中已经遇到过，在这些领域中，技术被视为一种自行推动改进的力量。第二，它避免把西北欧一小块地方、以及该地域内一个更小地区兰开夏历史上的“例外性断裂”变成一种范式，用来解释世界每个角落工业化的成败或“发展”的成败。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-117"></a>[117](#note-ch3-117)第三，它用一种从未来攫取方式、即资本化来理解资本的路径，取代生产主义的资本主义理解，后者不可避免地<a id="page-120"></a>〔原书第120页〕以工业生产的故事为中心。

To approach the rise of modern industrial life as a historical detour has several advantages. First, it helps avoid the issue of technical determinism, a problem already encountered in the history of colonial irrigation, the story of Uber, and many other areas, where technology is taken to be a self-moving force of improvement. Second, it avoids turning an ‘exceptional discontinuity’ in the history of a small corner of northwest Europe, and of an even smaller region within that territory, Lancashire, into a paradigm that can explain the success and failure of industrialisation or ‘development’ in every corner of the world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-117"></a>[117](#note-ch3-117) Third, it replaces a productivist understanding of capitalism, which inevitably <a id="page-120-en"></a>〔原书第120页〕centres on the story of industrial production, with an approach that understands capital in terms of modes of capture of the future, or capitalisation.

<a id="ch03-0068"></a>

这种路径并不要求低估英国所发生之事后来的重要性。但它可以从临界点的角度来界定这种重要性。绕道和中断可能偶然启动新的过程，产生广泛影响。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-118"></a>[118](#note-ch3-118)其中之一就是雇佣劳动所促成的信用生产转变，我们现在就来讨论这一点。

This approach does not require minimising the subsequent significance of what happened in Britain. But it can frame that significance in terms of tipping points. Detours and disruptions can accidentally set in motion new processes, with wide repercussions.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-118"></a>[118](#note-ch3-118) One of those is the transformation in credit production enabled by wage labour, to which we now turn.

<a id="ch03-0069"></a>

### 恶是小额货币之根

### Evil Is the Root of Small Money

<a id="ch03-0070"></a>

我们现在可以讨论对生产主义、技术驱动、欧洲中心的资本史或资本化史论的第二个修正。工业革命是一次绕道。它提供了一条新的循环回路，一种把从债务创造中获利的机会折向不同路径、扩大攫取装置的办法。但它做到这一点，不仅是通过建立需要融资的新路线和新商品。它还附带创造了一套庞大的新信用机器：大批工人被组织进工厂和煤矿，领取货币工资。

We can now consider the second modification to productivist, technology-driven, European-centred arguments about the history of capital, or capitalisation. The industrial revolution was a detour. It offered a new circuit, a way of bending onto a different path the opportunities for profiting from the creation of debt, amplifying the apparatuses of capture. But it did this not only through establishing new routes and goods to be financed. It incidentally created an extensive new machinery of credit: large bodies of workers, organised into factories and coal mines, who were to be paid a monetary wage.

<a id="ch03-0071"></a>

雇佣劳动常被视为现代工业资本主义的一个决定性特征，尤其是工厂生产中受纪律约束、受时间管理的劳动。工资把人类行动者分为提供劳动者和拥有资本者，把制造业及其他生产的产品分为付给雇员的工资和资本所有者索取的利息与利润。一方面是小时工资或月工资，另一方面是利息和利润，这种对比似乎使工人劳动所得与资本非劳动所得之间非同寻常的差异显得正常。对于莫伊舍·波斯通——上一代最有影响力的马克思理论重新阐释者之一——来说，工资对于“价值”效果至关重要，资本主义下的社会支配正是通过这种效果组织起来的。波斯通认为，即使承认生产过程产生的剩余并非全都是劳动的产物——这不同于较早的马克思主义研究，而恰恰在承认这一点时尤其如此——工资仍然发挥着强大的功能。它以统一的时间增量衡量劳动价值，从而使一切劳动变得可比。这种*估值*过程把所有生产性工作转化为同一种<a id="page-121"></a>〔原书第121页〕看似抽象的活动的单位。小时和分钟的同质、空洞的统一性——按既定费率支付，并表现为该劳动的“价格”——作为一种支配性抽象运作，创造出一种支配模式：把越来越大份额的收益分配给不为此工作的人。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-119"></a>[119](#note-ch3-119)

Wage labour is often seen as a defining feature of modern, industrial capitalism, especially the disciplined, time-managed labour of factory production. The wage separates human agents into those who provide labour and those who own capital, dividing the product of manufacturing and other production into wages paid to employees and the interest and profit claimed by owners of capital. The contrast between an hourly or monthly wage, on the one hand, and interest and profit, on the other, appears to normalise the extraordinary difference between the earned income of the worker and the unearned income of capital. For Moishe Postone – among the most influential reinterpreters of Marxian theory of the last generation – the wage is central to the effect of ‘value’ through which social domination under capitalism is organised. Even if one acknowledges, unlike older Marxian scholarship, that not all of the surplus generated by processes of production is a product of labour, indeed especially with that acknowledgement, Postone argues, the wage still performs a powerful function. It makes all labour comparable, by measuring its value in uniform increments of time. This process of *valuation* transforms all productive work into units of the same <a id="page-121-en"></a>〔原书第121页〕seemingly abstract activity. The homogeneous, empty uniformity of hours and minutes of labour, paid at a given rate and appearing as the ‘price’ of that labour, operates as a governing abstraction, creating the mode of domination that allocates a larger and increasing share of earnings to those who do not work for them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-119"></a>[119](#note-ch3-119)

<a id="ch03-0072"></a>

这一分析虽然有说服力，却忽略了一点。工资作为一种抽象而运作，不仅在于：对许多工人而言，工资的“价值”是用抽象的小时和分钟来表示的。它以另一种或许更有效的方式抽象。与以小时和分钟计算价值的装置一样，这种效果依赖于对时间的部署。然而，它不是工厂雇佣那种一丝不苟的“时间纪律”，尽管那可能很重要。它是那种不精确、未经计量、由来已久的推迟和延迟机制——只是以新的规模实行。与从生产性劳动中获利的较早形式一样，延迟采取的形式是工作履行与工资支付之间的时间间隔，尤其是工资支付与其用于消费支出之间的间隔。这样看待工资，不是把焦点从生产领域转向交换和消费领域——这些区分在今天越来越没有意义——而是理解工资作为信用生产装置的意义。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-120"></a>[120](#note-ch3-120)我们将看到，工资以信用货币支付。从中获得的利润是*绕道*进入制造业的意外后果。这一后果的表现和持续时间都将超过制造业本身的优势。

This analysis, for all its persuasiveness, overlooks something. The wage operates as an abstraction not only through the abstractness of the hours and minutes in which, for many workers, its ‘value’ is presented. It abstracts in another, perhaps more effective way. Like the device of calculating value in hours and minutes, this effect rests on the deployment of time. However, it is not the meticulous ‘time discipline’ of factory employment, significant as that may be. It is the inexact, unmeasured, age-old mechanism of postponement and delay – practised on a new scale. As with older forms of profiting from productive labour, the delay takes the form of the gap in time between the performance of work and its payment, and, even more so, between the paying of the wage and its spending on consumption. To see the wage in this way is not to shift focus from the sphere of production to that of exchange and consumption – distinctions that make less and less sense today – but, rather, to understand the significance of the wage as a device for the production of credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-120"></a>[120](#note-ch3-120) The wage was paid in credit money, as we will see. The profit to be made from it was an unanticipated consequence of the *detour* into manufacturing. It was a consequence that would outperform and outlast the advantages of manufacturing itself.

<a id="ch03-0073"></a>

什么是工资，又如何支付？工厂的不同寻常之处，在于把几十名、有时几百名工人置于一家企业的控制之下。这产生了一个问题：在一个主要依靠账面信用组织起来、家庭仆人和许多其他工作人员大多以食物和衣物支付报酬的世界里，如何找到给他们发钱的手段？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-121"></a>[121](#note-ch3-121)习惯于只在特殊情况下使用硬币、或只在账簿无法“结算”或无法用更多信用来对账时结清年度账目的商人，突然需要一种每周或每月末进行大量小额支付的手段。许多货币史研究把这描述为一场危机，导致人们反复努力寻找某种得到广泛使用的“小额货币”形式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-122"></a>[122](#note-ch3-122)然而，我们可以不把这视为工业扩张的障碍，而视为工业扩张所创造的机会。事实上，它可能是理解这种扩张的关键。当代经济<a id="page-122"></a>〔原书第122页〕理论中一个有影响的论点提出，对货币的需要源于交换行为参与者之间缺乏信任，因此“恶是一切货币之根”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-123"></a>[123](#note-ch3-123)或许更好的看法是，以工厂劳动剥削条件为形态的恶，是*小额*货币之根：如今突然需要用来支付工资的硬币、代金券和纸币。这些轻小的象征物——以*物品*形式存在的货币——很快就会被人误认为货币的一般本质。

What was a wage, and how was it paid? The factory was unusual in bringing under the control of one firm dozens and, in some cases, hundreds of workers. This produced a problem: how to find the money to pay them, in communities organised largely on the use of book credit, in a world where domestic servants and many other kinds of staff were paid mostly in food and clothing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-121"></a>[121](#note-ch3-121) Merchants accustomed to using coinage only in exceptional circumstances, or to settle yearly accounts when the books could not be ‘reckoned’, or reconciled, with further credits, suddenly needed a means of making large numbers of small payments at the end of every week or month. Many studies of monetary history portray this as a crisis, leading to repeated efforts to find a means of introducing some widely used form of ‘small money’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-122"></a>[122](#note-ch3-122) However, we can see this not as an obstacle to the expansion of industrial production but as the opportunity it created. In fact, it may be a key to understanding that expansion. An influential argument in contemporary economic <a id="page-122-en"></a>〔原书第122页〕theory proposes that the need for money arises from the lack of trust between those involved in an act of exchange, and thus that ‘evil is the root of all money’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-123"></a>[123](#note-ch3-123) It may be better to see evil, in the shape of the exploitative conditions of factory labour, as the root of *small* money: the coins, chits, and banknotes now suddenly required for paying wages. These slight, token things – money in the form of *objects* – would soon come to be mistaken for the nature of money in general.

<a id="ch03-0074"></a>

以前，大商人往往不仅参与获取货物，还参与为货物生产融资，办法是一种被称为外放制的信用操作：商人把材料借贷给农民、织工或布商。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-124"></a>[124](#note-ch3-124)以支付工资为基础的工厂生产强化了这种控制，但也代表了一种从信用创造中获利的新方法。在外放制中，无论农业还是手工业，商人通常借出种子、羊毛、亚麻或其他必需品，而耕作者或织工借出自己的劳动。商人以折扣价提前“购买”成品，生产者则用产品全额偿还预付款。由此产生的产品为这些贷款带来利润。商人和工人之间的利润分配反映了他们力量的不平等。在工厂生产中，工人如今向厂主提供信用。他们工作一整天或一整周，把自己的劳动借给雇主。这笔贷款产生剩余，即所付劳动工资与该劳动产品价值之间的差额，这笔剩余由雇主获得。

Previously, large merchants had often been involved not only in procuring goods but in financing their production, through the credit operation known as the putting-out system, where merchants loaned materials to a farmer, weaver, or clothier.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-124"></a>[124](#note-ch3-124) Factory production, based on the payment of a wage, intensified this control, but also represented a new method to profit from credit creation. In putting out, both in farming and in handicraft, the merchant typically loaned the seed, wool, flax, or other requirements, while the cultivators or weavers loaned their labour. The merchant paid a discounted price to ‘purchase’ in advance the finished product, while the producer repaid the advance in full with the product. The resulting product yielded a profit on these loans. The share of profit going to merchant and worker reflected their unequal strength. With factory production, the workers now advanced credit to the mill owner. They worked an entire day or week, loaning their labour to the employer. This loan yielded a surplus, the difference between the wage paid for the labour and the value of the product of that labour, a surplus that was acquired by the employer.

<a id="ch03-0075"></a>

商品和服务生产中大规模组织劳动，如何成为另一种攫取装置？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-125"></a>[125](#note-ch3-125)现代商业银行的货币创造能力，最初是通过为对外贸易、战争和奴役提供融资发展起来的。正是通过那些特殊的装置，货币被“物质化”，从单纯的记账单位转变为对未来付款的具体索取权——变成“真正的”货币。然而，当工业生产把一种国内的工资支付制度普遍化时，货币可以通过第二种方式物质化，即通过国内的劳动过程。就连日常的商品制造过程，也可以成为攫取未来的装置。棉纺织业特别适合这一角色：作为世界商业的“怪胎”，它以奴隶种植园和工厂中的劳动资本化为基础，使通过信用攫取剩余的机会翻倍。

How does the large-scale organisation of labour in the production of goods and services become another apparatus of capture?<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-125"></a>[125](#note-ch3-125) Modern commercial banking developed its powers of money creation initially through the financing of foreign trade, warfare, and enslavement. It was through those exceptional apparatuses that money was ‘materialised’, transformed from a mere unit of account into a concrete claim on future payments – into ‘real’ money. However, when industrial production generalised a domestic regime of wage payment, money could be materialised in a second way, through the labour process at home. Even the daily process of making goods could become an apparatus for the capture of the future. Cotton manufacturing was particularly suited to this role: as a ‘freak’ of world commerce, based on the capitalisation of labour both on slave plantations and in factories, it doubled the opportunities for the capture of surplus through credit.

<a id="ch03-0076"></a>

大规模雇佣的组织通常被理解为通过支付工资“购买”劳动。但这种<a id="page-123"></a>〔原书第123页〕市场交换的形象是一种虚构——尽管不是通常所解释的那种虚构方式。雇主或企业通常不用过去积累的资金支付工人。工人以信用货币获得报酬：他们的工资是一笔贷款。起初，信用体系的运作相当明显。例如，1820 年代的英格兰，约克郡纺织织造商约翰·福斯特父子公司在工人劳动一个月后才“支付”工资，而且不是用现金，而是给每个织工的账户记一笔信用。与此同时，公司向雇员供应货物，包括“煤、蜡烛、布匹、面粉、麦芽、牛奶、糖、糖浆和奶酪”，使他们持续负债。工资只是从这些长期债务中扣除。其他公司直接用“实物”或物质商品支付工人。truck（实物支付）一词最初意味着用一种物品交换另一种物品，但实物支付并不是物物交换安排。工资被记为账面信用，预支给工人，用于购买雇主供应的货物。这些货物通常定价过高，有时只是未售出的纺织品或企业的其他产品。或者，工人得到代金券、代币或纸币，只能在公司自营商店兑现。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-126"></a>[126](#note-ch3-126)

The organisation of large-scale employment is usually understood as the ‘purchase’ of labour, via the payment of a wage. But that image of a <a id="page-123-en"></a>〔原书第123页〕market exchange is a fiction – although not in the way the fiction is usually explained. The employer or firm does not typically pay workers with funds accumulated from the past. The workers are paid in credit money: their wage is a loan. Initially, the working of the credit system was quite visible. In England in the 1820s, for example, the Yorkshire textile-weaving firm of John Foster and Sons ‘paid’ its workers one month in arrears, and not in cash but by assigning a credit to each weaver’s account. Meanwhile, the firm supplied its employees with goods, including ‘coal, candles, cloth, flour, malt, milk, sugar, treacle and cheese’, leaving them continuously in debt. The wage was simply a deduction from these standing debts. Other firms paid their workers directly in ‘truck’, or material goods. The term trucking originally implied giving or trafficking one item in exchange for another, but payments in truck were not barter arrangements. The wage was recorded as book credit, advanced to the worker, to be spent on goods supplied by the employer. The goods were typically overpriced, and sometimes consisted of just unsold textiles or other produce of the business. Or the workers were paid in vouchers, tokens, or notes that were redeemable only at the company-owned shop.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-126"></a>[126](#note-ch3-126)

<a id="ch03-0077"></a>

1806 年，曼彻斯特商人塞缪尔·希伯特匿名出版了一本小册子，论述使用“小面额纸币”的弊端。这种做法的出现，源于制造商发行期票

In 1806, Samuel Hibbert, a Manchester merchant, published anonymously a pamphlet on the evil of the use of ‘small notes’. Their use had arisen from the practice of manufacturers issuing promissory notes

<a id="ch03-0078"></a>

> 以支付其雇工；本来每周都必须筹措一笔现金来支付这些雇工；如果用这种方便的纸片就能满足他们，那么应付给他们的工资——随着时间推移必然达到相当可观的数额——就可以由雇主用于贸易。这种流通还因如下想法而受到进一步鼓励：对于由此获得的信用，他们不必支付任何利息。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-127"></a>[127](#note-ch3-127)

> to pay persons in their service, for whom a quantity of cash must be procured each week; and if they can be satisfied with such convenient paper, the wages due to them, which in the course of time, must amount to a very considerable sum, can be used by their employers in trade. Such a circulation is still farther encouraged, by the reflection, that for credit thus obtained, they pay no interest.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-127"></a>[127](#note-ch3-127)

<a id="ch03-0079"></a>

换言之，正如殖民商人与其说从货物供应中获利，不如说从信用创造中获利，而种植园奴隶制和货物供应是这种信用创造的机制；同样，新兴的大型纺织制造商——其中多数人起家于长途贸易商人——发现制造业的剩余不必来自机械化生产日益提高的效率。技术效率永远不可能成为长期差别利润的来源，即使像让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊或他兄弟糖业公司所经历的那种故障、挫折和事故被克服，因为竞争对手公司很快就会达到<a id="page-124"></a>〔原书第124页〕同样的效率。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-128"></a>[128](#note-ch3-128)更可靠的剩余来源，可以是新信用体系的规模——在这个体系中，工人的工资不是以现金支付，而是以雇主的期票或账面信用支付。

In other words, just as colonial merchants made their profit not so much from the supply of goods, but from the creation of credit for which plantation slavery and the supply of goods was the mechanism, in the same way the emergent large textile manufacturers, most of whom began as long-distance merchants, discovered that the surplus from manufacturing did not have to arise from the increasing efficiency of mechanised production. Technical efficiency could never be a longterm source of differential profit, even once the breakdowns, setbacks, and accidents experienced by men like Jean-Baptiste Say or his brother’s sugar company were overcome, as rival firms would soon adopt the <a id="page-124-en"></a>〔原书第124页〕same efficiencies.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-128"></a>[128](#note-ch3-128) Surplus could arise more reliably from the scale of the new system of credit, in which the wages of workers were paid not in cash, but in the employer’s promissory notes or book credit.

<a id="ch03-0080"></a>

议会曾多次试图取缔实物支付的做法，1831 年的《实物工资法》在许多行业中禁止这种做法，1887 年又将禁令扩大到更多领域。1831 年的立法是《工厂法》的前身；《工厂法》代表着规范工资及其与工时关系的更广泛尝试，帮助确立了一种印象：工资是时间与劳动的直接交换，而不是信用体系的一个方面——在这个体系中，雇主实际上攫取了贷款利息。但甚至在实物支付被取缔之前，用来支付工资的信用货币创造就已经变得如此普遍，以至于它不再表现为贷款，也不再依赖个别雇主发行自己的票据或代币。

Parliament attempted repeatedly to outlaw the practice of truck payment, banning it in many trades in the Truck Act of 1831, and extending the ban more widely in 1887. The 1831 legislation was a precursor to the Factory Acts, which represented a wider attempt to regulate wages and their relation to hours of work, helping to establish the impression that the wage was a direct exchange of time for labour rather than the aspect of a credit system in which the employer in effect captured the interest on a loan. But even before truck payments were outlawed, the creation of credit money to pay wages had become so general that it no longer appeared as a loan, and no longer depended on individual employers issuing their own notes or tokens.

校注：底本此处确作“时间与劳动的直接交换”（a direct exchange of time for labour），与本章其他地方的工资与劳动交换表述有异。译文照录，未擅自将time改为money。 

<a id="ch03-0081"></a>

在英格兰，随着十八世纪末和十九世纪初制造业的发展，涌现出数百家小银行，通常由当地商人和商人兼制造商创办。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-129"></a>[129](#note-ch3-129)它们的信用创造能力最初是通过为贸易融资发展起来的，如今可以在雇佣劳动这一新领域扩展，这需要银行发行面额更小但数量更大的纸币。“在地方上，小面额纸币成为支付工资的常见方式，到 1825 年，许多地区银行家发行量的一半或更多是面额低于 5 英镑的纸币。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-130"></a>[130](#note-ch3-130)随着催生现代工业的更广泛商人信用和银行体系的发展，商人或银行会通过创造信用货币来预支支付工资的钱。工人用这些信用购买自己和他人生产的商品。这些购买是把资金返还银行体系、偿还信用创造所依凭之贷款的手段。这些购买代表了工人所生产之物的全部价值，因为信用货币只能相对于它将据以收回的未来产品和服务而被创造出来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-131"></a>[131](#note-ch3-131)与实物工资制一样，利润是通过这个信用装置“攫取”的：制造商和零售商对货物的定价高于其生产成本。

In England, hundreds of small banks emerged with the development of manufacturing in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century, typically formed by local merchants or merchant manufacturers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-129"></a>[129](#note-ch3-129) Their power of credit creation, initially developed through financing trade, could be expanded in the new field of wage labour, requiring the issuing of paper notes by the banks in smaller denominations, but in larger quantities. ‘In the provinces small notes became the common method of paying wages, and by 1825 one-half or more of the issues of the bankers in many districts were notes of less than £5.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-130"></a>[130](#note-ch3-130) As the wider system of merchant credit and banking that spawned modern industry developed, merchants or banks would advance the money for wages, by the creation of credit money. Workers spent these credits on the goods that they and others produced. These purchases were the means of returning the funds to the banking system, in repayment of the loan through which the credit had been created. The purchases represented the entire value of what the workers produced, for credit money can be created only in relation to the future products and services through which it will be recaptured.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-131"></a>[131](#note-ch3-131) As with the system of truck, profit was ‘captured’ through this credit apparatus, by the manufacturer and retailer charging more for the goods than the cost of their production.

<a id="ch03-0082"></a>

为了使这套体系普遍化，信用创造逐渐由一个独特的实体——银行——来管理，银行逐渐从最初兼营贸易、信用创造和生产安排的商人商行中分离出来。银行发行的信用货币被标准化为支付工人“工资”的手段。银行发行纸币的做法逐渐统一。最终，只有<a id="page-125"></a>〔原书第125页〕一种纸币，即中央银行或财政部的纸币——在此即英格兰银行的纸币——被使用。货币取代了商人、雇主和地方银行发行的多种货币，呈现出统一的全国性制度的外观。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-132"></a>[132](#note-ch3-132)然而，尽管政府逐渐垄断了纸币印刷，正如它们先前垄断了硬币铸造，私人商业银行仍保留着创造货币的权力。几乎所有货币仍然是通过私人创造的：银行为企业和个人客户开立账户，客户开具支票或安排付款，使这种信用货币在企业之间或从雇主向工人转移。大型企业——尤其在美国——也在货币创造中发挥作用，不仅通过发行股票和债券，还通过创造商业票据；美国大型企业广泛使用商业票据支付工资。

To generalise this system, the creation of credit came to be managed by a distinct entity, the banking house, which gradually separated itself from the merchant houses that had originally combined trade, credit creation, and the arranging of production. The credit money issued by banks was standardised as a means of payment of a worker’s ‘wage’. The issuing of notes by banks was gradually made uniform. Eventually, only <a id="page-125-en"></a>〔原书第125页〕one note, that of the central bank or treasury – in this case, the Bank of England – was used. In place of multiple kinds of money issued by merchants, employers, and local banks, money took on the appearance of a uniform, national institution.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-132"></a>[132](#note-ch3-132) However, while governments came to monopolise the printing of paper money, just as they had earlier monopolised the minting of coins, private commercial banks retained their power to create money. Almost all money continued to be privately created, through banks opening accounts for business and individual customers, who wrote cheques or arranged payments that transferred this credit money between firms or from employers to workers. Large enterprises, especially in the United States, also played a role in money creation, not only through issuing shares and bonds, but through the creation of commercial paper, widely used by large firms in the United States to pay wages.

<a id="ch03-0083"></a>

这种创造信用货币以支付工资的安排，确认了“抽象劳动”的效果，即一种印象：工人只是在参与交换行为，用其劳动的使用权换取标准化的“货币”支付。从这个角度看，工业革命代表着信用关系的扩展和重组，而不是从商业资本向产业资本的转变。

This arrangement of creating credit money to pay wages confirmed the effect of ‘abstract labour’, the impression that workers were simply involved in an act of exchange, trading the use of their labour for a standardised payment in ‘money’. From this perspective, the industrial revolution represented an extension and reorganisation of credit relations, rather than a shift from commercial capital to industrial capital.

<a id="ch03-0084"></a>

### 城市与商业

### City Business

<a id="ch03-0085"></a>

还有另一种方式可以让我们把工业化视为某种绕道。另外两种机制很快就将超越并取代工厂，成为组织未来资本化的主要场所。与工厂一样，它们各自提供了一种攫取装置，把未来收入转化为当下可以折扣价获得的资产；它们也各自提供了一种安排或场所，用来组织关于货币和物质生活的知识。其中之一后来被称为“商业”，另一种被称为城市生活或“城市”。商业和城市都不是用来理解物质过程的新对象。但在十九世纪后期和二十世纪初，无论是在欧洲还是在殖民世界的许多地方，二者都成为值得关注的事项，很像几十年前的“工业”，因为它们各自成为扩张性新攫取权力的焦点。考察它们的出现，将有助于我们重新定位工业生产的地位——并理解后来向“经济”观念的转向，这个问题将在接下来的章节中探讨。

There is a further way in which we can see industrialisation as something of a detour. Two other mechanisms were soon to overtake and displace the factory as principal sites of organising the capitalisation of the future. Like the factory, each of these provided an apparatus of capture that transformed future revenue into assets that could be acquired at a discount in the present; each also provided an arrangement or site for organising knowledge about money and material life. One of these came to be known as ‘business’, the other as urban life or ‘the city’. Neither business nor the city was a new object for making sense of material processes. But, in the later nineteenth and early twentieth century, both in Europe and in many parts of the colonised world, each emerged as a matter of concern, much like ‘industry’ in earlier decades, as each became the focus of expansive new powers of capture. Looking at their emergence will help us resituate the significance of industrial production – and to understand the later turn to the idea of ‘the economy’, a question to be explored in the chapters that follow.

<a id="ch03-0086"></a>

<a id="page-126"></a>〔原书第126页〕十九世纪的资本家似乎很少乐意通过工业过程来攫取收入。制造业既费力又常常危险，即使对厂主来说也是如此。让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊因为机器故障造成的困难而放弃制造业，这并不例外。欧内斯特·克罗尼耶在一次工业事故中失去一根手指——此人后来把萨伊家族的炼糖帝国变成投机贸易生意，并使其破产——则是又一个提醒。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-133"></a>[133](#note-ch3-133)约克郡的商人兼制造商威廉·布鲁克被热靛蓝染料溅到而失明后，把纱厂的管理权交给儿子们，自己转而投资铁路股票。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-134"></a>[134](#note-ch3-134)格雷格家族的纱厂已经成为英国最大的纺织制造商，却发现自己几乎无利可图，部分原因是父亲把公司传给四个儿子后，仍就建筑和机器的最初成本收取租金，从不折旧。儿子们很快厌倦了这种辛苦，甚至连罗伯特也是如此，他经营的是贸易和融资业务，而不是纱厂本身。“我会发现我在买好棉花、卖好价和融好资上花费的时间、注意力和焦虑都毫无回报，”他向父亲抱怨道。另一个儿子则想知道还要过多久“在这里过这种狗一样的生活。我从不打开一本书……早上五点半起床，晚上十点上床，整天像划桨奴隶一样劳作”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-135"></a>[135](#note-ch3-135)和父亲一样，也像大多数商人一样，儿子们对成为食租者的兴趣，甚至超过了对没有回报的制造业的兴趣。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-136"></a>[136](#note-ch3-136)公司通过收购其他纱厂而扩张，部分是以接收纱厂来抵偿别人因利润更高的棉花贸易业务而欠他们的债务，但也因为他们能以 3.25% 的利率抵押纱厂借入资金，然后用借来的资金投机，赚取 5% 的收益。最终，无论是奎里班克纱厂还是他们拥有的其他任何纱厂——那些气势恢宏、标志性的工业革命场所——都不再靠制造业赚钱。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-137"></a>[137](#note-ch3-137)

<a id="page-126-en"></a>〔原书第126页〕Nineteenth-century capitalists seldom seemed to enjoy having to capture revenue through the industrial process. Manufacturing was laborious and often dangerous, even for the mill owners. Jean-Baptiste Say was not exceptional in abandoning manufacturing due to the difficulties caused by the breakdown of machinery. The finger lost in an industrial accident by Ernest Cronier, the man who then turned the Say family’s sugar-refining empire into a speculative trading business, and bankrupted it, was another reminder.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-133"></a>[133](#note-ch3-133) William Brooke, a merchant-manufacturer in Yorkshire, handed the management of his yarn-making mill to his sons after becoming blind from being splashed with hot indigo, and invested instead in railway shares.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-134"></a>[134](#note-ch3-134) The Greg family, whose mills had become the largest textile manufacturer in Britain, found themselves making little or no profit, in part because the father, having passed the firm onto his four sons, continued to claim a rent on the initial cost of the buildings and machinery, never depreciating their value.
