The sons soon tired of the effort, even Robert, who ran the trading and financing operations rather than the mills themselves. ‘I shall find I have given my time, attention and anxiety in buying cotton well, selling well and financing well, for nothing,’ he complained to his father. Another son wondered how long ‘to continue the dog’s life I am leading here. I never open a book . . . rise at 5:30 a.m., go to bed at 10 p.m. and toil like a galley-slave all day’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-135"></a>[135](#note-ch3-135) Like the father, and like most business people, even the sons were more interested in becoming rentiers than the unrewarding work of manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-136"></a>[136](#note-ch3-136) The company expanded through acquiring other mills, partly in settlement of debts owed from the more lucrative cotton-trading operations, but also because they could borrow funds at 3.25 per cent mortgaged on the mills, then earn 5 per cent by speculating with the borrowed funds. Eventually, neither Quarry Bank nor any of their other mills, those imposing, iconic sites of the industrial revolution, was making money from manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-137"></a>[137](#note-ch3-137)

<a id="ch03-0087"></a>

格雷格家族、萨伊炼糖公司以及许多其他人的经历，代表了一种更大的变化。几十年内，制造业已被另一种转变超越，即“商业”的兴起。这是十九世纪后期出现的一个术语，用来命名一种新现象：现代股份公司和它的新伙伴机构投资银行同时发展起来。

The experience of the Greg family, the Say refinery company, and many others typifies a larger change. Within a few decades, manufacturing had been overtaken by another transformation, the rise of ‘business’. This was the term that emerged in the later nineteenth century to name a new phenomenon, the simultaneous development of the modern joint-stock company and its new partner institution, the investment bank.

<a id="ch03-0088"></a>

正如[第一章](#ch01-0001)所指出的，从 1860 年代到 1914 年的半个世纪，以两项相互关联的发展为标志。在第一次世界大战前的两<a id="page-127"></a>〔原书第127页〕代人的时间里，北半球少数几个强国巩固了对全球南方大多数国家以及北美现存原住民的帝国统治。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-138"></a>[138](#note-ch3-138)与此同时，这个时代以新规模的改造地球工程为特征：长途铁路、大型船运运河和海港、跨洋电报、城市照明和电力发展，以及河流系统的重新工程化。同样，它也以帝国权力和技术项目的新规模所促成的债务创造新形式为特征。

As noted in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), the half-century from the 1860s to 1914 was marked by two interconnected developments. Within the space of two <a id="page-127-en"></a>〔原书第127页〕generations before the First World War, a handful of powers in the northern hemisphere consolidated imperial rule over most countries of the Global South, as well as the surviving native peoples of North America.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-138"></a>[138](#note-ch3-138) At the same time, it was an era defined by terraforming projects on a new scale: long-distance railways, large ship canals and sea ports, trans-oceanic telegraphs, the development of municipal lighting and electric power, and the re-engineering of river systems. Equally, it was defined by the novel forms of debt creation that the new scale of imperial power and technical projects enabled.

<a id="ch03-0089"></a>

帝国的批评者用新术语“帝国主义”来描述由金融驱动的支配扩张。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-139"></a>[139](#note-ch3-139)许多批评者逐渐把这种金融扩张及其输出海外视为一种“过剩”资本的流动，这种剩余是由“资本在已进入机器经济的制造业中拥塞”以及低工资造成的剩余“储蓄”所创造的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-140"></a>[140](#note-ch3-140)这种观点反映了我们在此考察过的对货币的同样误解。金融资本在很大程度上，并不是由现有企业的剩余或储蓄经银行或私人投资者转投新项目而形成的。它是金融业制造的信用货币，是一种把未来收入在当下资本化的手段。它的创造不取决于是否有过去积累的剩余可供吸收，而取决于能否把未来建构为一种对尚待获取的剩余的可靠索取权，使这种索取权能够在当下变现和交易。

Critics of empire described the finance-driven expansion of domination with the new term ‘imperialism’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-139"></a>[139](#note-ch3-139) Many of the critics came to see this expansion of finance and its export abroad as the flow of an ‘excess’ of capital, a surplus created by the ‘congestion of capital in the manufacturing industries which have entered the machine economy’ and the ‘saving up’ of surplus because of low wages.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-140"></a>[140](#note-ch3-140) This view reflects the same misunderstanding of money we have examined here. Finance capital, for the most part, does not come into being as the surplus or savings from existing business, redirected through banks or private investors into new ventures. It is credit money, manufactured by the industry of finance, as a means of capitalising in the present a future revenue. Its creation depends not on the availability of a surplus to absorb from the past, but on the construction of a future in the form of a reliable claim on a surplus to be acquired, in a manner that can be realised and traded in the present.

<a id="ch03-0090"></a>

因此，十九世纪后期信用机制的这次扩张不应被理解为一种与先前工业扩张相对的“金融”扩张，而应理解为一种技术政治扩张。信用的创造不仅需要日益增多的金融家、投资银行家和股票推销商的努力。它需要技术设备和改造地球，从而通过一种机制制造和控制未来收入流；这种机制在可靠性、产权、帝国扩张和暴力执行方面的形式，使这些收入流在当下可得。这些安排补充了管理未来收入的较早装置——无论是通过殖民贸易、奴隶种植园和政府发动战争，还是甚至通过煤矿开采和制造业的绕道——在大多数情况下最终超越了它们。

This later-nineteenth-century expansion of credit mechanisms should therefore be understood not as a ‘financial’ expansion, in contrast to the industrial expansion that preceded it, but as a technopolitical one. The creation of credit required not just the efforts of a proliferating class of financiers, investment bankers, and stock promoters. It required the technical equipment and terraforming through which future flows of revenue could be manufactured and controlled via a mechanism whose forms of reliability, property, imperial expansion, and violent enforcement made them available in the present. These arrangements supplemented the older apparatuses for governing future revenue, whether through colonial trade, slave plantations, and government war-making, or even the detour of coal mining and manufacturing, in most cases eventually overtaking them.

<a id="ch03-0091"></a>

正如我们所见，1860 年代至 1914 年期间的技术和科学发展具有一组相互关联的特征，它们促进了这种新的收入攫取，同时又<a id="page-128"></a>〔原书第128页〕受到这种攫取的鼓励——技术与物质耐久性的新形式，伴随着法律和经济学的变化，为建造收入攫取装置提供了新方法。这些还涉及货币创造的新方法。

As we saw, the technical and scientific developments of the period from the 1860s to 1914 had a set of interrelated characteristics that facilitated this new capture of revenue and were simultaneously <a id="page-128-en"></a>〔原书第128页〕encouraged by it – the new forms of technical and material durability, accompanied by changes in law and economics, allowing new ways to build apparatuses for the capture of revenue. These also involved new methods of money creation.

<a id="ch03-0092"></a>

作为一台代际财富转移的机器，股份公司需要另一个组织——投资银行——的协助。投资银行不同于较早的商人银行，后者为殖民贸易和动产奴隶制提供融资，并创造那些活动所依赖的新规模战争所需的政府债务。它们也不同于伴随制造业发展和货币工资支付而出现的地区性和地方银行。投资银行服务于不同的目的，提供一种新的货币创造形式。它们的出现既不是为了服务贸易，也不是为了服务工业，而是为了承销股份公司的创建并从中获利，主要是为修建铁路和其他基础设施，往往还是帝国规模的基础设施。它们管理公司债券和股票的发行，处理失败企业的重组，并安排合并和收购。与通常以合伙形式经营的较早银行不同，投资银行本身常常就是股份公司，出售从股票营销业务中获取的未来利润的索取权。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-141"></a>[141](#note-ch3-141)它们获得了惊人的货币创造权力。新的大型基础设施所许诺的未来收入的耐久性，以及帝国权力不断扩大的规模，使信用货币创造的装置得以大幅扩展。

As a machine for the intergenerational transfer of wealth, the joint-stock corporation needed the assistance of another organisation, investment banking. Investment banks differed from the older merchant banks, which financed colonial trade and chattel slavery and created the government debt required for the new scale of warfare on which those depended. They also differed from the provincial and local banks that accompanied the development of manufacturing and the payment of money wages. Investment banking served a different purpose, providing a new form of money creation. They emerged to serve neither trade nor industry, but to underwrite and profit from the creation of joint-stock companies, principally for the building of railways and other infrastructure, often on an imperial scale. They managed the issuing of corporate bonds and shares, handled the reorganisation of failed ventures, and arranged mergers and acquisitions. Unlike older banks, which were usually run as partnerships, they were frequently themselves joint-stock companies, selling claims on the future profits to be made from the business of marketing shares.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-141"></a>[141](#note-ch3-141) They acquired an astonishing power to create money. The durability of the future revenue promised by new, large-scale infrastructure and the growing scale of imperial power allowed a vastly expanded apparatus for the creation of credit money.

<a id="ch03-0093"></a>

除了商业这一新领域，还出现了第二种构造这种扩大了的未来关系的机制：现代城市。从十九世纪后期起，大都市经历了一系列类似的技术变革，这些变革之所以可能，是因为用钢铁和混凝土建造，燃煤发电站的发展，电动安全电梯、电动有轨电车和电气轻轨的发明，以及利用法律安排和种族歧视来规划和管理空间的使用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-142"></a>[142](#note-ch3-142)城市房地产开发商如今可以做与铁路企业家相同的事（他们常常就是同一批人）：竖起一座建筑，其价值从建成之日起就与建造成本关系不大。在靠碳燃料驱动的现代化城市里，房地产的价格对应于投机者出售未来几十年在该地块居住权的资本化价值。

Alongside the new sphere of business, there was a second object that emerged as a mechanism for constructing this expanded relationship to the future: the modern city. From the late nineteenth century, the metropolis was undergoing a similar set of technical changes, made possible by building with iron and steel and concrete, by the development of coal-fuelled electric power stations, by the invention of the electric safety elevator, the electric-powered tram, and electric light railways, and by employing legal arrangements along with race discrimination to plan and regulate the use of space.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-142"></a>[142](#note-ch3-142) Developers of urban property could now do the same thing as railway entrepreneurs (they were frequently the same persons): erect a structure whose value, from the day it was built, had little to do with the cost of its construction. The price of real estate, in the carbon-fuelled modernising city, corresponded to the capitalised value at which the speculator could sell the right to live for the next several decades on that spot of land.

<a id="ch03-0094"></a>

<a id="page-129"></a>〔原书第129页〕大多数作家未能把城市理解为一种装置，一种像大型商业公司那样从未来攫取付款的装置。当政治经济学家和开发商不得不向人们解释，为什么住房价格可以远高于建造建筑的成本时，他们并没有从建筑物作为一种从未来抽取收入的机器所具有的扩大能力来解释这种差异；他们把在起作用的机制伪装起来，把剩余归因于自然不断变化的价值。他们说，城市开发把自然的或“未改良的”土地变成房地产。建造成本与建筑可售价格之间的差异，被归因于“土地”不断上涨的“价值”。1900 年，正如我们在导论中指出的，一位纽约建筑师把一座快速建成的商业建筑简单描述为“一台让土地付钱的机器”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-143"></a>[143](#note-ch3-143)但付款并不来自土地，而来自空间未来的租户或购买者。土地只是托词。亨利·乔治和其他大多已被遗忘的政治经济学家等论者，曾反对用这种过于简单的方式，来解释投机者凭借房地产开发这一装置攫取未来收入的奇特能力。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-144"></a>[144](#note-ch3-144)然而，价格体系的新理论家把价值解释为一种产物，不是攫取装置的产物，而是一种被描绘为供求相互作用的简单机制的产物。这种耐久装置在技术上的新颖性很快就从视野中消失了，而价格机制在该装置中仅起次要作用。

<a id="page-129-en"></a>〔原书第129页〕Most writers failed to understand the city as an apparatus, like the large business corporation, for capturing payments from the future. When political economists and developers had to explain to people why the price of housing could become so much higher than the cost of erecting the building, they did not explain the difference in terms of the expanded ability of buildings to work as machines that extract revenue from the future; they disguised the mechanism at work by attributing the surplus to the changing value of nature. Urban development, they said, transformed natural or ‘unimproved’ land into real estate. The difference between the cost of construction and the price at which a building could be sold was ascribed to the rising ‘value’ of the ‘land’. In 1900, as we noted in the introduction, a New York architect described a rapidly built commercial building as simply ‘a machine that makes the land pay’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-143"></a>[143](#note-ch3-143) But the payment came not from the land, but from the future renters or purchasers of the space. Land was merely the alibi. Writers like Henry George and other mostly forgotten political economists fought against this simplistic way of explaining the strange ability of speculators to capture future revenue through the device of property development.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-144"></a>[144](#note-ch3-144) However, the new theorists of the price system explained value as the product, not of an apparatus of capture, but of the simple mechanism pictured as an interaction of supply and demand. The technical novelty of the durable apparatus, in which the price mechanism played a minor part, soon disappeared from view.

<a id="ch03-0095"></a>

人们可以把经济学家与一门新城市科学——城市规划领域——的创始人加以对比。苏格兰规划师和社会理论家帕特里克·格迪斯受到托斯丹·凡勃伦的影响，并像凡勃伦一样受到亨利·乔治的影响；他属于那些理解城市房地产非劳动价值如今代表的并非市场力量的作用、而是这种对未来、并因而对那些将通过住房成本上涨来偿还它的人之劳动的索取权的作家。格迪斯写道，现代城市“破败街道”和“破败房屋”中积累的财富，主要在于“对其他地区他人破败街道的文书索取权，以及对其*未来*劳动的索取权”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-145"></a>[145](#note-ch3-145)他和其他人提出的补救办法，是一种新实践——城市规划，用公民财富的创造和分配来平衡私人对未来劳动索取权的积累，尤其是通过建设花园城市——一种混合形式，用“城市与乡村生活健康、自然和经济的结合”取代工业城市的“破败街道”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-146"></a>[146](#note-ch3-146)花园城市的先驱埃比尼泽·霍华德解释说，这种新型城乡形式的<a id="page-130"></a>〔原书第130页〕目的，是通过收取全部地租并将其存入社区信托来获取房地产开发所创造的非劳动所得剩余。信托反过来支付公共工程、公园和其他设施的费用，并提供退休养老金以及事故和疾病保险。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-147"></a>[147](#note-ch3-147)在霍华德影响下，“红色维也纳”的规划师和建筑师——这座把公共住房作为两次世界大战之间欧洲城市生活社会民主愿景基础的城市——创造了共同攫取城市生活所创造价值的最戏剧性范例。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-148"></a>[148](#note-ch3-148)然而在实践中，这些优托邦式方案最容易在欧洲的海外殖民地推广，例如开罗周边赫利奥波利斯、马阿迪和花园城等街区的开发；把新德里建成殖民印度新首都；以及大雅法计划——巴勒斯坦城市雅法与其郊外不断扩张的犹太复国主义定居点特拉维夫组成的集合城市，由帕特里克·格迪斯本人绘制总体规划。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-149"></a>[149](#note-ch3-149)然而在大多数地方，规划者缺乏推行这种集体方案的权力；而殖民版本依靠种族排斥来管理空间使用，没有实施任何集体攫取和重新分配剩余的计划。由于建筑和产权具有新的耐久性和规模，城市生活成为另一种装置——与现代商业公司并列——企业家可以在其中把从后来者那里攫取的收入提前变现于当下。对空间的殖民化依赖于对时间的殖民化力量。

One can contrast the economists with the founders of a new science of the city, the field of urban planning. The Scottish planner and social theorist Patrick Geddes, influenced by Thorstein Veblen and, like Veblen, by Henry George, was among the writers who understood that the unearned value of urban property now represented not the working of market forces but this claim on the future, and thus on the labour of those who would repay it through the increased cost of their housing. The wealth accumulated in the ‘mean streets’ and ‘mean houses’ of the modern city, Geddes wrote, consists chiefly in ‘documentary claims upon other people’s mean streets elsewhere, and upon their labour *in the future*’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-145"></a>[145](#note-ch3-145) The remedy that he and others proposed was the new practice of town planning, to balance the accumulation of private claims upon future labour with the creation and distribution of civic wealth, in particular through the building of garden cities – a hybrid form in which the ‘mean streets’ of the industrial city would be replaced with ‘a healthy, natural, and economic combination of town and country life’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-146"></a>[146](#note-ch3-146) The pioneer of the garden city, Ebenezer Howard, explained that the <a id="page-130-en"></a>〔原书第130页〕purpose of this new urban-rural form was to capture the unearned surplus created by the development of property by collecting all ground rent and holding it in a community trust. The trust, in turn, would pay for public works, parks, and other amenities and for the provision of retirement pensions and insurance against accident and sickness.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-147"></a>[147](#note-ch3-147) Influenced by Howard, the planners and architects of Red Vienna, the city that made public housing the basis of a social democratic vision for urban life in interwar Europe, produced the most dramatic example of the shared capture of the value that urban living creates.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-148"></a>[148](#note-ch3-148) In practice, however, it was in Europe’s overseas colonies that these eutopic schemes were most easily promoted, with the development of districts such as Heliopolis, Maadi, and Garden City around Cairo; the building of New Delhi as a new capital for colonial India; and the plan for Greater Jaffa, the conurbation of the Palestinian city of Jaffa and the expanding Zionist settlement on its outskirts, Tel Aviv, for which Patrick Geddes himself drew up the master plan.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-149"></a>[149](#note-ch3-149) In most places, however, planners lacked the power to impose such collective schemes, while the colonial versions, relying on racial exclusion to manage the use of space, implemented none of the plans for the collective capture and redistribution of surplus. Thanks to the new durability and scale of buildings and property rights, urban living became another apparatus, alongside the modern business corporation, in which entrepreneurs could realise revenues in the present captured from those who would come later. The colonisation of space relied upon the powers of colonising time.

<a id="ch03-0096"></a>

### 金融与实体

### The Financial and the Real

<a id="ch03-0097"></a>

让我们回到货币及其作为信用的制造这一问题，以及这种对货币的理解如何被遗忘。随着现代投资银行与现代商业公司和现代城市一同出现，那些论述新货币体系如何运作的人，可以毫无困难地说明货币是银行创造的东西。苏格兰政治经济学家亨利·邓宁·麦克劳德出版了最有影响的论述。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-150"></a>[150](#note-ch3-150)本章开篇提到的常驻开罗金融专家米切尔—英尼斯承认自己得益于麦克劳德的著作。麦克劳德写道，银行“不是‘借入’和‘贷出’货币的机构，而是一家信用的制造厂”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-151"></a>[151](#note-ch3-151)

Let us return to the question of money and its manufacture as credit, and how this understanding of money was forgotten. As modern investment banking emerged alongside the modern business corporation and the modern city, those who wrote about how the new monetary system worked had no problem in explaining that money was something created by banks. A Scottish political economist, Henry Dunning Macleod, published the most influential account.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-150"></a>[150](#note-ch3-150) Mitchell-Innes, the Cairo-based financial expert with whom this chapter began, acknowledged his debt to Macleod’s work. A bank, Macleod wrote, ‘is not an office for “borrowing” and “lending” money, but it is a Manufactory of credit’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-151"></a>[151](#note-ch3-151)

<a id="ch03-0098"></a>

到二十世纪中叶，这种理解已在很大程度上消失。1960 年出版的一部经典著作*《金融理论中的*<a id="page-131"></a>〔原书第131页〕*货币》*的作者们知道，大部分货币是由私人银行创造的。但他们把这视为一种残余现象。正如书名所示，他们的目的不是解释货币在银行中如何运作——他们没有研究实际的银行业务——而是说明如何让货币在“一种理论”中发挥作用。他们所说的理论，是指新古典经济学的假设。正统经济科学假定，所有经济现象都可以被理解为仿佛像价格机制那样组织起来：买卖双方交易商品和服务的安排。在这个理想化的世界里，贸易没有障碍。由于一种被称为“市场”的无摩擦金融平衡机制的运作，一种商品的供给总会自我调整到与需求相等。因此，货币是不需要的。在构成现代新古典经济学科学基础的经典阿罗—德布鲁模型中，货币并不存在。因此，货币和银行理论的目标不是弄清货币实际如何运作，而是在这个无摩擦的世界里为它安排一个人为的位置。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-152"></a>[152](#note-ch3-152)

By the mid-twentieth century, this understanding had largely disappeared. The authors of a classic text published in 1960, *Money in a* <a id="page-131-en"></a>〔原书第131页〕*Theory of Finance*, were aware that most money was created by private banks. But they treated this as a residual phenomenon. As the book’s title indicated, their aim was not to explain how money works in banks – they made no study of actual banking – but how money can be made to work within ‘a theory’. By theory, they meant the assumptions of neoclassical economics. Orthodox economic science assumes that all economic phenomena can be understood as if they were organised as a price mechanism, an arrangement of buyers and sellers trading goods and services. In this idealised world there are no impediments to trade. The supply of a good always self-adjusts, thanks to the operations of a frictionless financial balancing mechanism called ‘the market’, to equal demand. As a result, there is no need for money. In the classic Arrow–Debreu model that formed the scientific basis of modern neoclassical economics, money does not exist. So, the goal of a theory of money and banking was not to find out how money actually worked. It was to make an artificial place for it in this frictionless world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-152"></a>[152](#note-ch3-152)

<a id="ch03-0099"></a>

随着现代银行业的发展，私人创造信用货币的权力变得越来越不透明。日常实践掩盖了货币创造过程。人们变得对从未来攫取的方式浑然不觉。如果说工业化实现了“银行”与工厂的分离、以及“生产”时刻与信用供给的分离，那么公司、后来被称为“商业”的现象以及现代房地产的兴起，进一步加深了这种分离效果。

With the development of modern banking, the private power to create credit money became increasingly opaque. Everyday practices concealed the process of money creation. People became oblivious to the modes of extraction from the future. If industrialisation effected the separation of the ‘bank’ from the factory, and the moment of ‘production’ from the supply of credit, then the rise of the corporation, of the phenomenon that came to be called ‘business’, and of modern real estate, furthered this effect of separation.

<a id="ch03-0100"></a>

与货币的本质一样，银行业的作用也一直被误解。在通俗看法中，银行是存放和贷出货币的地方，而不是制造货币的行业。银行似乎从客户那里吸收存款，然后把同样的资金贷给其他客户。正统经济理论采纳并强化了这种常识观点。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-153"></a>[153](#note-ch3-153)银行业提供一种教科书称之为“金融中介”的服务，把买者与卖者、借款人与储蓄者配对，并促进他们之间的互动。在这种观点中，银行可能还有进一步的作用，但只在银行彼此之间的关系中，即作为一种支付机制，执行国家的金融记账。

As with the nature of money, the role of banking has been misunderstood. In the popular view, a bank is a place that stores and lends out money, not an industry that manufactures it. Banks appear to take in deposits from their customers, then loan out those same funds to other customers. Orthodox economic theory adopts and reinforces this common-sense view.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-153"></a>[153](#note-ch3-153) Banking provides a service that textbooks describe as ‘financial intermediation’, aligning those who purchase with those who sell, and those who borrow with those who save, and facilitating their interaction. Banks may have a further role, in this view, but only in their relations with one another, operating as a payments mechanism that carries out the nation’s financial bookkeeping.

<a id="ch03-0101"></a>

这种关于货币体系如何运作的通俗理解，被经济理论所复制，最近逐渐被认为在很大程度上是一种虚构。当银行向借款人提供资金时，它们并不是把吸收的存款贷出去。它们是在创造新货币。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-154"></a>[154](#note-ch3-154)制造过程如下。<a id="page-132"></a>〔原书第132页〕一位个人客户或企业向银行申请贷款，比方说金额为 10 万美元。如果银行同意，它为借款人设立一个账户，并在账簿中记录该账户有这一数额的正余额。这笔钱并不是从其他资金——例如其他客户的储蓄——转移过来的。它是凭空创造的，仅仅通过记录一个 10 万美元的余额这一简单行为。银行可以无中生有地创造货币，因为这些资金虽然记入客户名下的账户，却从未离开银行。借款人不会提着一个装有现金的公文包走出银行（除非在极少数情况下，而且金额很小），也不会在结束网上交易时拿到现金。相反，借款人收到的是一份纸质对账单或电子记录，表明新资金可以使用。当客户决定花掉这些资金时，钱离开客户的账户——但仍留在银行体系的账簿中。例如，如果这笔钱作为购买房地产的首付花出去，银行会把资金记为从借款人账户中扣除，并贷记到出售房地产者的账户。如果卖方是同一家银行的客户，资金就留在该银行的账簿中。如果卖方使用不同的银行，两家机构就在银行之间的每日账目结算中，记录一笔从一家银行账簿到另一家银行账簿的转移。

This popular understanding of how the monetary system works, reproduced in economic theory, has recently come to be understood as largely a fiction. When banks make funds available to borrowers, they are not lending out the money they have taken in as deposits. They are creating new money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-154"></a>[154](#note-ch3-154) The manufacturing works as follows. <a id="page-132-en"></a>〔原书第132页〕An individual customer or firm requests a loan from the bank, say in the amount of $100,000. If the bank agrees, it sets up an account for the borrower and records in its books that the account has a positive balance of that amount. This money is not transferred from some other fund, such as the savings of other customers. It is created from scratch, by the simple act of recording a $100,000 balance. The bank can create money out of nothing because the funds, although credited to an account in the customer’s name, do not leave the bank. The borrower does not walk out of the bank’s premises, or terminate an online transaction, with actual cash in a briefcase (except in rare cases, and only in small amounts). Rather, the borrower receives a paper statement or an electronic record indicating the availability of the new funds. When the customer decides to spend the funds, the money leaves the customer’s account – but stays within the books of the banking system. If the money is spent as the deposit on the purchase of a property, for example, the bank marks the funds as debited from the account of the borrower, and credits them to the account of the person selling the property. If the seller is a customer of the same bank, the funds remain in the books of that bank. If the seller uses a different bank, the two institutions record a transfer from the ledger of one bank to the other, as part of the daily settlement of accounts between banks.

<a id="ch03-0102"></a>

虽然上例中的银行创造了新的信用货币，但这些资金是通过相应的未来债务产生的。银行体系内创造的这些资金是对未来的索取权；其创造取决于对偿还这笔债务的未来付款的可靠支配。在接下来的数月或数年里，借款人将从未来收入中支付贷款金额，再加上银行收取的额外费用，作为使这笔未来债务付款今天可以由卖方即期获得的成本。这笔额外费用被称为贷款的“利息”。最好反过来看。未来债务将被全额偿还——其全部价值是本金加上“利息”。银行今天以折扣价把它提供给卖方——即未来向银行付款的贴现值。这个折扣（今天的较低价值）代表卖方为即期获得资金而支付的溢价。银行之所以能够今天即期提供未来资金，不是因为它向其他客户借入资金，而是因为它不断汇集其他客户的债务偿还。对未来债务的贴现正是货币的来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-155"></a>[155](#note-ch3-155)

While the bank in this example has created new credit money, the funds have been brought into being through a corresponding future debt. The funds created within the banking system are a claim on the future; their creation depends on this reliable command of the future payment of the debt. Over the following months and years, the borrower will pay from future income the amount of the loan, plus the surplus charged by the bank as the cost of making that future debt payment available on demand to the seller today. This surcharge is described as the ‘interest’ on the loan. It is better to see it in reverse. The future debt will be repaid in full – its full value being the principal plus the ‘interest’. The bank makes it available to the seller today at a discount – the discounted present value of the future payment to the bank. The discount (the lower value today) represents a premium the seller pays in exchange for immediate access to the funds, on demand. The bank is able to offer the future funds on demand today, not because it takes in loans from other customers, but because it continuously pools the debt repayments of other customers. The discounting of future debts is the very source of money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-155"></a>[155](#note-ch3-155)

<a id="ch03-0103"></a>

<a id="page-133"></a>〔原书第133页〕根据贷款期限和贴现率（被描绘为利率）以及任何相关费用，从未来收入中支付的金额可能达到所创造原始金额的两倍或更多。这样一来，银行体系对货币的创造本身就发挥着把未来收入转移到当下、并从这种对未来榨取中获利的作用。

<a id="page-133-en"></a>〔原书第133页〕Depending on the duration of the loan and the discount rate (portrayed as the rate of interest) along with any associated fees, the money paid from future income may amount to double the original sum created, or more. In this way, the very creation of money by the banking system operates to transfer future income to the present, and to profit from this extraction from the future.

<a id="ch03-0104"></a>

随着现代银行业的出现，从未来攫取的方式不仅支配我们已经考察的具体领域——进行长途贸易、支付工资、建设基础设施、提供住房或创建股份公司。它支配着所有这些领域以及其他领域，而所有这些都使货币的制造成为一种使未来负债的方式。所有这一切反过来又取决于国家的作用；国家并不像通俗想象的那样是货币的来源，而是承认银行创造的信用为货币的机构，特别是通过接受它以缴纳税款。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch3-156"></a>[156](#note-ch3-156)

With modern banking, the mode of extraction from the future comes to govern not only the specific fields we have already considered – the conduct of long-distance trade, the payment of wages, the building of infrastructure, the provision of housing, or the creation of joint-stock companies. It governs all these and more, all of which enable the manufacture of money as a mode of indebting the future. All of them depend, in turn, on the role of the state, which operates not as the source of money, as is popularly imagined, but as the agency that recognises bank-created credit as money, in particular via its acceptance of this for the payment of taxes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch3-156"></a>[156](#note-ch3-156)

<a id="ch03-0105"></a>

我们现在可以理解，为什么我们通常看不到货币如何运作。这里有三个问题。第一，可以称之为国家效应：只有极少量货币——估计约为 3%——采取硬币和纸币这种现成、可见的形式。这一小部分有形货币由公共造币厂或货币机构发行，并印有权威标志。我们把这个可见对象误认为整体，并假定所有货币都源自政府，通过公共手段生产。第二，日常经验效应：当个人或企业确实遇到银行创造货币的权力时——例如借款购买一辆车或一处房产，或取得公司贷款——他们得到一个自己名下的账户，列明新增资金。由于这如今是客户的钱，它似乎不再属于银行。然而，正如我们现在所知，尽管账户上写着客户的名字，这笔钱从未离开银行。

We can now understand why we do not normally see how money works. There are three issues. First, what one could call the state effect: only a very small amount of money, estimated at around 3 per cent, takes the ready, visible form of coins and banknotes. That small, tangible part is issued by a public mint or monetary agency and printed with symbols of authority. We mistake this visible object for the whole and assume that all money originates in government and is produced through public means. Second, the effect of everyday experience: when individuals or firms do encounter the power of banks to create money – for example, when borrowing funds to purchase, say, a vehicle or a property, or when taking out a company loan – they are given an account in their own name listing the new funds. Since this is now the customer’s money, it seems no longer to belong to the bank. Yet, as we now know, despite the name on the account, that money never leaves the bank.

<a id="ch03-0106"></a>

第三，也是最重要的，是我们不妨称之为经济效应的东西。正如我们将在[第五章](#ch05-0001)中看到、并在最后一章进一步探讨的，在二十世纪，把经济建构为政治和科学对象，只给金融留下一个次要位置。经济是一种衡量和描绘真实商品与服务流动的方式，以价格为代表。这种流动主要发生在两个部门之间，即企业和家庭，它们被表现为整体的互补部分。企业生产商品和服务，而家庭在同一时间点购买这些<a id="page-134"></a>〔原书第134页〕商品和服务，以其劳动作为交换。货币只被认为是促进这种即时交换的手段，而不是一种组织起来从这一过程和其他过程的时间运作中攫取剩余的信用装置。经济理论反映了这种简单的安排。经济在促成物质与货币、实体与表象、商业与银行之间表面上的分离方面的这一作用，是接下来各章要探讨的特征。

Third, and most important, there is what we might call the economy effect. As we will see in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001) and explore further in the final chapter, in the twentieth century, the construction of the economy as an object of politics and science allowed only a secondary place for finance. The economy was a way of measuring and picturing the movement of real goods and services, represented by prices. This movement happened largely between two sectors, business firms and households, represented as complementary parts of a whole. Firms produced goods and services, while households in the same temporal moment purchased those goods <a id="page-134-en"></a>〔原书第134页〕and services in exchange for their labour. Money was considered only a means of facilitating this instantaneous exchange, not as an apparatus of credit organised to extract a surplus from the temporal operation of this and other processes. Economic theory reflected this simple arrangement. This role of the economy in effecting the apparent separation of the material and the monetary, the real and the represented, the business and the bank, is a feature to be explored in the coming chapters.

<a id="ch03-0107"></a>

我们如今全神贯注于我们与未来的关系，却在很大程度上对其最日常的机制浑然不觉。货币，我们以为只是一种便利的简单物品，或一种记录实际事物价值的表象体系，结果却是一种从未来抽取收入的无所不在的机制。然而，它无法独自做到这一点。

We are preoccupied today with our relationship to the future, but largely oblivious of its most everyday mechanism. Money, which we think of as just a simple object of convenience or a system of representation for recording the values of actual things, turns out to be a ubiquitous mechanism for the extraction of future income. However, it cannot do this alone.

<a id="ch03-0108"></a>

大多数关于我们与未来关系的论述都是倒着写的。问题不仅在于时间顺序的颠倒，还在于解释与被解释现象之间的颠倒。习惯做法是从一种简单的唯物主义出发，把生活视为一系列需要满足的未来需求。为了满足这些需求，必须生产和分配商品。生产需要土地、设备、能源供应和分配基础设施。这些又需要信用供给，信用还可以为原料供应和成品购买提供资金。简单的唯物主义始于一个简单的未来，即由这样一种决定所召唤的未来：从必须满足的预期需求出发开始解释。这些需求把未来与当下连接起来。信用供给被描绘成对一系列似乎源于物质生活条件之要求的回应。在这种本末倒置的叙述中，信用随后才出现，作为一种补充。它为当下提供了一条回到那个未来的路径。

Most accounts of our relationship to the future are written backwards. The problem is a reversal not just of the temporal sequence, but of the explanation and the phenomenon to be explained. The habit is to begin from a simple materialism, where life is thought of as a set of future needs to be met. To satisfy those needs, goods must be produced and distributed. Their production requires land, equipment, the supply of energy, and an infrastructure of distribution. These, in turn, require the provision of credit, which can also finance the supply of raw materials and the purchase of finished goods. Simple materialism starts in a simple future, the future conjured by the decision to begin the explanation from the standpoint of prospective needs that must be satisfied. Those needs connect the future back to the present. The supply of credit is portrayed as a response to a set of requirements that appear to arise from the material conditions of life. Credit comes afterwards, in this back-to-front account, as a supplement. It supplies the present with a path back to that future.

<a id="ch03-0109"></a>

我们现在已经颠倒了这一顺序，避开了它简单的唯物主义。我们已经知道，随着大规模商业关系的扩展，信用并不是为服务贸易需要而创造的次要事物。恰恰相反，贸易是为了服务于信用创造而被组织起来的。同样，银行业也不只是一个“中介”，通过匹配借款人的需求与贷方可提供的资金来服务家庭和企业的需要。它变成了一家“制造厂”，一座制造信用货币的大型工场。

We have now reversed this sequence, avoiding its simple materialism. We already know that, with the spread of large-scale commercial relations, credit was not something secondary, created to serve the needs of trade. If anything, trade was organised to serve the creation of credit. Likewise, banking was not just an ‘intermediary’ that served the needs of households and businesses, by matching the demands of borrowers to the availability of lenders. It became a ‘Manufactory’, a large workshop for the manufacturing of credit money.

<a id="ch03-0110"></a>

这种颠倒并不要求我们放弃对物质过程的分析，转而研究金融的非物质形式。它要求一种不同的唯物主义：在这种唯物主义中，金融不是<a id="page-135"></a>〔原书第135页〕实体的对立面；相反，这种对立的生产——金融似乎与实体分离——本身就是一种需要研究和解释的效果。它还要求一种不同的未来观：不把未来视为由物质需求投射所召唤的想象世界，而视为为了从后来者那里、以牺牲共同未来为代价，占有财富和生计而建造的具体装置。

This reversal does not require us to abandon the analysis of material processes in favour of studying the immaterial forms of finance. It requires a different materialism, one in which the financial is not the <a id="page-135-en"></a>〔原书第135页〕opposite of the real, but, rather, one in which the production of this opposition, in which finance appears to stand apart from the real, is an effect to be studied and explained. And it requires a different approach to the future, seeing it not as the imaginary world conjured by the projection of material needs, but as the concrete apparatus built for the appropriation of wealth and livelihoods from those who come later, and at the expense of the common future.


# 第四章　解读未来之书

<a id="ch04-0001"></a>

<a id="page-136"></a>〔原书第136页〕

<a id="page-136-en"></a>〔原书第136页〕

<a id="ch04-0002"></a>

## 第四章　解读未来之书

## 4 Reading the Book of the Future

<a id="ch04-0003"></a>

我们已经进入这样一个世界：非凡的财富从未来索取，然后由后来者的生计来偿还。与此同时，当下大多数人的收入背负着偿还先前索取之成本的负担。这种跨时间获取收入的方式，并不是我们社会和经济生活标准图景的一部分。那幅图景围绕着一个不同的对象组织起来。我们想象自己当下通过一种我们称之为“经济”的安排相互联系。经济并不只是一种虚构，因为它对我们的生活方式产生真实影响。事实上，经济观念是资本托词的拱心石，它产生了对与未来关系的另一种理解。它掩盖了以未来为代价的生活方式。

We have come to inhabit a world in which extraordinary wealth is claimed from the future, then repaid from the livelihoods of those who come later. Meanwhile, the earnings of most people in the present carry the burden of repaying the cost of previous claims. This mode of capturing income across time is not part of the standard picture of our social and economic lives. That picture is organised around a different object. We imagine ourselves to be connected in the present by an arrangement that we name ‘the economy’. The economy is not a mere fiction, for it has real effects on the way we live. In fact, the idea of the economy is a keystone of the alibi of capital, producing a different understanding of relations to the future. It obscures the mode of living at the future’s expense.

<a id="ch04-0004"></a>

我们在过去三章中探索的那些世界，早于“这个经济整体”（the economy）这一观念的出现。当代的经济观念只能追溯到二十世纪中叶。虽然这个词本身古老得多，但直到第二次世界大战爆发前的几年，经济学家才开始把“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）本身视为一个对象。在两次世界大战之间，统计学家已经发展出估算价格、收入、购买和储蓄总量的方法。与此同时，经济学家设计出一种图式，把这些总量描绘成一个整体的各个部分。为了使这些数字显得构成一个对象——一个由相互作用的部分组成的独立结构——该图式必须估算各种总量，包括产品、企业、家庭、收入等等。但它也必须确定——正如我们将看到的——如何掩盖以未来为代价的生活成本，为我们的贫困化方式提供托词。到 1950 年代，这个整体开始被习惯性地描述为“<a id="page-137"></a>〔原书第137页〕经济”。在接下来的几十年里，在西方工业化国家（但不一定在其他地方），经济成为政治的中心对象。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-001"></a>[1](#note-ch4-001)

The worlds we have been exploring in the last three chapters precede the emergence of ‘the economy’. The contemporary idea of the economy dates only from the mid-twentieth century. While the term itself is much older, only in the years just before the Second World War did economists begin to refer to ‘*the* economy’ as an object in itself. In the interwar period, statisticians had developed methods of estimating aggregate levels of prices, incomes, purchasing, and savings. Meanwhile, economists devised a schema that pictured these aggregates as parts of a whole. To make the numbers appear to form an object – a freestanding structure of interacting parts – the schema had to estimate various totals, for products, firms, households, incomes, and more. But it also had to determine, as we will see, how to disguise the cost of living at the expense of the future, providing an alibi for our modes of impoverishment. By the 1950s, this whole came to be described routinely as ‘the <a id="page-137-en"></a>〔原书第137页〕economy’. Over the following decades, in the industrialised countries of the West but not necessarily elsewhere, the economy became the central object of politics.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-001"></a>[1](#note-ch4-001)

<a id="ch04-0005"></a>

在了解到经济作为独立对象的出现是多么晚近之后，大多数学者忽视了其发明的意义，继续把经济概念投射到更早的时期。这个词被非历史地使用，尤其是在历史学家当中，作为一个可以适用于任何时期的抽象概念，例如在讨论中世纪经济或古埃及经济时。既然更早的社会从事农业、制造商品、发展商业关系、创造信用并征收赋税，那么可以肯定地说它们拥有经济吧？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-002"></a>[2](#note-ch4-002)

On learning how recently the economy emerged as an object in itself, most scholars ignore the significance of its invention and continue to project the concept of the economy onto earlier periods. The term is used ahistorically, especially among historians, as an abstraction that can apply to any period, as in discussions of the medieval economy or the economy of Ancient Egypt. Since older societies engaged in agriculture, manufactured goods, developed commercial relations, created credit, and levied taxes, surely, they can be said to have had an economy?<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-002"></a>[2](#note-ch4-002)

<a id="ch04-0006"></a>

人们可以对这一观念采取那种态度，但没有必要这么做。前面几章探讨了几个世纪的货币、商业和物质生活史，却从未提到一种叫做“经济”的东西。这些章节避免使用这个词，因为它的非历史使用是有代价的。

One can take that approach to the idea, but there is no need to do so. The previous chapters have explored several centuries of the history of money, commerce, and material life without once referring to something called ‘the economy’. The chapters avoided the term because its ahistorical use comes at a cost.

<a id="ch04-0007"></a>

气候崩溃以及对地球系统和共同未来的其他威胁，要求我们放松“经济”对我们思想和行动方式的控制。近几十年来，经济推理和经济的需要，为未能充分应对这些威胁提供了最有力的理由。要对抗关于经济的论点和假设的力量，我们必须追问：这个二十世纪的实体是如何组织起来的，它如今如何支配我们，又如何塑造我们与未来的关系。这些问题将在下一章更充分地讨论，并在本书结尾再次讨论。但如果我们不先追问——正如本章所要做的——在经济被发明之前，财富、改善、对他人的义务和福祉是如何被治理和理解的，那么回答这些问题将更加困难。

Climate breakdown and other threats to Earth systems and collective futures require us to loosen the hold of ‘the economy’ over the way we think and act. In recent decades, economic reasoning and the needs of the economy have provided the most powerful justifications for failing to adequately address those threats. To counter the force of arguments and assumptions about the economy, we must ask how this twentieth-century entity was organised, how it governs us in the present, and how it shapes our relationship to the future. Those questions will be taken up more fully in the next chapter and again at the end of the book. But answering them will be more difficult if we do not first ask, as this chapter sets out to do, how wealth, improvement, obligation to others, and well-being were governed and understood prior to the invention of the economy.

<a id="ch04-0008"></a>

任何人类集体用来安排其生活形式、确立责任和义务的语言，都是构成这些生活形式的一部分——即使语言从未完全把握它所指称的世界。忽视一个集体生活赖以被理解的关键词，把另一个时代的术语当作普遍概念或普遍现代概念强加进来，就无法恰当理解那种生活。虽然这对所有语言和所有人类社会性形式都适用，但对经济学的语言尤其切题。正如最近几项研究所表明的，经济科学的方法是述行性的。也就是说，它力图使自己所描述的图式成为现实，并优化它们或<a id="page-138"></a>〔原书第138页〕使它们更有效。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-003"></a>[3](#note-ch4-003)虽然几乎任何科学都可以被证明与其对象有这种双向关系——力图把世界变成一个其模型或解释能够繁盛的地方——经济学在试图格式化其对象即经济方面发挥着显著作用。其原因部分在于经济学的计算性质，作为一门旨在为行动者和机构提供更好确定行动方针之手段的科学。原因还在于经济学与其他科学相比在辩护中的特殊作用——解释集体世界*为何*如此存在。

The language that any human collective employs to order its forms of life and establish duties and obligations is part of what constitutes those forms – even if language never fully apprehends the worlds it designates. Ignoring the key words in which a collective life is grasped and imposing terms from another age, treated as universal concepts, or universally modern concepts, fails to properly understand that life. While this is true of all language and all forms of human sociality, it acquires a special pertinence with the language of economics. The method of economic science, as several recent studies have shown, is performative. That is, it seeks to bring into being, and to optimise or <a id="page-138-en"></a>〔原书第138页〕make more effective, the schemas that it describes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-003"></a>[3](#note-ch4-003) While almost any science can be shown to have this two-way relation with its object, seeking to make of the world a place where its models or explanations can thrive, economics plays a marked role in attempting to format its object, the economy. The reasons for this lie partly in the calculative nature of economics, as a science oriented towards equipping agents and agencies with the means to better determine courses of action. They also lie in the special role that economics plays, compared with other sciences, in justification – in explaining *why* the collective world exists as it does.

<a id="ch04-0009"></a>

辩护的运作不仅通过为事物现状提供具体理由，还通过确立一种自然秩序。经济学把经济自然化为其对象，并假定自利是天赋的、通过经济作为一种根本秩序原则发挥作用，其运作方式类似于宗教实践在近代早期的角色。宗教哲学家使用“神义论”一词，指宗教话语在使世界上存在苦难和恶合理化方面的作用，尽管存在着全能和仁慈的神。可以说，经济话语执行着类似的操作，预设一种自然秩序即经济的存在，其交换过程趋向和谐。约瑟夫·福格尔借用希腊词*oikos*（经济一词*oikonomia*最初由此派生）提议，把经济学的这种操作称为“经济义论”（oikodicy）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-004"></a>[4](#note-ch4-004)这里的类比并非意在暗示经济学今天取代了宗教。事实上，“宗教”概念在西方出现的时间，与本章将要探讨的关于“经济”的观念相同，而且确实属于对辩护模式的同一重组过程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-005"></a>[5](#note-ch4-005)相反，它意在提示，“宗教”和“经济”的共同生产促成了经济学在辩护苦难方面未被承认的作用。

Justification operates not only by offering specific reasons for the way things are, but by establishing a natural order. In naturalising the economy as its object, and assuming that self-interest is innate and works through the economy as a fundamental principle of order, economics operates in a manner analogous to the early modern role of religious practice. Philosophers of religion use the term ‘theodicy’ to refer to the role of religious discourse in rationalising the presence of suffering and evil in the world, despite the existence of an allpowerful and benevolent deity. Economic discourse can be said to perform an analogous operation, positing the existence of a natural order, the economy, whose processes of exchange tend towards harmonisation. Drawing on the Greek term *oikos*, from which the word economy (*oikonomia*) was originally derived, Joseph Vogl suggests we refer to this operation of economics as ‘oikodicy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-004"></a>[4](#note-ch4-004) The analogy is not intended to imply here that economics operates today as a replacement for religion. In fact, the concept of ‘religion’ emerged in the West in the same period as the ideas about ‘economy’ to be explored in this chapter, and, indeed, as part of the same reordering of modes of justification.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-005"></a>[5](#note-ch4-005) Rather, it is to suggest that the coproduction of ‘religion’ and ‘economy’ facilitated the unacknowledged role of economics in the justification of suffering.

<a id="ch04-0010"></a>

使用经济概念来理解这个词在二十世纪中叶被发明之前的世界，还有另一种代价。正如我们将看到的，经济学的语言似乎通过未来来论述当下。它诊断当前状况，以提供关于事物走向的预测。撇开它做这件事有多成功、以及它如何导致我们误解自己与未来的关系这一问题，这种预测性、面向未来、非历史的经济推理方式还掩盖了这种思维模式的另一个后果：它帮助生产了过去。也就是说，它把当下框定为一般原则的结果——例如物质需求、<a id="page-139"></a>〔原书第139页〕自利、技术发展和增长动力——而这些原则始终具有决定作用。

There is another cost to using the concept of the economy to understand worlds prior to the invention of the term in the mid-twentieth century. As we will see, the language of economics appears to address the present in relation to the future. It diagnoses current conditions to offer predictions about where things are headed. Leaving aside the issue of how successfully it does this, and, indeed, how it causes us to misapprehend our relation to the future, the predictive, future-oriented, ahistorical mode of economic reasoning conceals another consequence of this mode of thought: it helps produce the past. That is, it frames the present as the outcome of general principles, such as material needs, <a id="page-139-en"></a>〔原书第139页〕self-interest, the development of technology, and the dynamic of growth, that are always determining.

<a id="ch04-0011"></a>

把经济这样的概念当作适用于所有时代、甚至只适用于被称为资本主义现代性的时代，会制造一种虚假的连续性。关于富足与苦难、改善与衰落、美德与自利、自然与社会、法律与政府的思想史，其令人惊讶之处之一，就是突然断裂出现得如此频繁——即使只在过去两个世纪里——早先的理解形式被抛弃。

Taking a concept like the economy as applicable to all times, or even just to the era known as capitalist modernity, creates a false continuity. One of the surprising things about the history of ideas about opulence and suffering, improvement and decline, virtue and self-interest, nature and society, and law and government is the frequency of sudden breaks, even over just the last two centuries, in which earlier forms of understanding were abandoned.

<a id="ch04-0012"></a>

这种不连续性具有特殊意义。突然的转变和中断——新的知识对象和辩护语言在其中出现——告诉我们一些关于以未来为代价生活的过程。攫取未来总是伴随着不确定性和脱位、危机的时刻。这些脱位可以部分地通过集体生活赖以被理解、组织和辩护的知识形式之突然变化来追踪。在过去一个世纪里，人们采用一套统一的“经济”和“经济的”概念语言，以及关于其治理和“增长”的语言，并把它投射回十九世纪及更早时期；这样一来，从未来抽取所固有的政治不确定性和不稳定性，就被一种观念的连续性遮掩了。

This discontinuity has a special significance. The sudden shifts and interruptions, in which a new object of knowledge and language of justification emerge, tell us something about the process of living at the expense of the future. Capturing the future is always open to uncertainty and moments of dislocation and crisis. These dislocations can be tracked, in part, in the abruptly changing forms of knowledge through which collective life is comprehended, organised, and justified. By adopting over the last century a uniform conceptual language of ‘the economy’ and ‘the economic’, and of its government and its ‘growth’, projected back onto the nineteenth century and earlier, the very political uncertainty and instability of extracting from the future is papered over in a continuity of conceptions.

<a id="ch04-0013"></a>

不仅如此，十九世纪政治经济学的写作和二十世纪经济学的写作，在力图管理这种不连续性方面发挥了决定性作用。从 1824 年 J. R. 麦克库洛赫的*《论政治经济学的兴起、进步、特殊对象与重要性》*开始，每一部关于财富、改善和物质进步问题的重要著作，都把自己呈现为对先前著作的发展、澄清和批判。先前著作被描绘成同一种关于世界的知识形式的不成熟、不完善的版本。政治经济学和经济学的教学与写作，在遮蔽思想的不连续性和生活形式的脱位方面发挥了作用。

More than that, the writing of political economy in the nineteenth century, and of economics in the twentieth century, played a decisive role in attempting to manage this discontinuity. Starting in 1824 with J. R. McCulloch’s *Discourse on the Rise, Progress, Peculiar Objects and Importance of Political Economy*, every significant text on questions of wealth, improvement, and material progress presented itself as the development, clarification, and critique of earlier writings. Earlier writings were portrayed as simply immature and imperfect versions of the same form of knowledge about the world. The teaching and writing of political economy and economics played a role in occluding the discontinuities in thought and dislocations in forms of life.

<a id="ch04-0014"></a>

需要考虑四个问题，才能把这些不连续性纳入视野，并把它们与本书其他章节所探讨的更广泛脱位联系起来。第一，在economy一词指称*这个*经济整体之前，它是如何被使用的？那些用法又如何反复变化？答案将依赖于不把过程与事物混为一谈。第二，即使可以表明经济只是在二十世纪中叶才被发明，为什么不把它的发明主要视为词汇的变化？十九世纪——如果不是更早的话——<a id="page-140"></a>〔原书第140页〕难道不是已经出现了一个独特的“经济”领域吗？这个新领域难道不是一门新科学即政治经济学的对象吗？事实上，有人会声称，“经济的”与“政治的”的分离本身，正是现代资本主义社会获取财富和安排集体生活的方式区别于较早模式之处——“经济的”标示了一种独特的资本主义权力行使方式。这里的答案将取决于不把重组世界的不完整过程与已完成的结构混淆——事实上，取决于把一种结构化效果理解为一种由其无法完成来定义的过程，而且确实由对其任何描述的不完整性来定义。第三，如果我们承认经济可能只是在二十世纪中叶才被发明，那么是什么导致了它的发明？在它被创造之前，十九世纪末和二十世纪初发生了哪些动荡？既然这一时期恰逢现代经济学学科的形成，那么该学科的对象是什么？为什么到两次世界大战之间它似乎失败了？最后，进入两次世界大战之间的岁月，经济概念最初是作为对哪些紧迫问题的回答而出现的？

There are four questions to consider to bring these discontinuities into view and connect them with wider dislocations explored in other chapters of this book. First, how was the term economy used before it referred to *the* economy and how did those uses repeatedly change? The answer will rely on not confusing a process with a thing. Second, even if it can be shown that the economy was invented only in the midtwentieth century, why not see its invention as mainly a change in vocabulary? Surely there had already emerged in the nineteenth century, <a id="page-140-en"></a>〔原书第140页〕if not earlier, a distinct sphere of ‘the economic’? Was this new sphere not the object of a new science, political economy? In fact, some would claim that the very separation of ‘the economic’ from ‘the political’ is what distinguishes the organisation of modern capitalist societies from earlier modes of acquiring wealth and ordering collective life – that ‘the economic’ designated a distinctively capitalist mode of exercising power. The answer here will depend on not confusing an incomplete process of restructuring the world with an accomplished structure – in fact on understanding a structuring effect as a process defined by the impossibility of its completion; and, indeed, by the incompleteness of any description of it. Third, if we acknowledge that the economy may have been invented only in the mid-twentieth century, what led to its invention? What upheavals in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century preceded its creation? Since that period coincides with the formation of the modern academic discipline of economics, what was the object of that discipline and why by the interwar period did it appear to have failed? Finally, moving into the interwar years, to what immediate problems did the concept of the economy first emerge as an answer?

<a id="ch04-0015"></a>

### 政治经济学已死

### Political Economy Lies Dead

<a id="ch04-0016"></a>

在*这个*经济整体被发明之前，economy一词是如何使用的？较早的政治经济学科学指的是什么？当经济学研究在十九世纪后期作为学术领域出现时，它的对象是什么？

How was the word ‘economy’ used prior to the invention of *the* economy? To what did the older science of political economy refer? And when the study of economics emerged as an academic field, in the later nineteenth century, what was its object?

<a id="ch04-0017"></a>

在二十世纪中叶之前，经济一词指的是一个过程，而不是一个事物。该词在英语中的较早用法意味着持家、家务管理或资源管理。它可以用于任何有待管理事务的实体，从人体到家庭再到大型农业庄园。正如基思·特赖布指出的，这个词暗示的是管理和保存，而不是获取和贸易。其他语言中也有同源词。例如在奥斯曼世界，从十六世纪起，土耳其语和阿拉伯语中都发展出一种关于家务管理或庄园管理的论述（*‘ilm tadbir al-manzil*，即管理家务的科学）。这门科学借鉴古典阿拉伯作家，是实践哲学的一个分支，提供“维持上层和下层阶级生计的准则”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-006"></a>[6](#note-ch4-006)到十八世纪中叶，随着法国、英格兰和<a id="page-141"></a>〔原书第141页〕普鲁士等中央集权国家发展出增强的暴力手段，得以取代西班牙、葡萄牙、荷兰和奥斯曼的较早帝国，经济一词被赋予新用途。法国、苏格兰和英格兰的作家用它来指支持和反对扩大君主在改善贸易、人口和福利方面作用的论点。最初保留了一些较早的管理含义，新的*政治*经济学话语论述君主追求人民和国家其他生产资源的“经济”或良好治理的义务。大量辩论涉及君主权利或“国家理由”是否应当优先——例如在商业治理中——还是应当受自然正义原则限制的问题。在一个相互竞争的商业国家组成的欧洲，这些国家试图为国家支持的殖民贸易垄断辩护，或扩大这种垄断，政治经济学一词被用来指十七和十八世纪关于商业问题的一组较早文本。这些文本主要关注政府在保护和改善殖民贸易方面的作用，以及这种扩大了的军事化权力所依赖的国内财政制度。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-007"></a>[7](#note-ch4-007)

Before the mid-twentieth century, the term economy referred to a process, not a thing. Earlier uses of the word in English connoted husbandry, household management, or the administering of resources. It could be used in reference to any entity with affairs to be managed, from the human body to the household and the large agrarian estate. As Keith Tribe notes, the word suggested stewardship and preservation rather than acquisition and trade. Cognate terms were found in other languages. In the Ottoman world, for example, a discourse concerned with household management or the stewardship of an estate (*‘ilm tadbir al-manzil*, or the science of managing the household) developed from the sixteenth century in both Turkish and Arabic. Drawing on classical Arabic authors, the science was a branch of practical philosophy offering ‘guidelines for the sustenance of the upper and lower classes’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-006"></a>[6](#note-ch4-006) By the mid-eighteenth century, as centralising states like France, England, and <a id="page-141-en"></a>〔原书第141页〕Prussia developed enhanced means of violence that allowed them to displace the older empires of the Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, and Ottomans, the term economy was repurposed. French, Scottish, and English writers used it to refer to arguments for and against expanding the role of the sovereign in the improvement of trade, population, and welfare. Retaining, at first, some of the older sense of stewardship, the new discourse of *political* economy addressed the duty of the sovereign to pursue the ‘economy’ or good government of the people and of other productive resources of the country. Much of the debate concerned the question of whether sovereign rights, or ‘reasons of state’, should prevail, for example in the government of commerce, or should be limited by principles of natural justice. In a Europe of competing commercial states attempting to justify or expand state-sponsored colonial trading monopolies, the term political economy was adopted to refer to an older set of texts from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries on the topic of commerce. Their main concern was the role of government in the protection and improvement of colonial trade and the fiscal regime at home on which this expanded, militarised power depended.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-007"></a>[7](#note-ch4-007)

<a id="ch04-0018"></a>

“经济”的这一部署不仅可以借助较早的持家和妥善管理观念，还可以借助中世纪和近代早期该概念在神学辩论中的用法。在基督教神学中，“神圣经济”指天意在规范尘世事务中的作用。乔治·阿甘本认为，这种神学遗产在援引天意般的“看不见的手”来规范人类商业时、或在更一般地诉诸自然法时，重新浮现。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-008"></a>[8](#note-ch4-008)一个被称为*la secte économiste*（经济学派）的法国作家学派坚持认为，自然或自然法是良好治理原则的来源，并倡导“重农主义”。这个词援引了这种天意自然的统治。

This deployment of ‘economy’ could draw upon not only earlier notions of husbandry and proper management, but also medieval and early modern uses of the concept in theological debate. In Christian theology, the ‘divine economy’ referred to the role of providence in regulating earthly affairs. This theological heritage resurfaces, Giorgio Agamben suggests, in the invocation of a providential ‘hidden hand’ in the regulation of human commerce, or in the more general appeal to laws of nature.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-008"></a>[8](#note-ch4-008) One school of French writers, the group known as *la secte économiste*, insisted that nature or natural law was the source of the principles of good government and advocated ‘physiocracy’. The term invoked the rule of this providential nature.

<a id="ch04-0019"></a>

十八世纪关于这些问题最有影响的作家亚当·斯密，是政治经济学的反对者。在*《国富论》*（1776）中，他攻击政治经济学这一观念本身，即认为政治体需要某种经济或“养生法”来改善自身。与法国重农学派一样，他主张自然法而非国家理由应当指导立法者和君主。与他们不同，他拒绝这样一种论点：立法者需要一套政治经济学“体系”，即一套应遵循的规定，以弥补自然法或自然法理学原则在纠正坏政府不良影响方面的失败。他写道，正如人体“自身包含某种未知的<a id="page-142"></a>〔原书第142页〕保存原则”，政治体中也一样，“每个人不断为改善自身境况而作出的自然努力，是一种保存原则，能够在许多方面防止和纠正政治经济学的不良影响”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-009"></a>[9](#note-ch4-009)

The most influential eighteenth-century writer on these questions, Adam Smith, was an opponent of political economy. In *The Wealth of Nations* (1776), he attacked the very idea of political economy, or the view that the political body needs some economy or ‘regimen’ for its improvement. Like the French Physiocrats, he argued that natural law rather than reasons of state should guide legislators and sovereigns. Unlike them, he rejected the argument that legislators needed a ‘system’ of political economy, meaning a set of prescriptions to follow, to compensate for the failure of natural laws, or the principles of natural jurisprudence, to correct for the ill-effects of bad government. Just as the human body ‘contains in itself some unknown principle of <a id="page-142-en"></a>〔原书第142页〕preservation’, he wrote, so in the political body ‘the natural effort which every man is continually making to better his own condition, is a principle of preservation capable of preventing and correcting, in many respects, the bad effects of a political economy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-009"></a>[9](#note-ch4-009)

<a id="ch04-0020"></a>

在*《国富论》*问世同一年，英国的一批北美殖民地宣布反抗欧洲商业垄断和殖民统治体系——这一体系正是支持和反对政治经济学辩论的焦点。到十九世纪初，正如我们在上一章所见，大西洋世界、南亚、奥斯曼帝国和欧洲的革命性变化，迫使英国、法国和其他强国开始用扩展了的国内未来攫取方式来补充通过帝国商业进行的资本化。为了应对这个变化了的世界及其所要求的新的辩护方式，政治经济学一词的含义被重新发明。政治经济学成为这样一种话语：它确立的不再是天意规定的良好治理原则，而是人类社会的世俗法则。

In the same year that *The Wealth of Nations* appeared, a group of Britain’s North American colonies declared a revolt against the system of European commercial monopolies and colonial rule that had been the focus of debates for and against political economy. By the early nineteenth century, as we saw in the last chapter, revolutionary change in the Atlantic world, in South Asia, and in the Ottoman Empire and Europe had forced Britain, France, and other powers to begin supplementing capitalisation through imperial commerce with expanded domestic modes of capturing the future. To address this changed world, and the new modes of justification it demanded, the meaning of the term political economy was reinvented. Political economy became a discourse for establishing not the providentially ordained principles of proper government but the secular laws of human society.

<a id="ch04-0021"></a>

一门世俗的社会科学似乎需要与“神圣经济”规范人类事务的观念决裂。在英格兰，盘踞于牛津和其他学术中心的圣公会建制派反对教授这样一些学说：它们不从经文、而从科学推导人的行为规则——尤其是一门把自利之恶变成公共美德、把贫穷这一基督教美德变成集体之恶的科学。为了克服这些反对意见，1825 年，富有的伦敦银行家和新教福音派传教士亨利·德拉蒙德在牛津捐资设立了英格兰第一个政治经济学教席。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-010"></a>[10](#note-ch4-010)同为福音派的理查德·惠特利在 1831 年当选该教席，提议放弃“选择得最不幸的”政治经济学一词，因为它不敬神地专注于获取财富，改而使用新名称“交换学”（catallactics），即“交换的科学”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-011"></a>[11](#note-ch4-011)

A secular science of society appeared to require a break with the idea of a ‘divine economy’ regulating human affairs. In England, the Anglican establishment, entrenched at Oxford and other centres of learning, opposed the teaching of doctrines that derived rules of human conduct not from scripture but from science – especially a science that turned the vice of self-interest into a public virtue, and the Christian virtue of poverty into a collective vice. To overcome these objections, in 1825, Henry Drummond, a wealthy London banker and Protestant evangelist, endowed the first chair in political economy in England, at Oxford.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-010"></a>[10](#note-ch4-010) A fellow evangelical, Richard Whately, elected to the new chair in 1831, proposed abandoning the ‘most unfortunately chosen’ term political economy, with its ungodly preoccupation with the acquisition of wealth, replacing it with the new name ‘catallactics’, or the ‘science of exchanges’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-011"></a>[11](#note-ch4-011)

校注：底本记惠特利于1831年当选牛津政治经济学教席。埃默里大学Pitts神学图书馆所藏惠特利书信的传记说明记为1829年当选、1831年离任。正文年份照录。 https://dia.pitts.emory.edu/archives/text/mss102.html

<a id="ch04-0022"></a>

然而，该领域的领军人物——法国作家让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊及其英国追随者约翰·斯图亚特·密尔——决定恢复政治经济学一词，作为这门新科学的名称，将其理解为社会经济科学的一个子领域。（在普鲁士，萨伊的德语译者创造了对应的术语*Nationalökonomie*（国民经济学），它开始取代十八世纪被称为官房学派的德国科学，后者曾指导财政和福利的公共管理。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-012"></a>[12](#note-ch4-012)）这些作家赞同亚当·斯密对旧政治经济学的拒绝，但在很大程度上也拒绝亚当·斯密本人。他们重新使用政治经济学这个名称，不是用来描述君主的义务，也不是<a id="page-143"></a>〔原书第143页〕自然法的原则，而是某些“社会法则”。正如密尔所写，这个词指称涉及人“作为渴望占有财富、并能够判断获取该目的之手段相对效力的存在”的法则。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-013"></a>[13](#note-ch4-013)密尔主张，这些社会法则应当取代主权权力。政治经济学被重新定义，指的是不通过君主或立法机构、而通过调节密尔所谓“社会致富”的不变规则来治理。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-014"></a>[14](#note-ch4-014)

However, the leading figures in the field, the French writer Jean-Baptiste Say and his English follower John Stuart Mill, decided to revive the term political economy as the name of the new science, understood as a subfield of the science of social economy. (In Prussia, Say’s German translator coined the parallel term *Nationalökonomie*, which began to replace the eighteenth-century German science known as cameralism, which had guided the public administration of finance and welfare.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-012"></a>[12](#note-ch4-012)) These writers agreed with Adam Smith’s rejection of the old political economy, but also largely rejected Adam Smith. They repurposed the name political economy to describe not the duties of the sovereign, nor <a id="page-143-en"></a>〔原书第143页〕the principles of natural law, but certain ‘laws of society’. The term designated the laws, as Mill wrote, that concern man ‘as a being who desires to possess wealth, and who is capable of judging of the comparative efficacy of means for obtaining that end’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-013"></a>[13](#note-ch4-013) These social laws, Mill argued, should take the place of sovereign powers. Political economy was redefined to refer to governing not through the sovereign or legislature but through the unchanging rules that regulated what Mill called ‘the enrichment of society’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-014"></a>[14](#note-ch4-014)

<a id="ch04-0023"></a>

坚持认为政治经济学的规则如今构成一门世俗科学，实际上并没有消除天意秩序的问题。假定人在追求财富时按照自利原则行动——这是一条科学原则，其运作被视为社会秩序和集体致富的来源——也许消除了对神圣之手的指称；但这种假定仍然作为一种先验真理发挥作用——也许在神的指称被省略后，其作用更加强大。对苦难和恶的辩护仍然建立于一种看不见的原则的运作之上，只不过这种原则如今用世俗科学的语言、而非神圣经文的语言来表达。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-015"></a>[15](#note-ch4-015)

The insistence that the rules of political economy now formed a secular science did not, in fact, remove the question of a providential order. The assumption that man acted on a principle of self-interest in the pursuit of wealth, a scientific principle whose operation was the source of social order and collective enrichment, may have eliminated the reference to a divine hand; but the assumption still operated as a transcendental truth – perhaps more powerfully so with the reference to the deity elided. The justification of suffering and evil still rested on the work of an unseen principle, albeit one now expressed in the language of secular science rather than sacred scripture.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-015"></a>[15](#note-ch4-015)

<a id="ch04-0024"></a>

与此同时，这种“世俗的形成”本身并不只是世俗化。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-016"></a>[16](#note-ch4-016)确立“经济”的法则，同样也是确立一种新的基督教“宗教”概念，作为政治和社会经济——理性、自利的致富——领域之外的事物的容器。经济与宗教这两个术语相互依赖，各自通过指涉对方获得新的意义和重要性。而通过宗教视角去把握的那个“领域之外”，如今同时是一个私人空间和一个地理—殖民空间。在欧洲，宗教逐渐指一个私人信仰的残余领域。在欧洲之外，随着商人和传教士把注意力从失去的北美殖民地转向北非、埃及和黎凡特的新致富机会，“宗教”概念获得了扩大了的、殖民化的力量。在伊斯兰的土地上——人们认为理性自利尚未在那里支配一切——宗教取代了世俗社会科学的位置。事实上，东方学把宗教观念发展为一个主导概念，它对于理解伊斯兰世界的重要性，正像经济正逐渐对欧洲世界具有的重要性一样。

At the same time, this ‘formation of the secular’ was not itself simply secularising.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-016"></a>[16](#note-ch4-016) Establishing the laws of ‘economy’ was equally the establishing of a new Christian concept of ‘religion’, as the container for what lay beyond the realm of political and social economy – of rational, selfinterested enrichment. The terms economy and religion were codependent, each acquiring a novel meaning and import through reference to one another. And the ‘beyond’ to be grasped through the lens of religion was now simultaneously a private and a geographical-colonial space. In Europe, religion was coming to designate a residual realm of private belief. Beyond Europe, as its merchants and missionaries turned their attention from the lost colonies of North America to the new opportunities for enrichment in North Africa, Egypt, and the Levant, the concept of ‘religion’ took on an expanded, colonising force. In the lands of Islam, where rational self-interest, it was thought, did not yet govern, religion took the place of a secular science of society. Indeed, the science of Orientalism elaborated the idea of religion into a master concept, as central to understanding the Islamic world as economy was becoming for the world of Europe.

<a id="ch04-0025"></a>

正如吉尔·阿尼贾尔所指出的，在这种基督教对东方的关切中心，矗立着“一座特定的东方城市、一片特定的东方土地，以及一种（或两种）特定的宗教”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-017"></a>[17](#note-ch4-017)在这方面值得指出的是，银行家和福音派传教士亨利·德拉蒙德在<a id="page-144"></a>〔原书第144页〕捐资设立牛津政治经济学新领域教席的同时，还创立了一个预言运动，警告基督即将第二次降临。他资助瑞士东方学家约翰·伯克哈特前往埃及和黎凡特旅行，希望让穆斯林皈依基督教。传教努力失败了——伯克哈特皈依了伊斯兰教，并按照自己的要求以穆斯林身份下葬。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-018"></a>[18](#note-ch4-018)更有希望的是，德拉蒙德的运动主张让欧洲犹太人定居巴勒斯坦，为末日做准备。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-019"></a>[19](#note-ch4-019)

At the centre of this Christian preoccupation with the Orient, as Gil Anidjar notes, there stood ‘one particular Oriental city, one particular Oriental land, and one (or two) particular religion(s)’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-017"></a>[17](#note-ch4-017) It is useful in this regard to note that the banker and evangelist Henry Drummond, <a id="page-144-en"></a>〔原书第144页〕while endowing the teaching of the new field of political economy at Oxford, simultaneously founded a prophetic movement warning of the imminent Second Coming of Christ. He funded the Swiss Orientalist Johann Burckhardt’s travels to Egypt and the Levant in the hope of converting Muslims to Christianity. The proselytizing effort failed – Burckhardt converted to Islam and was buried at his own request as a Muslim.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-018"></a>[18](#note-ch4-018) More promisingly, Drummond’s movement advocated the settlement of European Jews in Palestine, in preparation for the apocalypse.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-019"></a>[19](#note-ch4-019)

<a id="ch04-0026"></a>

如同它在十八世纪的前身，十九世纪的政治经济学科学寿命短暂——其原因部分与它和东方之间未解决的关系有关。“我们的政治经济学，”英国散文家、银行家沃尔特·白芝浩在 1876 年写道，“在公众心中已死。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-020"></a>[20](#note-ch4-020)其批评者抱怨，经济法则只是假设性的，以假定人类仅凭自私本能行动为基础，忽视了“作为负责任道德存在的人”。这门科学描述的是一个由自利支配的社会，而自利只在“欧洲某些地区，而且只是在最近”才成为至高力量，即使在那里也不是唯一的人类动机。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-021"></a>[21](#note-ch4-021)因此，它只处理“一个非常有限而独特的世界”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-022"></a>[22](#note-ch4-022)即使在欧洲，这门科学也无法充分解释工会主义、合作主义等集体安排的兴起，以及日益强大的私有土地所有权和大企业制度。“工资、利润、积累、消费、人口、济贫法、土地制度、合伙、租佃、工会、合作——这些事物涉及伟大的人类本能、需求和制度；而在大多数情况下，它们超出了单纯经济学家的能力范围。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-023"></a>[23](#note-ch4-023)

Like its eighteenth-century predecessor, the nineteenth-century science of political economy had a short life – for reasons connected in part with its unresolved relation to the Orient. ‘Our Political Economy’, wrote the English essayist and banker Walter Bagehot in 1876, ‘lies rather dead in the public mind’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-020"></a>[20](#note-ch4-020) Its critics complained that the laws of economy were hypothetical, based on assuming humans to act only on selfish instincts, ignoring ‘man as a responsible moral being’. The science described a society governed by self-interest, a paramount force ‘only in certain parts of Europe in very recent times’, and not the only human motive even there.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-021"></a>[21](#note-ch4-021) So it dealt only with ‘a very limited and peculiar world’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-022"></a>[22](#note-ch4-022) Even in Europe, the science could not adequately explain the rise of collective arrangements such as trade unionism and co-operativism, and the increasingly powerful institutions of private land ownership and large business. ‘Wages, profits, accumulation, consumption, population, poor-laws, land-systems, partnership, tenancy, trade-unions, co-operation, these are things which involve the great human instincts, wants, and institutions; and they are for the most part beyond the reach of a mere economist.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-023"></a>[23](#note-ch4-023)

<a id="ch04-0027"></a>

批评者承认，在特殊情况下，经济法则可能适用。这些例外值得注意。它们往往是“独立于一般制度和习惯”的情境，建立在“临时性”人际关系或努力以及“特殊且高度人为的过程”之上。一位作家列举了以下例子：“公开市场中的价格、通货、汇票、货币惯例、保险、贸易限制以及税收”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-024"></a>[24](#note-ch4-024)所以，这些法则可能适用于金融市场以及货币兑换、税收和保险等相关领域，也适用于“公开市场”（market overt）。后者是一个法律术语，指经授权的公共市场，一个特殊空间，商品价格在其中公开协商，因而变得可见。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-025"></a>[25](#note-ch4-025)换言之，经济规则似乎与大多数<a id="page-145"></a>〔原书第145页〕人的物质生活关系不大——与手艺、专业和大多数其他雇佣关系（其中许多受新的主仆法管辖，这些法律把违反雇佣合同和其他工人“不服从”行为定为犯罪）关系不大，与土地所有权和租佃关系不大，与企业及其客户之间的货物供应关系不大，几乎与每一种物质关系都关系不大。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-026"></a>[26](#note-ch4-026)但是，在专业化且不断扩张的金融世界，以及某些其他不寻常的交换场所中，经济原则可能适用。

The critics acknowledged that there could be exceptional circumstances where the laws of economy might apply. These exceptions are interesting to note. They were situations that tended to be ‘independent of general institutions and habits’, resting on ‘temporary’ human relations or efforts and on ‘special and highly artificial processes’. One writer gave the following list of examples: ‘Prices in market overt, currency, bills of exchange, monetary practices, insurance, restrictions on trade, [and] taxation’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-024"></a>[24](#note-ch4-024) So the laws might apply in financial markets and such related areas as currency exchange, taxation, and insurance, and in ‘market overt’, or open market. The last of these was a legal term for an authorised public market, an exceptional space in which prices for goods are openly negotiated and thus made visible.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-025"></a>[25](#note-ch4-025) In other words, the rules of economy appeared to have little relevance to the majority of <a id="page-145-en"></a>〔原书第145页〕human material life – to crafts, the professions, and most other employment relations (many of which were governed by new master and servant laws, which criminalised the breaking of employment contracts and other worker ‘disobedience’), to land ownership and tenancy, to the supply of goods among businesses and their customers, to almost every kind of material relationship.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-026"></a>[26](#note-ch4-026) But, in the specialised and expanding world of finance, along with certain other uncommon sites of exchange, the principles of economy might apply.

<a id="ch04-0028"></a>

为什么这些特殊场所和实践似乎适合经济学家的理论化？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-027"></a>[27](#note-ch4-027)英国货币市场的主要作家白芝浩这样解释：它们之所以特殊，是因为它们交易一种标准化的商品，产生可知的价格。例如，证券交易所在一个关键方面“是最简单的市场”，因为“在其中不存在商品物理品质的问题：一张 1858 年的土耳其债券与另一张一样好或一样坏；一张铁路普通股与任何其他普通股完全相同”。相比之下，在其他情况下，“每个样本的品质都不同，每个市场都需要学习判断品质，品质如此之多，等级又如此细微”。经济学家曾试图通过编制统计表来解决确定谷物（此处指小麦）等普通商品“价格”的困难。但统计表无法告诉你价格：“在一百个案例中，你可能会看到‘价格’被相互比较，仿佛它们是同一事物的价格，而事实上它们是不同事物的价格。*《公报》*的小麦均价就这样不断被比较，但它几乎从来不是任何两年中品质完全相同的小麦的价格。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-028"></a>[28](#note-ch4-028)

Why did these exceptional sites and practices seem to lend themselves to the theorising of the economists?<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-027"></a>[27](#note-ch4-027) Bagehot, the leading English writer on the money markets, explained it as follows: they are exceptional because they trade a standardised good that generates knowable prices. The stock exchange, for example, in one key respect, ‘is the simplest of markets’, because ‘there is no question in it of the physical quality of commodities: one Turkish bond of 1858 is as good or bad as another; one ordinary share in a railway exactly the same as any other ordinary share’. In other situations, by contrast, ‘each sample differs in quality, and it is a learning in each market to judge of qualities, so many are they, and so fine their gradations’. Economists had tried to solve this difficulty in determining ‘the price’ of an ordinary commodity, such as corn (wheat), by compiling tables of statistics. But tables cannot tell you the price: ‘in a hundred cases you may see “prices” compared as if they were prices of the same thing, when in fact they are prices of different things. The *Gazette* average of corn is thus compared incessantly, yet it is hardly the price of the same exact quality of corn in any two years.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-028"></a>[28](#note-ch4-028)

<a id="ch04-0029"></a>

这就是摆脱 1870 年代开始的政治经济学失败的线索，这种失败促成了一门新学科的诞生，它后来被称为“经济学”。这门学科并没有用“经济”这个宽泛术语来界定自己的对象。相反，它作为一个领域产生，放弃了把人作为“渴望占有财富的社会存在”来研究，而把焦点放在这些“特殊且高度人为的过程”上。正如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)所指出的，也如白芝浩所确认的，一个关键现象是某一种特定过程的发展：股市。

This is the clue to the way out of the failure of political economy that began in the 1870s, leading to the birth of a new discipline, which came to be called ‘economics’. The discipline did not define its object with the broad term ‘the economy’. Rather, it came into being as a field that abandoned the study of man ‘as a social being who desires to possess wealth’ and took as its focus these ‘special and highly artificial processes’. A critical phenomenon, as we noted in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001) and as Bagehot confirms, was the development of one particular process, the stock market.

<a id="ch04-0030"></a>

### 经济学的诞生

### The Birth of Economics

<a id="ch04-0031"></a>

虽然股市的特殊作用是新现象，但这并不是知识对象第一次随着一个新的、有界的、有详细记录的场所出现而转移。政治<a id="page-146"></a>〔原书第146页〕经济学家及其批评者长期以来一直依赖“有限而独特的世界”，作为他们可以描述“人为”过程、并将其转化为模型的场所，以解释人类不平等和福祉的安排，以及支配和辩护这些安排的自然法或社会法则。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-029"></a>[29](#note-ch4-029)亚当·斯密曾提出，一国财富的增长源于劳动分工的扩大。为了论证这一点，他给出的著名例子很不寻常：一家制造裁缝用大头针的工场中各道独立工序的增加。他从一系列法国记述中借用了这个例证，这些记述主要由法国科学院委托撰写，并收录于狄德罗的*《百科全书》*；每篇文本大多基于较早版本，源于当地贸易检查员的报告，回应法国君主记录和规范专门手艺知识的愿望，而制针正是其中的典型例子。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-030"></a>[30](#note-ch4-030)斯密关于操作多样性的论证，部分建立在连续报告中累积的误读之上。然而更值得注意的是，它依赖于一个范例案例的可得性。有详细记录的制针过程形成了一个人为的微观过程，斯密可以从中读出人类物质进步的全部历史。

While the unusual role of stock markets was new, this was not the first time that a shift in the object of knowledge had followed the emergence of a novel, circumscribed, and closely documented site. Political <a id="page-146-en"></a>〔原书第146页〕economists and their critics had for a long time relied upon ‘limited and peculiar worlds’ as the places where they might describe ‘artificial’ processes and translate them into models for explaining arrangements of human inequality and well-being and the laws of nature or society that governed and justified them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-029"></a>[29](#note-ch4-029) Adam Smith had proposed that the increase in a nation’s wealth arose from the increasing division of labour. To make his argument, he famously offered the unusual example of the multiplication of discrete operations in a workshop for the manufacture of dressmakers’ pins. He borrowed the illustration from a series of French accounts, commissioned mainly by the French Academy of Sciences and reproduced in Diderot’s *Encyclopédie*, each text based largely on earlier versions, originating in reports of local trade inspectors and responding to the desire of the French monarchy to document and regulate specialised craft knowledge, for which pin making served as a paradigmatic example.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-030"></a>[30](#note-ch4-030) Smith’s argument about the multiplicity of operations rested in part on an accumulation of misreadings in successive reports. However, the more interesting fact is that it relied on the availability of an exemplary case. The closely documented making of the pin formed an artificial microprocess in which Smith could read the entire history of human material progress.

<a id="ch04-0032"></a>

不如制针工场著名，但在塑造*《国富论》*论证方面更重要的，是斯密为其年轻赞助人巴克卢公爵——英国最大的地主之一——提供建议的经历，内容涉及如何“改良”其苏格兰庄园上的 434 个农场。改良的形式包括圈地、修路、排干湿地和清理高地荒原，以便通过拍卖把农场以商业方式出租。这类“改良”案例证明了斯密的一个观点——它比劳动分工对古典政治经济学的论证更为关键——即人类的改善取决于商业关系或和平交换的扩大，以及“土地应当像任何其他商品一样进入商业”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-031"></a>[31](#note-ch4-031)同样，为了证明支配和辩护劳动、投入资本与地主地租之间收益分配的法则，大卫·李嘉图借鉴了当时关于农场改良实践试验的记述——轮作、排水、施肥、畜牧——这些记述发表在手册和期刊上，其中许多被收录在 1814 年上议院关于《谷物法》的一份报告中。这些关于试验农业的报告是对拿破仑战争引发的粮食危机的回应；正如玛丽·摩根所提示的，它们形成了一个实验室，产生<a id="page-147"></a>〔原书第147页〕数字和例子，李嘉图从中构建了一个模型，通过这种新兴的“经济义论”来解释社会各阶级之间财富的不平等分配。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-032"></a>[32](#note-ch4-032)

Less famous than the pin factory, but more important in shaping the argument of *The Wealth of Nations*, was Smith’s experience in advising his young benefactor, the Duke of Buccleuch, one of the largest landowners in Britain, on measures to ‘improve’ the 434 farms on his Scottish estates. Improvement took the form of enclosure, road building, the draining of wetlands, and the clearing of upland heaths, in order to lease the farms commercially by auction. Such cases of ‘improvement’ demonstrated Smith’s point, more critical to the arguments of classical political economy than the division of labour, that human improvement depended on the increase in relations of commerce, or peaceful exchange, and that ‘land should be as much in commerce as any other goods’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-031"></a>[31](#note-ch4-031) In a similar way, to demonstrate the laws governing and justifying the distribution of gains between labour, invested capital, and landowners’ rent, David Ricardo drew on contemporary accounts of practical experiments in farm improvement – crop rotation, drainage, manuring, animal husbandry – published in pamphlets and journals, many of which were collected in a House of Lords report in 1814 on the Corn Laws. A response to the food crisis brought on by the Napoleonic wars, these reports on experimental farming, as Mary Morgan suggests, formed a laboratory generating <a id="page-147-en"></a>〔原书第147页〕numbers and examples from which Ricardo produced a model explaining, through this emergent ‘oikodicy’, the unequal distribution of wealth among the different classes of society.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-032"></a>[32](#note-ch4-032)

<a id="ch04-0033"></a>

马克思的著作提供了第三个例子，说明这种关系：关于范例场所的报告和试验的流通——往往与对当前威胁和危机的官方调查有关——与政治经济学不断变化的范式的生产之间的关系。在*《资本论》*第一卷中，马克思著名地区分了两种劳动形式，他声称这一区分是他自己的价值理解与较早政治经济学家著作之间的关键差异。尽管他的前辈把一般劳动理解为剩余价值的来源，马克思却主张，劳动如今已被转化为两种类型：特定生产任务的“具体”劳动和“抽象”劳动。蒸汽驱动的工业机器控制了人的身体，使工厂主能够细致控制每个操作的时间，并不断加速商品制造。对加速生产时间的控制提高了雇主所获剩余的相对份额，因为劳动份额被限制在工资支付之内，而工资由维持和再生产劳动者的成本决定。然而更重要的是，这种剩余如今不再以不同种类的具体劳动来衡量，而是以同质的劳动时间单位来衡量。这些单位排除了实际人类劳动的特殊性，显得不是特定个人生产活动的结果，而是一种抽象——一种由“价值”的普遍单位构成的结构。马克思把这种抽象结构或社会生活“形式”命名为“价值形式”。在资本主义生产组织下，资本对劳动的支配通过这种抽象的异己力量运作。

The work of Marx provides a third example of this relationship between the circulation of reports and experiments on exemplary sites, often in connection with official investigations into current threats and crises, and the production of the changing paradigms of political economy. In Volume 1 of *Capital*, Marx famously made a distinction between two forms of labour, the distinction that he claimed to be the key difference between his own understanding of value and the writing of earlier political economists. Although his predecessors understood labour in general to be a source of surplus value, Marx argued that labour had now been transformed into two kinds, the ‘concrete’ labour of particular productive tasks and ‘abstract’ labour. Industrial machinery, driven by steam power, had taken control of human bodies, allowing factory owners to control minutely the time of each operation and to continuously speed up the making of goods. The control of accelerating production time increased the relative share of the surplus going to employers, as labour’s share was limited to the payment of a wage, determined by the cost of sustaining and reproducing the labourer. More importantly, however, that surplus was now measured not in different kinds of concrete labour, but in homogeneous units of labour time. These units, emptied of the particularity of actual human labour, appeared not as the result of the productive activity of specific individuals but as an abstraction – a structure of universal units of ‘value’. Marx named this abstract structure, or ‘form’ of social life, the ‘value-form’. Under the capitalist organisation of production, the domination of capital over labour operated through the alien power of this abstraction.

<a id="ch04-0034"></a>

马克思关于劳动“价值”如今如何以同质时间单位衡量、并表现为一种抽象中介或结构的论述，并不是基于他自己对工厂中发生之事的观察。他从阅读大量工厂检查员和医学检查员的报告中得出这一论述，这些人的工作是旨在减轻工业劳动中虐待现象的自由主义改革的成果。改革者急于强调对时间和劳动控制的系统化、无情的增长。因此，“抽象性”部分来自对工厂生活的规范、记录、再现和复制性记述。只有极少数人口在工厂工作。并非所有人都遵循报告以及马克思所依赖的其他资料来源——例如查尔斯·巴贝奇关于<a id="page-148"></a>〔原书第148页〕机械化生产组织的研究*《论机器和制造业的经济》*（1832），以及安德鲁·尤尔的*《制造业哲学》*（副标题为*《工厂制度的科学、道德和商业经济阐述》*）——所描述的逻辑。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-033"></a>[33](#note-ch4-033)我们从当时的记述中知道，工厂劳动往往与这些关于“制造业经济”或“工厂制度经济”的描述大不相同（同样，“经济”在这里指有效率的组织）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-034"></a>[34](#note-ch4-034)但测量、记录、报告和引用工作促成了抽象性的生产。像斯密的模范制针工场以及他和李嘉图的试验农场一样，工厂提供了一个特殊而不寻常的场所，一门科学可以从中发展出来——在这个例子中，抽象化本身不仅成为一种脑力练习，而且成为真实过程，成为社会支配日常机制的一部分。

Marx’s account of how the ‘value’ of labour was now measured in homogeneous units of time, appearing as an abstract mediation or structure, was not based on his own observations of what happened in factories. He drew it from reading the proliferating reports of factory inspectors and medical examiners, whose work was the result of liberal reforms intended to ameliorate the abuse of industrial labour. The reformers were keen to emphasise the systematic and relentless increase in the control of time and labour. So, the ‘abstractness’ was partly a result of the regulating, recording, representing, and replicating accounts of factory life. Only a very small part of the population worked in factories. Not all followed the logic described by the reports and by other sources on which Marx relied, such as Charles Babbage’s study of <a id="page-148-en"></a>〔原书第148页〕the organisation of mechanised production, *On the Economy of Machinery and Manufactures* (1832), and Andrew Ure’s *The Philosophy of Manufactures* (subtitled *An Exposition of the Scientific, Moral and Commercial Economy of the Factory System*).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-033"></a>[33](#note-ch4-033) We know from contemporary accounts that factory labour was often very different from these descriptions of the ‘economy of manufactures’ or the ‘economy of the factory system’ (again, ‘economy’ refers here to efficient organisation).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-034"></a>[34](#note-ch4-034) But the work of measuring, recording, reporting, and referencing contributed to the production of abstractness.
