Like Smith’s model pin workshop and his and Ricardo’s experimental farms, the factory provided an exceptional and unusual site from which a science could be developed – in this case, one in which abstracting itself became not just a mental exercise but a real process, part of the daily mechanism of social domination.

<a id="ch04-0035"></a>

此后政治经济学的消亡和经济学的诞生，也可以置于这种试验和抽象场所不断转移的序列中。正如我们不久将看到的，这一转变使马克思本人在只出版了*《资本论》*第一卷——重点论述工厂生产——之后，在很大程度上放弃了写作政治经济学批判的计划。在十九世纪的最后三分之一时段，另一个范例场所成为观察和关注的焦点，也成为新解释范式的来源。证券交易所和其他货币市场——投资者和投机者在那里以越来越大的数量和频率交易股票、货币和汇票——以类似但更集中的方式运作，创造了另一种抽象形式，或许还可以说，另一种支配方式。它们也允许另一种科学的可能：新兴经济学学术学科的边际效用理论。新学科放弃了研究人类的伟大“需求和制度”，转而研究“价格”，认为价格代表人类需求的规模以及相应供应的商品数量。正如白芝浩所指出的，金融市场的安排产生了商品的统一“品质”、可知价格的同步运动，以及买卖双方的简单识别，每一方都等同于所有其他方。正是股市，而不是工厂受管制的劳动过程，产生了经济学如今可以据以建立的简化、数字化组织的世界。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-035"></a>[35](#note-ch4-035)

The subsequent demise of political economy and the birth of economics can also be situated in this sequence of shifting locations of experimentation and abstraction. As we will see shortly, the shift caused Marx himself to largely abandon the project of writing a critique of political economy, after publishing just the first volume of *Capital*, with its focus on factory production. In the last third of the nineteenth century, another exemplary site became the focus of observation and concern, and the source of a new paradigm of explanation. The stock exchanges and other money markets, where investors and speculators traded in shares, currencies, and bills of exchange at an increasing volume and frequency, operated in a similar yet more focused way, creating another form of abstraction – and, we might add, another mode of domination. They too allowed the possibility of a different science: the marginal utility theory of the emergent academic discipline of economics. Abandoning the study of the great human ‘wants and institutions’, the new discipline substituted the study of ‘prices’, taking them to represent the scale of human wants and the volume of commodities supplied in response. A financial market was arranged to produce, as Bagehot noted, the uniform ‘quality’ of the commodity, a synchronised movement of knowable prices, and the simple identification of buyers and sellers, each one equivalent to all the others. It was the stock market, rather than the regulated labour process of the factory, that generated the simplified, numerically organised world on which economics could now be built.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-035"></a>[35](#note-ch4-035)

<a id="ch04-0036"></a>

科学知识的新微观场所也产生了确立这种知识的更大需要。这种需要源于一个事实：<a id="page-149"></a>〔原书第149页〕股票和商品交易所不仅产生了可计量的价格体系，作为一种“实在抽象”，而且产生了反复危机的模式。这些危机与价格体系所建立于其上的过程有关——欧洲日益加紧地试图从非欧洲世界获利并重组它。那个世界开始像幽灵一样出现：一个新科学几乎无法把握的形象，一个既要求又逃避其理解的未知者。

The new microsite of scientific knowledge also created an increased need to establish such knowledge. The need arose from the fact that <a id="page-149-en"></a>〔原书第149页〕stock and commodity exchanges produced not just a measurable price system, as a ‘real abstraction’, but a pattern of repeated crisis. The crises were connected with the process on which the price system was constructed – Europe’s intensifying attempt to profit from and reorganise the non-European world. That world began to appear as a spectre: a figure just beyond the grasp of the new science, the unknown that both demanded and escaped its understanding.

<a id="ch04-0037"></a>

### 半成形与半文明

### Half-Finished and Half-Civilised

<a id="ch04-0038"></a>

因此，还有另一个原因，使股市突然似乎成为理想场所，不仅可以理解通过价格形成而运作的致富机制，还可以理解影响这一过程的危机。货币市场是把价格现象与似乎最应对其不稳定性负责的环境联系起来的场所：正如前几章所指出的，“帝国主义”的新权力。

There was thus a further reason why the stock markets suddenly seemed an ideal place to understand, not just the working of mechanisms of enrichment, through the formation of prices, but the crises affecting this process. The money markets were the site that connected the phenomenon of prices to the circumstances that seemed most responsible for their instability: the new powers, as noted in previous chapters, of ‘imperialism’.

<a id="ch04-0039"></a>

到 1870 年代中期，货币市场陷入动荡。1873 年恐慌是一系列似乎几乎每十年发生一次的金融危机中最严重的一次。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-036"></a>[36](#note-ch4-036)这场危机由北美铁路项目失败以及芝加哥、柏林和维也纳投机性城市开发的崩溃触发（在维也纳，1873 年世界博览会未能迎来预期人潮，导致房地产价值暴跌），摧毁了北美和欧洲的贸易和企业，导致印度卢比价值暴跌，导致伊斯坦布尔和开罗的奥斯曼政府破产（使白芝浩所说的“1858 年土耳其债券”以及为支持它而创造的所有后续贷款价值尽失），并导致英国征服和占领埃及。

By the mid-1870s, the money markets were in turmoil. The Panic of 1873 was the worst in a series of financial crises that seemed to occur almost every decade.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-036"></a>[36](#note-ch4-036) Triggered by the failure of North American railway ventures and the collapse of speculative urban development in Chicago, Berlin, and Vienna (where the absence of anticipated crowds at the 1873 World Exhibition caused property values to crash), the crisis destroyed trade and businesses across North America and Europe, caused the value of the Indian rupee to collapse, and led to the bankruptcy of the Ottoman governments in Istanbul and Cairo (destroying the value of Bagehot’s ‘Turkish bond of 1858’ and all the subsequent loans created in its support) and to the British conquest and occupation of Egypt.

<a id="ch04-0040"></a>

经济学与帝国危机之间的联系，可以在沃尔特·白芝浩的著作中看到。白芝浩写道，有必要更好地理解“商业的事实”，还要理解“大商业”的事实，尤其是与当时“新问题”相关的事实。他集中讨论了两个这样的问题。一是如何理解反复出现的全球金融衰退——似乎以周期性方式折磨货币市场的恐慌和危机。一些作家曾提出对周期性的气象学解释。似乎“太阳状态的变化”遵循规律周期，可以与“地球的总体生产力”联系起来。白芝浩<a id="page-150"></a>〔原书第150页〕问道，由此产生的“产业效率的周期性变化”会对商业产生什么影响？那么，太阳变化影响整个地球，因而与“货币市场困难时期的规律性重现有很大关系”，这似乎是可能的，是否属实？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-037"></a>[37](#note-ch4-037)另一个问题是如何理解英国首次向欧洲以外政府提供的大额贷款的影响。正当奥斯曼和埃及政府在向其提供信用的欧洲银行家面前宣告破产时，他使用了这种帝国金融所依赖的种族优越论语言，指出“我们向半成形和半文明的共同体强加不可估量的巨款”。这些共同体几乎可以获得任何数额的信用货币。他补充说，“从来没有初生的文明，也从来没有停滞的文明，曾经拥有这种便利”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-038"></a>[38](#note-ch4-038)

The connection between economics and imperial crisis can be seen in the writings of Walter Bagehot. There was a need, Bagehot wrote, to better understand not just ‘the facts of commerce’, but those of ‘the great commerce’, especially in relation to the ‘new problems’ of the time. He focused on two such problems. One was how to understand the repeated, worldwide financial downturns – the panics and crises that seemed to afflict the money markets in cyclical fashion. Some writers had proposed a meteorological explanation for the cycles. It appeared that ‘changes in the state of the sun’ followed regular cycles that could be linked to ‘the general productiveness of the earth’. What effect, Bagehot <a id="page-150-en"></a>〔原书第150页〕asked, would the resulting ‘cyclical variation in the efficiency of industry’ have upon commerce? Was it therefore true, as seemed likely, that the solar variations, affecting the whole Earth, ‘have much to do with the regular recurrence of difficult times in the money market’?<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-037"></a>[37](#note-ch4-037) The other problem was how to understand the effect of the large loans England had been making for the first time to governments outside Europe. At the moment when the Ottoman and Egyptian governments were declared bankrupt before the European bankers who had extended credit to them, using the language of racial superiority on which such imperial finance relied, he noted how ‘we press upon half-finished and half-civilised communities incalculable sums’. These communities had been offered credit money in almost any amount. ‘No incipient and no arrested civilisations’, he added, ‘ever had this facility before.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-038"></a>[38](#note-ch4-038)

<a id="ch04-0041"></a>

这两个需要经济科学来解答的新问题，都源于金融市场。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-039"></a>[39](#note-ch4-039)两者都涉及欧洲与其正在殖民的世界之间的新金融关系。虽然金融不稳定性与帝国主义不稳定性之间的这种联系，在向所谓“半文明”共同体提供银行贷款的案例中十分明显，但如今看来，这种联系也可以解释信用周期。对信用周期性充裕和稀缺最有希望的解释，基于农业——财富的主要来源——与气候之间的关系。气象周期或许可以解释金融危机重现的想法，从十九世纪初起就有人讨论。有人提出，天气变化——也许与太阳活动周期有关——会引起谷物和其他作物价格波动，导致信用可得性和成本的周期。但人们没有发现任何决定性关系。然而在 1870 年代，经济学家威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯提出了可能解释这种关系的统计证据。确实，太阳黑子与欧洲谷物和其他主粮作物价格之间没有相关性。杰文斯提出，这是因为“我们气候的条件太复杂了”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-040"></a>[40](#note-ch4-040)但信用市场的巨大扰动，可能是欧洲与热带地区贸易扩大所造成的问题。在热带国家，天气逐季变化较小，因此气候不那么复杂。这种稳定性一方面促进了长期信用的创造，另一方面也使这种信用容易受到长期周期性变化的影响，例如与太阳黑子有关的变化。印度贸易大概就是这种情况，“热带非洲、美洲、<a id="page-151"></a>〔原书第151页〕西印度群岛，甚至黎凡特，都很可能受到同一种气象影响”。杰文斯声称，太阳黑子导致热带每十年一次的饥荒，因此“正是那些对世界这些地区贸易规模最大、*并向其客户提供长期信用*的国家，受这些危机之害最深”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-041"></a>[41](#note-ch4-041)

Both examples of the new problems for which economic science was needed arose from financial markets.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-039"></a>[39](#note-ch4-039) And both concerned the new financial relations between Europe and the world it was colonising. While this connection between the instability of finance and the instability of imperialism was clear in the case of bank loans extended to so-called ‘half-civilised’ communities, the connection could also, it now seemed, account for credit cycles. The most promising explanation for the cyclical abundance and scarcity of credit was based on the relationship between agriculture – the main source of wealth – and climate. The idea that meteorological cycles might explain the recurrence of financial crises had been discussed since the early nineteenth century. Variations in weather, perhaps associated with cycles of solar activity, it had been proposed, would cause fluctuations in the price of grain and other crops, leading to cycles in the availability and cost of credit. But no conclusive relation had been found. In the 1870s, however, the economist William Stanley Jevons developed statistical evidence that might explain this relationship. It was true that there was no correlation between sunspots and the price of grain and other staple crops in Europe. This was because, Jevons suggested, ‘the conditions of our climate are too complicated’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-040"></a>[40](#note-ch4-040) But large disturbances in the credit market might be a problem caused by Europe’s expanded trade with the tropics. In tropical countries the weather was less variable from season to season and the climate therefore less complicated. This stability on the one hand facilitated the creation of long-term credit. On the other, it made that credit vulnerable to long-term cyclical variations, such as those associated with sunspots. This was probably the case with the Indian trade, and ‘it is quite possible that tropical Africa, America, the <a id="page-151-en"></a>〔原书第151页〕West Indies, and even the Levant are affected by the same meteorological influence’. Jevons claimed that sunspots caused decennial famines in the tropics, so ‘it is the nations which trade most largely to those parts of the world, *and which give long credits to their customers*, which suffer most from these crises’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-041"></a>[41](#note-ch4-041)

<a id="ch04-0042"></a>

如果股市把金融不稳定与帝国主义联系起来，那么会产生一个奇怪的后果。当政治经济学在欧洲似乎已经死去时，它在非欧洲世界却突然复活，并被赋予新用途。这种重新利用促成了资本的另一种托词，即“帝国的托词”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-042"></a>[42](#note-ch4-042)如果经济学新科学诞生于货币市场的模型空间，那么政治经济学的旧科学也在同一时期带着新目的获得重生。它正成为一种治理这些金融过程受害者的手段，即那些被白芝浩贬称为半成形和半文明的人。到 1880 年代，政治经济学说正被克罗默勋爵等人物复兴为殖民治理的工具；克罗默是英国驻埃及总督，而英国在金融危机把该国统治者推向破产之后占领了埃及。随后发生的事可以被称为“殖民唯物主义”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-043"></a>[43](#note-ch4-043)殖民统治中的操作性区分不是经济与政治之间的区分，而是物质与道德之间的区分；这两个词不是指社会世界的不同领域，而是指对人类行动的治理。在克罗默看来，埃及农民和所有人一样，天生自利，因此有能力支配自己的*物质*改善。但在其*道德*生活中，他落后了，无法为更高层次的共同善而努力。个人自利与道德落后之间的这一区分，为殖民支配的巨大不公提供了辩护，即经济义论。克罗默在两卷本埃及殖民行政记述中，只以节俭这一常规含义使用 economy 一词。他写道，在英国占领该国的早期，“必须实行最大程度的节俭”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-044"></a>[44](#note-ch4-044)他只用过几次 economic 一词，而且不是指社会世界的一个领域，而是指治理的规则和问题。他长达 1,200 页的文本触及殖民统治声称带来的物质和道德改善的方方面面，但使用 economy 一词时除了节俭外没有其他含义，使用 economic 时则不是描述物质生活，而是描述政策的道德法则或原则。殖民埃及从来与一个叫做“经济”的对象或“<a id="page-152"></a>〔原书第152页〕经济的”领域无关。这种特定的辩护语言，只有在殖民秩序崩溃时才会出现。

If the stock markets connected financial instability to imperialism, there was a curious consequence. While, in Europe, political economy seemed to lie dead, in the non-European world, it was suddenly brought back to life and repurposed. The repurposing served the creation of another of the alibis of capital: the ‘alibi of empire’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-042"></a>[42](#note-ch4-042) If the new science of economics was born out of the model space of the money markets, the old science of political economy was reborn at the same time with a new purpose. It was becoming a means to govern the victims of these financial processes, those disparaged by Bagehot as half-finished and half-civilised. By the 1880s, the doctrines of political economy were being revived as an instrument of colonial government by men like Lord Cromer, the British viceroy in Egypt, the country Britain had occupied after the crisis in the financial markets pushed its ruler into bankruptcy. What followed might be labelled ‘colonial materialism’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-043"></a>[43](#note-ch4-043) The operative distinction in colonial rule was not between the economic and the political, but between the material and the moral, words that refer not to discrete domains of the social world but to the government of human action. The Egyptian peasant, in Cromer’s view, like all human beings, was naturally self-interested, and therefore capable of governing his own *material* improvement. But in his *moral* life he was backwards, incapable of working towards a higher, common good. This distinction between individual self-interest and moral backwardness provided the justification, the oikodicy, for the great injustice of colonial domination. In the two-volume account of his colonial administration of Egypt, Cromer used the word economy only with the conventional meaning of parsimony. In the early years of the British occupation of the country, he wrote, ‘the utmost economy had to be practised’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-044"></a>[44](#note-ch4-044) He used the word ‘economic’ only a handful of times, and in reference not to a realm of the social world but to rules and questions of government. His 1,200-page text touched on every aspect of the material and moral improvement that colonial rule claimed to bring but used the word economy with no meaning other than frugality, and the word economic to characterise not material life but the moral laws or principles of policy. Colonising Egypt was never concerned with an object called ‘the economy’ or a realm of ‘the <a id="page-152-en"></a>〔原书第152页〕economic’. That particular language of justification would emerge only when the colonial order was collapsing.

<a id="ch04-0043"></a>

在随后考察一个世纪后新自由主义经济思想的章节中，我们将看到新自由主义学说如何在全球南方获得第二重幽灵般的生命，在北方已在很大程度上失去信誉之后，仍作为一种僵尸思想徘徊许久。同样，古老、古典的政治经济学也获得了幽灵般的来世——在埃及，用来治理当地人。在这种情况下，殖民地不是新科学的实验室，而是一门垂死科学的幽灵家园。

In a subsequent chapter examining neoliberal economic thought a century later, we will see how the doctrines of neoliberalism acquired a second, spectral life in the Global South, lingering as a kind of zombie thought long after they had been largely discredited in the north. So too the old, classical political economy acquired a ghostly afterlife – in Egypt, to govern natives. The colonies were not in this case a laboratory for a new science, but a spectral home for a dying science.

<a id="ch04-0044"></a>

与此同时，除了用于日益无关紧要的政治经济学科学名称之外，“经济”一词在英语中继续主要在一种更狭窄的意义上使用。它仍与持家或家务的原始含义相关，但范围更窄，指审慎使用资源或有效率地管理一项事业。马克思*《资本论》*中少数使用“经济”一词的地方之一，出现在一段关于木材生长的文字中，引用了德国一本关于土地经济的便览。该便览作者指出，林业“为了实现其常规经营，需要比谷物种植更大的面积”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-045"></a>[45](#note-ch4-045)更常见的是，这个词不仅指有效管理，还指节省成本或节俭，例如马克思在后来成为*《资本论》*第三卷的手稿中所说，“在空间，因而也在建筑物等方面作出的大量*节省*，结果把工人挤在狭小的环境中”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-046"></a>[46](#note-ch4-046)

Meanwhile, apart from its use in the title of the increasingly irrelevant science of political economy, the word ‘economy’ continued to be used in English mainly in a more restricted sense. Still associated with the original meaning of husbandry or householding, but narrower in scope, the word denoted the prudent use of resources, or the efficient management of an undertaking. One of the rare uses of the term ‘economy’ in Marx’s *Capital* occurs in a passage on the growing of timber, quoting from a German handbook on land economy. Forestry, the author of the handbook notes, ‘requires for its regular economy a larger area than grain culture’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-045"></a>[45](#note-ch4-045) More frequently, the word referred not just to efficient administration but to cost-saving or frugality, as when Marx remarked in the manuscript that later became volume three of *Capital* ‘how much *economy* on space and therefore on buildings, etc., results in crowding workers together in cramped conditions’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-046"></a>[46](#note-ch4-046)

<a id="ch04-0045"></a>

正如经济一词持家意义上的原始含义先前曾被借用来指更广泛意义上的良好治理，节俭意义上的经济不仅可以用于具体的审慎和效率行为，还可以用来描述一般政府政策。它指一种更高效、更审慎地使用资源的纲领。

Just as the original meaning of the word economy in the sense of husbandry had previously been borrowed to denote the wider idea of good government, economy in the sense of frugality could be used not just for specific acts of prudence and efficiency but to describe government policy in general. It designated a programme of more efficient and prudent use of resources.

<a id="ch04-0046"></a>

当这种政策在国内被倡导为帝国主义的替代方案时，它可能被称为“*国民*经济”。英国批评克罗默等帝国主义者的主要论者、社会主义作家 J. A. 霍布森这样使用该短语，以推动国内改善纲领。在 1902 年出版的经典论著*《帝国主义》*中，霍布森主张，帝国强国外部获取海外领土和资源的驱动力——通常涉及战争——可以用国内更有效地使用资源来取代，办法是“用对国民资源的集约经营替代粗放经营”。他总结说，“这样一种国民经济不仅会摧毁战争的主要动机，还会深刻改变<a id="page-153"></a>〔原书第153页〕各国政府从事的工业斗争”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-047"></a>[47](#note-ch4-047)在这类著作中，经济一词和“国民经济”短语指的是对物质资源的有效管理，而不是被管理的对象。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-048"></a>[48](#note-ch4-048)这种用法不应与二十世纪中叶以后用“*这个*国民经济整体”（the national economy）指称这样一种对象的做法相混淆。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-049"></a>[49](#note-ch4-049)前一种用法指一个过程，而不是一个事物。

When advocated at home as an alternative to imperialism, such a policy might now be called ‘*national* economy’. The leading English critic of imperialists like Cromer, the socialist writer J. A. Hobson, used the phrase in this way to promote a programme of domestic improvement. In his classic essay *Imperialism*, published in 1902, Hobson argued that the external drive by imperial powers to acquire territory and resources overseas, usually involving warfare, could be replaced with the more efficient use of resources at home, by ‘substituting an intensive for an extensive economy of national resources’. He concluded that ‘such a national economy would not only destroy the chief motives of war, it would profoundly modify the industrial struggle in which <a id="page-153-en"></a>〔原书第153页〕governments engage’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-047"></a>[47](#note-ch4-047) The word economy, and the phrase national economy, refer in such writings to an efficient administering of material resources, not to the object being administered.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-048"></a>[48](#note-ch4-048) This usage should not be confused with the later deployment of the phrase ‘*the* national economy’, from the mid-twentieth century, to denote such an object.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-049"></a>[49](#note-ch4-049) The wording refers to a process, not a thing.

<a id="ch04-0047"></a>

### 经济化

### Economisation

<a id="ch04-0048"></a>

这类论点忽视了二十世纪经济发明的意义，后面各章将对此进行探讨。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-050"></a>[50](#note-ch4-050)正如我们将看到的，经济“不只是”一种再现，而是一种复杂装置，用来通过其未来治理人口（[第五章](#ch05-0001)），并管理那种未来占有借以进行的种种托词（[第八章](#ch08-0001)）。然而，这些论点也误解了先前发生的事情。这类论点背后是一种关于资本主义社会或资本化社会如何运作的更大观点。正如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所指出的，大多数关于资本主义的历史叙述是演化论的：它们把资本主义的出现归因于商业关系、生产方式、军事力量或人类占有欲的逐渐发展。但另一条源自马克思的思想线索，把资本主义的诞生定位于一种更具断裂性的变化：一个剥夺过程，最早见于近代早期英国，它创造了一个庞大的无土地、无财产人口，这些人依赖向如今控制其生存所需手段的人出卖劳动力。在这种分析中，一旦大多数人依靠向他人出卖劳动力为生，一种新的政治秩序就出现了，它建立在不同的强制安排之上。大多数人别无选择，只能把劳动力卖给有手段购买劳动力的人，后者不仅获得劳动的使用和控制权，还获得劳动产品的所有权。这种重组创造了一种不同的治理人口的方法。以前，有权势者只有在商品生产出来*之后*才能获得对剩余财富的控制。这种获取依赖于建立人身依附关系，而这种关系需要社会辩护、宗教和司法特权以及强制权力。如今，他们通过商品生产的方式本身获取剩余。生产装置——无论是煤矿、麦田还是棉纺厂——成为私有化场所，有权势者在那里组织控制并攫取剩余。

Such arguments overlook the significance, to be explored in subsequent chapters, of the twentieth-century invention of the economy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-050"></a>[50](#note-ch4-050) The economy, as we will see, was not ‘just’ a representation, but a complex device for governing a population through its future ([chapter 5](#ch05-0001)), and for managing the alibis under which the appropriation of that future proceeded ([chapter 8](#ch08-0001)). However, they also misunderstand what came before. Underlying such arguments is a larger view of the way a capitalist, or capitalising, society works. As we noted in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), most historical accounts of capitalism are evolutionary: they attribute its emergence to the gradual development of commercial relations, methods of production, military power, or human acquisitiveness. But a different line of thought, drawn from Marx, locates the birth of capitalism in a more disjunctive change: a process of dispossession, first seen in early modern Britain, that created a large landless and propertyless population dependent on selling its labour to those who now controlled the means they required to survive. Once the majority of people depended for their existence on the sale of their labour to others, in this analysis, a new political order emerged, based on a different arrangement of coercion. The majority had no choice but to sell their labour to those with the means to buy it, and the latter acquired not only the use and control of the labour but ownership of what it produced. This reorganisation created a different method of governing populations. Previously, the powerful acquired control of surplus wealth only *after* goods had been produced. Its acquisition relied upon creating relations of personal dependence that required social justifications, religious and judicial prerogatives, and coercive powers. Now they acquired the surplus through the very way goods were produced. The apparatus of production, whether a coalmine, a corn field, or a cotton mill, became the privatised site where the powerful organised control and captured the surplus.

<a id="ch04-0049"></a>

<a id="page-154"></a>〔原书第154页〕让我们暂且搁置这样一个事实：较早形式的商业社会往往允许商人和统治者通过债务和税收义务工具来安排和治理生产。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-051"></a>[51](#note-ch4-051)也让我们暂且搁置另一个事实：今天的大多数人并不受雇于物质生产，而消费、债务、治安和政治强制等形式是剩余攫取装置的重要方面（马克思本人也意识到这一点）。让我们把关于经济及其增长如何成为治理许多人口的最有力抽象之一的解释，推迟到下一章。相反，我们继续关注与工业生产兴起相关的剥夺和强制形式；对这一变化有时会作这样一种简单描述：攫取装置已从政治领域转移到经济领域。这种表述往往意味着政治和经济是超历史范畴，描述所有社会的功能划分。更好的说法或许是：这种安排剩余攫取的方法采取了经济与政治分离这一历史特定形式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-052"></a>[52](#note-ch4-052)这就是如下论点所指的意思：在资本主义现代性中，经济成为一种*实在*抽象。它不仅是思想中新兴的范畴，而且是一种在集体世界组织中得到实现的抽象。它如何实现？关键要素在于人的劳动成为一种可以买卖的商品。用格奥尔格·卢卡奇的话说，资本主义下的劳动“成为社会的一个范畴，决定性地影响着由此出现的社会中事物和人的客观形式”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-053"></a>[53](#note-ch4-053)这种劳动生产的产品不是生产者的财产，而是购买劳动使用权者所拥有的商品。一系列私法安排和市场机制——买卖劳动的合同，以及授予个人对土地、劳动力或商品绝对控制权而不论由谁耕种、培育或创造的产权规则——使剩余攫取成为受财产法和市场交换规则管辖的私人安排。

<a id="page-154-en"></a>〔原书第154页〕Let us leave aside for now the fact that older forms of commercial society often allowed merchants and rulers, through the instruments of debt and tax obligation, to arrange and govern production.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-051"></a>[51](#note-ch4-051) Let us also leave aside for now the fact that most people today are not employed in material production, and that forms of consumption, debt, policing, and political coercion are significant aspects of the apparatuses for the capture of surplus (as Marx himself was aware). Let us hold off, until the next chapter, an explanation of how the economy and its growth became among the most powerful abstractions through which many populations are governed. Staying, instead, with the forms of dispossession and coercion associated with the rise of industrial production, a simple way this change is sometimes described is to say that the apparatus of capture had been relocated from the political realm to the economic. That formulation often implies that the political and the economic are trans-historical categories describing the functional divisions of all societies. A better approach might be to say that this method of arranging the capture of surplus took the historically specific form of a separation of the economic from the political.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-052"></a>[52](#note-ch4-052) This is what is meant by the argument that, in capitalist modernity, the economic becomes a *real* abstraction. It is not just an emergent category of thought, but an abstraction that is realised in the organising of the collective world. How is it realised? The key element is that human labour becomes a commodity that can be bought and sold. Labour under capitalism, in the words of Georg Lukács, ‘becomes a category of society influencing decisively the objective form of things and people in the society thus emerging’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-053"></a>[53](#note-ch4-053) The goods produced by that labour are not the property of the producer, but commodities owned by whoever purchases the use of the labour. A series of private legal arrangements and market mechanisms – contracts to buy and sell labour and rules of ownership that award an individual absolute control over land, labour power, or goods irrespective of who cultivates, nurtures, or creates them – render the capture of surplus a private arrangement governed by laws of property and rules of market exchange.

<a id="ch04-0050"></a>

然而，把这个过程简单描述为“经济的”（以及“劳动”）作为一个实在抽象的创造，似乎简化了实际发生的事。这种抽象化并不是轻易、瞬间或孤立于它所依赖的其他过程而发生的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-054"></a>[54](#note-ch4-054)我们可以再次提到莫伊舍·波斯通的著作（见[第三章](#ch03-0001)）。波斯通超越卢卡奇，对实在抽象作出了有力分析。如果以时间纪律为基础的工厂生产把劳动变成一种实在抽象，其意义就在于产生“价值”的效果，即按<a id="page-155"></a>〔原书第155页〕统一的劳动时间单位来计算。“价值”，波斯通认为，成为似乎决定财富如何分配的抽象尺度。这种尺度、这种抽象使我们误解不平等的来源，并作为一种支配结构运作。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-055"></a>[55](#note-ch4-055)与政治支配的公开制度不同，“经济的”范畴即价值，通过物质生活的日常组织运作。在这个意义上，资本主义依赖于政治与经济的“实在”分离。

However, to describe this process simply as the creation of ‘the economic’ (and of ‘labour’) as a real abstraction seems to simplify what occurs. Such abstracting does not happen easily, instantly, or in isolation from other processes on which it depends.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-054"></a>[54](#note-ch4-054) We can refer again to the work of Moishe Postone (see [chapter 3](#ch03-0001)). Moving beyond Lukács, Postone develops a powerful analysis of real abstraction. If factory production, based on time discipline, turns labour into a real abstraction, its significance lies in producing the effect of ‘value’, counted in <a id="page-155-en"></a>〔原书第155页〕uniform units of labour time. ‘Value’, Postone argues, becomes the abstract measure that appears to determine how wealth is distributed. Causing us to misapprehend the source of inequality, this measure, this abstraction, operates as a structure of domination.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-055"></a>[55](#note-ch4-055) Unlike the overt institutions of political domination, an ‘economic’ category, value, operates through the mundane organisation of material life. In this sense, capitalism depends upon the ‘real’ separation of the political from the economic.

<a id="ch04-0051"></a>

我们可以接受这一分析，但仍然存在分歧。波斯通描述的是一种抽象，而不是抽象化的过程。生产这种抽象与其说是一次性的历史转变，不如说是每日的重演。要使某种劳动用途或某件商品获得“价值”，并作为“商业”或“市场”现象运作，它必须与其他关系和纠葛分离，例如持家、相互义务、人身依附、国家权力和身体强制。此外，正如卡罗琳·哈丁所提示的，产生支配性抽象的攫取装置，不仅通过工资支付、也通过其他领域运作，例如通过债务关系以及管理自身未来“风险”的强制。虽然这种“通过债务支配”今天可能显得更加普遍，但正如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所论证的，负债的力量内在于工资的运作之中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-056"></a>[56](#note-ch4-056)

We can follow this analysis but still be left with a disagreement. Postone describes an abstraction, but not the process of abstracting. Producing the abstraction is not so much a singular historical transformation as a daily reoccurrence. For a particular use of labour or item of merchandise to acquire ‘value’ and operate as a ‘commercial’ or ‘market’ phenomenon, it must be separated from other ties and entanglements, such as those of householding, mutual obligation, personal dependence, state power, and physical coercion. Furthermore, as Carolyn Hardin suggests, the apparatuses of capture producing governing abstractions operate through spheres other than the payment of the wage, for example through relations of debt and the compulsion to manage ‘risks’ to one’s future. While such ‘governing by debt’ may appear more prevalent today, the force of indebtedness was, as we argued in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), internal to the operation of the wage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-056"></a>[56](#note-ch4-056)

<a id="ch04-0052"></a>

我们可以在另一位学者的著作中看到把握“经济的”这一困难；这位学者更多地与“经济的”在十九世纪作为一个独立领域出现的观念联系在一起，即卡尔·波兰尼。很长一段时间里，波兰尼的经典著作*《大转型》*（1944）被误读为一部关于十九世纪“经济”从社会中脱嵌的记述。这本书并没有这样说；它的论证构思于 1930 年代，当时“经济”观念尚未真正出现。它或许促成了这种观念的出现，尤其是在 1950 年代以后，波兰尼及其追随者用那个十年新颖的语言重述其论证，把它变成了一部关于十九世纪“经济”脱嵌的记述。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-057"></a>[57](#note-ch4-057)这本书本身是一个关于“市场关系”或“市场社会”的论证，描述十九世纪的“市场”如何被构造成一种从互惠、义务和道德论证的纽带中脱嵌的制度——这些纽带先前曾约束市场。（这是针对弗里德里希·哈耶克等新自由主义先驱奥地利人的论证，我们将在本章结尾回到他们。）然而，脱嵌是一个误导性的术语。

We can see this difficulty of grasping ‘the economic’ in the work of another scholar, one more widely associated with the idea of the emergence of the ‘economic’ as a separate sphere in the nineteenth century, Karl Polanyi. For a long while, Polanyi’s classic work *The Great Transformation* (1944) was misread as an account of the nineteenth-century disembedding of ‘the economy’ from society. This was not what the book said; its argument was conceived in the 1930s, before the idea of ‘the economy’ had properly emerged. It perhaps contributed towards its emergence, especially after Polanyi and his followers, from the 1950s, restated its argument in the novel language of that decade as an account of the nineteenth-century disembedding of ‘the economy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-057"></a>[57](#note-ch4-057) The book itself was an argument about ‘market relations’ or ‘market society’, describing how ‘the market’ in the nineteenth century was formulated as an institution disembedded from the ties of reciprocity, obligation, and moral argument that had previously contained it. (It was an argument against men like Friedrich Hayek and other Austrians, the pioneers of neoliberalism, to whom we will turn at the end of this chapter.) However, disembedding is a misleading term.

<a id="ch04-0053"></a>

<a id="page-156"></a>〔原书第156页〕一方面，正如波兰尼本人所阐明的，“市场社会”从未成功摆脱那些纠葛。家庭住户、政治权威、身体强制和社会义务都被重组，以支持、执行或补偿新财产法和合同法的运作。另一方面，经济脱嵌的观念假定经济市场作为一种抽象空间存在，其中已经充满买者、卖者和商品。正如米歇尔·卡隆所指出的，这一概念往往忽视为了把劳动、资本或商品“嵌入”市场交换关系而必须进行的持续工作。事实上，要把某个行动主体构成为买者、把另一个构成为卖者，要把对未来付款的索取权认定为“资本”，要把某些安排认定为商品、把另一些认定为经济行动者，每一项都取决于将某些财产界定为资产的规则、价格形成机制、对商品进行协商性描述和分类的方式、安排工作过程的方法，以及组装行动能力的技术。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-058"></a>[58](#note-ch4-058)每一次经济交换行为，都只有通过援引、确立和重新实施这些规则、机制和分类才能发生。像“市场”或“经济的”这样的抽象，指的不是某种独立的社会现实领域，而是一种处于持续建构和争夺之中的安排。

<a id="page-156-en"></a>〔原书第156页〕On the one hand, as Polanyi himself makes clear, ‘market society’ never successfully frees itself from those entanglements. The domestic household, political authority, physical compulsion, and social obligation are all reorganised to support, enforce, or compensate for the operation of new laws of property and contract. On the other, the idea of the disembedding of the economic assumes that the economic market exists as a kind of abstract space, already populated with its buyers, sellers, and commodities. As Michel Callon points out, the concept tends to overlook all the continuing work that must be done to ‘embed’ labour, capital, or merchandise in relations of market exchange. In fact, to constitute some agency as a buyer and another as a seller, to recognise a claim on future payments as ‘capital’, and to identify some arrangements as items of merchandise and others as economic agents, in each case depends upon rules for defining certain property as assets, mechanisms of price formation, negotiated descriptions and categorisations of goods, ways of arranging work processes, and techniques of assembling agency.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-058"></a>[58](#note-ch4-058) Every act of economic exchange occurs only by invoking, establishing, and re-enacting these rules, mechanisms, and categorisations. An abstraction such as ‘the market’ or ‘the economic’ designates not some freestanding sphere of social reality but an arrangement under continual construction and contestation.

<a id="ch04-0054"></a>

换句话说，不是在十八世纪、而是在十九世纪末出现的“经济的”概念，不应被理解为集体生活中一个独立领域的创造——即在“经济”一词本身尚未如此使用之前就制造出“经济”——而应被理解为对一个过程的指称。形成和指定何为经济的过程——以独特方式使世界可计算——可以被称为“经济化”。在资本主义发展的图示性叙述中，这一转变被描述为“经济的”作为实在抽象的创造；更好的理解是，“经济化”是一项持续不断、从未完成的工作。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-059"></a>[59](#note-ch4-059)

Another way to say this is that the concept of ‘the economic’ that emerged, not in the eighteenth century but towards the end of the nineteenth, should be grasped not as the creation of a distinct sphere of collective life, the making of ‘the economy’ before the word itself was used in this way, but the designation of a process. The process of forming and designating what is economic – of rendering the world calculable in distinctive ways – can be described as ‘economising’. The transformation characterised in schematic accounts of the development of capitalism as the creation of ‘the economic’ as a real abstraction is better understood as the continual, never-completed work of ‘economisation’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-059"></a>[59](#note-ch4-059)

<a id="ch04-0055"></a>

虽然本书关注的是资产化或资本化过程，即把未来商品转化为当下可以控制、贴现和交易的资产，但资本化始终依赖于经济化的行为。

While our focus in this book is on the process of assetisation or capitalisation, by which future goods are converted into assets that can be controlled, discounted, and traded in the present, capitalisation always depends on acts of economisation.

<a id="ch04-0056"></a>

我们将在本章后面回到经济化问题，以理解马克斯·韦伯著作中对经济化过程的分析——其部分动机来自资本化的挑战——如何无意中促成了把它转化为一个对象，即“这个经济整体”（the economy）。目前，经济化有两个特征值得注意。第一，<a id="page-157"></a>〔原书第157页〕使事物变得可计算的过程的一个重要方面是经济学文本的写作。在十九世纪确立政治经济学作为科学领域时，这些著作与其说是在描述“经济的”，不如说是在力图把获取和保护财富确立为社会生活的一个独立领域，服从于自身的计算和法则。以英语世界最有影响的著作为例，约翰·斯图亚特·密尔的*《政治经济学原理》*。它的主题不是“经济的”（密尔没有把这个词用作名词），而是财富，更具体地说，“人类……从事获取和保存财富”的活动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-060"></a>[60](#note-ch4-060)在他有影响的文章《论政治经济学的定义及其研究方法》中，密尔坚持认为，政治经济学是更广泛领域“社会经济学”（或“政治科学”）的一个分支，是其中仅把人作为“渴望占有财富的存在”来关心的部分。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-061"></a>[61](#note-ch4-061)这种存在方式，即人作为财富的渴望者，在经济科学的*规则*中被表述和促成。（十九世纪政治经济学中的“经济的”一词不仅是形容词而非名词；它还从不描述物质世界的一个方面，而是——正如我们刚才在讨论克罗默勋爵治理埃及的记述时所指出的——描述道德世界的一个方面，即一组期望中的规则、原则、社会法则或心理习惯。）因此，政治经济学执行了抽象化、经济化的一部分工作。关于这一主题的著作持续运作，以分离其论题、区分它所适用的物质过程，并建构其行动者应当遵循的原则。据说实在抽象所对应的“真实世界”，是一个包含政治经济学工作的世界。

We will come back to economisation later in the chapter, to understand how the analysis of the process of economising in the work of Max Weber, motivated, in part, by the challenges of capitalisation, inadvertently contributed to its transposition into an object, ‘the economy’. For now, there are two features of economisation to note. First, a <a id="page-157-en"></a>〔原书第157页〕significant aspect of the process of rendering things calculable was the writing of texts on economics. In establishing political economy in the nineteenth century as a scientific field, such works were not so much describing ‘the economic’ as attempting to secure the acquisition and protection of wealth as a distinct realm of social life, subject to its own calculations and laws. Take the most influential work in English, John Stuart Mill’s *Principles of Political Economy*. Its subject is not ‘the economic’ (a term Mill does not use as a noun) but wealth, and more specifically ‘mankind as occupied . . . in acquiring and conserving wealth’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-060"></a>[60](#note-ch4-060) In his influential essay ‘On the Definition of Political Economy; and on the Method of Investigation Proper to It’, Mill insists that political economy is a branch of the wider field of ‘social economy’ (or the ‘science of politics’), being the part concerned with man ‘solely as a being who desires to possess wealth’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-061"></a>[61](#note-ch4-061) This mode of being, man as desirer of wealth, is formulated and facilitated in the *rules* of economic science. (The term ‘economic’ in nineteenth-century political economy is not only an adjective, rather than a noun; it is also one that never describes an aspect of the material world but rather, as we noted just now in discussing Lord Cromer’s account of governing Egypt, an aspect of the moral world – a set of desired rules, principles, social laws, or mental habits.) Thus, political economy performs part of the work of abstracting, of economisation. Writings on the subject operate continually to separate its topic, distinguish those material processes to which it applies, and construct the principles on which its agents should act. The ‘real world’ to which a real abstraction is said to correspond is a world that includes the work of political economy.

校注：正文此处以《政治经济学原理》为例，但紧随引句的原注060所列出处为〈论政治经济学的定义〉第138页。书名与注中出处不一致，均保留原作。 

<a id="ch04-0057"></a>

第二，这种区分和具体化的过程——无论是通过政治经济学、法律、治理还是生产组织的工作——不断受到削弱。这是一项差异化的工作，只能通过重复、通过反复排除不属于“经济的”计算的东西来运作。但在这一过程中，被排除者不断施加压力，通过其被排除而塑造那个将它排除在外的范畴本身。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-062"></a>[62](#note-ch4-062)因此，“政治的”“家庭的”以及外部的或“殖民的”等范畴，都作为被内化的外部而运作。分离的不完整性不只是历史过程的症状，也不是随时间推移、随着过程趋于完成而得到弥补的东西。它是“经济的”这类抽象效果得以产生的方式中一个必要且永无止境的特征。

Second, this process of differentiation and specification, whether through the work of political economy, law, government, or productive organisation, is continually undermined. It is a work of difference that can operate only by repetition, by repeatedly excluding what does not belong to the calculation of ‘the economic’. But, in the process, what is excluded continually exerts pressure upon, shaping by its exclusion, the very category from which it is excluded.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-062"></a>[62](#note-ch4-062) Thus categories such as ‘the political’, ‘the domestic’, and the external or ‘colonial’ all operate as the internalised outside. The incompleteness of the separation is not just a symptom of a historical process, remedied over time as the process tends towards completion. It is a necessary and never-ending feature of the way an abstract effect like ‘the economic’ is produced.

<a id="ch04-0058"></a>

<a id="page-158"></a>〔原书第158页〕

<a id="page-158-en"></a>〔原书第158页〕

<a id="ch04-0059"></a>

### 信用的代言人

### Spokesmen of Credit

<a id="ch04-0060"></a>

一位十九世纪思想家理解了政治经济学的经济化工作，然后认识到这种工作如何从内部受到削弱、如何改变，并创造出新的对象。卡尔·马克思在 1844 年开始研究他所谓的亚当·斯密、让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊和大卫·李嘉图的“经典著作”，当时他才二十五岁上下。三年后，他指出这些著作与真理有一种特殊关系。它们所发展的法则，只有在如下假设下才是真实的：

One nineteenth-century thinker understood the economising work of political economy, and then learned how it was undermined from within, was altered, and created new objects. Karl Marx began his study of what he called ‘the classical works’ of Adam Smith, Jean-Baptiste Say, and David Ricardo in 1844, when still in his mid-twenties. Three years later, he remarked that these writings had a particular relationship to the truth. The laws they developed were true only under the supposition that

<a id="ch04-0061"></a>

> 竞争完全自由，不仅在一个国家之内，而且在全世界范围内。A. 斯密、萨伊和李嘉图所发展的这些法则，即财富据以生产和分配的法则——这些法则随着自由贸易的实现而变得更加真实、更加精确，然后不再只是抽象。

> competition be perfectly free, not only within a single country, but upon the whole face of the earth. These laws, which A. Smith, Say, and Ricardo, have developed, the laws under which wealth is produced and distributed – these laws grow more true, more exact, then cease to be mere abstractions, in the same measure in which Free Trade is carried out.

<a id="ch04-0062"></a>

因此，他总结说，经济学家“对未来社会的了解，比对当下社会的了解更多。如果你想读一读未来之书，就翻开斯密、萨伊、李嘉图的著作。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-063"></a>[63](#note-ch4-063)政治经济学是一门随时间推移会变得更加准确的科学，因为社会关系和物质关系会逐渐按照其原则组织起来——或者说经济化。

As a consequence, he concluded, the economists ‘know more about society as it will be, than about society as it is. If you wish to read in the book of the future, open Smith, Say, Ricardo.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-063"></a>[63](#note-ch4-063) Political economy was a science that would become more accurate with time, as social and material relations were gradually organised – or economised – according to its principles.

<a id="ch04-0063"></a>

然而，未来的发展并非如此。马克思后来发现，经济化的过程——经济法则借以“变得更加真实”的过程——总是不完整的。这个过程周期性地被逼上另一条道路。他曾着手写作一部政治经济学“批判”，这个项目持续写作和重写了随后二十年。1867 年，他终于出版了成果，即*《资本论》*第一卷；正如我们指出的，该卷主要论述十九世纪中叶的英国工厂制度。但那时，正如沃尔特·白芝浩不久后所指出的，政治经济学已经在失去对公众头脑的掌控。马克思本人显然已经放弃了撰写这部政治经济学批判的计划。他最初计划再写几卷*《资本论》*，但从未完成。另外两卷由弗里德里希·恩格斯在马克思去世后根据其早期笔记和片段整理而成。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-064"></a>[64](#note-ch4-064)这种放弃似乎反映了这样一个事实：政治经济学著作所设想的建立在自由竞争基础上的“商业社会”或“资产阶级社会”并未出现。然而，那种未来愿景并非败于马克思试图展开的<a id="page-159"></a>〔原书第159页〕揭露其内部矛盾的“批判”，也并非败于那些矛盾螺旋式扩张所预示的革命性自我毁灭。它正让位于新的财产所有权定义、新的集体实验和新的攫取未来的方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-065"></a>[65](#note-ch4-065)

Yet the future did not unfold that way. The process of economising, by which the laws of economics ‘grow more true’, Marx was to discover, was always incomplete. Periodically, the process was forced onto a different path. He had set to work on a ‘critique’ of political economy, a project whose writing and rewriting consumed the following two decades. In 1867, he finally published the result, volume one of *Capital*, which, as we noted, dealt mainly with the English factory system of the mid-nineteenth century. But, by then, as Walter Bagehot was soon to point out, political economy was already losing its hold on the public mind. Marx himself had evidently given up on the project of its critique. He had originally planned several further volumes of *Capital* but never completed them. Two further volumes were pieced together posthumously by Friedrich Engels from Marx’s earlier notebooks and fragments.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-064"></a>[64](#note-ch4-064) The abandonment seems to reflect the fact that the ‘commercial society’ or ‘bourgeois society’ built on free competition that the works of political economy envisioned had not come about. That vision of the future had succumbed, however, not to the ‘critique’ <a id="page-159-en"></a>〔原书第159页〕exposing its internal contradictions that Marx had attempted to develop, nor to the revolutionary self-destruction predicted to follow from the spiralling expansion of those contradictions. It was giving way to new definitions of property ownership, new collective experiments, and new modes of capturing the future.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-065"></a>[65](#note-ch4-065)

<a id="ch04-0064"></a>

政治经济学曾预见的未来，其部分替代方案正在别处得到巩固，例如废除农奴制后俄罗斯村社中重新出现的共同所有制形式，马克思对此产生了兴趣。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-066"></a>[66](#note-ch4-066)然而，另一些替代方案则从英国工厂制度本身发展出来。一个例子是企业合作所有制，马克思称赞它“不仅是一个伟大的实践成功”，而且是“劳动的政治经济学对财产的政治经济学的一场胜利”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-067"></a>[67](#note-ch4-067)一个更重大的发展是现代股份公司，以及促成它的信用创造能力的扩展。马克思著名地把生产私人所有权向股东所有权的过渡，视为“资本主义生产方式内部的资本主义生产方式的废除”——尤其是因为资本如今可以像他所说的那样“虚构地”创造出来，作为对未来生产的索取权。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-068"></a>[68](#note-ch4-068)他从古典政治经济学家那里借用了虚拟资本的概念，后者曾用这个短语描述融通汇票（上一章已提到），即在没有底层商品销售的情况下作为信用货币创造的汇票。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-069"></a>[69](#note-ch4-069)然而，到马克思出版*《资本论》*第一卷时，所谓“虚拟”信用已不只是商人银行家用来创造汇票的工具。在推动修建铁路、港口和城市地产的股份公司大量涌现的过程中，大部分资本是通过“虚构”创造并出售对一项将由未来支付的收入的股份而产生的。这种虚构如今相当真实。

Some of these alternatives to the future that political economy had once anticipated were being consolidated elsewhere, such as forms of communal ownership re-emerging in the village communities of Russia following the abolition of serfdom, in which Marx developed an interest.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-066"></a>[66](#note-ch4-066) Others, however, grew out of the English factory system itself. One example was the cooperative owning of enterprises, which Marx celebrated as ‘not only a great practical success’, but a ‘victory of the political economy of labour over the political economy of property’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-067"></a>[67](#note-ch4-067) A more significant development was the modern joint-stock company, together with the expanded powers of credit creation that enabled it. Marx famously saw the transition from the private ownership of production to its ownership by shareholders as ‘the abolition of the capitalist mode of production within the capitalist mode of production itself’ – not least because capital could now be created ‘fictitiously’, as he put it, as a claim on future production.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-068"></a>[68](#note-ch4-068) He borrowed the notion of fictitious capital from the classical political economists, who had used the phrase to describe bills of accommodation (mentioned in the previous chapter), meaning bills of exchange created as credit money where there was no underlying sale of goods.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-069"></a>[69](#note-ch4-069) By the time Marx published volume one of *Capital*, however, so-called ‘fictitious’ credit was not just a device used by merchant bankers to create bills. In the proliferation of joint-stock companies promoting the construction of railways, ports, and urban property, most capital was coming into being through the ‘fiction’ of creating and selling shares in a revenue to be paid from the future. The fiction was now quite real.

校注：正文把两段赞语连用于合作所有制，但原注067所引全文中，“不仅是一个伟大的实践成就”指十小时法案；后面的劳动政治经济学对财产政治经济学的胜利才转指合作运动。正文保留原作引述方式，请与原注合读。 

<a id="ch04-0065"></a>

马克思意识到，塑造和预测社会未来进程的已不再是古典政治经济学家，而是扩大信用创造的先驱。他举了两个例子。一个是约翰·劳，这位声名狼藉的十八世纪苏格兰裔法国金融家，他曾任法国财政总监，接管了一个失败的殖民项目——密西西比公司，并授予其法国在北美和西印度群岛全部贸易的垄断权。该计划与建立一家有权发行纸币信用的私人国家银行相结合，制造了一个投机泡沫，于 1720 年破灭。另一个例子是马克思的同时代人伊萨克·佩雷尔，一位法国<a id="page-160"></a>〔原书第160页〕铁路企业家，他与兄弟埃米尔共同创办了金融公司动产信贷银行。该公司开创了一种新颖的股份融资模式，用“投资银行”的新业务取代私人、绅士式的商人银行，向公众出售金融项目以及银行本身的股份。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-070"></a>[70](#note-ch4-070)该项目通过推销铁路股票、政府战争贷款、房地产开发和其他债务，创造了数亿法郎的信用货币，包括向奥斯曼政府提供贷款，以及在马赛开发港口和铁路连接；人们曾预计，苏伊士运河建成后，马赛将成为可与利物浦匹敌的国际航运枢纽。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-071"></a>[71](#note-ch4-071)1867 年 9 月，也就是*《资本论》*第一卷终于问世的那个月，这家银行及其房地产帝国在债务中崩溃。原因包括马赛未能成为新的利物浦，以及当年巴黎世界博览会未能吸引预期的数百万游客，削弱了巴黎的房地产投机——这是六年后维也纳世界博览会失败、进而引发 1870 年代全球金融危机的先兆。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-072"></a>[72](#note-ch4-072)马克思后来评论说，约翰·劳、伊萨克·佩雷尔和其他这类“信用的代言人”，具有“骗子和先知令人愉快的混合性格”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-073"></a>[73](#note-ch4-073)

Marx realised that it was no longer the classical political economists whose work shaped and predicted the future course of society. It was the pioneers of expanded credit creation. He offered two examples. One was John Law, the infamous eighteenth-century Scottish French financier who as Controller General of Finances in France took over a failing colonisation project, the Mississippi Company, and granted it a monopoly of all French trade in North America and the West Indies. Combined with establishing a private national bank with the power to issue paper credit, the scheme created a speculative bubble that burst in 1720. The other example was a contemporary of Marx, Isaac Pereire, a French <a id="page-160-en"></a>〔原书第160页〕railway entrepreneur who with his brother Émile founded the finance company Crédit Mobilier. Pioneering a novel model of joint-stock finance, the Company replaced private, gentlemanly merchant banking with the new business of ‘investment banking’, selling shares in financial ventures, and in the bank itself, to the public.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-070"></a>[70](#note-ch4-070) The venture created hundreds of millions of francs in credit money by marketing railway shares, government war loans, property development, and other debt, including the supply of loans to the Ottoman government and the development of port and rail connections at Marseilles, a city that was expected to rival Liverpool as a node of international shipping following the building of the Suez Canal.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-071"></a>[71](#note-ch4-071) In September 1867, the same month in which volume one of *Capital* had finally appeared, the bank and its property empire collapsed in debt. The causes included the failure of Marseilles to become a new Liverpool and the weakening of Paris property speculations when the Exposition Universelle that year failed to attract the millions of expected visitors – a precursor to the failure of the Vienna world exhibition six years later that was to trigger the global financial crisis of the 1870s.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-072"></a>[72](#note-ch4-072) John Law, Isaac Pereire, and other such ‘spokesmen of credit’, Marx later observed, were endowed ‘with the pleasant character mixture of swindler and prophet’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-073"></a>[73](#note-ch4-073)

<a id="ch04-0066"></a>

马克思退回到这样一种观念：这些骗子创造的资本是“虚拟的”，理由是他们以公司股份和其他资产形式出售的未来剩余尚未被创造出来。这种观点源于他较早的理解，即资本是从过去积累起来、然后通过物质生产劳动转化为更大数额的资金。但正如我们所见，资本本身是作为对未来的有效索取权而产生的。工业劳动及其工资——工资以未来消费为依据、作为信用预支——只是日益增多的从未来索取的方法中的一个方面。未来并非只由骗子和先知召唤的虚构，而是一套精心建造的攫取装置，其组织方式使控制它的人能够在当下以折扣价实现未来收入，然后把偿还作为负担强加给未来。

Marx fell back on the idea that capital created by such swindlers was ‘fictitious’, on the grounds that the future surplus they were selling in the form of company shares and other assets had not yet been created. This view followed from his earlier understanding of capital as a fund accumulated from the past and then transformed through the labour of material production into a larger amount. But, as we have seen, capital itself comes into being as an effective claim on the future. Industrial labour and its wage, advanced as credit against future consumption, is only one aspect of the proliferating methods of claiming from the future. The future is not a fiction conjured up only by swindlers and prophets, but an elaborate apparatus of capture organised to allow those who control it to realise future revenues at a discount in the present and then impose repayment as a burden on the future.

<a id="ch04-0067"></a>

由此可知，经济化工作从来不像在经济与政治之间建构一道分界那样简单。它需要新财产形式的大量涌现，尤其是那些作为未来索取权存在的财产形式，例如公司股份。而且它容易受到一切未来关系不稳定性的影响。

The work of economising, it follows, is never as simple as constructing a divide between the economic and the political. It requires the proliferation of new forms of property, in particular those forms of property that exist as claims on the future, such as the company share. And it is open to the instability of all relations to the future.

<a id="ch04-0068"></a>

<a id="page-161"></a>〔原书第161页〕

<a id="page-161-en"></a>〔原书第161页〕

<a id="ch04-0069"></a>

### 商业问题

### The Business Problem

<a id="ch04-0070"></a>

股市帮助创造了独特化商品的现象——这种商品召唤出买者、卖者和可知的价格——新兴的、更狭窄的经济学学科可以围绕它组织起来。然而，这种价格机制的科学难以确立自身。在十九世纪后期的早年，其实践者仍然觉得需要谈论价格体系之外的某些东西；几十年过去后，大多数经济学家才同意把其知识领域缩小到价格机制的研究。这种缩小伴随着其他概念的出现，用以指称经济学家当时已在很大程度上排除在其研究之外的价格体系以外的物质过程。正如我们在前面几章所指出的，其中最重要的概念将是“技术”一词，它最终成为一个包罗万象的术语——实际上也是一种托词——用来描述那些反复扰乱价格形成之稳定钟摆的所谓非经济力量。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-074"></a>[74](#note-ch4-074)但在十九世纪末，许多经济学家仍然觉得需要在解释中纳入价格机制之外技术政治世界的某些东西。

The stock market helped create the phenomenon of the singularised commodity that summons into being a buyer, a seller, and a knowable price, in association with which the new and narrower discipline of economics could be organised. Yet the science of this price mechanism struggled to establish itself. In these early years, during the late nineteenth century, its practitioners still felt the need to speak about something more than the system of prices; several decades passed before most economists agreed to narrow their field of knowledge to the study of the price mechanism. That narrowing would be accompanied by the emergence of other concepts, to reference the material processes outside the price system that economists by then had largely excluded from their study. The most significant of these, as we have suggested in earlier chapters, was to be the word ‘technology’, which eventually operated as a catchall term – and indeed an alibi – to describe so-called noneconomic forces that repeatedly disturbed the stabilising pendulum of price formation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-074"></a>[74](#note-ch4-074) But, in the late nineteenth century, many economists still felt the need to incorporate into their explanations something of the technopolitical world beyond the price mechanism.

<a id="ch04-0071"></a>

剑桥大学经济学家阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔的著作可以说明这些困难。在剑桥，马歇尔把政治经济学研究从道德科学领域的原有位置移出，建立了一个独立的经济学系。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-075"></a>[75](#note-ch4-075)他的*《经济学原理》*第一版于 1890 年问世，最初打算作为两卷本教科书的一半，它在四十多年里帮助界定了这门新学科的范围和方法。马歇尔推广了一种把商品或货物表示为机制的图表，形式是一张曲线图，横轴表示商品数量递增，纵轴表示价格上升。一条向右上方上升的曲线描绘“供给”，假定它随价格上升而增长；一条向右下方下降的曲线描绘“需求”，假定它随价格上升而减少。这创造了一种竞争体系的抽象再现，其中供给和需求形成相互抵消的“力量”，其交点是一个平衡点或“均衡”点。教科书第二卷原本打算用价格体系之外其他过程的“现实”记述，来补充这种把市场描绘为自动机制的抽象图景。马歇尔最终放弃了这一尝试。“我把计划定得太大了，”他指出，“随着当前这一代工业革命的每一次脉动，它的范围都扩大了，<a id="page-162"></a>〔原书第162页〕尤其是在现实方面；这场工业革命在速度和运动广度上都远远超过了一个世纪前的变革。”他提出，“完成这项任务需要四卷厚书”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-076"></a>[76](#note-ch4-076)

The work of Alfred Marshall, the leading Cambridge economist, can illustrate these difficulties. At Cambridge, Marshall removed the study of political economy from its existing home as part of the field of moral sciences and established a separate faculty of economics.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-075"></a>[75](#note-ch4-075) His *Principles of Economics*, whose first edition appeared in 1890 and was initially intended as one-half of a two-volume textbook, helped define the scope and method of the new discipline for more than four decades. Marshall popularised a diagram representing a commodity or good as a mechanism, in the form of a graph with the quantity of the good increasing along the x-axis and its price rising up the y-axis. A curve ascending towards the right depicted ‘supply’, assumed to grow as the price rose, while one descending towards the right pictured the ‘demand’ for it, assumed to decline as its price increased. This created an abstract representation of a competitive system in which supply and demand formed counteracting ‘forces’ whose intersection was a point of balance or ‘equilibrium’. The second volume of the textbook was intended to complement this abstract portrayal of the market as an automatic mechanism with a ‘realistic’ account of other processes, beyond those of the price system. Marshall eventually abandoned the attempt. ‘I had laid my plan on too large a scale’, he noted, ‘and its scope widened, especially <a id="page-162-en"></a>〔原书第162页〕on the realistic side, with every pulse of that Industrial Revolution of the present generation, which has far outdone the changes of a century ago, in both rapidity and breadth of movement.’ He suggested that ‘four thick volumes would be needed for the task’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-076"></a>[76](#note-ch4-076)

<a id="ch04-0072"></a>

马歇尔曾希望借助一个新颖观念——*组织*过程——来理解正在发生的更广泛运动。他抛开价格机制的物理学，转向生物学的隐喻。他提出，组织概念表达了一种复杂性不断增加的历史过程，其特征是相互依赖和各种力量的相互作用。关注点集中在“工业斗争”——J. A. 霍布森的*《帝国主义》*曾提到这一点——以及马歇尔等人开始称之为“工业*体系*”的东西。体系和组织的概念指的是一个相互锁合的世界：铁路网络、钢铁制造、煤炭和石油生产、发电、工业化学和大规模机器过程，连同发展起来控制这些过程的大型新股份公司和金融企业；霍布森将这一切称为“一个单一的有机整体”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-077"></a>[77](#note-ch4-077)

Marshall had hoped to make sense of the wider movements at work by means of a novel idea, the process of *organisation*. Leaving aside the physics of the price mechanism, he turned to metaphors from biology. He proposed that the concept of organisation expressed a historical process of increasing complexity, characterised by interdependence and the interaction of forces. The concern focused on the ‘industrial struggle’, to which J. A. Hobson’s *Imperialism* referred, and on what Marshall and others began to call the ‘industrial *system*’. The concepts of system and organisation referred to the interlocking world of railway networks, iron- and steelmaking, coal and oil production, electrical power generation, industrial chemistry, and large-scale machine processes, together with the sizeable new joint-stock companies and financial firms that grew to control these processes and made them what Hobson termed ‘a single organic whole’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-077"></a>[77](#note-ch4-077)

<a id="ch04-0073"></a>

股市、商品交易所、货币交易商和其他金融机制制造了一个可以记录和绘制的价格世界，但它们是这场大得多的重组中可见的、简化的部分。使这种价格生产成为可能的更广泛安排，正如我们所见，包括为了供应大宗商品而对地区进行的生态改造，从被改造成整齐划一麦田的美国中西部草原，到被排干以建立棉花和甘蔗种植园的尼罗河围堤蓄水田区；运送军队、病原体、金融票据和作物的铁路计划——铁路公司在可交易股票的公司中占据多数；安排和担保信用供给的银行和保险公司；以及许多其他相互锁合的过程。“体系”和“组织”等术语试图把这些相互依赖和不稳定的形式，与较早政治经济学家所研究的那种离散的“工业”形式区分开来。但正如马歇尔未能完成其后续卷册所证明的，价格抽象科学无法与对这个生态、帝国和工业过程广阔空间及其展开斗争的理解相协调。

While stock markets, commodity exchanges, currency dealers, and other financial mechanisms manufactured a world of prices that could be recorded and charted, they were the visible, simplified part of this much larger reorganisation. The wider arrangements that made possible the production of such prices included, as we have seen, the ecological remaking of regions to supply bulk commodities, from the prairies of the American Midwest homogenised into wheat fields, to the flood basins of the Nile dried out to create cotton and sugar plantations; the railway schemes that moved armies, pathogens, financial paper, and crops and accounted for the majority of firms whose shares could be traded; the banks and insurance companies that arranged and guaranteed the supply of credit; and many other interlocking processes. Terms like ‘system’ and ‘organisation’ attempted to distinguish these forms of interdependence and instability from the discrete forms of ‘industry’ that earlier political economists had studied. But as Marshall’s failed attempt to produce the subsequent volumes of his textbook testified, the abstract science of prices proved impossible to reconcile with understanding this wide space of ecological, imperial, and industrial processes and the struggles unfolding there.

<a id="ch04-0074"></a>

摆脱这一僵局、并为经济诞生准备基础的办法，同样可以理解为一种经济化过程。研究对象本身产生了<a id="page-163"></a>〔原书第163页〕科学反过来帮助抽象、形式化和计算的推理、理性和可计算性模式。我们可以通过考察另一个观念的发展来审视这是如何发生的；这个观念在“经济”被发明之前的几十年里开始在英语中通用——我们在上一章结尾注意到其出现的对象，即“商业”领域。经济学家提到一个由“商人”或“金融城人士”（city men）组成的世界。他们甚至承认，自己的著作主要适用于这些人的计算，并将改进他们的核算。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-078"></a>[78](#note-ch4-078)在美国经济学家中，对这些过程更宽泛的说法是“商业企业”，例如托斯丹·凡勃伦 1905 年的批判性著作*《商业企业理论》*。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-079"></a>[79](#note-ch4-079)这个说法越来越多地被简称为“商业”。这个有机体系波动的命运成为一个重要的调查主题。尤其是它反复出现的扩张和衰退，如今被作为“商业周期”问题来研究。1913 年，凡勃伦最著名的学生韦斯利·克莱尔·米切尔出版了一部 600 页的研究*《商业周期》*，主张萧条和金融危机不是由战争、作物歉收或技术发明等“异常现象”引起的，而是由“商业企业之间的相互依赖”本身引起的，由于这种相互依赖，它们如今“构成一个体系”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-080"></a>[80](#note-ch4-080)正如我们将看到的，思考随后经济诞生的一种方式，是认为后一个术语把“商业”作为有机体系的观念翻译成一个扩大了的、带有更受规整的时间性的概念。

The solution that emerged to this impasse, and that was to prepare the ground for the birth of the economy, can be grasped, again, as a process of economisation. The object of study itself produced the <a id="page-163-en"></a>〔原书第163页〕modes of reason, rationality, and calculability that the science in turn helped to abstract, formalise, and calculate upon. We can examine how this happened by considering the development of another idea that came into common use in English, in the decades prior to the invention of ‘the economy’ – the object whose emergence we noted at the end of the previous chapter, the realm of ‘business’. Economists referred to a world populated by ‘men of business’, or ‘city men’. They even acknowledged that it was to the calculations of these men that they thought their work mainly applied, and whose reckonings it would improve.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-078"></a>[78](#note-ch4-078) Among American economists a wider term for these processes was ‘business enterprise’, as portrayed in books such as Thorstein Veblen’s critical 1905 work, *The Theory of Business Enterprise*.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-079"></a>[79](#note-ch4-079) Increasingly the phrase was shortened to just ‘business’. The fluctuating fortunes of this organic system became an important subject of investigation. In particular, its repeated episodes of expansion and decline were now studied as the problem of ‘business cycles’. In 1913, Veblen’s most famous student, Wesley Clair Mitchell, published a 600-page study, *Business Cycles*, arguing that episodes of depression and financial crisis were caused not by ‘abnormal phenomena’ such as war, crop failure, or technical inventions, but by the very ‘interdependence of business enterprises’, as a consequence of which they now ‘constitute a system’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-080"></a>[80](#note-ch4-080) One way to think of the subsequent birth of the economy, as we will see, is that the latter term provided a translation of the idea of ‘business’ as an organic system into an expanded concept, equipped with a more regulated temporality.

<a id="ch04-0075"></a>

铁路公司，尤其是美国的铁路公司，是这种不断扩张的攫取装置的主要例子——即使在当时，它看起来也是一种向未来征税的方式。

The railroad companies, especially those of the United States, were the main example of this expanding apparatus of capture – a mode of taxing the future, as it appeared even at the time.

<a id="ch04-0076"></a>

十九世纪末出现了一波突然的合并和收购浪潮——1894 年后十年间的“大合并运动”，食品制造、石油、煤炭、金属和运输行业的公司合并或被接管，形成许多二十世纪最大的公司。到二十世纪中叶，这些公司的股市价值指数——尤其是标普 500 指数，代表从每个产业部门中选出的最大公司——与国内生产总值（GDP）一起，成为衡量经济健康以及政府成败的主要指标之一。

A sudden wave of mergers and acquisitions took place at the end of the nineteenth century – the ‘great merger movement’ of the decade after 1894, in which companies in food manufacturing, petroleum, coal, metals, and transport merged or were taken over to form many of the largest corporations of the twentieth century. By the mid-twentieth century, indices of the stock market value of these companies – notably the S&P 500, representing the largest firms selected to represent every sector of industry – became, alongside the gross domestic product, or GDP, one of the principal measures of the health of the economy and the success and failure of government.

<a id="ch04-0077"></a>

在这里，人们可以简洁地看到经济化过程在起作用。商业研究中有一个关于<a id="page-164"></a>〔原书第164页〕大型企业兴起的标准故事。这一故事在阿尔弗雷德·D. 钱德勒 1977 年的经典著作*《看得见的手》*中得到阐述。钱德勒反驳凡勃伦的观点——凡勃伦把商业企业解释为一种基于扰乱工业体系能力的剩余攫取方式——主张大型一体化企业是对协调问题的自然回应。随着民族国家规模扩大、人口增长、交通基础设施扩展，市场关系不再是协调供应者、制造商、分销商和消费者之间交换的最有效方式。职能协调和材料分配由专业管理者处理更为有效。这些管理者位于大公司的各个部门内部。管理型企业的成长，是对现代工业生活日益增长的技术复杂性的回应。

Here, one can see succinctly the processes of economisation at work. There is a standard story in business studies about the rise of the <a id="page-164-en"></a>〔原书第164页〕large business firm. It was laid out in Alfred D. Chandler’s classic work of 1977, *The Visible Hand*. Countering the views of Veblen, who had explained business enterprise as a mode of capturing surplus based on the ability to disrupt the industrial system, Chandler argued that the large, integrated firm was a natural response to the problem of coordination. As nation-states expanded in size, as their populations grew, and as transportation infrastructures spread, market relations were no longer the most efficient way to coordinate exchanges among suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and consumers. The coordination of functions and allocation of materials was more efficiently handled by professional managers. These were located within the different divisions of the large corporation. The growth of the managerial firm was a response to the growing technical complexity of modern industrial life.

<a id="ch04-0078"></a>

钱德勒的叙述主要基于铁路公司的历史。这并不奇怪。1880 年代，在纽约证券交易所交易的百余家公司中，约九十家是铁路公司，其余大多是相关企业——电报公司、快递公司和类似企业。钱德勒认为，铁路运营带来的巨大挑战和机遇——制定时刻表、计算运费、协调机车和车厢的移动等等——促成并推动了新管理技能的发展，大型公司正是由这些技能塑造而成。

Chandler’s account was based largely on the history of railroad firms. This is no surprise. In the 1880s, some ninety of the hundred-plus firms traded on the New York stock exchange were railway companies, and most of the rest were related businesses – telegraph companies, express mail firms, and similar enterprises. Chandler argued that the great challenges and opportunities presented by the running of railways – setting timetables, calculating freight prices, coordinating the movement of locomotives and rail cars, and so on – enabled and spurred the development of the new managerial skills out of which the large corporation was formed.

<a id="ch04-0079"></a>

让我们以另一种方式考虑这个故事，不是由技术复杂性日益增加这一简单逻辑——由“技术”的力量——驱动，而是以它例示经济化运作的方式。铁路的建设和运营需要新型工程知识和计算知识。*《美国铁路杂志》*早在 1832 年就已创刊，通过汇集关于桥梁、转车台、机车和其他机械及技术结构工程的技术知识，来教育年轻工程师。但铁路不仅、或许甚至主要不是一种提高运输和通信速度与规模的技术系统。正如我们所知，它们还是吸引股东投资、从土地价格投机以及铁路建设所产生的其他机会中获利的手段。因此，铁路不仅要求并鼓励工程知识的发展，也要求并鼓励新形式金融信息和计算的发展。它们自己公布的运费、票价、轨道里程、股价和其他运营数据，正是这个金融世界的<a id="page-165"></a>〔原书第165页〕构建材料。它们是经济化过程的重要部分。

Let us consider this story differently, in a way that is not driven by a simple logic of increasing technical complexity – by the force of ‘technology’ – but in the way it exemplifies economisation at work. The building and running of railways required new kinds of engineering and calculative knowledge. The *American Railroad Journal* was a publication that had been launched as early as 1832 to educate young engineers by gathering know-how about the engineering of bridges, turntables, locomotives, and other machinery and technical structures. But railways were not only, or perhaps even primarily, a technical system for improving the speed and scale of transport and communication. As we know, they were also a means of attracting shareholder investment and profiting from speculation in land prices and other opportunities to which railway construction gave rise. So, the railways required and encouraged the growth not only of engineering know-how, but of new forms of financial information and calculation. Their own published freight rates, ticket prices, track mileage, share prices, and other operational data were the building blocks <a id="page-165-en"></a>〔原书第165页〕of this financial world. They were a vital part of the process of economisation.

<a id="ch04-0080"></a>

工业装置与经济及金融信息格式化之间的这种关系，可以从*《美国铁路杂志》*的演变中看出来。1849 年，新英格兰铁路大亨约翰·普尔买下该杂志，并让其兄弟亨利·瓦纳姆·普尔担任编辑。随着铁路组建公司并发行债券和股票，亨利·普尔开始在刊载工程知识之外发布金融信息。该杂志发展出再现和传播铁路正在产生并赖以生存的金融数据的方式。从 1868 年起，瓦纳姆·普尔每年以*《美国铁路便览》*这一新形式系统列表整理这些信息，详细列出每条铁路的债券、股票、里程、收益和开支，以及每家公司的历史。最终，*《便览》*每年发布 128 家铁路公司的数据。

This relation between an industrial apparatus and the formatting of economic and financial information can be seen in what happened to the *American Railroad Journal*. In 1849, a New England railway magnate, John Poor, purchased the journal and gave its editorship to his brother, Henry Varnum Poor. Alongside engineering knowledge, Henry Poor began to publish financial information, as railways were incorporated and issued bonds and stocks. The journal developed ways of representing and circulating the financial data that railroads were generating and depending upon. From 1868, Varnum Poor tabulated this information systematically each year in a new form called the *Manual of the Railroads of the United States*, detailing for each railroad their bonds, stocks, mileage, earnings, and expenses, along with a history of each corporation. Eventually the *Manual* was publishing annual data on 128 railroad companies.

<a id="ch04-0081"></a>

这种经济化工作是由资本化的困难驱动的。*《便览》*第一卷的导言提请注意“铁路名义*资本*不断增加、而其获利能力没有任何增加”这一“大恶”。瓦纳姆·普尔举例说，一条造价 4,868,428 美元的铁路，通过连续发行股票和债券，创造了 11,250,000 美元的资本账户。铁路没有降低运价，而是“把沿线商业和旅行课税到最大限度”，以支付这些资本的利息和股息。“一项本应按 4,868,428 美元成本收费的运输，如今却要按这一数额的两倍半收费。”普尔写道，这是众多此类侵害之一，“不仅侵害了铁路经济的真正原则，也侵害了公众权利”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-081"></a>[81](#note-ch4-081)*《便览》*意在制衡这些“侵害”，希望监督和规范把此类未来索取权推向市场的过程，以及它们借此把未来商业和旅行“课税到最大限度”的做法。资本化未来的实践本身，开始反过来产生统计知识形式，“经济的”或许可以通过这些形式被认识和规范。

This economising work was driven by the difficulties of capitalisation. The introduction to the first volume of the *Manual* drew attention to the ‘great evil’ of the ‘constant increase in the nominal *capitals* of railroads, without any addition to their capacity to earn’. Varnum Poor gave the example of a railroad built at a cost of $4,868,428, which had made successive issues of stocks and bonds to create a capital account of $11,250,000. Instead of reducing rates, ‘the commerce and travel of the route is taxed to the utmost extent’, to pay the interest and dividends on this capital. ‘A traffic which should have paid on a cost of $4,868,428, is made to pay on two and a half times this sum.’ This was one of many such violations, Poor wrote, ‘not only of the true principles of railway economy but of popular right’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-081"></a>[81](#note-ch4-081) The *Manual* was intended as a check on these ‘violations’, hoping to monitor and regulate the very process of marketing such claims to the future and their practice of thereby taxing future commerce and travel ‘to the utmost extent’. The very practice of capitalising the future began to generate in reaction the forms of statistical knowledge through which ‘the economic’ might be known and regulated.

校注：按本段所列数额计算，11,250,000÷4,868,428约为2.31，与引文的“两倍半”不符。数额与引文均按底本保留。 

<a id="ch04-0082"></a>

1916 年，普尔的出版公司开始编制并出售它收集信息的那些公司所发行债务的信用评级。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-082"></a>[82](#note-ch4-082)另一家公司标准统计公司早十年前成立，为非铁路公司编制同样的信息（以易于更新的 5×7 英寸索引卡形式出版），并于 1922 年开始出售自己的评级。1941 年，两家公司合并组成标准普尔，这家信用评级和金融<a id="page-166"></a>〔原书第166页〕信息机构建立了世界上第一个按市值加权的股市指数，也创设了今天所称的标普 500 指数。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-083"></a>[83](#note-ch4-083)

In 1916, Poor’s publishing firm began to compile and sell ratings of the creditworthiness of the debt issued by the firms on which it collected information.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-082"></a>[82](#note-ch4-082) Another company, the Standard Statistics Bureau, founded a decade earlier to compile the same information for non-railroad companies (published in the form of 5 x 7–inch index cards that could be easily updated), began to sell its own ratings in 1922. In 1941, the two firms merged to form Standard and Poor’s, the credit rating and financial <a id="page-166-en"></a>〔原书第166页〕information agency that established the world’s first value-weighted Stock Market Index, and what is today known as the S&P 500.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-083"></a>[83](#note-ch4-083)

<a id="ch04-0083"></a>

这说明经济化如何运作：它不是绘制一张预先存在的地形图，而是铺设轨道和连接，这些轨道和连接同时是运送货物和人员、创造对未来的商业和旅行“征税”的资本、以及构成和流通使这种对未来征税得以进行的数量、价格、指数和期货的手段。经济正是从这些相同的相互关联过程中产生，成为知识与规制的对象。

This illustrates how economisation works: not as the mapping of a pre-existing terrain, but as the laying out of tracks and connections that are simultaneously a means of moving goods and people, of creating the capital that ‘taxes’ future commerce and travel, and of constituting and circulating quantities, prices, indices, and futures that enables this taxation of the future to proceed. It was out of these same interconnected processes that the economy would emerge, as an object of knowledge and regulation.

<a id="ch04-0084"></a>

经济化也通过学术知识的生产来运作。事实上，通过同样的连接和流通，产生了“商业”现象的*历史*，这种历史可以用来为这种攫取未来的方式辩护，并成为其进一步的托词。亨利·瓦纳姆·普尔的私人文件由他的女儿露西·普尔保存。后来，这些文件在她位于马萨诸塞州剑桥附近布鲁克莱恩的房子的储藏室里，被她的一位侄孙发现，后者在她去世后搬进了这所房子。这位侄孙是瓦纳姆·普尔的曾孙，他利用这些文件在哈佛大学撰写了博士论文，内容包括对瓦纳姆·普尔的研究、美国铁路史，以及公司金融和管理的发展。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-084"></a>[84](#note-ch4-084)这篇博士论文的作者是阿尔弗雷德·杜邦·钱德勒。作为哈佛研究生，他受到塔尔科特·帕森斯以及帕森斯对韦伯组织理论解释的影响——我们很快将讨论这一点——并间接受到已故约瑟夫·熊彼特的影响。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-085"></a>[85](#note-ch4-085)他后来写了*《看得见的手》*，这本书确立了他作为美国商业史学界领袖的地位。钱德勒仔细研读其曾祖父汇编的统计和组织数据，为他那一代人做了“普尔曾做过的事”，从铁路的账簿和组织图中推导出对美国资本主义的理解——实际上是一种关于其独特形式即大型投资者所有公司的理论。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-086"></a>[86](#note-ch4-086)

Economisation also works through the production of academic knowledge. In fact, through the same connections and circulations, a *history* of the phenomenon of ‘business’ was generated, one that could serve to justify and become a further alibi for this mode of capture of the future. Henry Varnum Poor’s personal papers were kept by his daughter, Lucy Poor. They were later discovered in a storeroom of her house in Brookline, near Cambridge, Massachusetts, by her great nephew, who moved into the house after her death. The nephew, a great grandson of Varnum Poor, used the papers to write his PhD thesis at Harvard, comprised of a study of Varnum Poor, the history of the American railways, and the development of corporate finance and management.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-084"></a>[84](#note-ch4-084) The author of the PhD was Alfred DuPont Chandler. As a graduate student at Harvard, he worked under the influence of Talcott Parsons and the Parsonian interpretation of Weberian organisation theory, to which we will shortly turn, and indirectly under the influence of the late Joseph Schumpeter.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-085"></a>[85](#note-ch4-085) He went on to write *The Visible Hand*, the book that established him as the dean of American business historians. Poring over the statistical and organisational data that his greatgrandfather had compiled, Chandler did for his own generation ‘just what Poor had done’, deriving from the account books and organisational charts of the railways an understanding of American capitalism – indeed a theory of its distinctive form, the large investor-owned corporation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-086"></a>[86](#note-ch4-086)

<a id="ch04-0085"></a>

钱德勒的论文帮助推翻了托斯丹·凡勃伦关于大企业兴起的叙述，后者认为商人追求金钱利益会导致低效率和蓄意破坏。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-087"></a>[87](#note-ch4-087)*《看得见的手》*则主张，在 1880 年代至 1920 年代期间，在美国铁路开创先河之后，公司*组织*——组织图——取代了市场机制，并作为一种更有效地管理大型技术过程的方式做到了这一点。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-088"></a>[88](#note-ch4-088)经济化借以进行的图表、<a id="page-167"></a>〔原书第167页〕账簿、商业记录和预测世界，帮助产生了商业世界日益依赖的辩护，即经济义论。

Chandler’s thesis helped overturn Thorstein Veblen’s account of the rise of big business, in which the pecuniary advantage pursued by businessmen led to inefficiency and sabotage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-087"></a>[87](#note-ch4-087) *The Visible Hand* argued instead that in the period from the 1880s to the 1920s, after pioneering by American railroads, corporate *organisation* – the organisational chart – took the place of market mechanisms, and did so as a more efficient way to manage large, technical processes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-088"></a>[88](#note-ch4-088) The world of charts, <a id="page-167-en"></a>〔原书第167页〕account books, business records, and projections through which economisation proceeds helped generate the justification – the oikodicy – on which the world of business increasingly depended.

<a id="ch04-0086"></a>

### 经济将（不再）意味着经济化（economising）

### Economy Shall (No Longer) Mean Economising

<a id="ch04-0087"></a>

关于“经济”（economy）在“这个经济整体”（the economy）诞生之前的历史，让我们转向最后一个问题。是什么脱位或中断，导致了从把经济理解为过程到把经济理解为对象的转变？这种转变如何与“商业”的兴起、以及理解大型公司企业世界似乎所属的信用危机和“商业周期”的紧迫努力联系在一起？答案是，到两次世界大战之间，这些危机开始威胁未来本身，而资本化过程正有赖于这种未来的生产。资本主义——这个体系如今将被如此命名——被资本化危机削弱，似乎即将崩溃。回应就是发明“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）。

Let us turn to a final question about the history of ‘economy’ before the birth of ‘the economy’. What dislocations or disruptions led to the change from understanding economy as process to economy as object? In what way was the shift connected to the rise of ‘business’, and to urgent attempts to understand the credit crises and ‘business cycles’ to which the world of large corporate firms seemed to belong? The answer is that by the interwar period these crises were beginning to threaten the very future on whose production the capitalising process depended. Weakened by the crises of capitalisation, capitalism itself, as the system would now be named, appeared about to collapse. The response was the invention of *the* economy.

<a id="ch04-0088"></a>

这种转变似乎先出现在德国作家的著作中，然后才出现在英语中。这或许反映了德国学者对将其研究领域界定为“社会经济学”（*Sozialökonomik*）的关切。约翰·斯图亚特·密尔曾呼应让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊，把政治经济学置于这一更广泛领域的一个分支，而正如我们刚看到的，阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔等人却难以把分析扩展到价格机制这一狭窄主题之外。正是在十九世纪末和二十世纪初的德国，马克斯·韦伯等领军学者坚持把经济与社会作为相互关联的过程来研究。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-089"></a>[89](#note-ch4-089)也正是在那里，经济过程管理的现代观念得到最清晰的发展。德国政治的危机——包括该国在第一次世界大战中被北大西洋世界帝国强权击败，以及战败后社会主义革命的可能性——呼唤新的观念。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-090"></a>[90](#note-ch4-090)

The shift appears to have occurred among the works of German writers before it appeared in English. This reflects perhaps the concern of German scholars to define their field of research as ‘social economy’ (*Sozialökonomik*). While John Stuart Mill, echoing Jean-Baptiste Say, had situated political economy as a branch of this wider field, men like Alfred Marshall, as we just saw, struggled to expand their analysis beyond the narrow topic of the price mechanism. It was in Germany in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century that leading scholars such as Max Weber insisted on studying economy and society as connected processes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-089"></a>[89](#note-ch4-089) It was there that modern conceptions of the management of economic processes were most clearly developed. The crises of German politics, including the country’s defeat in the First World War by the imperial powers of the North Atlantic world, and the possibility of socialist revolution in the wake of that defeat, called for new conceptions.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-090"></a>[90](#note-ch4-090)

<a id="ch04-0089"></a>

英美思想接受这些观念较慢，它们往往通过翻译德国和奥地利社会理论家的著作进入英语。把关键的德语术语译成英语的困难，从*Wirtschaft*（经济）一词开始，有助于说明这些挑战。我们可以通过详细考察社会经济学家马克斯·韦伯的案例来结束本章。他的代表作*《经济与社会》*1922 年以德文出版，二十五年后英译本问世时被<a id="page-168"></a>〔原书第168页〕误译了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-091"></a>[91](#note-ch4-091)这些误译揭示了一些东西。问题始于书名中的两个词。在第二次世界大战后的时期，即英译本终于问世之时，经济与社会正逐渐被理解为自身存在的对象，各自形成一个由可识别、可衡量的关系构成的稳定领域。另一方面，正如基思·特赖布在其具有里程碑意义的文本重译中所指出的，韦伯仍然较少关注结构，更多关注过程。就社会一词而言，他关注的不是书名中使用的*Gesellschaft*，而是形成社会和其他联合体的过程，即*Vergesellschaftung*，字面意思是“社会化”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-092"></a>[92](#note-ch4-092)但另一个术语“经济”呢？鉴于这个词到二十世纪中叶将在英语中获得的新含义的分量，要避免后来经济作为对象的含义来进行翻译就更加困难。在韦伯文本中阐述理解经济生活范畴的第二章里，他明确指出该词指一个过程：“在实践中，经济［*Wirtschaft*］意味着在目的之间仔细选择”，同时考虑可得手段的稀缺性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-093"></a>[93](#note-ch4-093)在同一章开头的概念正式定义中，他通过用该词自己的动名词来界定自己的用法，确认了这一含义：他写道，经济应指“*Wirtschaften*”——字面意思是经济化。后者指对资源“和平行使处置权”，这种权力“有计划地”（理性地）指向经济目的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-094"></a>[94](#note-ch4-094)

Anglo-American thought was slower to adopt these ideas, which often arrived in English through the translation of the work of German and Austrian social theorists. The difficulty in translating key German terms into English, starting with the word *Wirtschaft*, or economy, helps illuminate these challenges. We can close this chapter by looking in detail at the case of the social economist Max Weber. His masterwork, *Economy and Society*, published in German in 1922, was <a id="page-168-en"></a>〔原书第168页〕mistranslated when it appeared in English twenty-five years later.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-091"></a>[91](#note-ch4-091) The mistranslations reveal something. The problem begins with the two words of the book’s title. In the period after the Second World War, when the English version finally appeared, economy and society were coming to be understood as objects in themselves, each forming a stable domain composed of relations that can be identified and measured. Weber, on the other hand, as Keith Tribe points out in his landmark retranslation of the text, was still interested less in structures than in processes. For the term society, he focused not on the word used in the title, *Gesellschaft*, but on the process of forming society – and other associations – or *Vergesellschaftung*, meaning literally ‘societisation’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-092"></a>[92](#note-ch4-092) But what about the other term, ‘economy’? Given the weight of the new meaning the word was to acquire in English by the mid-twentieth century, it is more difficult to translate in a way that avoids the later sense of economy as an object. In chapter 2 of his text, where he lays out the categories for understanding economic life, Weber makes clear that the term refers to a process: ‘in practice economy [*Wirtschaft*] means the careful choice between ends’, taking into account the scarcity of available means.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-093"></a>[93](#note-ch4-093) In the formal definition of the concept with which the same chapter opens, he confirms this meaning by defining his use of the word in terms of its own verbal noun: economy, he writes, shall mean ‘*Wirtschaften*’ – literally, economising. The latter term refers to ‘a peaceful exercise of a power of disposition’ over resources, a power that is ‘planfully’ (rationally) oriented to economic ends.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-094"></a>[94](#note-ch4-094)

<a id="ch04-0090"></a>

正如我们所见，“经济化”（economising）一词需要在一种不寻常的意义上使用，才能捕捉*Wirtschaften*的含义。在韦伯时代，英语经济一词被用来表示资源的有效处置，而 economising 通常传达更狭窄的节俭行事含义。这个词已失去其更广泛的意义，即指使某些商品或行动成为经济的那些过程和推理。威廉·斯马特在世纪之交前后把一些关键德文文本译成英文，他在翻译奥地利经济学派领军人物欧根·冯·庞巴维克的*《资本实证论》*时，试图在这一更广泛意义上使用该词：

As we have seen, the word ‘economising’ needs to be used in an unusual sense to capture the meaning of *Wirtschaften*. While the English term economy was used in Weber’s time to indicate the efficient disposition of resources, economising usually conveyed the narrower idea of acting with frugality. The word had lost its wider meaning referring to the processes and reasonings that render certain goods or actions economic. William Smart, who translated key texts from German into English around the turn of the century, tried using the term in this broader sense in translating *The Positive Theory of Capital* by Eugen von Bohm-Bawerk, a leading member of the Austrian school of economics:

<a id="ch04-0091"></a>
