> 在作为人类生产组合基础的大量自然禀赋中，有一部分特别引起经济学的兴趣，那就是自然仅以<a id="page-169"></a>〔原书第169页〕有限数量提供的那些有用之物……自然世界的这些有限赠予和能量，对我们具有一种特殊的*经济*重要性。不节约它们将是愚蠢的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-095"></a>[95](#note-ch4-095)

> Of the vast natural endowment which serves as foundation for man’s productive combinations, one portion particularly claims the interest of economics, and that is, those useful things offered by nature only in <a id="page-169-en"></a>〔原书第169页〕limited amount . . . These limited gifts and energies of the natural world obtain for us a peculiar *economic* importance. It would be foolish not to economise them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-095"></a>[95](#note-ch4-095)

<a id="ch04-0092"></a>

然而，即使在当时，更不用说今天，“economising”一词也使人想到节俭或吝啬，而不是使事物成为经济的。

However, even then, and more so today, ‘economising’ suggests thrift or parsimony, rather than rendering things economic.

<a id="ch04-0093"></a>

绕过这一困难的一条途径，或许是把*Wirtschaften*译为“经济化”（economisation）；正如上文所指出的，米歇尔·卡隆用这个术语指把特定安排和行动定性为经济的过程，经济行动者和理论家都参与其中。用当代词汇来说，这一含义似乎呼应了韦伯方法的某些方面。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-096"></a>[96](#note-ch4-096)在 economisation（经济化）的意义上，economising 一词把韦伯与奥地利经济学派联系起来，正如我们将看到的，他与该学派关系密切。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-097"></a>[97](#note-ch4-097)这种联系使我们能够理解，韦伯的著作如何反常地促成了后来把经济理解为经济化的观念消失，并促使其转变为作为对象的“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）。

One route around the difficulty might be to translate *Wirtschaften* as ‘economisation’, the term, as noted above, that Michel Callon proposes for the process of qualifying specific arrangements and actions as economic, in which both economic agents and theorists engage. Using a contemporary vocabulary, this meaning seems to echo aspects of Weber’s approach.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-096"></a>[96](#note-ch4-096) In the sense of economisation, the term ‘economising’ connects Weber to the Austrian school of economics, with which, as we will see, he was closely associated.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-097"></a>[97](#note-ch4-097) The connection allows us to understand how Weber’s work contributed, perversely, to the future disappearance of the understanding of economy as economising and its transformation into *the* economy as an object.

<a id="ch04-0094"></a>

对韦伯以及十九世纪和二十世纪初的其他作家来说，经济过程可以在不同尺度上被识别。它并不以“*国民*经济”为前提；国家尺度只是在把“经济”变成一个独立对象的过程中才成为默认尺度。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-098"></a>[98](#note-ch4-098)人们可以指家庭经济、村庄经济、城市经济和国民经济（*Volkswirtschaft*）的过程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-099"></a>[99](#note-ch4-099)韦伯的同时代人把这种尺度差异理解为从较简单形式到较复杂形式的历史进步。然而在*《经济与社会》*中，韦伯对写作发展论叙述不感兴趣。他的目标是为理解当下澄清概念。

For Weber, as for other writers of the nineteenth and early twentieth century, the process of economy could be identified at different scales. It did not presuppose ‘*national* economy’, which became the default scale only as part of the way in which ‘economy’ was made into an object in itself.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-098"></a>[98](#note-ch4-098) One could refer to the processes of household economy, village economy, urban economy, and national economy (*Volkswirtschaft*).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-099"></a>[99](#note-ch4-099) Contemporaries of Weber read this difference in scale as a historical progression, from simpler to more complex forms. In *Economy and Society*, however, Weber was not interested in writing a developmentalist account. His goal was to clarify concepts for understanding the present.

<a id="ch04-0095"></a>

就我们的目的而言，在把经济化与资本化联系起来时，有趣的一点不是韦伯像其同时代人一样把经济理解为一个过程——经济化——而是他在定义这个词时，设定了两种经济化之间的区分。这一区分指向对商业或商业企业问题及其在资本化中作用的理解。韦伯引入这一区分，正是为了确立经济的定义：“‘Wirtschaft’ soll ein autokephal, ‘Wirtschaftsbetrieb’ ein betriebsmäßig geordnetes kontinuierliches Wirtschaften heißen. <a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-100"></a>[100](#note-ch4-100)（“经济”应指一种自主的经济化，“企业经济”应指一种按企业经营方式有序组织的持续经济化。）”

The interesting point for our purpose, in connecting economisation to capitalisation, is not that Weber, like his contemporaries, understands economy as a process – economisation – but that, in defining the term, he sets up a distinction between two kinds of economising. The distinction points towards understanding the problem of business or business enterprise and its role in capitalisation. Weber introduces the distinction to establish the very definition of economy: ‘“Wirtschaft” soll ein autokephal, “Wirtschaftsbetrieb” ein betriebsmäßig geordnetes kontinuierliches Wirtschaften heißen.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-100"></a>[100](#note-ch4-100) (“Economy” shall mean an autocephalous, “enterprise-economy” a continuously ordered economising.)’

<a id="ch04-0096"></a>

韦伯不是孤立地定义经济，而是通过<a id="page-170"></a>〔原书第170页〕*Wirtschaft*（经济）与*Wirtschaftsbetrieb*（字面意思是企业经济）之间的对比来定义。他说，第一个术语应指“自主的”（自我治理的）经济化，第二个则应指企业规模的“持续有序”的经济化。

Weber defines economy not in isolation, but via a contrast between <a id="page-170-en"></a>〔原书第170页〕*Wirtschaft* (economy) and *Wirtschaftsbetrieb* – literally, enterpriseeconomy. The first term, he says, shall mean an ‘autocephalous’ (self-governing) economisation, whereas the second shall mean an enterprise-scale ‘continuously ordered’ economising.

<a id="ch04-0097"></a>

用于构成复合词*Wirtschaftsbetrieb*的*Betrieb*一词，可以译为“企业”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-101"></a>[101](#note-ch4-101)因此，这一措辞可能暗示自主经济（例如以家庭为基础的经济化）与企业经济之间的区分。然而，这里的“企业”具有误导性，因为它通常指一个离散的经营单位——单个公司或工厂。韦伯明确指出，他的意思指的不是一个单位，而再次是一个过程。事实上，这种更大尺度上经济化的目的，恰恰在于它是一种计算活动——正如我们将看到的——使彼此分离的经济单位和过程得以连接起来。它使跨产品、地点、或关键的时间周期差异来安排和处置经营活动成为可能。这种可计算性使自主形式的经济生活得以转化为一个持久、相互关联、持续有序的过程的组成部分。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-102"></a>[102](#note-ch4-102)

The term *Betrieb*, used to form the compound word *Wirtschaftsbetrieb*, can be translated as ‘enterprise’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-101"></a>[101](#note-ch4-101) So the wording might suggest the distinction between autocephalous economy, such as household-based economisation, and enterprise-based economy. However, ‘enterprise’ here is misleading, as it usually designates a discrete business unit – an individual firm or factory. Weber makes clear that his meaning refers not to a unit but, once again, to a process. In fact, the purpose of economisation at this larger scale is precisely that it is the calculative activity, as we will see, that allows separate economic units and processes to be connected. It enables the arranging and disposing of operations across differences in product, location, or, critically, period of time. Such calculability allows the transformation of self-governing forms of economic life into parts of an enduring, interconnected, continuously ordered process.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-102"></a>[102](#note-ch4-102)

<a id="ch04-0098"></a>

因此，经济化采取两种形式：不连续的（或自主的）与持续相互关联的。为什么用不连续与“持续有序”之间的差异、而不是家庭与企业之间的差异来定义经济概念本身？原因是，对韦伯来说，耐久性和连续性——在空间和*时间*两个维度上的延伸——是由一种特定计算形式的经济化力量促成的，这种计算既可复制，又能不断自我复制。该书对当时资本主义生活的解释就建立在这一差异之上。这种解释把资本化所依赖的*未来可计算性*形式置于经济化的中心。

Economisation, then, takes two forms, discontinuous (or autonomous) versus continuously interconnected. Why define the very concept of economy in terms of the difference not between household and business enterprise, but between the discontinuous and the ‘continuously ordered’? The reason is that, for Weber, durability and continuity – extension in both space and *time* – are made possible by the economising power of a specific form of calculation, one that is both replicable and continuously replicating. The text’s explanation of contemporary capitalist life rests on this difference. It is an explanation that places at the centre of economisation the forms of *calculability of the future* on which capitalisation depends.

<a id="ch04-0099"></a>

韦伯区分了两种经济计算形式：实物核算和货币核算。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-103"></a>[103](#note-ch4-103)简言之，实物核算（*in natura*）比较性质相似但在数量或产出上不同的材料或过程。另一方面，货币核算指一种计算形式，其中完全不同的过程或材料可以通过用共同的记账单位（通常是货币单位）来表示而变得可比。

Weber distinguishes between two forms of economic calculation, accounting in kind and accounting in money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-103"></a>[103](#note-ch4-103) Put simply, accounting in kind, or *in natura*, compares materials or processes that are similar in nature, but differ in quantity or in output. Accounting in money, on the other hand, refers to a form of calculation in which entirely different processes or materials can be made comparable, by expressing all of them in a common unit of account, typically a monetary unit.

<a id="ch04-0100"></a>

两种核算形式之间的区分与资本化未来直接相关。任何规模的企业都可以采用*in natura*核算，通过以其他物品或过程来估算某一物品或过程的成本，从而计算某一过程的成本或盈利能力。例如，<a id="page-171"></a>〔原书第171页〕一台特定类型的机器可以使用能源、劳动和材料的不同组合来生产某种产品。然而，正如韦伯所解释的，要用*in natura*估价来扩大和复制这种计算，很快就会变得笨重难行。如果企业多元化生产另一种产品，就难以跨不同生产过程计算成本和收入；如果它考虑在第二个地点增加一项业务，或希望把当前成本与稍后某一时刻的成本相比较，*以便对未来收入进行贴现*，那就更加困难。这种跨过程、地点、尤其是时间跨度差异的企业扩张，依赖于第二种计算形式，即货币核算。

The distinction between the two forms of accounting relates directly to capitalising the future. Any business at any scale can employ accounting *in natura* to calculate the costs or profitability of a process, by estimating the cost of one item or process in terms of others. For example, <a id="page-171-en"></a>〔原书第171页〕a machine of a given type can produce a certain product using various combinations of energy, labour, and materials. However, as Weber explains, to scale up and replicate such calculations using evaluations *in natura* soon becomes unwieldy. If the firm diversifies into another kind of product, it becomes difficult to calculate cost and income across different production processes, and even more so if it considers adding an operation at a second location or wishes to compare present costs with those at a subsequent moment in time, *for the purpose of discounting future revenue*. Such business expansion across differences in process, location, and, above all, duration of time depends upon the second form of calculation, money accounting.

<a id="ch04-0101"></a>

在把“货币核算”描述为两种经济化模式之一的基础时，韦伯关心的不只是计算盈利能力的某种特定技术，例如复式记账（尽管那可能起作用）。相反，他是在阐述经济化在建造一个持久、面向未来、大规模企业世界中所发挥的具体作用：把差异转化为单一的比较标准，其基础是作为记账单位的货币。换言之，这种经济化是资本化扩张所必需的。这种转化不一定需要实际使用货币支付或市场交易。货币价格可以用来创造交换过程的“虚构”，或确定未来获利的机会。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-104"></a>[104](#note-ch4-104)事实上，它们的主要用处可能在企业内部：企业扩张和跨时间“持续”经济化的机会，包括对未来成本的预测，都依赖于货币核算的使用。当然，这种核算也会延伸到企业之外的交易，并可以为关于是在内部还是从外部供应商获得某种产品或服务的决策提供依据。这种与其他企业或消费者的商业互动，确立并推广了货币核算过程。虽然经济化主要在企业内部组织，但如果没有商业交换的可能性，企业活动的扩张和协调就会失败。这个不断扩展的可计算性网络——其核心是货币核算所促成的未来可计算性——正是韦伯区分“持续有序”的经济化与单纯的自主“经济”时所想到的东西。

In describing ‘accounting in money’ as the basis of one of the two modes of economisation, Weber is not concerned simply with a particular technique for calculating profitability, such as double-entry bookkeeping (although that may play a part). Rather, he is laying out the specific role that economisation plays in building a world of durable, future-oriented, large-scale enterprise: the conversion of difference into a single standard of comparison, based on money as a unit of account. In other words, economisation of this kind is required for the expansion of capitalisation. The conversion does not necessarily require the actual use of monetary payments, or market transactions. The money prices can be deployed to create ‘the fiction’ of exchange processes or to determine the opportunities for future gain.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-104"></a>[104](#note-ch4-104) In fact, their main usefulness may lie within the firm, whose opportunities for expansion and for ‘continuous’ economisation across time, including the projection of future costs, rest on the use of money accounting. Of course, such accounting will also extend to transactions outside the business and can inform decisions about whether to obtain a certain product or service in-house or from an outside vendor. Such commercial interaction with other firms, or with consumers, establishes and generalises the process of monetary accounting. Although economisation is largely organised within business enterprise, without the possibility of commercial exchange the expansion and coordination of business activity would fail. This expanding network of calculability, and centrally the calculability of the future, made possible by money accounting, is what Weber has in mind in distinguishing ‘continuously ordered’ economisation from mere self-governing (autocephalous) ‘economy’.

<a id="ch04-0102"></a>

<a id="page-172"></a>〔原书第172页〕

<a id="page-172-en"></a>〔原书第172页〕

<a id="ch04-0103"></a>

### 没有经济计算就没有经济

### Without Economic Calculation There Is No Economy

<a id="ch04-0104"></a>

为什么韦伯把这种核算过程、而不是市场扩张、劳动剥削、垄断权力的扩散或他叙述中同样出现的其他历史发展，置于其对当时资本主义经济化理解的中心？结果发现，韦伯对核算的兴趣并非源于理解资本主义历史发展的关切，而是源于某种更紧迫之事：资本主义即将灭亡的可能性。

Why does Weber place at the centre of his understanding of contemporary capitalist economisation this process of accounting – rather than, say, the expansion of markets, the exploitation of labour, the spread of monopoly power, or other historical developments that also figure in his account? Weber’s interest in accounting, it turns out, arises not from a concern with understanding the historical development of capitalism, but from something more urgent: the imminent possibility of its demise.

<a id="ch04-0105"></a>

在韦伯写作此书时，社会党正在俄罗斯、德国、巴伐利亚共和国、奥地利和欧洲其他地区掌权或威胁掌权。在韦伯看来，国家或共同体接管工业和金融的所有权与管理，其问题不仅在于取消产权、废除市场或消除竞争。问题在于瓦解以货币核算为基础的协调机制，即允许扩展的、持续的、不断扩张的经济化——因而也是资本化——的计算原则。在社会主义“计划经济”下，关于资源的集中决策取代了商业交换，经济化过程无法产生一套价格。这种价格可能来自交换，但也可能来自卡特尔安排、劳动协议、企业内部核算或其他来源。消失的不只是“市场”，而是整个“有效”价格的过程——无论它们如何产生——大企业正是通过这一过程配置资源、持续扩张并计算和贴现未来收入。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-105"></a>[105](#note-ch4-105)

As Weber was writing his text, socialist parties were coming to power, or threatening to do so, in Russia, Germany, the Bavarian Republic, Austria, and other parts of Europe. As Weber saw it, the problem with the state or community taking over the ownership and management of industry and finance lay not simply in the elimination of property rights, the abolition of markets, or the removal of competition. It lay in undoing the coordination mechanism based on money accounting, the principle of calculation that allows extended, continuous, and expanding economisation – and thus capitalisation. Under socialist ‘planned economy’, where centralised decisions about resources replace commercial exchange, the process of economisation fails to generate a set of prices. Such prices may arise from exchange, but also from cartel arrangements, labour agreements, internal business accounting, or other sources. What disappears is not simply ‘the market’, but the entire process of ‘effective’ prices, however they arise, through which large enterprises allocate resources, continuously expand, and calculate and discount future revenue.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-105"></a>[105](#note-ch4-105)

<a id="ch04-0106"></a>

韦伯发展*in natura*计算与货币核算之间的区分，不仅是为了理解资本主义的生活形式，而且是为了论证大规模“计划经济”在技术上的不可能性。结果，该书的大部分内容归结为仅仅两种经济化模式之间的对比：“计划经济”与“货币经济”。在作出这一对比时，经济一词开始失去其与计算方法的联系——计算方法可以发生在多个尺度上——并似乎指把经济过程的整体作为自身对象来把握的一种方式。为了证明社会主义项目的不可能性——该项目旨在把经济化作为一个整体来治理——韦伯无意中促成了把这一整体当作一个对象来思考的可能性。

Weber develops the distinction between calculation *in natura* and money accounting not just to understand capitalist forms of life, but to argue for the technical impossibility of large-scale ‘planned economy’. As a result, much of the text resolves into a contrast between just two modes of economisation, ‘planned economy’ and ‘money economy’. In making this contrast, the term economy begins to lose its association with calculative methods, which can occur at multiple scales, and appears to designate a way of grasping the totality of economic processes as an object in itself. To demonstrate the impossibility of the socialist project, which aims to govern economisation as a whole, Weber has inadvertently contributed to the possibility of thinking of that whole as an object.

<a id="ch04-0107"></a>

因此，韦伯偏爱研究过程而不是结构，可以看作不仅是方法论上的选择。它记录了其写作所处的政治<a id="page-173"></a>〔原书第173页〕语境。中央经济计划提出了如何把握经济生活之整体的问题，这既是经济计划者的问题，因而也是社会经济解释的问题。韦伯的答案是，它只能作为一个分散但相互关联的过程的结果来把握。然而，在韦伯著作之后的岁月里，由于一种根本不同的集体生活治理方式即社会主义的出现，计划经济和货币经济将被解读为治理共同对象的两种模式：“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）。

Thus, Weber’s preference for the study of processes rather than structures can be seen as not merely methodological. It registers the political <a id="page-173-en"></a>〔原书第173页〕context in which he is writing. Central economic planning presents the problem of how the entirety of economic life can be grasped, both by economic planners and, as a consequence, by social-economic explanation. Weber’s answer is that it can be grasped only as the outcome of a dispersed, but interconnected, process. However, in the years after Weber’s work, thanks to the appearance of a fundamentally different mode of governing collective life, in socialism, planned economy and money economy will come to be read as two modes of governing a common object: *the* economy.

<a id="ch04-0108"></a>

韦伯今天被认为是二十世纪或许最有影响的经济生活社会理论家。但他的影响并非来自他关于经济的著作，而是来自他反对这一观念的努力。他于 1920 年 6 月去世。与此同时，在战后的维也纳，一群被称为米塞斯圈子的知识分子——他们与韦伯有联系并受其影响——已经开始发展关于经济计算的类似论点。这些论点后来成为被称为新自由主义的智识运动的核心（我们将在[第六章](#ch06-0001)讨论这一运动后来的重要性）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-106"></a>[106](#note-ch4-106)路德维希·冯·米塞斯的文章《社会主义共同体中的经济计算》（1920）在韦伯自己的著作仍在校对时引起了他的注意。韦伯此后不久去世，当时他的出版商正在排版*《经济与社会》*的第一部分。该书的其他部分后来根据韦伯较早著作的草稿汇编而成，形成一部笨重、不连贯、艰深的巨著。然而，由于米塞斯圈子，这本书从相对默默无闻中被抢救出来，最终得以出版英译本。这项抢救工作始于十五年之后，是当时以英语世界为中心、反对“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）作为对象出现的新一轮努力的一部分。

Weber is known today as perhaps the most influential twentieth-century social theorist of economic life. But he owes his influence not to his writings on the economy, but to his efforts to oppose the idea. He died in June 1920. Meanwhile, in postwar Vienna, the group of intellectuals known as the Mises Circle, who were associated with and influenced by Weber, had begun developing similar arguments about economic calculation. The arguments were to become the core of the intellectual movement later named neoliberalism (a movement to whose later significance we will turn in [chapter 6](#ch06-0001)).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-106"></a>[106](#note-ch4-106) An essay by Ludwig von Mises, ‘Economic Calculation in the Socialist Commonwealth’ (1920), came to Weber’s attention while his own work was in proof. Weber died shortly thereafter, just as his publisher was typesetting part one of *Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft*. The other parts of the book were assembled later from drafts of Weber’s earlier writings, creating an unwieldy, disconnected, and difficult tome. Thanks to the Mises Circle, however, the book was rescued from relative obscurity and eventually made available in English. Begun a decade and a half later, the rescuing was part of a renewed effort, now centred in the English-speaking world, to oppose the emergence of *the* economy as an object.

<a id="ch04-0109"></a>

1935 年，米塞斯圈子成员、新兴新自由主义运动的关键人物弗里德里希·哈耶克出版了米塞斯那篇关于经济计算文章的英文译本。他将其收入一本旨在提醒英语读者注意反对经济计划可行性的论点的文集，此时这种计划即使在英国和美国也正成为一种威胁。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-107"></a>[107](#note-ch4-107)在该书导言中，哈耶克把韦伯与米塞斯并列为最早发展这一论点的人。

In 1935, Friedrich Hayek, a member of the Mises Circle and lynchpin of the emerging neoliberal movement, published an English translation of the Mises essay on economic calculation. He included it in a collection intended to alert English readers to the argument against the feasibility of economic planning, which was now emerging as a threat even in Britain and the United States.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-107"></a>[107](#note-ch4-107) In his introduction to the book, Hayek names Weber alongside Mises as those who had first developed this argument.

<a id="ch04-0110"></a>

然而，哈耶克本人不再以旧方式使用“经济”一词。对米塞斯和对韦伯来说一样，经济是一个计算过程。事实上，对米塞斯而言，社会主义下货币核算的消除标志着经济本身的缺席：“Ohne Wirtschaftsrechnung keine <a id="page-174"></a>〔原书第174页〕Wirtschaft”，他写道（没有经济计算就没有经济）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-108"></a>[108](#note-ch4-108)十五年后，哈耶克在新的政治语境中向英语读者介绍这篇文章时，颠倒了这个词的用法。

Hayek himself, however, no longer used ‘economy’ in the old way. For Mises, as for Weber, economy was a process of calculation. Indeed, the elimination of money accounting under socialism signalled for Mises the very absence of economy: ‘Ohne Wirtschaftsrechnung keine <a id="page-174-en"></a>〔原书第174页〕Wirtschaft’, he wrote (without economic calculation there is no economy).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-108"></a>[108](#note-ch4-108) Introducing this essay to English readers fifteen years later, in a new political context, Hayek reverses the use of the word.

<a id="ch04-0111"></a>

在总结反对计划的论点时，他只是把“经济”用作贬义词，指当时作为两次世界大战之间危机四伏的资本主义替代方案而出现的凯恩斯主义或新政方案。他在“计划经济”“中央指导的经济”或干脆“社会主义经济”等短语中使用这个词。为了描述其对立面，即一种由个人或企业自利计算支配的生活方式，他一次也没有使用经济一词，而宁愿使用“自由社会的制度”“基于交换的体系”或“纯粹竞争的社会”等短语。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-109"></a>[109](#note-ch4-109)四十年后，哈耶克仍反对使用“经济”一词，转而提出“交换秩序”（catallaxy）一词（经由米塞斯从上面提到的理查德·惠特利 1831 年牛津讲座中借用）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-110"></a>[110](#note-ch4-110)然而到那时，正如我们将在[第六章](#ch06-0001)看到的，哈耶克的追随者正用更简单的抽象取代“自由社会的制度”等短语，这一抽象后来作为经济观念的替代品被广泛采用：“市场”。然而，即使在 1930 年代，对哈耶克来说，“经济”如今所指的整体也只是集中计划的不可能对象，是“资本主义社会”的对立面。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-111"></a>[111](#note-ch4-111)

In summarising the argument against planning, he uses ‘economy’ only as a negative term, to designate what was now emerging as a Keynesian or New Deal alternative to the crisis-ridden capitalism of the interwar period. He employs the word in phrases such as ‘a planned economy’, ‘a centrally directed economy’, or simply ‘a socialist economy’. To describe its opposite, a mode of life governed by the calculation of individual or corporate self-interest, he never once uses the term economy, preferring phrases such as ‘the institutions of a free society’, ‘a system based on exchange’, or a ‘purely competitive society’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-109"></a>[109](#note-ch4-109) Four decades later, Hayek was still objecting to the use of the term ‘economy’, proposing instead the word ‘catallaxy’ (borrowed – through Mises – from Richard Whately’s Oxford lectures of 1831, mentioned above).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-110"></a>[110](#note-ch4-110) By then, however, as we will see in [chapter 6](#ch06-0001), Hayek’s followers were replacing phrases like ‘the institutions of a free society’ with a simpler abstraction, later to be widely adopted as an alternative to the idea of the economy: ‘the market’. Even in the 1930s, however, for Hayek the totality to which ‘the economy’ now referred designated only the impossible object of centralised planning, the antithesis of ‘a capitalistic society’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-111"></a>[111](#note-ch4-111)

<a id="ch04-0112"></a>

大约同一时期，正如特赖布告诉我们的，哈耶克帮助招募了一位年轻的苏格兰经济学家，开始把韦伯*《经济与社会》*的第一部分译成英文。这项翻译工作后来由美国社会学家塔尔科特·帕森斯（阿尔弗雷德·钱德勒的老师）接手并重新加工。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-112"></a>[112](#note-ch4-112)由于战争而推迟，译本直到 1947 年才问世。到那时，正如我们将在下一章看到的，经济已经成为一个对象，而且在帕森斯手中确实成为一个“系统”。韦伯对这个词的定义——“经济应指……经济化”——如今被相应改写为：帕森斯在其误译中让韦伯说，一个“经济*系统*”（*Wirtschaft*）是一个“经济行动的*系统*”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-113"></a>[113](#note-ch4-113)“系统”一词在韦伯文本中从未出现。原文也不含不定冠词 an（“一个”），而英文译本中的这个冠词起着把作为过程的经济转化为作为对象的经济的作用。二十年后，韦伯文本的修订英译本出版。这个版本删去了“系统”一词，但保留了不定冠词。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-114"></a>[114](#note-ch4-114)到 1960 年代，“一个经济”这一概念本身已经指帕森斯试图指认的结构性系统。

Around the same time, as Tribe tells us, Hayek helped recruit a young Scottish economist to start translating part one of Weber’s *Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft* into English. The translation was taken over and reworked by the American sociologist Talcott Parsons (the teacher of Alfred Chandler).<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-112"></a>[112](#note-ch4-112) Delayed by the war, it appeared only in 1947. By then, as we will see in the next chapter, economy had become an object, and indeed in the hands of Parsons, ‘a system’. Weber’s definition of the term – ‘economy shall mean . . . economisation’ – was now rewritten accordingly: ‘An “economic *system”* (*Wirtschaft*)’, Parsons makes Weber say in his mistranslation of the text, is a ‘*system* of economic action’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-113"></a>[113](#note-ch4-113) The word ‘system’ occurs nowhere in Weber’s text. Nor does the original contain the indefinite article ‘an’, which in the English translation operates to transform economy as process into economy as an object. Twenty years later, a revised English translation of Weber’s text was published. This version removed the word ‘system’, while retaining the indefinite article.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-114"></a>[114](#note-ch4-114) By the 1960s the concept of ‘an economy’ signified by itself the structural system that Parsons had tried to identify.

<a id="ch04-0113"></a>

基思·特赖布对*《经济与社会》*的重译，使我们能够把书名中的两个关键术语读作社会化和经济化：也就是说，读作<a id="page-175"></a>〔原书第175页〕过程，而不是对象。但它也使我们能够在文本本身中读出，韦伯对其时代政治的紧迫智识回应，如何促成了那些使经济不再被理解为经济化的发展。

Keith Tribe’s retranslation of *Economy and Society* allows us to read the two key terms of its title as sociation and economisation: that is, as <a id="page-175-en"></a>〔原书第175页〕processes, not objects. But it also allows us to read, in the text itself, the way Weber’s urgent intellectual response to the politics of his times contributed to the developments through which economy would no longer be understood as economisation.

<a id="ch04-0114"></a>

关注韦伯对经济一词的使用，使我们能够恢复“这个经济整体”（the economy）被发明之前思考经济的一种方式。这不仅是一个历史兴趣问题。在过去二十年里，一些关于如何思考经济的最重要著作建议我们用经济化概念取代经济一词。这个概念可以用来指使过程和材料成为经济的安排、计算、定性和推理。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch4-115"></a>[115](#note-ch4-115)这个术语使我们认识到，“这个经济整体”不是人类社会生活的普遍领域，而是特定计算、装置和行动的产物。这引起人们对本章所探讨问题的注意，而这个问题被我们日常使用经济一词所掩盖：为了资本化过程，必须持续进行学术和实践工作，使事物成为经济的；这种工作总是不完整的，并容易受到扰乱。

Paying attention to Weber’s use of the term economy enables us to recover a way of thinking about economy before the invention of ‘the economy’. This is not only a matter of historical interest. Over the last two decades, some of the most important writing addressing how to think about the economic has proposed that we replace the term economy with the concept of economisation. The concept can be used to denote the arranging, calculating, qualifying, and reasoning through which processes and materials are rendered economic.<a id="ref-en-note-ch4-115"></a>[115](#note-ch4-115) The term brings into view the realisation that ‘the economy’ is not a universal realm of human social life but the product of particular calculations, devices, and actions. This draws attention to the issue explored in this chapter, obscured by our everyday use of the word economy: the continuous academic and practical work that must be done, in service of the process of capitalisation, always incomplete and open to disruption, to render things economic.


# 第五章　经济治理术：未来如何进入治理

<a id="ch05-0001"></a>

<a id="page-176"></a>〔原书第176页〕

<a id="page-176-en"></a>〔原书第176页〕

<a id="ch05-0002"></a>

## 第五章　经济治理术：未来如何进入治理

## 5 Economentality: How the Future Entered Government

<a id="ch05-0003"></a>

1947 年，一位名叫阿德里亚诺·达尼诺斯的埃及企业家在开罗一份科学期刊上发表提案，建议在尼罗河上修建一座新水坝。新坝位于五十年前英国人在阿斯旺修建的较小砌石拦河堰上游——本书开头几章曾讨论过后者——这座新的堆石结构将极其巨大，其形成的水库将向南延伸五百多公里。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-001"></a>[1](#note-ch5-001)“达尼诺斯是一个身负使命的人，”华盛顿世界银行的一位官员在达尼诺斯后来前往推销其计划时报告说。这位官员指出，该计划不仅涉及建坝，还涉及“与之相关的土地开垦和灌溉、发电，以及建设工厂，利用电力进行采矿、制造肥料、其他制造业，可能还有钢铁生产”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-002"></a>[2](#note-ch5-002)在发表计划之前，达尼诺斯曾参观美国田纳西河流域管理局，以及法国西南部利穆赞地区类似的综合水电、河流控制、灌溉和工业化项目。这些重新组织自然力量、农业系统、能源流动、劳动力能力和物质生产的庞大计划，被称为“总体开发”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-003"></a>[3](#note-ch5-003)

In 1947, an Egyptian entrepreneur named Adriano Daninos published a proposal in a scientific journal in Cairo to build a new dam across the Nile. Placed upstream of the smaller masonry barrage built fifty years earlier by the British at Aswan, discussed in the opening chapters of this book, the new rock-filled structure would be so large that the reservoir it created would stretch more than 500 kilometres to the south.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-001"></a>[1](#note-ch5-001) ‘Daninos is a man with a mission’, reported an official at the World Bank in Washington, where he later went to pitch his plan. The official noted that the scheme concerned not just building the dam but ‘land reclamation and irrigation connected therewith, production of power, and construction of plants to use that power in mining, making fertilizers, other manufacturing, and possibly iron and steel’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-002"></a>[2](#note-ch5-002) Before publishing his plan, Daninos had visited the Tennessee Valley Authority in the United States and similar integrated hydro-electric, river control, irrigation, and industrialisation projects in the Limousin in southwest France. These gargantuan schemes for reorganising forces of nature, systems of agriculture, flows of energy, powers of labour, and material production were known as ‘total development’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-003"></a>[3](#note-ch5-003)

<a id="ch05-0004"></a>

尽管项目规模巨大，达尼诺斯并没有向世界银行要钱。他只寻求帮助协调美国和欧洲工程公司的参与。资金将来自伦敦或巴黎——或者来自埃及政府在战争期间于英格兰银行积累的大额英镑债权余额，或者来自英法所有的苏伊士运河公司；该公司在水坝建成后不久就应归还埃及所有。随着战后经苏伊士运河运输的石油增长，<a id="page-177"></a>〔原书第177页〕该公司的收入和利润正在激增。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-004"></a>[4](#note-ch5-004)正如苏伊士运河公司的一位董事私下向世界银行官员指出的，航运公司未来支付的运河通行费可以覆盖偿还建设贷款的成本。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-005"></a>[5](#note-ch5-005)这座水坝是把战时债务和战后石油收入——预期中的石油繁荣将带来这些收入——加以资本化的手段。

Despite the scale of the venture, Daninos was not asking the World Bank for money. He merely sought help coordinating the involvement of US and European engineering firms. The capital would come from London or Paris – either from the large credits in sterling built up by the Egyptian government at the Bank of England during the war or from the Anglo-French-owned Suez Canal Company, which was due to revert to Egyptian ownership soon after the building of the dam. The <a id="page-177-en"></a>〔原书第177页〕company’s income and profits were surging with the postwar growth of oil shipments through the Canal.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-004"></a>[4](#note-ch5-004) As a director of the Suez Canal Company pointed out in private to officials at the World Bank, the future canal tolls paid by shipping companies could cover the cost of repaying the construction loans.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-005"></a>[5](#note-ch5-005) The dam was a means of capitalising the wartime debts and postwar oil revenues that the prospective petroleum boom would bring.

<a id="ch05-0005"></a>

但世界银行不愿只扮演边缘角色。它被排除在欧洲战后重建之外，急于把自己重新塑造为向全球南方国家提供经济建议和推销华尔街贷款的渠道。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-006"></a>[6](#note-ch5-006)因此它主动提出协调政府和私人对水坝的融资。世界银行的参与并没有使该项目变得更便宜。相反，欧洲工程公司曾估计水坝成本约为 2 亿英镑，但当世界银行完成计算后，估计数字增加了一倍多，达到 5 亿英镑。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-007"></a>[7](#note-ch5-007)世界银行在方案中加上了开挖灌溉运河的成本，这些运河将使埃及农民能够减少快速生长的粮食作物，扩大生长较慢的工业作物——棉花和甘蔗——的种植面积，而这些工业作物是偿还世行将在华尔街发行的债券所必需的。但世界银行还添加了别的东西：一整套关于未来的新计算。表述这种被计算的未来的新颖方式，就是把它称为“经济”（the economy）。

But the Bank was unwilling to play only a marginal role. Excluded from postwar reconstruction in Europe, it was keen to reinvent itself as the conduit for the supply of economic advice and the selling of Wall Street loans to countries of the South.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-006"></a>[6](#note-ch5-006) So it put itself forward to coordinate government and private financing of the dam. The Bank’s involvement did not make the project any cheaper. On the contrary, European engineering firms had estimated the cost of the dam at about £200 million sterling, but when the Bank finished its calculations the estimate had more than doubled, to £500 million.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-007"></a>[7](#note-ch5-007) The Bank had added to the scheme the cost of digging irrigation canals that would allow Egyptian farmers to replace fast-growing food crops with more hectares of the slower-growing industrial crops – cotton and sugar cane – needed to pay off the bonds the Bank would raise on Wall Street. But the Bank had added something more: a new set of calculations about the future. The novel way to represent this calculated future was to refer to it as ‘the economy’.

<a id="ch05-0006"></a>

### 错置的确定性

### Misplaced Definiteness

<a id="ch05-0007"></a>

大约在 1948 年，谈论经济在美国政治辩论中变得普遍。政府和报纸对这个对象的提及开始以例行、重复的方式出现，使经济第一次显得像一件既成事实。人们不再总是需要解释这个词的含义，或以某种方式对它加以限定。

Around 1948, it became common in American political debate to talk about the economy. References to this object in government and newspapers were starting to appear in a routine, repetitive way that made the economy appear for the first time as a matter of fact. It was no longer always necessary to explain what the term meant or to qualify it in some way.

<a id="ch05-0008"></a>

“经济整体”（the economy）这一观念本身已经存在了至少十多年。但在第二次世界大战之前的时期，这个词仍常常带有上一章所探讨的较早含义的余韵，当时“经济”描述的是一种过程，而不是一个事物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-008"></a>[8](#note-ch5-008)在日常用法中，这个词仍指经济化的行为，或审慎使用有限资源的行为。例如，1933 年美国《节约法》（Economy Act）不是规制经济整体的法律。它是一项实行节约、<a id="page-178"></a>〔原书第178页〕节省开支的法案，旨在通过削减政府工作人员薪资来减少联邦赤字。在更广泛的意义上，正如我们所见，经济一词常常指治理模式本身。如同较早的“政治经济学”短语，它仍指与有效管理人的生活和物质资源有关的行政形式和技术知识。即使在 1930 年代后期，随着这个词的新含义出现，这种较早的治理含义通常仍然存在。这个词频繁出现在报纸讨论中，话题包括计划经济与市场经济、日本的战争经济，以及德国控制经济的实验。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-009"></a>[9](#note-ch5-009)

The idea of ‘the economy’ itself had been around for at least a dozen years. But in the period before the Second World War the word still often carried echoes of the older sense explored in the previous chapter, when ‘economy’ described a process, not a thing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-008"></a>[8](#note-ch5-008) In everyday usage, the term still referred to the act of economising, or making prudent use of limited resources. The US Economy Act of 1933, for example, was not a law to regulate the economy. It was an act of economy, or <a id="page-178-en"></a>〔原书第178页〕economising, intended to cut the federal deficit by reducing the pay of government workers. In a wider sense, as we saw, the word economy had often meant modes of government itself. As in the older phrase ‘political economy’, it still referred to forms of administration and know-how concerned with the efficient management of human lives and material resources. Even in the late 1930s, as a new meaning of the term emerged, this older sense of governing was usually still present. The word occurred frequently in newspaper discussion of topics such as planned economy versus market economy, the war economy in Japan, and the German experiment in controlled economy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-009"></a>[9](#note-ch5-009)

<a id="ch05-0009"></a>

在战前几年，这个词的新含义偶尔明确出现，指作为一个独特空间或对象的“*这个*经济整体”（the economy）。1938 年 1 月，*《纽约时报》*报道了社会研究新学院两位经济学家出版的一部专著。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-010"></a>[10](#note-ch5-010)该研究使用罗斯福新政所得税的新数据，主张对较富裕者征税造成了“美国经济中”投资资本的稀缺。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-011"></a>[11](#note-ch5-011)正如*《纽约时报》*所指出的，作者们“属于这样一个经济思想学派：它把政府干预经济视为现代危机政策的必要既定条件，英国的约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯是该学派的一位著名代言人”，这或许并非巧合。同样重要的是，新政的各项税收法案通过纳税申报表，使大量公民成为数据的生产者，从而使讨论“经济”成为可能。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-012"></a>[12](#note-ch5-012)雷曼兄弟为这两位经济学家提供了资金，让他们聘请一个统计学家团队，从纳税申报表中转录数字，并将其转化为对经济的衡量。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-013"></a>[13](#note-ch5-013)

Occasionally, in the years before the war, the new meaning of the term appeared explicitly, referring to *the* economy, as a distinct space or object. In January 1938, the *New York Times* reported on a monograph published by two economists at the New School for Social Research.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-010"></a>[10](#note-ch5-010) Using data from the new Roosevelt income taxes, the study argued that taxing the better-off had created a scarcity of investment capital ‘in the American economy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-011"></a>[11](#note-ch5-011) It was perhaps no coincidence that the authors were, as the *New York Times* noted, ‘members of the school of economic thought that holds governmental intervention in the economy to be a necessary datum of modern crisis policy, of which John Maynard Keynes of England is a prominent spokesman’. Equally significant was the fact that the revenue acts of the New Deal had turned a large number of citizens, through their tax returns, into producers of the data that made it possible to discuss ‘the economy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-012"></a>[12](#note-ch5-012) Lehman Brothers had provided funds for the two economists to hire a team of statisticians to transcribe figures from the tax returns and translate them into measurements of the economy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-013"></a>[13](#note-ch5-013)

<a id="ch05-0010"></a>

尽管对一家关注所得税减少投资之证据的银行来说，这种计算很有用，但它使许多经济学家感到警觉。一位书评人报告说，这本书有“严重缺陷”，尤其是其“错置的确定性”，以及“在未向读者充分警示的情况下使用高度试探性的储蓄统计数据”。“鉴于这些缺陷，”评论总结道，“希望这本书不会得到广泛追捧，尽管若无这些缺陷，凭其吸引人的形式、清晰的文风和作者显而易见的才干与诚实，它本应获得这样的反响。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-014"></a>[14](#note-ch5-014)评论作者阿尔伯特·盖洛德·哈特是凯恩斯思想的皈依者，但正在研究不确定性。

Although useful to a bank interested in the evidence that income taxes reduced investment, this kind of calculation alarmed many economists. One reviewer reported that the book had ‘grave defects’, in particular its ‘misplaced definiteness’ and its use of ‘highly tentative savings statistics without adequate warnings to the reader’. ‘In view of these defects’, the review concluded, ‘it is to be hoped that the book will not have the popular following which its attractive form and lucid style and the manifest competence and honesty of its authors would otherwise deserve.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-014"></a>[14](#note-ch5-014) The review’s author, Albert Gailord Hart, was a convert to Keynes’s ideas but was working on a study of uncertainty.

<a id="ch05-0011"></a>

这种“错置的确定性”不受学术经济学家欢迎，却找到了更有效的塑造舆论方式。次年，即 1939 年，美国预算局从<a id="page-179"></a>〔原书第179页〕商务部转移到新设立的总统行政办公室。那本“有缺陷”书的主要作者格哈德·科尔姆被任命为预算局新设财政处首席经济学家。在那里，他把统计学家西蒙·库兹涅茨设计的国民收入账户估算新方法引入联邦预算编制。战后，科尔姆加入杜鲁门总统新设的经济顾问委员会。在委员会，他把用于联邦预算的核算方法转用于估算所谓的“国家经济预算”。在委员会旨在教育总统和公众进行经济预测和计算的年度报告中，格式化经济的工作继续进行。经济的“错置的确定性”获得了范围更广的界定。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-015"></a>[15](#note-ch5-015)

Unpopular with academic economists, this kind of ‘misplaced definiteness’ found a more effective way to shape opinion. The following year, in 1939, the US Bureau of the Budget was moved from the <a id="page-179-en"></a>〔原书第179页〕Commerce Department to the new Executive Office of the President. The lead author of the ‘defective’ book, Gerhard Colm, was appointed as a chief economist in the Bureau’s new Fiscal Division. There, he introduced into federal budget making the novel methods of estimating national income accounts devised by the statistician Simon Kuznets. After the war, Colm joined the staff of President Truman’s new Council of Economic Advisers. At the Council, he transferred the accounting methods used for the federal budget to the estimating of something called ‘the nation’s economic budget’. In the annual reports of the Council, intended to educate the president and the public in economic forecasting and calculation, the work of formatting the economy proceeded. The ‘misplaced definiteness’ of the economy acquired a larger definition.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-015"></a>[15](#note-ch5-015)

校注：底本称预算局1939年从商务部转入总统行政办公室。美国财政部的机构史说明，预算局1921年设于财政部，1939年转入总统行政办公室；原文部门名有误，正文照录。 https://home.treasury.gov/about/history/history-overview/history-of-the-treasury

<a id="ch05-0012"></a>

在国民收入核算被引入联邦预算计算十年后，提及“经济”变得越来越平常。我们应如何理解这种指称集体生活的新方式的出现？经济是一个新对象，还是已经存在之物的旧名称？正如我们在上一章所见，两种选择都不令人满意。

A decade after the introduction of national income accounting into the calculations of the federal budget, it was becoming more commonplace to refer to ‘the economy’. How should we understand the emergence of this new way of referring to collective life? Was the economy a new object, or just an old name for things that already existed? As we saw in the previous chapter, neither option is satisfactory.

<a id="ch05-0013"></a>

我们可以说明经济如何显得是一个新对象：一个由价格总水平、工资、消费者支出、货币供应、购买力和储蓄组成的事物，由于新的商业程序、银行报告、家庭纳税申报表和其他核算形式，所有这些如今都可以估算。但经济不仅仅是一组总量。这些账户可以用来把集体世界划分为一系列单位：企业、家庭和政府部门。这些核算单位之间的货币互动可以被估算，估算值随后可以被调整，使一个账户的增加等于另一个账户的减少。账户不必只估算年度增减，还可以细分为月度报告，使资金在单位之间的流动可以被描绘为一个动态过程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-016"></a>[16](#note-ch5-016)这些逐单位、逐月的流动，如今不仅表现为总量，而且表现为一个相互作用体系的各个部分。

We can show how the economy appeared to be a new object: a thing made up of aggregate price levels, wages, consumer spending, money supply, purchasing power, and savings, all of which could now be estimated, thanks to new business procedures, banking reports, household tax returns, and other forms of accounting. But the economy was more than just a set of aggregates. These accounts could be used to divide the collective world into a series of units: firms, households, and government departments. The monetary interactions among these accounting units could be estimated and the estimates then adjusted, so that additions to one account equalled the subtractions from another. Instead of attempting to estimate only annual additions and subtractions, the accounts could be broken down into monthly reports, so that the movement of funds between units could be depicted as a dynamic process.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-016"></a>[16](#note-ch5-016) These movements, from unit to unit, month by month, now appeared not just as aggregates but as parts of an interacting system.

<a id="ch05-0014"></a>

使这个体系可见和可衡量的核算程序不仅仅是再现形式。它们是向民众征收财政收入、管理国家财政、营销和消费商品以及谋生的新方式。经济不仅提供了政府政策的新对象，就像政府也曾经关注公共<a id="page-180"></a>〔原书第180页〕卫生、城市更新或社会福利那样。经济提供了一种更普遍的效果，这种效果此后一直未受注意：一种*把未来带入治理*的方式。

The accounting procedures that made this system visible and measurable were more than just forms of representation. They were new ways of raising revenue from a population, managing national finance, marketing and consuming goods, and earning livings. The economy provided not just a new object of government policy, in the way that governments had also become concerned with, for example, public <a id="page-180-en"></a>〔原书第180页〕health, or urban renewal, or social welfare. The economy provided a more pervasive effect, one that has since then escaped attention: a way to *bring the future into government*.

<a id="ch05-0015"></a>

经济的制造确立了一种新的时间图式，过去、现在和未来在其中被重新定位。我们可以把这一转变作为一种新的预测结构来研究：在这种结构中，未来被动员为裁断和管理当下索取权的一种方式，并在一段危机时期之后，为资本化的目的而被稳定下来。

The making of the economy established a new temporal scheme in which past, present, and future were relocated. We can study this shift as a new prognostic structure, one in which the future was mobilised as a mode of adjudicating and managing claims in the present, and stabilised – after a period of crisis – for the purposes of capitalisation.

<a id="ch05-0016"></a>

正如我们在上一章结尾简要指出的，两次世界大战之间时期在资本化过程中造成了深刻危机。第一次世界大战、社会主义政府上台、1929 年股灾、随后的大萧条以及法西斯主义和总体战争的兴起，不仅对最近被称为“资本主义”的体系构成深刻挫折，更具体地说，也对资本化过程所依赖的那种稳定、可预测的未来感构成深刻挫折。这也是作为同一过程一部分而出现的帝国主义秩序的危机时代，在中东尤为严重。第一次世界大战后奥斯曼帝国崩溃，英国和法国试图通过保护国和委任统治制度控制从埃及到伊拉克的整个地区，但在很大程度上失败了。最大的失败在巴勒斯坦，1936—9 年大起义——巴勒斯坦人反对英国对巴勒斯坦的占领及其推动的犹太复国主义殖民——需要十万英军才能暴力镇压。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-017"></a>[17](#note-ch5-017)我们将在下文回到这场暴力在巴勒斯坦和该地区其他地方造成的后果，把它与经济制造以及发现“经济”似乎许诺的、通过战后“发展”方案实现的未来联系起来。与此同时，本章旨在把发展的诞生——中东是其首要试验场——与新兴帝国中心美国政治中平行的未来生产联系起来。

As we noted briefly at the end of the previous chapter, the interwar period produced a deep crisis in the processes of capitalisation. The Great War, the coming to power of socialist governments, the Crash of 1929, the Great Depression that followed, and the rise of fascism and total war marked profound setbacks not only for the system that had recently come to be known as ‘capitalism’, but more specifically for the sense of a stable, predictable future on which the capitalising process depended. This was also an era of crisis in the order of imperialism that had emerged as part of the same process, nowhere more than in the Middle East. Following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire after the First World War, Britain and France had attempted to control the entire region from Egypt to Iraq through a system of protectorates and mandates, and largely failed. The greatest failure was in Palestine, where the Great Revolt of 1936–9, the Palestinian uprising against Britain’s occupation of the country and the Zionist colonisation it promoted, required 100,000 British troops for its violent suppression.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-017"></a>[17](#note-ch5-017) We will return below to the aftermath of this violence, in Palestine and other parts of the region, to connect it to the making of the economy and the kinds of future, through schemes of postwar ‘development’, that the discovery of ‘the economy’ appeared to promise. At the same time, this chapter aims to connect the birth of development, for which the Middle East formed a prime testing ground, with a parallel production of the future in the politics of the emergent imperial centre, the United States.

<a id="ch05-0017"></a>

通过未来新形式所想象的当下治理，将在一种新的时间变化度量即“增长”的衡量中运作。这种度量可以追溯到新的经济计算方法。然而，确立衡量过程不仅涉及设计计算技术。它还需要确保和稳定若干支持这种新计量学的场所。本章通过追溯对资本化工作日益关键的一个方面来说明这是如何发生的：<a id="page-181"></a>〔原书第181页〕能源供应的流动和监管。

The government of the present, as it was imagined through new forms of the future, would come to operate within a new metric of temporal change, the measurement of ‘growth’. This metric can be traced in novel methods of economic calculation. However, establishing the process of measurement involved more than just devising calculative techniques. It required securing and stabilising a number of sites that would support the new metrology. This chapter illustrates how this happened by tracing one aspect of the process that was <a id="page-181-en"></a>〔原书第181页〕increasingly vital to the work of capitalisation: the flow and regulation of energy supplies.

<a id="ch05-0018"></a>

### 1948 年：民主的基础设施

### 1948: An Infrastructure of Democracy

<a id="ch05-0019"></a>

有时人们认为，现代以化石燃料为基础的新能源体制，使工业化社会中可获得的能源数量呈指数增长，是时间突然加速和未来不可预测性的重要来源。虽然能源消费、尤其是石油消费从二十世纪中叶前后迅速攀升，但这种消费矛盾地促成了一个时代，在其中未来一度成为治理人口的稳定工具的一部分。

It is sometimes argued that the new energy regime of the modern era, based on fossil fuels, which allowed the quantity of energy available in industrialising societies to increase exponentially, was an important source of the sudden acceleration of time and the unpredictability of futures. While the consumption of energy, in particular from oil, climbed rapidly from around the middle of the twentieth century, this consumption, paradoxically, contributed to an era in which the future became, for a while, part of a stable instrument for governing populations.

<a id="ch05-0020"></a>

据说现代的权力通过我们有时称为治理术的理性形式、计算模式和控制策略来运作：以人口为对象、通过改善其健康、财富和福祉来治理的权力方法。米歇尔·福柯认为，这些方法的传播导致“国家的治理化”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-018"></a>[18](#note-ch5-018)如果二十世纪中叶出现的新政治理性形式和计算实践把经济构成为其对象，并把未来引入治理，或许我们可以把这种治理术称为“经济治理术”（economentality）。

Power in the modern era is said to work through forms of reason, modes of calculation, and tactics of control that we sometimes refer to as governmentality: methods of power that take the population as their object and govern through the improvement of its health, wealth, and well-being. Michel Foucault argued that the spread of these methods leads to the ‘the governmentalization of the state’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-018"></a>[18](#note-ch5-018) If new forms of political reason and calculative practice emerging in the mid-twentieth century formed the economy as their object and introduced the future into government, perhaps we can refer to this mode of governmentality as ‘economentality’.

<a id="ch05-0021"></a>

经济治理术依托于我们在上一章称为“经济化”的那些过程：把行动、装置和领域集合起来，由经济学家和其他人定性并格式化为经济性的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-019"></a>[19](#note-ch5-019)目的不是把注意力从经济转向经济化，而是把经济的制造理解为一种经济化参与其中的效果。经济学从不只是再现经济，但我们只有在经济学与其他治理模式——那些利用经济治理术之可能性的治理模式——的关系中，才能理解经济学的工作。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-020"></a>[20](#note-ch5-020)

Economentality draws upon those processes that, in the previous chapter, we identified as ‘economisation’: the assembling of actions, devices, and fields that are characterised and formatted by economists and others as being economic.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-019"></a>[19](#note-ch5-019) The aim is not to shift attention from the economy to economisation but to understand the making of the economy as an effect in which economisation plays a part. Economics never merely represents the economic, but we can understand the work of economics only in its relation to other modes of government that draw upon the possibilities of economentality.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-020"></a>[20](#note-ch5-020)

<a id="ch05-0022"></a>

经济治理术，以及由此形成的经济整体，是作为围绕资本化的斗争的一部分而出现的。两次世界大战之间的危机代表着全世界整个通过企业利润资本化从未来攫取收入体系的近乎崩溃。战后，在北美、欧洲和世界许多其他地区，有组织的工人和社会主义政府努力发展企业资本化的替代方案，其基础是工业的<a id="page-182"></a>〔原书第182页〕国家所有制、工会的加强、工人在企业利润分配中的权利，以及在埃及和全球南方许多地区对工商业外资所有权的限制。这些努力引发了一个前所未有的劳工斗争时期——参与工人人数之众、世界各地斗争场所范围之广，都前所未有。

Economentality, and thus the economy, emerged as part of a struggle over capitalisation. The crises of the interwar period represented the near collapse, around the world, of the entire system of capturing income from the future through the capitalising of corporate profit. After the war, in North America, Europe, and many other parts of the world, organised workers and socialist governments made efforts to develop alternatives to corporate capitalisation, based on the state <a id="page-182-en"></a>〔原书第182页〕ownership of industry, the strengthening of labour unions, worker rights in the allocation of corporate profits, and – in Egypt and many parts of the South – limits on the foreign ownership of businesses. These efforts provoked a period of unprecedented labour struggle – unprecedented in the number of workers involved and the range of sites around the world where the battles occurred.

<a id="ch05-0023"></a>

人们可以通过追踪单一年份的冲突，追溯政府如何回应这些斗争，以及美国、欧洲和中东之间如何形成新联系。1948 年 5 月 10 日，杜鲁门总统命令美国军队接管全国铁路，置于军事运营之下。与此同时，一位联邦地区法官对铁路工会领袖发出禁令。接管和禁令阻止了原定次日早晨举行的全国铁路罢工。一个月前，法院曾被类似地用来结束 40 万煤矿工人要求公司退休养老金的为期四周的罢工。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-021"></a>[21](#note-ch5-021)前一年通过的《塔夫脱—哈特利法》赋予法院阻止罢工的新权力，撤销了新政期间赢得的一些劳工权利。该法案是对美国历史上最大规模劳工行动浪潮的回应。1945—6 年的罢工从已被置于军队控制下的美国炼油厂开始，蔓延到铁路、电气工人、电力公司、钢铁业和汽车制造业。联邦政府曾部署武装部队接管炼油厂，随后又（两次）接管煤矿，并且至少在此前一次接管过铁路。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-022"></a>[22](#note-ch5-022)

One can trace the way in which governments responded to these struggles by following in a single year of strife the making of new connections among America, Europe, and the Middle East. On 10 May 1948, President Truman ordered the US army to seize control of the country’s railways and place them under military operation. At the same time, a federal district judge issued an injunction against the leaders of the railroad unions. The seizure and injunction prevented a national railway strike planned for the following morning. A month before, the courts had been used in a similar way to end a four-week strike by 400,000 coal miners seeking company retirement pensions.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-021"></a>[21](#note-ch5-021) The Taft–Hartley Act of the previous year gave courts a new power to prevent strikes, undoing some of the labour rights won during the New Deal. The act was a response to the largest wave of industrial action in US history. Starting in the country’s oil refineries, which had been placed under army control, the 1945–6 strikes had spread to railways, electrical workers, power companies, the steel industry, and automobile manufacturing. The federal government had deployed the armed forces to seize control of the oil refineries, then the coal mines (twice), and, on at least one previous occasion, the railways.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-022"></a>[22](#note-ch5-022)

<a id="ch05-0024"></a>

新的《塔夫脱—哈特利法》权力不能用于铁路工会，后者受单独法律制度《铁路劳动法》管辖。为了绕开这个问题并阻止 1948 年 5 月的新罢工，法院声称拥有阻止铁路罢工的一般权力。它为这种扩大了的权力辩护，理由是全国铁路停运将“危害国民健康与安全”，并妨碍“至关重要且必要的政府职能”。法院主张，它有权采取行动防止国家遭受这种“不可弥补的伤害”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-023"></a>[23](#note-ch5-023)通过援引对国民安全的威胁来为和平时期使用军事力量辩护，把政府在国内对有组织工人要求的打击与新的国家安全话语联系起来。1947 年 7 月的《国家安全法》开启了政府的重新军事化，设立了国防部、中央情报局和国家安全委员会。杜鲁门总统在总统<a id="page-183"></a>〔原书第183页〕专机——一架绰号*“圣牛”*的道格拉斯 C-54“空中霸王”——上签署该法案成为法律，这似乎再合适不过。和平时期的军国主义将成为美国的神圣不可侵犯之物，越来越不受批评。有人声称，如今需要和平时期的军国主义来保护欧洲，并越来越多地用来保卫中东油田。波斯湾能源资源对美国“安全”至关重要这一新观念，与国内的劳工斗争联系在一起。

The new Taft–Hartley powers could not be used against rail unions, which were governed under a separate legal regime, the Railway Labor Act. To get around this problem and prevent the new strike in May 1948, the court claimed a general power to prevent rail strikes. It justified this expanded power on the grounds that a nationwide rail stoppage would ‘imperil national health and safety’ and obstruct ‘vital and necessary Government functions’. The court was empowered to act, it argued, to prevent this ‘irreparable injury’ to the country.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-023"></a>[23](#note-ch5-023) Justifying the peacetime use of military power by invoking the threat to national safety linked the government’s domestic fight against the claims of organised workers to a new idiom of national security. The National Security Act of July 1947 inaugurated the remilitarisation of government, setting up the Department of Defense, the Central Intelligence Agency, and the National Security Council. It seems only appropriate that President Truman signed the act into law aboard his presidential <a id="page-183-en"></a>〔原书第183页〕aircraft, a Douglas C-54 Skymaster nicknamed *The Sacred Cow*. Peacetime militarism was to be America’s sacred cow, acquiring an increasing immunity from criticism. Peacetime militarism was now required, it was claimed, for the protection of Europe and, increasingly, to defend the oil fields of the Middle East. The novel idea that the energy resources of the Persian Gulf were important to the ‘security’ of the United States was connected to the labour struggles at home.

校注：底本把1947年设立的机构直接称为国防部。美国国会访客中心对档案的说明区分1947年的National Military Establishment与1949年修法后采用的Department of Defense名称。正文保留原作概述。 https://www.visitthecapitol.gov/artifact/new-organization-national-defense-chart-accompanying-statement-secretary-war-robert-p

<a id="ch05-0025"></a>

为回应战后煤炭和铁路罢工，电力公司和铁路公司开始加强自身以对抗劳工要求，办法是开发替代能源，从使用煤炭转向燃烧石油，从而削弱大众民主扩大了的诉求。部分因此，1948 年美国历史上首次成为石油净进口国，尽管当时它正生产世界供应的 60%。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-024"></a>[24](#note-ch5-024)

In response to the postwar coal and railway strikes, electric power companies and railroad firms began to strengthen themselves against labour demands, thus weakening the expanded claims of popular democracy by developing an alternative source of energy, switching from using coal to burning oil. Partly as a result, in 1948 the United States became, for the first time in its history, a net importer of oil, even though it was then producing 60 per cent of the world’s supply.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-024"></a>[24](#note-ch5-024)

<a id="ch05-0026"></a>

美国希望在欧洲策划类似的劳工运动削弱。就在全国铁路罢工被击败的同一天，大西洋彼岸的波尔多，第一艘运载马歇尔计划援助的船只开始卸货，船上载有 8,800 吨美国小麦。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-025"></a>[25](#note-ch5-025)美国援助不仅旨在重建欧洲，还旨在加强其商业阶级，以对抗比美国更强大的矿工、铁路工人和其他有工会组织的力量。在英国、法国和欧洲大陆其他地区，由煤矿工人及其在其他工会的盟友领导的罢工，要求扩大第一次世界大战之前及此后赢得的社会和民主权利，包括在工业管理或所有权中发挥作用的集体权利。对于管理欧洲复兴计划（马歇尔计划的正式名称）的美国商人来说，美国援助将被用来削弱这种左翼对企业所有权和工业控制的威胁。部分出于这个原因，马歇尔计划资金的最大支出不是用于美国谷物，而是用于中东石油。美国补贴了欧洲主要化石燃料来源从煤炭向石油的转换。这种转换部分旨在削弱欧洲煤矿工人，从而破坏左翼的力量。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-026"></a>[26](#note-ch5-026)

The United States hoped to engineer a similar weakening of the labour movements in Europe. On the same day that the national railroad strike was defeated, across the Atlantic in Bordeaux, the first ship carrying Marshall Plan aid began unloading its cargo, 8,800 tons of American wheat.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-025"></a>[25](#note-ch5-025) US aid was intended not just to rebuild Europe but to strengthen its business class against miners, railway workers, and other unionised forces even more powerful than those in the United States. In Britain, France, and other parts of the continent, strikes led by coal miners and their allies in other unions were demanding an extension of the social and democratic rights won before and since the First World War, including a collective right to a role in the management or ownership of industry. For the American businessmen who ran the European Recovery Plan, as the Marshall Plan was formally known, US aid was to be used to weaken this left-wing threat to the corporate ownership and control of industry. Partly for this reason, the largest expenditure of Marshall Plan funds was not on US grain but on oil from the Middle East. The United States subsidised the conversion of Europe’s principal source of fossil fuel from coal to oil. The conversion was intended, in part, to weaken the coal miners of Europe and thus undermine the power of the left.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-026"></a>[26](#note-ch5-026)

<a id="ch05-0027"></a>

作为一种能源，石油具有若干优势，使其较不容易受到劳工要求的影响，因而也较不容易受到对资本化的威胁。仅仅通过补充煤炭供应，它就削弱了煤矿工人在铁路工人和码头工人协同下关闭一国碳能源系统的能力。总罢工的武器——随着 1880 年代煤炭、铁路和电力网络的<a id="page-184"></a>〔原书第184页〕建设而组装起来，此后在工业化世界迅速用来赢得争取更民主、更平等的集体生活形式的斗争——如今被拆除了。石油可以用泵和管道开采到地表并分配，因此其生产和分配所需工人更少，也更难以用罢工行动中断。与煤炭不同，石油足够轻，容易跨洋运输。因此，以前使用煤炭实现工业化的地区——把工业建在能源来源附近，因而容易受到当地能源供应中断的影响——如今可以开始把能源供应外包出去。

Oil had a number of advantages as a source of energy that made it less vulnerable to the demands of labour and thus to threats against capitalisation. Simply by supplementing coal supplies, it weakened the ability of coal miners, in alliance with railwaymen and dockworkers, to shut down a country’s carbon energy system. The weapon of the general strike – assembled with the building of coal, rail, and electric networks <a id="page-184-en"></a>〔原书第184页〕in the 1880s, and used rapidly thereafter across the industrialising world to win battles for more democratic and egalitarian forms of collective life – was now dismantled. Oil could be raised to the surface and distributed using pumps and pipelines, so its production and distribution required fewer workers and was more difficult to interrupt with strike actions. Unlike coal, it was light enough to be moved easily across oceans. So, regions that had previously industrialised using coal, building industries close to the source of energy and thus vulnerable to the interruption of local energy supplies, could now begin to outsource the supply of energy.

<a id="ch05-0028"></a>

战后中东石油的开发可以视为欧洲工业生产的外包。制造业外包再过二三十年才变得重要，那是在集装箱航运发展之后；集装箱航运使发达工业化国家能够开始从东亚进口大量制成品。另一方面，能源可以说在远洋油轮和长途管道发展之后就已被“集装箱化”了。

The postwar development of Middle Eastern oil can be viewed as an outsourcing of European industrial production. The outsourcing of manufacturing did not become significant for another two or three decades, following the development of containerised shipping, which allowed the advanced industrialised countries to begin importing large quantities of manufactured goods from East Asia. Energy, on the other hand, had already been containerised, as it were, ever since the development of the ocean-going oil tanker and the long-distance pipeline.

<a id="ch05-0029"></a>

1947 年，沙特阿拉伯的工人开始修建跨阿拉伯输油管道，这是当时世界上最大的管道。购买了沙特阿拉伯石油生产权的美国公司计划把石油从该国东海岸经陆路输送到巴勒斯坦海法港的一个储油库；海法是一条由英国修建、从伊拉克出发的既有输油管道的终点。这些管道及相关油轮航线提供了把西方能源生产转移到海外的设施。在这个过程中，它们也在建设一种新的民主基础设施，争取更有保障的集体生活的斗争将在这一更广阔的网络中展开。

In 1947, workers in Saudi Arabia had begun constructing the Trans-Arabian Pipeline, the world’s largest pipeline at that time. The US companies that had purchased rights to produce oil in Saudi Arabia planned to pump the oil overland from the eastern shore of the country to an oil depot at the port of Haifa in Palestine, the terminus of an existing British-built pipeline from Iraq. Such pipelines and the associated tanker routes provided the infrastructure for moving the West’s energy production offshore. In the process, they were also building a new infrastructure of democracy, in which struggles for a less precarious collective life would be waged over a more extended network.

<a id="ch05-0030"></a>

在杜鲁门宣布对美国铁路实施军事控制的 1948 年 5 月同一周，另一场军事对抗在巴格达以西四十英里、幼发拉底河畔的伊拉克城镇费卢杰以失败告终。

In the same week of May 1948 that Truman was declaring military control of American railways, another military confrontation was culminating in a defeat at the Iraqi town of Falluja, on the Euphrates River, forty miles west of Baghdad.

<a id="ch05-0031"></a>

费卢杰的失败是一场酝酿了两年的斗争的最后一步。1946 年 6 月，基尔库克英美合资伊拉克石油公司油田——石油从那里经管道输往海法——的一次罢工被镇压；石油工人当时要求组建工会的权利、疾病和伤残保险以及养老金。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-027"></a>[27](#note-ch5-027)一队骑警冲进数百名工人聚集在城外加乌帕吉花园的集会，杀死十名工人，打伤另外二十七人。1948 年初，一系列学生<a id="page-185"></a>〔原书第185页〕和工人罢工引发了反对英国支持的君主制和英国经营的石油公司的全国抗议。这一次，石油工人没有把行动集中在油田，而是在“基尔库克—海法和基尔库克—的黎波里两条管道的分岔点，即哈迪萨附近的 K3 泵站”，并使其停运。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-028"></a>[28](#note-ch5-028)停运持续了两周，直到公司用机枪和装甲车包围现场并切断食物供应。罢工者无法冒着重演加乌帕吉屠杀的风险，决定向一百五十多英里外的巴格达进军。他们于 5 月 12 日出发，即美国铁路罢工失败后的第二天。经过三天行军，沿途支持不断增加，他们进入费卢杰，“落入……警察的陷阱”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-029"></a>[29](#note-ch5-029)石油工人被送回 K3，罢工领袖被送进监狱。

The Falluja defeat was the last step in a struggle that had been building for two years. In June 1946, a strike at the Anglo-American-owned Iraq Petroleum Company fields in Kirkuk, the site from which oil was piped to Haifa – by oil workers demanding the right to a union, sickness and disability insurance, and a pension – had been crushed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-027"></a>[27](#note-ch5-027) A force of mounted policemen charged the meeting of several hundred workers gathered in the Gawupaghi Gardens outside the town, killing ten workers and injuring another twenty-seven. In early 1948 a series of student <a id="page-185-en"></a>〔原书第185页〕and worker strikes led to nationwide protests against the British-backed monarchy and the British-run oil company. This time, the oil workers focused their action not on the oil fields but at ‘the point of bifurcation of the Kirkūk–Haifa and the Kirkūk–Tripoli pipelines, the K3 pumping station near Hadīthah’, which they shut down.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-028"></a>[28](#note-ch5-028) The stoppage lasted two weeks, until the Company surrounded the site with machine guns and armoured cars and cut off supplies of food. Unable to risk a repeat of the massacre at Gawupaghi, the strikers decided to march on Baghdad, more than 150 miles away. They set out on 12 May, the day after the defeat of the railroad strike in the United States. After three days of marching, with increasing support along the way, they entered Falluja and ‘fell into . . . a police trap’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-029"></a>[29](#note-ch5-029) The oil workers were sent back to K3, and the strike leaders to prison.

<a id="ch05-0032"></a>

伊拉克石油工人的失败，在同一时期伊朗以及后来巴林和沙特阿拉伯的石油罢工被打破时重演。沙特石油工人要求美国石油公司阿美公司提高工资和改善生活条件，要求组建工会的权利，要求政府制定政治宪法，并要求取消美国石油公司的治外法权。在埃及，正如我们即将看到的，一波罢工在与伊拉克石油工人抗议同一周被终结。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-030"></a>[30](#note-ch5-030)

Defeat for Iraqi oil workers was repeated in the breaking of oil strikes in Iran in the same period, and later in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. The Saudi oil workers demanded better pay and living conditions from the American oil company Aramco, the right to form a union, a political constitution from the government, and the removal of extra-territorial privileges for the American oil company. In Egypt, as we will shortly see, a wave of strikes was brought to an end in the same week as the oil workers’ protests in Iraq.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-030"></a>[30](#note-ch5-030)

<a id="ch05-0033"></a>

1948 年以两次将塑造战后中东的挫折为标志。一是伊拉克石油工人在费卢杰的失败，这对以石油开采为基础的工人运动是一次逆转——这些运动分散在地区各处、远离欧洲，因而无法像欧洲煤矿工人那样享有相互联动、能够中断生产和供应的民主集体行动的可能性，因为欧洲煤矿工人与能源使用场所紧密相连。二是殖民权力的重组，其中心是同年发生在巴勒斯坦的灾难。战前，殖民列强通常通过声称有权“保护”某些人口——特别是欧洲定居者殖民地和宗教少数群体社区——来为他们在该地区的存在辩护。随着美国开始取代英国和法国成为该地区主要帝国强权，它开始围绕一种新学说即“安全”学说来重塑其权力辩护——首先是石油安全，后来是刚刚采用“以色列”名称的新定居者国家的安全。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-031"></a>[31](#note-ch5-031)第一次挫折，如前所述，发生在伊拉克费卢杰；第二次挫折发生在巴勒斯坦，恰好在一个同名之地以失败告终。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-032"></a>[32](#note-ch5-032)

The year 1948 was marked by two setbacks that would shape the postwar Middle East. One was the defeat of the Iraqi oil workers at Falluja, a reversal for worker movements based in oil extraction – movements whose dispersion across the region and distance from Europe deprived them of the possibilities for interconnected, disruptive, democratic collective action that coal workers in Europe, tied closely to the sites of energy use, had enjoyed. The second was a reconfiguring of colonial power, centred in the calamity that same year in Palestine. Before the war, colonial powers had typically justified their presence in the region by claiming the right to ‘protect’ certain populations, specifically colonies of European settlers and communities of religious minorities. As the United States began to replace Britain and France as the principal imperial power in the region, it started to recast the justification for its power around a new doctrine, the doctrine of ‘security’ – first of oil and later of the new settler state that had just adopted the name ‘Israel’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-031"></a>[31](#note-ch5-031) The first of these setbacks, as already mentioned, took place in Falluja, Iraq; the second, in Palestine, happened to culminate in defeat at a place that shared the same name.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-032"></a>[32](#note-ch5-032)

<a id="ch05-0034"></a>

<a id="page-186"></a>〔原书第186页〕

<a id="page-186-en"></a>〔原书第186页〕

<a id="ch05-0035"></a>

### 经济的诞生

### The Birth of the Economy

<a id="ch05-0036"></a>

1948 年，华盛顿新成立的经济顾问委员会（CEA）发表了第二份“总统向国会提交的年度报告”。上一年的首份报告包含了美国经济的第一批官方统计再现。但那份报告没有把其对象命名为经济，也很少使用这个新词，更愿意讨论“国家经济预算”。然而仅仅一年后，在 1948 年报告中，人们可以看到经济观念的熟悉化，这个词开始越来越频繁地被使用。五年后，即 1953 年，报告删去了“国家经济预算”一词。年度账户的导言解释说，它们阐明了“经济内部的变革和调整过程”。与此同时，报告警告说，年度账户无法捕捉这个对象的动态运动。这些账户更像是“间隔拍摄的快照，而不是展示变化过程的电影”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-033"></a>[33](#note-ch5-033)

In 1948, the new Council of Economic Advisors (CEA) in Washington published its second ‘Annual Report of the President to Congress’. Its inaugural report the previous year had contained the first official statistical representations of the American economy. But that report did not name its object as the economy and contained few uses of the new term, preferring to discuss ‘the nation’s economic budget’. But, only a year later, in the 1948 report, one can see the familiarisation of the idea of the economy, which begins to be used with increasing frequency. Five years later, in 1953, the report dropped the term ‘nation’s economic budget’. The introduction to the annual accounts explains that they illuminate ‘the process of change and adjustment within the economy’. The report warned, at the same time, that annual accounts could not capture the dynamic movement of this object. The accounts were more like ‘snapshots taken at intervals than like a moving picture which shows the process of change’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-033"></a>[33](#note-ch5-033)

<a id="ch05-0037"></a>

历史学家强调经济顾问委员会设立过程中的两点。第一，它的创建标志着学术专业知识在行政部门中前所未有地发挥影响。对经济学家来说，经济顾问委员会是他们为国家服务的“制度顶峰”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-034"></a>[34](#note-ch5-034)第二，这种专业知识代表着“经济增长术”的出现和胜利。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-035"></a>[35](#note-ch5-035)为了理解通过治理未来来确保资本化的新方式的出现，我们可以对这段叙述提出两点修改。

Historians have emphasised two points about the setting up of the CEA. First, its creation marks an unprecedented influence of academic expertise within executive office. For economists, the CEA was ‘the institutional zenith’ for their service to the state.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-034"></a>[34](#note-ch5-034) Second, this expertise represents the emergence and triumph of ‘economic growthmanship’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-035"></a>[35](#note-ch5-035) We can propose two modifications to this story for understanding the emergence of new modes of securing capitalisation through governing the future.

<a id="ch05-0038"></a>

第一，经济顾问委员会的设立不是为了让经济学家进入政府，而是为了把他们排除在外。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-036"></a>[36](#note-ch5-036)更准确地说，它旨在实现权力分立，创造一种类似于联邦储备委员会、最高法院或新参谋长联席会议准独立地位的安排，或者从另一种意义上说，类似于“国家安全”新领域——中东是这一领域的重要参照点。经济顾问委员会将在政治辩论的日常争夺之外生产公开的经济知识，促成经济作为独立于国家的对象的平行效果，使它作为一种独立于治理过程的可见机制运作。

First, the CEA was set up not to allow economists into government but to keep them out.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-036"></a>[36](#note-ch5-036) More precisely, it was intended to effect a separation of the powers, creating an arrangement analogous to the quasiindependence of the Federal Reserve, the Supreme Court, or the new Joint Chiefs of Staff, or analogous in another sense to the new realm of ‘national security’ for which the Middle East served as an important reference point. The CEA would produce public economic knowledge outside the day-to-day contestations of political debate, contributing to the parallel effect of the economy as an object separate from the state that operated as a visible mechanism independent of the process of government.

<a id="ch05-0039"></a>

国会设立经济顾问委员会，是对战后《充分就业法案》提案的反应，该提案本会把充分就业确立为一项集体权利。就业权的反对者把设立委员会的计划插入《就业法案》，以削弱<a id="page-187"></a>〔原书第187页〕战时经济学家在政府中的影响，以及他们在战争期间为最大化就业和控制价格而发展出的机制。反对者希望通过让学术经济学家在华盛顿发声，来削弱这些政府经济学家：经济顾问委员会将表达决策过程之外专家的观点。与隐藏在政府部门内部的经济学家不同，这些“借调学者”将被迫通过向国会新设联合委员会提交年度报告，公开他们的建议及其依据的证据。通过使经济计算公开化，右翼势力希望揭露其不确定性并限制其影响。经济顾问委员会将成为这种公开化的装置，用于“经济教育”（从教育总统开始）。它的定期报告将有助于使经济这一对象得以形成。

Congress created the CEA in reaction against postwar proposals for a Full Employment Act, which would have established full employment as a collective right. Opponents of the right to employment inserted the plan for the Council into the Employment Bill, to weaken the influence <a id="page-187-en"></a>〔原书第187页〕of wartime economists in government and the mechanisms they had developed during the war for maximising employment and controlling prices. The opponents hoped to undermine these government economists by giving a voice in Washington to academic economists: the CEA would express the views of specialists from outside the decision-making process. In contrast to economists hidden from view inside government departments, these academics-on-loan would be forced to make public their advice and the evidence on which it was based, through an annual report to a new joint committee of Congress. By making economic calculation public, right-wing forces hoped to be able to expose its uncertainties and limit its influence. The CEA was to be a device for this making of things public, for an ‘economic education’ (starting with the education of the president). Its regular reports would help bring the economy into effect.

<a id="ch05-0040"></a>

第二，经济专业知识往往关注增长问题：人口增加、贸易扩大、自然资源过剩或短缺，或货币供应膨胀。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-037"></a>[37](#note-ch5-037)在这个历史节点上，新的不是增长术，而是将要增长的对象：不是人口、贸易、资源或财富，而是某种更少物质性、因而更有效的东西：经济。经济的增长不是资源治理或国家财政管理的问题。它是一种把未来带入治理的方式——通过其未来来治理人口。

Second, economic expertise had often been concerned with problems of growth: the increase in population, the expansion of trade, a surfeit or shortage of natural resources, or inflation in the supply of money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-037"></a>[37](#note-ch5-037) What was new in this historical juncture was not growth-manship but the object that would grow: not population, trade, resources, or wealth, but something less material and therefore more effective: the economy. The growth of the economy was not a question of the government of resources or the management of national finance. It was a means of bringing the future into government – of governing populations through their futures.

<a id="ch05-0041"></a>

经济这一效果有什么用处？部分答案是，它允许一种既代表对立社会力量、又指出使这些对立面达到平衡之手段的治理模式。这是经济顾问委员会报告的主要方法和目的：代表并平衡“商业”和“劳工”的诉求。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-038"></a>[38](#note-ch5-038)面对经济不断变化的指标，商人将被迫考虑过度涨价的影响，而工人则被迫节制工资要求。第三方即银行家将看到把信用创造引向消费或投资这两种选择各自的效果。

What was the effect of the economy good for? Part of the answer is that it allowed a mode of government that both represented opposing social forces and indicated the means of bringing these opposites into balance. This was the chief method and purpose of the CEA reports: to represent and balance the claims of ‘business’ and ‘labor’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-038"></a>[38](#note-ch5-038) Exposed to the changing metrics of the economy, businessmen would be pressured to consider the impact of excessive price increases, while workers would be forced to moderate wage demands. A third party, the bankers, would see the effect of directing credit creation towards consumption versus investment.

<a id="ch05-0042"></a>

经济是一种通过部署未来——以经济单位之间资金不断变化的流动来计算——来实现这种平衡的装置。相互竞争的政治力量如今将看到不同要求和选择如何影响未来的平衡。经济将把人们的政治生活嵌入未来，引导他们按照其再现来计算。它将把人们定位在<a id="page-188"></a>〔原书第188页〕与以一种特定方式形成的未来的关系中，即作为不同力量之间的平衡或权衡；这些力量如今被作为等值物铭刻进国民账户结构，一边是工资劳动者/消费者，另一边是商业和银行业。

The economy was a device for achieving this balance by deploying the future, calculated in terms of the changing movements of funds among economic units. Rival political forces would now see how different demands and choices affected the future balance. The economy would embed people’s political lives in the future, by leading them to calculate according to its representation. It would locate them in <a id="page-188-en"></a>〔原书第188页〕relation to a future formed in a particular way, as a balance, or trade-off, between forces now inscribed as equivalents in the structure of national accounts, with wage earners/consumers on one side, and business and banking on the other.

<a id="ch05-0043"></a>

在此之前，经济学家通常对预测工作持怀疑态度。预测是一种不可预测、因而危险的艺术，据说其过度和失败在苏联式计划的事例中显而易见。约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯在论述“困扰现代世界经济生活的信心危机”时指出，“我们据以估算十年后一条铁路、一座铜矿、一家纺织厂、一种专利药品的商誉、一艘大西洋客轮、伦敦金融城一座建筑之收益的知识基础，微不足道，有时甚至等于零”。他不相信经济计算能够克服“包裹着我们未来的时间和无知的黑暗力量”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-039"></a>[39](#note-ch5-039)这种对不可知时间力量的恐惧，如今可以让位于一种被计算的未来；这种未来越来越自信地被投射到当下的政治上。

Until this point, economists had typically been suspicious of the work of forecasting. It was an unpredictable and therefore dangerous art, whose excesses and failures were said to be visible in the example of Soviet-style planning. Writing about ‘the crises of confidence which afflict the economic life of the modern world’, John Maynard Keynes had pointed out that ‘our basis of knowledge for estimating the yield ten years hence of a railway, a copper mine, a textile factory, the goodwill of a patent medicine, an Atlantic liner, a building in the City of London amounts to little and sometimes to nothing’. He did not believe that economic calculation could overcome ‘the dark forces of time and ignorance which envelop our future’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-039"></a>[39](#note-ch5-039) This fear of unknowable temporal forces could now give way to a calculated future, projected with increasing confidence onto the politics of the present.

<a id="ch05-0044"></a>

通过未来来治理，不仅是一个计算后来被称为国民生产总值（GNP）（后来是国内生产总值，GDP）的新资金流通的问题，或把经济当作政治对象来讨论的问题。我们可以追溯另外两项更具体的创新，它们说明生产和支配未来所需的是何种工作。

To govern through the future was not just a question of calculating the new circulations of funds that were to be known as the gross national product (GNP) (and later the gross domestic product, or GDP) or discussing the economy as a political object. We can trace two more specific innovations which illustrate the kind of work required to produce and command the future.

<a id="ch05-0045"></a>

第一个例子是价格平减指数，即调整数字以计入通货膨胀、从而可以在较长年份跨度内进行比较的方法。GNP 是一个年度数字。像公司的账簿一样，它需要一个任意的起点和终点，创造出一个时间单位，其中一切必须平衡，从而产生一个总量——一个由经济实体之间无穷无尽的支付流通制造出来的固定数量。然后可以把一个时间单位内产生的总量与下一个时间单位的总量相比较，就像公司比较其季度或年度利润一样。但与报告公司利润的人不同，计算 GDP 的人希望使总量不仅可以与前一年或后一年比较，而且可以在数年甚至数十年间比较。这种延长的时间序列需要一种调整数字的方法，以计入货币购买力下降或价格通胀现象。

The first example is the price deflator, or the method of adjusting figures to account for inflation so that comparisons could be made over a wide span of years. The GNP was an annual figure. Like a company’s books, it required an arbitrary starting and ending point, creating a unit of time within which everything had to balance, generating a total – a fixed quantity manufactured out of the endless circulation of payments between economic entities. The total produced from within one unit of time could then be compared to the next, just as a firm compares its quarterly or annual profits. But, unlike those reporting company profits, those calculating GDP wished to make it possible to compare the total from one year not just to the preceding or following year but across several years or even decades. This extended temporal sequence required a method of adjusting the numbers to allow for the declining purchasing power of money or the phenomenon of price inflation.

<a id="ch05-0046"></a>

通货膨胀是经济学家从十九世纪物理学借用的词语之一。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-040"></a>[40](#note-ch5-040)它以前指把额外信用货币供应泵入货币<a id="page-189"></a>〔原书第189页〕体系的机械行为。如今它成为一个术语，可以指新的国家层面总量；对这些总量的计量，正在形成经济这一对象。政府预算办公室的工作人员最初拒绝计算价格通胀率的要求，认为定期收集大量商品代表性价格数据，并处理这些数字来计算总体年度通胀率，是一项过于复杂和昂贵的操作。然而最终，平减指数在建构经济方面的有用性克服了这些反对意见。

Inflation was one of those words borrowed by economists from nineteenth-century physics.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-040"></a>[40](#note-ch5-040) It was previously used to refer to the mechanical act of pumping additional supplies of credit money into the currency <a id="page-189-en"></a>〔原书第189页〕system. It was now a term that could refer to the new national-level aggregates whose measurement was taking shape as the economy. The staff of the government budget office initially refused the request to calculate the rate of inflation in prices, arguing that gathering representative data on the prices of numerous commodities at regular intervals and manipulating the figures to calculate an aggregate annual inflation rate was far too complex and costly an operation. Eventually, however, the usefulness of the deflator in constructing the economy overcame these objections.

<a id="ch05-0047"></a>

平减指数使衡量 GDP 的变化不仅可以从一年到另一年进行，而且可以跨越一系列年份或数十年。这种延长的衡量使一个动态过程——经济的增长——变得可见。通过通货膨胀调整，如今可以估算美国自 1875 年以来每一年的国民生产总值总量。估算表明，美国经济一直在以每年 3.75% 的速度增长，其间有起有落。

The deflator made it possible to measure the change in GDP not just from one year to the next but over a sequence of years or decades. This extended measurement made visible a dynamic process – the growth of the economy. With adjustments for inflation, it was now possible to estimate totals for the gross national product of the United States for every year back to 1875. The estimates suggested that the American economy had been growing, with ups and downs, at a rate of 3.75 per cent per year.

<a id="ch05-0048"></a>

第二项创新在于经济学家描绘增长的方式。经济顾问委员会在其年度报告中开始用图表描绘国家“经济预算”、后来是其经济的变化。纵轴表示 GDP 水平，横轴标记年份的连续。增长现象被描绘为 GDP 的增加，如今可以在图表表面上形成一条从左向右上升的线。这条线始于过去，穿过现在，并被投射到未来。这种可视化意在教育公众，鼓励工人、雇主和金融家依据这个被投射的未来行动。它可以表明，不合理的政治要求——尤其是工人要求基于收入份额增加、而非基于自身生产率提高的更高工资——有可能使这条线偏离轨道。同样，金融业过度创造信用将危及未来的稳定。

A second innovation came in the way economists pictured growth. In its annual reports, the CEA began portraying changes in the nation’s ‘economic budget’, and later its economy, with a chart. The vertical axis indicated the level of GDP, while the horizontal axis marked the succession of years. The phenomenon of growth, portrayed as the increase in GDP, could now form a line ascending from left to right across the surface of the chart. The line started in the past, moved through the present, and was projected forwards into the future. The visualisation was intended to educate the public, encouraging workers, employers, and financiers to act in relation to this projected future. Unreasonable political demands, it could be shown, especially the demand of workers for higher wages based on an increased share of revenues, rather than on increases in their own productivity, would threaten to throw the line off its path. Similarly, excessive creation of credit by the financial industry would risk the stability of the future.

<a id="ch05-0049"></a>

然而，在产量以每年接近 4% 的速度增长的情况下，这条将要支配人们生活的线并不是直线。画在图表上，它形成一条指数曲线。它起初是一个平缓上升的斜坡，但迅速升高，不久就会达到几乎垂直的角度，数值趋近无穷大。

However, with production growing at close to 4 per cent a year, this line that was to rule people’s lives was not straight. Drawn on a chart, it formed an exponential curve. It started as a gently rising slope but gathered height rapidly and before long would reach an angle that was almost vertical, with values approaching infinity.

<a id="ch05-0050"></a>

指数曲线的问题有两方面。第一，当这条线接近垂直时，不同政治力量诉求的微小调整所带来的有益效果无法轻易在图表上<a id="page-190"></a>〔原书第190页〕显现。第二，如果未来是一条加速曲线——一条指数增长线——它如何能成为规训和控制的工具？它看起来已经失控。

The problem of the exponential curve was twofold. First, with the line moving close to vertical, the beneficial effect of minor adjustments in the demands of different political forces could not easily be made <a id="page-190-en"></a>〔原书第190页〕visible on the graph. Second, if the future was an accelerating curve – a line of exponential growth – how could it be made an instrument of discipline and control? It appeared out of control.

<a id="ch05-0051"></a>

到目前为止，这不仅是绘制图表的问题，也是未来本身的问题。现代的增长经验以前从未提供稳定点或控制焦点。几何变化率总是显得不可持续。托马斯·马尔萨斯 1798 年首次出版的*《人口原理》*是这一问题最著名的表述。但许多其他十九世纪政治经济学家也进行了类似计算，并对未来产生了同样的恐慌。我们在[第四章](#ch04-0001)遇到的威廉·杰文斯是 1870 年代边际效用理论的建构者之一；他在完成一份 1865 年出版的英国煤炭储量报告后，放弃了增长问题。该研究预测，英国煤炭开采和消费的指数增长将在大约五十年内达到煤炭产量峰值，然后加速下降。这一预测被证明是准确的，峰值出现在 1913 年。到二十世纪初，经济学家普遍关注几何增长的后果，包括自然资源枯竭。

Until now, this had been the problem not just with the drawing of graphs but with the future itself. The modern experience of growth had not previously offered a point of stability or a focus of control. Geometric rates of change always appeared unsustainable. Thomas Malthus’s *Essay on the Principle of Population*, first published in 1798, was the best-known expression of this problem. But many other nineteenth-century political economists carried out similar calculations with the same resulting alarm about the future. William Jevons, whom we met in [chapter 4](#ch04-0001) as one of the architects of marginal utility theory in the 1870s, had abandoned the question of growth after completing a report on Britain’s coal reserves, published in 1865.
