The study predicted that the exponential growth in Britain’s mining and consumption of coal would lead to a peak in coal production within about fifty years, and then an accelerating decline. The prediction proved accurate, with the peak arriving in 1913. By the early twentieth century, there was a widespread preoccupation among economists with the consequences of geometric growth, including the exhaustion of natural resources.

<a id="ch05-0052"></a>

这种关切不只出现在政治经济学家中间。莱因哈特·科泽勒克认为，在现代，几何变化率界定了现代性的体验本身。他提出，现代性是通过“一个超越了此前可预测之物的未来”被体验到的，因为变化速度不断加快。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-041"></a>[41](#note-ch5-041)换言之，未来在当下被体验为这种活生生的加速感。这种体验与过去造成断裂，过去如今必须被重新配置为一种不可企及的“传统”，因为较早的历史“未必能用来否定未来可能呈现的他异性”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-042"></a>[42](#note-ch5-042)新的期待视野导致了过去与未来相对位置的重新定位。

This concern was found not just among political economists. Reinhart Koselleck argues that in the modern era geometric rates of change defined the very experience of modernity. Modernity was encountered, he suggests, in terms of ‘a future that transcended the hitherto predictable’ because of the phenomenon of the ever-increasing speed of change.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-041"></a>[41](#note-ch5-041) The future, in other words, was experienced in the present as this lived sensation of acceleration. The experience created a rupture with the past, which now had to be refigured as an inaccessible ‘tradition’ because earlier history ‘might not count against the possible otherness of the future’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-042"></a>[42](#note-ch5-042) The new horizons of expectation caused a repositioning, as it were, of the relative locations of past and future.

<a id="ch05-0053"></a>

在二十世纪初的几十年里，作家们继续把现代性体验与加速变化、因而不可预测的未来联系起来。这种体验常常与人类如今可以利用的“自然能量”有关。“技术时代运作的一个方面，以其对自然能量前所未有的支配……需要明确关注，”约翰·杜威在*《公众及其问题》*（1927）中写道。“较早的公众作为地方共同体，彼此之间在很大程度上同质，而且正如俗话所说，也是静止的。”杜威认为，“对运动和速度的狂热<a id="page-191"></a>〔原书第191页〕是社会生活动荡不安的症状，它反过来加剧了它所由产生的那些原因。钢铁取代木材和砖石用于建筑；钢筋混凝土改造钢铁，某种发明可能带来进一步的革命。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-043"></a>[43](#note-ch5-043)

In the early decades of the twentieth century, writers continued to associate the experience of modernity with accelerating change and thus unpredictable futures. Very often the experience was related to the ‘natural energies’ that humans could now exploit. ‘One phase of the workings of a technological age, with its unprecedented command of natural energies, . . . needs explicit attention’, John Dewey wrote in *The Public and Its Problems* (1927). ‘The older publics, in being local communities, largely homogeneous with one another, were also, as the phrase goes, static.’ Dewey argued that ‘the mania for motion and speed <a id="page-191-en"></a>〔原书第191页〕is a symptom of the restless instability of social life, and it operates to intensify the causes from which it springs. Steel replaces wood and masonry for buildings; ferroconcrete modifies steel, and some invention may work a further revolution.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-043"></a>[43](#note-ch5-043)

<a id="ch05-0054"></a>

像阿德里亚诺·达尼诺斯——阿斯旺大坝计划推动者——这样的人后来提出的战后发展愿景，当时尚未成形。相反，在两次世界大战之间，巨大基础设施项目可以例示变化的速度，正是这种速度使可靠的未来计算无法进行。美国国会花了十多年时间辩论如何处理在阿拉巴马州马斯尔肖尔斯田纳西河上修建巨型水坝的停滞项目，之后才设计出田纳西河流域管理局方案；该方案启发了达尼诺斯等人，成为战后综合发展愿景的典范。十多年来，水坝问题在美国国会占用的时间比任何其他问题都多。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-044"></a>[44](#note-ch5-044)对杜威来说，马斯尔肖尔斯的失败——连同其生产弹药和化肥的相关硝酸盐工厂——所体现的不是把未来作为经济和物质增长纲领来掌握，而是不断增多的能源来源如何使新项目几乎立即过时。“新方法，”他写道，“已经使所谓大量积累水力的需要变得过时。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-045"></a>[45](#note-ch5-045)

The later, postwar visions of development presented by men like Adriano Daninos, the promoter of the scheme to build the Aswan Dam, had not yet taken shape. On the contrary, in the interwar period mammoth infrastructure projects could exemplify the speed of change that made reliable calculations of the future impossible to carry out. The US Congress spent more than a dozen years debating what to do with the stalled project to build a giant dam on the Tennessee River at Muscle Shoals, Alabama, before devising the scheme for the Tennessee Valley Authority that was to inspire Daninos and others as a model for postwar visions of integrated development. For more than a decade, the problem of the dam occupied more time in the US Congress than any other issue.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-044"></a>[44](#note-ch5-044) For Dewey, the failure at Muscle Shoals, with its associated nitrate plants built to produce munitions and fertiliser, epitomised not a mastery of the future as a programme of economic and material growth but the way in which proliferating sources of energy made new projects almost immediately redundant. ‘New methods’, he wrote, ‘have already made antiquated the supposed need of great accumulation of water power.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-045"></a>[45](#note-ch5-045)

<a id="ch05-0055"></a>

对其他作家来说，加速的动力被认定为货币。二十世纪早期，格奥尔格·齐美尔在论述他所谓“货币经济”的心理体验时，探讨了“货币供应增加对经济—心理过程发展的加速效应”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-046"></a>[46](#note-ch5-046)难怪人们怀疑金融预测不可靠且危险。齐美尔所回应的信用创造新力量，制造了未来的不稳定性。

For other writers, the motor of acceleration was identified as money. Writing earlier in the century about the mental experience of what he called ‘money economy’, Georg Simmel explored ‘the accelerating effects of an increase in the supply of money on the development of the economic–psychic process’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-046"></a>[46](#note-ch5-046) No wonder there was a suspicion of financial forecasting as unreliable and dangerous. The new powers of credit creation, to which Simmel was responding, generated the instability of the future.

<a id="ch05-0056"></a>

苏联中央计划的例子或许提供了一种控制未来的替代方式，但它看起来并不更好。作为 1929 年“国民经济发展五年计划”的核心项目，苏联政府聘请芝加哥工程公司亨利·弗赖恩公司设计马格尼托哥尔斯克综合钢铁厂，这是苏联计划中最大的单一项目。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-047"></a>[47](#note-ch5-047)该设计以巨大规模复制了弗赖恩的工程师为印第安纳州加里的美国钢铁公司设计的工厂。这是德国军事模式的突击动员，创造了“一个技术完善的未来的集结地”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-048"></a>[48](#note-ch5-048)<a id="page-192"></a>〔原书第192页〕计划意味着工厂混乱地倍增、反复的临时应付、一个数量不断增殖且年度目标不可能完成的未来。苏联中央计划以其雄心和速度启发了世界各国政府，但它把未来计算为实体工厂和物质产出的迅速倍增，使当下变得更加而非更少混乱。

The example of Soviet central planning might have offered an alternative way to control the future, but it appeared no better. As a centrepiece of the 1929 ‘Five Year Plan for the Development of the National Economy’, the Soviet government hired the Chicago engineering firm of Henry Freyn and Company to design an integrated iron and steel complex at Magnitogorsk, the largest single venture in Soviet planning.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-047"></a>[47](#note-ch5-047) The design reproduced on a gargantuan scale the plant that Freyn’s engineers had designed for the US Steel Company at Gary, Indiana. This was crash mobilisation, on the German military model, creating ‘a rallying point for a technologically perfected future’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-048"></a>[48](#note-ch5-048) <a id="page-192-en"></a>〔原书第192页〕Planning meant the chaotic multiplication of factories, repeated improvisation, a future of proliferating numerical quantities and impossible annual targets. Soviet central planning inspired governments around the world with its ambition and speed, but its deployment of the future calculated as the rapid multiplication of physical plant and material output rendered the present more rather than less chaotic.

<a id="ch05-0057"></a>

值得一提的是，凯恩斯——关注苏联实验的人之一——并不是经济增长的理论家。他把摆脱经济萧条下行螺旋所需的扩张时期，想象为有限的暂时加速时期，通向未来的稳定状态。对凯恩斯来说，增长不是成功的指标，而是一种潜在的不稳定力量。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-049"></a>[49](#note-ch5-049)

Keynes, it is worth remembering – one of those who followed the Soviet experiment – was not a theorist of economic growth. He imagined the period of expansion required to escape from the downward spiral of economic depression as a limited period of temporary acceleration, leading to a future steady state. For Keynes, growth was not a metric of success but a potentially destabilising force.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-049"></a>[49](#note-ch5-049)

<a id="ch05-0058"></a>

在 1940 年代后期之前，经济学家把增长作为周期性实体扩张问题来讨论。在新政、战争和战后生产重组的背景下，他们把增长视为让闲置工厂重新投入运营、为失业者创造就业的问题。这种“扩张”被设想为生产活动增长和收缩的周期性过程——商业周期——的一部分。扩张本身不是目的。相反，目标是熨平高峰和低谷，必要时限制扩张以减轻衰退的严重程度，并努力减少可能妨碍从停滞中复苏的商品或劳动力供应瓶颈。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-050"></a>[50](#note-ch5-050)

Before the late 1940s, economists discussed growth as a question of periodic physical expansion. In the context of the New Deal, the war, and postwar restructuring of production, they saw growth as a question of putting idle plants back into service and creating jobs for those out of work. Such ‘expansion’ was envisioned as part of a cyclical process of the growth and contraction of productive activity – the business cycle. Expansion was not an end in itself. Instead, the goal was to smooth out peaks and troughs, restricting expansions where necessary to decrease the severity of downturns, and attempting to reduce bottlenecks in the supply of goods or labour that might hamper recovery from stagnation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-050"></a>[50](#note-ch5-050)

<a id="ch05-0059"></a>

到 1930 年代，早先对物质生活长期扩张的期望，已经让位于关于达到实体增长极限所导致的停滞的论点。在 1932 年的一次总统竞选演讲中，富兰克林·D. 罗斯福警告说：

By the 1930s, earlier prospects of a long-term expansion of material life had given way to arguments about a stagnation brought on by reaching the limits of physical growth. In a presidential campaign speech in 1932, Franklin D. Roosevelt warned:

<a id="ch05-0060"></a>

> 我们的工业设施已经建成；眼下的问题是，在现有条件下，它是否已经过度建设。我们最后的边疆早已到达，实际上不再有可自由取得的土地……我们无法邀请欧洲移民来分享我们无尽的富足。我们如今正在为本国人民提供单调乏味的生活……显然，这一切都要求重新评估价值。一个只会建造更多工业设施、创建更多铁路系统、组织更多公司的人，既可能带来帮助，也同样可能带来危险……我们现在的任务不是发现或开发自然资源，也不一定是生产更多商品。我们现在的任务是更冷静、更不戏剧化的事务：管理已有的资源和工厂……使现有经济组织服务于人民。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-051"></a>[51](#note-ch5-051)

> Our industrial plant is built; the problem just now is whether under existing conditions it is not overbuilt. Our last frontier has long since been reached, and there is practically no more free land . . . We are not able to invite the immigration from Europe to share our endless plenty. We are now providing a drab living for our own people . . . Clearly, all this calls for a re-appraisal of values. A mere builder of more industrial plants, a creator of more railroad systems, an organizer of more corporations, is as likely to be a danger as a help . . . Our task now is not discovery or exploitation of natural resources, or necessarily producing more goods. It is the soberer, less dramatic business of administering resources and plants already in hand . . . of adapting existing economic organizations to the service of the people.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-051"></a>[51](#note-ch5-051)

<a id="ch05-0061"></a>

<a id="page-193"></a>〔原书第193页〕1938 年，阿尔文·汉森在美国经济学会主席演讲中表达了同样的观点，即“长期停滞”学说。十年后，战后经济及其增长的效果，用围绕一个新对象——这个对象似乎具有无限增长的能力——的政治，取代了这种商业生活长期扩张和停滞的过程。

<a id="page-193-en"></a>〔原书第193页〕In 1938, the same views were expressed by Alvin Hansen in his address as President of the American Economic Association, as the doctrine of ‘secular stagnation’. A decade later, the postwar effect of the economy and its growth replaced this process of secular expansion and stagnation of commercial life with a politics oriented around a new object that was somehow capable, it seemed, of perpetual growth.

<a id="ch05-0062"></a>

### 技术知识中不可估量的资源

### Imponderable Resources in Technical Knowledge

<a id="ch05-0063"></a>

鉴于此前所有这些经验，如何才可能把一种指数增长模式转化为稳定效果？一个微小但重要的解决办法是一种新的再现方法：对数图。在绘制这个新对象即经济的增长图表时，人们可以不按线性纵轴、而按调整过以显示变化率的纵轴来标绘 GDP 随时间的增长；换言之，使用对数尺度，纵轴上的间隔代表比率。这一技巧把指数曲线变成一条直线。以每年 3.75% 增长的经济，于是可以表现为一条平稳的线，平缓而均匀地向上延伸，横贯页面。稳定的不是增长过程，而是其增长率。政治要求或经济决策的微小变化所产生的效果，如今可以清晰地投射在纸上——未来不再显得是一种无法阻挡的加速。

How, given all this previous experience, was it possible to turn a pattern of exponential growth into a stabilising effect? One small but significant solution to the problem was a new method of representation, the log plot. In drawing charts of the growth of this new object, the economy, one could plot the growth of GDP over time not against a linear vertical scale but with the scale adjusted to show the rate of change; in other words, by using a logarithmic scale, in which the intervals on the vertical axis represent ratios. This trick turns an exponential curve into a straight line. An economy growing at 3.75 per cent per year can then be represented as a steady line, rising gently and uniformly across the page. What is steady is not the process of increase, but its rate. The effect of small changes in political demands or economic decisions could now be clearly projected on paper – and the future no longer appeared as an unstoppable acceleration.

<a id="ch05-0064"></a>

通过这类物质性铭写，经济作为一个非物质对象出现了，一组计算把现代性的加速增长转化为一个看似稳定的未来。以这种方式以及许多其他方式，经济——也许仅仅持续了二三十年——使未来成为一种治理工具。

Through such material inscriptions, the economy emerged as a nonmaterial object, a set of calculations that converted the accelerating growth of modernity into an apparently stable future. In ways like this and many others, the economy, perhaps just for two or three decades, made the future an instrument of government.

<a id="ch05-0065"></a>

对数图虽然有用，但远不是使未来显得可治理的唯一装置。GDP 的计算——以及它排除了什么——本身也很重要。但伊拉克和其他中东国家那些工人同样重要。他们以两种方式提供了帮助。

The log plot, although useful, was far from the only device to make the future appear governable. The calculation of GDP – and what that excluded – was itself important. But so too were those workers in Iraq and other countries of the Middle East. They helped in two ways.

<a id="ch05-0066"></a>

第一，把能源生产外包到中东，帮助打破了战后北美、尤其是欧洲的劳工抗议浪潮；在这些抗议中，有组织的工人要求对集体财富的索取权进行更彻底的重新配置。煤矿工人与码头工人和铁路工人结盟，在把大众民主和更平等的生活形式带给西方方面发挥了关键作用。他们对抗资本化力量，在两次世界大战之间和战争年代促成了<a id="page-194"></a>〔原书第194页〕一次前所未有的财富再分配。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-052"></a>[52](#note-ch5-052)然而从现在起，工人收入的增加将不是来自利润再分配，而是来自那条稳定上升的线。输油管线和图表线条将协同运作。当然，如果增长率走平或回落，大多数人的收入将“自然地”停滞或下降。

First, the outsourcing of energy production to the Middle East helped break the postwar wave of labour protests, in North America and even more so in Europe, in which organised workers were demanding a more far-reaching reconfiguration of claims to collective wealth. Coal miners had played a critical role, in alliance with dockers and railway workers, in bringing popular democracy and more egalitarian forms of life to the West. Working against the forces of capitalisation, they had engineered <a id="page-194-en"></a>〔原书第194页〕an unprecedented redistribution of wealth in the interwar and wartime decades.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-052"></a>[52](#note-ch5-052) From now on, however, increases in the income of workers were to come not from a redistribution of profits but from the steadily rising line. Pipelines and graph lines would work together. If the rate of growth levelled off or dropped back, of course, the income of most people would ‘naturally’ stagnate or decline.

<a id="ch05-0067"></a>

第二，由于石油，生产率得以增长，从而收入得以增加；1945 年后的四分之一世纪里，石油供应增加，价格逐渐下降。石油公司竭力限制供应，并力图把供应欧洲的中东石油价格固定在美国石油高得多的水平上——这一价格由美国各州层面的生产配额设定，旨在维持石油稀缺，从而维持非同寻常的企业利润水平。但这些限制从来不够充分，产油国政府不断施压要求增加产量或提高收入份额，石油公司越来越难以应对这种压力。结果，石油价格逐渐下降。到 1970 年，石油实际价格自 1920 年以来每个十年都在下降。因此，几十年来，能源供应似乎无限，其成本对许多用途来说微不足道。如果说经济显得能够无限增长，那是由于二十世纪中叶能源体制的实际原因。

Second, productivity could grow, and thus incomes increase, thanks to oil, which for a quarter century after 1945 increased in supply and gradually declined in price. Oil companies tried hard to restrict supply and fix the price of Middle Eastern oil supplied to Europe at the much higher level of oil produced in the United States – a price set by state-level production quotas designed to maintain the scarcity of oil and thus extraordinary levels of corporate profit. But these restrictions were never adequate, and there was a constant pressure from the governments in oil-producing countries for increased output or an increased share of revenues, a pressure the oil companies found it increasingly difficult to manage. As a result, the price of oil gradually declined. By 1970, oil’s price in real terms had been declining in every decade since 1920. Thus, for several decades, the supply of energy seemed unlimited and its costs, for many purposes, negligible. If the economy appeared capable of unlimited growth, this was for practical reasons of the mid-twentieth-century energy regime.

<a id="ch05-0068"></a>

人们还可以探讨，经济中新的增长计算如何解决了和平时期军费开支的问题。在经济被制造出来之前，很难想象 1947—8 年之后建立永久军事化社会的决定，如何不以牺牲大多数人的福利和工资改善为代价。中东那些脆弱点——美国“国家安全”很快被认为在那里尤其面临风险——构成了这种新政治经济效果的一部分。

One could also explore how the new calculation of growth in an economy solved the problem of peacetime military spending. Before the making of the economy, it was difficult to imagine how the decision to build a permanently militarised society after 1947–8 was not somehow at the expense of improvements in welfare and wages for the majority. Those points of vulnerability in the Middle East, where US ‘national security’ was soon deemed to be especially at risk, formed part of this new political-economic effect.

<a id="ch05-0069"></a>

通过未来来治理人民，也成为管理前殖民地世界人口的一种装置。1940 年，经济统计学家科林·克拉克——他曾发展英国用于计算国民收入的方法——公布了各地国民收入的第一批估算。他对富国与穷国之间不平等程度的计算引起了震动。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-053"></a>[53](#note-ch5-053)但经济效果的这种普遍化和重复也引发了问题。例如，西蒙·库兹涅茨没有预料到他的 GDP 估算方法会被用来进行简单的跨国比较。这些统计暗示每个国家都有一个<a id="page-195"></a>〔原书第195页〕对等的经济，一种相似的货币化关系安排，可以进行比较和排序。然而，即使据说每个国家都有一个经济，在如今将被称为欠发达地区的地方产生这种效果，也需要不同的方法，并提供不同的政治可能性。其中最重要的可能性之一是，工业化国家可以试图不仅治理本国人口，还通过其余世界的未来来治理与它们的关系。

Governing people through their future also became a device for managing populations in the formerly colonised world. In 1940 the economic statistician Colin Clark, who had developed the methods used in Britain for the calculation of national income, published the first estimates of national incomes everywhere. His calculations of the degree of inequality between rich and poor countries caused a shock.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-053"></a>[53](#note-ch5-053) But this generalisation and repetition of the effect of the economy also raised questions. Simon Kuznets, for example, had not expected his methods of estimating GDP to be used to produce simple inter-country comparisons. The statistics implied that every country had an <a id="page-195-en"></a>〔原书第195页〕equivalent economy, a similar arrangement of monetarised relations, which could be compared and ranked. However, even if every country was said to have an economy, producing this effect in what were now to be called underdeveloped areas required different methods and offered different political possibilities. One of the most significant of these possibilities was that industrialised states could attempt to govern not only their own populations but also relations with the rest of the world through their futures.

<a id="ch05-0070"></a>

在国际关系中，未来出人意料地进入了治理。哈里·杜鲁门在 1949 年 1 月的总统就职演说中宣布了“发展”时代的到来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-054"></a>[54](#note-ch5-054)这一宣布是一个事后补充。当被要求提出一幅指导总统第二任期的未来愿景时，国务院官员提出了三点：支持联合国、马歇尔计划和北大西洋公约组织。但这些是总统在 1948 年秋整个竞选期间一直在讨论的现有政策。杜鲁门的一位助手告诉国务院，他需要第四点，某种“稍微有点原创性的东西”。国务院的人发现很难想象未来。“那些日子里，人们听到许多关于需要长远思考和长远规划的话，国务院的人也试图为此组织起来，”其中一人后来解释说。但“他们的规划努力通常陷入时事问题，例如如何处理大西洋下的意大利电缆，或购买锡应支付什么价格”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-055"></a>[55](#note-ch5-055)

In international relations, the future entered government unexpectedly. Harry Truman announced the arrival of the era of ‘development’ in his January 1949 inaugural presidential address.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-054"></a>[54](#note-ch5-054) The announcement was an afterthought. Asked to formulate a vision of the future to guide the president’s second term, officials in the State Department came up with three points: support for the United Nations (UN), the Marshall Plan, and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). But these were existing policies that the president had been discussing throughout the election campaign in the fall of 1948. An assistant for Truman told the State Department that he needed a fourth point, something ‘that’s just a bit original’. The men at State found it difficult to imagine the future. ‘One heard a great deal of the need for long-range thinking and long-range planning in those days, and the State Department men tried to organise themselves for it’, one of them later explained. But ‘their efforts at planning generally bogged down in topical questions, such as what to do with the Italian cable under the Atlantic, or what price to pay for tin’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-055"></a>[55](#note-ch5-055)

校注：本段用北约名称概述1948年竞选期间的政策。北约官方历史记载，正式公开条约谈判于1948年12月开始，北大西洋公约于1949年4月4日签署。这里应区分此前的联盟构想与已经成立的组织。正文保留原作追述。 https://nato.int/en/about-us/organization/founding-treaty

<a id="ch05-0071"></a>

一位一直协助拉丁美洲技术援助项目的官员建议，这类援助也可以提供给世界其他地区。这个想法被匆忙插入演讲。杜鲁门宣布了后来被称为“第四点”的内容（当时没有时间给这个想法命名）：“一项大胆的新计划，使我们科学进步和工业发展的益处可用于欠发达地区的改善和增长”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-056"></a>[56](#note-ch5-056)战后美国的发展政治并非作为帝国愿景、而是作为事后的补充而出现。

An official who had been helping with technical assistance programmes in Latin America suggested that such aid could also be offered to other parts of the world. The idea was hastily inserted in the speech. Truman announced what became known as Point Four (there had been no time to name the idea): ‘A bold new program for making the benefits of our scientific advances and industrial progress available for the improvement and growth of underdeveloped areas’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-056"></a>[56](#note-ch5-056) The postwar US politics of development emerged not as an imperial vision but as an afterthought.

<a id="ch05-0072"></a>

与国内国民经济这一装置一样，新的发展政治代表了一种把未来带入治理的新方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-057"></a>[57](#note-ch5-057)这种愿景不是关于美国如何与世界分享其财富，或支持中东石油工人争取获得石油公司利润更大份额、创造更公平生活形式的权利。1948 年 3 月，在古巴哈瓦那举行的联合国<a id="page-196"></a>〔原书第196页〕贸易与就业会议通过了《国际贸易组织宪章》。该组织与国际货币基金组织和世界银行并列，构成第三个机构，旨在治理国际贸易，包括石油和其他商品贸易。根据该协定，石油公司卡特尔和其他私人贸易安排将被公共监管的协定取代。国际投资和贸易将受劳工权利原则和充分就业权治理。印度和其他全球南方国家希望利用这一新组织，把更大份额的商品生产和贸易利润转给生产国。同时还有要求为这些国家制定马歇尔计划的呼声，以物质援助形式返还部分利润。美国反对这些提案。在美国国会拒绝批准《国际贸易组织宪章》后，建立该组织的协议破裂了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-058"></a>[58](#note-ch5-058)

As with the device of the national economy at home, the new politics of development represented a novel way of bringing the future into government.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-057"></a>[57](#note-ch5-057) The vision was not one of how America would share its wealth with the world or support the rights of oil workers in the Middle East trying to access a better share of oil company profits and create more equitable forms of life. In March 1948, the UN Conference on <a id="page-196-en"></a>〔原书第196页〕Trade and Employment in Havana, Cuba, had adopted the charter of an International Trade Organization. Forming a third body alongside the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, the organisation was intended to govern international trade, including trade in oil and other commodities. Under the agreement, oil company cartels and other private trade arrangements would be replaced with publicly regulated agreements. International investment and trade would be governed by principles of labour rights and the right to full employment. India and other countries from the South hoped to use the new organisation to redirect a greater share of the profits from production and trade in goods to the producer countries. There were concurrent demands for a Marshall Plan for such countries, to return some of those profits in the form of material assistance. The United States opposed such proposals. The agreement to create the International Trade Organization collapsed after the US Congress refused to ratify its charter.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-058"></a>[58](#note-ch5-058)

校注：底本概括为美国国会拒绝批准宪章。世界贸易组织的历史说明具体记为：国会反对强烈，美国政府于1950年宣布不再寻求国会批准《哈瓦那宪章》。原作概述不宜据此理解为一次明确的否决表决。 https://www.wto.org/English/thewto_e/whatis_e/tif_e/fact4_e.htm

<a id="ch05-0073"></a>

作为对国际贸易监管和把劳工权利扩展至伊拉克石油工人等群体的替代方案，杜鲁门的演讲动员了未来，如今被理解为各国经济的发展或增长。美国将作出的贡献不是物质援助，也不是对劳工权利的支持，而是某种无限的东西：技术知识。“我们能够用于援助其他民族的物质资源是有限的，”杜鲁门解释说。此外，“其资源和劳动力投入这些发展的人民的利益”，必须通过“对投资者的保障”来“平衡”。与这些必要的限制相反，“我们在技术知识方面不可估量的资源不断增长，取之不尽”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-059"></a>[59](#note-ch5-059)没有多余资本，不会有针对伊朗、埃及或印度等国的马歇尔计划，也不会支持组织工会或集体行动以改善就业和交换条件的权利。美国将用技术知识和建议的托词，取代物质资源和曾在西方创造广泛富裕的劳工权利。这些技术知识将在各个领域提供，但越来越多地采取一种主要形式：经济计算。这是一种与有限物质资源相反的、取之不尽的专门知识。

As a substitute for the international regulation of trade and the extension of labour rights to people like the oil workers of Iraq, Truman’s speech mobilised the future, now understood as the development or growth of national economies. The contribution the United States would make was not material assistance, or support for labour rights, but something unlimited: technical know-how. ‘The material resources which we can afford to use for assistance of other peoples are limited’, Truman explained. The ‘interest of the people whose resources and whose labor go into these developments’, moreover, had to be ‘balanced’ by ‘guarantees to the investor’. In contrast to these necessary limitations, ‘our imponderable resources in technical knowledge are constantly growing and are inexhaustible’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-059"></a>[59](#note-ch5-059) There was no capital to spare, and there would be no Marshall Plan for countries such as Iran, Egypt, or India, and no support for the right to unionise or act collectively to improve terms of employment and exchange. In place of material resources and the labour rights that had created widespread affluence in the West, the United States would offer the alibi of know-how and technical advice. The know-how would be offered in various fields, but, increasingly, in one main form: economic calculation. A know-how that, in contrast to limited material resources, was inexhaustible.

<a id="ch05-0074"></a>

<a id="page-197"></a>〔原书第197页〕

<a id="page-197-en"></a>〔原书第197页〕

<a id="ch05-0075"></a>

### 讲求物质的埃及人

### The Materially Minded Egyptian

<a id="ch05-0076"></a>

让我们回到 1948 年 5 月的阿拉伯世界，当时伊拉克石油工人的抗议在费卢杰以失败告终。碰巧的是，这座城镇把自己的名字给了那年夏天另一次挫折，即巴勒斯坦法卢贾发生的事件。法卢贾是加沙地区的一个村庄，大约位于沿海加沙城和山城哈利勒（希伯伦）之间；它得名于村民为一位来自伊拉克的十四世纪苏菲导师沙哈卜丁·法卢吉修建的圣陵，因而间接得名于那座伊拉克城镇。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-060"></a>[60](#note-ch5-060)1948 年 5 月的同一周对巴勒斯坦来说是命运攸关的一周。

Let us return to the Arab world in May 1948, where the protests of Iraqi oil workers had ended in defeat at Falluja. As it happens, the town gave its name to a second setback that summer, an event in Faluja, Palestine. A village in the District of Gaza, lying about halfway between the town of Gaza on the coast and the hill town of al-Khalil, or Hebron, Faluja was named after a shrine the villagers had built to a fourteenth-century Sufi master from Iraq, Shahab al-Din al-Faluji, and thus indirectly after the Iraqi town.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-060"></a>[60](#note-ch5-060) The same week of May 1948 was a fateful one for Palestine.

<a id="ch05-0077"></a>

英国曾宣布 5 月 14 日星期五将是其占领巴勒斯坦的最后一天。联合国曾提出一项方案，把该国在犹太复国主义定居者——他们集中在最大的城镇中的六个以及一些农业定居点——与土著人口——他们居住在该国各个地区，人数约为犹太移民的两倍——之间进行分治。但没有人同意实施分治，或组织把巴勒斯坦人从他们的城镇和村庄迁走，而族群分离的计划似乎要求这样做。当美国铁路工人被杜鲁门政府强迫复工、伊拉克大规模石油罢工遭到失败时，巴勒斯坦人面临一场更大的灾难。

Britain had announced that Friday, 14 May, would be the final day of its occupation of Palestine. The UN had proposed a scheme to partition the country between the Zionist settlers, who were concentrated in half a dozen of the largest towns and a number of agricultural settlements, and the indigenous population, who inhabited every region of the country and outnumbered the immigrant Jewish population by about two to one. But no one had agreed to implement the partition or organise the removal of the Palestinian people from their towns and villages, as the plan for ethnic separation apparently required. While railway workers in the United States were forced back to work by the Truman government, and the mass oil strike in Iraq met defeat, Palestinians faced a larger calamity.

<a id="ch05-0078"></a>

到英国人撤离时，组织良好的犹太复国主义部队的军事行动和恐怖行动已经使多达 40 万巴勒斯坦人逃离家园。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-061"></a>[61](#note-ch5-061)次日，5 月 15 日，埃及士兵从南方进入巴勒斯坦，而来自外约旦的一支与埃及方面竞争的军队（在与犹太复国主义领导层秘密谈判后）控制了约旦河西岸。埃及人最初控制了该国南部，但当犹太复国主义部队后来突破防线进入南部时，埃及军队的一个旅被困在法卢贾的一小块领土上——这个村庄连接着后来的西岸和加沙地区残余部分（后来称为加沙地带）。在四个月后的停战谈判中，埃及被迫放弃后来被称为“法卢贾口袋”的地区，尽管 1947 年的分治提案和 1948 年夏天联合国修订计划都曾要求保留该地区，作为残余巴勒斯坦国的一部分。作为埃及撤出被围部队的交换，新的犹太复国主义国家政府——其领导人经过一番辩论后决定把它称为“以色列”国而不是锡安——<a id="page-198"></a>〔原书第198页〕同意让该地区的巴勒斯坦人口留在原地。协议达成后几周内，法卢贾村民就在枪击、殴打、强奸未遂和其他恐怖行动中被赶走，这些行动由南巴勒斯坦犹太复国主义种族清洗行动指挥官伊扎克·拉宾“策划”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-062"></a>[62](#note-ch5-062)沿海地带与山地之间的人口联系和领土连续性被切断，为包围加沙地带和在南巴勒斯坦建立犹太复国主义定居点扫清了道路。

By the time the British departed, military actions and terror campaigns carried out by the well-organised Zionist forces had already driven as many as 400,000 Palestinians from their homes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-061"></a>[61](#note-ch5-061) On the following day, 15 May, Egyptian soldiers entered Palestine from the south, while a rival army from Transjordan (following secret talks with the Zionist leadership) took control of the west bank of the Jordan River. The Egyptians initially held the southern parts of the country, but, when the Zionist forces later broke through their lines into the south, an Egyptian brigade was trapped in a pocket of territory at Faluja, the village linking what would become the West Bank and a remnant of Gaza District, later termed the Gaza Strip. In the armistice negotiations four months later, Egypt was forced to abandon the Faluja Pocket, as the area became known, although the partition proposal of 1947 and a revised UN plan in the summer of 1948 had called for retaining that area as part of the rump Palestinian state. In exchange for Egypt withdrawing its besieged force, the government of the new Zionist state, whose leaders – after some debate – had decided to call it the state of ‘Israel’ rather than Zion, <a id="page-198-en"></a>〔原书第198页〕agreed to leave the area’s Palestinian population in place. Within weeks of the agreement, the villagers of Faluja were forced out, through a campaign of shootings, beatings, attempted rape, and other acts of terror, ‘orchestrated’ by the commander of the Zionist ethnic cleansing operations in southern Palestine, Yitzhak Rabin.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-062"></a>[62](#note-ch5-062) The population link and territorial contiguity between the coastal strip and the hills was severed, and the way cleared for the encirclement of the Gaza Strip and the Zionist settlement of southern Palestine.

<a id="ch05-0079"></a>

1948 年发生在伊拉克费卢杰和巴勒斯坦法卢贾这两个同名之地的失败，标志着同一相连过程的两面。埃及的失败巩固了犹太复国主义对南巴勒斯坦的控制，并把设法留在该国的大多数巴勒斯坦人限制在西岸和加沙地带两个飞地内。英国支持犹太复国主义定居点，部分是因为一个欧洲定居者少数群体的形成造成了一个脆弱点，需要帝国存在来保护它。第二次世界大战后，英国再也无力维持这种旧式保护国，其基础是需要对欧洲定居者提供武装保护。而定居者本身在战时军事化以及美苏竞相支持他们的竞争中得到加强，帮助迫使英国撤出。1948 年后，帝国保护采取新形式，建立在新的脆弱性之上。扩大石油生产使伊拉克、伊朗以及后来阿拉伯地区的劳工组织得以兴起，但也让美国作为保护者进入该地区，保护伊朗和沙特阿拉伯等国政权，这些政权将监控并阻止劳工组织。试图清除巴勒斯坦社会将造成另一个脆弱性，华盛顿后来作为以色列国保护者加以利用。

The two Faluja defeats of 1948, in Iraq and Palestine, mark two sides of a connected process. The Egyptian defeat consolidated the Zionist control of southern Palestine and the confinement of most of the Palestinians who managed to remain in the country within two enclaves, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. Britain had supported Zionist settlement in part because the creation of a European settler minority established a point of vulnerability that required an imperial presence for its protection. After the Second World War, Britain could no longer afford to run this old kind of protectorate, based on the need for armed protection of European settlers. And the settlers themselves, strengthened by their own wartime militarisation and by a competition between the United States and the USSR to support them, had helped force the British out. After 1948, imperial protection took new forms, based on new vulnerabilities. Expanding oil production enabled the rise of labour organising in Iraq, Iran, and later in Arabia, but it also allowed the United States into the region as the protector of regimes in countries such as Iran and Saudi Arabia that would police and prevent labour’s organisation. The attempted removal of Palestinian society would create another vulnerability that Washington was later to take advantage of, as protector of the state of Israel.

<a id="ch05-0080"></a>

在埃及，一场规模超过海湾国家、且有着悠久政治行动历史的劳工运动，在 1947—8 年组织了一波罢工和工业抗议。罢工从大型纺织厂和其他工业企业开始，然后蔓延到经营苏伊士运河的英法公司、苏伊士的壳牌炼油厂、石油分销商和许多其他企业。1948 年 4 月和 5 月巴勒斯坦的紧急状态使政府得以实施戒严、打破罢工，并监禁数千名政权的主要反对者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-063"></a>[63](#note-ch5-063)

In Egypt, a labour movement that was larger than those of the Gulf states and which had enjoyed a long history of political action had organised a wave of strikes and industrial protests in 1947–8. The strikes began in the large textile mills and other industrial enterprises, then spread to the Anglo-French company operating the Suez Canal, the Shell oil refinery at Suez, petroleum distributors, and many others. The emergency in Palestine in April and May 1948 allowed the government to impose martial law, break the strikes, and imprison thousands of leading opponents of the regime.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-063"></a>[63](#note-ch5-063)

<a id="ch05-0081"></a>

埃及军队在巴勒斯坦的失败激励了一群初级军官，他们组成了一个秘密组织“自由军官”，以打击该国军事和政治<a id="page-199"></a>〔原书第199页〕领导层的腐败，并支持结束英国在埃及持续帝国存在的民众运动。该组织领导人贾迈勒·阿卜杜勒·纳赛尔就是被困法卢贾口袋四个月的人之一。1952 年 7 月推翻英国支持的君主制后，自由军官推出了一项温和计划，把王室地产和其他大宗地产分配给无地者。这些政策遭到旧秩序的抵制，旧秩序的基础在大地主之中，而左翼团体则要求更激进的变革。1954 年 3 月，与反对者的摊牌以亲纳赛尔工会组织的大罢工告终——运输工人、银行雇员和苏伊士工人参与其中。这场力量展示使纳赛尔得以击败左右两方面的反对。为了扩大民众支持，政权宣布革命新时代，并采取一项宏伟计划来改造埃及的物质和集体生活。然而，这场革命不是要通过尼罗河谷的进一步土地再分配来运作，而是要通过一项扩展河谷的计划，即在阿斯旺修建高坝。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-064"></a>[64](#note-ch5-064)

The defeat of the Egyptian army in Palestine galvanised a group of junior army officers, who formed a secret organisation, the Free Officers, to combat the corruption of the country’s military and political <a id="page-199-en"></a>〔原书第199页〕leadership and support a popular movement to end Britain’s continuing imperial presence in Egypt. The leader of the group, Gamal Abd al-Nasser, was one of those who had been trapped for four months in the Faluja Pocket. After overthrowing the British-supported monarchy in July 1952, the Free Officers introduced a modest programme to redistribute the royal estates and other very large landholdings to the landless. These policies met resistance from the old order, with its base among large landowners, while leftist groups demanded more radical change. In March 1954, a showdown with opponents culminated in a general strike organised by pro-Nasser unions – transport workers, bank employees, and the workers at Suez. The show of strength enabled Nasser to defeat opposition from right and left. To extend its popular support, the regime declared a new era of revolution and adopted a grand plan to remake Egyptian material and collective life. The revolution, however, was to operate not through a further redistribution of land in the Nile Valley but through a scheme to expand the valley, by building the High Dam at Aswan.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-064"></a>[64](#note-ch5-064)

<a id="ch05-0082"></a>

世界银行提出帮助资助阿斯旺项目的故事广为人知。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-065"></a>[65](#note-ch5-065)由于资助欧洲战后重建的使命已由马歇尔计划接替，世界银行抓住机会表明自己已从金融机构转变为如今可称为“发展”机构的组织，提出为世界上最大的堆石坝提供融资。这家银行甚至考虑把大坝作为解决巴勒斯坦问题的工具：把灌溉水从苏伊士运河下引到西奈北部，并在那里安置巴勒斯坦难民，或许可以让联合国近东巴勒斯坦难民救济和工程处——为救济难民而设立的机构——分担大坝成本。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-066"></a>[66](#note-ch5-066)但犹太复国主义者对西奈另有计划。1955 年 2 月，以色列对加沙的埃及军队发动袭击，由此迈出了向南巴勒斯坦其余地区和西奈推进、占领直至苏伊士的埃及领土的第一步。

The story of the World Bank’s offer to help fund the Aswan project is well known.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-065"></a>[65](#note-ch5-065) Having lost its mission of funding postwar reconstruction in Europe to the Marshall Plan, the Bank seized the opportunity to demonstrate its transformation from a financial institution into what could now be called a ‘development’ agency, by offering to finance the largest rock-fill dam in the world. The Bank even contemplated using the dam as an instrument for solving the Palestine question: bringing irrigation water under the Suez Canal to northern Sinai and settling Palestine refugees there might have allowed the UN Relief and Works Agency, the agency set up to provide relief for the refugees, to contribute to the cost of the dam.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-066"></a>[66](#note-ch5-066) But the Zionists had other plans for Sinai. In February 1955 Israel launched an attack on the Egyptian forces in Gaza, taking the first step to capture the remainder of southern Palestine and seize Sinai, occupying Egyptian territory as far as Suez.

<a id="ch05-0083"></a>

与此同时，英国正在制定在埃及发动军事反政变和暗杀纳赛尔的计划，以重新扶植一个新殖民政权。军情六处内部的策划者在暗杀装置设计上遇到困难——一台装有炸药的雷明顿剃须刀未能正常运作——而且无论如何，阴谋被揭发了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-067"></a>[67](#note-ch5-067)

Meanwhile, the British were developing plans for a military countercoup in Egypt and the assassination of Nasser, to reinstall a neocolonial regime. The plotters within MI6 had difficulties with the design of the assassination devices – a Remington shaver fitted with explosives failed to operate properly – and, in any case, the plot was uncovered.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-067"></a>[67](#note-ch5-067)

<a id="ch05-0084"></a>

美国人断定，有更简单的办法应对埃及民族主义政府的威胁。他们不消灭总统，而是消灭本应增强其权力的机制，即修建水坝。1956 年 7 月，<a id="page-200"></a>〔原书第200页〕华盛顿取消了对水坝融资的参与，令世界银行感到意外，并使其无法继续提供贷款。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-068"></a>[68](#note-ch5-068)然而，像那把雷明顿剃须刀一样，这一装置未能摧毁目标。取消贷款给了纳赛尔把苏伊士运河公司国有化的机会；该公司的资本化收入最初曾被视为资助水坝的手段。

The Americans decided that there was an easier way to deal with the threat of a nationalist government in Egypt. Rather than eliminating the president, they would kill the mechanism that was supposed to increase his power, the construction of the dam. In July 1956, <a id="page-200-en"></a>〔原书第200页〕Washington cancelled its participation in the funding for the dam, surprising the World Bank and leaving it unable to proceed with the loan.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-068"></a>[68](#note-ch5-068) Like the Remington shaver, however, the device failed to destroy its target. Cancellation of the loan offered Nasser the opportunity to nationalise the Suez Canal Company, whose capitalised revenues had been originally discussed as the means to finance the dam.

<a id="ch05-0085"></a>

英国的反应是搁置暗杀计划，支持以色列——已得到法国支持——入侵埃及、夺取运河并以武力推翻纳赛尔政府的计划。然而，10 月底发动的英法以三方进攻很快暴露了新殖民暴力的局限。入侵者试图把夺取西奈和运河描绘为一场确保重要交通通道的警察行动，这是八年前杜鲁门接管美国铁路的帝国版本。但英国战争策划者意识到军事力量的局限，也希望借助一种经济装置来协助军事行动：一种在普通埃及人中间运作的计算形式。

Britain responded by putting aside its assassination plans and supporting the Israeli scheme, already backed by the French, to invade Egypt, take the canal, and overthrow Nasser’s government by force. Yet the Anglo-French-Israeli attack, launched at the end of October, quickly exposed the limits of neocolonial violence. The invaders tried to portray the seizing of Sinai and the canal as a police action that secured a vital communication route, an imperial version of Truman’s seizure of the US railways eight years earlier. But British war planners, aware of the limits of military power, also hoped to enlist an economic device to assist the military operation: a form of calculation operating among ordinary Egyptians.

<a id="ch05-0086"></a>

英国不会试图强行入侵开罗。他们计划在运河登陆，通过摧毁铁路、发电站和炼油厂来破坏国家稳定。军事策划者认为，这种对埃及能源基础设施的破坏所造成的经济后果，将制造公众对政变的支持。他们推论说，既然“讲求物质的埃及平民不大可能长期承受战时艰苦或实际战斗经历”，“问题看来就不大可能是‘公众对政权的支持是否会崩溃’，而是‘崩溃会多快发生’”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-069"></a>[69](#note-ch5-069)在这种军事工程化的经济力量支持下，纳赛尔的将军们将把他赶下台，英国将不战而入开罗。

The British would not attempt to invade Cairo by force. They planned to land troops at the canal and destabilise the country by destroying railways, power stations, and oil refineries. The economic consequences of this destruction of the country’s energy infrastructure, the military planners argued, would create public support for a coup. Since ‘the materially-minded Egyptian civilian is unlikely long to sustain the rigours of wartime or the actual experience of battle’, they reasoned, ‘it seems less likely to be a question of “if there is a collapse of public . . . support for the Regime” as “how quickly that will take place”’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-069"></a>[69](#note-ch5-069) Backed by this military-engineered economic force, Nasser’s generals would remove him from power and the British would occupy Cairo without a battle.

<a id="ch05-0087"></a>

英国人从未有机会尝试以军事手段激发这些地方经济计算的力量。美国急于保护它正在该地区构建、以与沙特阿拉伯结盟为基础、由公司构建的“石油秩序”，拒绝支持入侵。那年夏天沙特石油工人又举行了一次总罢工，因此，虽然美国急于削弱纳赛尔，却不愿把其帝国手段与殖民占领联系在一起。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-070"></a>[70](#note-ch5-070)美国人认定在更大规模上部署经济计算更为有效，认为剥夺埃及的发展援助是更有效的武器。然而，经济治理术的新方法<a id="page-201"></a>〔原书第201页〕在国内提供了军事行动的替代方案，而在埃及，试图在海外强加集体经济计算的规训却未能取得结果。

The British never had the chance to try provoking militarily these forces of local economic calculation. Anxious to protect the corporate-built ‘petroleum order’ it was constructing in the region, based on an alliance with Saudi Arabia, the United States refused to support the invasion. Saudi oil workers had staged another general strike that summer, so, while the United States was keen to weaken Nasser, it was unwilling to associate its imperial methods with colonial occupation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-070"></a>[70](#note-ch5-070) Having decided that deploying economic calculation on a larger scale was more effective, the Americans thought depriving Egypt of development assistance was a more effective weapon. But whereas the new methods of economentality had offered an alternative to military action <a id="page-201-en"></a>〔原书第201页〕at home, the attempt in Egypt to impose the discipline of collective economic calculation abroad had failed to achieve results.

<a id="ch05-0088"></a>

美国通过发展埃及经济来约束埃及的计划失败，始于一个事实：埃及不需要世界银行贷款。大坝的最初计划曾得到一个德国工程公司联合体的支持。德国人引入英国公司，作为获得信用货币的途径：埃及拥有大量外汇储备，即在伦敦积累的英镑债权余额，来自第二次世界大战期间向英国提供的商品和服务。英国公司游说伦敦释放这些余额，并试图把释放条件设为通过英德联合体修建水坝。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-071"></a>[71](#note-ch5-071)对于在战后萧条的欧洲急需业务的工程公司来说，大坝与其说是拦蓄和引流尼罗河水的计划，不如说是把伦敦的英镑债权余额经由南埃及的绕道转入公司收入的计划。未来硬通货资金的另一个来源是经过苏伊士运河的航运通行费，每年总计 1,200 万至 1,500 万英镑，并随着石油运输增长而迅速增加。这些收入的三分之二从航运国直接流向巴黎和伦敦。但到 1968 年，大约在大坝贷款缓期支付的利息可能到期之时，运河将归还埃及所有。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-072"></a>[72](#note-ch5-072)

The failure of the US plan to discipline Egypt through the development of its economy began with the fact that Egypt did not need the World Bank loan. Initial plans for the dam had been backed by a consortium of German engineering firms. The Germans brought British firms on board, as a way to access credit money: Egypt had large foreign reserves, sterling credits built up in London from goods and services it had provided to Britain during the Second World War. British firms lobbied London to release the credits and tried to get the release conditional on building a dam through the Anglo-German consortium.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-071"></a>[71](#note-ch5-071) To engineering firms, desperate for business in a depressed postwar Europe, the dam was not a scheme to store up and divert the Nile so much as a scheme to divert the sterling credits in London, via a detour through southern Egypt, into company revenue. An alternative source of future hard-currency funds was the shipping tolls from traffic passing through the Suez Canal, which totalled 12 to 15 million sterling per year and were increasing rapidly as oil shipments grew. Two-thirds of this income went from the shipping countries directly into Paris and London. But by 1968, about the time the delayed interest on a loan for the dam might become due, the canal would revert to Egyptian ownership.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-072"></a>[72](#note-ch5-072)

<a id="ch05-0089"></a>

事实上，埃及甚至不需要这座水坝。这大概是世界银行 1950 年代初首席发展经济学家保罗·罗森斯坦—罗丹的看法。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-073"></a>[73](#note-ch5-073)他曾反对通过投资水坝、运河和水电站等基础设施来发展“落后地区”，因为这需要进口建筑机械、涡轮机和其他昂贵资本品。他认为，这些国家应专注于小规模、劳动密集型制造业。这种制造业必须扩展到足够大的范围，以利用相互关联的小企业聚集所产生的社会利润，创造工资劳动者，而这些工资劳动者又会产生对其他工资劳动者所生产商品的需求——这种在“国民经济”层面上的互补效应，是个别投资者在企业层面计算未来利润时无法计算的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-074"></a>[74](#note-ch5-074)

In fact, Egypt did not even need the dam. This was probably the view of the Bank’s leading development economist in the early 1950s, Paul Rosenstein-Rodan.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-073"></a>[73](#note-ch5-073) He had argued against developing ‘backward regions’ through investment in infrastructure such as dams, canals, and hydro-electric power stations, which required imports of construction machinery, turbines, and other expensive capital goods. Such countries, he believed, should focus on small-scale, labour-intensive manufacturing. This had to be done extensively enough to take advantage of the social profit that arises from the clustering of interrelated small firms, producing wage earners who would create a demand for goods produced by other wage earners – the kind of complementary effects at the level of the ‘national economy’ that individual investors, figuring future profit at the level of the enterprise, were unable to calculate.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-074"></a>[74](#note-ch5-074)

<a id="ch05-0090"></a>

但世界银行无法资助工业化。它必须通过出售债券来筹集投资资本。为了在华尔街推销这些债务，它需要大型、可衡量、可资本化的结构。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch5-075"></a>[75](#note-ch5-075)农业和小工业过于地方化、过于微小、过于短期，也过于依赖各种形式的社会利润，银行家无法据以计算未来债务偿还的当下<a id="page-202"></a>〔原书第202页〕价值。正如我们将在[第七章](#ch07-0001)探讨的，水坝、道路和发电厂等大型基础设施项目产生的未来回报，可以在经济而非企业层面上计算。而且，由于这个可计算的未来即经济，如今是政府的责任，主权国家可以被要求承担偿还贷款的责任，从而降低华尔街的风险。

But the Bank could not fund industrialisation. It had to raise investment capital by selling bonds. To market these debts on Wall Street, it needed large, measurable, capitalisable structures.<a id="ref-en-note-ch5-075"></a>[75](#note-ch5-075) Agriculture and small industry were too localised, too small, too short-term, and too dependent on forms of social profit for bankers to calculate the current <a id="page-202-en"></a>〔原书第202页〕value of future debt payments. Large infrastructure projects such as dams, roads, and power plants, as we will explore in [chapter 7](#ch07-0001), produced future returns that could be calculated at the level of the economy, rather than the enterprise. And because this calculable future, the economy, was now the responsibility of government, a sovereign state could be made liable for the repayment of loans, reducing Wall Street’s risks.

<a id="ch05-0091"></a>

当世界银行参与水坝融资时，它对项目成本进行了自己的计算。通过这样做，它引入了一种不同的计算方式。首先，建设成本不仅包括建造水坝和供应涡轮机的工作。该项目需要全国性电网和配水系统。但更重要的是，成本核算必须把未来纳入计算。这些包括贷款利息支付，这部分相对容易确定。但也包括用于修建水坝及其相关基础设施的贷款的未来影响。随着建筑工人的工资转化为消费形式，需求将上升，价格将攀升，货币将贬值。进口成本反过来将增加，国际借贷成本将上升。所有这些相互关联的未来成本，如今都可以通过经济的衡量和计算呈现出来。

When the Bank became involved in the funding of the dam, it performed its own calculation of the costs of the project. By doing so, it introduced a different calculus. The construction costs, first of all, comprised not just the work of building the dam and supplying turbines. The project needed a nationwide electrical grid and water distribution system. But, more importantly, the costs had to calculate the future. These included interest payments on the loan, which were relatively simple to determine. But they also included the future effects of the loans spent on construction of the dam and its associated infrastructure. As wages for construction workers were turned into forms of consumption, demand would rise, prices would climb, and the currency would be devalued. The cost of imports, in turn, would increase, and the cost of international borrowing would go up. All these interconnected future costs could now be brought into view by the measurement and calculation of the economy.

<a id="ch05-0092"></a>

鉴于这些高得多的成本，世界银行计算出，在贷款期内，水坝将耗尽埃及政府的全部可支配支出。因此，作为贷款的交换，世界银行提议，政府必须在十五年或更长的贷款偿还期内将其预算提交国际检查和管控。水坝的规模造就了一个可以在国民经济计算层面上监测的项目。修建水坝需要铺设一个未来，一个在时间中展开的经济，埃及如今将通过它受到治理。纳赛尔政权选择把运河国有化，从而拒绝接受这种治理模式。

Given these much higher costs, the Bank calculated that the dam would consume the entire disposable spending of the Egyptian government for the period of the loan. So, in exchange for the loan, the Bank proposed that the government would have to submit its budget to international inspection and control for the fifteen years or more of loan repayment. The scale of the dam created a project that could be monitored at the level of the calculation of the national economy. Building the dam required putting in place a future, an economy unfolding in time, through which Egypt would now be governed. In opting instead to nationalise the Canal, the Nasser regime refused to accept this mode of government.

<a id="ch05-0093"></a>

第二次世界大战后的几年里，一个新的未来到来了。它作为一套用于治理当下关系的特定技术而被创造出来，以便管理经济；经济不仅被理解为一个数值总体，而且被理解为一组动态力量，被快照捕捉并处于管理之下。经济不只是治理的新对象，更是一种效果：一系列反复计算的产物。

In the years after the Second World War, a new future arrived. It was brought into being as a specific set of techniques for governing relations in the present in order to manage the economy, understood not just as a numerical totality but as a dynamic set of forces, caught in snapshot and under management. The economy was not simply a new object of government but rather an effect: the product of a series of iterated calculations.

<a id="ch05-0094"></a>

<a id="page-203"></a>〔原书第203页〕然而，这种效果依赖的不仅是新的计算技术。它是在技术和物质上被建构的。在这里考察的案例中，我们看到工业化国家国内政治生活的经济化如何依赖于能源外包；这一变化部分是对战后有组织工人努力争取另一种集体未来——在这种未来中，股东即资本化受益者的利润必须调整以适应当下人们的索取权——的回应。反过来，能源成本下降、尤其是中东石油成本下降，帮助产生了经济作为一种能够无限增长之对象的效果。正如我们将在最后一章进一步看到的，经济的增长将为扩大了的资本化提供托词。经济的计算实践依赖于在中东维持专制和不平等的统治形式。西方战后的经济治理术作为一种围绕经济及其增长组织起来的治理模式，部分是中东制造出来的效果。

<a id="page-203-en"></a>〔原书第203页〕Yet the effect depended on more than just new calculative techniques. It was constructed technically and materially. In the case examined here, we have seen how the economisation of domestic political life in industrialised countries depended upon the outsourcing of energy, a change brought about partly in response to the efforts of organised workers in the postwar years to claim a different collective future, one in which the profits of shareholders – the beneficiaries of capitalisation – would have to be adjusted to the claims of those in the present. In turn, the decreasing cost of the energy, in particular of oil from the Middle East, helped generate the effect of the economy as an object capable of unlimited growth. The growth of the economy, as we will see further in the final chapter, would provide the alibi for an expanded capitalisation. The calculative practices of the economy depended on maintaining forms of autocratic and inegalitarian rule in the Middle East. The postwar economentality of the West, as a mode of government organised around the economy and its growth, was an effect manufactured partly in the Middle East.

<a id="ch05-0095"></a>

经济作为一种通过未来进行治理的模式，只有效地运作了二三十年。到 1960 年代后期，它所依赖的生产率增长、能源使用、廉价石油和中东政治形式都承受着压力。我们以时间加速的方式思考现代性，以当下体验的时间与一个似乎正以指数变化率向前移动的未来的关系来思考。大约从二十世纪中叶起，仅仅几十年间，一个不同的未来进入了治理。

The economy worked effectively as a mode of government through the future for only two or three decades. By the late 1960s, the forms of productivity growth, energy use, cheap oil, and Middle Eastern politics on which it depended were all under pressure. We think of modernity in terms of accelerating time, of time experienced in the present in relation to a future that appears to be moving ahead at an exponential rate of change. From around the mid-century, for just a few decades, a different future had entered government.


# 第六章　市场的属性

<a id="ch06-0001"></a>

<a id="page-204"></a>〔原书第204页〕

<a id="page-204-en"></a>〔原书第204页〕

<a id="ch06-0002"></a>

## 第六章　市场的属性

## 6 The Properties of Markets

<a id="ch06-0003"></a>

在二十世纪最后二十五年，横跨北大西洋世界及其他地区，一种新的治理模式确立起来，它在对“经济”的治理之外兴起，与之并存，并很快在重要性上与之匹敌。人们发现自己的生活通过一种新颖而更强大的抽象得到管理，这种观念将为以未来为代价的生活提供新的托词。这种抽象被称为“市场”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-001"></a>[1](#note-ch6-001)

In the last quarter of the twentieth century, across the North Atlantic world and beyond, a new mode of government took hold, emerging alongside the government of ‘the economy’ and soon rivalling it in importance. People found their lives managed through a novel and more powerful abstraction, an idea that was to provide a new alibi for living at the expense of the future. The abstraction was called ‘the market’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-001"></a>[1](#note-ch6-001)

<a id="ch06-0004"></a>

当然，市场交换的观念并不新鲜。古典政治经济学家曾大量论述“商业社会”。然而，两项变化把市场转变为一种更有效的治理机制。第一项我们已注意到。十九世纪末的帝国时代，交换行为开始被理解为一种数学装置。正如我们在[第四章](#ch04-0001)所见，货币市场的突然增长促成了经济学新科学的诞生。股市和其他交易所产生了“高度人为的过程”，标准化商品在其中以即时可知的价格交易。经济学家以这些场所为范例，首次基于边际效用原则制定了供求法则。人的劳动、商品或货币的价值，如今据说不是由其内在品质、而仅仅由其价格决定。定价是一个自动过程，供给和需求的微小增量在那里达到均衡点。所谓“新古典”经济学的信条被普遍接受花了一些时间。但在这种观点的信奉者中间，市场可以被视为一台有效决定资源和回报分配的机器。

The idea of market exchange, of course, was nothing new. The classical political economists had written extensively on the topic of ‘commercial society’. However, two changes transformed the market into a more effective mechanism of government. The first of these we have already noted. Towards the end of the nineteenth century, in the age of empire, the act of exchange came to be understood as a mathematical device. As we saw in [chapter 4](#ch04-0001), the sudden growth of money markets helped create the new science of economics. Stock markets and other exchanges produced ‘highly artificial processes’, where a standardised good was traded at instantly knowable prices. Taking such sites as exemplary, economists formulated the laws of supply and demand, based for the first time on the principle of marginal utility. The value of human labour, goods, or money was now said to be determined not by their intrinsic qualities, but simply by their price. Pricing was an automatic process, in which small increments of supply and demand reached a point of equilibrium. It took some time before the tenets of what became known as ‘neoclassical’ economics were generally accepted. But, among the adherents of this view, the market could be considered a machine that efficiently determined the allocation of resources and rewards.

<a id="ch06-0005"></a>

<a id="page-205"></a>〔原书第205页〕第二项变化发生在一个世纪之后。从 1970 年代后期起，这些“人为过程”开始被视为某种大得多的东西：一种治理共同世界关系的普遍机制。这类机制的增殖如今以单数形式被称为“市场”。这一第二项变化由一个组织良好的政治运动赋予力量。该运动被称为新自由主义，它把自己的项目界定为削减国家的作用，让市场的底层法则自由运作。然而在实践中，该运动帮助生产了市场作为一般抽象的产物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-002"></a>[2](#note-ch6-002)

<a id="page-205-en"></a>〔原书第205页〕A second change occurred a century later. From the late 1970s, these ‘artificial processes’ came to be seen as something much more: a general mechanism for the government of relations in the common world. The proliferation of such mechanisms was now referred to in the singular, as simply ‘the market’. This second change was given force by a well-organised political movement. Known as neoliberalism, the movement defined its project as curtailing the role of the state to allow free operation to the underlying laws of the market. In practice, however, the movement helped to produce the market as a general abstraction.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-002"></a>[2](#note-ch6-002)

<a id="ch06-0006"></a>

市场作为治理性抽象的出现，是一个与上一章所探讨的、早一代人的经济出现相平行的过程。在这两个案例中，先前被理解为一组多样过程的东西，都被转变成某种自身存在的对象。事实上，人们可以认为，“经济”和“市场”最初是并排出现的，作为捕捉集体生活应据以被治理之整体的相互竞争概念。在两次世界大战之间，强调政府在监管和规划经济关系中作用的经济学家开始把这些通过新统计知识形式揭示出来的关系称为“经济”。同一时期，政府计划和监管的反对者——正如我们先前在接过马克斯·韦伯工作的人中所见——主张，统计知识永远无法准确衡量经济关系的复杂性。作为替代，他们提出，个体经济行动者所拥有的分散知识——往往是默会知识——，通过市场交换转化为他们买卖的价格。从整体来看，价格作为一个知识体系运作，类似于政府关于经济的统计知识，却比后者更优越。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-003"></a>[3](#note-ch6-003)这类论点使人们有可能把“市场”想象为经济的二重身，模仿其自称构成自身对象的说法。二十世纪中叶战争时期和凯恩斯主义经济计划的兴起，把这种竞争性观念推入背景。一代人之后，随着新自由主义运动从边缘出现并开始决定经济话语和政策的框架，市场走向前台。

The appearance of the market as a governing abstraction was a process that paralleled the emergence of the economy a generation earlier, as explored in the last chapter. In both cases, what was previously understood as a diverse set of processes was transformed into something like an object in itself. One could argue, in fact, that, initially, ‘the economy’ and ‘the market’ emerged side by side, as rival concepts for capturing the totality through which collective life should be governed. In the interwar years, economists who emphasised the role of government in the regulation and planning of economic relations began to refer to those relations, revealed through new forms of statistical knowledge, as ‘the economy’. In the same period, opponents of government planning and regulation, as we saw earlier among those who took up the work of Max Weber, argued that statistical knowledge could never accurately measure the complexity of economic relations. As an alternative, they proposed that the dispersed, often tacit knowledge of individual economic actors is translated by market exchange into the prices at which they buy and sell. Taken as a whole, prices operate as a knowledge system, analogous but superior to the government’s statistical knowledge of the economy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-003"></a>[3](#note-ch6-003) Such arguments made it possible to imagine ‘the market’ as a double or doppelganger of the economy, mimicking its claims to form an object in itself. The ascendancy of wartime and Keynesian economic planning in the middle decades of the twentieth century pushed this rival conception into the background. A generation later, as the neoliberal movement emerged from the margins and began to determine the framework of economic discourse and policy, the market came to the forefront.

<a id="ch06-0007"></a>

新古典经济学的批评者常常指责它错误再现。经济学家把社会生活的复杂性简化为理性行动者计算的结果：这些行动者回应以价格表达的激励，以使自身利益最大化。批评者<a id="page-206"></a>〔原书第206页〕声称，这样一来，他们把任何关于行动主体如何构成、利益如何形成、激励如何管理或资源最初如何分配的论述都排除在画面之外。这种批评很有力，但也有一个明显弱点：它假定经济学的工作是为一个外在于自身的世界建模。

Critics of neoclassical economics often accuse it of misrepresentation. Economists reduce the complexities of social life to the outcomes of the calculations of rational agents responding to incentives, expressed as prices, in ways that maximise their interests. In doing so, the critics <a id="page-206-en"></a>〔原书第206页〕claim, they leave out of the picture any account of how agencies are constituted, interests are formed, incentives are managed, or resources are initially distributed. This criticism has plenty of force, but also a clear weakness: it assumes that the work of economics is to model a world external to itself.

<a id="ch06-0008"></a>

如果我们以不同方式看待经济学呢？假设它从技术政治世界内部运作，而不是从某个外部位置运作。假设它提供一套计算工具和其他技术装置，其力量不在于对外部现实的再现，而在于对组织技术实践——被理解为市场——的有用性。这就是经济化过程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-004"></a>[4](#note-ch6-004)用唐纳德·麦肯齐的话说，产生市场价格的算法应被视为“一台引擎，而不是一台相机”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-005"></a>[5](#note-ch6-005)新古典经济学的狭隘因此有其目的。它有助于执行米歇尔·卡隆所谓的“框定”操作，即“纠缠”和“解缠”的过程。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-006"></a>[6](#note-ch6-006)经济理论必须假定一个已经由买者、卖者和待交换商品或服务组成的世界。然而，除非世界被简化以创造买者、卖者和商品，否则交换无法发生。复杂的人类与非人类力量之间的依附能力和依赖关系必须被解缠，才能创造出像理性经济行动者或即时可得、可衡量的商品或服务这样简单的东西。如果不存在某些安排来排除某些依附、把许多成本或索取权排除在计算之外、使共同世界的大部分变得不可知，并否认对气候崩溃、物种灭绝和种族灭绝等灾难性后果的责任，市场交换就无法运作。同样，正如卡隆所示，如果没有某种产生重新纠缠的过程、逐步在行动者和商品之间创造依附，交易也无法进行。

What if we think of economics differently? Suppose it operates from within the technopolitical world, not from some place outside it. Suppose it provides a set of instruments of calculation and other technical devices, whose strength lies not in their representation of an external reality but in their usefulness for organising technical practices, understood as markets. This is the process of economisation.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-004"></a>[4](#note-ch6-004) In the words of Donald MacKenzie, the algorithms that produce market prices should be thought of as ‘an engine, not a camera’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-005"></a>[5](#note-ch6-005) The narrowness of neoclassical economics then serves a purpose. It helps perform the operations that Michel Callon calls ‘framing’, or the process of ‘entangling’ and ‘disentangling’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-006"></a>[6](#note-ch6-006) Economic theory must assume a world that already consists of buyers, sellers, and goods or services to be exchanged. However, an exchange cannot take place unless the world is simplified to create the buyer, the seller, and the good. Complex powers of attachment and relations of dependence among human and nonhuman forces must be disentangled to create something as simple as a rational economic agent, or an instantly available and measurable good or service. Market exchange would not work if arrangements were not in place to exclude some attachments, leave many costs or claims out of the calculation, render large parts of the common world unknowable, and deny responsibility for catastrophic consequences, such as climate collapse, species extinction, and genocide. Equally, as Callon shows, transactions could not take place if there were not some process of producing the re-entanglements that progressively create attachments between agents and goods.

<a id="ch06-0009"></a>

经济分析并不描述这些排除和依附过程。相反，它帮助生产这些过程。它提供方法来区分在交换行为中什么可以计入、什么不能计入，哪些安排构成行动者、哪些不能，以及什么必须被计入、什么不应被计入。从这个角度看，不应根据经济学所再现——或未能再现——的现实来分析经济学，而应根据它帮助产生的安排、纠缠和排除来分析。

Economic analysis does not describe these processes of exclusion and attachment. Rather, it helps to produce them. It provides ways to distinguish what can count in the act of exchange from what cannot, which arrangements constitute agents and which do not, and what must be accounted for and what should not. From this perspective, economics should be analysed not in terms of the reality it represents – or fails to represent – but in terms of the arrangements, entanglements, and exclusions it helps to produce.

<a id="ch06-0010"></a>

经济学把对其所建模的世界进行格式化的工作置于视野之外，这个世界似乎已经由买者、<a id="page-207"></a>〔原书第207页〕卖者和商品组成。这样做时，它还做了另一件事。它把资产化工作——把未来生活形式转化为收入流、并使这种未来收入成为当下可以交易商品的过程——置于视野之外。这正是从未来榨取所依赖的过程。在这方面，“市场”观念执行了双重抽象。它抽象掉像卡隆这样的学者所描述的一切框定和（解）缠工作，复杂世界由此被简化为市场关系。但它也抽象掉一个时间过程，其中对未来的支配被误认为市场交易的非时间性、瞬时事件。市场是一种有效抽象，不仅因为它略去了或简化了生产行动者和商品世界的工作，而且因为它略去了生产一个可在当下被攫取的未来的工作。这样，市场交易看似瞬时的时间性——正如经济学工作中所框定的那样——促成了资本的托词。

Economics places out of sight the work that is performed to format the world it models, a world that seems already made up of buyers, <a id="page-207-en"></a>〔原书第207页〕sellers, and commodities. In doing so, it does something else. It places out of sight the work of assetising, or the process of turning future forms of life into streams of revenue and making that future revenue into a commodity that can be traded in the present. This is the very process on which extraction from the future depends. In this respect, the idea of ‘the market’ performs a double abstraction. It abstracts from all the framing and (dis)entangling that scholars like Callon describe, in which complex worlds are simplified into market relations. But it also abstracts from a temporal process, in which the command of the future is mistaken for the atemporal, instantaneous event of a market transaction. The market is an effective abstraction, not only because it abstracts from, or simplifies, the work of producing a world of agents and commodities, but because it abstracts from the work of producing a future open to capture in the present. In this way, the seemingly instantaneous temporality of a market transaction, as framed in the work of economics, contributes to the alibi of capital.

<a id="ch06-0011"></a>

经济学并不单独运作。它与其他技术、信息集合、安排和机构一起运作，具有不同的力量和资源。框定市场和资产化未来不仅通过经济学可能提供的分类或计算方法来进行。资产化和市场化所依赖的排除采取多种形式，并获得不同程度的效力和效果。另一组相互关联的安排是法律。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-007"></a>[7](#note-ch6-007)合同必须可计算，但也必须可执行。财产必须可转让，并可能被没收或收回。雇员必须被安排工作，也可能因雇主停工而被拒绝入厂，或被解雇。企业可能被接管或关闭。这类过程涉及技术、计算装置、控制方法和力量较量的混合。

Economics does not work alone. It operates together with other techniques, sets of information, arrangements, and agencies, with different strengths and resources. Enframing a market and assetising the future do not happen only by employing the methods of classification or calculation that economics may provide. The exclusions on which assetisation and marketisation depend take a variety of forms and acquire different degrees of force and effectiveness. Another, interrelated set of arrangements is the law.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-007"></a>[7](#note-ch6-007) Contracts must be calculable, but also enforceable. Property must be transferable and open to being forfeited or reclaimed. Employees must be put to work, or they may be locked out or fired. Businesses may be taken over or shut down. Such processes involve a mixture of technologies, calculative devices, methods of control, and trials of strength.

<a id="ch06-0012"></a>

这些安排从哪里获得它们所需的强制形式？首先来自所谓的法治。市场依赖于一种政治形式，其中行动者之间以及跨时间的关系受财产和合同规则治理。这些是市场社会中独特的权力和义务技术，产生各种微型主权、规训制度和强制力量。

Where do these arrangements acquire the forms of compulsion they require? In the first place, from what is called the rule of law. Markets depend upon a form of politics in which relations among agents, and across time, are governed by rules of property and contract. These are among the distinctive technologies of power and obligation in market societies, generating a variety of micro-sovereignties, disciplinary regimes, and coercive forces.

<a id="ch06-0013"></a>

财产安排往往相对稳定，但从不静止。财产形式不断增多。工程和技术科学产生新的对象、利益和行动者，例如把土地转化为可资本化资产的灌溉计划，允许把部分无线电频谱拍卖给电话公司的蜂窝<a id="page-208"></a>〔原书第208页〕设备，从在线搜索中提取私人控制数据的算法，或者把大西洋鳕鱼转化为资产，使所有权主张可以附着其上并进而被交易的“海洋大经济化”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-008"></a>[8](#note-ch6-008)财产的本质本身不断有待重新谈判，需要新的框定和解缠形式，以及新边疆的管理。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-009"></a>[9](#note-ch6-009)

Property arrangements are often relatively stable, but they are never static. Forms of property proliferate. Engineering and technoscience develop new objects, interests, and agents, as for example with irrigation schemes that transform land into capitalisable assets, cellular <a id="page-208-en"></a>〔原书第208页〕devices that allow parts of the radio spectrum to be auctioned to phone companies, algorithms that extract privately controlled data from online searching, or the ‘great economisation of the ocean’ that transforms the Atlantic cod into an asset to which claims of ownership can be attached and then traded.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-008"></a>[8](#note-ch6-008) The very nature of property is continually up for renegotiation, requiring new forms of enframing and disentangling, and the management of new frontiers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-009"></a>[9](#note-ch6-009)

<a id="ch06-0014"></a>

但财产关系还有另一种限制。虽然无线电波或海洋可以被重新安排为新财产形式，从而转化为可销售资产并加以资本化，但还有其他场所，其中的财产关系已存在数十年甚至数代，却仍与市场规则保持距离。事实上，世界上大多数地区的多数人，其生活方式在许多方面受到保护，免受私有财产规则和资产化过程的影响。他们可能住在自己建造、但并未正式拥有地块的住房里，或耕种受保护免遭外部购买的农地，或生产主要供家庭消费的粮食。婚姻或继承安排可能起作用，确保土地、牲畜或其他商品不会因代际更替而落入市场。

But property relations have another kind of limit. While the airwaves or the oceans can be rearranged into new forms of property, and thus transformed into marketable assets and capitalised, there are other sites that have known property relations for decades or generations yet have kept the rules of the market at arm’s length. In fact, most people in most of the world live lives in many ways protected against the rules of private property and the process of assetisation. They may live in self-built housing on plots they do not formally own, or farm agricultural land that is protected against outside purchase, or produce food intended largely for household consumption. Marriage or inheritance arrangements may operate to ensure that land, livestock, or other goods are not lost to the market through the turnover of generations.

<a id="ch06-0015"></a>

正式的财产规则有助于确定什么是合法和非法、什么是公共和私人。这类区分界定了市场，但也创造了在市场之外、或在区分所开辟的路径和空间中生存的方式。人们可能生产和交易非法商品，例如大麻或鸦片，合法的财产权通常无法适用于这些商品。他们的主要资源可能是城市街道的公共空间，例如在汽车拥堵的第三世界城市较富裕街区，人们在那里建立地盘，以非正式停车管理员身份谋生；或者政府办公室的走廊，在那里，获得合法许可和批准的困难使非正式“跑腿者”得以兴旺。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-010"></a>[10](#note-ch6-010)

Formal rules of property help determine what is legal and illegal and what is public and private. Such distinctions define the market but also create ways to survive outside it or in the pathways and spaces that these distinctions open up. People may produce and trade illicit goods, such as hemp or opium, in which legal property rights are typically unavailable. Their main resource might be the public space of an urban street, as in the wealthier neighbourhoods of car-choked third-world cities, where people establish a territory and earn a living as informal parking attendants, or the corridors of a government office, where the difficulty of obtaining legal permits and approvals enables informal expediters to thrive.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-010"></a>[10](#note-ch6-010)

<a id="ch06-0016"></a>

这些非正式或非市场实践过去被视为某种残余，代表着抵抗经济化的飞地或占据某种中间空间的过渡区域。但正如非正式城市住房等例子所表明的，许多这类安排正在不断扩张，可能比正式财产安排扩张得更快。尽管它们被认为存在于市场之外、财产法之外，却绝非没有规则约束。即使相对较新，例如帕沙·查特吉所描述的加尔各答棚户区，它们也具有复杂的道德主张、社会权利和政治义务特征。正如朱莉娅·埃利亚查尔<a id="page-209"></a>〔原书第209页〕所示，它们可以体现替代性的经济成功模式，并提供一些最有活力的经济生活形式。正如劳伦斯·梁对“多孔法律性”的论述所提示的，它们也可以渗透法律的路径，渗入受到更严密治理的财产和市场安排。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-011"></a>[11](#note-ch6-011)

These kinds of informal or nonmarket practice used to be thought of as something residual, representing pockets of resistance to economisation or transitional regions occupying some intermediate space. But as examples such as informal urban housing suggest, many of these arrangements are constantly expanding, possibly faster than formal property arrangements. Although they are thought to exist outside the market, and outside the laws of property, they are far from lawless. Even when relatively new, such as the squatter settlements in Calcutta described by Partha Chatterjee, they are characterised by complex moral claims, social rights, and political obligations. As Julia Elyachar <a id="page-209-en"></a>〔原书第209页〕shows, they can embody alternative modes of economic success and offer some of the most vibrant forms of economic life. As Lawrence Liang’s account of ‘porous legalities’ suggests, they also can penetrate the pathways of the law, seeping into the more closely governed arrangements of property and the market.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-011"></a>[11](#note-ch6-011)

<a id="ch06-0017"></a>

尽管这类安排具有多孔性，一种观念仍然存在：市场、实际上整个资本主义，有一个边界。这个边界被认为把市场与似乎存在于其界限之外的大片物质活动和资源区分开来。对西方以外的国家来说，边界观念提供了一种常见方式，不仅用来思考这些地方，还用来诊断其问题并设计适当补救方案。在新自由主义发展方案下，这类补救办法越来越流行。处理非西方发展的较早方式通常指经济的不同部门，例如传统部门与现代部门、农村部门与城市部门，或农业部门与工业部门。这些部门有移动的、有时重叠的边界。发展可以被规划为一系列转变，人口和资源从一个部门转移到另一个部门，或者市场的扩张在不同时刻改造经济的不同部分。由于变化随时间发生，非市场与市场、非资本主义与资本主义之间的差异，既是领域性转变，也同样是时间性转变。

Despite the porosity of such arrangements, the idea persists that the market, indeed capitalism in general, has a boundary. The boundary is thought to separate the market from the large areas of material activity and resources that seem to exist beyond its limit. For countries outside the West, the idea of a boundary provides a common way not just to think about these places but to diagnose their problems and design appropriate remedies. Under neoliberal development programmes, such remedies became increasingly popular. Older ways of approaching non-Western development typically referred to different sectors of the economy, such as the traditional and the modern, the rural and the urban, or the agrarian and the industrial. These sectors had moving and sometimes overlapping boundaries. Development could be planned as a series of transitions, in which people and resources were to be moved from one sector to another, or in which the expansion of the market transformed different parts of the economy at different moments. Since the changes occurred over time, the difference between the non-market and the market, or the non-capitalist and the capitalist, represented as much a temporal transition as a territorial one.

<a id="ch06-0018"></a>

本章考察这种市场观念及其界限。它提出一种不同方式来理解市场边界，以及市场与非市场之间差异的地位。本章主张，市场与非市场、资本主义与非资本主义、资产化与非资产化之间的区分，不应被视为一条细线，而应被视为一个广阔地带，实际上是一个覆盖所谓资本主义全部领土的边疆地区。这个地区是政治斗争的场所，新的道德主张、关于正义的论点和权利形式在那里被锻造。当经济学帮助设计技术机制，把人和资产从市场之外越过一条线转移到市场之内时，它参与了这种政治。这类机制并不把事物移过一条固定的线，但它们确实重新安排了资产的控制和分配。这条线是这些机制所创造的东西，是重新分配和控制斗争的一部分。对经济学来说，这涉及一种不妨称之为错误再现的工作，因为外部必须根据其与市场的关系来构成——也就是说，根据其缺陷来构成，<a id="page-210"></a>〔原书第210页〕作为非市场，作为某种有缺陷或死寂的东西。然而，称之为错误再现是不够的，因为它暗示从资本主义话语内部充分再现非市场是可能的。在实践中，非市场是一个无知领域，经济学的真理需要它才能运作。更有用的做法是考虑这种（错误）再现帮助组织了什么样的世界。

This chapter investigates this conception of the market and its limits. It proposes a different way of understanding the boundary of the market and the status of the difference between the market and the non-market. The chapter argues that the distinction between market and nonmarket, capitalist and non-capitalist, or assetised and non-assetised should be considered not as a thin line but as a broad terrain, in fact a frontier region that covers the entire territory of what is called capitalism. The region is the scene of political battles, in which new moral claims, arguments about justice, and forms of entitlement are forged. When economics helps to devise technical mechanisms to move people and assets across a line from outside the market to inside, it plays a part in this politics. Such mechanisms do not move things across a fixed line, but they do rearrange the control and distribution of assets. The line is something created by these mechanisms, as part of the battle over redistribution and control. For economics, this involves what might be called a work of misrepresentation, for the outside must be constituted in terms of its relation to the market – that is, in terms of its deficiencies, <a id="page-210-en"></a>〔原书第210页〕as the non-market, as something defective or dead. Yet it is inadequate to call this a misrepresentation, for it implies the possibility of an adequate representation of the non-market from within a capitalist discourse. In practice, the non-market is a realm of ignorance that is required for the truths of economics to operate. It is more useful to consider what kind of world the (mis)representation helps to organise.

<a id="ch06-0019"></a>

再现技术在这些安排中声称发挥双重作用。一方面，经济分析试图通过再现市场之外的世界来帮助重组技术政治生活，作为似乎把它带入市场之内、或使其资产化过程的一部分。另一方面，在描述这个非市场世界缺乏什么时，经济学往往把其缺陷诊断为缺乏再现技术。事物之所以卡在市场之外，是因为它们没有得到恰当再现——通过产权记录、价格、激励或其他指涉系统。然而，经济学所做的不是再现先前未知和未被再现的东西，而是重组再现的流通和控制。经济学的力量不一定在于让人们接受其（错误）再现；相反，在帮助构成市场与非市场、或资产化与非资产化之间表面边界的过程中，经济学促成了技术政治机制的工作，这些机制重组人们的生活方式、他们所能提出的政治主张，以及他们所能控制的资产。我认为，它的特殊作用在于格式化一种排除—纳入形式。

Technologies of representation claim a double role in these arrangements. One the one hand, economic analysis tries to help reorganise technopolitical life by representing a world outside the market, as part of the process of seeming to bring it inside, or assetise it. On the other, in describing what this non-market world lacks, economics tends to diagnose its defects as an absence of techniques of representation. Things are stuck outside the market because they are not properly represented – by property records, prices, incentives, or other systems of reference. What economics does, however, is not to represent what was previously unknown and unrepresented, but to reorganise the circulation and control of representations. The power of economics does not necessarily lie in getting people to adopt its (mis)representations; rather, in helping to constitute the apparent border between the market and the non-market, or the assetised and the non-assetised, economics contributes to the work of technopolitical mechanisms that reorganise how people live, the political claims they can make, and the assets they can control. Its particular role, I argue, is in formatting a form of exclusion-inclusion.

<a id="ch06-0020"></a>

在新自由主义下，把发展视为从传统到现代转变的观点，让位于一个更简单的观念：“市场”被一条边界包围，边界之外是非资本主义、非市场世界。“发展”的任务是帮助把市场规则和资产化过程扩展到这些其他空间。这类提案的流行程度可以从赫尔南多·德·索托著作的成功来衡量；这位秘鲁企业家和经济学家有两本书，*《另一条道路》*（1989）和*《资本的奥秘》*（2000），它们成为一代人中最广泛引用的非西方经济发展研究。进行这些书中研究的秘鲁自由与民主研究所（ILD），一度被称为世界上影响力排名第二的智库。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-012"></a>[12](#note-ch6-012)这两本书都描述了存在于资本主义经济之外的财富和物质活动形式，诊断了把它们拒之门外的障碍的性质，并提出了把它们带入其中的资产化技术。自由与民主研究所在亚洲、非洲<a id="page-211"></a>〔原书第211页〕和拉丁美洲的几个国家开展工作，设计程序，使被困于资本主义之外的东西能够被带入。这些机制的技术设计和实施，成为全球南方经济发展问题最流行的解决方案之一。

Under neoliberalism, the view of development as a transition from traditional to modern gave way to a more simple idea: the ‘market’ is surrounded by a boundary, outside which stands the non-capitalist, non-market world. The task of ‘development’ is to help extend the rules of the market and the process of assetisation into these other spaces. The popularity of such proposals can be gauged by the success of the work of Hernando de Soto, a Peruvian entrepreneur and economist, whose two books, *The Other Path* (1989) and *The Mystery of Capital* (2000), became the most widely cited studies of non-Western economic development in a generation. The Institute for Liberty and Democracy (ILD) in Peru, which carried out the research presented in these books, was at one point called the second most influential think tank in the world.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-012"></a>[12](#note-ch6-012) Both books described the forms of wealth and material activity that exist outside the capitalist economy, diagnosed the nature of the barrier that keeps them out, and proposed techniques of assetisation for bringing them in. The ILD worked in several countries in Asia, Africa, <a id="page-211-en"></a>〔原书第211页〕and Latin America devising procedures to enable what is trapped outside capitalism to be brought in. The technical design and implementation of these mechanisms became one of the most popular solutions to the problem of economic development in the Global South.

<a id="ch06-0021"></a>

### 一本非常了不起的书

### A Very Great Book

<a id="ch06-0022"></a>

德·索托在*《资本的奥秘》*中呈现了来自五个国家的研究结果，主张西方以外大多数国家未能仿效西方经济发展的主要原因，是其大量财富存在于正式经济之外。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-013"></a>[13](#note-ch6-013)这些财富被困在无法进入市场的形式中，因此无法被资产化或资本化以创造更多财富。这种财富被称为“死资本”，主要由土地和住房构成。非西方国家的多数人居住在所有权未在国家正式登记的住房中，因此缺乏对其财产的适当产权。德·索托说，这些人“处于全球经济之外，实际上处于市场经济之外，当然也处于资本主义经济之外”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-014"></a>[14](#note-ch6-014)由于他们的土地和房屋在经济之外，他们无法将其用作抵押品来借款。他们的资产被锁定在住宅的物质形式中，无法转化为现金或信用。信用是“活”资本，可以积累、投资于商业项目，并转化为进一步收入。

Presenting the findings from research in five countries, de Soto argued in *The Mystery of Capital* that the main reason why most countries outside the West had failed to emulate the West’s economic development is that a large amount of their wealth lies outside the formal economy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-013"></a>[13](#note-ch6-013) It is trapped in forms that cannot enter the market, and therefore cannot be assetised or capitalised to create further wealth. Described as ‘dead capital’, this wealth consists principally of land and housing. Most people in non-Western countries live in housing whose ownership is not formally registered with the state and thus lack proper title to their property. These people, said de Soto, ‘are outside the global economy, are in fact outside the market economy, are certainly outside the capitalist economy’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-014"></a>[14](#note-ch6-014) Because their land and houses are outside the economy, they are unable to use them as collateral to borrow funds. Their assets are locked in the material form of their homes and cannot be transformed into cash or credit. Credit is ‘live’ capital that can be accumulated, invested in business ventures, and turned into further income.

<a id="ch06-0023"></a>

根据德·索托的简单图式，活资本是通过设计再现技术创造的。对物质资产的再现把其价值转化为抽象形式，这些形式可以与其物理存在并行，过一种“无形的平行生活”。西方发明了创造这些无形形式的程序。西方个人可以解锁积累在实体财产中的资产，把物质财富转化为抽象资本。德·索托写道，用房屋作为贷款抵押品，是创办小企业的重要信用来源，提供了刺激经济增长的大量资金储备。他主张，成功的资本主义经济与世界其他地区之间最重要的差异，不在于它们拥有的财富，而在于财富的持有方式。世界其他地区以“有缺陷的形式”持有资产。缺乏产权及其所能促成的信用机制，是西方以外资本主义发展失败的主要原因。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-015"></a>[15](#note-ch6-015)

Live capital, according to de Soto’s simple schema, is created by devising techniques of representation. Representations of material assets transform their value into abstract forms, which can live an ‘invisible, parallel life’ alongside their physical existence. The West has invented procedures to create these invisible forms. Individuals in the West can unlock the assets accumulated in physical property, transforming material wealth into abstract capital. Using a house as collateral for loans, wrote de Soto, is an important source of credit for launching small businesses, providing a large reserve of funds to stimulate economic growth. The most important difference between successful capitalist economies and the rest of the world lies not in the wealth they possess, he argued, but in how that wealth is held. The rest of the world holds its assets in ‘defective forms’. The absence of property title and the mechanism of credit it enables are the principal reason for the failure of capitalist development outside the West.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-015"></a>[15](#note-ch6-015)

<a id="ch06-0024"></a>

<a id="page-212"></a>〔原书第212页〕因此，解决全球贫困的办法，是在每个国家构建一个简单的再现装置，把死资本转化为活资产。这套机器由基于社区的项目组成，使人们能够登记财产所有权，并配有简化规则，允许把财产用作获得信用的抵押品。德·索托为这些提案组织了广泛支持。1994 年，他说服秘鲁政府在自由与民主研究所指导下启动一项产权登记计划，到 2002 年已向 120 万城市家庭发放正式产权。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-016"></a>[16](#note-ch6-016)随后许多其他国家聘请自由与民主研究所作为顾问，衡量本国未登记资产的规模，并设计将其推向市场的机制。

<a id="page-212-en"></a>〔原书第212页〕The solution to global poverty, it follows, is to construct in every country a simple apparatus of representation that will transform dead capital into live assets. The machinery consists of neighbourhood-based programmes to enable people to register ownership of their property and simplified rules for using the property as collateral for obtaining credit. De Soto organised wide support for these proposals.
