In 1994, he persuaded the government of Peru to launch a property titling programme under the ILD’s direction that by 2002 gave formal title to 1.2 million urban households.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-016"></a>[16](#note-ch6-016) Numerous other countries subsequently recruited the ILD as a consultant, to measure the extent of their countries’ untitled assets and devise mechanisms for moving them into the market.

<a id="ch06-0025"></a>

德·索托的研究人员在埃及发现了最令人印象深刻的结果。他们估计，该国多达 92% 的住房以有缺陷的形式持有，代表 2,480 亿美元未充分利用的资产。在他们被最广泛引用的统计数据之一中，他们说这些死资本相当于现代埃及有记录以来全部外国直接投资总额的五十五倍以上，包括十九世纪修建苏伊士运河和二十世纪修建阿斯旺高坝的投资。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-017"></a>[17](#note-ch6-017)

De Soto’s researchers found their most impressive results in Egypt. They estimated that as much as 92 per cent of the country’s housing was held in defective form, representing $248 billion in underused assets. In one of their most widely repeated statistics, they said that this dead capital represented more than fifty-five times the amount of all the direct foreign investment ever recorded in modern Egypt, including constructing the Suez Canal in the nineteenth century and building the Aswan High Dam in the twentieth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-017"></a>[17](#note-ch6-017)

<a id="ch06-0026"></a>

这些项目具有吸引力的一些原因很容易理解。与其他发展问题诊断相比，德·索托对全球南方大多数人的资源和潜力作出了积极得多的描述。他较早的著作*《另一条道路》*是对秘鲁非正式经济部门的研究，主张不受监管的经济活动比过度监管的正式经济更有活力、更有效率。非正式部门的规模并非落后的标志，而是对正式经济活动过度官僚监管的理性回应。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-018"></a>[18](#note-ch6-018)*《资本的奥秘》*表明，穷人不仅拥有创业技能，还拥有资产。未能充分开发这些资产，不是资产所有者的过错，因此不能归咎于穷人落后或传统的文化。这是正式部门的过错。德·索托主张，全球南方政府未能引入法律安排和金融机制，而正是这些未被注意的秘密促成了西方资本主义发展的成功。过去两个世纪现代产权的发展如此成功，以至于西方如今把这一装置视为理所当然，未能注意到它在西方以外大多数国家的缺失或不完整。

Some of the reasons for the appeal of these programmes are easy to see. Compared with other diagnoses of the problems of development, de Soto offered a much more positive account of the resources and potential of the majority of the people of the Global South. His earlier book, *The Other Path*, a study of the informal economic sector in Peru, argued that unregulated economic activity was more dynamic and more efficient than the over-regulated formal economy. The size of the informal sector was not an indication of backwardness but a rational response to excessive bureaucratic regulation of formal economic activities.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-018"></a>[18](#note-ch6-018) *The Mystery of Capital* showed that the poor possessed not just entrepreneurial skills but also assets. The failure fully to develop these assets was not the fault of those who owned them and therefore could not be blamed on the backward or traditional culture of the poor. It was the fault of the formal sector. Governments in the Global South had failed to introduce the legal arrangements and financial mechanisms that were the unnoticed secret, de Soto argued, of the success of capitalist development in the West. The development of modern property rights during the previous two centuries was so successful that the West now takes this apparatus for granted and fails to notice its absence or incompleteness in most countries outside the West.

<a id="ch06-0027"></a>

<a id="page-213"></a>〔原书第213页〕这些论点是对关于穷人的流行观念——认为他们因自身传统或文化而丧失能力——的有用替代。它们把穷人呈现为有能力的经济行动者，只需获得适当的技术装备，就能被带入市场。但德·索托论点的成功还有更多原因。它们提供了一种把穷人带入新自由主义论点和方案的方式。

<a id="page-213-en"></a>〔原书第213页〕These arguments were useful alternatives to popular ideas about the poor as people incapacitated by their own traditions or culture. They presented the poor as competent economic agents who needed to acquire only the proper technical equipment to be brought into the market. But the success of de Soto’s arguments was due to something more. They provided a way to bring the poor into the arguments and programmes of neoliberalism.

<a id="ch06-0028"></a>

德·索托的提案在欧美新自由主义运动的政治机构和资金资源网络中发展、传播。该运动始于 1940 年代后期，最初是一个由企业资助者支持的保守经济学家和政治理论家小团体，其最有影响的思想家和组织者是奥地利出生的英国经济学家弗里德里希·哈耶克（我们曾在[第四章](#ch04-0001)遇到他）。此后几十年间，它成长为一个跨大西洋的智库、学院经济学家和政策制定者网络，由私人基金会和企业资助，在西方政府政策的形成中发挥了有影响力的作用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-019"></a>[19](#note-ch6-019)

De Soto’s proposals were developed and circulated within the network of political agencies and financial resources of the Euro-American neoliberal movement. From its beginnings in the late 1940s as a small association of conservative economists and political theorists supported by corporate benefactors, with the Austrian-born British economist Friedrich Hayek (whom we met in [chapter 4](#ch04-0001)) as their most influential thinker and organiser, the neoliberal movement grew over the following decades into a transatlantic network of think tanks, academic economists, and policy makers, funded by private foundations and corporations, that came to play an influential role in the shaping of government policy in the West.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-019"></a>[19](#note-ch6-019)

<a id="ch06-0029"></a>

1981 年，该运动的重要组织者和资助者安东尼·费舍尔在华盛顿特区附近建立了阿特拉斯经济研究基金会，以协调不断壮大的智库网络，并发起“一项协同努力”（哈耶克在一封支持信中的说法），“在世界各地建立类似的机构”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-020"></a>[20](#note-ch6-020)哈耶克是在从秘鲁访问归来后写下这封信的，他在那里的一次会议上发表演讲，会议得到德国新自由主义者的资助，由赫尔南多·德·索托组织。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-021"></a>[21](#note-ch6-021)在哈耶克的敦促下，阿特拉斯基金会帮助德·索托建立了自由与民主研究所。阿特拉斯提供资金支持，并让德·索托及其合作者接受新自由主义经济思想及其为政治组织和倡导而发展出的技术的培训。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-022"></a>[22](#note-ch6-022)

In 1981, Antony Fisher, a leading organiser and benefactor of the movement, established the Atlas Foundation for Economic Research, based near Washington, DC, to coordinate the growing network of think tanks and launch ‘a concerted effort’, in the words of a letter of support from Hayek, ‘to create similar institutes all over the world’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-020"></a>[20](#note-ch6-020) Hayek wrote the letter after returning from a trip to Peru, where he spoke at a conference funded by German neoliberals and organised by Hernando de Soto.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-021"></a>[21](#note-ch6-021) At Hayek’s urging, the Atlas Foundation helped de Soto set up the ILD. Atlas provided financial support and trained de Soto and his collaborators in the economic ideas of neoliberalism and the techniques it had developed for political organisation and advocacy.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-022"></a>[22](#note-ch6-022)

<a id="ch06-0030"></a>

哈耶克和新自由主义运动的支持，使自由与民主研究所能够开展关于产权与穷人的研究——这些研究发表在*《另一条道路》*和*《资本的奥秘》*中——并在秘鲁推出第一批产权登记计划。这些计划对家庭贫困没有产生任何影响。本应弥补这一失败的其他好处同样虚幻。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-023"></a>[23](#note-ch6-023)然而，这些失败并未妨碍德·索托的成功。新自由主义作家和智库对他的著作给予好评，并通过广为人知的奖项表彰作者及其组织。*《另一条道路》*得到两位美国前总统的推荐，并获得<a id="page-214"></a>〔原书第214页〕阿特拉斯基金会的一个奖项。*《资本的奥秘》*得到玛格丽特·撒切尔、珍妮·柯克帕特里克、托马斯·弗里德曼、弗朗西斯·福山和小威廉·F. 巴克利的推荐。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-024"></a>[24](#note-ch6-024)德·索托获得加图研究所的米尔顿·弗里德曼促进自由奖、*《福布斯》*杂志的“战略方向指南针奖”、亚当·斯密奖、戈德华特奖以及其他几个奖项。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-025"></a>[25](#note-ch6-025)与此同时，他为穷人辩护的民粹主义语调，使其他人把他视为进步派。自由与民主研究所曾在网站上报告，即使偏左的英国刊物*《新政治家》*也写道，德·索托的工作“使他跻身我们时代伟大进步知识分子的殿堂”。尽管该刊并没有这样写，德·索托还是设法宣称自己拥有远超新自由主义运动范围的支持者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-026"></a>[26](#note-ch6-026)

The support from Hayek and the neoliberal movement enabled the ILD to carry out its research into property rights and the poor, published in *The Other Path* and *The Mystery of Capital*, and to introduce its first property titling programmes in Peru. The programmes failed to have any effect on household poverty. Other benefits that were supposed to compensate for this failure were equally illusory.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-023"></a>[23](#note-ch6-023) Yet the failures did not prove an obstacle to de Soto’s success. Neoliberal writers and think tanks gave his books favourable reviews and recognised the author and his organisation with well-publicised awards. *The Other Path* carried endorsements from two former US presidents and received a prize from <a id="page-214-en"></a>〔原书第214页〕the Atlas Foundation. *The Mystery of Capital* received endorsements from Margaret Thatcher, Jeane Kirkpatrick, Thomas Friedman, Francis Fukuyama, and William F. Buckley Jr.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-024"></a>[24](#note-ch6-024) De Soto received the Milton Friedman Prize for Advancing Liberty from the CATO Institute, the Compass Award for Strategic Direction from *Forbes Magazine*, the Adam Smith Award, the Goldwater Award, and several other prizes.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-025"></a>[25](#note-ch6-025) At the same time, the populist tone of his arguments on behalf of the poor persuaded others to see him as a progressive. The ILD reported on its website that even the left-of-centre British journal *The New Statesman* had written that de Soto’s work ‘has put him in the pantheon of great progressive intellectuals of our age’. Although this was not what the journal wrote, de Soto managed to claim supporters well beyond the limits of the neoliberal movement.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-026"></a>[26](#note-ch6-026)

<a id="ch06-0031"></a>

自由与民主研究所的工作还得益于将其与学院经济学联系起来的新自由主义网络。德·索托是实践者，不是学者，其研究是在智库而非大学中进行的。学院经济学家称赞他的工作，不是因为它对学术理论有所贡献，而是因为它实际展示了新古典经济学关于产权的真理。两位诺贝尔经济学奖得主罗纳德·科斯和米尔顿·弗里德曼为*《资本的奥秘》*撰写推荐。科斯称它“是一本非常了不起的书：有力而且完全令人信服”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-027"></a>[27](#note-ch6-027)这种积极接受使其论点回流到学院经济学。德·索托的工作成为进一步大学研究的基础，并为经济学教材提供了素材；这些教材获得了弗里德曼以及道格拉斯·诺斯等经济学家的认可，其中弗里德曼再次给予了支持。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-028"></a>[28](#note-ch6-028)

The ILD’s work also benefited from the neoliberal networks connecting it to academic economics. De Soto was a practitioner, not a scholar, producing research in a think tank rather than a university. Academic economists praised his work not as a contribution to academic theory but as a practical demonstration of neoclassical economic truths about property rights. Two Nobel laureates in economics, Ronald Coase and Milton Friedman, endorsed *The Mystery of Capital*. It is ‘a very great book’, wrote Coase: ‘Powerful and completely convincing’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-027"></a>[27](#note-ch6-027) This positive reception enabled its arguments to flow back into academic economics. De Soto’s work became the basis for further university research and provided the subject matter for teaching materials in economics, endorsed by economists such as Friedman, again, and Douglass North.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-028"></a>[28](#note-ch6-028)

<a id="ch06-0032"></a>

尽管始终没有可靠证据表明他的想法行之有效，德·索托仍被描述为世界领先的发展专家之一。世界银行为秘鲁的自由与民主研究所产权登记计划提供资金，国际货币基金组织（IMF）宣传其理念，美国国际开发署为该智库的海外业务提供持续资助，国际劳工组织任命德·索托为全球化社会影响世界委员会成员。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-029"></a>[29](#note-ch6-029)2005 年 9 月，联合国开发计划署（UNDP）支持设立“贫困者法律赋权高级别委员会”，由德·索托和美国前国务卿马德琳·奥尔布赖特共同担任主席，目标是进一步为德·索托的政治纲领争取国际支持。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-030"></a>[30](#note-ch6-030)

Despite the continuing absence of reliable evidence that his ideas worked, de Soto came to be described as one of the world’s leading experts on development. The World Bank funded the ILD titling programme in Peru, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) promoted its ideas, the United States Agency for International Development provided the think tank with continuous funding for its overseas operations, and the International Labor Organization appointed de Soto to its World Commission on the Social Dimension of Globalization.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-029"></a>[29](#note-ch6-029) In September 2005, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) supported the establishing of the High Level Commission on the Legal Empowerment of the Poor, cochaired by de Soto and Madeleine Albright, the former US Secretary of State, with the goal of generating further international support for de Soto’s political programme.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-030"></a>[30](#note-ch6-030)

<a id="ch06-0033"></a>

*《资本的奥秘》*的成功及其作者获得的认可，是德·索托在欧美<a id="page-215"></a>〔原书第215页〕新自由主义运动帮助下通过公关努力制造出来的；这些使自由与民主研究所能够把自己的活动转化为一种财产形式。在向世界各国政府推销其产权计划时，德·索托的方法是绕过政府部委和地方发展机构，直接寻求国家元首的授权和支持。这使该研究所能够赢得政府独家咨询合同，这类合同的授予通常不按正常程序邀请其他咨询公司竞标。

The success of *The Mystery of Capital* and its author’s recognition, manufactured by de Soto’s public relations efforts with the help of the <a id="page-215-en"></a>〔原书第215页〕Euro-American neoliberal movement, enabled the ILD to transform its own activities into a form of property. In marketing his property rights programme to governments around the world, de Soto’s method was to bypass government ministries and local development agencies and seek authorisation and support directly from a country’s head of state. This enabled the ILD to win exclusive government consulting contracts, typically awarded without the normal request for competitive bids from rival consulting firms.

<a id="ch06-0034"></a>

例如在坦桑尼亚，德·索托在两人都被任命为全球化世界委员会成员时与该国总统会面。他利用这层关系获得一份未经招标的政府合同，尽管其他发展机构多年来一直在进行坦桑尼亚产权改革工作。自由与民主研究所为其独家合同辩解，理由是*《资本的奥秘》*所阐述的消除全球贫困方法独一无二，无法与现有计划结合。合同于 2004 年 11 月签署，其中要求坦桑尼亚政府“尊重自由与民主研究所对其提供的方法和技术所享有的知识产权”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-031"></a>[31](#note-ch6-031)在解释为什么不允许其他发展机构参与竞标时，该研究所执行主任曼努埃尔·马约尔加说：

In Tanzania, for example, de Soto met the country’s president when both of them were appointed to the World Commission on Globalization. He used this connection to obtain a no-bid government contract, even though other development agencies had been working on the reform of Tanzanian property rights for many years. The ILD justified its exclusive contract on the grounds that its method of ending global poverty, explained in *The Mystery of Capital*, was unique and could not be combined with existing programmes. Signed in November 2004, the contract included a requirement that the Tanzanian government ‘respect ILD’s intellectual property rights over the methodology and techniques it provides’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-031"></a>[31](#note-ch6-031) Explaining why other development agencies had not been allowed to bid for the contract, the executive director of the ILD, Manuel Mayorga, said that

<a id="ch06-0035"></a>

> 在这一特定领域，是我们发明了轮子。理解正式法律部门与法外部门之间的差距，分析这两个平行部门如何运作，评估它们的问题……量化其经济影响，以及如何在一种法治之下将它们整合起来，创造一个现代、富有生产力的经济，这些正是自由与民主研究所率先开拓的领域。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-032"></a>[32](#note-ch6-032)

> in this particular area, we invented the wheel. Understanding the gap between the formal legal and extralegal sectors, analysing how these two parallel sectors operate, evaluating their problems . . . quantifying their economic effects, and how they might be integrated under one rule of law creating a modern, productive economy is the area that the ILD has pioneered.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-032"></a>[32](#note-ch6-032)

<a id="ch06-0036"></a>

因此，德·索托对市场知识的所有权主张——他对这种知识的资产化——成为资本积累的手段。与资产化的一贯情形一样，积累依赖于保护他自己的活动免受市场竞争。

Thus de Soto’s claim to ownership of knowledge about markets – his assetisation of that knowledge – became a means to the accumulation of capital. As always with assetisation, the accumulation depended on protecting his own activities from competition in the market.

<a id="ch06-0037"></a>

在埃及，自由与民主研究所获得了贾迈勒·穆巴拉克的支持。他是埃及总统之子，也是埃及大型企业家中一个较年轻派系里最富有、最有权势的人物；该派系寻求加强私有财产的权力，以此撤销上一代人的社会改革。这个团体利用德·索托的论点帮助推动新的经济措施在议会通过，包括一部抵押贷款法、一项产权登记计划，以及小企业许可<a id="page-216"></a>〔原书第216页〕新规。自由与民主研究所帮助起草这些法律，并开展公关活动以赢得政治支持。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-033"></a>[33](#note-ch6-033)与秘鲁一样，立法结果令人失望，但宣传活动即刻获得了成功。*《福布斯》*杂志 2004 年 2 月发表一篇报道，预测该国新财产法将“戏剧性地把其经济转变为创造财富、分配财富的强劲引擎，引领数百万埃及人进入一个充满活力、日益民主的中产阶级”。该刊编辑写道，这个国家准备成为“与爱尔兰或香港匹敌的经济奇迹”，并补充说，这样一来，“埃及将对全球恐怖主义造成毁灭性打击”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-034"></a>[34](#note-ch6-034)

In Egypt, the ILD gained the backing of Gamal Mubarak, the son of the country’s president and the wealthiest and most powerful of a younger faction among large Egyptian entrepreneurs seeking to strengthen the powers of private property as a means of undoing an earlier generation of social reforms. This group used de Soto’s arguments to help push new economic measures through parliament, including a mortgage law, a property titling programme, and new rules <a id="page-216-en"></a>〔原书第216页〕for licensing small businesses. The ILD helped draft the laws, along with a public relations campaign to win political support.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-033"></a>[33](#note-ch6-033) As in Peru, the outcome of the legislation was disappointing, but the publicity campaign was an immediate success. *Forbes Magazine* published a story in February 2004 predicting that the country’s new property laws would ‘dramatically transform its economy into a wealth-creating, wealth-distributing dynamo that will lead millions of Egyptians into a vibrant, increasingly democratic middle class’. The country was poised to become ‘an economic miracle rivaling Ireland or Hong Kong’, the magazine’s editor wrote – adding that in doing so ‘Egypt will deal a devastating blow to global terrorism’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-034"></a>[34](#note-ch6-034)

<a id="ch06-0038"></a>

既然埃及提供了德·索托所诊断缺陷最戏剧性的例子，而克服这些缺陷据说能带来经济奇迹，那么埃及的证据就值得考察。它能告诉我们德·索托论点的效力如何？尽管缺乏支持证据，这些观念实际上又是如何发挥作用的？

Since Egypt provided the most dramatic instance of the defects that de Soto diagnoses, and overcoming these defects was said to promise an economic miracle, it is worth looking at the evidence from Egypt. What can it tell us about the force of de Soto’s arguments? How are these ideas, despite the lack of evidence to support them, actually put to work?

<a id="ch06-0039"></a>

### 市场之外

### Outside the Market

<a id="ch06-0040"></a>

关于埃及，首先要注意的是，自由与民主研究所提出的补救办法此前已被尝试过。一百五十年前，从 1850 年代开始，一系列法律引入现代私有财产制度，并配套建立自己的法院、财产登记处和强制执行机制。在多数情况下，这些程序承认奥斯曼法和地方法下现有的土地主张，但也使为购置和转让土地而抵押贷款成为可能，并为希望用财产作抵押的人提供了信贷来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-035"></a>[35](#note-ch6-035)正如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)和[第二章](#ch02-0001)所见，随之而来的是“尼罗河上的克朗代克”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-036"></a>[36](#note-ch6-036)地方地主和欧洲债权人把贷款扩展到农村新的灌溉计划、土地开垦和蒸汽抽水设备，以及城市的住房和现代基础设施。到二十世纪之交，埃及股票市场——其最大持股集中在抵押贷款公司和房地产开发——已是世界上最活跃的市场之一。

The first thing to note about Egypt is that the remedy the ILD proposed had been tried before. One hundred and fifty years earlier, beginning in the 1850s, a series of laws introduced a modern system of private property, implemented with its own courts, property registers, and mechanisms of enforcement. In most cases, these procedures recognised existing claims to the land under Ottoman and local law, but they also made possible mortgages for the acquisition and transfer of land, and as a source of credit for those who wished to use their property as collateral.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-035"></a>[35](#note-ch6-035) As we saw in [chapters 1](#ch01-0001) and [2](#ch02-0001), there followed a ‘Klondike on the Nile’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-036"></a>[36](#note-ch6-036) Local landowners and European creditors extended loans for new irrigation schemes, land reclamation, and steam-powered pumping equipment in the countryside and for housing and modern infrastructure in the cities. By the turn of the twentieth century, the Egyptian stock market, whose largest shareholdings were in mortgage companies and property development, was one of the most active in the world.

<a id="ch06-0041"></a>

结果是一场灾难。在埃及农村，小农面临迅速上涨的物价。税款大幅增加，用以支付统治家族地产的抵押贷款。1861 年和 1863—4 年的一场牛瘟杀死了该国大部分役畜，造成进一步困难。正如我们在[第二章](#ch02-0001)所见，这场瘟疫在 1870 年代和<a id="page-217"></a>〔原书第217页〕1880 年代再次出现。为了获得贷款渡过这些危机，农民如今不得不抵押自己的土地。债权人得以利用新的止赎权力，夺取无力按时偿债者的资产。农民把执行止赎裁决的法院描述为“一台转移土地的机器”，把小农的土地转给富人。债权人不仅可以占有田地，还可以占有役畜和犁，并可以夺取或拆毁债务人的房屋。一份当时的报告告诉我们，债务水平使小农越来越难以架设水车，而主要粮食生产依赖水车。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-037"></a>[37](#note-ch6-037)

The result was a disaster. In rural Egypt, small farmers faced rapidly rising prices. Tax payments increased sharply, to cover mortgage payments on the estates of the ruling family. A cattle plague in 1861 and 1863–4 killed most of the country’s draft animals, causing further difficulties. The plague returned, as we saw in [chapter 2](#ch02-0001), in the 1870s and <a id="page-217-en"></a>〔原书第217页〕1880s. To obtain loans to survive such crises, farmers now had to mortgage their own land. Creditors were able to use the new powers of foreclosure to seize the assets of those unable to keep up debt payments. Farmers described the courts that enforced foreclosure decisions as ‘a machine for transferring the land’ from small farmers to the wealthy. Creditors could take possession of not only the fields but also draught animals and ploughs and could seize or demolish debtors’ houses. The level of debt made it increasingly difficult for small farmers to erect waterwheels, a contemporary report tells us, on which the production of staple food depended.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-037"></a>[37](#note-ch6-037)

<a id="ch06-0042"></a>

个人所有者遭受的灾难，又借助同样的新财产和有担保贷款安排，在更大规模上重演。如先前各章所见，资产化、债务和止赎的机器为殖民占领提供了杠杆。1874 年，全球经济萧条开始，起因是欧洲投机性银行业的危机，包括向开罗的奥斯曼总督提供贷款，而他曾以大块棉花和甘蔗种植园作为抵押品。随着萧条导致棉花和糖价下跌，并让进一步信贷无从获得，政府无法推迟财政崩溃。1876 年，英法银行在开罗设立债务委员会，接管该国财政，并利用新法院占有总督的地产。当他抵制接管时，英法政府废黜了他，扶植其子上台。后者随后在与一场由下级军官和心怀不满的显贵领导的民众立宪运动的较量中逐渐失势。1882 年，英国人入侵该国，建立军事占领以铲除民众运动，并重新确立欧洲对财政和抵押财产的控制，包括大片总督地产。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-038"></a>[38](#note-ch6-038)

The disaster suffered by individual owners was repeated on a larger scale, using the same new arrangements of property and secured loans. As we saw in earlier chapters, the machinery of assetisation, debt, and foreclosure provided the leverage for colonial occupation. In 1874 a global economic depression began, brought on by the crisis of speculative European banking, including loans to the Ottoman viceroy in Cairo, for which he had pledged his large cotton and sugar cane estates as collateral. As the depression caused the price of cotton and sugar to fall, and made further credit unavailable, the government was unable to postpone the financial collapse. In 1876, the British and French banking houses established a Debt Commission in Cairo, which took control of the country’s finances and used the new courts to take possession of the viceroy’s estates. When he resisted the takeover, the British and French governments had him deposed in favour of his son. The latter began to lose power to a popular constitutionalist movement, led by junior army officers and disaffected notables. In 1882 the British invaded the country, established a military occupation to eradicate the populist movement, and reasserted European control over finances and mortgaged property, including the extensive viceregal estates.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-038"></a>[38](#note-ch6-038)

<a id="ch06-0043"></a>

英国人试图巩固新的私有财产安排。他们进行土地测量，绘制全国每一英亩农地的所有权，并把信息记录在财产登记册中。测量和财产登记于 1907 年完成，比当时英国已知的任何同类工作都更全面。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-039"></a>[39](#note-ch6-039)与此同时，殖民当局被迫采取措施限制新财产规则的适用。1912 年，为了减缓村民失去土地和家园的速度，他们出台《五费丹法》。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-040"></a>[40](#note-ch6-040)该法以英国为处理印度西北部旁遮普类似问题而采取的措施为蓝本，防止<a id="page-218"></a>〔原书第218页〕债权人夺取小农最后五英亩（费丹）土地、基本农具、两头役畜和他们的房屋。然而到 1920 年代，据估计尼罗河三角洲超过三分之一的农业人口已经失去土地。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-041"></a>[41](#note-ch6-041)第二次世界大战期间，政府出台租金管制法，以打击急剧涨价和牟取暴利。类似措施保护了城市住房的租户。1952 年政变结束最大地主的权力后，埃及实行土地改革，为佃农提供更广泛的保障，并给予城市房产居民类似保护。

The British attempted to consolidate the new arrangements of private property. They carried out a land survey, mapping the ownership of every acre of agricultural land in the country and recording the information in property registers. Completed in 1907, the survey and property register were more comprehensive than anything known in that period in Britain.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-039"></a>[39](#note-ch6-039) At the same time the colonial authorities were forced to introduce measures to limit the application of the new property rules. In 1912, in an attempt to slow down the rate at which villagers were losing their land and their homes to creditors, they introduced the Five Feddan Law.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-040"></a>[40](#note-ch6-040) Modelled on measures the British had introduced to deal with similar problems in Punjab in northwest India, the law prevented <a id="page-218-en"></a>〔原书第218页〕creditors seizing from small farmers their last five acres (feddans) of land, their essential farm tools, two draft animals, and their house. Nevertheless, by the 1920s, it was estimated that more than one-third of the agricultural population in the Nile Delta had become landless.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-041"></a>[41](#note-ch6-041) The government introduced rent control laws during the Second World War, to combat steep price rises and profiteering. Similar measures protected tenants in urban housing. Following the 1952 coup d’etat that ended the power of the largest landowners, Egypt adopted a land reform that gave more extensive security to tenant farmers and similar protections to urban property dwellers.

<a id="ch06-0044"></a>

埃及经验对自由与民主研究所更为当代的提案提出了若干问题。第一，欧洲人并非把在国内创造私有财产的成功视为理所当然，以至于忽视了在其他地区引入这种制度。若要说有哪种情况成立，倒是恰恰相反。欧洲关于私有财产之性质和重要性的许多现代思考，都是在殖民统治背景下形成的，无论是在爱尔兰、印度、埃及和澳大利亚的英国人，还是在北非和其他领土的法国人。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-042"></a>[42](#note-ch6-042)殖民地不同之处在于，当地有能力减缓或阻止资产化过程。

The Egyptian experience raises a number of questions about the ILD’s more contemporary proposals. First, it is not the case that Europeans took their success in creating private property at home so much for granted that they overlooked its introduction in other parts of the world. If anything, it was the other way round. Much of modern European thinking about the nature and importance of private property was worked out in the context of colonial rule, whether by the British in Ireland, India, Egypt, and Australia or the French in North Africa and other territories.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-042"></a>[42](#note-ch6-042) What was different in the colonies was the local ability to slow down or prevent the process of assetisation.

<a id="ch06-0045"></a>

第二，德·索托忽视了一个事实：即使国内的“成功”也是有条件的，而且代价巨大。十八、十九世纪在英国巩固正式产权的人兴旺发达，但大多数人口并未如此。圈占农村社区共有土地、建立大型私有地产，迫使数十万家庭陷入贫困，被赶出乡村。在整个欧洲，数百万人被迫移居，前往城市，更多人迁往国外。他们去了北美和南美、澳大利亚、非洲南北部以及世界其他角落。在埃及和印度，当地人口有力量和政治组织来抵抗欧洲定居和土地收购造成的彻底失地；而在北美、澳大利亚等定居者殖民地，原住民被推到一边并逐渐消灭，以便欧洲财产所有权的扩张和正式化。

Second, de Soto overlooked the fact that even the success at home was a qualified one. It was achieved at great cost. Those who consolidated formal property rights in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Britain, for example, prospered. But a large majority of the population did not. The enclosure of lands held in common by rural communities and the creation of large private estates forced hundreds of thousands of households into poverty and drove them from the countryside. Across Europe, millions were forced into emigration, moving to the cities and, in even greater numbers, abroad. They moved to North and South America, Australia, northern and southern Africa, and other corners of the world. In contrast to Egypt and India, where the local population had the power and the political organisation to resist the complete loss of their land to European settlement and land acquisition, in settler colonies like North America and Australia the native population was pushed aside and gradually eliminated, to enable the expansion and formalisation of European property ownership.

<a id="ch06-0046"></a>

奇怪的是，德·索托在讨论这部全球私有财产史时，只详细考察了一个案例——而且大部分细节都缺失了。他描述了美国向西扩张<a id="page-219"></a>〔原书第219页〕殖民过程中，如何把非正式所有者纳入正式财产制度，特别是加州占地者和矿工协会所确立的财产主张如何得到接受。在德·索托看来，这个案例例证了把非正式财产的“死”资本转变为国家承认并监管的法律秩序中的活资本的成功过程。他无视“死”资本问题本身部分是由正式化造成的事实。许多定居者被迫以占地者身份夺取土地，因为土地投机者已经控制了最新法定土地定居点之外较好的土地。他忽略了：在从墨西哥夺占该领土后，加州欧洲占地者和矿工的主张，是通过否认其所驱赶的大多数美洲原住民和墨西哥人口享有任何同等权利而确立的。而且，由于他把定居者殖民主义当作证据，他忽视了欧洲更大规模的剥夺和驱逐问题，而定居者殖民主义正是对这些问题的回应。只有剥去其历史的每一层，十九世纪加州的案例才会呈现为一种可供当代发展中国家改革者效仿的成功。

Curiously, de Soto’s discussion of this global history of private property examined only one case in detail – and most of the detail is missing. He describes the incorporation of informal owners into the formal property regime of the United States as the country expanded its <a id="page-219-en"></a>〔原书第219页〕colonisation westward, in particular the acceptance of the property claims established by squatters’ and miners’ associations in California. This case exemplifies for de Soto the successful process of turning the ‘dead’ capital of informal property into the live capital of a legal order recognised and regulated by the state. He disregards the fact that the problem of ‘dead’ capital was itself partly created by formalisation. Many settlers had been forced to seize land as squatters because land speculators had taken control of the better land just beyond the most recent legal land settlements. He ignores the fact that the claims of European squatters and miners in California, following the seizure of the territory from Mexico, were established by denying any equivalent rights to most of the native American and Mexican populations they pushed aside. And, by using as evidence the example of settler colonialism, he overlooks the larger problems of dispossession and eviction back in Europe to which settler colonialism was a response. The case of nineteenth-century California illustrates a success that contemporary reformers in developing countries might emulate only if one strips it of every layer of its history.

<a id="ch06-0047"></a>

与北美定居者殖民主义的成就及其给原住民社群带来的灾难相比，欧洲在埃及和印度等国的殖民主义不那么成功。它遇到的是土地占有安排已建立数百年的人口，其土地主张更难通过资产化和止赎予以根除，也无法将这些实际居住于此的人口消灭。即使在巴勒斯坦，犹太复国主义定居者曾希望利用资产化、土地购买、止赎和驱逐来暗中夺取整个国家，原住民人口也大体上进行了抵抗，导致定居者运动——如我们在上一章所述——转向以军事力量进行剥夺。在世界其他地区，尽管建立欧洲财产制度的尝试在若干国家引发了一系列“维多利亚晚期大屠杀”，数千人、有时数百万人丧生，大多数人口仍能抵抗彻底剥夺，并在二十世纪设法限制甚至扭转私有财产权力的实施。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-043"></a>[43](#note-ch6-043)

In contrast to the achievements of settler colonialism of North America, and the disaster it entailed for native communities, European colonialism in countries like Egypt and India was less successful. It encountered populations whose land tenure arrangements had been established over several centuries, whose claims to the land were more difficult to eradicate through assetisation and foreclosure, and whose physical presence could not be eliminated. Even in Palestine, where Zionist settlers had hoped to use assetisation, land purchase, foreclosure, and eviction to take over the country by stealth, the native population largely resisted, causing the settler movement, as we noted in the last chapter, to turn to dispossession by military force. In other parts of the world, although the attempt to establish European property regimes helped trigger a series of ‘late Victorian holocausts’ in several countries, in which thousands and, in some cases, millions of people lost their lives, most populations were able to resist complete dispossession and in the twentieth century managed to limit and even roll back the implementation of the powers of private property.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-043"></a>[43](#note-ch6-043)

<a id="ch06-0048"></a>

虽然*《资本的奥秘》*无视正式产权发展所伴随的剥夺历史，德·索托却意识到，当前问题的关键取决于保障问题。他说，非正式财产安排的问题在于，它们让人们太有保障，其免于被剥夺的权利<a id="page-220"></a>〔原书第220页〕受到太强的保护。他说，在西方之外，“法律和官方机构被早期殖民法和罗马法所困，这些法律偏向于保护所有权”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-044"></a>[44](#note-ch6-044)如同十九世纪欧洲人在埃及所要求的那样，他所主张改革的一个核心要素就是取消这种保护。只有把规则和权力安排得使债权人能够夺取违约债务人的财产，土地和住房才能被资产化，作为扩大信贷的抵押品。

While *The Mystery of Capital* ignores the history of dispossession that accompanied the development of formal property rights, de Soto is aware that the issues at stake in the present hinge on questions of security. He says that the problem with informal property arrangements is that they leave people too secure, with their rights against dispossession <a id="page-220-en"></a>〔原书第220页〕too strongly protected. Outside the West, he says, ‘the law and official agencies are trapped by early colonial and Roman law, which tilt towards protecting ownership’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-044"></a>[44](#note-ch6-044) One of the central elements of the reforms that he advocates, as Europeans demanded in Egypt in the nineteenth century, is the removal of this protection. Land and housing can only be assetised, serving as collateral for the extension of credit, if rules and powers are arranged to enable creditors to seize the property of debtors who default.

<a id="ch06-0049"></a>

虽然承认需要这些新权力，*《资本的奥秘》*却未能探讨它们可能导致何种后果。撇开上文所述的殖民历史不谈，即使在今天，这些后果也不难观察到。以美国农业为例。十九世纪美国扩张期间，土地主张被纳入正式财产制度的白人占地者，大多在二十世纪失去了财产。小农场主以及后来的中等农场主逐渐被淘汰。1930 年代至 1980 年代之间，三分之二的美国农场停业并失去财产。在推广德·索托思想时，这一剥夺过程完全被忽视。*《经济学人》*一篇讨论自由与民主研究所面向贫困国家产权登记提案的文章指出：“在富国，如果农场主想投资更好的种子或更大的拖拉机，他大概可以用自己的土地作担保借到所需现金。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-045"></a>[45](#note-ch6-045)这通常不是农场主想不想的问题，而是迫不得已。到 1980 年代，美国农用物资产业超过四分之三由四家公司控制，大多数农产品贸易也受类似垄断支配。农场主受到上下游垄断的挤压，不得不以财产作抵押借钱维持经营。止赎机制逐渐迫使他们离开土地。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-046"></a>[46](#note-ch6-046)土地被效率较低但更有权势的公司经营实体接管，这些公司利用其政治资源获得越来越大的政府补贴。全球南方国家永远无力承受让私有财产、抵押品和信贷机制造成如此规模灾难的后果。

Although it acknowledges the need for these new powers, *The Mystery of Capital* fails to explore the kinds of consequence to which they can lead. Leaving aside the colonial history outlined above, even today these consequences are not hard to observe. Take the example of farming in the United States. Most of the white squatters whose land claims were incorporated into the formal property system of the United States during its nineteenth-century expansion lost their property in the course of twentieth century. Small and later medium farm owners were gradually eliminated. Between the 1930s and the 1980s, two-thirds of American farms went out of business and lost their property. This process of dispossession is entirely overlooked in the promotion of de Soto’s ideas. ‘In rich countries’, notes an article in *The Economist* discussing the ILD’s property titling proposals for poor countries, ‘if a farmer wants to invest in better seeds or bigger tractors, he can probably borrow the necessary cash using his land as security.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-045"></a>[45](#note-ch6-045) This is not usually a question of what the farmer wants, more an issue of necessity. By the 1980s, more than three-quarters of the American farm supply industry was controlled by four firms, and similar monopolies governed trade in most farm products. Squeezed by monopolies on both sides, farmers were obliged to use their property as collateral to borrow money to stay in business. The mechanism of foreclosure gradually forced them off the land.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-046"></a>[46](#note-ch6-046) The land was taken over by less efficient but more powerful corporate operations, which used their political resources to gain ever-larger government subsidies. The countries of the Global South could never afford to allow the mechanisms of private property, collateral, and credit to produce a disaster on this scale.

<a id="ch06-0050"></a>

上述事件轮廓提供了一种不同方式来理解这个问题：为什么埃及等国如此多的人持有尚未纳入正式财产制度的土地或住房？以及一个更大的问题：我们是否应把这些资产视为存在于市场经济“之外”，或资本主义之外？<a id="page-221"></a>〔原书第221页〕这些安排之所以出现，不是因为这类国家的人民不懂私有财产，也不是因为西方忽视了把这一制度输出到国外的必要性。与欧洲和北美财产正式化和资产化的受害者不同，农村和城市人口能够延缓其实施、改变其路径或限制其范围。他们处于这些财产机制“之外”的位置，是对遭受剥夺的一种长期、往往暴力、但最终相对成功的抵制的结果——欧洲和北美农村人口遭受了这种剥夺，而在定居者殖民主义得以推行的世界部分地区，原住民人口则被彻底边缘化或消灭。

This outline of events suggests a different way of understanding the question of why so many people in countries such as Egypt hold land or housing that has not been incorporated into a formal property system, and the larger question of whether we should think of these assets as existing ‘outside’ the market economy, or outside capitalism. These <a id="page-221-en"></a>〔原书第221页〕arrangements have not arisen because people in such countries are ignorant of private property or because the West overlooked the need to export the system abroad. Unlike the victims of property formalisation and assetisation in Europe and North America, rural and urban populations were able to delay, divert, or limit the extent of its implementation. Their position ‘outside’ these property mechanisms was the outcome of a long, often violent, but ultimately relatively successful objection to undergoing the dispossession inflicted on the rural populations of Europe and North America or the complete marginalisation or elimination of native populations in parts of the world where settler colonialism was carried through.

<a id="ch06-0051"></a>

把这些事件的结果描述为存在一个市场之外的世界，实在奇怪。对自由与民主研究所来说，这个“外部”是由无知和缺乏机会造成的。正式安排的好处从未扩展到那里。更有启发性的做法是把这一结果视为一片边疆。人们看到正式财产安排推进、后退、再推进。他们有时避开这些安排，有时被其吞没。他们从内部与之斗争，有时又将其转为地方上的优势。这片边疆一直是战场。它不是一条标示市场与非市场、正式与非正式、资产化与非资产化之间屏障的细线。它是横跨整个市场空间、贯穿所谓资本主义全部历史的战争地带。如果这是一个外部，那么它是随处可见的外部，是一个似乎界定着可以辨识出正式制度或资本主义的每一个地点的战斗场景。因此，它是一个“包容性排除”的地带，因为被宣布处于市场之外的东西，已经通过这种排除宣言以及围绕纳入的持续斗争，在其中扮演了角色。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-047"></a>[47](#note-ch6-047)

It is curious to describe the outcome of these events as the existence of a world outside the market. For the ILD, this outside is a place shaped by ignorance and lack of access. It is a place to which the benefits of formal arrangements were never extended. It would be more instructive to think of the outcome as a frontier. People have seen formal property arrangements advance, recede, and advance again. They have sometimes evaded them and sometimes been overtaken by them. They have worked against them from the inside and sometimes turned them to local advantage. The frontier has been a battleground. It is not a thin line marking the barrier between market and non-market, or formal and informal, or assetised and non-assetised. It is a terrain of warfare spread across the entire space of the market, the entire length of what is called the history of capitalism. If it is an outside, then it is an outside found everywhere, a scene of battle that seems to define every point at which the formal or the capitalist can be identified. It is therefore a zone of ‘inclusive exclusion’, since what is declared to be outside the market already plays a role within it, through the declaration of exclusion and the continuous battles over its inclusion.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-047"></a>[47](#note-ch6-047)

<a id="ch06-0052"></a>

### 家宅资产

### Homely Assets

<a id="ch06-0053"></a>

通过产权登记和资产化改造全球南方的提案，设想了三个不同步骤来纳入被宣布为排除在外的东西：把财产变为抵押品，把抵押品变为信贷，把信贷变为增加的收入。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-048"></a>[48](#note-ch6-048)有什么证据表明产权登记能够释放信贷，而新获得的信贷会带来这一系列后果？把市场“之外”的资产转变为市场之内金融繁荣的机制是什么？

The proposals for transforming the Global South through property titling and assetisation envision three distinct steps for including what is declared to be excluded: turning property into collateral, collateral into credit, and credit into increased income.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-048"></a>[48](#note-ch6-048) What is the evidence that property titling unlocks credit and that the newly available credit has this set of consequences? What is the mechanism that turns assets ‘outside’ the market into financial prosperity within?

<a id="ch06-0054"></a>

<a id="page-222"></a>〔原书第222页〕*《资本的奥秘》*对这个问题着墨很少。书中的主要论点是顺带提及一个观念：在美国，许多人用住房作抵押借款来创办小企业。这种信贷来源有多重要？德·索托对这一说法没有提供任何证据，而美国小企业信贷的现有数据也不提供多少支持。在极小型企业中，40% 根本不借款，而借款者最常见的来源是个人信用卡。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-049"></a>[49](#note-ch6-049)

<a id="page-222-en"></a>〔原书第222页〕*The Mystery of Capital* has little to say on this question. The main argument presented in the book is a passing reference to the idea that, in the United States, many people launch small businesses by borrowing funds using their homes as collateral. How significant is this source of credit? De Soto cites no evidence for the claim, and the data available on small business credit in the United States does not offer much support. Among very small businesses, 40 per cent borrow no funds at all and the most common source of loans for those that do is a personal credit card.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-049"></a>[49](#note-ch6-049)

<a id="ch06-0055"></a>

资产化和抵押住房在为商业投资融资方面的作用可能不如自由与民主研究所认为的那么重要，原因之一是，在西方，大多数人没有可供抵押的住房。虽然自有住房率从德国和瑞典的 40%、法国的 54%，到美国和英国高达 68% 不等，但这些数字包括已抵押但尚未还清贷款的住房，也包括居住者欠款超过房屋价值的情况。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-050"></a>[50](#note-ch6-050)从历史上看，自有住房率更低。例如在 1914 年之前的英国，多达 90% 的住房是私人租赁。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-051"></a>[51](#note-ch6-051)对西方大多数家庭来说，把住房用于商业贷款抵押并不是一个可选项。

One reason why assetising and mortgaging one’s home may play a less significant role in financing business investments than the ILD believes is that, in the West, most people do not have homes to mortgage. While home ownership rates range from 40 per cent in Germany and Sweden to 54 per cent in France and as high as 68 per cent in the United States and Britain, these figures include homes that are mortgaged and not yet paid for, including those whose occupants owe more than the value of the house.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-050"></a>[50](#note-ch6-050) Historically, rates of home ownership were even lower. In Britain, for example, before 1914, as much as 90 per cent of housing was privately rented.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-051"></a>[51](#note-ch6-051) For a majority of households in the West, using one’s home as collateral for a business loan is not an option available.

<a id="ch06-0056"></a>

在全球南方，自有住房率往往高得多，例如印度和墨西哥超过 80%。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-052"></a>[52](#note-ch6-052)由于住房信贷在这些国家作用极小，大多数住房由房主全额持有，不负担购房贷款。*《资本的奥秘》*主张，南方的低收入房主拥有一些资产，如果他们生活在北方，就会把这些资产转化为活资本。事实上，他们拥有的资产，如果他们生活在北方，在大多数情况下根本就不会拥有。

In the Global South, rates of home ownership are often much higher, above 80 per cent in India and Mexico, for example.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-052"></a>[52](#note-ch6-052) Because of the minimal role of housing credit in these countries, most of these homes are owned outright. *The Mystery of Capital* argues that low-income homeowners in the South possess assets that, if they lived in the North, they would transform into live capital. In fact, they possess assets that, if they lived in the North, in most cases they would not own.

<a id="ch06-0057"></a>

德·索托把全球南方的非正式财产制度描述为资本的一种缺陷形式。比较自有住房率的数据表明，它们或许反而应被视为一项重大成就。它们使数百万家庭能够居住在自己的住房中，免于抵押债务和止赎的威胁，尽管其收入只有西方家庭的一小部分，而西方能负担得起房产的家庭要少得多。

De Soto describes the informal property systems of the Global South as a defective form of capital. The figures on comparative homeownership rates suggest that they might, instead, be seen as a significant achievement. They enable millions of households to occupy their own dwellings, free of mortgage debt and the threat of foreclosure, even though their incomes are a fraction of those of households in the West, where far fewer can afford to own property.

<a id="ch06-0058"></a>

至少从 1940 年代起，非正式住房的优点就得到承认。当时，埃及建筑师哈桑·法西等人提倡乡土住房，作为战后政府计划——出钱让商业承包商建造不宜居住且相对昂贵的混凝土公寓楼——的替代方案。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-053"></a>[53](#note-ch6-053)到 1970 年代，<a id="page-223"></a>〔原书第223页〕发展实践者（但与大型承包商有联系的政府除外）已广泛接受非正式住房具有显著优势，尤其是如果采取措施克服非正式性的一些缺点。这些缺点可能包括服务不足、场地布局差、权属无保障——但不包括无法用房产作抵押。

The advantages of informal housing have been recognised since at least the 1940s, when people like the Egyptian architect Hassan Fathy promoted vernacular housing as an alternative to the plans of postwar governments to pay commercial contractors to build inhospitable and relatively expensive blocks of concrete apartments.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-053"></a>[53](#note-ch6-053) By the 1970s, it <a id="page-223-en"></a>〔原书第223页〕was widely accepted among development practitioners (but not by governments with ties to large contractors) that informal housing had significant advantages, especially if measures were taken to overcome some of the drawbacks of informality. These drawbacks might include inadequate services, poor site layout, and insecure tenure – but not an inability to use the property as collateral.

<a id="ch06-0059"></a>

2004 年对埃及南部一个村庄的观察所得的证据，可以说明这些优势近年来如何继续发挥作用。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-054"></a>[54](#note-ch6-054)第一，非正式住房往往是自建的。在村里，住房从最贫困的几户人家居住的、用棕榈秆涂抹泥土搭成的简陋棚屋，到泥砖（土坯）建造的坚固房屋，再到钢筋混凝土框架和烧制砖块建成的四五层建筑，有时同一大家庭每层住一户。许多家庭自己建房，通常得到男性亲属的帮助。另一些家庭雇请建筑工，建筑工可能是亲戚或邻居，通常还会借助该家庭成员的帮忙。使用当地可得、有时免费的建材也降低了费用。砖由泥土制成，混凝土用当地沙子，天花板梁和板条来自椰枣树（通常是雄性树，不结果实）的树干和枝条。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-055"></a>[55](#note-ch6-055)窗户、门和家具由当地木匠制作，而较便宜的家具由修剪树木的男人们用棕榈秆组装。回收的油罐被锤打拼接起来，做成最简陋房屋的门。安装电气和管道系统时，一些家庭雇请电工和水管工，但多数家庭能够自己安装，或在亲戚帮助下完成。这种自建、亲属服务和地方手艺行业的混合，使住房价格可负担，同时也支撑了相当规模的地方建筑业。

Evidence drawn from observations of a village in southern Egypt in 2004 can illustrate how its advantages still operated in recent years.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-054"></a>[54](#note-ch6-054) First, informal housing is often self-built. In the village, houses range from simple huts built of palm stalks plastered with mud, occupied by a few of the poorest households, to substantial houses made of mud brick (adobe), to four- and five-storey structures built with reinforced concrete frames and fired brick, sometimes accommodating a separate household of the same extended family on each floor. Many households build their own dwellings, often with the help of male relatives. Others hire a builder, who may be a relative or neighbour and usually employs help from the household. Expenses are also reduced by using building materials available locally, sometimes at no cost. Bricks are made from the earth, concrete from local sand, and ceiling joists and laths from the trunks and branches of date palms (usually the male trees, which do not produce fruit).<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-055"></a>[55](#note-ch6-055) Windows, doors, and furniture are made by local carpenters, while cheaper furniture is assembled from palm stalks by the men who trim the trees. Recycled oil cans are hammered together to make doors for the simplest houses. To install electrical and plumbing systems some households employ electricians and plumbers, but most are able to install these systems themselves or with the help of a relative. This mixture of self-building, the services of relatives, and local crafts and trades keeps housing affordable while also supporting a significant local construction industry.

<a id="ch06-0060"></a>

非正式、主要靠自建住房的其他优势包括：可以选择逐步建造，随着需求的发展和收入的到账，增建房间、楼层或添置设施，甚至日后用更耐久的材料重建整座住宅；使用适合当地的方法和建材；能够按居住者需要设计房屋布局，并在需求变化时加以改动——例如把前屋改成一间小店铺，或把后院改成作坊。

Other advantages of informal, largely self-built housing include the option to build incrementally, adding extra rooms, floors, or fixtures as needs develop and income arrives, or even to rebuild the entire dwelling in more durable materials later on; the use of locally appropriate methods and building supplies; and the ability to design the layout of the house to suit the occupants’ needs and to alter it as those needs change – converting a front room into a small store, for example, or a rear yard into a workshop.

<a id="ch06-0061"></a>

自建农村住房的成功取决于这样一个事实：它很少需要购买土地，而土地超出大多数家庭的负担能力。新住房的空间靠拆除较旧、<a id="page-224"></a>〔原书第224页〕较不坚固或需要翻新的建筑，靠扩建现有房屋、往往以减少原先用于家畜的土地为代价，或靠填补住宅之间的空隙来获得。没有土地建房的人寻找小块空地。有些人找到政府承认占地者住房并收取小额租金的高处、不可耕种地块。另一些人找到自己或亲戚农地的未用边缘，通常沿运河和道路边缘，或耕作区与沙漠交界处。1971 年阿斯旺高坝建成后，可以在农地上建房；此前，每年为灌溉而淹没田地的做法，使大部分农地免于被用于建房。1983 年通过的一项禁止在农地上建房的法令，以及 1996 年一项军事命令的强化，减少了农田损失，但未能消除这种做法。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-056"></a>[56](#note-ch6-056)2011 年革命起义之后，农地上不受监管的建造激增。2018 年的进一步立法和 2022 年出台的更严厉处罚，都未能阻止农田流失。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-057"></a>[57](#note-ch6-057)大多数新建筑位于现有村庄边界内或未利用土地上。然而，未利用地块短缺，加上政府无法促进沿沙漠边缘、军事用地和其他未充分利用土地的自建项目，加剧了获得适当地块的问题。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-058"></a>[58](#note-ch6-058)

The success of self-built rural housing depends on the fact that it seldom requires the purchase of land, which would be beyond the reach of most families. Space for new housing is found by pulling down older, <a id="page-224-en"></a>〔原书第224页〕less substantial structures or those in need of renewal, by adding to existing houses, often by reducing the land previously used for domestic animals, or by filling the gaps between dwellings. Those who own no land on which to build look for small plots of vacant land. Some find patches of higher, uncultivable ground, where the government recognises squatter housing and charges a small rent. Others find the unused margin of their own or a relative’s plot of agricultural land, typically along the edges of canals and roads or at the border where the cultivation meets the desert. The completion of the Aswan High Dam in 1971 made it possible to build on agricultural land, much of which was previously protected from building by the annual flooding of the fields for irrigation. A law passed in 1983 to ban construction on agricultural land, and reinforced by a military order of 1996, reduced the loss of farmland but failed to eliminate the practice.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-056"></a>[56](#note-ch6-056) Following the revolutionary uprisings of 2011, there was a surge in unregulated building on agricultural land. Further legislation in 2018 and harsher penalties introduced in 2022 were unable to prevent the loss of farmland.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-057"></a>[57](#note-ch6-057) Most new construction takes place within existing village boundaries or on unused land. However, the shortage of unused plots as well as the inability of the government to facilitate self-build projects along the desert margin and on military property and other underutilised land exacerbates the problem of access to suitable land.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-058"></a>[58](#note-ch6-058)

校注：底本称阿斯旺高坝于1971年建成。埃及水资源与灌溉部工程史区分了1970年7月主体工程完成与1971年1月15日正式揭幕两个时间节点。正文保留底本年份，读者宜注意竣工与揭幕口径之别。 https://www.mwri.gov.eg/?page_id=33310&lang=en

<a id="ch06-0062"></a>

以这种方式建造的住房可能是合法的、半合法的（例如违反建筑法规），或非法的（例如在农地上建造的住房）。所有业主都希望自己的住房合法，但不是因为他们打算把住房用作抵押品。合法住房不必承担违法建筑因频繁传唤和罚款而产生的费用，也可能更容易接通水和电。后者自 1990 年代以来已不那么成问题，当时一系列政府法令规定，违反农地建房禁令或建筑法规建造的住房，仍有资格接通公用设施。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-059"></a>[59](#note-ch6-059)

The housing built in this way may be legal, semi-legal (infringing building regulations, for example), or illegal (such as housing built on agricultural land). All owners would prefer their homes to be legal, but not because they plan to use them as collateral. Legal housing does not carry the expense of the frequent summonses and fines imposed on unlawful construction and may be easier to connect to the water and electricity supply. The latter has been less of a problem since the 1990s, when a series of government decrees ruled that houses built in violation of laws banning construction on agricultural land or of building regulations were nevertheless eligible for connection to utilities.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-059"></a>[59](#note-ch6-059)

<a id="ch06-0063"></a>

然而，合法也有缺点。主要问题是它使土地变得难以负担。2004 年，村里农地售价约为每基拉特 1,000 埃镑。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-060"></a>[60](#note-ch6-060)有时，农业部会把一块土地从村庄的耕地范围（*zimam*）中移出，例如因为它被建筑包围，不再获得足够日照而无法耕种。这使该地块可以合法建房。合法化使土地价值至少升至原来的十倍，达到每基拉特 10,000 埃镑以上。在更有价值的地点，<a id="page-225"></a>〔原书第225页〕例如主要城镇边缘的农地，合法化可使价值升至原来的三十到四十倍。

Legality, however, also has drawbacks. The main problem is that it makes land unaffordable. In 2004, agricultural land in the village sold for about e£1,000 per qirat.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-060"></a>[60](#note-ch6-060) Occasionally, the Ministry of Agriculture would remove a plot of land from the cultivated area (the *zimam*) of the village; for example, because it was surrounded by buildings and no longer received enough sunlight for cultivation. This made it legal to build on the plot. Legalisation increased the value of land by a factor of at least ten, to more than e£10,000 per qirat. In more valuable locations, <a id="page-225-en"></a>〔原书第225页〕such as agricultural land on the edge of a major town, legalisation could increase the value by a factor of thirty or forty.

<a id="ch06-0064"></a>

城市住房在若干方面明显不同于农村住房，但许多相同的原则仍然适用。在埃及，1967—74 年占领结束后以色列军队撤出苏伊士运河区，伊斯梅利亚城的重建包括一个成功项目，展示了“地块与基础设施”计划的优势——既促进自建，又避免服务不足、场地布局差和权属无保障的问题。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-061"></a>[61](#note-ch6-061)这个自筹资金项目提供了配有建筑地块和基础设施的开发用地，以及小额贷款和低成本建材供应。地块获得者有很长时间来偿还土地的未改良价值。要求立即建造、业主自住和延迟取得产权的规定，抑制了投机者和资产化。该项目认识到，提供正式土地产权可能妨碍低成本住房供应，因为这鼓励房地产投机者通过资产化抬高房价。反过来，如果不能通过业主自住等要求来抑制资产化，住房就会变得更难负担、更少可得。2016 年，据估计埃及城市有 640 万套住房空置。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-062"></a>[62](#note-ch6-062)

Urban housing differs in several obvious ways from rural, yet many of the same principles apply. In Egypt, the rebuilding of the city of Ismailiya following the withdrawal of the Israeli army from the Suez Canal zone after the 1967–74 occupation included a successful project to demonstrate the advantages of ‘site and service’ programmes to facilitate self-building while avoiding the problems of inadequate services, poor site layout, and insecure tenure.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-061"></a>[61](#note-ch6-061) The self-funding project made available development sites laid out with building tracts and services, along with small loans and supplies of low-cost building materials. The recipients of the plots were given long periods to repay the unimproved value of the land. Provisions requiring immediate construction, owner occupancy, and delayed acquisition of title discouraged speculators and assetisation. The project recognised that offering formal title to the land can hamper the provision of low-cost housing, as it encourages property speculators, by assetising housing, to bid up its price. Conversely, the failure to discourage assetisation, through requirements such as owner occupancy, makes housing less affordable and less available. In 2016, it was estimated that 6.4 million housing units in urban Egypt were unused.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-062"></a>[62](#note-ch6-062)

<a id="ch06-0065"></a>

### 财产的边界

### Boundaries of Property

<a id="ch06-0066"></a>

自由与民主研究所承认非正式住房的许多优点。然而其提案坚持认为，通过产权登记实现正式化是经济发展的唯一道路。这一坚持基于的不是非正式住房的相对好处，而是获得抵押品和信贷的机会。它声称，只有正式财产制度才能释放非正式住房中持有的死资本。现在是时候更具体地转向这一论点——一个关于通过资本化实现发展的论点。

The ILD acknowledges many of the advantages of informal housing. Yet its proposals insist that formalisation through property titling is the only route to economic development. The insistence is based on an argument not about the relative benefits of the informal but about access to collateral and credit. Only a formal property system, it is claimed, can release the dead capital held in informal housing. It is time to turn more specifically to this argument – an argument about development through capitalisation.

<a id="ch06-0067"></a>

埃及农村再次提供了可供开端的证据。尽管自由与民主研究所为埃及起草的提案集中于城市住房正式化，但在之前十年，他们主张的一些改革已在农村实施。这些改革（实际上是撤销早先对农业财产市场设限的改革）包括允许农民用土地作为农业发展<a id="page-226"></a>〔原书第226页〕银行贷款抵押品的措施，以及逐步取消农地租金管制，最终于 2002 年废除所有租佃保障。此后，地主可以自由重新谈判租金，甚至驱逐佃户——这些家庭在多数情况下自 1952 年土地改革之前就以名义租金耕种土地。两项改革合在一起，似乎恰好许诺了*《资本的奥秘》*所描述的东西：让业主释放锁定在土地中的资本，或者把土地抵押贷款，或者以更高收入水平出租。

Once again, the case of rural Egypt provides evidence with which to begin. Although the proposals the ILD drew up for Egypt were focused on the formalisation of urban housing, over the preceding decade some of the reforms they advocated had already been carried out in the countryside. The reforms (actually, the undoing of earlier reforms that had set limits on the agrarian property market) included measures allowing farmers to use their land as collateral for loans from the Agricultural <a id="page-226-en"></a>〔原书第226页〕Development Bank, and a gradual lifting of rent controls on agricultural land, culminating in the abolition of all security of tenure in 2002. After that date, landowners were free to renegotiate rents or even evict their tenants – households that in most cases had been farming the land at nominal rents since before the land reform of 1952. Taken together, the two reforms seemed to promise exactly what *The Mystery of Capital* described, enabling owners to free up the capital locked in their land, either by pledging it as collateral for loans or renting it at increased levels of income.

校注：本段及下段将农地租佃保障取消记为2002年。Reem Saad在英国学术院发表的1992年租佃法研究指出，1992年第96号法给予地主在五年过渡期后驱逐佃户的权利，过渡期于1997年结束。底本年份与该法时间表不符；正文照录。 https://www.thebritishacademy.ac.uk/documents/3888/96p387.pdf

<a id="ch06-0068"></a>

当时没有足够证据对改革的影响作出一般性结论，部分原因是各村情况差异很大。例如，在该国一些地区，整个小村落耕种从单一所有者租来的土地。在这些情况下，2002 年废除租佃保障，把整个社群从土地的实际占有人变为无地农民，他们要么失去使用土地的机会，要么被迫以高得多的租金租地。在我一直描写的这个村庄里，出租地块分散得多。这往往有利于佃户。三户人家——都是兄弟——合种四英亩土地，其中三英亩自有，一英亩租来。出租一英亩的所有者住在同村一个邻近小村落，是原所有者的第二代继承人，根本不知道自家土地的确切位置。这块地位于另外三英亩中间的某处，但由于埃及的单块土地没有树篱或其他永久边界标志，无法确定其位置。原租赁合同规定了它相对于其他地块的位置，但那些地块也没有标记。即使所有者设法找到了自家地块，他们也无法把灌溉水引到那里。他们未曾获得使用穿过邻居田地的沟渠的权利，也没有单独的沟渠供应这一英亩。所有者要求把年租金从 300 埃镑（约 50 美元）提高到 1,200 埃镑。兄弟们拒绝，最终同意支付 600 埃镑。如果所有者不是来自邻近小村落，兄弟们还会付得更少。

There was insufficient evidence to draw any general conclusions about the impact of the reforms, in part because circumstances vary greatly from one village to another. In some parts of the country, for instance, entire hamlets farmed land rented from a single owner. In these cases, the abolition of security of tenure in 2002 transformed the whole community from effective possessors of the land into landless farmers, who either lost access to the land or were forced to rent at much higher rates. In the village about which I have been writing, the rental plots were much more widely dispersed. This tended to favour the tenants. One group of three households, all brothers, together farmed four acres of land, three acres of which they owned and one of which they rented. The owners of the rented acre lived in a neighbouring hamlet of the same village but were the second-generation heirs of the original owner and had no idea of the exact location of their land. It lay somewhere in the middle of the other three acres, but, since individual plots in Egypt have no hedgerows or other permanent boundary markers, there was no way to establish its position. The original rental contract specified its position in relation to other plots of land, but these were also unmarked. Even if the owners had managed to locate their plot, they would not have been able to bring irrigation water to it. They had established no rights to use the ditches that carried water across neighbours’ fields, and no separate ditch supplied their acre. The owner demanded an increase in annual rent from e£300 (about US$50) to e£1,200. The brothers refused and eventually agreed to pay e£600. If the owners had not been from a nearby hamlet, the brothers would have paid even less.

<a id="ch06-0069"></a>

这个案例——若干类似案例之一——说明了一些有用的要点。第一，就新法增加业主权利的方面而言，其效果并不是把死资本变成活资本。所有者提高了租金，但增加部分来自佃农，他们的收入每年减少 300 埃镑。这标志着财富从农民的生产性劳动<a id="page-227"></a>〔原书第227页〕转向食租者的非生产性劳动。第二，这种收入转移受财产记录薄弱的限制。出租一英亩的所有者无法完全确立其土地主张，使佃农得以支付较低租金。耕种者关于土地的地方知识，比德·索托视为资本主义发展秘诀的不完整“抽象”产权知识更有效力。这种知识的不完整，限制了收入从耕种和熟悉土地的人手中转入相对陌生者手中的程度。正式财产制度破坏这种地方知识，把所有权与所谓更抽象、肯定更遥远的各种形式连接起来，这些形式可以被外人积累、管理并当作租金来源。防止这类知识落入外人之手或财产登记册，是保护地方收入的一种资源。

This case, one of several similar cases that came to light, illustrates some useful points. First, to the extent that the new law increased the rights of property owners, its effect was not to turn dead capital into live. The owners increased their rent, but the increase came from the tenant farmers, whose income declined by e£300 a year. This marked a <a id="page-227-en"></a>〔原书第227页〕shift in wealth from the productive labour of farmers to the unproductive labour of a rentier. Second, this transfer of income was limited by the weakness of property records. The inability of the owners of the rented acre to establish fully their claim to the land enabled the tenant farmers to pay a lower rent. The local knowledge of those who farmed the land was more powerful than the incomplete ‘abstract’ knowledge of property entitlement that de Soto sees as the secret to capitalist development. The incompleteness of such knowledge was a means of limiting the diversion of income away from those who worked and knew the land, into the hands of relative strangers. Formal property systems undermine this local knowledge by linking ownership into what are called more abstract, certainly more distant, forms, which can be accumulated, managed, and made sources of rent by outsiders. Preventing the transfer of this kind of knowledge into the hands of outsiders or property registers was a resource for protecting local income.

<a id="ch06-0070"></a>

这一案例并非孤立。村里有许多类似案例。它们得到我们关于财产积累和不平等创造的所有证据的印证。正式法定产权和财产登记的产生，成为资产化的机器，从而使财产从小所有者手中转移，集中到越来越大的所有者手中。我们已经注意到这台机器在十九世纪中叶至二十世纪中叶埃及的运作，以及政府被迫采取的限制其效力的措施。巴拉圭农村一项土地产权登记计划的证据表明，收益只流向相对富裕的生产者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-063"></a>[63](#note-ch6-063)进一步证据来自新农业法另一部分对村庄的影响——农业发展银行取得土地作为贷款抵押品、并在借款人违约时夺取土地的新权力。几年之内，就有几起农民因此失去土地的案例，而且违约者无一例外都是小所有者。唯一有能力购买以这种方式释放之土地的人，是极少数大所有者，在数千户中不过十来户。其他研究显示了用土地作抵押品的其他不利后果。家庭用土地作抵押时，不得不在计算中加入相对低效的保险措施，以应对歉收或其他意外冲击，办法是坚持种植低风险、低回报作物——在埃及这一地区是甘蔗。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-064"></a>[64](#note-ch6-064)鉴于这些缺点，更有效的做法是积累和使用那些即使损失，对家庭造成的<a id="page-228"></a>〔原书第228页〕灾难性打击也较小的信用形式，例如生产和储存粮食、饲养牲畜。

This case was not an isolated one. There were numerous similar cases in the village. Together, they are corroborated by all the evidence we have about the accumulation of property and the creation of inequality. The creation of formal legal title and property registration becomes a machinery for assetisation and hence for transferring property from small owners and concentrating it into larger and larger hands. We have already noted the operation of this machinery in Egypt between the mid-nineteenth and mid-twentieth century, and the measures the government was forced to adopt to limit its effectiveness. Evidence from a land titling programme in rural Paraguay suggests that gains go only to relatively wealthy producers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-063"></a>[63](#note-ch6-063) Further evidence comes from the impact on the village of the other part of the new agrarian laws – the new powers of the Agricultural Development Bank to take land as collateral for loans, and to seize the land if the borrower defaults. Within a few years there were several cases of farmers losing their land by this mechanism, and in every case the defaulters were small owners. The only people in a position to buy land that became available in this way were the small handful of large owners, no more than a dozen households out of several thousand. Other studies show other adverse consequences of using land as collateral. When households use their land as collateral they have to add to their calculations relatively inefficient insurance measures that help them deal with poor harvests or other unexpected shocks, by keeping to low-risk, low-return crops – sugar cane in this region of Egypt.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-064"></a>[64](#note-ch6-064) Given these drawbacks, it is more efficient to build up and draw upon forms of credit whose loss is less <a id="page-228-en"></a>〔原书第228页〕catastrophic to the household, such as producing and storing grain and raising animals.

<a id="ch06-0071"></a>

用财产作信贷抵押品的另一个问题是，穷人很少能从资产损失中恢复。他们往往被迫在几乎没有有效需求时（衰退期间或歉收之后）低价出售财产，而在正常时期价格较高时又不得不买回来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-065"></a>[65](#note-ch6-065)从历史上看，这类困境中的被迫出售在财产所有权集中中发挥了重要作用，并与地方风险管理方式的丧失相关。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-066"></a>[66](#note-ch6-066)

A further problem with using property as collateral for credit is that the poor are seldom able to recover from asset losses. They are often forced to sell property at low prices (during a recession or after a bad harvest), when there is little effective demand, and have to buy back in normal times, when prices are higher.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-065"></a>[65](#note-ch6-065) Historically, such distress sales play an important role in the concentration of property ownership, and are connected with the loss of local ways of managing risk.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-066"></a>[66](#note-ch6-066)

<a id="ch06-0072"></a>

至于声称的用财产作贷款抵押品的好处呢？现有证据表明，正面影响很小，甚至没有。如果非正式财产持有者寻求产权，那也不是为了用它担保贷款而使财产承受风险。自由与民主研究所自己设计并管理的秘鲁产权登记计划是同类中规模最大的之一，清楚表明了这一点。四项独立研究都发现，该计划对商业信贷供给没有可察觉的影响。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-067"></a>[67](#note-ch6-067)正如一项研究所总结的，“标准商业银行和非正式贷款机构的贷款申请批准率都不受住房所有权状况影响”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-068"></a>[68](#note-ch6-068)泰国一项大型产权登记计划也被发现不影响获得银行贷款的可能性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-069"></a>[69](#note-ch6-069)其他农村产权登记计划研究则发现，“产权可能使大生产者更容易获得信贷，但不会使小土地所有者达到贷款机构的授信要求，这种情况会加深原先的不平等”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-070"></a>[70](#note-ch6-070)产权登记计划还可能在其他方面产生不利后果。在男子与正式制度打交道的场合，妇女可能失去她们在非正式财产制度下拥有的主张。按需登记产权“往往给穷人带来灾难性后果，因为政治关系良好的人常常能够绕过原住民、妇女或其他弱势群体的土地权利”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-071"></a>[71](#note-ch6-071)世界银行发展经济学家的研究、出版物和会议汇集了数十个案例研究的证据，表明自由与民主研究所的提案行不通。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-072"></a>[72](#note-ch6-072)

What about the alleged benefits of being able to use property as collateral for loans? The evidence available shows that there is little or no positive impact. If those with informal property seek title, it is not to risk it in taking out loans. The titling programme the ILD itself devised and managed in Peru, one of the largest, demonstrated this clearly. Four separate studies of the programme found that it had no discernible effect on the supply of business credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-067"></a>[67](#note-ch6-067) As one study concluded, ‘loan acceptance rates of both standard commercial banks and informal lenders are unaffected by residential ownership status’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-068"></a>[68](#note-ch6-068) A large property titling programme in Thailand was also found to have no effect on the likelihood of receiving bank loans.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-069"></a>[69](#note-ch6-069) Other studies of rural titling programmes have found that ‘the title might make it easier for large producers to access credit but would not make small landowners creditworthy, a situation that would deepen preexisting inequalities’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-070"></a>[70](#note-ch6-070) Titling programmes can have adverse consequences in other ways as well. Women may lose claims they have under informal property systems, in situations where men deal with the formal system. Titling on demand ‘has often had disastrous consequences for the poor because individuals with good political connections can often bypass the land rights of indigenous people, women, or other vulnerable groups’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-071"></a>[71](#note-ch6-071) Research, publications, and conferences organised by development economists at the World Bank brought together the evidence from dozens of case studies indicating that the ILD’s proposals would not work.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-072"></a>[72](#note-ch6-072)

<a id="ch06-0073"></a>

我们在这里面对的不再是一个简单图景：死资本躺在市场之外、正式经济的边界之外。我们看到的是另一幅图景：这条边界变成谈判、权利主张、权力关系、侵占和排除尝试的地带。问题不是把资产从边界外转移到边界内，而是权力、不平等和贫困的重新安排。

We are no longer dealing here with a simple image of dead capital lying outside the market, beyond the boundary of the formal economy. We have a different picture, in which this boundary turns into a terrain of negotiations, the claiming of rights, relations of power, attempts at encroachment and exclusion. Rather than a problem of transferring assets from outside the boundary to inside, there are rearrangements of power, inequality, and poverty at stake.

<a id="ch06-0074"></a>

<a id="page-229"></a>〔原书第229页〕

<a id="page-229-en"></a>〔原书第229页〕

<a id="ch06-0075"></a>

### 有所可失

### Having to Lose

<a id="ch06-0076"></a>

那么，现在该考虑的不是资本的奥秘，而是*《资本的奥秘》*的奥秘。它的论点似乎以一种缺陷形式存在，无视历史经验，也没有任何现有当代证据的支持。是什么神秘过程把这类有缺陷的分析转变为活生生的政治项目？

It is time to consider, then, not the mystery of capital, but the mystery of *The Mystery of Capital*. Its arguments appear to exist in defective form, ignoring historical experience and unsupported by any of the available contemporary evidence. What is the mysterious process that transforms such defective analysis into live political projects?

<a id="ch06-0077"></a>

似乎没有证据支持自由与民主研究所的论点——产权登记是解开西方之外资本主义发展问题的钥匙。大量证据表明，这无助于改善现状；而且有充分理由认为，对大多数人口来说，这会让他们的未来更糟。这些研究对具体项目的成败作了详细评估，而自由与民主研究所关于全球转型的笼统提案完全缺少这类评估。既然如此，这些论点从哪里获得力量？它们又如何传播得如此广泛？

There appears to be no evidence to support the ILD’s argument for property titling as the key to unlocking the problem of capitalist development outside the West. There exists a large amount of evidence to indicate that this will do nothing to improve the situation, and a strong case can be made that for the majority of the population it will make things worse for their futures. These studies provide the kind of detailed evaluations of the success and failure of particular projects that is entirely missing from the ILD’s sweeping proposals for global transformation. Given this evidence, where do such arguments acquire their power? How do they come to circulate so widely?

<a id="ch06-0078"></a>

前文所述德·索托项目通过新自由主义政治网络进行的营销，提供了部分答案；德·索托对解决资本主义奥秘之专有技术的主张，也提供了部分答案。但仅凭这些，无法解释他所主张的特定纲领为何被迅速采纳，而该纲领只是若干新自由主义政治改革之一。世界银行、美国国际开发署和其他资助德·索托项目机构的报告表明，该纲领与其他新自由主义改革的不同之处在于，它似乎格外具有成本效益。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-073"></a>[73](#note-ch6-073)它似乎提供某种东西，却几乎不费分文。我们被告知，全球南方的问题在于人们贫穷。自由与民主研究所提供的不是财富，而是一种在未来实现无人知晓他们拥有的财富的手段。这种效果是如何实现的？

The marketing of de Soto’s project through the political networks of neoliberalism, described earlier, provides part of the answer, as does de Soto’s claim to proprietary techniques for solving the mystery of capitalism. But these alone do not explain the rapid adoption of the particular programme de Soto advocates, which is one of several kinds of neoliberal political reform. The reports of the World Bank, USAID, and other agencies that have funded de Soto’s programme suggest that what distinguishes the programme from other neoliberal reforms is that it appears to be extraordinarily cost-effective.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-073"></a>[73](#note-ch6-073) It seems to offer something for almost nothing. The problem of the Global South, we are told, is that people are poor. The ILD offers them, not riches, but a means of realising wealth in the future that no one knew they had. How is this effect achieved?

<a id="ch06-0079"></a>

几乎无需付出成本就获得收益的可能性，建立在市场有一个“外部”的观念上。如果没有各种安排让事物可以说是存在于经济之外，那么“用目前被视为无物的东西创造货币”这一提案就毫无意义。货币将因看似把资源从外部移入内部的操作而无中生有。市场之外地点的产生，创造了价值既存在又不存在的资产的可能。资产作为物质财富存在，但不是作为资本存在。把这种有缺陷的财富带入经济内部的行为，把它从惰性之物变成活跃之物，从死变为生。

The possibility of getting something for nothing rests on the notion that the market has an ‘outside’. The proposal that money can be created out of what presently counts as nothing would make no sense without arrangements whereby things can be said to exist outside the economy. Money is to be created out of nothing by the action of seeming to move resources from the outside to the inside. The production of a place outside the market creates the possibility of assets whose value is both existent and non-existent. The assets exist as material wealth, but not as capital. The act of bringing this defective wealth inside the economy transforms it from something inert into something active, from death to life.

<a id="ch06-0080"></a>

<a id="page-230"></a>〔原书第230页〕这种外部与内部之间边界的说法之所以有力量，并非来自它对经济关系的描述准确。它来自为确立这种包容性排除、执行资产转移而提供的工具和论点。自由与民主研究所帮助整理未记录资产的数据，识别其流动障碍，并具体说明这种转移所需的法律和金融机制。它的工作帮助把地方政客、国际金融机构、房地产开发商甚至穷人代言人的特定联盟拉到一起，以执行这种转移。与此同时，它试图让其他类型的主张和其他形式的政治噤声。

<a id="page-230-en"></a>〔原书第230页〕The power of this account of a boundary between an outside and an inside does not arise from the accuracy of its description of economic relations. It comes from the tools and arguments that are made available for establishing this inclusive exclusion and performing the transfer of assets. The ILD helps organise the data on unrecorded assets, identify obstacles to their movement, and specify legal and financial mechanisms needed for this transfer. Its work helps pull together particular alliances of local politicians, international financial institutions, property developers, and even spokespersons for the poor, to carry out the transfer. At the same time, it attempts to silence other kinds of claims and other forms of politics.

<a id="ch06-0081"></a>

让我们更仔细地考察，把资产从市场“之外”移入“之内”的操作如何使资本得以产生。当未纳入正式制度的住房或土地的所有者取得正式产权时，财产价值往往上升。如前所述，在村里，使土地可以合法建房会使其价值升至原来的十倍。在非正式住房已经建成的地方，合法化带来的价值增幅较小，但仍然显著。在巴西，一项产权登记计划使土地价值翻了一倍。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-074"></a>[74](#note-ch6-074)另一项研究发现增幅为 25%，其他估算介于这两个数字之间。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-075"></a>[75](#note-ch6-075)这些增长在意料之中。正如世界银行一项关于农地产权登记的研究所解释的，“把未抵押土地用作抵押品的能力之价值，会资本化进土地价格”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-076"></a>[76](#note-ch6-076)

Let us consider more closely how the action of moving assets from ‘outside’ the market to the inside brings capital into being. When owners of irregular housing or land acquire formal title, the value of the property tends to increase. In the village, as noted above, making land legal for building increases its value by a factor of ten. Where informal housing is already built, the increase in value that comes with legalisation is less, but still significant. In Brazil, a property titling programme led to a doubling in the value of land.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-074"></a>[74](#note-ch6-074) Another study found an increase of 25 per cent, and other estimates fell between these two figures.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-075"></a>[75](#note-ch6-075) These increases are to be expected. As a World Bank study explained in relation to the titling of agricultural land, ‘the value of the ability to use unmortgaged land as collateral would be capitalised into land prices’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-076"></a>[76](#note-ch6-076)

<a id="ch06-0082"></a>

原则上，所有未纳入正式制度的财产的所有者都从这种价值增长中受益。但极少有人能出售房产，因为那会使他们无家可归。无论如何，购买另一处房产的需要也会抵消任何收益。只有那些持有房产不是为自身需要、而是为投机的人才会受益。同样，由于已经讨论过的原因，只有富有的所有者才能承担用住房作贷款抵押品的风险，并把增加的价值变成投资信贷。随着时间推移，产权登记导致财产集中到那些有能力按目前更高价值购买的人手中，并创造出投机者，这些人也因为此类房产如今提供的租金收入机会而受益。

In principle, all owners of irregular property benefit from this increase in value. But very few can sell their properties, since that would leave them homeless. In any case, the need to purchase another property would eliminate any gain. Only those holding property not for their own needs but for speculation would benefit. Likewise, for reasons already discussed, only wealthy owners could take the risk of using their dwelling as collateral for a loan and turn its increased value into credit for investments. Over time, titling leads to the concentration of property in the hands of those able to purchase it at the higher values it now commands, and creates speculators, who also benefit from the opportunities for income from the rent that such property now offers.

<a id="ch06-0083"></a>

财产价值的增长有两个来源，其中没有一个代表“死”资本被激活。短期内，增长来自投机性投资。这种投资只是把信贷创造从更具生产性的项目中抽走，加剧了因缺乏对创造就业活动的投资而造成的更广泛问题。但财产价值增长的绝大部分<a id="page-231"></a>〔原书第231页〕只有在较长期内、当下一代人寻求住房时才能实现。土地成本上升使未来住房更加昂贵。它如今带有支付投机者和食租者收入的溢价。因此，那些在当下为希望未来建造的房屋储蓄的人，必须更努力、更长久地工作，存更多的钱。

The increase in property value comes from two sources, neither of which represents ‘dead’ capital brought to life. In the short term, it comes from speculative investment. Such investment simply draws credit creation away from more productive ventures, exacerbating broader problems caused by the lack of investment in activities that create employment. But the bulk of any increase in property value is <a id="page-231-en"></a>〔原书第231页〕realised only in the longer term, when the next generation of individuals seeks housing. The rising cost of land makes future housing more expensive. It now carries the premium of paying the income of speculators and rentiers. So those saving in the present for a house they hope to build in the future must work harder and longer and save more funds.

<a id="ch06-0084"></a>

结果是财富的代际转移。大所有者和投机者立即从财产价值增长中获益。小财产所有者则看不到价值增长带来的好处。大所有者和投机者的收益，由未来一代所有者支付，他们面临为住房支付越来越多钱的前景。这种“收益”是从未来攫取的。

The outcome is an intergenerational transfer of wealth. Large owners and speculators gain immediately from the increased value of property. Small owners of property see no benefit from increased values. The gains of large owners and speculators are paid for by a future generation of owners, who face the prospect of paying increasing amounts for housing. The ‘gain’ is a capture from the future.

<a id="ch06-0085"></a>

怎么可能对这种从穷人向富人的代际财富转移重新安排，使它看起来像免费的钱，像把死资本变成活资本的简单行为？实现这一壮举的重要手段，是从一个假定开始：资本主义有一个“奥秘”，一个在德·索托文本中再现之前不可见的秘密。甚至在秘密被揭示和争论之前，存在这种奥秘的许诺就解除了文本读者或自由与民主研究所政策提案接受者的武装。据说资本主义有一个隐藏的钥匙或原则。剥夺、主张、暴力、组织和抵抗有多种形式，我们一直在讨论它们的多样性和流动性；这些形式被想象为表达着一个潜在原则，其名为资本主义。我们被告知，在多样性和暴力之下，有某种规则或法则，其隐藏存在使每一个历史案例都成为同一神秘本质形式的表达。德·索托成功的奥秘始于这个观念：存在一个奥秘。这确实是资本的托词的一部分。

How is it possible to reorganise this intergenerational transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich so that it appears as free money, as a simple act of turning dead capital into live? An important means of achieving this feat is to begin with the assumption that there is a ‘mystery’ to capitalism, a secret that is not visible until it is represented in de Soto’s text. Even before the secret is revealed and argued over, the promise that there is such a mystery disarms the reader of the text, or the recipient of the ILD’s policy proposals. Capitalism is said to have a hidden key or principle. The multiple forms of expropriation, claim, violence, organisation, and resistance whose diversity and motility we have been discussing are imagined to express an underlying principle, whose name is capitalism. Beneath the diversity and violence, we are told, there is some rule or law, whose hidden existence makes every historical case an expression of the same mysterious essential form. The mystery of de Soto’s success begins with the notion that there is a mystery. This indeed is part of the alibi of capital.

<a id="ch06-0086"></a>

在德·索托的案例中，资本主义奥秘的钥匙是我们此前在本书第一章遇到过的人物：企业家。拥有闲置资产可供创业的人越多，资本主义就越多。人们期望，向大量人口提供用财产作贷款抵押品的机会，会产生这种资本主义转变。

In de Soto’s case, the key to the mystery of capitalism is the figure we have met before, in the first chapter of this book: the entrepreneur. The more people there are with spare assets for entrepreneurship, the more capitalism there will be. Offering large numbers of people the opportunity to use their property as collateral for loans was expected to produce this capitalist transformation.

<a id="ch06-0087"></a>

当对自由与民主研究所秘鲁产权登记改革的连续几项研究都表明改革没有产生预期结果、用财产作抵押品的做法也没有增加时，经济学家仍然找到了积极结果。一项关于改革影响的研究声称表明，虽然新获产权所有者未能用住房作抵押，他们确实获得了重要好处：开始更努力地工作。据说数据显示，在屋外工作的小时数惊人地增加了 40%。<a id="page-232"></a>〔原书第232页〕研究作者主张，产权登记必定使住户摆脱了留在家中保卫财产的需要，使他们能够在市场上寻求更多就业。正是这项研究被*《纽约时报》*报道为自由与民主研究所改革产生显著影响的证据，并让另一位重要经济学家对经济学的未来抱有希望。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-077"></a>[77](#note-ch6-077)

When successive studies of the ILD’s property titling reforms in Peru all showed that they had not had the predicted results, and that there was no increase in the use of property as collateral, economists still found a positive outcome. A study of the impact of the reforms claimed to show that, while newly titled property owners failed to use their houses as collateral, they did realise an important benefit. They began to work harder. The data was said to show an astonishing 40 per cent <a id="page-232-en"></a>〔原书第232页〕increase in the number of hours worked outside the house. The author of the study argued that property titling must have freed householders from the need to stay home to defend their property, enabling them to seek more employment in the market. It was this research that was reported in the *New York Times* as evidence of the remarkable impact of the ILD’s reforms and gave another leading economist hope for the future of economics.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-077"></a>[77](#note-ch6-077)

<a id="ch06-0088"></a>

是什么使这篇论文如此受欢迎？它提供了一个图景：住户突然能够放下他们被迫用来在市场之外无法无天的世界里保护自身权利的武器。产权得到保障后，他们走向有利可图、和平的市场世界，在那里辛勤工作如今将得到回报。然而不幸的是，用于支持该论文结论的证据却显示，这些结论完全错了。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-078"></a>[78](#note-ch6-078)

What made the paper so popular? It offers an image of householders suddenly able to put down the weapons with which they were forced to protect their rights in the lawless world beyond the market. With property titles secured, they head off into the profitable, peaceful world of the market, where hard work will now be rewarded. Unfortunately, however, the evidence for the paper’s conclusions suggests that they are completely mistaken.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-078"></a>[78](#note-ch6-078)

<a id="ch06-0089"></a>

### 一种无形的平行生活

### An Invisible Parallel Life

<a id="ch06-0090"></a>

德·索托论点的说服力，也可以联系到埃及、秘鲁和许多其他在 1990 年代经历新自由主义经济重组计划的国家正式财产制度的危机。在开罗，稳定货币、削减政府开支、国有企业私有化和刺激私人投资的措施受到国际货币基金组织称赞，称其实现了“埃及宏观经济命运的显著好转”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-079"></a>[79](#note-ch6-079)同一时期，政府和法院开始修改保护商业和住宅租户的法律，使房地产开发商摆脱租金管制的约束。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-080"></a>[80](#note-ch6-080)改革刺激的信贷创造主要流入房地产——投机者在那里建造大量豪华和中档住宅——以及提供移动电话通信或麦当劳餐饮等服务、供应电子产品、汽车和其他奢侈品进口的独家特许权。换言之，资本化尽可能被改道到租金来源，而不是生产性活动。制造业在经济中的份额下降，也没有为大规模增加就业作出任何重大努力。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-081"></a>[81](#note-ch6-081)

The persuasiveness of de Soto’s arguments can also be connected to crises in the formal property system in Egypt, Peru, and many other countries that had experienced neoliberal economic restructuring programmes in the 1990s. In Cairo, measures to stabilise the currency, reduce government spending, privatise state-owned enterprises, and stimulate private investment had been praised by the IMF for achieving a ‘remarkable turnaround in Egypt’s macroeconomic fortunes’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-079"></a>[79](#note-ch6-079) In the same period, the government and the courts began to alter the laws protecting commercial and residential tenants, freeing property developers from the constraint of rent controls.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-080"></a>[80](#note-ch6-080) The credit creation stimulated by the reforms flowed primarily into real estate, as speculators threw up large luxury and middle-income developments, and into exclusive concessions to provide services, such as mobile phones or McDonald’s restaurants, or supply imports of electronics, cars, and other luxury goods. In other words, capitalisation was re-routed wherever possible into sources of rent rather than into productive activity.
