The share of manufacturing in the economy declined, and no significant efforts were made to increase large-scale employment.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-081"></a>[81](#note-ch6-081)

<a id="ch06-0091"></a>

房地产投机以及奢侈品进口和服务的繁荣，到 2000 年以深度衰退告终。豪华公寓价格下跌一半以上，房地产开发商发现自己有数万套未售出公寓。<a id="page-233"></a>〔原书第233页〕解决这些困难的办法，似乎在于自由与民主研究所的抵押贷款法提案。

The boom in property speculation and in luxury imports and services ended in a deep recession by the year 2000. The price of luxury apartments dropped by more than half, and property developers found themselves with tens of thousands of unsold apartments. <a id="page-233-en"></a>〔原书第233页〕A solution to these difficulties seemed to lie in the ILD’s proposal for a mortgage law.

<a id="ch06-0092"></a>

如前所述，2001 年议会通过了该法，此前自由与民主研究所及其当地合作伙伴埃及经济研究中心为经济部起草了立法草案和实施提案。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-082"></a>[82](#note-ch6-082)又过了两年，才设立监管新行业的机构，并成立第一家抵押贷款公司——国有住房与发展银行的子公司。该银行还与政府测量机构共同建立了一家测量和登记非正式财产的公司。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-083"></a>[83](#note-ch6-083)到 2005 年，只成立了两家抵押贷款公司，交易数量仍然非常有限。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-084"></a>[84](#note-ch6-084)拖延的原因以及未能成立更多抵押贷款公司的原因，颇能说明问题。首先是筹资问题。计划是通过在埃及股市出售证券（抵押债券）来为行业提供资本。但无论是程序还是投资者都不具备。如果德·索托的论点成立，这个障碍就说不通。产权登记和抵押贷款法本应通过释放不规范房地产的死资本来创造资金。现实中并没有死资本可以释放。相反，新抵押贷款制度试图把其他投资者拉入房地产，以拯救投机者。可用资本很少，因此改革陷入停滞。

In 2001, parliament passed the law, as mentioned earlier, following draft legislation and implementation proposals drawn up for the Ministry of the Economy by the ILD and its local partner, the Egyptian Center for Economic Studies.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-082"></a>[82](#note-ch6-082) It took a further two years to set up a body to regulate the new industry and to establish the first mortgage company, a subsidiary of the state-owned Housing and Development Bank. The Bank also established a company to survey and register informal property, co-owned with the government survey authority.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-083"></a>[83](#note-ch6-083) By 2005, only two mortgage companies had been established, and the number of transactions remained very limited.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-084"></a>[84](#note-ch6-084) The reasons for the delays and for the failure to establish additional mortgage companies are instructive. First, there was a problem in raising funds. The plan was to capitalise the industry by selling securities (mortgage bonds) on the Egyptian stock market. But neither the procedures nor the investors were available to do this. If the ILD’s arguments were valid, this obstacle would not make sense. Property titling and a mortgage law were supposed to create funds, by unlocking the dead capital of irregular real estate. In reality, there was no dead capital to unlock. Instead, the new mortgage system attempted to draw other investors into real estate, to bail out the speculators. There was little capital available, so the reforms stalled.

<a id="ch06-0093"></a>

第二个也是更重要的障碍，以及投资者缺乏热情的一个原因，据说是担心政府不会执行赋予抵押贷款公司止赎权力的新规定。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-085"></a>[85](#note-ch6-085)

The second and more important obstacle, and a reason for the lack of enthusiasm from investors, was said to be a fear that the government would not enforce new provisions giving mortgage companies the power of foreclosure.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-085"></a>[85](#note-ch6-085)

<a id="ch06-0094"></a>

德·索托承认，新财产制度就是要让财产所有者更没有保障。他声称，全球南方的人民仍“被困在前资本主义世界肮脏的地下室里”，不是因为他们没有财产，而是“因为他们没有财产可失去”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-086"></a>[86](#note-ch6-086)如果没有驱逐违约借款人的权力，整个从死资本释放财富的项目都会失败。但殖民时期长期反对止赎权力的斗争，使任何驱逐权力都难以使用。1952 年埃及革命的主要成就之一，就是巩固了对租户权利的保护。此后数十年间，众多地方斗争强化了一种广泛的政治主张：国家不应参与使人无家可归。事实上，在 2011 年革命起义之后，埃及<a id="page-234"></a>〔原书第234页〕新宪法明确规定了公民享有“充足、安全且健康住房”的权利。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-087"></a>[87](#note-ch6-087)自由与民主研究所的提案完全没有说明如何克服这一长期政治主张，也没有说明如何建立并有效实施资本化所依赖的新强制形式。

De Soto had acknowledged that the new property system was about making property owners less secure. People of the Global South remain ‘trapped in the grubby basement of the precapitalist world’ not because they have no property, he claimed, but ‘because they have no property to lose’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-086"></a>[86](#note-ch6-086) Without the power to evict borrowers who fell into default, the entire project of releasing wealth from dead capital would fail. But a long history of struggle against the powers of foreclosure in the colonial period had made it difficult to use any powers of eviction. One of the main achievements of the 1952 revolution in Egypt had been to consolidate the protection of tenants’ rights. Numerous local struggles over the ensuing decades had reinforced a widespread political claim that the state should not be involved in making people homeless. Indeed, following the revolutionary uprisings of 2011, the new Egyptian <a id="page-234-en"></a>〔原书第234页〕Constitution made explicit the right of citizens to ‘adequate, safe and healthy housing’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-087"></a>[87](#note-ch6-087) Nothing in the ILD’s proposals explains how this long-standing political claim was to be overcome, or how the new forms of coercion on which capitalisation depends were to be put in place and made effective.

<a id="ch06-0095"></a>

德·索托没有说明所涉及的力量关系，而是提供了一个简单得多的图景，描述把未登记资产变为活资本所需的程序。他把这一过程描述为再现，这个概念在他的论述中居核心地位。再现是把穷人的资产送入“市场”的操作。

In place of an account of the relations of forces involved, de Soto offers a much simpler picture of the procedures required to turn unregistered assets into live capital. He describes the process as one of representation, a concept that plays a central role in his account. Representation is the operation that moves the assets of the poor into ‘the market’.

<a id="ch06-0096"></a>

如果穷人以其所说的缺陷形式持有资产，那么缺陷就在于它们不可见——也就是说，对市场不可见。德·索托解释说，在西方，财产所有权再现于一份文件中，这份文件是“一个庞大隐藏过程的可见标志，这个过程把所有这些资产与经济其余部分连接起来”。由于这一再现过程，“资产可以在与其物质存在并行的层面上，过一种无形的生活”。其他国家没有这种再现过程，这解释了为什么人们无法生产足够资产使资本主义运转。只有西方拥有解码物质资产无形蕴藏的资本所需的“转换过程”。“这就是资本的奥秘。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-088"></a>[88](#note-ch6-088)

If the poor hold their assets in defective form, the defect is that they are not visible – not visible, that is, to the market. In the West, de Soto explains, property ownership is represented in a document, which is ‘the visible sign of a vast hidden process that connects all these assets to the rest of the economy’. Thanks to this process of representation, ‘assets can lead an invisible, parallel life alongside their material existence’. Other countries do not have this representational process, and this explains why people have not been able to produce sufficient assets to make capitalism work. Only the West possesses the ‘conversion process’ needed to decode the capital that material assets invisibly harbour. ‘This is the mystery of capital.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-088"></a>[88](#note-ch6-088)

<a id="ch06-0097"></a>

再现如何实现这种转换？答案是，与实物资产不同，资产的再现摆脱了物质约束，因此可以轻易移动、组合、分割，并用于创办企业。通过把资产的经济价值与其物质形式解耦，再现使资产具有可替代性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-089"></a>[89](#note-ch6-089)

How does representation achieve this conversion? The answer is that, unlike physical assets, representations of assets are set free from material restraints and therefore can be easily moved around, combined, divided, and used to launch business ventures. By uncoupling the economic value of an asset from its physical form, a representation makes the asset fungible.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-089"></a>[89](#note-ch6-089)

<a id="ch06-0098"></a>

首先应当指出，这种对西方再现过程的描述具有误导性。在许多西方财产制度中，包括美国和英国，并不存在德·索托所主张的那种产权文件。从历史上看，使用这类文件是被避免的，因为它可能过时，也可能被故意篡改，因而会招致欺诈。再现可能是危险之物，因为其使用并不总能受到控制。正如我下文所论证的，区分不同再现技术的不是其抽象性，而是其受控制的程度。在美国和英国，财产主张通过使用产权契据来确立。契据不是财产所有权的再现，而是对这种所有权的施行。它是一种法律文书，用来实施转移——不是<a id="page-235"></a>〔原书第235页〕对象（财产）的转移，而是权利（所有权）的转移。要具有法律效力，它必须包含“特此”之类的词语，表明契据是一种述行性工具。这种行为还必须通过实际动作来完成，即在证人面前把文书从原所有者交给新所有者。英国和美国的产权由一系列契据累积构成，标示权利从一个所有者向下一个所有者转移的连续行为。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-090"></a>[90](#note-ch6-090)

We should note, first, that this description of the process of representation in the West is misleading. In many Western property systems, including those of the United States and Britain, there was no title document of the sort that de Soto advocates. Historically, the use of such a document was avoided, because it could be outdated or might be deliberately altered and was therefore an invitation to fraud. Representations can be dangerous things, as their use cannot always be controlled. What distinguishes different techniques of representation, as I argue below, is not their abstractness but the degree of their control. In the United States and Britain, property claims were established through the use of title deeds. A deed is not a representation of property ownership, but its performance. It is a legal instrument used to perform the transfer – not <a id="page-235-en"></a>〔原书第235页〕of an object (property), but of a right (ownership). To be legally valid, it had to include a term such as ‘hereby’, indicating that the deed is a performative instrument. And it had to be physically performed, by handing the instrument from the previous owner to the new owner in the presence of a witness. Property titles in Britain and the United States consisted of an accumulation of deeds, marking the successive acts of transfer of rights from one owner to the next.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-090"></a>[90](#note-ch6-090)

<a id="ch06-0099"></a>

即使在今天，按德·索托主张的方式引入财产登记册的尝试在美国也未成功。多数州实行私人产权保险与交易公开登记相结合的制度。这些方法往往昂贵，因为它们容易受到价格操纵以及私人利益对立法监管的俘获。但以财产登记备案——由国家记录所有财产的所有权和转移——取代这些方法的尝试并不受欢迎，因为这些程序造成长时间拖延。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-091"></a>[91](#note-ch6-091)

Even today, attempts to introduce property registers in the way de Soto advocates have been unsuccessful in the United States. Most states use a system of private title insurance, combined with public registration of transactions. These methods tend to be expensive, as they are open to price fixing and the capture of legislative regulation by private interests. But attempts to replace them with property recordation, in which the state records the ownership and transfer of all property, were unpopular because of the long delays these procedures introduced.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-091"></a>[91](#note-ch6-091)

<a id="ch06-0100"></a>

说非正式财产制度缺乏复杂的再现系统，同样具有误导性。我们可以简要回到先前讨论的村庄。村民不断把资源投入各种资产、又从其中取出，程度相当惊人。最常见的例子是饲养家畜。几乎每户都饲养小动物（鸡、鸭、鹅、兔子和鸽子），许多人家养绵羊和山羊，超过一半拥有奶牛或水牛。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-092"></a>[92](#note-ch6-092)这些投资具有生产性，为餐桌提供食物，并自行繁殖。但当需要现金时，可以卖掉一只羊、一些鸡或一头牛犊。有剩余收入时，可以转化为更有保障的资产，通常是家畜（也包括以首饰形式储存的黄金）。家庭还组织轮流储蓄会，为购买炉子或水牛等大件物品筹资。卖掉一头大牲畜，可以帮助支付小本经营，例如买一台缝纫机承接裁缝活，或开一个小亭子向邻居出售香烟或日用品（糖、肥皂、灯泡）。

It is also misleading to suggest that informal systems of property lack complex systems of representation. We can return briefly to the village discussed earlier. It is remarkable the extent to which villagers are constantly moving resources into and out of a variety of assets. The most common instance is the raising of domestic animals. Almost every household is involved in raising small animals (chickens, ducks, geese, rabbits, and pigeons), many have sheep and goats, and more than half own a cow or a water buffalo.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-092"></a>[92](#note-ch6-092) These investments are productive, providing food for the table and making their own offspring. But, when a need for cash arises, a sheep, some chickens, or a calf can be sold. When surplus income arrives, it can be converted into more secure assets, typically domestic animals (but also gold, stored in the form of jewellery). Households also organise rotating credit unions to raise funds for large purchases, such as a new stove or a water buffalo. Selling a large animal can help pay for a small business venture, such as acquiring a sewing machine to take in dressmaking work or setting up a kiosk to sell cigarettes or household items (sugar, soap, light bulbs) to neighbours.

<a id="ch06-0101"></a>

与用土地和住房作信贷抵押品相比，这类储蓄和投资有几个优点。第一，它们把储蓄引入生产性活动，而不是房地产投资。第二，它们通常由妇女掌控，而妇女比男子更可能把收入用于儿童和家庭的基本需要。第三，这些资产可以相互转换，但又不至于过于容易转换。以家畜形式持有的资源在急需时可以换成现金，但足够实在，不会在随意购物中一点点流失。

Such kinds of saving and investment have several advantages over using land and housing as collateral for credit. First, they draw savings into productive activity rather than real estate investment. Second, they are typically controlled by women, who are more likely than men to direct income towards the basic needs of children and the household. Third, assets are fungible, but not too fungible. Resources held in the form of domestic animals can be converted to cash when urgent needs arise but are solid enough not to drip away on casual purchases.

<a id="ch06-0102"></a>

<a id="page-236"></a>〔原书第236页〕这些积累和流通资产的方法，与德·索托视为资本奥秘秘诀的方法有何不同？差异不在于再现的有无，也不在于其抽象程度。德·索托或许正确地指出，某些财富形式或某些再现资产的方式变得更具流动性、可以流通到更远的地方、更容易组合和积累。然而，这种流动性并非来自抽象程度，而是来自控制技术的建立，这些技术使资产能够远程、跨时间管理，并大量积累。

<a id="page-236-en"></a>〔原书第236页〕What is the difference between these methods of accumulating and circulating assets and those that de Soto sees as the secret to the mystery of capital? The difference does not lie in the presence or absence of representations, or their degree of abstraction. De Soto may be correct that certain forms of wealth, or certain ways of representing assets, become more mobile, travel further distances, and are more easily combined and accumulated. However, this mobility does not derive from the degree of abstraction. It derives from establishing techniques of control, which make it possible to manage assets at a distance and over time and accumulate them in larger quantities.

<a id="ch06-0103"></a>

在村里，多数家庭财富以直接监管控制的资产形式持有。财富积累在家畜、屋外田地、田地另一头亲戚家旁的灌溉泵，或下一个小村落的一块土地里。这一切都相对容易管理。大地主面临大得多的监管挑战。他们雇守卫保护粮食储备，让依附于他们的家庭操作不同地产区域内的灌溉泵，依靠劳务承包商提供收割工人队。十九世纪和二十世纪初建立的更大地产，在 1952 年后被拆解，只有在监督和规训大批劳动力的方法创新之后才成为可能；这些方法基于专门建造的工人住房单元，工人夜间可以被锁在里面，受到持续监视。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-093"></a>[93](#note-ch6-093)最大的地产拥有“一支名副其实的雇员队伍，其唯一职业就是以最紧密、最严格的方式持续监督工人”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch6-094"></a>[94](#note-ch6-094)监督权力，包括新法院、法警、监狱和武装警察，对于在新规模上积累财富的“再现”都至关重要。

In the village, most household wealth is held in assets controlled by direct supervision. The wealth is accumulated in domestic animals, the fields outside the house, an irrigation pump adjacent to a relative’s house across the fields, or a plot of land in the next hamlet. All this is relatively easy to manage. Large landowners face much greater challenges of supervision. They hire guards to protect stores of grain, use client families to operate irrigation pumps in different areas of landholding, and rely on labour contractors to supply gangs of workers for harvesting. The much larger estates built up in the nineteenth and early twentieth century, dismantled after 1952, were possible only after innovations in methods of monitoring and disciplining large labour forces, based on purpose-built worker housing units in which workers could be locked at night and kept under continuous supervision.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-093"></a>[93](#note-ch6-093) The largest properties possessed ‘a veritable brigade of employees whose sole occupation was to supervise the workers, continuously and in the closest and most rigorous fashion’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch6-094"></a>[94](#note-ch6-094) The powers of supervision, including the new courts, bailiffs, prisons, and armed police forces, were all essential to the accumulation of ‘representations’ of wealth on a new scale.

<a id="ch06-0104"></a>

如前所述，德·索托设想的财富积累，依赖于重新引入止赎和驱逐的权力，而这些权力在二十世纪面对民众抗议和经济混乱已被废止。换言之，问题不在于创造某种更抽象的东西，真要说来，反而在于某种更具物理强制性的东西——更广泛的驱逐和控制权力。尽管已有适当立法和监管机构、贷款公司和产权登记制度，抵押贷款银行的设立仍然拖延，这归根结底是因为未能获得最直接的物理强制权力。

The accumulation of wealth that de Soto has in mind depends, as I have noted, on the reintroduction of powers of foreclosure and eviction that were abrogated, in the face of popular protest and economic dislocation, in the course of the twentieth century. In other words, rather than a question of creating something more abstract, it is, if anything, a question of something more physical – more extensive powers of eviction and control. The delay in establishing mortgage banks, despite the appropriate legislation and regulatory body, the setting up of loan companies, and a property titling system, comes down to the failure to secure the most physical of powers.

<a id="ch06-0105"></a>

德·索托的计划设想通过把所谓死资本转变为活资本，大规模创造财富。在实践中，证据<a id="page-237"></a>〔原书第237页〕表明，这不会从死资本中产生活资本，而是把财富从较不富裕者转移给较有保障者，尤其是以未来穷人为代价，使当代较富裕者更加富有。

De Soto’s plans envisage a vast creation of wealth, by the transformation of so-called dead capital into live capital. In practice, the evidence <a id="page-237-en"></a>〔原书第237页〕suggests that this will produce not live capital out of dead, but a transfer of wealth from the less affluent to the more secure, and, in particular, serve to enrich the more prosperous among the present generation at the expense of the future poor.

<a id="ch06-0106"></a>

实现这一点的办法，不是把市场之外的东西移入市场之内，而是以新的方式部署这种边界机制。它不是通过再现目前不可见的东西来实现，而是通过改变再现的流通和管理来实现。它将通过重新安排各方力量而发生。而且它需要建立强制机制。

This is to be accomplished not by moving what is outside the market to the inside, but by deploying this boundary mechanism in new ways. It is not to be accomplished by representing what is currently invisible, but by altering the circulation and management of representations. It is to occur through a reorganisation of forces among a variety of parties. And it requires the creation of mechanisms of compulsion.

<a id="ch06-0107"></a>

新自由主义经济改革方案把未被记录、受治理较少的社会经济生活形式描述为存在于经济之外；它们事实上并非之外，但也并非简单地之内。它们可以被理解为一片边疆或边界，一种既不属于市场外部也不属于市场内部的状态。它们部分在外，因为这些资产无法由市场定价，正如控制这些资产者的劳动不容易为资本主义企业所用。经济学通过生产和验证规则与程序，帮助管理这条边界，把某些生活形式划定为非正式或非市场。然而这些生活形式在某些方面又在内部，因为所谓“资本主义”或“市场”所采取的安排——例如精英借以再生产其财富的主要手段即赚取租金的方式——是与这个所谓外部长期持续互动的结果。

The unrecorded and less closely governed forms of socioeconomic life that are described by neoliberal economic reform programmes as lying outside the economy are not in fact outside, but nor are they simply inside. They can be understood as a frontier or border, a status that is neither exterior nor interior to the market. They are partially outside, because these assets cannot be priced by the market, just as the labour of those who control them is not easily available for capitalist enterprise. Economics helps to manage this border, by producing and validating rules and procedures that demarcate certain forms of life as informal or non-market. Yet those forms of life are, in some ways, inside, because the arrangements taken by what is called ‘capitalism’ or ‘the market’, such as the ways of earning rent that are the principal means for an elite to reproduce its wealth, are the outcome of a long and continuing interaction with this so-called outside.

<a id="ch06-0108"></a>

德·索托的纲领——在联合国开发计划署贫困者法律赋权高级别委员会等机构推动下得到进一步推广——涉及把资产从外部移到内部。这种重新安排提供了创造财富的手段。但财富不是按德·索托论述所暗示的方法产生的。产权登记和用财产作抵押品的过程，创造了从未来投机获利、集中财富和积累租金的机会。穷人现有资产不是这种新财富的物质来源。相反，它们是包容性排除的对象。通过德·索托式的方案，它们被转变为实施这种重新安排和积累的装置。穷人仍处在这一过程“之外”，因为产权登记和财产抵押的结果是，土地和住房对穷人来说更加难以负担。他们进一步被排除在资源积累机会之外。然而，<a id="page-238"></a>〔原书第238页〕与此同时，他们又在过程“之内”。他们的房屋和未来生活必须被改造，才能完成对未来财富的攫取。这种改造的起点是使这些生活方式成为有缺陷的、近乎死寂的，办法是按照据说它们所缺乏的经济理性和再现形式来把握它们。既然正是其缺陷性使积累成为可能，那么这就是一个所谓内部所依赖的外部。

De Soto’s programme, further promoted by bodies like the UNDP’s High Level Commission on Legal Empowerment of the Poor, involves the movement of assets from the outside to the inside. This reordering offers a means to create wealth. But the wealth is not produced by the method de Soto’s account implies. The process of property titling and the use of property as collateral bring into being opportunities for speculative gain from the future, for the concentrating of wealth, and for the accumulation of rents. The existing assets of the poor are not the material source of this new wealth. Rather, they are the objects of an inclusive exclusion. Through schemes such as de Soto’s, they are turned into the apparatus through which this reorganisation and accumulation is carried out. The poor remain ‘outside’ this process, for the outcome of a process of property titling and the mortgaging of property is that land and housing become even less affordable to the poor. They are further excluded from opportunities for the accumulation of resources. Yet, at <a id="page-238-en"></a>〔原书第238页〕the same time, they are ‘inside’ the process. Their houses and their future lives must be transformed in order to carry out the capture of this future wealth. The starting point of this transformation is to render these ways of life defective, almost dead, by grasping them in terms of the economic rationality and forms of representation they are said to lack. Since their defectiveness is what makes the accumulation possible, it is an outside on which the so-called inside depends.

<a id="ch06-0109"></a>

对德·索托提案的常规批评，会揭露其借以获得可信度和流行度的新自由主义谬误。它会提请注意德·索托著作所忽视的产权斗争史，以及他无法解释替代性财产安排所提供的道德主张、财务保护、实际灵活性和可负担性——无论这些安排有什么缺陷。在把他的著作贬为新自由主义正典最新通俗读本之后，人们就可以揭示他的思想作为一块薄弱挡板所掩护的真实利益。

A conventional critique of de Soto’s proposals would expose the neoliberal fallacies on which they rely for their plausibility and popularity. It would draw attention to the history of battles over property rights that de Soto’s writings ignore and his inability to account for the moral claims, financial protections, practical flexibility, and affordability offered, whatever their defects, by alternative property arrangements. Having dismissed his writings as no more than the latest vulgate of the neoliberal canon, one could then reveal the real interests for which his ideas are such a flimsy screen.

<a id="ch06-0110"></a>

然而，新自由主义的工作并不在挡板背后进行。如果德·索托论点的谬误似乎出奇地容易揭露，那是因为其效力并不取决于它们对特定财产安排运作的捕捉有多精确。经济学的力量不取决于其再现准确与否。德·索托的著作是新自由主义项目装备的一部分。它们提供了一种手段，把新古典经济学的某些事实与发展机构规划、房地产开发商资源和地方政权政治权力结成联盟。它们构成一种新颖装置的一部分，用以拯救投机者、迫使穷人放弃住房、创造新的财富形式，并扩大未来的贫困化。

The work of neoliberalism, however, does not lie behind a screen. If the fallacies of de Soto’s arguments seem surprisingly easy to expose, that is because their effectiveness does not rest on the precision with which they capture the workings of particular property arrangements. The power of economics does not rest on the accuracy or inaccuracy of its representations. De Soto’s writings form part of the equipment for neoliberal projects. They provide a means of mobilising certain facts of neoclassical economics in alliance with the planning of development agencies, the resources of property developers, and the political powers of local regimes. They form part of the novel apparatus by which speculators are to be rescued, the poor made to give up their houses, new forms of wealth created, and the impoverishment of the future extended.


# 第七章　基础设施作用于时间

<a id="ch07-0001"></a>

<a id="page-239"></a>〔原书第239页〕

<a id="page-239-en"></a>〔原书第239页〕

<a id="ch07-0002"></a>

## 第七章　基础设施作用于时间

## 7 Infrastructures Work on Time

<a id="ch07-0003"></a>

基础设施承诺增强我们对空间的控制。公路、航运运河、铁路、电网和数据网络体现了各种地球改造式的变动；如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)所述，人类主要在过去一个半世纪里通过这些变动改造了地球。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-001"></a>[1](#note-ch7-001)反过来，通过征服空间，基础设施增强了对时间的掌控，加快了能源、数据、货物和人员流动的速度。这种加速也许是我们表达资本主义现代性体验的最常见方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-002"></a>[2](#note-ch7-002)

Infrastructures promise to increase our control over space. Highways, ship canals, railways, power grids, and data networks embody the kinds of terraforming modifications through which, largely over the last century and a half, as we noted in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), humans have transformed the Earth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-001"></a>[1](#note-ch7-001) By conquering space, in turn, infrastructures increase the command of time, speeding up the rate at which energy, data, goods, and people flow. This acceleration is perhaps the most common way in which we express the experience of capitalist modernity.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-002"></a>[2](#note-ch7-002)

<a id="ch07-0004"></a>

然而，基础设施在与资本化的关系中扮演着不同角色。这些塑造地球的大型项目与时间还有另一种关系；没有这种关系，我们今天所知的资本化将会崩溃。基础设施的产生不是为了加速，而是为了引入一种延迟。从这个角度看，基础设施的优点不是加速时间，而是能够把未来推得更远。这一思路改变了我们对资本的理解，也改变了我们对现代人类为何要改造自身与地球之关系的理解。它还使我们能够重新思考气候变化、栖息地破坏和物种灭绝危机的政治。要考察这一点，我们必须从颠倒我们思考基础设施如何作用于时间的方式开始。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-003"></a>[3](#note-ch7-003)

However, infrastructures have a different role in relation to capitalisation. These large, Earth-shaping projects have another relationship to time, without which capitalisation, as we know it today, would collapse. Infrastructures are brought into being not to speed things up but to introduce a delay. The virtue of infrastructure is not the acceleration of time, from this perspective, but the ability to place the future further away. This approach changes our understanding of capital and the purposes for which modern humans modify their relations with the Earth. It also enables us to rethink the politics of climate change, the destruction of habitat, and the crisis of species extinction. To consider this, we need to start from a reversal of the way we think about how infrastructures work on time.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-003"></a>[3](#note-ch7-003)

<a id="ch07-0005"></a>

关于基础设施的常规写法从空间问题出发，把时间视为结果。基础设施创造通道和连接，把分散的点联系起来，便利其间的移动。中国政府 2013 年发起的“一带一路”倡议，为连接亚洲、非洲和欧洲各地的公路、铁路<a id="page-240"></a>〔原书第240页〕、海港和电站建设提供融资，例证了基础设施与征服距离之间的这种联系。作为世界各地正在建设的若干“超大走廊”中最大的一个，其推动者强调大陆之间的相互连接和海洋之间的相互连通。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-004"></a>[4](#note-ch7-004)然而，这种把基础设施视为征服空间方式的关注，掩盖了建设基础设施时往往最重要的东西。

The standard way of writing about infrastructure is to start from the question of space and treat time as a consequence. Infrastructures create channels and connections that link separate points, facilitating movement between them. China’s Belt and Road Initiative, launched by the Chinese government in 2013 to finance the building of roads, rail lines, <a id="page-240-en"></a>〔原书第240页〕seaports, and power stations connecting locations across Asia, Africa, and Europe, exemplifies this association between infrastructure and the command of distance. As the largest of several ‘mega-corridors’ under construction around the world, its promoters emphasised the interlinking of continents and the interconnection of oceans.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-004"></a>[4](#note-ch7-004) Yet this focus on infrastructures as a mode of conquering space obscures what is often most important in building them.

<a id="ch07-0006"></a>

从常识角度看，对时间控制的增强是征服空间的结果。公路和铁路、管道和集装箱港口、输电线路和通信网络，似乎都提供更快连接的好处。作为我们借以理解资本主义历史的“技术进步”的象征，它们承诺提高流动速率。粮食供应、工人、电力、原油、新闻报道、数据存储、监控和武装力量，都依赖专门建造的网络来克服距离。网络的每一次技术改进和空间延伸，都可能缩短输送一定数量线路所载物资所需的时间。

From a common-sense perspective, increased control over time comes as a consequence of the conquest of space. Roads and railways, pipelines and container ports, transmission lines and communication networks all appear to offer the benefit of faster connections. Emblematic of the ‘technical improvement’ through which we understand the history of capitalism, they promise to improve the rate of flow. Food supplies, workers, electrical power, crude petroleum, news reports, data storing, surveillance, and armed force all depend on purpose-built networks to overcome distance. Each technical improvement and spatial extension of the network can reduce the time it takes to convey a given quantity of the material the line carries.

<a id="ch07-0007"></a>

更快连接和更高流动速率的主张，支持了建设大型基础设施的大多数经济论据。世界银行一项关于“一带一路”倡议的研究，估算新基础设施将产生的效益时，只考虑产品从一国运往另一国速度的提高。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-005"></a>[5](#note-ch7-005)该报告呼应了经济学家中间一个古老但重新流行的论点。对基础设施的大规模投资缩短了货物运输时间，产生的改进被衡量为人类福利的增加，并促成了“明天会更好”的承诺。

The claim of faster connections and improved rates of flow supports most economic arguments for the building of large infrastructures. A World Bank study of the Belt and Road Initiative estimated the benefits that the new infrastructure would produce by considering only the increasing speed at which products would move from one country to another.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-005"></a>[5](#note-ch7-005) The report echoed an old but newly popular argument among economists. Large investments in infrastructure reduce the time it takes to move goods, producing an improvement that is measured as an increase in human welfare, and contributing to the promise of a better tomorrow.

<a id="ch07-0008"></a>

从这个角度看，可以证明殖民主义改善了被殖民者的生活。例如，英国企业家在殖民地印度修建的铁路缩短了运输农产品的时间和成本——使地主得以提高主要市场作物的价格并增加地租。在最近一项关于这一过程的研究中，价格上涨被假定为福利增加的衡量指标。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-006"></a>[6](#note-ch7-006)这项研究以及另一篇证明十九世纪美国铁路建设带来益处的论文，为作者赢得了美国经济学会的约翰·贝茨·克拉克奖——授予被认为四十岁以下最优秀的经济学家。这类研究有助于基础设施发展所依赖的经济化工作，其<a id="page-241"></a>〔原书第241页〕引人注目之处，既在于衡量铁路对价格影响的高超技巧，也在于对其他被广泛研究、却难以通过价格衡量的建设后果的漠视，包括饥荒、流行病、贫困化、生态破坏和种族灭绝。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-007"></a>[7](#note-ch7-007)时间的经济化被呈现为此类大型基础设施项目所带来益处的关键要素。时间与空间相连，因此对前者的经济化或压缩自然与后者相关。

From this perspective, colonialism can be shown to have improved the life of the colonised. The railways that British entrepreneurs built across colonial India, for example, reduced the time and thus the cost of shipping agricultural products – allowing landowners to raise the price of the main market crops and increase land rents. In a recent study of this process, the rising prices were assumed to measure an increase in welfare.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-006"></a>[6](#note-ch7-006) This research, and a companion paper demonstrating the benefits that the building of railroads brought to the United States in the nineteenth century, won their author the John Bates Clark Medal of the American Economic Association, awarded to the person considered to be the best economist under forty. Contributing to the work of economisation on which the development of infrastructure depends, such <a id="page-241-en"></a>〔原书第241页〕research is as remarkable for the skill with which it measures the impact of railways on prices, as it is for its obliviousness towards other widely studied effects of their construction not easily measurable via prices, including famine, epidemic disease, impoverishment, ecological destruction, and genocide.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-007"></a>[7](#note-ch7-007) The economisation of time is presented as the key element in the benefits brought by such large infrastructure projects. Time and space are linked, so the economisation or compression of the first is naturally associated with the second.

<a id="ch07-0009"></a>

对更快连接的关注，使大型基础设施的其他后果可以被当作副作用。正是这种关注，使经济学家的模型能够以价格衡量福利，并在殖民地铁路案例中忽视不平等和饥荒问题，忽视霍乱弧菌和其他病原体的传播，或例如其建设造成的大规模森林砍伐。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-008"></a>[8](#note-ch7-008)为减少脱轨和延误，木制铁路枕木（横枕）平均每七年就必须更换。到 1860 年，全球每年估计生产 1.77 亿根枕木，需要砍伐 88.5 万英亩森林。到 1880 年，每年砍伐面积增至三倍，到 1900 年又增至三倍。森林还因薪柴和沿铁路新路线扩大耕作而被毁。在印度，1860 年代和 1870 年代每年砍伐 7 万英亩森林，到 1890 年代翻倍，导致洪水和侵蚀加剧。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-009"></a>[9](#note-ch7-009)正如我们在[第二章](#ch02-0001)所见埃及灌溉工程的影响一样，这些后果并非只是副作用。基础设施开辟的新空间和走廊，为多种行动者——人类和非人类——提供了更好的连接。它们为人的军队和其他生物的军队创造路线。苏伊士运河的开挖使数百种入侵性海洋生物开始殖民地中海；正如我们所见，运河和水坝让水葫芦堵塞下埃及的水道，印度各河流域也是如此，而携带血吸虫病和钩虫病的螺类与线虫则肆虐乡村。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-010"></a>[10](#note-ch7-010)更便利的连接和更快的旅行时间，适用于所有利用新路线者，而不只是那些移动被运费率、市场价格和基础设施建设产生的其他数字所追踪的人。

The focus on faster connections allows other consequences of large infrastructures to be treated as side effects. It is this focus that enables the economists’ models to measure welfare in terms of prices, and in the case of colonial railways to ignore questions of inequality and famine, or the spread of the cholera vibrio and other pathogens, or, for example, the extensive deforestation that their construction caused.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-008"></a>[8](#note-ch7-008) To reduce derailments and delays, wooden railway sleepers (crossties) had to be replaced on average every seven years. By 1860, an estimated 177 million ties were produced each year globally, which required the clearing of 885,000 acres of forest. The area cleared each year had tripled by 1880 and tripled again by 1900. Forests were also destroyed for fuel wood and to expand farming along the new routes served by rail. In India, 70,000 acres of forests were removed each year in the 1860s and 1870s, and double that rate by 1890s, leading to increased flooding and erosion.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-009"></a>[9](#note-ch7-009) As with the impact of irrigation works in Egypt, as we saw in [chapter 2](#ch02-0001), such consequences were not just side effects. The new spaces and corridors that infrastructures open allow improved connections for multiple agents, human and nonhuman. They create routes for armies of men and armies of other creatures. The digging of the Suez Canal enabled hundreds of invasive species of marine life to begin to colonise the Mediterranean, just as canals and dams, as we saw, allowed water hyacinth to clog the waterways of Lower Egypt, as it did in the river basins of India, and the snails and nematodes carrying bilharzia and hookworm disease to infest the countryside.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-010"></a>[10](#note-ch7-010) Easier connections and faster travel times apply to all those who take advantage of a new route, not just to those whose movements are tracked by freight rates, market prices, and other numbers generated by the building of infrastructures.

<a id="ch07-0010"></a>

撇开经济学家关于流动速率改善之益处的傲慢论述所遗漏的东西不谈，还有另一种方式理解基础设施如何作用于时间。基础设施可以产生一种延迟；这种延迟不仅以我们通常想象的方式发生，也构成资本化工作的一部分。

Leaving aside what is missing from economists’ hubristic accounts of the benefits of improved rates of flow, there is a different way to understand how infrastructures work on time. Infrastructures can produce a delay; and they do this not only in the way we commonly imagine, but as part of the work of capitalisation.

<a id="ch07-0011"></a>

<a id="page-242"></a>〔原书第242页〕任何连接上的改善都带来延迟增加的可能。这可能是一种非计划性后果，其例子广为人知。开通或改善一条路线会创造自身需求。原本可能使用其他方式的交通转向新路线，而原先仅在本地范围内进行的流动，则开始利用更广泛的连接。使用改善路线的车辆可能变得更大、更难操控。由于所有这些原因，新基础设施本应减少的延迟可能反而加剧。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-011"></a>[11](#note-ch7-011)有时，改善所造成的延迟非常戏剧性，这种现象或可称为“长赐号效应”。2015 年，埃及政府完成了苏伊士运河的部分拓宽工程，为其中一段增设平行航道，并拓宽、加深其他河段。船舶最大载重量从 21 万载重吨增至 24 万载重吨（1869 年运河开通时，最大载重量为 5,000 吨）。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-012"></a>[12](#note-ch7-012)该十年初最多运载 1 万个集装箱的集装箱船，如今建造得可运载 2 万多个。更大的船更难操控，尤其是在狭窄航道中，船体排开的水可能把船尾吸向河岸。2021 年 3 月，这种“岸壁效应”可能促成了巨型集装箱船“长赐号”搁浅，堵塞运河六天，使价值数十亿美元的全球商品运输受阻。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-013"></a>[13](#note-ch7-013)

<a id="page-242-en"></a>〔原书第242页〕Any improvement in connections brings the possibility of increased delay. This can be an unplanned consequence, examples of which are well known. Opening or improving a route creates its own demand. Traffic that might have moved using other modes switches to the new route, while movements that enjoyed a local circulation take advantage of wider connections. The vehicles using the improved route may become larger and less manoeuvrable. For all these reasons, the delays that the new infrastructure had promised to reduce can be exacer-bated.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-011"></a>[11](#note-ch7-011) On occasion, the delay created by improvement is dramatic, a phenomenon that might be termed the Ever Given effect. In 2015, the Egyptian government completed a partial enlarging of the Suez Canal, doubling one section of the waterway and widening and deepening other stretches. The maximum tonnage a vessel could carry grew from 210,000 to 240,000 deadweight tons (when the Canal opened in 1869, the maximum was 5,000 tons).<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-012"></a>[12](#note-ch7-012) Container ships, which at the start of that decade carried up to 10,000 containers, were now built to carry more than 20,000. Larger ships are less manoeuvrable, especially in narrow channels, where the water displaced by the hull can suck the stern of the vessel towards the bank. In March 2021, this ‘bank effect’ may have contributed to the grounding of the giant container ship Ever Given, which blocked the canal for six days and stranded the global shipment of commodities worth billions of dollars.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-013"></a>[13](#note-ch7-013)

校注：底本把2015年扩建与最大载重由21万吨提高至24万吨相接叙述。苏伊士运河管理局历史表列2001年为21万吨，2010年已为24万吨，2015年仍为24万吨。因此该吨位提升不宜全归于2015年工程；正文数字和叙述保留。 https://www.suezcanal.gov.eg/English/About/SuezCanal/Pages/CanalCharacteristics.aspx

<a id="ch07-0012"></a>

超大型基础设施计划通常还关联另一种非计划性后果：建设完工的延迟。在建设最大型项目——水坝、桥梁、运河、隧道、铁路、深海油田——时，工期大幅超期是常态，通常被归咎于技术复杂性、范围变更、异常地质构造或极端气候条件。负责者通常把这些因素说成意外，但它们如此频繁发生，反映的不是知识或经验的缺乏，而是推动者和规划者的自利乐观。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-014"></a>[14](#note-ch7-014)推动基础设施建设的人还必须构建一幅足够简单的世界图景，使基础设施能按计划获得批准。未知和意外不是有待克服的边疆，而是作为资本化要求而生产出来的另一种无知。

Very large infrastructure schemes are commonly associated with another form of unplanned consequence: the delay in completing their construction. In building the largest projects – dams, bridges, canals, tunnels, rail lines, deep-offshore oil fields – long overruns are the norm, typically blamed on technical complexity, changes in scope, unusual geological formations, or extreme climate conditions. Those responsible usually describe these elements as unexpected, but they occur so routinely that they reflect not an absence of knowledge or experience but the self-interested optimism of the promoters and planners.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-014"></a>[14](#note-ch7-014) Those who promote the building of infrastructures must also build a picture of a world that is simple enough for the infrastructure to be approved as planned. The unknown and the unexpected are not a frontier to be overcome, but another ignorance produced as a requirement of capitalisation.

<a id="ch07-0013"></a>

<a id="page-243"></a>〔原书第243页〕

<a id="page-243-en"></a>〔原书第243页〕

<a id="ch07-0014"></a>

### 目的与价格

### Purpose and Price

<a id="ch07-0015"></a>

然而，与这些非预期结果相反，另一种延迟往往是基础设施项目的真正目的。虽然建设基础设施可以以运送人员或物资的需要为理由，但其主要用途往往是为另一种流动提供载体：资金的流动。十九世纪美国伟大的横贯大陆铁路的推动者宣传这些线路对运输粮食、牛群和人员的重要性，但其价值往往在于作为建设金融网络的手段。用理查德·赖特的话说，铁路的一个主要目的是运送纸张。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-015"></a>[15](#note-ch7-015)

In contrast to such unintended outcomes, however, a different kind of delay is often the very purpose of an infrastructure project. While the building of infrastructure may be justified by a need to move people or supplies, their principal use is often to provide vehicles for another form of movement: the flow of finance. The promoters of the great transcontinental railways of nineteenth-century America advertised the importance of the lines for shipping grain, cattle, and people, but their value was often as a means to construct financial networks. A main purpose of the railways, as Richard Wright puts it, was to move paper.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-015"></a>[15](#note-ch7-015)

校注：底本此处及原注015作Richard Wright；《Railroaded》作者实为Richard White，与本章原注006一致。英文底本照录。 https://web.stanford.edu/group/spatialhistory/railroaded/about-author.html

<a id="ch07-0016"></a>

如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)所述，大型基础设施项目以公司债券、银行贷款和股票凭证的形式运送投资票据。它们建成不是为了在空间上运输这些金融工具，而是为了提供创造它们并让它们穿越时间的手段。在这种情形中，制造延迟不是建设基础设施的非预期结果，而是其目标。

Large infrastructure projects move investment paper, as we noted in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), in the form of corporate bonds, bank loans, and share certificates. They are built not to transport these financial instruments across space, but to provide the means to create them and carry them through time. In this case, creating the delay is not an unintended outcome of the building of infrastructure, but its goal.

<a id="ch07-0017"></a>

我们再次可以区分这种情况发生的两种方式。第一，建设基础设施可以成为实施工业破坏的手段：先垄断一条路线，然后拖延其开发或减缓物资流动。例如，二十世纪大部分时间里，中东石油基础设施就是按这一原则建设和运营的。取得该地区石油储量的垄断权的大型石油公司力图最大化的不是石油流量，而是利润流量。更高的利润来自确保石油永远不会太容易获得。为了维持限制供应所能产生的异常高额金融收益，石油公司拖延钻井或完井，阻挠管道建设或扩建，并挑起争端，以便关闭泵站和炼油厂。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-016"></a>[16](#note-ch7-016)托斯丹·凡勃伦在二十世纪初论证，这些以及其他蓄意破坏方法——利用大公司扰乱或干扰产业间复杂相互依赖关系的能力——已经成为现代“工业体系”下赚取商业利润的主要手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-017"></a>[17](#note-ch7-017)“蓄意破坏”（sabotage）一词最初大约在同一时期被用来描述工人的力量，特别是操作一国铁路的工人，能够制造轻微技术干扰，从而引发整条铁路线或网络减速或瘫痪。工人能够运用这种伴随现代基础设施和能源系统而来的新力量，<a id="page-244"></a>〔原书第244页〕争取更好的工作条件和更高的工资。然而，蓄意破坏最有利可图的运用掌握在大型商号手中，在许多产业中，威胁或实施破坏成为常规的致富手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-018"></a>[18](#note-ch7-018)作为资本的托词运作的“技术改进”修辞，使我们无法理解蓄意破坏。

Once again, we can distinguish two ways in which this happens. First, the building of infrastructure can be the means to carry out industrial sabotage, by first monopolising a route and then delaying its development or slowing the movement of supplies. For much of the twentieth century, for example, the oil infrastructure of the Middle East was built and run according to this principle. The major oil firms that acquired monopoly rights to the region’s petroleum reserves sought to maximise not the flow of oil but the flow of profits. Higher profits came from ensuring that oil was never too readily available. In order to maintain the extraordinary levels of financial gain that could be generated by restricting the supply, oil firms delayed the drilling or completion of wells, blocked the construction or expansion of pipelines, and triggered disputes that allowed the shutting down of pumping stations and refineries.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-016"></a>[16](#note-ch7-016) Thorstein Veblen argued early in the twentieth century that these and other methods of sabotage, taking advantage of the ability of large firms to disrupt or disturb the complex interdependencies among industries, had become a principal means of making business profit under the modern ‘industrial system’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-017"></a>[17](#note-ch7-017) The term sabotage had first been used, around the same time, to describe the power of workers, in particular those who ran a country’s railways, to introduce a minor technical disruption that might trigger the slowing or breakdown of an entire rail line or network. Workers were able to use this new power that <a id="page-244-en"></a>〔原书第244页〕came with modern infrastructures and energy systems to campaign for better conditions of work and increased wages. The most profitable use of sabotage, however, was in the hands of large business firms, whose threat or use of sabotage became in many industries a routine method of enrichment.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-018"></a>[18](#note-ch7-018) The trope of ‘technical improvement’ that operates as an alibi of capital distracts us from understanding sabotage.

<a id="ch07-0018"></a>

第二，除了破坏和干扰行为所能带来的利润之外，基础设施所产生的金融商品与基础设施运载的其他物资有着不同的时间关系。投资价值的来源不是使事物更接近的速度，而是把事物推向未来的延迟。这一特质源于基础设施不仅作为运输装置、还作为支付机制运作。它是一种攫取未来付款的装置，付款形式包括运费、客运票价、港口费、桥梁和公路通行费、水费、燃料费、电费、房产租金、互联网订阅费、流媒体付费等等。基础设施制造了一种未来流量，不仅是货物或服务的流量，也是收入的流量。对未来收入的主张是一种金融资产，可以在当下提供出来。

Second, beyond the profits to be made from practices of sabotage and disruption, the financial goods that infrastructures bring into being enjoy a different relation to time from that of the other materials that infrastructures carry. The investment acquires its value not from the speed that brings things closer together, but from the delay that pushes things into the future. This quality arises from the fact that an infrastructure operates not only as a transportation device, but as a payment mechanism. It is an apparatus for the capture of future payments, in the form of freight charges, passenger fares, port fees, bridge and highway tolls, water rates, fuel costs, electricity bills, property rents, internet subscriptions, streaming payments, and more. The infrastructure manufactures a future flow, not simply of goods or services, but of revenues. The claim to those future revenues is a financial asset that can be made available in the present.

<a id="ch07-0019"></a>

有几种方法可以把未来主张货币化，但从历史上看，最常见的方法是把基础设施项目组织为股份制公司。出售给投资者的公司股份，代表对流动所产生的未来费用或收入的主张。货物和服务往往可以通过更快交付而增值，但对未来收入流量的主张——我们将会看到——是通过延迟而获得价值的。

There are several ways to monetise the future claim, but, historically, the most common method has been to organise the infrastructure project as a joint-stock company. The shares in the company, sold to investors, represent claims on the future fees or revenues arising from the flows. While goods and services may often increase in value through faster delivery, the claim upon a future flow of revenue, as we will see, acquires its value through delay.

<a id="ch07-0020"></a>

任何金融工具都可以因时间流逝而增值。事实上，仅仅通过延长时间就能增值的奇特能力，正是界定某种安排为金融资产的部分原因。这一特质使我们所谓的金融或资本对基础设施产生特殊依赖。基础设施项目是一种把时间流逝向前拉伸的装置。并非所有金融都由基础设施项目创造，但金融总是需要一种基础设施过程来建构被推迟的付款。基础设施是创造延迟的典范装置。

Any financial instrument can increase in value thanks to the passage of time. In fact, the strange ability to grow in value through the mere extension of time is part of what defines an arrangement as a financial asset. This quality gives what we call finance or capital a particular dependence on infrastructure. The infrastructure project is a device for stretching forwards the passing of time. Not all finance is created through infrastructure projects, but finance always requires an infrastructural process for the construction of postponed payments. Infrastructure is the paradigmatic apparatus for the creation of a delay.

<a id="ch07-0021"></a>

要考察基础设施究竟如何被建造来创造延迟，我们必须首先重新排列我们思考大型技术项目以及一般资本的标准术语。基础设施塑造了我们对空间和时间、对物质性和<a id="page-245"></a>〔原书第245页〕货币、对人类建构世界的理解，阻碍我们以不同方式思考。

To consider how exactly an infrastructure is built to create delays, we must first reorder the standard terms in which we think about large technical projects, and about capital in general. Infrastructure has shaped our conceptions of space and time, of materiality and <a id="page-245-en"></a>〔原书第245页〕money, and of human world-making, impeding us from thinking differently.

<a id="ch07-0022"></a>

如果我们倾向于从速度而非推迟、从流量加快而非延迟的角度思考基础设施，也许原因是，修建铁路、港口、公路系统、管道或公用事业网络，邀请我们把公开宣称的目的与成本分离。此类项目的提案和计划通常先呈现物质目的，再呈现货币安排。这种区分有助于支撑基础设施规划所特有的乐观，甚至傲慢。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-019"></a>[19](#note-ch7-019)一部分似乎物质、可触、可见，另一部分似乎金融、无形、难以想象。一个是目的，另一个只是手段。

If we tend to think of infrastructure in terms of speed rather than postponement, in terms of the quickening of flows rather than their delay, perhaps the reason is that the building of a rail line, port, road system, pipeline, or utility network invites us to separate the avowed purpose from the cost. The proposals and plans for such projects typically present the material purpose first, and the monetary arrangement second. This distinction helps underwrite the optimism, even the hubris, that is a characteristic of infrastructure planning.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-019"></a>[19](#note-ch7-019) One part seems material, tangible, and visible, the other financial, intangible, and difficult to visualise. One is the end, the other merely the means.

<a id="ch07-0023"></a>

物质与金融、实体与货币、可见与无形之间的区分，部分是基础设施的效果。在实践中，基础设施项目的每个方面都是两者的混合。航运线路运送的货物或公用事业网络输送的能源，由物质、力、管理、价值和管理规定的各种组合构成，包括质量控制、价格机制和劳动力成本；同样，项目所产生的投资产品也依赖于生产此类“纸张”的材料和机制。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-020"></a>[20](#note-ch7-020)无论是印成股票凭证还是在计算机网络中生成，金融工具都涉及传输、登记、拍卖，尤其是未来付款强制执行的方法。而且，没有未来将为之付款的货物或服务，它们就无法存在。然而，尽管货物和金融都是物质与价值、有形与无形的混合体，基础设施建设似乎把它们分开，变出一个似乎划分为物质商品与货币、目的与手段、目的与价格、实体与金融、基础设施与其成本的世界。

The distinction between material and financial, real and monetary, visible and intangible, is partly an effect of infrastructure. In practice, each aspect of an infrastructure project is a mixture of both. The goods carried by a shipping line or the energy moved by a utility network are made up of various combinations of matter, force, management, value, and regulation, including quality controls, price mechanisms, and labour costs; likewise, the investment products that a project brings into being depend on the materials and mechanisms that produce such ‘paper’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-020"></a>[20](#note-ch7-020) Whether printed as stock certificates or generated in computer networks, financial instruments involve methods of transmission, registration, auction, and, above all, enforcement of future payment. And they cannot exist without the future good or service for which that payment will be made. But, although both the goods and the finance are hybrids of matter and value, of the tangible and the intangible, the building of infrastructures appears to separate them, conjuring a world that seems divided into material goods versus money, ends versus means, purpose versus price, the real versus the financial, the infrastructure versus its cost.

<a id="ch07-0024"></a>

在造成这个看似分裂的世界时，基础设施项目还赋予它一种等级秩序。新项目的推动者通常以物质需要而非金融机会向公众证明其合理性。将因新基础设施而更快流动的人员和物资，被呈现为必须满足的要求、生活的必需品、福祉的条件、一种改善，或如经济学家所称的福利增加或“增长”。金融——尽管暗中是唯一为增长而存在、其可能性本身就在于自身扩张的要素——则显得是次要的东西。资本借由这一托词，假装事后才到来，来使<a id="page-246"></a>〔原书第246页〕需要得到满足。基础设施项目通过促成一种划分为实体与金融的世界效果，强化了实体或物质、生理需要和人类欲望的表面首要性，并把金融置于仆从、从属要素的位置，其存在只是为了帮助满足这些需要。它们产生一种形而上学效果——实体与金融的对立——这种效果在金融学和经济学理论中、在更广泛的社会科学中被复制。

In effecting this seemingly divided world, infrastructural projects also give it a hierarchy. The promoters of new projects usually justify them to the public by material needs, not financial opportunities. The movements and supplies that will flow faster thanks to new infrastructure are presented as a requirement to be met, a necessity for life, a condition of well-being, an improvement, or, as economists call it, an increase in welfare, or ‘growth’. The finance – although secretly the only element that actually exists in order to grow, the one factor whose very possibility lies in its own expansion – appears as something secondary. Claiming this alibi, capital pretends to arrive after the fact, to enable <a id="page-246-en"></a>〔原书第246页〕needs to be met. In contributing to the effect of a world divided into the real and the financial, infrastructure projects reinforce the apparent primacy of the real or the material, of physical needs and human wants, and place finance as the servant, the subservient element existing only to help meet such needs. They generate a metaphysical effect, the real versus the financial, that is reproduced in theories of finance and economics, and in social science more generally.

<a id="ch07-0025"></a>

### 资本的延迟

### Delay of Capital

<a id="ch07-0026"></a>

让我们颠倒这一优先顺序，至少暂时把金融问题放在首位——尽管我们稍后会重新表述这个问题。为什么资本似乎想要延迟？答案是，推迟使资本得以产生，并使其能够增殖。事实上，延迟——把某物推向未来却仍能控制它的技术能力——可以理解为资本的本质，以及资本那种被称为货币的流动形式的本质。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-021"></a>[21](#note-ch7-021)

Let us reverse this order of priority and, at least provisionally, put the question of finance first – although we will later rephrase the question. Why does capital appear to want delay? The answer is that postponement brings capital into being and allows it to multiply. In fact, the delay – the technical ability to push something into the future yet continue to control it – can be understood as the very nature of capital, and of the liquid form of capital known as money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-021"></a>[21](#note-ch7-021)

<a id="ch07-0027"></a>

按照惯例，如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所述，正统经济学家通常把货币仅仅描述为便利交换、储存价值或记录账户的手段。然而，我们现在知道，或者说重新发现了这样一种知识：虽然货币可以发挥这些用途，但它大部分是以信用形式产生的。信用是一种会计机制——也就是说，既是一种会计，也是一种机制或技术装置。通过这一机制的运作，被许诺的未来收入在当下变得可用。如果债权人可以用这种付款承诺清偿其他债务，那么信用账户就作为货币运作。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-022"></a>[22](#note-ch7-022)

By convention, as we noted in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), orthodox economists usually describe money as just a means to facilitate exchange, store value, or record accounts. However, we now know, or rather have rediscovered the knowledge, that while money can serve these purposes, for the most part it comes into being as credit. Credit is an accounting mechanism – that is, both an accounting, and a mechanism or technical apparatus. Through the working of the mechanism, promised future revenues are made accessible in the present. If the creditor can use that promise-to-pay to settle other debts, then the credit account operates as money.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-022"></a>[22](#note-ch7-022)

<a id="ch07-0028"></a>

虽然把货币理解为一种作为信用机制被创造的东西，而不只是储存价值或便利交换的手段，最近开始受到新的关注，但关于这个主题的许多写作都狭隘地集中于银行和其他金融机构研究。例如，虽然已有关于支持货币创造和运作的法律装置的重要研究，但很少有人探讨这里所呈现的信贷和资本创造的更广泛技术政治装置。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-023"></a>[23](#note-ch7-023)对货币的研究仍然着重于信任、社会关系和法律规制，而不把它作为一种技术政治关系来处理。甚至那些提出不应通过价值理论、而应把资本理解为一种权力关系的开创性文本，也往往依赖相当笼统的支配概念。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-024"></a>[24](#note-ch7-024)<a id="page-247"></a>〔原书第247页〕它们通常不从物质和技术层面考察特定的信用生产装置是如何建构的。

Although the understanding of money as something created as a credit mechanism, rather than simply a means of storing value or facilitating exchange, has recently begun to receive new attention, much of the writing on the topic is focused narrowly on the study of banking and other financial institutions. While there have been important studies of, for example, the legal apparatus that supports the creation and operation of money, there is little exploration of the wider technopolitical apparatuses of credit and capital creation presented here.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-023"></a>[23](#note-ch7-023) Money is still approached with an emphasis on trust, social relations, and legal regulation – not as a technopolitical relation. Even the seminal texts proposing that capital is to be understood not through value theory but as a power relation often rely on rather general notions of domination.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-024"></a>[24](#note-ch7-024) <a id="page-247-en"></a>〔原书第247页〕They do not usually consider in material and technical terms how a specific apparatus of credit production is constructed.

<a id="ch07-0029"></a>

如果一种会计机制不仅指在纸上或电子方式进行的实践，而且指一种技术政治的物质装置，那么，许诺和攫取未来收入的装置在技术上和政治上越可靠，这一机制能向未来延伸得越远，创造信用货币的机会就越大。

If an accounting mechanism does not refer merely to practices carried out on paper, or electronically, but to a technopolitical, material apparatus, then the more reliable the apparatus for promising and capturing future revenue, both technically and politically, and the further the mechanism can be extended into the future, the greater the opportunity for the creation of credit money.

<a id="ch07-0030"></a>

这就是理解基础设施与金融关系的方式：基础设施不只是恰好需要借入大量资金的物质投资。它们是创造大量信用货币的安排——这些安排像所有货币一样，通过一套延展的物质装置而产生。

This is how to understand the relationship between infrastructure and finance: infrastructures are not simply material investments that happen to require the borrowing of large amounts of money. They are the arrangements through which large amounts of credit money are created – arrangements that, like all money, come into being through an extended material apparatus.

<a id="ch07-0031"></a>

从这个角度看，货币本身可以被视为一种基础设施。然而，我们必须谨慎对待这一类比。亚当·斯密在*《国富论》*中把金属货币比作允许商品流通的道路或铁路。他写道，货币就像“一条公路，它流通并把乡间所有牧草和谷物运往市场，但自身不生产一堆草或谷物”。他用这个隐喻解释银行发行纸币的作用：“银行审慎的操作，如果我可以允许自己使用这样一个大胆的隐喻，提供了一条穿越空中的马车轨道，使国家得以将其大部分公路变成良好的牧场和粮田。”<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-025"></a>[25](#note-ch7-025)马车轨道是木制铁路，承载马拉货车，是斯密时代在苏格兰大规模修建的新基础设施，主要用于把煤从煤矿运到港口。斯密借用当代基础设施方案的这一隐喻，来应对 1760 年代和 1770 年代银行信用激增的问题，特别是 1772 年的一场银行危机：艾尔银行倒闭引发遍及苏格兰的“商业地震”，并使斯密自己的赞助人、英国最大的地主之一巴克卢公爵面临破产威胁。这场灾难使斯密推迟五年出版*《国富论》*，因为他重新思考银行创造信用的问题以及政府监管的必要性。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-026"></a>[26](#note-ch7-026)把信用货币描绘为“一条穿越空中的马车轨道”，从此一直是一个不充分的意象。金融不是由空气构成的，也不是实体货物的某种空灵对应物。它也不只是便利那些实体材料流通的手段。它自身就是一种物质基础设施，其存在<a id="page-248"></a>〔原书第248页〕不仅是为了便利实体运动，而且本身就是要由基础设施增殖来便利的运动。

From this perspective, money can itself be approached as an infrastructure. However, we must be careful with this analogy. In *The Wealth of Nations*, Adam Smith compared metallic money to a road or railway, allowing the circulation of goods. Money, he wrote, is like ‘a highway, which, while it circulates and carries to market all the grass and corn of the country, produces itself not a single pile of either’. He used this metaphor to explain the role of banks in issuing paper money: ‘The judicious operations of banking, by providing, if I may be allowed so violent a metaphor, a sort of waggon-way through the air, enable the country to convert, as it were, a great part of its highways into good pastures and corn-fields.’<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-025"></a>[25](#note-ch7-025) Waggon-ways were wooden railways carrying horse-drawn wagons, a new infrastructure built extensively in Scotland in Smith’s time, mainly to carry coal from collieries to harbours. Smith employed this metaphor from contemporary infrastructure schemes to grapple with the problem of the proliferation of bank credit in the 1760s and 1770s, and, in particular, a banking crisis in 1772 when the collapse of Ayr Bank caused a ‘commercial earthquake’ across Scotland and threatened Smith’s own benefactor, the Duke of Buccleuch, one of the largest landowners in Britain, with bankruptcy. The calamity caused Smith to delay the publication of *The Wealth of Nations* by five years as he rethought the problem of bank-created credit and the need for its regulation by government.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-026"></a>[26](#note-ch7-026) Portraying credit money as ‘a sort of waggon-way through the air’ has remained an inadequate image ever since. Finance is not built out of air, as some ethereal counterpart to real goods. And it is not merely a means to facilitate the circulation of those real materials. It is itself a material infrastructure, and one that exists <a id="page-248-en"></a>〔原书第248页〕not merely to facilitate real movement, but as the movement to be facilitated by the proliferation of infrastructures.

校注：底本称1772年危机使《国富论》推迟五年出版，但未交代这五年的起算点。《国富论》初版为1776年；原注所引Rae传记收录的1772年9月5日斯密致Pulteney信中，只说疾病及帮助陷于危机的友人迫使出版再延后数月。因此不宜直接把底本“五年”理解为从1772年危机发生之日起计算；正文保留，精确延误年数仍有疑点。 https://www.econlib.org/book-chapters/chapter-chapter-16/ https://era.ed.ac.uk/items/97be930c-78b6-40af-bdcf-d63fea980bbb

<a id="ch07-0032"></a>

如果建构一种攫取未来收入的装置创造了货币的可能，它也赋予货币一种奇特能力：显得能够“增长”。换言之，延迟的基础设施不仅产生货币的可能——即对某项未来资产的主张——而且产生资本的可能：一种看起来是货币自我扩张力量的东西。这种表象通过利用界定未来生产的两个特征的过程而产生：未来可以被推迟，其进程并不确定。

If the construction of an apparatus to capture revenue that lies in the future creates the possibility of money, it also gives money its peculiar ability of appearing to ‘grow’. In other words, the infrastructure of delay gives rise to the possibility not just of money, in the sense of a claim on a future asset, but of capital: of what appears as the self-expanding power of money. This appearance comes about through processes that take advantage of two features that define the making of the future: it is subject to delay, and its course is not certain.

<a id="ch07-0033"></a>

那些设计并取得一系列未来付款主张之控制权的人——例如一项持久基础设施项目所许诺的付款，或者简单如未来销售的承诺收入——可能决定在当下出售这些主张或承诺的一部分，也许是为了清偿早先的债务或支持建造新的付款机器，或者只是为了兑现这种控制可能带来的意外收益。重复[第三章](#ch03-0001)中一个简单的例子：信用票据的持有者可以把这份付款承诺卖给第三方；这张票据代表另一个人的承诺，即在未来某一固定日期支付一定金额，以换取某种货物的交付。由于付款被推迟到未来，加上任何治理未来事件的安排都带有不确定性因素，这类未来收入主张通常可以以较低价格购得。这使未来收入可以按折扣获得。

Those who engineer and acquire control of a set of claims on future payments, such as those promised by a durable infrastructural project, but also something as simple as the promised income from a future sale, may decide to sell a part of those claims or promises in the present, perhaps to settle earlier debts or to support the building of new payment machines; or simply to realise the windfall to which such control may give rise. To repeat a straightforward instance from [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), the owner of a credit note – a promise from someone else to pay a certain sum on a fixed day in the future, in exchange for the delivery of a certain good – might sell that promise-of-payment to a third party. Due to the postponement of the payment into the future, and the element of uncertainty that attaches to any arrangement for governing prospective events, such claims to future revenue can usually be purchased at a reduced price. This makes the future income available at a discount.

<a id="ch07-0034"></a>

让我们简要重述这一过程如何运作。一年后可得的一笔 100 美元付款主张，现在也许可以按折扣价购买，比如 10% 的折扣，即 90 美元。如果许诺付款的日期可以被推得更远，折扣可以在收入被推迟的每一年复合，成倍放大其效果。因此，七年后的一笔 100 美元收入主张，按同样的年折扣率，现在也许能以约 50 美元购得。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-027"></a>[27](#note-ch7-027)只要延迟装置在政治上和技术上可靠，剩余不确定性可以得到管理，这种安排就允许投资者以 50 美元的价格购买 100 美元收入的主张。换言之，在 10% 的折扣率下，50 美元可以在七年内显得规模翻倍，而投资者乃至资金本身都无需付出任何努力。（资金并不代表建造延迟装置的成本，即使部分收入可能用于支付这些成本；它们代表的是其未来<a id="page-249"></a>〔原书第249页〕收入的折价购买价格。）这样，延迟机制就允许创造信用货币，并赋予它那种奇特的增长能力。

Let us recount out briefly how this process works. The claim to a payment of $100 that will be available one year from now might be purchased in the present at a discount, say of 10 per cent, or for the price of $90. If the date of the promised payment can be pushed further into the future, the discount can be compounded each year that the revenue is postponed, multiplying its effect. Thus the claim to a revenue of $100 in seven years’ time might be purchased in the present, at the same annual discount rate, for about $50.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-027"></a>[27](#note-ch7-027) Provided the apparatus of postponement is politically and technically reliable and the residual uncertainty can be managed, this arrangement allows an investor to purchase the claim to an income of $100 at the price of $50. In other words, at a discount rate of 10 per cent, the sum of $50 can appear to double in size in seven years, through no effort on the part of the investor, or even of the funds themselves. (The funds do not represent the cost of building the apparatus of postponement, even if some of the income may be used to defray those costs; rather, they represent the discounted purchase price of its future <a id="page-249-en"></a>〔原书第249页〕revenues.) In this way, the mechanism of delay allows the creation of credit money and endows it with its curious capacity to grow.

<a id="ch07-0035"></a>

大多数投资者以及他们所属的公众，把这种七年间从 50 美元到 100 美元的转变视为货币“赚取利息”的力量。可以说，他们是从望远镜的另一端看问题，从当下凝视未来。从未来某个人的角度回望，一项资产规模缩小了，因为 100 美元收入的价值被减至 50 美元。但如果反过来看，从当下那一刻向前看，50 美元数额已经扩大了一倍。利息概念使这种增加显得是货币的自然属性。这种表象把注意力从必须完成的基础设施工作——以及必须组织的权力——上转移开，这些工作和权力用于建造和治理一套可靠的延迟、收入攫取和信用创造装置。

Most investors, and the wider public to which they belong, come to think of this transformation of $50 into $100 over a period of seven years as the power of money to ‘earn interest’. They see it, as it were, through the other end of the telescope, staring at the future from the present. From the perspective of a person in the future, looking back, an asset was shrunken in size, because an income of $100 was reduced in value to $50. But, seen in reverse, from that present moment looking forwards, the sum of $50 has enlarged to become double the size. The concept of interest makes the increase appear as a natural property of money. This appearance diverts attention from the infrastructural work that must be done – and the powers that must be organised – to build and govern a reliable apparatus of postponement, revenue capture, and credit creation.

<a id="ch07-0036"></a>

从历史上看，如我们所见，计算未来收入价值与其当下价格之间差额的做法被称为“贴现”，这个术语在金融界仍然常用。今天看起来像投资的“增长”，更有用的理解方式——正如贴现一词所暗示的——是未来的“缩减”。付款可以按其最终价值的一小部分从未来榨取。但这取决于建造使未来可用的机制。一定量货币看似能使自身规模翻倍的能力，并不依赖货币的任何物理膨胀力量。它是一套技术政治装置的后果，这套装置制造阻塞、中断和缩减。我们所谓的资本，或具有增长力量的货币，就是这种建造和治理付款之可靠推迟与贴现的安排。

Historically, the practice of calculating the difference between the value of a future revenue and its price in the present was known, as we have seen, as ‘discounting’, a term still commonly used in the world of finance. What today appears as the ‘growth’ of an investment can more usefully be understood, as the term discounting suggests, as the ‘reduction’ of the future. Payments can be extracted from the future at a fraction of their eventual value. But this depends on building the mechanism that makes that future available. The ability of a certain quantity of money to apparently double its size does not rest on any power of physical expansion of money. It is a consequence of a technopolitical apparatus that creates an obstruction, interruption, and shrinkage. What we call capital, or money with the power to grow, is this kind of arrangement for building and governing the reliable postponement and discounting of payments.

<a id="ch07-0037"></a>

先前问资本为什么*显得*想要延迟时，“显得”一词很重要。但最好重新表述问题。资本在这里可能显得是行动者，寻求使其能够扩张的可靠推迟形式。然而，既然资本是延迟过程的*结果*，把它仅仅视为这些过程的行动者就说不通了。资本不是从过去储存下来、寻求向未来扩张的东西。它是从未来获得的，途径是建造付款装置和强制执行机制，使预期收入能够在当下按折扣可靠地获得。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-028"></a>[28](#note-ch7-028)

In asking earlier why capital *appears* to want a delay, the term ‘appearance’ was important. But it is better to rephrase the terms of the question. Capital may appear here as the agent, seeking the forms of reliable postponement that allow it to expand. However, since capital is the *outcome* of the processes of delay, it does not make sense to consider it simply as the agent of those processes. Capital is not something stored up from the past, seeking expansion into the future. It is acquired from the future, through the building of payment devices and enforcement mechanisms that make prospective income reliably available at a discount in the present.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-028"></a>[28](#note-ch7-028)

<a id="ch07-0038"></a>

从未来获得的收入，主要由<a id="page-250"></a>〔原书第250页〕基础设施的使用者支付。在以股份制公司组织的基础设施项目中，购买公司股份的人确立了对公司部分利润的永久主张。此后，股东的主张成为使用和运营基础设施者必须承担的负担。它是加在货物运输费、乘客票价、水费和电费、服务订阅费之上的一项成本，也是强加在管理和操作这一过程者工资上的一笔开支。这些票价、费用、费率和工资不仅承担运营和维护基础设施的成本，还承担事先卖给股东的那项额外主张。

The revenue acquired from the future is paid largely by the users of <a id="page-250-en"></a>〔原书第250页〕the infrastructure. In the case of an infrastructure project organised as a joint-stock company, those who purchase shares in the company establish a perpetual claim on a portion of the company’s profits. Going forwards, the claim of the shareholder becomes a burden to be carried by those who use and run the infrastructure. It is a cost added to charges for shipping goods, or the fares paid by passengers, or the rates charged for water and electricity, or the fees for subscribing to a service, and it is an expense imposed on the wages of those who manage and operate the process. Those fares, fees, rates, and wages carry not only the cost of operating and maintaining the infrastructure, but the additional claim sold in advance to the shareholders.

<a id="ch07-0039"></a>

### 耐久

### The Durable

<a id="ch07-0040"></a>

通过被推迟付款的主张创造信用货币，本身并非新近的做法。然而，正如[第三章](#ch03-0001)所探讨的，在更早的世纪里，延迟的基础设施并非由钢铁、混凝土和石料、铜和光纤电缆，或今天通常用于建造持久未来付款攫取装置的其他材料构成。延迟不那么持久。在帝国时代之前，其最常见的装置是作物周期：下一季收获的许诺构成了可据以创造信用的未来。如我们所述，另一种延迟可以由延展的商业关系构成。大型贸易网络——例如横跨中世纪印度—伊斯兰世界及其以外的网络——允许建立信用票据或汇票等信贷安排。这些创造信用并予以贴现的技术后来扩展到欧洲。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-029"></a>[29](#note-ch7-029)作为为未来货物付款、在若干周或数月内交付的承诺，票据或汇票可以作为货币运作。它成为中世纪和近代早期世界最广泛使用的信贷和资本创造体系。

The creation of credit money through claims to delayed payments is not in itself a recent practice. However, as [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) explored, in earlier centuries the infrastructures of delay were not built of iron and steel, concrete and masonry, copper and fibre-optical cabling, or the other materials typically used today to build durable apparatuses for the capture of future payments. Delay was less durable. Its most common apparatus before the imperial age was the crop cycle, in which the promise of next season’s harvest constituted the future for which credit could be created. Another kind of delay, as we noted, could be built from extended commercial relations. Large trading networks, such as those organised across the medieval Indo-Islamic world and beyond, allowed the building of credit arrangements such as the promissory note or bill of exchange. These techniques of creating credit and discounting it were later extended to Europe.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-029"></a>[29](#note-ch7-029) As a promise to pay for future goods, due for delivery within a certain number of weeks or months, the note or bill could function as money. It became the most widely used system of credit and capital creation across the medieval and early modern world.

<a id="ch07-0041"></a>

随着欧洲人把中东—亚洲贸易从陆路和沿海路线改道至迂回的海路，制造信用的更大机会出现了。建造可靠的海船、军事贸易站和补给点，使欧洲人得以逐渐主导这一贸易。回顾[第一章](#ch01-0001)提出的观点：在铁路时代之前，武装帆船及其设防航线成为产生和贴现未来收入的最复杂、最昂贵的装置。“一艘船是一台极其<a id="page-251"></a>〔原书第251页〕复杂的机器，或者更确切地说，是大多数已知机器的组合，”法国造船师皮埃尔·福尔费在 1788 年写道。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-030"></a>[30](#note-ch7-030)正如一位造船学史学家所指出的，武装帆船“结合了船体和桅杆的厚重木质结构，令人眼花缭乱的支撑桅杆的固定索具，数百条控制横桁和帆的绳索与滑轮，起锚用的绞盘，转动舵的舵柄和舵轮，舱底泵等等”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-031"></a>[31](#note-ch7-031)这种强度与可控性的结合，构成了一种足够可靠、足够灵活、武装足够充分的装置，能够在远离贸易项目资助者的地方远程运作，通过殖民地贸易的新时间滞后，创造出有利可图的收入“延迟”。组织航运的荷兰和英国商人创立了第一批股份制公司，通过它们，未来收入的股份可以按折扣买卖。同样的信用创造方法扩展到欧洲的北大西洋和加勒比殖民地，扩展到被奴役人口的贸易及其生产的糖、烟草和其他货物。

Larger opportunities to manufacture credit arose with the European diversion of Middle Eastern–Asian trade from overland and coastal routes to circuitous seaborne passages. The building of reliable, oceangoing ships and military trading posts and provisioning points enabled Europeans to gradually dominate this trade. To recall a point made in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), before the age of railways, the armed sailing ship and its fortified route became the most complex and expensive apparatus for generating and discounting future revenue. ‘A vessel is an extremely <a id="page-251-en"></a>〔原书第251页〕composite machine, or rather it is a combination of most known machines’, wrote the French shipbuilder Pierre Forfait in 1788.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-030"></a>[30](#note-ch7-030) As a historian of naval architecture notes, armed sailing ships ‘combined the heavy wooden construction of the hull and masts with a dizzying array of standing rigging to support the masts, hundreds of lines and blocks to control the yardarms and sails, capstans for hauling up the anchors, tillers and wheels to turn the rudder, bilge pumps, and such’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-031"></a>[31](#note-ch7-031) This combination of strength and controllability formed an apparatus that was reliable enough, manoeuvrable enough, and sufficiently armed to operate at a great distance, remote from those who sponsored the trading venture, creating a profitable ‘delay’ in revenue, via the new time lag of colonial trade. The Dutch and English merchants who organised the shipping created the first joint-stock companies, through which shares in prospective revenues could be bought and sold at a discount. The same methods of credit creation were extended to Europe’s North Atlantic and Caribbean colonies, and to the trade in enslaved populations and the sugar, tobacco, and other goods they produced.

<a id="ch07-0042"></a>

为了支持和扩大这种殖民地贸易以及自身收入，欧洲国家建立海军并从事长期战争。殖民战争产生了一种更大的延期付款体系：商人预支信贷，为军事力量的部署提供资金。这种信贷供给形成了更新、更可靠的付款延迟，即所谓的国债，进而促成了国家货币的创造。这些货币后来被错误地视为货币的本质。随着政府发展更广泛的征税方式为这些付款融资，并配套建立扣押货物和因债务监禁的权力，国家权力的持久性以及日益增强的稳定性和规模，促成了新规模的资本创造。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-032"></a>[32](#note-ch7-032)

To support and expand this colonial trade, and their own revenues, European states built naval forces and engaged in protracted wars. Colonial warfare gave rise to a larger system of delayed payment, the credit advanced by merchants to fund the deployment of military force. This provision of credit formed the new and more reliable payment delays known as national debt, which led, in turn, to the creation of national currencies. These currencies would mistakenly come to be thought of as the very essence of money. As governments developed the more extensive modes of taxation required to finance these payments, and the accompanying powers of seizure of goods and imprisonment for debt, the longevity and increasing stability and scale of state power gave rise to capital creation on a new scale.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-032"></a>[32](#note-ch7-032)

<a id="ch07-0043"></a>

在现代、殖民规模的贸易和战争发展之前，通过未来金融贴现获利，受到创造可靠延迟收入之过程的有限持续时间和范围的制约。所能创造的延迟一般以作物周期和贸易路线所规定的月数来衡量，而不是以年或十年计，因此所谓“增长”的可能性受到限制。对未来遥远收入的索取主张价值不大。它们还受到互惠、义务、伦理提升和慷慨等实践的制约——这些无疑以各种组合构成所有道德传统的特征，但也许在某些大商业中心尤为显著，比如<a id="page-252"></a>〔原书第252页〕伊斯兰世界的中心——这些实践限制了非劳动所得的榨取和债务的强制执行。地产可以保证长期收入，但由于对未来收入的权利通常依赖于对历史久远的占有权的主张，或依赖保护的保证（奴隶种植园除外），它们不容易被出售给陌生人。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-033"></a>[33](#note-ch7-033)没有现成机制可以在当下交易这类未来份额。除了现代国家本身以及与其共同演化的殖民公司和种植园之外，没有任何装置能够产生足够可靠的收入，使其可以在数年内有利可图地延迟，又具有足够流动性，可以在当下按折扣交易。

Prior to the development of modern, colonial-scale trade and warfare, profiting through financial discounting of the future was constrained by the limited duration and extent of the processes that created a reliably delayed income. The delays that could be created were generally measured in the months laid out by crop cycles and trade routes, not in years or decades, so were restricted in the possibility of so-called ‘growth’. There was little value to a claim to revenue that lay far in the future. They were also constrained by practices of reciprocity, obligation, ethical improvement, and generosity – characteristic no doubt of all moral traditions in various combinations, but especially marked, perhaps, in some of the centres of great commerce, such as <a id="page-252-en"></a>〔原书第252页〕those of the Islamic world – that placed limits on the extraction of unearned income and the enforcement of debt. Landed estates might guarantee long-term income, but since the rights to that future revenue typically depended (with the exception of slave plantations) on claims to ancient possession, or on guarantees of protection, they could not easily be sold to strangers.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-033"></a>[33](#note-ch7-033) There was no readily available mechanism for trading shares in such futures in the present. Apart from the modern state itself, and the colonising corporations and plantations through which it coevolved, there was no apparatus for generating revenue that was reliable enough that it might be profitably delayed over several years, and liquid enough to trade at a discount in the present.

<a id="ch07-0044"></a>

正如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所探讨并在此可以概括的，资本创造对殖民扩张和战争、对奴役劳动和其他形式暴力的依赖，带来了中断风险。对这种中断的回应，造成了后来对延迟和推迟在资本创造中作用的误解，这种误解至今仍广泛流行。大约从 1775 年到 1815 年的约四十年间，整个通过远距离殖民地贸易创造信用的体系，因南亚、北美、奥斯曼帝国和加勒比地区的政治变革，随后又因遍及欧洲和近东的战争，而中断并几乎停顿。错乱的信贷和资本创造模式通过一个新的绕道得到重组：穿过兰开夏郡的水力棉纺厂。这个绕道利用并迅速发展了一种新的信用体系，它与时间性有着不同的关系。以往长期沿袭的做法，是商人把货物借给将其加工成纺织品的人；如今则由工人提供信用：工人把劳动借给那些转而建造工厂的商人。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-034"></a>[34](#note-ch7-034)这个绕道是艰苦的劳动，不仅对数万名被迫进入工厂劳动的人如此，对丧失了通过垄断基础设施创造财富这一更古老、更简便方法的商人也是如此。几十年内，建造垄断性基础设施的新机会出现了。但在此期间，马克思阅读了英国工厂视察员的报告，并从中得出一种基于这台新时间机器——工厂——的资本理论。

As we explored in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), and can summarise here, this dependence of capital creation on colonial expansion and warfare, and on enslaved labour and other forms of violence, brought risks of disruption. The response to this disruption created what became a misunderstanding of the role of delay and postponement in the creation of capital, a misunderstanding that still prevails widely today. Over roughly four decades from about 1775 to 1815, the entire system of credit creation through long-distance colonial trade was disrupted and almost brought to a halt by political transformations in South Asia, North America, the Ottoman Empire, and the Caribbean, and then by war across Europe and the Near East. Dislocated patterns of credit and capital creation were reorganised by means of a new detour: through the water-driven cotton mills of Lancashire. The detour took advantage of, and rapidly developed, a new credit system, one with a different relation to temporality. Rather than the long-standing practice of merchants loaning goods to those who made them into textiles, the credit was extended by workers, who loaned their labour to the merchants, now building mills.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-034"></a>[34](#note-ch7-034) This detour was hard work, not only for the tens of thousands forced into factory labour, but for the merchants deprived of the older and easier method of creating wealth through the monopoly of infrastructures. Within a few decades, new opportunities for building monopolistic infrastructure emerged. But, in the meantime, Marx had read the reports of English factory inspectors and derived from them a theory of capital based on this new time machine, the factory.

<a id="ch07-0045"></a>

从十九世纪后期起，可以建造持久得多、用于攫取未来的装置。其中大多数采取基础设施项目的形式。其典型是修建长途<a id="page-253"></a>〔原书第253页〕铁路。这类大型、长期建设项目为信用创造提供了新机会。

From the later nineteenth century, much more durable apparatuses for capturing the future could be built. Most of these took the form of infrastructure projects. They were typified by the building of long-distance <a id="page-253-en"></a>〔原书第253页〕railways. Such large, long-term construction projects offered new opportunities for the creation of credit.

<a id="ch07-0046"></a>

新基础设施项目的两个特征，促成了更大幅度的延迟。第一，正如我们在[第一章](#ch01-0001)所述，与其他攫取收入的手段相比，即使在今天，基础设施也异常耐久。铁路、水坝、港口、管道、公路、输电线、通信网络和数据中心由混凝土、钢铁、铜、热塑性塑料和其他耐久材料建成。技术韧性和耐久性是这类基础设施安排的构成特征。按照设计，它们必须比其所引导和便利流动的瞬态货物、车辆、液体、数据和人员更耐久。基础设施运载的材料往往打算在数月、数日、数分钟或更短时间内消耗掉，本身几乎不产生长期收入流；而基础设施的寿命通常以年或十年计。可以按折扣购买的未来收入，部分是这种必要差异的产物：意在消耗的供应品或流具有可分解性，而承载它们流动的装置具有不可分解性。

Two features of the new infrastructure projects contributed to making possible the much larger postponement of time. First, as we noted in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), compared with other means of capturing revenue, even today, infrastructures are unusually durable. Railways, dams, ports, pipelines, highways, power lines, communication networks, and data centres are built of concrete, steel, copper, thermoplastics, and other resilient materials. Technical resilience and durability are constituent features of such infrastructure arrangements. By design they must be more resilient than the transient goods, vehicles, liquids, data, and persons whose flow they channel and enable. While the materials carried by infrastructures are often intended to be consumed within months, days, minutes, or less, creating in themselves little in the way of long-term revenue streams, the life of infrastructure is typically measured in years or decades. The future revenue that can be purchased at a discount is, in part, the product of this necessary difference between the decomposability of supplies or streams intended to be consumed and the non-decomposing quality of the apparatus through which they flow.

<a id="ch07-0047"></a>

第二，与许多其他攫取收入的手段相比，基础设施通常还以另一种耐久性建造：一种政治和法律保障。作为简略说法，它们可以被描述为垄断。但这个词简化了保障的不同要素。作为安排和控制流动的装置，基础设施往往固定在原地、向外建成，是一种不动产（在某些用法中，基础设施几乎成为任何大于建筑的实体结构的标签）。像所有不动产一样，与可移动货物相对，这种结构具有垄断性，排他地占据空间，阻止其他使用者进入该空间，或向他们收费。收费可以小到向公用事业公司支付的家庭用水费，也可以大到集装箱船或油轮在“长赐号”事故发生前后，通行苏伊士运河所需支付的 50 万至 80 万美元通行费。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-035"></a>[35](#note-ch7-035)即使是数字基础设施也垄断空间，不仅通过把数字平台转变为具有产权归属的资产而在比喻和法律意义上如此，还通过占据关键地理位置或对电力供应、跨洋电缆和其他必需品的优先获取权来垄断空间。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-036"></a>[36](#note-ch7-036)

Second, more than many other means of capturing revenues, infrastructures are typically built with another kind of durability, a form of political and legal guarantee. As a shorthand, they can be described as monopolies. But that term simplifies the different elements of the guarantee. As an apparatus for the ordering and control of flows, an infrastructure tends to be fixed in place, built out, a form of real estate (in some uses, infrastructure becomes the label for almost any material structure larger than a building). Like all real property, in contrast to movable goods, the structure is monopolising, occupying space exclusively, blocking other users from that space, or charging them for its use. The charge can be as minor as the household rates paid to a utility company for the supply of domestic water, or as large as the $500,000 to $800,000 transit fee that a container ship or oil tanker was paying, at the time of the Ever Given disaster, to navigate through the Suez Canal.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-035"></a>[35](#note-ch7-035) Even digital infrastructures monopolise space, not only figuratively and legally, through transforming digital platforms into propertied assets, but by occupying key geographical locations or privileged access to electricity supplies, transoceanic cables, and other requirements.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-036"></a>[36](#note-ch7-036)

<a id="ch07-0048"></a>

此外，由于基础设施规模庞大、物质上延展，建造它们通常涉及政府权力和强制力量。水坝、港口、铁路、公路、电站<a id="page-254"></a>〔原书第254页〕和通信线路通常需要当局授予或批准的特许权，授予并强制执行对陆路、河道、港口、输电走廊或通信节点的排他控制。这不只是政府授予垄断权的问题。在现代国家时代，地方和国家政府的权力本身，都是通过法律体系、立法委员会、市政和港口当局以及其他声称拥有建造、许可、治安管理和管理基础设施之权力的机构的发展而出现的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-037"></a>[37](#note-ch7-037)政府和基础设施作为相互依赖、空间界定的权力形式共同演化，在信用创造的技术政治工作中合作。

Moreover, since infrastructures are large, materially extended arrangements, building them usually involves powers of government and forces of coercion. Dams, ports, railroads, highways, power stations, <a id="page-254-en"></a>〔原书第254页〕and communication lines typically require a concession or authorisation from an authority, awarding and enforcing exclusive control of a land route, river channel, harbour, transmission corridor, or communication node. This is not simply a question of governments granting monopoly rights. The very powers of government, in the era of the modern state, both local and national, emerged through the development of legal systems, legislative committees, municipal and port authorities, and other bodies that claimed powers to build, license, police, and manage infrastructure.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-037"></a>[37](#note-ch7-037) Government and infrastructure coevolved as interdependent forms of spatially defined power, collaborating in the technopolitical work of credit creation.

<a id="ch07-0049"></a>
