政府和基础设施的共同演化，使某些基础设施场址可以作为改变或中止普通政府权力的区域运作。殖民贸易公司建立的设防飞地是早期例子，黎凡特地区由欧洲商人各个“民族”居住的“商馆”或贸易站也是如此。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-038"></a>[38](#note-ch7-038)劳伦·本顿表明，帝国管辖权和主权通过“走廊”（如河流和道路网络）和“飞地”（如定居点和前哨）不均衡地扩张。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-039"></a>[39](#note-ch7-039)如今，正如黛博拉·考恩所指出的，这些“物流空间”继续例证着有组织暴力的强化，供应链的“致命生活”在那里集中。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-040"></a>[40](#note-ch7-040)当今最常见的例子是名称奇特的“自由区”。它可能是港口区域或类似飞地，通常靠近国际边界并与运输路线相连，由独立于国内法的当局授权并便利货物、资本、治安力量和劳动力的流动。该区域通常免征国家税和消费税，中止国家劳动法和环境立法的适用，并运营自己的安全和监控系统。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-041"></a>[41](#note-ch7-041)在埃及，苏伊士运河出口区提供了一个典型例子。在海湾部分地区，包括巴林和迪拜，国家的大量财富和权力都围绕创设这类区域而组织起来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-042"></a>[42](#note-ch7-042)

The coevolution of government and infrastructure allowed certain infrastructure sites to operate as zones in which ordinary government power is modified or suspended. The fortified enclaves created by colonial trading companies were an early example of this, as were the ‘factories’ or trading stations populated by the various ‘nations’ of European merchants in the Levant.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-038"></a>[38](#note-ch7-038) Lauren Benton shows that imperial jurisdiction and sovereignty expanded unevenly through ‘corridors’, such as river and road networks, and ‘enclaves’, such as settlements and outposts.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-039"></a>[39](#note-ch7-039) Today, as Deborah Cowen notes, these ‘logistics spaces’ continue to exemplify an intensification of organised violence, where the ‘deadly life’ of supply chains is concentrated.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-040"></a>[40](#note-ch7-040) The most common example today is the curiously named ‘free zone’. This might be a port area or similar enclave, typically close to an international border and connected to transportation routes, in which an authority independent of domestic law authorises and facilitates the movement of goods, capital, policing, and labour. The zone is typically exempt from national taxes and excise duties, suspends the application of national labour laws and environmental legislation, and operates its own security and surveillance systems.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-041"></a>[41](#note-ch7-041) In Egypt, the Suez Canal Export Zone provides a typical example. In some parts of the Gulf, including Bahrain and Dubai, much of the wealth and power of the state has been organised around the creation of such zones.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-042"></a>[42](#note-ch7-042)

<a id="ch07-0050"></a>

基础设施还有第三个增强其耐久性的特征：它们成为技术、经济和商业报道的对象，受到衡量、制表、压力测试、监测和指数化。[第四章](#ch04-0001)讨论的普尔的*《铁路手册》*就是这类实践的显著例子。这种对基础设施的报道、衡量和监测，要求并鼓励发展凯勒·伊斯特林所谓的“国家之外的治理术”：标准、可重复的公式<a id="page-255"></a>〔原书第255页〕和协议，它们构成治理空间的“操作系统”，尤其是看似处于国家直接治理之外的空间，例如自由区以及我们提到的、由大型基础设施促成和鼓励的其他设防例外场址。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-043"></a>[43](#note-ch7-043)

There is a third feature of infrastructures that enhances their durability: they become the object of technical, economic, and business reporting, which measures, tabulates, stress-tests, monitors, and indexes. Poor’s *Manual of the Railroads*, discussed in [chapter 4](#ch04-0001), was a notable example of such practices. This reporting, measuring, and monitoring of infrastructure requires and encourages the development of what Keller Easterling terms ‘extrastatecraft’: standards, repeatable formulas, <a id="page-255-en"></a>〔原书第255页〕and protocols which form the ‘operating system’ for the governing of space, especially spaces seemingly outside the direct government of the state, such as free zones and other fortified and exceptional sites that, as we noted, large infrastructures enable and encourage.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-043"></a>[43](#note-ch7-043)

<a id="ch07-0051"></a>

### 流动

### The Liquid

<a id="ch07-0052"></a>

然而，无论是技术耐久性还是政治耐久性，都只是从未来获利之力量扩张的一个方面。延长控制收入的时间跨度本身，并不能成为大量预期收益的来源。毕竟，即使古人也能随着时间推移建造大型、持久的物质结构和政治秩序。把时间组织为大规模创造资本的手段，需要耐久性与其反面相结合：流动性。

Durability, however, both technical and political, is only one aspect of the expanding power to profit from the future. Extending the length of time over which revenue is controlled cannot become the source of large prospective gain by itself. After all, even the ancients, over time, could build large, enduring material structures and political orders. The organisation of time as a means of creating capital on a large scale requires the combination of durability with its obverse: liquidity.

<a id="ch07-0053"></a>

只有当对未来付款的主张成为一种可以迅速进入流通的权利——一种对财产的法律主张——时，未来付款才能成为不断扩张的利润、差额收益的来源。未来收入主张的所有者必须能够随时将其转让给另一个所有者。这种可转让性首先使信用创造成为可能，开启了按折扣购买的可能，从而带来贴现利润。

Future payments can become a source of expanding profit, of differential gain, only when the claim to them becomes a right – a legal claim to property – that can be quickly put in motion. The owner of the claim on future revenue must be able to readily transfer it to another owner. This transferability allows the creation of credit in the first place, setting up the possibility of purchase at a discount and thus the profit from discounting.

<a id="ch07-0054"></a>

因此，用于攫取未来付款的持久装置的发展，在每个阶段都伴随着一个对应过程的发展：一种把对未来主张转化为可立即交换之物的机制。持久基础设施所产生的金融“票据”形式——票据、债券、股份、衍生品和其他货币工具——是硬化、耐久的攫取装置的轻质“液态”对应物。

So, the development of durable apparatuses for capturing future payments is accompanied at every stage by the development of a counterpart process: a mechanism for converting claims on the future into something immediately exchangeable. The forms of financial ‘paper’ to which durable infrastructures give rise – bills, bonds, shares, derivatives, and other kinds of monetary instrument – are the lightweight, ‘liquid’ corollary of the hardened, resilient apparatuses of capture.

<a id="ch07-0055"></a>

这些轻质法律装置，无论以纸质还是电子形式，都执行一种转译行为，把基础设施攫取未来收入的所有不同模式转化为同一种东西：信用货币。使对未来主张可转译、从而可立即从一个所有者转让给另一个所有者并可贴现，不只是给它们标上数字或价格的问题。股票凭证或汇票可能有面值，但其有效价值只能通过建立定价机制来确定，换言之，通过建立被称为“市场”的金融装置来确定。基础设施的建设伴随着货币市场的建设，也因货币市场而成为可能。殖民时代的军事化航线和<a id="page-256"></a>〔原书第256页〕战争，过去一个半世纪的运输、能源、水利和通信基础设施，以及最近几十年的数字通路和平台，都促进了创造、交换和贴现信用货币之新制度的形成。

These lightweight legal devices, whether in paper or electronic form, carry out an act of translation, converting all the different modes of infrastructural capture of future revenue into instances of the same thing: credit money. Making claims on the future translatable, and thus instantly transferable from one owner to another, and discountable, is not simply a matter of marking them with a number, or a price. A stock certificate or bill of exchange may have a face value, but its effective value can only be established by building a pricing mechanism, or, in other words, the financial apparatus known as a ‘market’. The building of infrastructures was accompanied, and made possible, by the building of money markets. The militarised shipping routes and warfare of <a id="page-256-en"></a>〔原书第256页〕the colonial age, the transportation, energy, hydraulic, and communication infrastructures of the last century and a half, and the digital pathways and platforms of the most recent decades each facilitated the forming of new institutions for creating, exchanging, and discounting credit money.

<a id="ch07-0056"></a>

流动性的创造还需要更多东西。货币装置的轻质特性使它们可以大量捆绑在一起。部分正是这种捆绑，使银行家能够提前以“折扣”提供任何一项未来主张。银行在当下发行的信用货币，由银行借以保证自身信用的未来付款的数量和多样性来担保。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-044"></a>[44](#note-ch7-044)与此同时，正如杰弗里·英厄姆所指出的，资本主义货币的独特之处在于一种机制，它把这些私人债务—信用契约转化为“货币”——一种由国家承认并实施的普遍许诺（通过接受以货币纳税）。这通过另一种“差异”的生产而发生：私人银行与政府货币当局或中央银行之间，以及政府与其债权人（债券持有人）和债务人（纳税人）之间的差异。中央银行用国家货币购买银行的私人债务——付款承诺。结果，私人信用货币被货币化，并变得在任何地方都可接受。这最初发生在英格兰银行贴现地方银行的票据之时。国家并不“控制”这一过程，而是试图加以规制。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-045"></a>[45](#note-ch7-045)

This creation of liquidity requires something more. The lightweight quality of the monetary devices allows them to be bundled together in large quantities. It is, in part, this bundling that enables bankers to make any one claim on the future available in advance, at a ‘discount’. The credit money issued by banks in the present is secured by the sheer quantity and variety of future payments with which the bank guarantees its credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-044"></a>[44](#note-ch7-044) Simultaneously, as Geoffrey Ingham points out, capitalist money is distinctive in the mechanism that converts these private debt-credit contracts into ‘money’ – a universal promise, recognised and implemented by the state (via its acceptance for the payment of taxes). This happens through another production of ‘difference’, between private banks and a government monetary authority or central bank, and between the government and its creditors (bondholders) and debtors (taxpayers). The central bank purchases the private debts of banks – promises to pay – with state money. As a result, private credit money is monetised, and made acceptable anywhere. This first happened when the Bank of England discounted the bills of country banks. The state does not ‘control’ this but attempts to regulate it.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-045"></a>[45](#note-ch7-045)

<a id="ch07-0057"></a>

十九世纪后期的大型碳燃料基础设施项目，帮助促成了现代商业银行业的形成；商业银行负责组织由新基础设施耐久性所促成的流动性和信用机制。如我们所见，它们还刺激了另一种通过贴现未来收益生产信贷的制度发展：股东所有的公司。此后一百五十年间，公司成为组织财富积累和集中也许最有效的安排。正是铁路的建设——尤其是十九世纪后期的横贯大陆铁路和其他长途殖民地铁路——催生了这种组织资本的新方式。铁路公司的股票是伦敦、纽约和其他金融中心不断扩张的证券交易所中最常见的投资品。此前，股份只代表对企业当前物质资产的部分所有权。在大型基础设施的新时代，股份被转变为对基础设施可靠地置于未来的收入的所有权主张。

The great carbon-fuelled infrastructure projects of the later nineteenth century helped create modern commercial banking, as organisers of the liquidity and credit mechanisms facilitated by the durability of the new infrastructures. They also spurred, as we have seen, the development of another institution for the production of credit via the discounting of future earnings: the shareholder-owned corporation. Over the following 150 years, the corporation became perhaps the most effective arrangement for organising the accumulation and concentration of wealth. It was the building of railways, especially the transcontinental and other long-distance colonial lines of the later nineteenth century, that gave rise to this new way of organising capital. Shares of railway companies were the most common investment traded on the expanding stock exchanges of London, New York, and other financial centres. Previously, shares represented simply the part ownership of the current material assets of a business. In the new age of large infrastructure, shares were transformed into the ownership claim on the revenues that infrastructures placed reliably in the future.

<a id="ch07-0058"></a>

<a id="page-257"></a>〔原书第257页〕能够获得信贷的人可以按折扣购买未来收入的一份——例如来自铁路线路开发商的收入。开发商将实现即时利润，实际上往往是一笔巨大的意外之财，因为未来收入可能值建设基础设施成本的许多倍。购买股份的投资者将获得未来收入，其贴现反映了该收入在五年、十年或五十年内不可得的事实。

<a id="page-257-en"></a>〔原书第257页〕Those with access to credit could purchase a share of the future revenue – from the developers of a railway line, for example – at a discount. The developers would realise an immediate profit, in fact often a great windfall, since the future revenues might be worth many times the cost of building the infrastructure. The share-buying investor would acquire the future revenue, discounted to reflect the fact that the revenue would not be available for five, ten, or fifty years.

<a id="ch07-0059"></a>

大型基础设施项目不是推迟和攫取未来的唯一装置。这一过程逐渐采取许多其他形式，包括其他大型股东所有的产业、投机性房地产和抵押贷款融资的发展、各种消费信贷形式，以及最终电子平台的建造和控制，随着资产化蔓延到越来越多的生活领域。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-046"></a>[46](#note-ch7-046)但在更早的几十年里，从十九世纪后期开始，铁路、初生的石油工业和其他大型基础设施公司开创了这些建构和攫取未来的形式，并成为最大的范例；它们继续例证着基础设施以其变化的形式，如何让我们理解以未来为代价的生活方式。

Large infrastructure projects were not the only apparatus for the postponement and capture of the future. The process gradually took many other forms, including other large shareholder-owned industries, speculative real estate and the development of mortgage financing, forms of consumer credit, and eventually the building and control of electronic platforms, as assetisation spread into more and more areas of life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-046"></a>[46](#note-ch7-046) But, in earlier decades, starting in the later nineteenth century, railways, the nascent oil industry, and other large infrastructure firms pioneered these forms of constructing and capturing the future and were the largest examples; they continue to exemplify many of the ways in which infrastructure, in its changing forms, allows us to understand the modes of living at the expense of the future.

<a id="ch07-0060"></a>

法律体系帮助赋予未来收入主张以耐久性和流动性，但所做的还不止这些。在裁决对收入流的相互竞争的主张时——例如在股东、债权人和享有工资或退休金债权者之间——它确立优先顺序。在多数法域，法律逐渐把企业股份视为一种财产形式，赋予其持有人不仅对公司实物资产的权利，还有对未来收入的所有权主张。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-047"></a>[47](#note-ch7-047)

The legal system helps to give claims to future revenue both their durability and their liquidity, but also does more. In adjudicating among rival claims to a stream of income, for example among those who own shares, those who are owed debts, and those who are owed wages or retirement pensions, it establishes priorities. In most jurisdictions, the law came to treat shares in a business venture as a form of property, giving their holders not only rights over the physical assets of a company but an ownership claim to revenue in the future.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-047"></a>[47](#note-ch7-047)

<a id="ch07-0061"></a>

虽然基础设施许诺耐久性，但在实践中，它很少可能享有这种许诺所暗示的稳定性。学者们过去认为，基础设施的特质之一是其不可见性。它通常在后台或地下运作，使大多数服务使用者对其运转无所察觉。与许多技术史一样，这种论述是从成功项目的立场、而非从技术系统设计者面对不确定结果时的立场写成的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-048"></a>[48](#note-ch7-048)更好的看法是，基础设施并非不可见，而是一种检测、报道和核算过程的组织，试图管理各种可见性形式。每一种技术装置都需要维护和修理，都可能发生故障、衰败和失效。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-049"></a>[49](#note-ch7-049)

While an infrastructure promises durability, in practice, it is seldom likely to enjoy the stability that the promise might imply. Scholars used to argue that one of the qualities of infrastructure was its invisibility. It typically operates in the background, or below ground, keeping most users of its services unaware of its functioning. As with much history of technology, this approach is written from the standpoint of successful projects, rather than the standpoint of those designing a technical system, when the outcome is uncertain.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-048"></a>[48](#note-ch7-048) Infrastructure is better seen not as invisible, but as an organisation of processes of testing, reporting, and accounting that attempts to manage the forms of visibility. Every technical apparatus requires maintenance and repair, and is subject to the possibility of malfunction, decay, and failure.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-049"></a>[49](#note-ch7-049)

<a id="ch07-0062"></a>

从失败的可能性可以推出，基础设施不仅是<a id="page-258"></a>〔原书第258页〕创造资本的手段，也是摧毁资本的手段。但这并不意味着资本的毁灭仅仅平衡其创造，抵消货币创造的力量。重要的是理解损耗、冗余、破坏、过时和衰败的形式——基础设施使这些形式变得可见，而在把资本主义仅仅视为对“货物”的“消费”的思维方式中，它们不那么明显；同时也要理解伴随任何从未来获取之组织的风险和损失因素。更重要的问题是，攫取装置的技术政治组织如何分配成本、风险和回报。

From the possibility of failure, it follows that infrastructures are a <a id="page-258-en"></a>〔原书第258页〕means not only to create capital, but to destroy it. But this does not mean that the destruction of capital simply balances its creation, cancelling out the power of money creation. It is important to understand the forms of wastage, redundancy, sabotage, obsolescence, and decay, all of which are made visible by infrastructures in a way that is less obvious with modes of thinking that focus on capitalism as simply the ‘consumption’ of ‘goods’; and to understand the elements of risk and loss that accompany any organisation of acquisition from the future. The more important issue is how the technopolitical organisation of apparatuses of capture distributes the costs, risks, and rewards.

<a id="ch07-0063"></a>

### 基础设施的气候

### The Climate of Infrastructure

<a id="ch07-0064"></a>

基础设施作用于时间，但不只以我们通常设想的方式。虽然它们可能加快货物运输、人员旅行或能源流动的速度，这种时间加速也许并非其最重要的属性。其技术耐久性和政治强度赋予它们另一目的。它们引入一种中断，一种未来与当下之间的间隙，当下正是从这个间隙中榨取未来的财富。

Infrastructures work on time, but not only in the ways we commonly assume. While they may increase the speed at which goods are transported, people travel, or energy flows, this acceleration of time may not be their most important attribute. Their technical durability and political strength give them another purpose. They introduce an interruption, a gap between the future and the present out of which the present extracts its wealth from the future.

<a id="ch07-0065"></a>

以这种方式理解资本——把它理解为一种从未来榨取的技术政治过程，基础设施的工作是其例证——为气候危机政治开启了若干问题。这些问题将在最后一章详细讨论。但让我们在此列出这些问题。

Understanding capital in this way, as a technopolitical process of extraction from the future, exemplified by the work of infrastructure, opens up several questions for the politics of the climate crisis. These will be taken up in detail in the final chapter. But let us lay out the issues here.

<a id="ch07-0066"></a>

第一，我们应如何思考增长问题？关于经济增长与气候危机的讨论通常主张，要么必须以不同方式衡量增长，把生态成本计入，要么必须放弃增长目标，代之以去增长政治。如果我们以不同方式理解增长，这些论点会如何变化？与其把增长视为经济扩张的（不充分）衡量，不如把它理解为一种被建构的托词——不仅是为了把某些成本排除在政治考虑之外，而且是为了从范畴上错误再现资本的本质以及我们以未来为代价的生活方式——这样理解会发生什么？

First, how should we think about the question of growth? Discussions of economic growth in relation to the climate crisis typically argue either that growth must be measured differently, to take account of ecological costs, or that it must be abandoned as a goal, replaced by a politics of degrowth. How do these arguments change if we consider growth differently? Rather than approaching it as an (inadequate) measure of economic expansion, what happens once we grasp growth as an alibi that has been constructed, not just to exclude certain costs from political consideration, but to categorically misrepresent the nature of capital and our mode of living at the expense of the future?

<a id="ch07-0067"></a>

第二，我们如何重新构想唯物主义、榨取主义与自然政治的问题？正如[第二章](#ch02-0001)和[第三章](#ch03-0001)所探讨的，我们关于物质生活的许多政治思考仍然陷于生产主义框架，其中<a id="page-259"></a>〔原书第259页〕物质的榨取和转化不仅代表一种普遍性的掠夺方式，而且被视为价值创造、人类被治理和剥削之过程的关键。这里提出的替代方案——剩余的实现是绕道和延迟方法的产物，也是组织和控制这些方法的技术政治装置的产物——能否让我们把物质生产看作这些绕道之一，而其中很大部分不是由人类需要、而是由破坏、浪费、故障、衰退和延迟的机会所驱动？

Second, how can we reframe questions of materialism, extractivism, and the politics of nature? As [chapters 2](#ch02-0001) and [3](#ch03-0001) explored, much of our political thinking about material life remains caught in the framework of productivism, in which the extraction and transformation of <a id="page-259-en"></a>〔原书第259页〕materials represents not just a pervasive mode of despoliation but the key to the process by which value is created and humans are governed and exploited. Can the alternative suggested here, in which the realisation of surplus is the product of methods of detour and delay, and the technopolitical apparatuses through which these are organised and controlled, allow us to see material production as one among those detours, much of it driven not by human need but by opportunities for sabotage, waste, breakdown, deterioration, and delay.

<a id="ch07-0068"></a>

第三，衰败、故障和失败的不可避免性，提出了关于基础设施如何作用于时间的进一步问题，这个问题对思考资本和气候危机尤为重要。许多应对气候紧急状态的尝试，都围绕基础设施的再利用或建造巨型新装置展开。正如我们在本书开头所说，基础设施例证了看似独特的人类改造地球的能力。其寿命和规模似乎违抗自然，按照人类目的重造世界。一个多世纪以来，现代基础设施的规模帮助重新定义了人类对自然的体验——驯服河流、照亮城市、穿越地景、征服距离、支配能量的能力。然而，尽管制造了这种人与自然的对立效果，而且实际上帮助变出了自然这一概念本身，基础设施的建设从来不只是人类的成就。

Third, the inevitability of decay, breakdown, and failure raises a further question concerning the way in which infrastructures work on time, a question of particular importance for thinking about capital and the climate crisis. Many attempts to address the climate emergency revolve around the repurposing of infrastructures or the building of new apparatuses on a gigantic scale. Infrastructures, as we said at the beginning of this book, exemplify what seems the distinctively human capacity to transform the Earth. Their longevity and size appear to defy nature, remaking the world according to human purposes. For more than a century, the scale of modern infrastructure has helped redefine the human experience of nature – the ability to tame rivers, illuminate cities, cut through landscapes, conquer distances, and command energies. Yet, despite creating this effect of humans versus nature, and, indeed, helping to conjure the very concept of nature, the building of infrastructure was never a human accomplishment alone.

<a id="ch07-0069"></a>

记住这一点是有益的：我们所设想的人类建构世界的活动，需要大量非人要素，从原材料和建筑设备到能源和计算装置。这些要素不只是被动的投入，而是贡献自身的属性、力量和倾向。它们形成自己的合金与化合物，创造自己的连接和断联层次，贡献稳定持久的倾向，或变得不稳定并引发燃烧。即使是我们所设想的一切复杂、耐久装置中属于人的部分，也由广泛分布的计算、记录、回忆、发送信号和指挥能力构成。每一种这样的能力都是技术、心理和身体成分的混合物，其中人与非人、有意行为与其他倾向之产物之间的确切分界，从来只是一种不确定的效果。

It is useful to remember that what we think of as human world-making requires a lot of nonhuman elements, from raw materials and construction equipment to energy sources and calculating devices. These elements are not just passive inputs, but contribute their own properties, powers, and propensities. They form their own alloys and compounds, create their own connections and layers of disconnection, and contribute tendencies to stabilise and endure or become volatile and cause combustion. Even what we think of as the human parts of any complex and enduring apparatus are composed of widely distributed powers to calculate, record, recall, signal, and command. Every such competence is an amalgam of technical, mental, and physical components, in which the exact divide between what is human and nonhuman, between what is intentional and the product of other propensities, is never more than an uncertain effect.

<a id="ch07-0070"></a>

但基础设施项目的耐久性和规模中，是否仍存在某种独特的人类要素？也许这种观点正是气候危机要我们重新审视的。地球系统比任何看似人类的干预都更<a id="page-260"></a>〔原书第260页〕复杂、相互关联和耐久。而我们所再现为大型、巨型项目的，只是享有特别强韧、持久相互关联的局部要素和安排。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch7-050"></a>[50](#note-ch7-050)

But does there remain a distinctively human element in the durability and scale of infrastructural projects? Perhaps that is a view that the climate crisis places in perspective. Earth systems turn out to be more <a id="page-260-en"></a>〔原书第260页〕complex, interconnected, and durable than any apparently human intervention. And what we represent as large-scale, mega projects are simply localised elements and arrangements that enjoy particularly strong and durable interconnections.<a id="ref-en-note-ch7-050"></a>[50](#note-ch7-050)

<a id="ch07-0071"></a>

最后，我们能否重新思考代际正义问题？这个问题通常被提成气候紧急状态带来的例外问题：当下必须紧急作出什么牺牲，才能让未来有可行的集体生活形式？然而，这里所呈现的理解我们与未来之关系的方法，以不同方式框定了问题。我们的生活方式威胁着后来者，这不仅是我们不顾后果地开发地球资源所造成的副产品，更因为这种生活方式本就建立在从未来夺取生计之上。

Finally, can we reconsider the question of intergenerational justice? The question is usually posed as an exceptional issue brought about by the climate emergency. What sacrifices have to be made urgently in the present to allow the possibility of viable forms of collective life in the future? However, the approach presented here to understanding our relation to the future frames the question differently. Our mode of living is a threat to those who come later, not just as a by-product of our own careless exploitation of the resources of the planet, but as a form of life built upon the taking of livelihoods from the future.


# 第八章　明天会更好，明天？气候危机与增长的托词

<a id="ch08-0001"></a>

<a id="page-261"></a>〔原书第261页〕

<a id="page-261-en"></a>〔原书第261页〕

<a id="ch08-0002"></a>

## 第八章　明天会更好，明天？气候危机与增长的托词

## 8 A Better Tomorrow, Tomorrow? Climate Crisis and the Alibi of Growth

<a id="ch08-0003"></a>

气候灾难要求我们发展新的概念——关于自由与政治、关于人与非人世界、关于代际和民族之间的正义——以便为应对不断展开的危机提供更好的工具。但这场灾难也要求我们解释政治上的失败：为什么未能及时行动。为什么现有的集体生活概念显得如此不受批评影响？有一个概念因其对反复提出的重塑或抛弃呼吁的抵抗而格外突出：经济观念。在无数关于气候政治的批评文本中，我们被敦促逃离经济及其狭隘的福祉定义，以更具生态意识的物质需要和限度概念取而代之，并与其无限增长的逻辑决裂。但经济观念——作为把握和衡量我们物质生活的一种方式——以及公众对其持续增长的执念，在很大程度上对这些批评免疫。为什么会这样？<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-001"></a>[1](#note-ch8-001)

The climate catastrophe demands that we develop new conceptions – of freedom and the political, of the human and nonhuman worlds, of justice between generations and peoples – to provide better tools for coping with the unfolding crisis. But the catastrophe also asks us to account for the political failure to have acted in time. Why have existing conceptions of collective life appeared so impervious to critique? One concept stands out for its resistance to repeated calls for its recasting or abandonment: the idea of the economy. In countless critical texts on climate politics, we are urged to escape from the economy, with its narrow definition of well-being, to replace it with a more ecological conception of our material needs and limits, and to break with its logic of limitless growth. But the idea of the economy, as a way of grasping and measuring our material life, and the public preoccupation with its continued growth, have been largely immune to such criticisms. Why is that so?<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-001"></a>[1](#note-ch8-001)

<a id="ch08-0004"></a>

答案有两方面。第一，我们一直缺乏对经济所做之事的理解。经济通常被理解为所有现代社会的一种自然特征，指物质生产和交换的领域。我们常常被告知，它需要得到更好的管理，以更好的方式衡量，从而更准确地捕捉社会不公和生态危害的形式。相反，经济应被视为一种装置或技术设备，一种作为臣服模式运作的东西——或者，我要借用福柯对杰里米·边沁全景敞视监狱的解读，称之为“经济全景装置”（EconoCon）。作为一种装置，经济被格式化的方式有助于生产政治<a id="page-262"></a>〔原书第262页〕臣服和集体主体性的形式，使当下的少数人能够以未来大多数人为代价生活——包括，正如本书所论证的，多数人如今受制于偿还此前从未来榨取的款项这一义务，这笔债务多数人必须持续且日益沉重地承担。

The answer is twofold. First, we have lacked an understanding of what the economy does. The economy is usually understood as a natural feature of all modern societies, designating the sphere of material production and exchange. It needs to be better managed, we are often told, and measured in better ways, to more accurately capture forms of social injustice and ecological harm. The economy should be seen instead as an apparatus or technical device, one that operates as a mode of subjection – or what I shall call, with a nod to Foucault’s reading of Jeremy Bentham’s Panopticon, the ‘EconoCon’. As a device, the economy is formatted in ways that help produce the forms of political <a id="page-262-en"></a>〔原书第262页〕subjection and collective subjectivity that enable a minority in the present to live at the expense of most people in the future – including, as this book has argued, their subjection today to the repayment of previous extractions from the future, a debt the majority must continually and increasingly bear.

<a id="ch08-0005"></a>

第二，我们一直缺乏对增长的理解。对多数人来说，经济增长显得是资本主义社会的自然运动，由不可避免的技术进步过程或过去资本不断积累、寻求进一步扩张机会所驱动。它几乎从不与资本化、或资本主义从未来榨取的模式联系起来。相反，我们不应把增长问题当作一种历史力量来处理——一种为避免比全球变暖已经预示的更灾难性后果而必须以某种方式加以限制或逆转的力量——而应把它当作一种偿付保障机制。增长是一种确保债务偿还的装置。这种思路并不会使增长对集体福祉的破坏性减少。但它确实使我们能够把增长理解为并非历史发展或资本主义扩张的必然运动，而是一种较近期的安排，它产生于——而非仅仅导致——我们从未来榨取的模式。

Second, we have lacked an understanding of growth. For most people, economic growth appears as the natural movement of capitalist society, driven by an ineluctable process of technological improvement or a continuous accumulation of capital from the past seeking further opportunities for expansion. It is almost never connected to capitalisation, or the capitalist mode of extraction from the future. Instead, we should approach the question of growth not as a historical force – one that, if we are to avoid even more calamitous consequences than those that global warming already has in store, we must somehow limit or reverse – but as a mode of indemnification. Growth is a device for securing the repayment of debt. This approach does not make growth any less damaging to collective well-being. But it does allow us to grasp it not as the inevitable movement of historical development or capitalist expansion, but as a more recent arrangement that arises from – rather than simply causing – our mode of extraction from the future.

<a id="ch08-0006"></a>

第三项论点从这两点中产生。在解释经济增长加速的现象时，我们误解了化石燃料的作用。它们在引发气候紧急状态中的作用毋庸置疑。但经济装置及其增长执念，与碳基能源使用的增加之间是什么关系？在这里，我们关于经济是所有现代社会共有的物质生活领域、其增长是资本主义自然扩张的平常观念，再次妨碍我们理解气候危机和我们对化石燃料的依赖。

A third argument emerges from these two. In explaining the phenomenon of accelerating economic growth, we have misunderstood the role of fossil fuels. Their role in causing the climate emergency is not in question. But what is the relation between the device of the economy and our preoccupation with its growth, on the one hand, and the increasing use of carbon-based energy, on the other? Here, again, our ordinary idea of the economy as the sphere of material life common to all modern societies, and of its growth as an expansion natural to capitalism, stands in the way of understanding the climate crisis and our dependence on fossil fuels.

<a id="ch08-0007"></a>

让我们从碳基能源及其与增长的关系这一问题开始，然后转向经济以及如何理解它在管理从未来榨取之模式中的作用。最后，我们将回到一种不同的理解：化石燃料与经济，以及作为资本托词的增长。

Let us begin with this question of carbon-based energy and its relation to growth, then turn to the economy and how to understand its role in managing modes of extraction from the future. We will return at the end to a different understanding of fossil fuels, the economy, and growth as an alibi of capital.

<a id="ch08-0008"></a>

<a id="page-263"></a>〔原书第263页〕

<a id="page-263-en"></a>〔原书第263页〕

<a id="ch08-0009"></a>

### 经济及其增长

### The Economy and Its Growth

<a id="ch08-0010"></a>

化石燃料时代由增长观念所界定。但什么是增长，它与碳能源有什么关系？我们如何开始相信，燃烧化石燃料创造了一个集体世界，而这个世界的界定特征就是增长？如果我们想要一个没有增长的世界，或具有不同增长形式、对地球系统和物种破坏较少的世界，我们必须追问：增长如何与化石燃料的榨取和燃烧联系在一起？

The era of fossil fuels has been defined by the idea of growth. But what is growth and how is it related to carbon energy? How did we come to believe that burning fossil fuels created a collective world whose defining character has been to grow? If we want a world without growth, or with a different form of growth, less destructive of Earth systems and species of life, we must ask how growth came to be associated with the extraction and burning of fossil fuels.

<a id="ch08-0011"></a>

答案乍看显而易见。如本书前几章所探讨的，过去两个世纪里，煤炭以及后来石油和天然气的开发，提供了集中且迅速增加的能源来源，为制造业、工业化农业、机械化战争、城市扩张以及贸易和帝国的领土扩张提供动力。这种增长可以被衡量为某种物质的东西。它表现为不断扩大的商品数量、建筑数目、运输里程、人口规模和资本主义生产控制下的领土面积。

The answer seems at first obvious. Over the last two centuries, as earlier chapters of this book explored, the exploitation of coal and later oil and natural gas made available a concentrated and rapidly increasing source of energy that fuelled manufacturing, industrial agriculture, mechanised warfare, the expansion of cities, and the territorial enlargement of trade and empire. This growth could be measured as something material. It appeared in the form of the expanding quantities of goods, numbers of buildings, miles of transportation, size of populations, and areas of territory under the control of capitalist production.

<a id="ch08-0012"></a>

但这个显而易见的答案并不有用。它误解了能源的历史，也误解了经济增长的本质。它带有技术决定论的毛病，仿佛历史本来不可能有其他样子——仿佛它是由人类进步和技术发展的不可避免性所驱动的。我们无法在此基础上建立应对气候危机的政治。

But the obvious answer is not a useful one. It misunderstands both the history of energy and the nature of economic growth. It suffers from a technical determinism, as if history could not have been otherwise – as if it were driven by the very unavoidability of human progress and technical development. We cannot build a politics to address the climate crisis on these terms.

<a id="ch08-0013"></a>

相反，让我们从可以说气候危机开始的地方开始，不是两百年前，而是二十世纪中叶。这场危机与过去六七十年的大加速有着特殊关系，因而与我们加速的化石燃料消费有着特殊关系，尤其与 1990 年代以来最近三十年更快的加速有关。自工业时代开始以来燃烧的所有化石燃料中，超过 80% 是 1960 年以后燃烧的，所有燃烧量的一半以上是 1990 年以后燃烧的。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-002"></a>[2](#note-ch8-002)但“经济”的增长与化石燃料及大气碳生产扩大之间的这种关系，需要一种新的解释。

Let us begin, instead, where the climate crisis itself can be said to begin, not 200 years ago but in the mid-twentieth century. The crisis has a particular relationship to the great acceleration of the last six or seven decades, and thus to our accelerated consumption of fossil fuels, and especially to the more rapid acceleration of just the last three decades, since the 1990s. More than 80 per cent of all fossil fuels burned since the start of the industrial age have been burned since 1960, and more than half of them since 1990.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-002"></a>[2](#note-ch8-002) But that relation – between the growth of ‘the economy’ and the expanding production of fossil fuels and atmospheric carbon – needs a new explanation.

<a id="ch08-0014"></a>

我们不应把增长问题定位于化石燃料的燃烧，也不应定位于需要化石燃料的技术装置（如蒸汽机、发电站或汽车）的历史，而应定位于另一种技术装置的发明：经济。正如我们在[第五章](#ch05-0001)所见，经济学家直到 1930 年代才开始使用“the economy”（作为对象的经济整体）这一说法（“economy”一词<a id="page-264"></a>〔原书第264页〕不带定冠词使用时的旧含义非常不同，如[第四章](#ch04-0001)所解释的）。它到 1950 年代才广泛使用。统计学家设计了一套协议和假定，用来估算这个新对象的规模和扩张，概括起来就是国内生产总值即 GDP 的衡量。经济不只是已经存在之物的新词。它标示了一个新的政治和计算对象，第一次被理解为自身存在的实体，一个由可识别、可衡量的关系组成的稳定领域。这一装置组装得如此迅速，以至于到 1950 年代中期，经济学家、政治学家和历史学家开始想象“经济”一直存在，尽管他们不过在一二十年前才得知它的存在。

We should locate the problem of growth not in the burning of fossil fuels or the history of technical apparatuses that demanded them, such as the steam engine, the electrical power station, or the automobile, but in the invention of a different technical apparatus, the economy. As we saw in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001), economists began to use the term ‘the economy’ only in the 1930s (older meanings of the word ‘economy’, <a id="page-264-en"></a>〔原书第264页〕used without the definite article, as [chapter 4](#ch04-0001) explained, were very different). It came into widespread use only in the 1950s. Statisticians devised a set of protocols and assumptions for estimating the size and expansion of this new object, summarised as the measurement of the gross domestic product, or GDP. The economy was not just a new word for what already existed. It designated a new object of politics and calculation, understood for the first time as an entity in itself, a stable domain composed of identifiable and measurable relations. So rapidly was this device assembled that, by the mid-1950s, economists, political scientists, and historians started to imagine that ‘the economy’ had always existed, even though they had learned of its existence only ten or twenty years before.

<a id="ch08-0015"></a>

应当指出，经济这一对象的出现主要发生于欧美。当欧洲人和美国人开始围绕本国经济的生产和衡量来管理政治生活时，并非每个国家都一开始同意跟随。这些分歧可能影响深远。如[第五章](#ch05-0001)所述，1956 年苏伊士危机由阿斯旺高坝融资争端引发，导致以色列、英国和法国入侵埃及、试图推翻其政府，部分就是一场关于新经济计算形式的分歧——帝国列强通过世界银行要求埃及政府采用这些形式。渐渐地，世界银行和其他国际机构要求全球南方国家采用这些方法，以产生看似可比的 GDP 数字和其他经济生活衡量指标。但这些衡量的适当性和可比性始终有待质疑。而且，通过衡量和管理经济及其增长来治理人口的方式，在不同地方并未采取相同形式或具有相同意义。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-003"></a>[3](#note-ch8-003)

The emergence of the economy, it should be noted, was largely a Euro-American story. When Europeans and Americans started managing their political life around the production and measurement of their economy, not every country agreed at first to follow. These disagreements could be far-reaching. As [chapter 5](#ch05-0001) noted, the 1956 Suez Crisis, triggered by a dispute over the financing of the Aswan High Dam, and leading to the invasion of Egypt by Israel, Britain, and France in an attempt to remove its government from power, was, in part, a disagreement over the new forms of economic calculation that the imperial powers, through the World Bank, demanded that the Egyptian government adopt. Gradually, the World Bank and other international institutions required the countries of the Global South to adopt the methods that produced what seemed comparable figures for GDP and other measures of economic life. But the suitability and comparability of these measurements was always open to question. And the mode of governing populations through the measurement and management of the economy and its growth did not take the same form or significance in different places.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-003"></a>[3](#note-ch8-003)

<a id="ch08-0016"></a>

GDP 不是物质财富的衡量。它衡量的是货币通过账户的流通。账户有三类：企业、政府和家庭。家庭被想象为微型企业，各有年度收入、支出和利润水平——一种剩余，被误导性地视为经济借以扩张的“投资”或“资本”来源，其假定是资本乃过去储蓄之物，而非从未来榨取。这些账户被呈现为统计抽象，因而是一种再现，但它再现的不是物质财富，而是收入。从较早计算国民<a id="page-265"></a>〔原书第265页〕财富的尝试转向计算总收入，似乎引入了一种分离——增长衡量与物质扩张之间的分离。随着经济的发明，一个国家如今可以在不扩张领土、不增加人口、甚至也许不生产更多物质商品的情况下实现“增长”。人们或许以为这种脱钩会引起对增长观念的质疑。但恰恰相反，资本主义现代性不是由扩张与收缩、贫困化与改善的周期、而是由无休止、不间断、指数增长的逻辑所界定的观念，变得自明。无止境的经济增长成为政治福祉和进步的衡量标准本身。

The GDP is not a measure of material wealth. Rather, it measures the circulation of money through accounts. The accounts are of three kinds: those of business firms, government, and households. Households are imagined as miniature businesses, each with an annual level of income, expenditure, and profit – a surplus that is seen misleadingly as the source of ‘investment’ or ‘capital’ through which the economy expands, on the assumption that capital is something saved from the past, not extracted from the future. The accounts are presented as a statistical abstraction, and thus as a representation, and not of material wealth, but of income. The change from older attempts to calculate national <a id="page-265-en"></a>〔原书第265页〕wealth to the calculation of gross income appeared to introduce a separation – between the measurement of growth and physical expansion. With the invention of the economy, a country could now ‘grow’ without expanding its territory, enlarging its population, or even, perhaps, producing more material goods. One might expect this decoupling to raise questions about the idea of growth. But, on the contrary, the notion that capitalist modernity was defined not by cycles of expansion and contraction, of impoverishment and improvement, but by the logic of endless, uninterrupted, and exponential growth became self-evident. Economic growth without end became the very measure of political well-being and progress.

<a id="ch08-0017"></a>

从一开始，开始应用这些新指标体系的统计学家、规划者和预算官员就意识到其局限。无限指数增长的观念荒谬，甚至仅从数学上看也是如此。画成图表曲线，代表经济增长的上升线迅速接近垂直。如[第五章](#ch05-0001)所述，其荒谬性通过采用对数尺度绘制纵轴（显示 GDP 增长）的惯例而部分被掩盖。对数图把上升曲线变成一条平缓得多的直线，使其路径显得几乎合理。GDP 计算方式的缺陷也被注意到。这些缺陷的清单长得惊人，并日益为人熟悉。几十年来，赫尔曼·戴利等生态经济学家、凯西·吉布森和朱莉·格雷厄姆等女性主义学者、让·加德雷和弗洛朗丝·雅尼-卡特里丝等发展替代财富衡量的异端经济学家，以及许多其他人，都探讨过这些问题。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-004"></a>[4](#note-ch8-004)最近，乔治·卡利斯、杰森·希克尔和其他几位学者的一系列重要著作提出了去增长观念，或“优先考虑福祉、公平与可持续性”的以更少的物质消耗过好生活的方式，以此作为与把增长当作集体生活目标之做法决裂的手段。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-005"></a>[5](#note-ch8-005)

From the start, the statisticians, planners, and budget officials who began to apply these new metrics were aware of their limitations. The idea of infinite exponential growth is absurd, even just mathematically. Drawn as the curve of a graph, the ascending line that represents the growth of the economy rapidly approaches the vertical. As mentioned in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001), its absurdity was partially disguised by adopting the convention of plotting the vertical axis, showing the increase in GDP, on a logarithmic scale. The log plot converted an ascending curve into a straight and much flatter line, making its path appear almost reasonable. Flaws in the way GDP is calculated were also noted. The list of these is astonishingly long, and increasingly familiar. Over several decades, ecological economists such as Herman Daly, feminist scholars such as Kathy Gibson and Julie Graham, heterodox economists developing alternative measures of wealth such as Jean Gadrey and Florence Jany-Catrice, and many others, have explored these issues.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-004"></a>[4](#note-ch8-004) More recently, an important series of works by Giorgos Kallis, Jason Hickel, and several others have proposed the idea of degrowth, or modes of living well with less, by ‘prioritizing wellbeing, equity and sustainability’, as a means of breaking with the use of growth as the goal of collective life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-005"></a>[5](#note-ch8-005)

<a id="ch08-0018"></a>

正如这些著作所指出的，GDP 作为福祉衡量是失败的：它排除大部分无酬劳动，尤其是持家、育儿和人类再生产的劳动——一种性别化、种族化的排除；它把有害支出也算作对繁荣的贡献，例如成瘾性或不健康消费，或军费开支、警察暴力和监禁的成本——因而第二次被种族化。它不重视闲暇，除非闲暇被付费。它不重视货物的可靠性或对浪费的避免，也不计入减少生产性资产价值的磨损。它把医疗和心理治疗支出<a id="page-266"></a>〔原书第266页〕、维持极端不平等的财产和收入获取渠道所需的法律服务和会计程序支出，以及修复全球变暖后果造成的损害支出，都当作正面因素——而且这样做时，没有充分评价那些可能来自更好照护个人、社群或地球的改善。除资源储量逐渐减少时开采成本上升之外，它不赋予有限资源耗竭任何价值。它也不对生物多样性丧失、物种灭绝或其他地球生命代价进行估值，除非这些代价已由人类对过程或材料的控制主张作为金融资产定价。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-006"></a>[6](#note-ch8-006)

As these works point out, GDP fails as a measure of well-being: it excludes most unpaid labour, in particular the labour of householding, childcare, and human reproduction – a gendered and racialised exclusion; it includes as contributions to prosperity harmful expenses, such as addictive or unhealthy consumption or the cost of arms spending, police violence, and incarceration – so is racialised a second time. It does not value leisure, except when this is paid for. It does not value the reliability of goods or the avoidance of waste, or account for the wear and tear that reduces the value of productive assets. It treats as positive <a id="page-266-en"></a>〔原书第266页〕the expenditure on medical treatment and psychological care; on the legal services and accounting procedures required to maintain grossly unequal access to property and income; and on repairing damage from the effects of global heating – and it does this in ways that do not adequately value improvements that might have arisen from better provision for care of the person, the community, or the planet. It attributes no value to the exhaustion of finite resources, beyond the increased cost of extraction as reserves are run down. And it includes no valuation of the loss of biodiversity, of species extinction, or other costs to life on Earth beyond those priced by human claims to the control of processes or materials as financial assets.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-006"></a>[6](#note-ch8-006)

<a id="ch08-0019"></a>

半个多世纪前，正统经济学家已被迫回应环保主义者的批评，他们为该衡量的有用性辩护。威廉·诺德豪斯和詹姆斯·托宾在 1972 年写道，如果 GDP 未能衡量环境和其他成本，那是由于“价格体系的缺陷”。补救办法将是生产更好的价格。至于“全球生态灾难”的危险，他们补充说，例如“我们将融化极地冰盖、淹没世界所有海港”的风险，对于“此类事件的原因和可能性似乎存在极大不确定性”。因此他们提出，“单靠经济学能说的非常少”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-007"></a>[7](#note-ch8-007)正统经济学家能够以确定性谈论经济，依赖于生产这种必要的不确定性和无知。

Orthodox economists, already forced to respond more than half a century ago to criticisms from environmentalists, defended the usefulness of the measure. If GDP failed to measure environmental and other costs, this was due to ‘a defect of the pricing system’, wrote William Nordhaus and James Tobin in 1972. The remedy would be to produce better prices. As for the danger of ‘global ecological catastrophes’, they added, such as the risk ‘that we will melt the polar icecaps and flood all the world’s seaports’, there seemed to be ‘great uncertainty about the causes and likelihood of such occurrences’. As a result, they proposed, there was ‘very little that economics alone can say’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-007"></a>[7](#note-ch8-007) The certainty with which orthodox economists could speak about the economy was dependent on producing this necessary uncertainty and ignorance.

<a id="ch08-0020"></a>

这些长期为人熟知的衡量经济及其增长的缺陷，使我们对这一概念的正常化更加不可思议。这些缺陷可以与第二种对经济增长的批评区分开来，后者通常更紧密地依托马克思主义思想传统：增长作为对自然日益加剧的榨取。

These long-familiar shortcomings in the measurement of the economy and its growth make our normalisation of the concept even more remarkable. Such flaws can be distinguished from a second kind of criticism of economic growth, usually drawing more closely on Marxian traditions of thought: growth as the increasing extraction from nature.

<a id="ch08-0021"></a>

对后者来说，增长问题不在于衡量或错误衡量的实践，不在于我们如何评价或贬低自然和其他非经济物品，而在于资本主义的底层本质。在这种观点的许多版本中——南希·弗雷泽或杰森·摩尔的著作就是好例子——资本主义的独特之处在于其榨取主义。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-008"></a>[8](#note-ch8-008)资本主义作为组织关系的特定模式而产生和扩张，这种关系不仅存在于人类之间，也存在于人类与自然世界之间。如果把资本主义理解为通过支配劳动生产商品来扩张价值和占有剩余，那么它依赖于把材料加工成商品的无限扩张。资本主义通过进一步的空间扩张和加强对自然材料的开发<a id="page-267"></a>〔原书第267页〕来解决自身危机；自然提供了不断扩张的储备，被视为“廉价”或免费的馈赠——阿丽莎·巴蒂斯托尼探讨过政治思想中的这一主题。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-009"></a>[9](#note-ch8-009)既然资本无情地寻求自我扩张，资本主义就依赖物质增长，而增长总是以自然资源为代价。无论怎样重新定义 GDP 或更好地衡量成本，都无法使资本主义摆脱这种破坏性、不可持续的自然关系。增长不是再现和评价资源方式不当的问题。它是资本主义生产方式底层的剥削动力。

For the latter, the problem of growth lies not in practices of measurement or mismeasurement, of how we value or disvalue nature and other noneconomic goods, but in the underlying nature of capitalism. What distinguishes capitalism, in many versions of this view – the work of Nancy Fraser or Jason Moore would be good examples – is its extractivism.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-008"></a>[8](#note-ch8-008) Capitalism came into being and expands as a specific mode of organising the relationship, not only among humans, but between humans and the natural world. If capitalism is understood as the expansion of value and appropriation of surplus through the command of labour to produce commodities, this depends on the endless expansion of the processing of materials into goods. Capitalism addresses its own <a id="page-267-en"></a>〔原书第267页〕crises through further spatial expansion and increased exploitation of materials from nature, which provide a constantly expanding reserve of what it treats as ‘cheap’ or free gifts – a theme in political thought that Alyssa Battistoni has explored.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-009"></a>[9](#note-ch8-009) Since capital relentlessly seeks its own self-expansion, capitalism depends upon material growth, and growth is always at the expense of natural resources. No amount of redefinition of GDP or better measurement of costs will free capitalism from this destructive and unsustainable relationship to nature. Growth is not a problem of improper ways of representing and valuing resources. It is the exploitative dynamic at the base of the capitalist mode of production.

<a id="ch08-0022"></a>

### 经济的效果

### The Effect of the Economy

<a id="ch08-0023"></a>

我们可以把这两种增长研究路径概括为一个问题：以 GDP 衡量的“经济”是一种*错误*的再现，还是*仅仅*一种再现。一边是那些人——例如有影响力的凯特·拉沃斯——主张我们应以替代性福祉计算取代以 GDP 衡量的增长指标，不一定反增长，但至少不预设支持或反对增长的立场。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-010"></a>[10](#note-ch8-010)另一边是资本理论家——近例可参见后殖民历史学家安德鲁·萨托里——他们认为二十世纪的“经济”概念相对不重要，因为它*仅仅*是一种再现。萨托里主张，这可以与另一种观念过程相对照，即“抽象”，特别是所谓实在抽象——劳动、财产、价值——它们主要出现于十九世纪，对资本的运作至关重要。

One could summarise the two approaches to growth as a question of whether ‘the economy’ as measured by GDP is a *mis*representation, or a *mere* representation. On one side are those – for example, the influential Kate Raworth – who propose that we should replace the metric of growth, as measured by GDP, with alternative calculations of wellbeing, and become, not necessarily anti-growth, but at least agnostic about it.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-010"></a>[10](#note-ch8-010) On the other side, the theorists of capital – see the postcolonial historian Andrew Sartori for a recent example – who suggest that the twentieth-century conception of ‘the economy’ is relatively unimportant, because it is *only* a representation. It can be contrasted, he argues, with a different kind of ideational process, that of ‘abstraction’ and specifically the so-called real abstractions – labour, property, value – that emerged mainly in the nineteenth century and are fundamental to the working of capital.

<a id="ch08-0024"></a>

无论采取哪一边，这场争论中双方的立场都有一个弱点，而且是同一个弱点。他们主张，经济虽然指涉某种真实的东西，但它是一种再现。或者说，它是一种再现、一种纯粹的约定，*因为*它指涉别的某种东西，指涉一种物质现实——物质生产过程。

Whichever side one takes, both positions in this argument suffer from a weakness – and the same one. While it refers to something real, they argue, the economy is a representation. Or rather, it is a representation, a mere convention, *because* it refers to something else, to a material reality – to a process of material production.

<a id="ch08-0025"></a>

尽管这些论点很有力量，这里所遵循的都不是。它们都没有考察“经济”为何如此晚近才被发明、它做了什么工作，或其政治臣服和控制的形式。经济既不是多数主流学术所设想的那种描绘物质现实的方式，也不是其（错误）再现、一种（错误衡量的）统计的纯粹产物。相反，正如[第四章](#ch04-0001)所考察的，它是<a id="page-268"></a>〔原书第268页〕一种制造物质世界与其再现相对立这一*效果*的特定方式：即以实体与金融对立的形式，或以物质世界与仅仅指涉它、管理它的账户、价格和金融交换体系相对立的形式。这种效果，这种安排事物与表象的秩序模式，这种装置或图表，正是资本主义的、或者说资本化攫取模式得以运作的机制。

Despite their power, neither of these arguments is the one followed here. Neither examines the reason why ‘the economy’ was invented so recently, the work it does, or its form of political subjection and control. The economy is neither a way of depicting a material reality, as most mainstream scholarship assumes, nor its (mis)representation, a mere product of (mismeasured) statistics. It is, rather, as [chapter 4](#ch04-0001) examined, <a id="page-268-en"></a>〔原书第268页〕a specific way of producing the *effect* of the material world versus its representation: namely in the form of the real versus the financial, or the material world and the system of accounts, prices, and financial exchanges that merely reference it and manage it. This effect, this mode of ordering things and appearances, this apparatus or diagram, is precisely the mechanism through which the capitalist, or rather the capitalising, mode of capture has come to operate.

<a id="ch08-0026"></a>

注意这里使用的两个术语：“效果”和“资本化”。“效果”比抽象之类更宏大的术语更有用，部分原因是它能把我们的注意力引向许多细小、看似微不足道的技术政治实践——例如政府办公室里金融统计的汇编，或在此前时代大型零售公司收银机的记账；或者如[第三章](#ch03-0001)所述，银行业从“产业”中逐渐分离的过程：两者起初是商人生活中相互关联的两个方面，后来才在建筑、立法和职业层面彼此分离。“效果”兼有纯粹表象和实效性的含义。它使我们注意抽象与它所抽象之物之间始终不稳定的差异——而“抽象”一词一旦不再用作表示过程的动词性名词，通常无法做到这一点。

Note the use of two terms here, ‘effect’ and ‘capitalising’: the term ‘effect’ is more useful than a grander term like abstraction, partly because it can direct our attention to many of the minor, seemingly insignificant technopolitical practices – for example, the compilation of financial statistics in government offices, or, in a previous era, the record keeping by cash registers of large retail companies; or, as [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) recounted, the gradual process by which banking houses were separated from ‘industry’, architecturally, legislatively, and professionally, after starting as two interconnected aspects of merchant life. The term ‘effect’ carries the meaning of both mere appearance and effectiveness. It draws our attention to the always unstable difference between an abstraction and what it abstracts from – something the term abstraction, once it ceases to be used as a verbal noun indicating a process, usually fails to do.

<a id="ch08-0027"></a>

这一论点与先前关于国家作为一种效果的论点相似。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-011"></a>[11](#note-ch8-011)但它有所不同，因为效果的生成方式不同。与国家的效果相比，经济的效果以不同方式治理我们。虽然经济像国家或社会一样是另一种抽象模式——我们通过指称它的捷径而看不到其组装过程——但有一种抽象化、构造差异的效果是经济生产所特有的。在这种模式的特殊性质中，我们必须理解并拆解增长问题。

This argument is analogous to one made previously about the state, as an effect.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-011"></a>[11](#note-ch8-011) But it is different, because the effect is produced differently. We are governed differently by the effect of the economy, compared with the effect of the state. While the economy is yet another mode of abstracting, like state, or society, whose process of assembling we fail to see in the shortcut of referencing it, there is an effect of abstracting, of constructing differences, that is particular to the production of the economy. In the specifics of that mode, we have to understand and disassemble the question of growth.

<a id="ch08-0028"></a>

第二，“资本化”一词。如常一样，我们的目标是取代指涉大型对象或结构（如资本主义）的术语，代之以描述反复过程的词语（如资本化）。指称大型、看似难以改变的结构会强化抽象的力量，而关注平凡、重复的程序则能把注意力引向脆弱之处或潜在的中断点。如本书通篇所示，“资本化”指剩余攫取的模式，这种模式不应被理解为对自然的掠夺，甚至也不应被理解为对劳动本身的掠夺，尽管它可能同时利用这两种资源及其他资源：它是对未来的掠夺。把一项资产资本化，是指<a id="page-269"></a>〔原书第269页〕确立对未来延伸的收入流——租金、购买付款、利润、费用、利息等等——控制权的政治—法律模式，然后在当下以折扣价榨取这些收入，从而使未来贫困化，让未来承担全额偿还的负担。

Second, the term capitalising. Our aim, as always, is to replace terms that refer to large objects or structures, like capitalism, with words that describe repetitive processes, such as capitalising. Referencing large, seemingly intractable structures reinforces the powers of abstraction, whereas focusing on mundane, reiterative procedures can draw attention to points of vulnerability or potential disruption. As seen throughout this book, the term ‘capitalising’ refers to the mode of capture of surplus, understood not as predation upon nature, nor even upon human labour per se, although it may make use of both resources, and of others: it is predation upon the future. To capitalise an asset refers to <a id="page-269-en"></a>〔原书第269页〕the politico-legal mode of establishing control of flows of revenue stretching into the future – rents, purchases, profits, fees, interest payments, and more – and then extracting them at a discounted price in the present, thereby impoverishing the future, on which the burden of full repayment is placed.

<a id="ch08-0029"></a>

这种掠夺如何运作？当下与未来的关系——对把“经济”理解为支配装置至关重要——提供了双重攫取模式，我们将在下文补充第三种。第一，通过财产权或其他权力关系确立对未来资产可靠控制的人，享有稳定的租金、销售款、股息或债务偿还流。然而，正如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)以及[第七章](#ch07-0001)所探讨的，未来收入主张的持有者不必等待未来。如果该主张得到可靠确立，并有法律和市场装置支持——尤其是使主张能够轻易、即时地从一人转让给另一人、因而具有“流动性”的装置——所有者就可以转让他人并立即获得意外之财。每一次主张的转移，例如公司股份交易或衍生品形成时，都会增加一个向未来提出索取的人。第二，也是更有助于理解经济及其表面增长的，购买未来收入主张的人通常可以按折扣获得它。重复前几章的例子：一年后可得的 100 美元收入——来自股息、销售或租金——今天可能以比如 90 美元购得。从未来获得的付款之折价，反映了在确立它时被设计进去的延迟或推迟，以及通过使其提前可用的机制所产生的溢价。购买未来收入，使 90 美元得以在一年内看起来“增长”超过 10%，变成 100 美元。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-012"></a>[12](#note-ch8-012)

How does the predation work? The relation between present and future – essential to grasping the ‘economy’ as an apparatus of domination – offers a double mode of capture, to which we will add a third, below. First, those who establish a viable hold on future assets, through rights of property or other power relations, enjoy a steady stream of rents, sales, dividends, or debt repayments. However, as we explored in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) and again in [chapter 7](#ch07-0001), the possessor of the claim to future revenue does not have to await the future. If the claim is reliably established and supported with legal and market devices, especially devices that make the claim easily and instantly transferable from person to person, and thus ‘liquid’, the owner can transfer it to others and enjoy an immediate windfall. Each successive transfer of the claim, as when corporate shares are traded, or when derivatives are formed, creates an additional claimant on the future. Second, and more important for making sense of the economy and its apparent growth, those who then purchase the claim to future revenue can typically acquire it at a discount. To repeat the example from previous chapters, an income of $100 available in a year’s time – from dividends, sales, or rents – might be purchased today for, say, $90. The discounted price of a payment acquired from the future reflects the delay or postponement engineered in establishing it, and the resulting premium generated through the mechanism that makes it available in advance. The purchase of a future revenue allows the $90 to appear to ‘grow’, over the course of a year, by more than 10 per cent, into the sum of $100.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-012"></a>[12](#note-ch8-012)

<a id="ch08-0030"></a>

我们栖居的世界不是由作为结构的资本主义、而是由作为过程的资本化所界定的。推迟的工程依赖于暴力、掠夺、基础设施、法律和流动性等形式，正是它催生了货币资本的可能性本身，赋予其奇特的增长力量。因此，货币不仅是便利交换或储存财富的手段，更是凭借推迟的秩序、主要作为一种对未来货物或收入的主张而被生产出来的。换言之，货币几乎总是信用货币：它总是指涉并索取更远的东西。它主要由私人商业银行发行（有政府担保作为后盾），所组织的不仅是交换<a id="page-270"></a>〔原书第270页〕或储存，还有对未来施加负担。由于推迟的效力、它所促成的贴现过程，以及货币创造被限制在私人的、营利性银行和金融公司手中（如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所见），货币的生产伴随着对“利息”收费的权力。（我们通常说货币“赚取”利息，把其增值能力自然化。）几乎所有货币都是信用，而所有信用，由于有按复利收取利息的权力，都必须偿还，且成本呈指数增长。例如在 3% 的利率下，货币成本二十四年翻倍；在 6% 下则十二年翻倍。但这只是另一种说法：那些制造信用货币、或能够获得信用货币制造能力的人，可以按折扣购买未来——十二年后可得的 100 美元收入，今天可以按 50 美元的折价购得。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-013"></a>[13](#note-ch8-013)

We inhabit a world that is defined, not by capitalism as a structure, but by capitalising as a process. The engineering of postponement, dependent on forms of violence, predation, infrastructure, law, and liquidity, gives rise to the very possibility of money capital, awarding it its curious power to grow. Thus, money is not merely a means to facilitate exchange or to store wealth, but is produced, thanks to the order of postponement, mainly as a claim on a future good or revenue. Money, in other words, is almost always credit money: it always refers to and claims something further. Issued largely by private commercial banks (backed by government guarantees), it organises not merely exchange <a id="page-270-en"></a>〔原书第270页〕or storage, but the encumbering of the future. Thanks to the effectiveness of postponement, the process of discounting that it enables, and the restricting of money creation to private, profit-making banks and financial firms, as we saw in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), the production of money comes with the power to impose a charge for ‘interest’. (We commonly refer to this as the money ‘earning’ interest, naturalising its ability to increase.) Almost all money is credit, and all credit, due to the power of charging interest, at a compound rate, has to be repaid, at a cost that increases exponentially. At 3 per cent, for example, the cost of money doubles in twenty-four years; at 6 per cent, in twelve years. But this is just another way of saying that those who manufacture or have access to the manufacturing of credit money can purchase the future at a discount – an income of $100 available twelve years from now can be purchased today at the discounted price of $50.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-013"></a>[13](#note-ch8-013)

<a id="ch08-0031"></a>

利率和贴现率是描述同一现象的两种方式，从同一架望远镜的两端观看（重提前一章的光学隐喻）。利率从当下向前看，计算一笔现款在未来某点的价值。贴现率从未来那一点出发向后推算，计算如果考虑到货币价值随时间“增长”的能力，那笔未来款项今天值多少。在一种循环推理过程中，一个概念常常用另一个概念来解释。于是，对未来收入价值的贴现被归因于货币赚取利息的“自然”过程。但事实上这一切都不是自然的。两种比率都源于权力关系，以本书探讨的所有方式。可靠地主张未来资产的权力——依赖于推迟的安排以及排除或减少他人主张的能力——与通过银行体系“汇集”这类主张使其流动的机制相结合，就是能够在当下出售该主张的来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-014"></a>[14](#note-ch8-014)未来主张出售时的折扣，随后被归因于货币赚取利息的力量，而不是归因于这些攫取、推迟和汇集的机制。

The interest rate and the discount rate are two ways of describing the same phenomenon, seen from opposite ends of the same telescope (to repeat the optical metaphor from the previous chapter). The interest rate looks forwards from the present and calculates the value of a present sum of money at a future point. The discount rate starts from that future point and works backwards, calculating what that future sum would be worth today if one allowed for the power of money to ‘grow’ in value over time. In a process of circular reasoning, one concept is often explained in terms of the other. Thus, discounting the value of future income is ascribed to the ‘natural’ process by which money earns interest. But none of this, in fact, is natural. Both rates arise from relations of power, in all the ways this book has explored. The power to reliably claim a future asset, dependent on the arrangement of postponement and the ability to exclude or reduce the claims of others, combined with the mechanism that ‘pools’ such claims through the banking system to make them liquid, is the source of the ability to sell the claim in the present.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-014"></a>[14](#note-ch8-014) The discount at which the future claim is sold is then ascribed, not to these mechanisms of capture, postponement, and pooling, but to the power of money to earn interest.

<a id="ch08-0032"></a>

我们关于货币或资本的朴素日常观念——标准经济理论所复制的一种观念——有助于遮蔽这种攫取未来的过程。标准观点不把资本视为对未来付款的控制形式，而如我们在[第三章](#ch03-0001)所见，视为从过去储蓄起来的资金。人们想象这些储蓄存放在银行里，银行再贷给企业家，通常用于投资“机器”或“技术”以赚更多钱。在一些<a id="page-271"></a>〔原书第271页〕想象中，以及在许多经济学家的模型中，机器本身成为“资本”的代表。利息支付于是可以被描述为付给那些表面上的“储蓄”被用来增长更多财富者的报酬——而不是享有国家授予的特权和保护、垄断信用创造的金融机构所收取的租金。

The obscuring of this process of capturing the future is aided by our naive, everyday conception of money or capital, a conception reproduced in standard economic theory. The standard view thinks of capital not as a form of control of future payments but, as we saw in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), as funds saved up from the past. These savings are stored in banks, it is imagined, which then lend them to entrepreneurs, typically to invest in the ‘machinery’ or ‘technology’ required to make more money. In some <a id="page-271-en"></a>〔原书第271页〕imaginations, and in many economists’ models, the machinery itself comes to represent ‘capital’. The payment of interest can then be described as the reward paid to those whose apparent ‘savings’ have been used to grow more wealth – rather than the rent charged by the financial institutions that, thanks to their state-granted privileges and protections, monopolize the creation of credit.

<a id="ch08-0033"></a>

事实上，除了为组织主张者带来的收益和按折扣购得主张所得的利润之外，还存在第三种由支配未来而产生的攫取模式。随着未来变得更确定或面临更多风险，对未来付款的主张在价值上始终可能发生波动。当然，风险可能反映一个资本化主张可能崩溃，摧毁对未来的权力所创造的全部资本。更常见的是，随着主张因银行、货币市场和各种计算装置的扩展而变得更具流动性，利润可以来自购买主张本身价值的涨跌前景，而非主张本身。于是，由基础资产衍生的流动性本身，可以成为被攫取的资产。如[第一章](#ch01-0001)所指出的，这类“衍生品”本身并不新鲜。1970 年代以来，一套类似物理学家熟悉的“热”方程、用纸笔推导出的定价公式——布莱克—斯科尔斯—默顿模型——的运用，使人们有可能把附着于任何金融工具的风险与基础资产分开“定价”。这些衍生品的价值不一定计算得十分精确，但足以令人信服，从而能够以更大规模把这类风险作为资产营销。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-015"></a>[15](#note-ch8-015)随着其制造增加，从“套利”中获利的机会也成倍增加，套利指“同一”事物在不同时间或不同地点价格的差异。正如罗伯特·迈斯特所解释的，制造流动性本身的梯度，成为这种差异的来源，从而成为攫取剩余之机会的来源。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-016"></a>[16](#note-ch8-016)与所有此类攫取一样，大部分收益将作为贡赋或税收强加于人，如我们在前几章所见，由生产、使用或维护未来资产——其收入已被攫取——的人支付。

There is, in fact, a third mode of capture that arises from the command of the future, besides the gain for those who organise the claim and the profit from acquiring it at a discount. Claims to future payments are always open to fluctuations in value, as the future becomes more certain or more subject to risk. Of course, the risk may reflect the fact that a capitalising claim might collapse, destroying the entire capital that a power over the future created. More frequently, as a claim becomes more liquid, thanks to the building out of banking, money markets, and calculative devices, profits can be made by purchasing, not the claim itself, but the prospect of its increase or decrease in value. Thus, the liquidity itself, derived from the underlying asset, can become an asset to be captured. Such ‘derivatives’, as pointed out in [chapter 1](#ch01-0001), are in themselves nothing new. The deployment from the 1970s of a pricing formula similar to the ‘heat’ equation familiar to physicists, and worked out with pen and paper, the Black–Scholes–Merton model, made it possible to ‘price’ the risk attached to any financial instrument separately from the underlying asset. The value of these derivatives was not necessarily calculated with great accuracy, but with sufficient persuasiveness to allow marketing such risks as assets on an even larger scale.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-015"></a>[15](#note-ch8-015) As their manufacture increases, the opportunities multiply to profit from ‘arbitrage’, meaning the difference in price of the ‘same’ thing at different moments in time or different locations. Manufacturing the very gradients in liquidity, as Robert Meister explains, becomes the source of this difference, and thus of the opportunity to capture surplus.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-016"></a>[16](#note-ch8-016) As with all such capture, the majority of the gain will be imposed as a tribute or tax, as we saw in earlier chapters, to be paid by those who produce, use, or maintain the future asset whose revenue has been captured.

<a id="ch08-0034"></a>

这种金融资产的增殖没有在“经济”的计算中得到恰当衡量。但这并不降低经济生产的用处。恰恰相反，即使经济作为多数人福祉的衡量越来越不适当，由于这一点以及我们提到的所有其他原因，它作为稳定力量反而愈加重要，因为它保障了可预测的未来<a id="page-272"></a>〔原书第272页〕，而资本化和贴现越来越依赖这样的未来。事实上，正如迈斯特所示，在 2007—8 年全球金融危机之类的事件中，“经济”可能“爆炸”的风险，恰恰成为那些从风险买卖中获利者可以挥舞的威胁。迈斯特建议，更好地理解这种炸毁经济的威胁，以及“经济”的稳定效果对金融业所代表的未被计算的价值，可以为更民主地质疑攫取未来的权力提供基础。

This proliferation of financial assets is not properly measured in calculations of ‘the economy’. But this does not reduce the usefulness of the production of the economy. On the contrary, even as the economy becomes less appropriate as a measure of most people’s wellbeing, for this and all the other reasons we have mentioned, it grows in importance as a stabilising force that secures the predictable future <a id="page-272-en"></a>〔原书第272页〕on which capitalising and discounting increasingly rely. Indeed, as Meister shows, the risk that the ‘economy’ might ‘explode’ becomes, in episodes such as the 2007–8 global financial crisis, precisely the threat that can be wielded by those who profit from the buying and selling of risk. A better understanding of this threat to blow up the economy, and the uncounted value that the stabilising effect of ‘the economy’ represents for the financial industry, Meister suggests, could provide the basis for a more democratic contestation of the power of the capture of the future.

<a id="ch08-0035"></a>

把资本化作为一个过程来关注，可以避免许多关于未来攫取模式增殖之研究面临的陷阱——那些通过金融化观念把握这些模式的研究。越来越多人的生活受到日益沉重的债务负担支配：在许多全球南方国家，债务主要在国家层面产生，并通过政府紧缩计划强加于个体家庭；而在多数全球北方国家，则主要发生在个人层面。在后者中，住房抵押贷款、学生贷款、汽车租赁、信用卡、私人医疗费用以及育儿和养老费用——所有这些都使生活的很大部分成为一份持续且不断扩大的还款时间表。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-017"></a>[17](#note-ch8-017)然而，金融化观念通常依赖于金融与“实体”经济之间的区分。我们很快就会看到，真实之物与纯粹金融之物之间的这种区分，是经济发明所产生的最强大效果之一。这一效果与其说通过区分两者来运作，不如说通过变出对金融的极其片面的理解——脱离刚刚描述的所有推迟和产品制造工作——以及同样片面的实体概念来运作。

The focus on capitalising as a process allows one to avoid the pitfall that faces many studies of the proliferation of modes of capture of the future – those that grasp them through the idea of financialisation. The lives of increasing numbers of people are governed by the growing burden of debt, whether incurred predominantly at the national level in many countries of the South, and imposed on individual households through programmes of government austerity, or mainly at the personal level, in most countries of the North. Among the latter, home mortgages, student loans, car leases, credit cards, private healthcare charges, and the costs of childcare and elder care – all these set up so much of life as a continuous and expanding repayment schedule.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-017"></a>[17](#note-ch8-017) However, the notion of financialisation usually depends on a distinction between finance and the ‘real’ economy. We will see shortly how this distinction between what is real and what is merely financial is one of the most powerful effects produced by the invention of the economy. The effect operates not so much by distinguishing the two, but by conjuring a very one-sided understanding of finance, divorced from all the kinds of work of postponement and product manufacture just described, and an equally one-sided conception of the real.

<a id="ch08-0036"></a>

金融化所表达的，我们已能看到只是更广泛过程的一个方面。占主导地位的剩余攫取装置以真实、物质的方式运作，把人和物质的依赖关系安排为“资产”，从中获得持续的投资收入。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-018"></a>[18](#note-ch8-018)这种攫取不仅通过公开的负债形式进行，还通过支配工作生活、电力、水和其他基础设施供应、社交媒体、娱乐、旅行和休闲、医疗等等——所有这些都日益处于投资者所有或股东所有企业的原则之下；并通过把许多国家的住房转变为难以负担的资产，抵押贷款还款占收入的份额越来越大。在这些安排下，每一个攫取未来<a id="page-273"></a>〔原书第273页〕付款的过程——从抵押贷款到租金，从公用事业费到娱乐订阅，从高等教育学费到医疗费用，再到各种消费购买——都成为一项资产，被资本化并转化为收入流，供投资者在当下按折扣获得，由未来按全价偿还——利润作为收费强加给后来的使用者。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-019"></a>[19](#note-ch8-019)

Financialisation expresses what we can already see to be only one aspect of a wider process. The dominant apparatuses for the capture of surplus operate in real, material ways, by arranging human and material dependencies as ‘assets’ from which a continuous investment income is derived.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-018"></a>[18](#note-ch8-018) The capture works not only through overt forms of indebtedness, but through the command of working life, the supply of electrical power, water, and other infrastructure, social media, entertainment, travel and leisure, healthcare, and more, all increasingly under the principle of investor- or shareholder-owned firms; and by the transformation of housing in many countries into unaffordable assets, for which the mortgage payments consume an ever-larger share of earnings. Under these arrangements, every process of capturing future <a id="page-273-en"></a>〔原书第273页〕payments, from mortgages to rents, utility charges to entertainment subscriptions, higher education fees to medical costs, to every kind of consumer purchase, becomes an asset, capitalised and converted to an income stream, available to investors at a discount in the present, to be repaid at full price from the future – a profit imposed as a charge on later users.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-019"></a>[19](#note-ch8-019)

<a id="ch08-0037"></a>

此外，当下生活对多数人来说日益被偿还先前攫取款的重负所累。与此同时，多少拥有资产的家庭——例如能够付清购房款、或通过退休基金建立股市股份所有权的人——开始依赖这些资产价值的上涨，无论是通过房价上涨还是股票价值飙升。由于就业收入水平很少能补偿资本化资产所强加的更高收费，扩大一个家庭资产的价值成为增加财富的主要手段，从而抬高下一代住房和其他服务的成本。即使是中等富裕者，也因此被鼓励通过强化以后来者为代价的生活方式，来保护自己的生活水平。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-020"></a>[20](#note-ch8-020)

Life in the present, moreover, is increasingly burdened for the majority with the repayment of earlier extractions. Meanwhile, households with some access to assets, such as those able to pay off the cost of purchasing a home or to build ownership of shares in stock markets through retirement funds, come to depend on the inflation of the value of such assets – whether through rising house prices or booming share values. With levels of income from employment seldom compensating for the increased charges imposed by capitalised assets, expanding the value of a household’s assets becomes a principal means of increasing wealth, thereby raising the cost of housing and other services for the next generation. Even the modestly well-off are thus encouraged to protect their own standard of life through the intensification of methods of living at the expense of those who come later.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-020"></a>[20](#note-ch8-020)

<a id="ch08-0038"></a>

### 更好的明天

### Better Tomorrows

<a id="ch08-0039"></a>

2011 年，美国最高法院取消了商业公司对竞选进行独立支出的限制。它们如今可以通过政治行动委员会（PAC）汇集无限资金。这些所谓的“超级政治行动委员会”开始协调企业付款，并代表企业开展政治竞选。美国电视喜剧演员斯蒂芬·科尔伯特用这一裁决作讽刺，自己成立了一个政治行动委员会，名为“为了明天会更好的美国人，明天”。“开国元勋们会希望是这样的，”他在电视节目中庆祝这一举动时说，“前提是他们创建的是*公司*，而不只是一个国家。”这一讽刺把两个主题连接起来：当凡勃伦甚至在一个世纪前就已指认的“主导制度”——商业公司——施加非凡影响时，政治生活的问题；以及一种关于推迟的政治修辞。这种修辞通过许诺更美好的未来来承诺福祉和改善，但其效果是延期。这种延期就是我所说的增长的托词。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-021"></a>[21](#note-ch8-021)

In 2011, the US Supreme Court removed the restrictions on independent spending on elections by business corporations. They could now pool their unlimited funds through political action committees, or PACs. The new super PACs, as they became known, began to coordinate corporate payments and run political campaigns on their behalf. The US television comedian Stephen Colbert parodied the Supreme Court decision by setting up a political action committee of his own, named Americans for a Better Tomorrow, Tomorrow. ‘It’s the way [the] founding fathers would have wanted it,’ he said, celebrating the event on his television show, ‘if they had founded *corporations*, instead of just a country.’ The parody connected two themes: the problem of political life when extraordinary influence is exercised by what Veblen, even a century earlier, had already identified as its ‘master institution’, the business corporation; and a political rhetoric of postponement. The rhetoric promises well-being and improvement through the pledge of a better future, but its effect is one of deferral. This deferral is what I have referred to as the alibi of growth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-021"></a>[21](#note-ch8-021)

校注：底本此处将美国最高法院取消公司独立竞选支出限制的裁决记为2011年。美国联邦选举委员会所载Citizens United v. FEC裁决日期为2010年1月21日；这与后文科尔伯特在2011年的讽刺活动是不同时间节点。正文保留底本年份。 https://www.fec.gov/updates/citizens-united-v-fecsupreme-court/ https://www.fec.gov/law/litigation/cu_sc08_opinion.pdf

<a id="ch08-0040"></a>

<a id="page-274"></a>〔原书第274页〕你如何组织和控制一个建立在剥夺未来之上的社会秩序——在其中，当下本身因先前的掠夺而贫困化，而建立哪怕中等财富的唯一手段就是参与同一个剥夺过程？你如何能不断许诺明天会更好，明天？答案是，你建立起一种所谓的效果，称之为经济，并把与未来的关系——即使掠夺和贫困化的过程在扩张——改写为其“增长”的必然运动。这种对资产资本化以及经济作为政治—技术效果的理解，将使我们更好地把握“经济”是如何以及为何被发明的。要理解经济作为治理装置的作用，我们必须先简要回顾资本化的较长历史、它所产生的过度，以及二十世纪中叶管理这些过度的较早方法的崩溃。如我们将会看到，经济作为治理装置的创造，为那场崩溃提供了回应。

<a id="page-274-en"></a>〔原书第274页〕How do you organise and control a social order built upon the deprivation of the future, in which the present is itself impoverished by previous predations, and the only means of building even moderate wealth is to participate in the same process of deprivation? How do you keep promising a better tomorrow, tomorrow? The answer is that you establish, as it were, an effect called the economy and recast the relationship to the future – even as the processes of predation and impoverishment expand – as the inevitable movement of its ‘growth’. This understanding of the capitalising of assets, and of the economy as a politico-technical effect, will allow us to better grasp how and why the ‘economy’ was invented. To understand the role of the economy as an apparatus of government, we must first briefly recap the longer history of capitalisation, the excesses to which it gave rise, and the collapse in the mid-twentieth century of earlier methods of managing that excess. The creation of the economy as an apparatus of government, as we will see, provided a response to that collapse.

<a id="ch08-0041"></a>

首先，回顾。资本化未来收入的方法本身并不新近。今天所谓的金融化资本主义——这些技术也许更为普遍——并非在根本上不同于工业资本主义，也不同于先于它的商业资本主义。甚至在一千年前，如我们在[第二章](#ch02-0001)和[第三章](#ch03-0001)所讨论的，法蒂玛和马穆鲁克时期埃及的商人就与统治家族合作，按类似原则管理农民缴税。变化的是这一过程发生的规模，以及攫取、资产化和资本化未来收入所凭借的装置。

First, the recap. Methods of capitalising future revenue are not in themselves recent. Today’s so-called financialised capitalism, where these techniques are perhaps more widespread, is not somehow fundamentally distinct from industrial capitalism, or the commercial capitalism that preceded it. Even a millennium ago, merchants in Fatimid and Mamluk Egypt, as we discussed in [chapters 2](#ch02-0001) and [3](#ch03-0001), collaborated with the ruling household to manage tax payments by farmers on similar principles. What has changed is the scale on which the process happens, and the apparatuses through which future revenues are captured, assetised, and capitalised.

<a id="ch08-0042"></a>

在这个伊斯兰世界的边缘，在近代早期的欧洲，未来收入的资本化最广泛地设计于远距离贸易中——一种殖民和奴隶制秩序，其运作不仅是为了供应货物，更是为了通过商业和奴隶制产生信用货币，主要形式是汇票。货物和被奴役者的运输和销售，是这种从信用中攫取剩余的装置。如[第三章](#ch03-0001)所探讨的，该体系的危机促成了另一种信用装置——工业工厂——的发展。

On the periphery of that Islamic world, in early modern Europe, the capitalising of future revenues was engineered most extensively in longdistance trade, a colonial and slave-based order that operated not simply to supply goods, but to generate credit money, through commerce and slavery, mainly in the form of bills of exchange. The shipping and sale of goods and enslaved persons was the apparatus for this capture of surplus from credit. A crisis in that system, as [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) explored, led to the development of a different credit apparatus, the industrial factory.

<a id="ch08-0043"></a>

十八世纪末、十九世纪初工业资本主义的出现，应以一种新方式理解。制造业并不代表与商业和信用世界的根本断裂。更重要的是，把雇佣劳动强制投入煤矿和工厂，使我们能以出奇清晰的形式看到信用创造问题，而“经济”是这一问题后来的解决方案。<a id="page-275"></a>〔原书第275页〕经济的发明是对一个有着更长历史的挑战——如何确保和稳定信用货币的生产——的二十世纪回答。

The emergence of industrial capitalism, in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century, should be understood in a new way. Manufacturing did not represent a fundamental break with the world of commerce and credit. More than that, the forcing of wage labour into coal mines and factories enables us to see in surprisingly clear form the problem of credit creation, for which ‘the economy’ was a later solution. <a id="page-275-en"></a>〔原书第275页〕The invention of the economy was a twentieth-century answer to a challenge that had a longer history – how to secure and stabilise the production of credit money.

<a id="ch08-0044"></a>

甚至工厂生产和煤矿开采也是一种资本化方法——一种通过信用货币的精心构建而对未来进行掠夺的形式。把生产转入机械化、后来用煤作动力的工厂，提出了一个独特问题：如何向大量工人支付周薪或月薪——在日常交易很少使用实体货币（硬币或金银）的背景下，几乎所有付款都通过账面信用、期票和汇票处理。如我们所见，支付工资结果不是一个问题，而是一个机会——也许甚至成为把劳动力集中到工厂的主要优势。在没有铸币的情况下支付工人的常见办法，是所谓的“实物工资制”。商人—制造商用账簿上的信用记录、或代金券和筹码支付工资。这些可以在当地商店兑换货物，商店往往属于同一个商人。商人可以从货物制造成本与雇员必须支付的购买价格之间的差额中获利，也可以从这类安排的其他方面获利：消费品的垄断供应；收取利息；通过预先向工人提供必需品、然后按全价记在账上的方式使工人负债；以及提供住房，其租金也从工资中扣除。在按信用支付的劳动与信用货币以购买或租金收费形式返还商人之间，正是这段延迟时间成为利润来源。这使实物工资制和账面信用具有高度剥削性，并导致试图限制它们的法律获得通过。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-022"></a>[22](#note-ch8-022)

Even factory production and coal mining were a method of capitalisation – a form of predation on the future through the elaboration of credit money. The diverting of production into mechanised and later coal-powered factories presented a singular problem: how to pay large numbers of workers a weekly or monthly wage – in a context in which physical money (coin or specie) was little used in everyday transactions, almost every payment being handled through book credit, promissory notes, and bills of exchange. As we saw, the payment of wages turned out to be not a problem but an opportunity – perhaps even becoming a main advantage of concentrating workforces into factories. A common solution for paying workers in the absence of coinage was the system of ‘truck’, as it was called. The merchant-manufacturer paid wages with a credit entry on his books, or with chits or tokens. These could be exchanged for goods at local shops, often owned by the same merchant. Merchants could profit from the difference between the cost of making goods and the price at which the employee had to purchase them, and from other aspects of such arrangements: a monopoly on the supply of consumption items; the charging of interest; the indebting of workers by providing them with necessities in advance that were then charged on the books at full price; and supplying them with housing whose rent was also deducted from wages. The very delay in time between the work that was being paid on credit and the purchase or rental charge with which the credit money was returned to the merchant was a source of profit. This made the use of truck and book credit highly exploitative and led to the passing of laws in an attempt to restrain them.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-022"></a>[22](#note-ch8-022)

<a id="ch08-0045"></a>

立法并没有消除这种通过信用榨取的机器。可以说，今天的雇佣劳动仍然是一种实物工资制。其显著特征是工人仍然以信用货币获得报酬。工资支付形式从商人信用或代币变为纸币，再变为薪金支票，今天则是银行账户之间的电子转账。但工资仍然作为信用货币而产生。而且可以说，它们仍然依赖“公司商店”，信用货币通过公司商店连本带息地返还银行体系。

Legislation did not eliminate this machinery of extraction through credit. Wage labour today, one might say, is still a truck system. Its distinctive feature is that workers are still paid in credit money. The form of the wage payment changed from merchant credit or tokens to banknotes, then to paychecks, and today to electronic transfers between bank accounts. But wages are still brought into being as credit money. And they still depend, so to speak, on the ‘company store’ through which the credit money is paid back into the banking system, with interest.

<a id="ch08-0046"></a>

然而，这家商店不再只是同一个商人控制的单独店铺。它现在是更庞大信用装置的一部分，<a id="page-276"></a>〔原书第276页〕即一整套话语性和非话语性装置，它们组织对工资的攫取，不是通过店铺或市场的简单装置，而是通过产品设计、贸易展、时尚、广告、品牌创造、消费者咨询和比较等技术。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-023"></a>[23](#note-ch8-023)这些机制早在十八世纪就伴随着制造业的发展，为富裕和中产阶层出现。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-024"></a>[24](#note-ch8-024)今天，经由互联网及其界面、平台、社交媒体网站和网红的改造，它们构成了庞大装置，工薪阶层通过它偿还“借来”的工资。工人为商品、服务及其营销广告支付的价格，包含贷款的加价——即对使用货币的收费，资本化货币体系正是依靠这种收费运作。这些界面和平台本身如今成为少数公司的主要利润来源，这些公司最近超过主要全球石油公司（沙特阿美除外），成为世界上资本化估值最高的公司——亚马逊、苹果、Alphabet 和 Meta。这些公司的收入来自对在线广告、数据和电子商务的近乎垄断，日益控制着“商店”的准入，借出的工资正是通过商店被重新捕获。事实上，这些云端巨型企业不仅依赖用户为在线商品和服务付费，还依赖用户生产这些“封地”所拥有的数据。因此，云端用户第二次贡献了自己的劳动，这一次是无偿的，甚至还要支付订阅费。他们的在线互动、浏览、购买和反应，既把自己生产为消费的欲望主体，也生产了巨型企业拥有并资本化的关于这些自我的海量数据。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-025"></a>[25](#note-ch8-025)

However, the store is no longer just a single shop under the control of the same merchant. It is now part of a much larger credit apparatus, <a id="page-276-en"></a>〔原书第276页〕namely the array of apparatuses, discursive and non-discursive, that organise the capture of wages, not through the simple device of a shop or marketplace, but through the technologies of product design, trade shows, fashion, advertising, brand creation, consumer advice, and comparison.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-023"></a>[23](#note-ch8-023) These mechanisms were already appearing in the eighteenth century, for the well-to-do and the middling classes, in tandem with the development of manufacturing.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-024"></a>[24](#note-ch8-024) Today, transformed by the internet, with its interfaces, platforms, social media sites, and influencers, they constitute the vast apparatus through which wage earners repay their ‘loaned’ wage money. The prices workers pay for goods, services, and their marketing and advertising include the mark-up for the loan, the charge for the use of money upon which a capitalising monetary system operates. The interfaces and platforms are themselves now the main source of profit for the handful of corporations that recently surpassed the major global oil firms (other than Saudi Aramco) as the most highly capitalised companies in the world – Amazon, Apple, Alphabet, and Meta. With revenues arising from the near monopoly of online advertising, data, and e-commerce, these firms increasingly control access to the ‘store’ through which loan wages are recaptured. Indeed, the cloud-based megacorporations rely upon their users not only to pay for online goods and services, but to produce the data that these ‘fiefdoms’ own. Thus, users of the cloud contribute their labour a second time, in this case unpaid or even at the cost of a subscription charge. Their online interacting, browsing, purchasing, and reacting manufactures both themselves as the desiring subjects of consumption and the vast data on those selves that the megacorporations own and capitalise.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-025"></a>[25](#note-ch8-025)

<a id="ch08-0047"></a>

早期工业体系中商人银行家创造信用与今天运作的安排之间的差异在于，从十九世纪中叶起，政府引入法规将制造商与银行家、工作场所与银行分开。事实上可以认为，从该世纪下半叶起在世界工业化地区开始出现的那种经济生活形式的独特要素，不再仅仅是工人与生产资料所有权的分离，也不只是生产与市场的表面分离，或所谓经济与政治的分离。它是工作场所和消费场所与货币来源的分离。以前既控制货物制造和营销方式、又提供信用的商人，被分成组织货物<a id="page-277"></a>〔原书第277页〕者和创造货币者。而且，不仅是货物制造和零售依赖信用供给，同样，信用的制造也依赖不断扩展的大规模就业体系，并进而与广告、品味塑造和消费相结合，这些今天日益被企业拥有的云端所垄断。
