The difference between the creation of credit by the merchant banker of the early industrial system and the arrangements operating today is that from the mid-nineteenth century governments introduced regulations to separate manufacturer and banker, workplace and bank. In fact, one could argue, the distinctive element of the form of economic life that began to emerge in the industrialised regions of the world from the second half of that century was no longer simply the separation of workers from the ownership of the means of production, nor the apparent separation of production from the market, nor the so-called economic from the political. It was the separation of the places of work and consumption from the source of money. Merchants who had previously combined the control of how goods were made and marketed with the supply of credit were separated into those who organised goods <a id="page-277-en"></a>〔原书第277页〕and those who created money. And it was not simply that the manufacturing and retailing of goods depended upon a supply of credit, but equally that the manufacturing of credit depended on a widening system of large-scale employment, combined in turn with advertising, taste-making, and consumption, with these increasingly monopolised today by the corporate-owned cloud.

<a id="ch08-0048"></a>

现代货币是银行生产的信用货币。今天银行创造了流通中 95% 以上的货币，几乎全部是银行体系内账户之间的数字转账。银行制造信用货币的能力，取决于一项合理保证：被指定为信贷的资金，日后将在创造它们的体系内被重新指定为购买的还款。事实上，银行发行的“票据”——无论是以钞票、支票还是电子账簿条目的形式——如果不存在通过购买货物、服务、订阅和其他租金来返还它的要求，就不会作为货币运作。

Modern money is bank-produced credit money. Banks today create more than 95 per cent of the money in circulation, almost all of it as digital transfers between accounts within the banking system. The ability of banks to manufacture credit money depends upon a reasonable guarantee that the funds designated as credit will later be redesignated within the system that creates them as repayments for purchases. In fact, the ‘paper’ issued by a bank, in the form of notes, cheques, or electronic ledger entries, would not function as money if there were no requirement to return it through the payment for goods, services, subscriptions, and other rents.

校注：底本“95%以上”未在本段标明地区、时期和货币统计口径。英格兰银行2014年说明中，97%指当时英国广义货币中的银行存款份额；这一常被引用的比例不能直接当作所有国家、所有货币口径的恒定比例。正文保留原数，未作全球比例复算。 https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/quarterly-bulletin/2014/quarterly-bulletin-2014-q1

<a id="ch08-0049"></a>

然而，银行不能只在内部制造货币。要成为真正的资产，银行制造的货币必须经过某种攫取装置，债务人通过该装置向债权人转移一份增量。因此，以工资形式贷出的货币，是相对于工资必须花在其上的购买和收费而被生产并产生效果的。只有对未来支出的保证，才能使银行资产创造得以进行。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-026"></a>[26](#note-ch8-026)信用货币只能作为技术和物质安排的一部分运作，在这种安排中，货币在未来某一点被花掉，并连本带息“返还”银行。对于制造出来支付工资的货币，利息支付不是作为单独费用强加给工人，而是内置于商品价格、服务收费和住房成本之中。这些价格、收费和成本在 GDP 计算中被衡量时，既包括产品的价值，也包括作为企业利润和对作为工资创造的信用货币之利息而强加的附加费。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-027"></a>[27](#note-ch8-027)

However, banks cannot just manufacture money internally. To become a real asset, bank-made money must pass through some apparatus of capture, through which the debtor transfers an increment to the creditor. Thus, the money loaned out in the form of wages is produced and given effect in relation to the purchases and charges on which the wage must be spent. Only the guarantee of that future spending enables the bank’s creation of assets to proceed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-026"></a>[26](#note-ch8-026) Credit money can operate only as part of a technical and material arrangement where at a future point the money is spent, and ‘returned’ to the bank with interest. With the money manufactured to pay wages, the interest payment is not imposed on the worker as a separate fee, but is built into the prices of commodities, the charges for services, and the cost of housing. These prices, charges, and costs, measured in the calculation of GDP, include both the value of the product, and the surcharge imposed as corporate profit and interest on the credit money created as wages.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-027"></a>[27](#note-ch8-027)

<a id="ch08-0050"></a>

### 经济取代黄金成为“不变标准”

### The Economy Replaces Gold as the ‘Invariant Standard’

<a id="ch08-0051"></a>

这种通过信用机制攫取剩余的能力——在时间中设置一道间隙，把当下与未来、劳动与其产品的购买、从而贷款与偿还分隔开来——并不限于工业体系和雇佣劳动。确切地说，正如[第三章](#ch03-0001)<a id="page-278"></a>〔原书第278页〕所提出的，现代工业是一个绕道。货物制造——涉及艰苦劳动、低利润率以及持续的竞争威胁——很快让位于其他攫取装置，这些装置更长期、更少受竞争威胁，尤其是那些通过重新增强的帝国扩张力量运作的装置，包括修建铁路、公用事业、土地开发计划和住房抵押贷款，以及较旧的攫取形式，特别是征收政府税。如前面几章所探讨的，所有这些都作为创造信用的装置运作：确立一种特定的可靠未来付款流——租金、票价、运费、公用事业费、税收和抵押贷款还款——然后在当下出售对这些未来付款的主张。现代股份制公司与帝国扩张一道出现，成为制造和动员这类主张的主要装置。随后，甚至先前主要由家族企业或合伙企业主导的工业生活，也按同一原则重组，采用股份制公司的形式，以便把未来收益资本化并从中获利。

This ability to capture surplus through a credit mechanism, by setting up a gap in time that separates present from future, labour from the purchase of its products, and thus loan from repayment, was not limited to the industrial system and wage labour. If anything, as [chapter 3](#ch03-0001) <a id="page-278-en"></a>〔原书第278页〕proposed, modern industry was a detour. The manufacturing of goods – involving hard work, low margins, and the constant threat of competition – soon gave way to other apparatuses of capture, which were more long-term and less subject to threats of competition, especially those operating through the renewed powers of imperial expansion, including the building of railways, utilities, land development schemes, and housing mortgages, alongside older forms of capture, in particular the imposing of government taxes. All of these, as explored in previous chapters, operated as apparatuses to create credit, by establishing a particular stream of reliable future payments, in the form of rents, fares, freight charges, utility bills, taxes, and mortgage payments, and then selling claims upon those future payments in the present. The modern joint-stock company emerged, in tandem with imperial expansion, as a principal device for the manufacture and mobilisation of such claims. Subsequently, even industrial life, previously the preserve mainly of family-owned businesses or partnerships, was reorganised on the same principle, adopting the form of the joint-stock company in order to capitalise and profit from future earnings.

<a id="ch08-0052"></a>

然而，创造信用以购买这些特定未来主张，与创造信用以支付工资之间，仍然存在差异。以公司股份或政府、公司和抵押债务等形式出售对特定收入的索取，被理解为出售“金融”产品。这类安排明确按照从未来攫取收入的原则运作，形式是股息、利息支付或其他用钱赚钱的方式。支付工资似乎以不同方式运作。它似乎属于一个“实体”世界，而不是金融世界；在实体世界中，支付工资所需的货币只是生产成本。尽管存在这种表面差异，金融产品和工资都依赖信用货币的创造；在信用货币创造中，确保可靠的未来支出和资金返还，是货币体系的基础。

There remained a difference, however, between the production of credit to purchase these specific claims on the future and the production of credit to pay wages. The selling of claims to specific revenues, in forms such as company shares or government, corporate, and mortgage debt, was understood as the sale of ‘financial’ products. Such arrangements operated explicitly on the principle of capturing income from the future, in the shape of dividends, interest payments, or other modes of using money to earn money. The payment of wages seemed to operate differently. It appeared to belong to a ‘real’ world rather than a world of finance, in which the money required to pay wages was simply a cost of production. Despite this apparent difference, both financial products and wages depended on the creation of credit money, in which securing a reliable future expenditure and a return of the funds was the basis for the monetary system.

<a id="ch08-0053"></a>

要使现代货币创造体系运转，仅把企业与银行分开还不够。私人银行业需要一种手段，使其付款承诺能够作为公共货币发挥作用。这需要现代国家的权力来担保这些承诺。这种权力并非通过国家干预、监管和担保私人信用货币体系而产生，而是通过私人商业银行与公共或准公共中央银行及政府的共同演化而产生。资本主义货币与<a id="page-279"></a>〔原书第279页〕监管权力共生发展；现代银行业与现代政府相互塑造。

To make the modern system of money creation work, it was not enough to separate businesses from banks. Private banking required a means of enabling its promises to pay to function as public money. This required the powers of the modern state, to guarantee those promises. Such powers came into being, not by the state intervening to regulate and guarantee the private system of credit money, but through the coevolution of private commercial banks and public or quasi-public central banks and governments. Capitalist money and the power of <a id="page-279-en"></a>〔原书第279页〕regulation developed symbiotically; modern banking and modern government formed one another.

<a id="ch08-0054"></a>

这种共同发展有两个要素。英格兰提供了典范案例，尽管英国商人银行家借鉴了荷兰人、以及更早的地中海商人和帝国城邦所发展的金融创造与治理方法。

This codevelopment had two elements. England provides the paradigmatic case, although English merchant bankers drew upon methods of creating and governing finance previously developed by the Dutch, and before them by merchants and imperial city-states in the Mediterranean.

<a id="ch08-0055"></a>

第一，通过有利可图的殖民贸易和奴隶贩卖积累起来的私人货币创造，获得了公共形式。十七世纪末，伦敦有权势的商人邀请荷兰商人银行家的盟友奥兰治亲王威廉入侵英格兰。威廉依赖他们获得新王位，并率领这个国家卷入其四百年来首次在欧洲进行的重大战争；他接受了一项安排：商人们组建新的股份制公司——英格兰银行——为战争提供信贷。这些战争越来越以扩张英国海外商业垄断为目的，而为战争筹集的贷款不再要求一年内偿还。它们被赋予“国家”债务的新形式（而非君主的私人债务或殖民地贸易公司的商业债务），并由关税和消费税的指定收入担保，尤其是酒类和烟草税，而穷人不成比例地承担这些税负。通过出售对这些未来国家收入的折扣主张，商人银行家如今可以创造有公共担保的私人信用货币。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-028"></a>[28](#note-ch8-028)早在“民族国家”出现之前，“民族”就被变了出来——被生产为承载这笔战争债务义务的人为躯体。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-029"></a>[29](#note-ch8-029)

First, private money creation, built up through profitable colonial trading and slaving ventures, was given a public form. At the end of the seventeenth century, powerful merchants in London invited an ally of the Dutch merchant bankers, Prince William of Orange, to invade England. Dependent on them for his new throne and leading the country into its first major war in Europe in 400 years, William accepted an arrangement where the merchants formed a new joint-stock company, the Bank of England, to provide credit to fund the war-making. The loans for wars, fought increasingly to expand English overseas commercial monopolies, no longer required repayment within the year. They were given the new form of ‘national’ debt (rather than a private debt of the monarch, or a commercial debt of the colonial trading companies) and were guaranteed by hypothecated revenues from customs and excise, especially duties on alcohol and tobacco, paid disproportionately by the poor. Selling discounted claims to those future state revenues, the merchant bankers could now create private credit money with a public guarantee.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-028"></a>[28](#note-ch8-028) Well before the emergence of the ‘nation-state’, the ‘nation’ was conjured into being – produced as the artificial body upon which this obligation for war debts was imposed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-029"></a>[29](#note-ch8-029)

<a id="ch08-0056"></a>

第二，该银行获得贴现私人汇票和发行见票即付银行票据的垄断权。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-030"></a>[30](#note-ch8-030)当工业就业的增长催生小型地方银行时，它们发行的票据只能在伦敦贴现，由英格兰银行担保所有私人创造的信用货币在最后关头都能兑换为金镑——尽管在实践中，英格兰银行按折扣接受地方银行纸币，交换的不是金币，而是它自己的纸币，后者逐渐具有了国家纸币的性质。纸币可按固定比率兑换为具有市场价值的贵金属黄金这一原则，产生了起作用的虚构：所有银行创造的信用货币，其价值都来自一种作为基础的国家商品货币。黄金价格的稳定产生了一种<a id="page-280"></a>〔原书第280页〕看似价值“标准”的东西，即金本位，据说它支配着可发行纸币的数量。然而事实上，在银行货币新体系下，工人工资的支付依赖于这种由准公共国家银行支持的私人货币创造安排。信贷名义上以黄金储备为担保，但在实践中，担保来自国家对维持英格兰银行盈利能力及其纸币可靠性的保证，而这一保证又通过银行对“国家”未来税收的主张来实现。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-031"></a>[31](#note-ch8-031)私人信用货币的创造，如今通过广泛的雇佣劳动和大规模消费体系运作，并由其与公共征税权力的联系来担保。

Second, the bank was granted a monopoly on the discounting of private bills of exchange and the issuing of bank bills payable on demand.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-030"></a>[30](#note-ch8-030) When the growth of industrial employment brought into being small provincial banks, the notes they issued could be discounted only in London, with the Bank of England guaranteeing that all privately created credit money could be redeemed, in the last resort, in gold sovereigns – although in practice the Bank accepted local banknotes at a discount in exchange not for gold coins but for its own notes, which gradually took on the character of a national paper currency. The principle that paper notes were convertible at a fixed rate to gold, a precious metal with a market value, gave rise to the working fiction that all bankmade credit money derived its value from an underlying national commodity-money. The stability of the price of gold generated what <a id="page-280-en"></a>〔原书第280页〕appeared as a ‘standard’ of value, the gold standard, that supposedly governed the quantity of paper money that could be issued. In fact, however, the payment of workers’ wages, under the new system of bank money, rested on this arrangement of private money creation backed by a quasi-public national bank. The credit was secured notionally against reserves of gold, but, in practice, against the state’s guarantee of maintaining the profitability of the Bank of England, and the reliability of its notes, through the bank’s claim on ‘the nation’s’ future tax payments.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-031"></a>[31](#note-ch8-031) The private creation of credit money, now operating through the extensive system of wage labour and mass consumption, was secured by its connection to the public power of taxation.

<a id="ch08-0057"></a>

尽管有这种担保，私人银行创造信用货币的不断扩大的权力仍必须进一步加以管理，以限制私人信用创造容易引发的危机。当大型金融投机失败，或长期战争带来对税负和未来消费稳定性的更广泛不确定性时，情况尤其如此。在实践中，只有英国实行金本位，其他主要货币的价值通过国际贸易与英镑挂钩，而大部分贸易由伦敦融资。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-032"></a>[32](#note-ch8-032)最终，在二十世纪两次世界大战之间的政治和经济危机中，金本位的虚构崩溃了。英格兰银行和其他国家银行被迫放弃黄金储备代表国家货币价值所依赖之不变标准的主张。

Despite this guarantee, the widening power of private banks to create credit money had to be further managed, to limit the crises to which private credit creation was prone. This was especially the case when large financial speculations failed, or when prolonged warfare brought wider uncertainty about tax burdens and the future stability of consumption. In practice, only Great Britain operated on a gold standard, with the value of other major currencies tied to sterling through international trade, most of which was financed through London.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-032"></a>[32](#note-ch8-032) Eventually, in the political and economic crises of the interwar decades of the twentieth century, the fiction of a gold standard collapsed. The Bank of England and other national banks were forced to abandon the claim that reserves of gold represented the invariant standard on which the value of national money was based.

校注：底本“只有英国实行金本位”的说法须区分制度采用与国际货币体系中英镑的主导地位。1876年美国外交文书明确记载德国采用黄金作为单一本位，并自1876年1月1日起以金马克为法定货币；因此不能将此句理解为其他国家从未采用金本位。正文保留作者论述，未擅自改写其关于国际信用体系的解释。 https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1876/d67

<a id="ch08-0058"></a>

战后时期，不变“标准”被重新发明，办法是设计一个新的参照物：“经济”。实物工资制的一般化安排——工资以私人制造的信用货币支付——不能再依赖黄金储备的虚构，即以此作为确立货币价值、限制信用创造的手段。相反，货币秩序将通过生产一个可预测的未来来稳定，其形式是关于经济指标的“客观知识”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-033"></a>[33](#note-ch8-033)国民收入账户体系本是战时用于规划军备生产的装置，战后被改用于管理信用的生产。对国民收入或 GDP 及其增长率、价格通胀、就业水平和利率的估算，提供了一组数字；对数字的解释取代黄金，确立了让私人货币创造得以进行的信用度。通过增长指标和其他“宏观经济”指标，中央银行如今可以监管和限制信用货币的创造，<a id="page-281"></a>〔原书第281页〕也可以限制工资要求和价格上涨。经济通过这些衡量技术被生产为一个自身存在的对象，已成为如今从未来榨取所依赖的工具。

The invariant ‘standard’ was then reinvented in the postwar period by devising a new referent: ‘the economy’. The generalised arrangement of truck, in which wages were paid in privately made credit money, could no longer depend on the fiction of reserves of gold as the standard establishing the value of money and the means of placing limits on the creation of credit. Instead, the monetary order would be stabilised by the production of a predictable future, in the form of the ‘objective knowledge’ of economic indicators.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-033"></a>[33](#note-ch8-033) A wartime device for planning the production of armaments, the system of national income accounts, was repurposed after the war as the means of managing the production of credit. The estimating of national income or GDP and its rate of growth, and of price inflation, employment levels, and interest rates, provided a set of numbers whose interpretation established, in place of gold, the creditworthiness that allowed the private creation of money to proceed. Through the metric of growth and other ‘macroeconomic’ indicators, central banks could now regulate and place limits on the creation of <a id="page-281-en"></a>〔原书第281页〕credit money – as well as on wage demands and price increases. Produced through these techniques of measurement as an object in itself, the economy had become the instrument on which extraction from the future would now depend.

<a id="ch08-0059"></a>

### 金融与实体

### The Financial and the Real

<a id="ch08-0060"></a>

也许有用的是，不仅把它理解为经济，还通过与杰里米·边沁全景敞视监狱的松散类比——福柯曾把它用作权力运作的图表——把它理解为“经济全景装置”。与全景敞视监狱一样，它是一种通过调节身体和组织欲望的方式产生知识形式的装置。作为不变标准，经济从来不可能只是对物质现实的再现，或只是统计制品、一组真理。它作为控制装置在物质层面运作，分解并重组人、家庭、材料、欲望和未来，产生稳定、结构和客观性的效果。

It may be useful to think of this arrangement not simply as the economy, but, by loose analogy with Jeremy Bentham’s Panopticon, deployed by Foucault as a diagram of the operation of power, as the EconoCon. Like the Panopticon, it is a device that produces forms of knowledge, through ways of regulating the body and organising desire. To operate as an invariant standard, the economy could never just be a representation of a material reality, or just a statistical artefact or set of truths. It operated materially, as an apparatus of control, decomposing and recomposing persons, households, materials, desires, and futures, creating an effect of stability, structure, and objectivity.

<a id="ch08-0061"></a>

要以这种方式运作，经济需要若干特征。这些要求使我们理解，经济衡量或再现福祉方式中的“缺陷”为什么不是有待识别、修正或取代的疏忽，而是其政治效力的关键。它们解释了为什么在气候危机面前，我们无法摆脱“增长”的动力。

To work in this way, the economy required a number of features. These requirements allow us to understand how the ‘flaws’ in the way the economy measures or represents well-being are not oversights, to be identified, revised, or replaced, but the key to its political effectiveness. They explain our inability, in the face of the climate crisis, to escape the dynamic of ‘growth’.

<a id="ch08-0062"></a>

第一，经济必须组织当下与未来之间的关系本身。它做到这一点，不是通过衡量诸如信用或资本化这类通过生产未来、延迟和绕道而运作的动态过程，而是通过按固定时间间隔组成一系列静态图像，然后把它们叠加起来比较差异。经济是按年度快照计算的，而不是某种能够衡量跨时间建构之关系的东西。这种静态形式允许为每一年计算一个单独总量，然后与前一年和后一年比较。如我们在[第五章](#ch05-0001)所见，快照的序列就是可作为“增长”衡量的东西。对经济来说，当下与未来不是一种内在时间性展开中的时刻，而是同一种政治技术的共时产物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-034"></a>[34](#note-ch8-034)

First, the economy must organise the very relation between present and future. It achieves this, not by measuring dynamic processes, such as credit or capitalisation, that operate through the production of futures, delays, and detours, but by composing a series of static images, at regular intervals in time, then superimposing one upon the next to compare their difference. The economy is calculated as an annual snapshot, not as something that can measure relations constructed across time. This static form allows a separate total to be calculated for each year, which can then be compared with the previous year, and the following. As we saw in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001), the sequence of snapshots is what is measurable as ‘growth’. For the economy, present and future are not moments in the unfolding of an internal temporality, but coeval products of a political technology.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-034"></a>[34](#note-ch8-034)

<a id="ch08-0063"></a>

第二，为使这些快照可以比较，必须赋予难以捉摸的“技术”因素以决定作用。当把一年的国民账户与下一年比较时，数字会<a id="page-282"></a>〔原书第282页〕按通胀进行调整。这需要判断货物或服务成本上升反映的是“实际”变化还是仅仅“货币”变化。一次医疗程序、一部手机、住房、娱乐订阅或优步行程的成本上升，应归因于某种技术改进，代表产品的“实际”增加，还是仅仅是价格通胀，须予折减以只衡量经济的“真正”增长？这一判断必须对经济生活的每个部门和每类产品作出。从国民收入核算的最初阶段起，这就被认为是一项“无法克服”的挑战，而且随着时间推移越来越如此，因为产品性质和品质的微小变化不断增加。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-035"></a>[35](#note-ch8-035)没有任何先验规则能作出这一判断。相反，必须就“技术”变化的贡献作出一系列临时判断。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-036"></a>[36](#note-ch8-036)技术改进似乎提供了解释增长的力量或动量。在实践中，它为从未来榨取提供了越来越普遍的托词。

Second, to make these snapshots comparable, a determining role is given to the elusive factor of ‘technology’. When the national accounts for one year are compared with those for the next, the figures are <a id="page-282-en"></a>〔原书第282页〕adjusted for inflation. This requires deciding whether the increased cost of a good or service reflects a ‘real’ change or merely a ‘monetary’ change. Is the increased cost of a medical procedure, a mobile phone, accommodation, an entertainment subscription, or an Uber ride attributable to some technical improvement, representing a ‘real’ increase in the product, or is it merely price inflation, to be discounted so as to measure only the ‘actual’ growth of the economy? This determination must be made across every sector of economic life, and for every category of product, a challenge that from the very beginnings of national income accounting was recognised as ‘insuperable’, and progressively so, since minor variations in the nature and qualities of products increased through time.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-035"></a>[35](#note-ch8-035) No a priori rule can make the determination. Rather, a series of ad hoc judgements must be made about the contribution of a change in ‘technology’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-036"></a>[36](#note-ch8-036) Technical improvement appears to provide the force or momentum that accounts for growth. In practice, it provides an increasingly pervasive alibi for extraction from the future.

<a id="ch08-0064"></a>

第三，以 GDP 衡量的经济由“产品”组成。与资本主义等较早的术语相比——资本主义被理解为投机性的、金融驱动的、与帝国主义纠缠在一起、本质上不稳定的——经济把集体生活再现为本质上稳定的，因为它是“生产性的”。它衡量和再现物质关系时，不是依据投机性投资、不平等的财产关系、不稳定的资本流动和货币变动，而是依据产品的流通，即价格被汇总以估算 GDP 的商品。具体而言，它衡量经济“价值”的生产——其基础是计算人们在新东西上花了多少钱，形式是货物和服务。这种“产品”充当可据以创造信用货币的未来。没有它，几乎不可能有任何货币。

Third, the economy, measured by GDP, is composed of ‘products’. In contrast to older terms like capitalism, understood as speculative, finance-driven, bound up with imperialism, and essentially unstable, the economy renders collective life as essentially stable, because it is ‘productive’. It measures and represents material relations not in terms of speculative investment, unequal relations of property, unstable flows of capital, and currency movements, but as the circulation of products, meaning the commodities whose prices are aggregated to estimate GDP. It is a measure, specifically, of production of economic ‘value’ – based on counting how much people spend on new stuff, in the form of goods and services. This ‘product’ functions as the future against which credit money can be created. Without it, there could scarcely be any money.

<a id="ch08-0065"></a>

经济被配置为“产品”的领域，铭刻了一种区分：产品被视为物质的，货币则被视为仅仅是衡量和比较其价值、并购买它们的手段。尽管货币的存在方式主要是通过它所购买的货物和服务而产生，因而只能物质地存在，而不是作为财富储存，经济仍把物质与货币呈现为两个分离的领域，一个被视为实在，另一个被视为非实在或虚构。这种区分被视为理所当然，而没有被理解为经济生产的效果——而且它继续影响甚至非常出色的“金融化”研究。

Configured as a realm of ‘products’, the economy inscribes a distinction: between products, considered material, and money, considered simply as a means to measure and compare their values, and to purchase them. Even though money exists largely, not as a store of wealth, but as something effected through the products and services on which it is spent, and thus as something that can exist only materially, the economy presents the material and the monetary as separate realms, one rendered real and the other nonreal or fictitious. This distinction is taken for granted, rather than understood as an effect of the production of the economy – and continues to inform even very capable studies of ‘financialisation’.

<a id="ch08-0066"></a>

<a id="page-283"></a>〔原书第283页〕产品与价格、物质与货币之间的区分，本身是不断被制造出来的东西。它是经济衡量的结果，而不是有待衡量的先在现实。可以从历史角度理解这种相互强化，但从更具分析性的角度看，既可以从物质方面、也可以从货币方面来看。在物质方面，正如米歇尔·卡隆向我们展示的，我们所谓的产品实际上更像过程，而不是事物。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-037"></a>[37](#note-ch8-037)例如，一辆汽车是由设计、评估、性能、欲望、依恋、维修和过时等持续操作组装而成的，更不用说道路、燃料、车辆贷款、交通法规、许可证和治安管理，没有这些，“产品”就无法作为价值物存在。此外，在大多数国家，被衡量为经济的产品中，有一半到四分之三甚至不像汽车那样呈现为物质事物。它们属于所谓的服务类别，最初是一个剩余类别，如今却成了一个笼统术语，指构成“经济”主要部分的过程、依恋、义务、付款和表演的增殖。经济在这里的作用不是衡量物质世界及其增长，而是把这种异质性化解为看似实在的事物及其价格。

<a id="page-283-en"></a>〔原书第283页〕The distinction between product and price, between the material and the monetary, is itself something continually manufactured. It is an outcome of the measurement of the economy, not a prior reality to be measured. This mutual reinforcement can be appreciated from a historical angle, but in more analytical terms it can be seen both from the side of the material, and from the side of money. On the material side, on the one hand, as Michel Callon shows us, what we call products are actually more like processes than things.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-037"></a>[37](#note-ch8-037) A car, for example, is assembled out of ongoing operations of design, evaluation, performance, desire, attachment, repair, and obsolescence, not to mention the arrangements of roadways, fuels, vehicle loans, traffic laws, permits, and policing without which the ‘product’ could not exist as an item of value. In most countries, furthermore, between half and three-quarters of the products that are measured as the economy, unlike a car, do not even present themselves as material things. They fall into the category of so-called services, originally a residual grouping but now a catchall term for the proliferation of processes, attachments, obligations, payments, and performances that constitute the major part of ‘the economy’. The economy functions, here, not to measure the material world and its growth, but to resolve this heterogeneity into what appears as real things and their price.

<a id="ch08-0067"></a>

另一方面，货币不是实在之物的对立面。金融并非与生产性相分离，原因很简单：货币作为信用关系，总是涉及一种物质化手段。虽然几乎所有货币都是在银行中通过开立信贷额度和相应借记创造的，但如果没有未来的物质过程、某种攫取付款的装置，使货币得以实现并产生，这一单独的会计行为就不会有效力。因此，购买住房的抵押贷款只有通过房屋的存在才能作为货币运作：贷款的偿还和利息费用可借房屋收取和强制执行，同时还涉及设计、规划监管、产权、治安管理、分区、种族隔离和红线划界以及止赎等过程，住房的价值正是通过这些过程被生产和担保。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-038"></a>[38](#note-ch8-038)同样，企业支付工人所需的信用货币，只有存在某种此后信用货币工资必须花在其上的企业产品，才能作为支付手段运作。金融这种混合形式——既是当下的信用付款，又是伸向未来、强制偿还的物质装置——正是<a id="page-284"></a>〔原书第284页〕经济的生产作为治理当下与未来之安排的模式所确保的东西。

Money, on the other hand, is not the opposite of what is real. The financial is not something separate from the productive, for the simple reason that money, as a relationship of credit, always involves a means of materialisation. While almost all money is created in banks by opening a line of credit and corresponding debit, that individual act of accounting would have no effectiveness if there were not a future material process, some apparatus for capturing payment, through which the money were to be realised, and brought into being. Thus, a mortgage loan to purchase a house functions as money only through the presence of a house on which repayments of the loan and the interest charge can be collected and enforced, along with the processes of design, planning regulation, property rights, policing, zoning, racial segregation and redlining, and foreclosure through which the value of housing is produced and guaranteed.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-038"></a>[38](#note-ch8-038) Likewise, the credit money that a business firm requires to pay its workers can function as a means of payment only if there is some business product on which that credit money wage must later be spent. This hybrid form of finance, as credit payment in the present and as an apparatus built out into the future that compels repayment, is what the production of the <a id="page-284-en"></a>〔原书第284页〕economy, as a mode of governing the arrangement of present and future, secures.

<a id="ch08-0068"></a>

生产实在与金融之间的差异需要工作。它被内置于经济的衡量本身。如我们刚刚所见，对每一种产品和服务的衡量，都必须在其成本的“实际”成分与纯粹“货币”成分之间作出判断。更重要的是，以 GDP 衡量的经济排除了金融产品的制造和购买成本，如股票、债券和衍生品；在最近一次国民账户重新校准中，其中一些不再被归类为成本，而被归类为最终“产品”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-039"></a>[39](#note-ch8-039)它还排除资产价值升值所产生的收入——即资本利得——因为资本利得通常不在年度快照中体现。这一未被衡量的过程占国民收入高达 25%，其中大部分流向极富者，但对于维持哪怕是中等富裕也日益重要。

Producing the difference between the real and the financial requires work. It is built into the very measurement of the economy. As we have just seen, for the measurement of every product and service, a decision must be made between the ‘real’ component of its cost and the merely ‘monetary’. More than this, the economy as measured by GDP excludes the cost of the manufacture and purchase of financial products, such as stocks, bonds, and derivatives, some of which, in a recent recalibration of national accounts, were requalified not as costs but as final ‘products’.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-039"></a>[39](#note-ch8-039) It also excludes income arising from the appreciation of the value of assets – that is, capital gains – because capital gains are not usually visible in an annual snapshot. This unmeasured process represents as much as 25 per cent of national income, the bulk of it going to the very rich, but increasingly important to maintaining even moderate forms of affluence.

<a id="ch08-0069"></a>

反过来，国民收入账户确实包括对非生产性活动的付款，只要这些活动广泛存在并可被视为一种“服务”。例如，住房租金被视为对住房服务的付款，即使房屋是多年前或几十年前建造的，租金与建造结构——提供服务——的原始成本毫无关系，而只是垄断土地财产准入者所强加的收费。奇怪的是，自住业主在国民账户中被认为获得了等值收入。他们被估算为享有住在自己房子里的“服务”。（因此，人类再生产和家庭中的其他无酬劳动不被计入，但房子本身却因*非*生产性的“劳动”——为所有者提供住所——而在国民账户中得到承认。）

Conversely, the national income accounts do include payments for unproductive activities, if they are widespread and can be considered a ‘service’. For example, the payment of rent for housing is considered a payment for housing services, even if the home was built years or decades before, and the rent has no connection to the original cost of building the structure – of providing the service – but is merely a charge imposed by those who monopolise access to landed property. Curiously, owners who occupy their own homes are considered in the national accounts to be receiving an equivalent income. They are imputed to enjoy the ‘service’ provided by the opportunity to live in their own house. (So reproductive and other unpaid household labour of humans is not counted, but the house itself is recognised in the national accounts for the *un*productive ‘labour’ of housing its owners.)

<a id="ch08-0070"></a>

财产租金和利息并不是从被建构为“生产性”经济之组成部分的资产控制中榨取付款的唯一模式。经济衡量的最重要特征是，甚至物质货物和有用服务的成本也包含一笔可观的金融收费。例如在德国，估算表明日常商品价格的 35% 至 40% 是制造商和供应商向银行及其他债权人支付利息的成本。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-040"></a>[40](#note-ch8-040)这种从未来大量且不断扩张的利息收入榨取，作为成本转嫁给货物和服务的最终消费者，已成为经济“增长”的一个重要组成部分。

Property rents and interest are not the only modes of extracting payment from the control of assets construed as part of the ‘productive’ economy. The most important feature of the measurement of the economy is that even the cost of material goods and useful services includes a significant financial charge. Estimates in the case of Germany, for example, suggest that 35 to 40 per cent of the price of everyday goods represents the cost of the interest payments that manufacturers and suppliers pay to banks and other creditors.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-040"></a>[40](#note-ch8-040) This vast and expanding extraction of interest income from the future, passed on as a cost to the final consumers of goods and services, has become an essential component of the ‘growth’ of the economy.

<a id="ch08-0071"></a>

<a id="page-285"></a>〔原书第285页〕经济被呈现为物质、生产性生活——表现为我们福祉衡量标准的经济“产品”——的衡量。但它的衡量不仅未能区分增进福祉的产品与危害生命的产品，也未能计入环境成本或无酬劳动，正如其他人所指出的；它还包括一整个所谓非生产性付款的体系——租金、利息、广告和其他收费——这些付款不被记录为以未来为代价的生活方式，而仅仅被记录为物品生产的成本。

<a id="page-285-en"></a>〔原书第285页〕The economy is presented as a measure of material, productive life, of the economic ‘product’ that appears as the measure of our well-being. But its measurement not only fails to distinguish between products that enhance well-being and those that are harmful to life, or to account for environmental costs or unpaid labour, as others have pointed out; it also includes an entire system of so-called unproductive payments for rent, interest, advertising, and other charges, which are recorded, not as a mode of living at the expense of the future, but simply as the cost of the production of things.

<a id="ch08-0072"></a>

经济通过与这些未来攫取模式的关系、实际上通过确保一种不同的未来关系来运作。它为信用和资本化实践建立并强化了某个位置。但它这样做靠的是否认。信用货币在账户体系中无处不在，同时又无处可寻。它无处不在，因为被衡量的不是资源、物质产品、劳动或不平等，而是价格。它被否认，因为货币被视为除中介之外什么都不是。换言之，“经济”的定义和衡量不仅确立了这个对象，还铭刻并强化了“实体经济”与“金融体系”之间、亦即“实际生产”与纯粹金融之间一种根本且完全成问题的区分。

The economy operates in relation to these modes of capture of the future by securing, in fact, a different relation to the future. It builds in and reinforces a certain place for practices of credit and capitalisation. But it does this by disavowal. Credit money is everywhere in the system of accounts, and at the same time nowhere. It is everywhere, because what is measured is not resources, or material products, or labour, or inequality, but prices. It is disavowed, because money is seen as nothing except an intermediary. In other words, the definition and measurement of ‘the economy’ not only establishes this object, but also inscribes and reinforces a fundamental but entirely problematic distinction between the ‘real economy’ and ‘the financial system’ – between ‘real production’ and mere finance.

<a id="ch08-0073"></a>

GDP 的计算和增长的衡量，如今可以被看作通过经济创造出一种结构效果，这种效果既用于稳定、也用于掩盖以未来为代价的生活方式。它把“实体”与“金融”之间的表面分离铭刻进政治的对象本身（经济）。这是经济全景装置的关键，是理解经济作为控制装置的关键。它是一种以局部方式安排人类行动的装置——作为生产者、消费者、户主、企业主。但它在更分子化的层面运作，生成经济与非经济之间、实体与金融之间、以及过去、现在与未来之间的关系。

The calculation of GDP and the measurement of growth can now be seen as the creation through the economy of the structural effect that was required to both stabilise and disguise the mode of living at the expense of the future. It does so by inscribing in the very object of politics (the economy) the apparent separation between the ‘real’ and the ‘financial’. This is the key to the EconoCon, to understanding the economy as an apparatus of control. It is an apparatus that orders human action in partial ways – as producer, consumer, householder, business owner. But it operates at a more molecular level, generating relations between economic and noneconomic, between real and financial, and between past, present, and future.

<a id="ch08-0074"></a>

这种理解经济的方法不仅解释了它作为政治装置的发明，也解释了它的界定特征：增长。增长是未来攫取运作所强加的东西。作为工资、抵押贷款或生产贷款提供的信用，带有利息收费。它必须偿还，不是以相同数额，而是连同一笔溢价——所谓利息的成本。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-041"></a>[41](#note-ch8-041)这种增长具有托词的性质。因为它实际上是以贫困化的形式发生的。

This approach to understanding the economy explains not only its invention as a political device, but its defining feature, growth. Growth is something forced by the operation of capture from the future. The credit supplied as wage, or as mortgage, or as production loan, carries an interest charge. It must be paid back, not in the same amount, but with a premium – the cost of so-called interest.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-041"></a>[41](#note-ch8-041) This growth has the character of an alibi. For it actually occurs as impoverishment.

<a id="ch08-0075"></a>

<a id="page-286"></a>〔原书第286页〕

<a id="page-286-en"></a>〔原书第286页〕

<a id="ch08-0076"></a>

### 碳增长

### Carbon Growth

<a id="ch08-0077"></a>

如果以 GDP 衡量的经济增长既不是错误再现，也不仅仅是再现，而是一种安排未来攫取的装置，组织身体、生活和材料，以便使后来者贫困，并为当下的贫困化提供道德辩护，即“经济义论”（重提[第四章](#ch04-0001)的术语），那么这与本章开头的问题——化石燃料、气候危机与增长现象之间的关系——有何关联？

If the growth of the economy, as measured by GDP, is neither a misrepresentation, nor merely a representation, but a device for ordering the capture of the future, organising bodies and lives and materials in order to impoverish those who come later, and providing the moral justification, the ‘oikodicy’ (to repeat a term from [chapter 4](#ch04-0001)), for present impoverishments, how does this relate to the opening question of this chapter, about the relationship between fossil fuels, climate crisis, and the phenomenon of growth?

<a id="ch08-0078"></a>

答案不在于某种底层的能源“需要”。相反，化石燃料，尤其是二十世纪后半叶的石油，特别适合这种攫取模式。正如按照安德烈亚斯·马尔姆的看法，从水力磨坊到“第一次”工业革命的燃煤蒸汽机的转变，最好理解为不是机械动力增加或效率提高，而是控制劳动的更有效手段，并且正如本书[第三章](#ch03-0001)所提出的，是一个允许增加信用制造的绕道的一部分；也正如“第二次”工业革命的巨大驱动力——铁路建设——并不反映对速度或通信的需要，而是反映了转移金融票据和征服领土的新机会，这些机会很快就被取代了；过去七十年石油和汽车时代同样如此。私家车和商业公路运输，是为驱动未来攫取而建造的载具。

The answer does not lie in some underlying ‘need’ for energy. Rather, fossil fuels, especially oil in the second half of the twentieth century, were uniquely suited to this mode of capture. Just as the transition from water mills to the coal-driven steam engines of the ‘first’ industrial revolution is best understood, following Andreas Malm, not in terms of increased mechanical power or greater efficiency but as a more effective means of controlling labour and, as suggested here in [chapter 3](#ch03-0001), as part of a detour allowing the increased manufacture of credit; and just as the great driver of the ‘second’ industrial revolution, the construction of railways, did not reflect a need for speed or communication, but new opportunities to move financial paper and conquer territory, opportunities that were soon superseded; so the same with the age of oil and automobiles of the last seven decades. The private car and commercial road transportation were vehicles built for driving the capture of the future.

<a id="ch08-0079"></a>

战后几十年的“大加速”时期，对化石燃料的依赖出现了惊人增长，这段时期造成了大气中几乎所有的过量碳。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-042"></a>[42](#note-ch8-042)1990 年以后，加速更加显著，该年是政府间气候变化专门委员会第一份评估报告发布之年。这一年开启的三十年，到 2020 年已造成 1750 年以来二氧化碳过量排放的一半以上。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-043"></a>[43](#note-ch8-043)但关键术语是这种“依赖”的性质。“增长”以何种方式依赖石油？我们知道能源消费与 GDP 之间没有简单关系。例如，美国的碳能源消费率，是多数享有相当或更好生活水平的其他工业化国家的两倍多。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-044"></a>[44](#note-ch8-044)

The ‘great acceleration’ of the postwar decades was a period of an astonishing increase in dependence on fossil fuels, a span of time responsible for almost all the excess carbon in the atmosphere.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-042"></a>[42](#note-ch8-042) The acceleration is even more marked since 1990, the date of the first Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. That year marked the start of the three decades responsible by 2020 for more than half the excess CO_{2}_ emissions since 1750.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-043"></a>[43](#note-ch8-043) But the critical term is the nature of this ‘dependence’. In what way was ‘growth’ dependent on oil? We know there is no simple relation between energy consumption and GDP. The United States, for example, consumes carbon energy at more than double the rate of most other industrialised countries that enjoy a comparable or better standard of living.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-044"></a>[44](#note-ch8-044)

<a id="ch08-0080"></a>

对石油的依赖反映的不是现代生活对高能源使用的普遍依赖，而是对经济生产的依赖，因而也是对资本化机会的依赖——建立一个当下可用的未来<a id="page-287"></a>〔原书第287页〕收入攫取体系，经济本身则是稳定它的工具。石油之所以具有如此巨大的重要性，不是因为它是生活必需品，而是因为这些相互关联的目的。一方面，如[第五章](#ch05-0001)所述并在别处更详细论证的，二十世纪中叶经济作为政治对象的创造，得益于石油的突然丰裕。战后获得相对廉价且看似取之不尽的碳能源——主要来自中东新石油产区——帮助支撑了“经济”作为能够无限增长之实体的新颖观念。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-045"></a>[45](#note-ch8-045)

The dependence on oil reflected a general dependence of modern life not on high levels of energy use, but on the production of the economy, and thus on opportunities for capitalisation – for building out a future <a id="page-287-en"></a>〔原书第287页〕of revenue capture that was available in the present, for which the economy itself was an instrument of stabilisation. Oil mattered on this enormous scale, not as a requirement for life, but for these interconnected purposes. On the one hand, as outlined in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001) and argued in greater detail elsewhere, the creation of the economy as an object of politics in the mid-twentieth century was assisted by a sudden abundance of oil. The postwar access to comparatively cheap and seemingly inexhaustible supplies of carbon energy, largely from the new oil regions of the Middle East, helped to underwrite the novel idea of ‘the economy’ as an entity capable of infinite growth.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-045"></a>[45](#note-ch8-045)

<a id="ch08-0081"></a>

另一方面，石油提供了一种攫取未来付款的非凡手段。战后几十年乃至二十世纪大部分时间里，石油公司都是超额、长期利润最可靠的来源。少数几家公司垄断了全球石油生产。只要碳氢化合物替代品（如核电、可再生能源或蓄电池）的研发能够被阻碍和拖延；只要石油生产、尤其是中东丰富油田的生产能够被放慢和破坏到足以保持未来利润高涨的程度；只要能够发展出推高石油“需要”的生活方式；只要中东产油国的预期收入随后能够被资产化——主要通过对购买军火的天文数字承诺，而其托词正是确保这种对石油的“需要”——那么石油生产的规模、尤其是其长期性，就比任何其他行业更能保证一条延伸到遥远未来的付款流。随着对拥有私家车和使用石油产品的依赖而扩张的郊区生活、抵押贷款还款、汽车金融和消费债务等形式，连同表面上“保障”这些生活方式的军火制造、战争和军事债务，都成倍扩大了信用的制造。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-046"></a>[46](#note-ch8-046)这条来自石油公司收入、来自为依赖石油的生活方式融资和“保护”的付款流，可以被资本化并在当下消费。

On the other hand, petroleum provided an exceptional means of commanding payments taken from the future. In the postwar decades, as through most of the twentieth century, oil firms were the most reliable source of extraordinary, long-term profits. A handful of companies monopolised the global production of oil. So long as the development of alternatives to hydrocarbons, such as nuclear power, renewables, or storage batteries, could be obstructed and delayed; so long as the production of oil, especially from the abundant fields of the Middle East, could be slowed and sabotaged just enough to keep future profits high; so long as ways of living could be developed to drive up the ‘need’ for oil; and so long as the prospective revenues of oil-producing states in the Middle East could then be assetised, largely through astronomical commitments to purchase arms, for which the alibi was to secure this same ‘need’ for oil; then the scale and above all the longevity of oil production guaranteed, more than any other industry, a stream of payments far into the future. The forms of suburban life, mortgage payment, vehicle finance, and consumer debt that expanded with dependence on owning private cars and using petroleum products, along with the arms manufacturing, war-making, and military debt that ostensibly ‘secured’ these ways of life, multiplied the manufacture of credit.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-046"></a>[46](#note-ch8-046) That stream of payments, from the revenues of oil companies and the financing and ‘protecting’ of oil-dependent ways of living, could be capitalised and consumed in the present.

<a id="ch08-0082"></a>

这种未来资产化中很少一部分真正代表能源生产、住房建造、汽车制造或安全生活形式的“成本”。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-047"></a>[47](#note-ch8-047)它代表的是一条异常丰厚的未来收入流的贴现现值。石油公司所投资的——连同房地产开发商、汽车公司和其他制造能源“需要”的企业，以及依赖所谓“保障”中东产油区来经营的武器公司，通过公共<a id="page-288"></a>〔原书第288页〕关系活动、智库、消费者广告、政治游说、为军售融资、妖魔化伊斯兰教、所谓的反恐战争、捍卫犹太复国主义，以及许多其他形式的宣传、国家补贴、破坏、战争和舆论塑造——是一个持续依赖碳燃料的未来。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-048"></a>[48](#note-ch8-048)经济很大程度上是一种被建造出来的对象，用以通过其增长的装置来稳定和管理这个未来的生产。最近几十年的大加速，以及它给我们带来的气候崩溃，并非由资本主义的一般发展或其能源需要所驱动，而是由可以通过高碳生活方式制造出来的特定资本化形式所驱动。

Very little of this assetising of the future represented the ‘cost’ of energy production or house building or vehicle manufacture or a secure form of life.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-047"></a>[47](#note-ch8-047) It represented the discounted present value of an extraordinary future revenue stream. What the oil companies invested in – along with the property developers, car firms, and other enterprises manufacturing the ‘need’ for energy, and the weapons firms dependent on allegedly ‘securing’ the oil regions of the Middle East, through public <a id="page-288-en"></a>〔原书第288页〕relations campaigns, think tanks, consumer advertising, political lobbying, the financing of military sales, the demonising of Islam, the so-called war on terror, the defence of Zionism, and many other kinds of promotion, state subsidy, sabotage, war-making, and opinion forming – was a future of continued dependence on carbon fuels.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-048"></a>[48](#note-ch8-048) The economy was an object largely built to stabilise and manage, through the device of its growth, the production of this future. The great acceleration of recent decades, and the climate collapse it has brought upon us, were driven not by the general development of capitalism, nor by its need for energy, but by the specific forms of capitalisation that could be manufactured through a carbon-heavy form of life.

<a id="ch08-0083"></a>

### 结局

### The Ending

<a id="ch08-0084"></a>

最后，让我们回到本章和本书开头提出的更大问题。我们建立了一种通过攫取未来财富来运作的生活方式，少数人得以靠当下异常水平的非劳动所得生活。与此同时，多数人日益被先前的强加款的偿还、以及支配他们生活的各种不稳定和风险的管理所累。随着这些强加款增加，即使中等富裕也只能通过进一步资产化来实现——购置房产、在退休基金中建立股份——从而确保未来的进一步贫困化。

In conclusion, let us come back to the larger issues with which this chapter, and this book, opened. We have built modes of living that operate through the capture of wealth from the future, in which a minority is able to live off extraordinary levels of unearned income in the present. The majority, meanwhile, are increasingly burdened with the repayment of previous impositions and with managing the forms of precarity and risk through which their lives are governed. As those impositions increase, even moderate affluence can be achieved only through further assetisation, via the acquisition of property and the building of shares in retirement funds, ensuring the further impoverishment of the future.

<a id="ch08-0085"></a>

本书考察了几个世纪、多个国家和大陆的资本化形式。目的不是写一部资本化过程的发展史。这样的目标不仅过于宏大，还会带来把历史理解为发展所固有的风险和误读。书中提供的许多来自其他时代和地点的例子，都揭示了此前历史片段的断裂性质，并强调了绕道和中断的意义。这些反映了对我们理解资本化至关重要的东西。如果未来是作为一组当下要被攫取和资产化的过程而发生的，那么就不应把它简单地视为当下发展的展开，而应视为一组当下和过去的计划，始终可能转向或受挫。这种断裂性质来自一切资本化计算都面临的不确定性；没有<a id="page-289"></a>〔原书第289页〕这种不确定性，贴现未来并从其缩减中获利的过程就无法运作。

The book has examined forms of capitalisation across several centuries and over a variety of countries and continents. The aim has not been to write a history of the development of the capitalising process. Such a goal would not only be too ambitious – it would bring the risks and misreadings inherent in any approach to history as development. Many of the examples from other times and places offered in the book have brought into view the disjunctive nature of previous episodes and stressed the significance of detours and interruptions. These reflect something important to our understanding of capitalisation. If the future occurs as a set of processes to be captured and assetised in the present, it should not be seen as simply the unfolding of present developments, but as a set of projects, now and in previous times, always open to diversion and setback. This disjunctive character arises from the uncertainty to which all capitalising calculation is exposed, without <a id="page-289-en"></a>〔原书第289页〕which the process of discounting the future and profiting from its diminishment could not operate.

<a id="ch08-0086"></a>

这些转移和绕道反映了资本化方案必须卷入的各种权力和能动性——人类的与超出人类范围的。资本化取决于对未来的控制，但那个未来由各种力量组成，有机的和无机的、促成稳定的和破坏稳定的，它们有自己的力量、目的和互动方式。<a id="ref-zh-note-ch8-049"></a>[49](#note-ch8-049)许多世纪以来，人们都体验过这种对未来依赖所产生的不确定性和断裂，例如远距离贸易的风险、预购农业产出的不可预测性，或为长期战争组织信贷的危险。随着资本化机会扩展——似乎伴随对自然过程和人类社群控制的增强——挫折和意外后果的可能性也扩展了。在种植园农业、城市扩张、矿产开采、水坝建设、通信基础设施和河流改道等地球改造项目中，破坏性后果来自对河流洪泛脉冲、土壤形成的生物与非生物过程、新物种和病原体移动的影响，尤其是把过量碳排入大气并使地球变暖的灾难。

The diversions and detours reflect the variety of powers and agencies, human and more than human, that capitalising schemes must engage. Capitalisation depends upon control of the future, but that future is composed of forces, organic and inorganic, stabilising and destabilising, that have their own powers, purposes, and modes of interaction.<a id="ref-en-note-ch8-049"></a>[49](#note-ch8-049) The uncertainties and disjunctures generated by this dependence on the future were experienced across many centuries, in the risks encountered in long-distance trade, for example, or in the unpredictability of the advanced purchase of agricultural production, or in the hazards of organising credit for extended warfare. As opportunities for capitalisation expanded, seemingly with increased control over natural processes and human communities, the possibility for setback and unanticipated outcomes expanded too. In such terraforming projects as plantation agriculture, urban expansion, mineral extraction, dam building, communication infrastructures, and river diversion, disruptive effects followed from the consequences for the flood pulse of a river, the biotic and abiotic processes of soil formation, the movement of new species and pathogens, and, above all, the catastrophe of placing excess carbon in the atmosphere and warming the planet.

<a id="ch08-0087"></a>

在探讨通过攫取未来而运作的转移、断裂、贫困化和致富模式时，本书同样关注另一种转移——托词的生产，字面上的“不在那里”、“别处”，那种促使我们到别处寻找我们生活方式之解释的误导。资本的托词首先正是指这一点：资本作为托词。资本*就是*托词，因为在其原义中（源自动产或货物），在其日常含义中（作为资金或资产），这个词误导我们以物的方式思考，而非以过程的方式思考；以从过去积累或当下商品生产的方式思考，而非以从未来攫取的方式思考。托词还意味着另一种误导：在解释资本主义的起源和发展时，倾向于指涉西方、指涉北大西洋世界的历史。为对抗这种倾向，本书反复回到来自别处的例子和历史片段，尤其是一个特定地方——埃及。这些绕道提醒我们，这里所考察的过程没有一个是西方历史所特有的。它们早于<a id="page-290"></a>〔原书第290页〕所谓的西方崛起，并且一直在多个地点运作，实际上往往依赖殖民占领或帝国争夺的空间。它们还使我们能够把注意力从资本主义之类大型结构和过程，转向具体的攫取、控制和理解场所，从而近距离看到资本化的工作。碰巧的是，埃及一次又一次地提供了一个个断裂而独特的时刻的场所：无论是十九世纪初穆罕默德·阿里在尼罗河上建立帝国；还是那个世纪后期修建水坝和河流改道的前所未有的规模，这些都在开头几章探讨过；或是 1948—58 年这十年间围绕发展、剥夺和再殖民化的非凡斗争，见[第五章](#ch05-0001)；还是二十一世纪之交作为全球贫困答案的资产化实验，见[第六章](#ch06-0001)。但与此同时，埃及也提供了一个地方，让我们思考这些资本化叙述中消失的东西，在[第二章](#ch02-0001)追踪水车的噤声。“资本主义”“发展”的历史本身不仅消灭了以水车为象征的另一种生活方式，也消灭了水车所促成的生活形式的更广阔历史，本书在此以碎片形式将其打捞。

In exploring the modes of diversion, disjuncture, impoverishment, and enrichment that operate through the capture of the future, the book has been equally concerned with another kind of diversion – the production of an alibi, literally the ‘not there’, the ‘elsewhere’, the misdirection that encourages us to look to some other place for explanations of our form of life. The alibi of capital refers, first of all, to just that: to capital, as alibi. Capital *is* the alibi, in the sense that in its original meaning, derived from chattel or goods, and in its everyday meaning, as fund or asset, the word misdirects us to think in terms of a thing, not a process, and in terms of accumulation from the past or the production of commodities in the present rather than capture from the future. The alibi connotes another misdirection, the tendency to refer to the West, to the history of the North Atlantic world, in accounting for the origins and development of capitalism. To counter this tendency, the book has returned repeatedly to examples and episodes from elsewhere, and especially from one particular place, the country of Egypt. These detours serve as reminders that none of the processes we have examined here are specific to the history of the West. They pre-date the <a id="page-290-en"></a>〔原书第290页〕so-called rise of the West and have always operated across multiple locations, in fact often depending on spaces of colonial occupation or imperial contest. They also allowed us to shift attention from large structures and processes, like capitalism, to specific sites of capture, control, and comprehension, allowing us to see the work of capitalisation up close. Again and again, as it happens, Egypt provided a site for disjunctive and distinctive moments, whether in Muhammad Ali’s building of an empire on the Nile in the early nineteenth century; or the unprecedented scale of dam building and river diversion later in that century, all explored in the opening chapters; or the extraordinary struggles over development, dispossession, and recolonisation in the decade of 1948–58, examined in [chapter 5](#ch05-0001); or the experiments in assetisation as an answer to global poverty at the turn of the twenty-first century, described in [chapter 6](#ch06-0001). But Egypt, at the same time, offers a place to consider what disappears from these accounts of the capitalising process, in tracing in [chapter 2](#ch02-0001) the silencing of the waterwheel. The very history of the ‘development’ of ‘capitalism’ eliminated, not only another mode of life, epitomised by the waterwheel, but the wider history of the forms of life that the waterwheel enabled, recovered here in fragments.

<a id="ch08-0088"></a>

资本的托词最终还指一组关键概念，它们在使我们看不到本书通篇考察的未来攫取方面发挥了强大作用，包括技术、经济及其增长。我们不用“技术”——它作为解释历史进程和攫取巨额非劳动财富的创新原则而运作——而更愿意使用技术政治一词，以提醒所谓的“技术”始终是多种材料、观念和能动性的安排，既有新颖的也有复用的，由力量和正当化的关系维系在一起。我们已经表明，“经济”是一项令人惊讶地晚近的发明。它不是一种错误再现，不是掩盖或误算资本主义真实成本的再现。它是拯救资本化过程的装置，使资本化得以重建，不是作为投机性不稳定，而是作为一种看似稳定的、通过未来进行治理的模式。通过组织当下与未来、今天与明天之间的关系，它继续通过今天的许诺来治理我们：明天会更好，明天。最后，“增长”不是资本主义发展的必然进程，而是一种管理资本化的晚近装置。作为一种与未来的关系，它与第二种矛盾的关系——气候崩溃——共存。气候崩溃虽然不可避免，却是晚近的。它不是“资本主义”。如果<a id="page-291"></a>〔原书第291页〕气候危机要求我们发展新的政治概念来理解它，它也需要对碳时代留给我们的语言——经济及其“增长”——有一种不同的理解。以这种把范围界定得更具体的方式理解资本主义及其增长，也许为我们提供了一种参与当前危机的替代方式——以及一个适度希望的理由。<a id="page-292"></a>〔原书第292页〕

The alibis of capital refer, finally, to a set of key concepts whose powerful role in blinding us to the capture of the future we have examined throughout the book, including technology, the economy, and its growth. In place of ‘technology’, which operates as a principle of innovation accounting for the course of history and the capture of great unearned wealth, we have preferred the term technopolitics, as a reminder that so-called technology is always an arrangement of diverse materials, ideas, and agencies, both novel and reused, held together by relations of force and justification. The ‘economy’, we have shown, is a surprisingly recent invention. It is not a misrepresentation, disguising or miscounting the real costs of capitalism. It is the apparatus that saved the process of capitalisation, allowing its reconstruction not as speculative instability, but as a seemingly stable mode of governing through the future. By organising the relation between the present and future, between today and tomorrow, it continues to govern us through the promise, today, of a better tomorrow, tomorrow. ‘Growth’, finally, is not the ineluctable course of capitalist development, but a recent device for the managing of capitalisation. As a relation to the future, it coexists with a second, contradictory relation – that of climate collapse. Climate collapse, although unavoidable, is recent. It is not ‘capitalism’. If the <a id="page-291-en"></a>〔原书第291页〕climate crisis demands of us new political concepts with which to understand it, it also requires a different understanding of the language bequeathed to us by the carbon age – the economy and its ‘growth’. Approaching capitalism and its growth in this more circumscribed way offers us, perhaps, an alternative way to engage with the current crisis – and a reason for modest hope.<a id="page-292-en"></a>〔原书第292页〕

46. Alfred Marshall 指出，“当代的工业革命……在变革的速度和广度上都远远超过了一个世纪前的变化”：*Principles of Economics*，第 5 版，London: Macmillan and Co.，1907：vi；J. A. Hobson 的 *The Evolution of Modern Capitalism*，第 2 版，London: The Walter Scott Publishing Co.，1906，描述了最近两种转变带来的“根本变化”：私人持股企业被股份公司取代，以及“股份公司的产物”——金融家——所占据的新位置（236–8）；David Ames Wells 认为，“过去四分之一世纪发生的经济变化……无疑比世界历史上任何以前的相应时期都更重要、更多样”。*Recent Economic Changes and Their Effect on the Production and Distribution of Wealth and the Well-Being of Society*，New York: D. Appleton and Company，1890：v。关于 Wells 的影响，参见 Michael Perelman，〈Retrospectives: Schumpeter, David Wells, and Creative Destruction〉，*Journal of Economic Perspectives*，9: 3，1995：189–97；以及 James Livingston，〈The Social Analysis of Economic History and Theory: Conjectures on Late Nineteenth-Century <a id="page-302"></a>〔原书第302页〕 American Development〉，*American Historical Review*，92: 1，1987：75，该文称 *Recent Economic Changes* 是“1890—1910 年间或许被引用最多的书”。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch1-046)

46. Alfred Marshall noted that the ‘Industrial Revolution of the present generation . . . has far outdone the changes of a century ago, in both rapidity and breadth of movement’: *Principles of Economics*, 5th edition, London: Macmillan and Co., 1907: vi; J. A. Hobson’s *The Evolution of Modern Capitalism*, 2nd edition, London: The Walter Scott Publishing Co., 1906, described the ‘radical change’ brought by two recent shifts, the displacement of privately held firms by joint-stock enterprises and the new place occupied by ‘a product of the joint-stock company’, the financier (236–8); David Ames Wells argued that ‘the economic changes that have occurred during the last quarter of a century . . . have unquestionably been more important and varied than during any former corresponding period of the world’s history’. *Recent Economic Changes and Their Effect on the Production and Distribution of Wealth and the Well-Being of Society*, New York: D. Appleton and Company, 1890: v. On the influence of Wells, see Michael Perelman, ‘Retrospectives: Schumpeter, David Wells, and Creative Destruction’, *Journal of Economic Perspectives*, 9: 3, 1995: 189–97, and James Livingston, ‘The Social Analysis of Economic History and Theory: Conjectures on Late Nineteenth-Century <a id="page-302-en"></a>〔原书第302页〕American Development’, *American Historical Review*, 92: 1, 1987: 75, which describes *Recent Economic Changes* as ‘probably the most cited book of the period 1890–1910’.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch1-046)

47. 在德语中，capitalism 一词的出现与 Werner Sombart 的 *Der moderne Kapitalismus*（Leipzig: Duncker and Humblot，1902）相关。在法语中，*capitalisme* 一词出现得更早，在十九世纪的第三个十年（1820年代），含义更为具体——指近几十年来出现的战争财政新体系，其中金融家或“capitalistes”为国家发动战争提供信贷。Michael Sonenscher，*Capitalism: The Story Behind the Word*，Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press，2022；Eve Chiapello，〈Accounting and the Birth of the Notion of Capitalism〉，*Critical Perspectives on Accounting*，18: 3，2007：263–96。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch1-047)

47. In German, the appearance of the term capitalism is associated with Werner Sombart’s *Der moderne Kapitalismus*, Leipzig: Duncker and Humblot, 1902. In French, the term *capitalisme* had appeared earlier, in the third decade of the nineteenth century, in a more specific sense – to refer to the new system of war finance emerging over recent decades, in which financiers or ‘capitalistes’ provided the state with credit for war-making. Michael Sonenscher, *Capitalism: The Story Behind the Word*, Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 2022; Eve Chiapello, ‘Accounting and the Birth of the Notion of Capitalism’, *Critical Perspectives on Accounting*, 18: 3, 2007: 263–96.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch1-047)

Davey 先生于 8 月 15 日致信克罗尼耶，此前他发现重要事项被瞒着他。*The Economist* 如此描述这起欺诈：“过去五年，埃及糖厂表面上一直在繁荣发展，而实际上其经营亏损惨重……定期支付股息，董事会成员获得过高报酬，臃肿的员工队伍获得高薪，四家工厂安装了造价最为昂贵的设备，而这一切都出自虚构的收入。正是已故克罗尼耶先生的才干和声望，使这些复杂事务保持平衡，而且如此成功，以至于不仅外界相信公司稳健而繁荣，看来董事会中至少有一位身在<a id="page-305"></a>〔原书第305页〕开罗的成员——英国管理者 A. J. Davey 先生——也持有同样的错觉——直到刚过去的8月15日”，他于当日致信克罗尼耶。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch1-083)

83. ‘The Bankruptcy of the Egyptian Sucreries’, *The Economist*, 4 November 1905, 1754–5, describing the Report of Experts set up to investigate the collapse of the firm. The report stated that the local administrator, Mr A. J. Davey, wrote to Cronier on 15 August, having discovered that important matters were being kept from him. *The Economist* describes the fraud: ‘For five years past the Egyptian sugar refineries have been apparently prospering in the midst of ruinous losses on their exploitations . . . Regular dividends were paid, excessive emoluments were given to the members of the board, and high salaries to an overgrown staff, while expensive plant of the most costly description was laid down in four factories, and all this out of a fictitious revenue. It was the simple ability and the prestige of the late M. Cronier that held these complex affairs in equilibrium, and with such success, that not only the outside world was convinced of the company’s soundness and prosperity, but it seems that at least one of the members of the board in <a id="page-305-en"></a>〔原书第305页〕Cairo, Mr. A.J. Davey, the English administrator, held the same delusion – up to August 15th last’, when he wrote to Cronier.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch1-083)

98. 参见 Rana Baker，〈Engineering Profit: Egyptian Railroads and the Unmaking of Prosperity 1847–1907〉，博士论文，Middle Eastern, South Asian, and African Studies Department, Columbia University，2023。克罗默在埃及任职的末期，人们开始偶尔看到“发展”一词在某种更广泛意义上的使用，涵盖土地开垦、灌溉工程和铁路建设，尤其是在苏丹。例如参见 Sir Auckland Colvin，*The Making of Modern Egypt*，London: T. Nelson & Sons，1910。熊彼特希望“发展”一词指经济过程内生的——而非外生的——变化，这种变化由企业家的力量驱动。他本更愿意使用“演化”一词，但不喜其达尔文主义联想：*Theory of Economic Development*：49–51。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch1-098)

98. See Rana Baker, ‘Engineering Profit: Egyptian Railroads and the Unmaking of Prosperity 1847–1907’, PhD thesis, Middle Eastern, South Asian, and African Studies Department, Columbia University, 2023. Towards the end of Cromer’s time in Egypt one begins to see occasional references to development in a somewhat wider sense, to encompass land reclamation, irrigation schemes, and railway building, especially in Sudan. See, for example, Sir Auckland Colvin, *The Making of Modern Egypt*, London: T. Nelson& Sons, 1910. Schumpeter wanted the term ‘development’ to indicate change that was endogenous to the economic process, rather than exogenous, driven by the force of the entrepreneur. He would have preferred to use the term ‘evolution’, but disliked its Darwinian associations: *Theory of Economic Development*: 49–51.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch1-098)

25. 这里指开罗以南的尼罗河谷。在北部尼罗河三角洲，土壤通常在播种前用犁翻耕；就小麦而言，播种后第六十天和第九十天各灌一次水，用水车从井中提水灌溉。Girard，〈Memoire sur l’agriculture〉：515–17。即使在今天，在其他河流流域实践洪水退落农业的地方，它仍然是最节省劳动力的耕作方式。Scott，*Against the Grain*：66。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-025)

25. This refers to the Nile Valley south of Cairo. To the north, in the Nile Delta, the soil was usually turned with a plough before sowing, and then in the case of wheat watered twice, at sixty and ninety days after sowing, using water raised from wells using a waterwheel. Girard, ‘Memoire sur l’agriculture’: 515–17. Even today, where it is practised in other river basins, flood-recession agriculture remains the most labour-saving form of farming. Scott, *Against the Grain*: 66.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-025)

<a id="note-ch2-026"></a>

26. 冬季作物在围堤田区种植时称为 *al-bayādī*，在河岸台地利用机械灌溉种植时称为 *al-shitawī*。初夏收获的作物称为 *al-gaidī*（القيظي）或 *al-sayfī*，这两个词都指夏季。第三个季节在尼罗河开始泛滥的月份，称为 *al-damīrī* 或 *al-nabārī*，有时也称为 *al-nīlī*，这些词都指河水上涨或泛滥。在河岸台地和河中岛屿种植的 *al-nīlī* 作物，通过机械从上涨的河水中提水灌溉；而围堤田区的作物在可用之处继续使用井水（见下两段）。Girard，〈Memoire sur l’agriculture〉：499–500；Barois，*Les irrigations*：56–9。三季种植和井的使用在 John Lewis Burckhardt，*Travels in Nubia*（London: John Murray，1819：22–3）以及 Edward William Lane，*Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians*（London: J. M. Dent，1954：334–7）中也有提及。水车既用于井，也用于<a id="page-310"></a>〔原书第310页〕水渠，ʻAbd al-Rahim ʻAbd al-Rahman ʻAbd al-Rahim 在 *al-Rif al-misri fi al-qarn al-thamin ʻashar*（Cairo: Jamiʻat ʻAyn Shams, Kulliyyat al-Adab，1974：179–80）中对此有顺便提及。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-026)

26. The winter crops were known as *al-bayādī* when grown in the flood basins, and *al-shitawī* when grown on the berms, using mechanical irrigation. The crops harvested in early summer were known as *al-gaidī* (القيظي) or *al-sayfī*, both terms referring to summer. The third season, in the months when the Nile started to flood, was known as *al-damīrī* or *al-nabārī*, or sometimes *al-nīlī*, terms referring to the swelling or flooding of the river. *Al-nīlī* crops grown on the berms and on islands in the river were irrigated by lifting water mechanically from the rising waters, while basin crops continued to use well water (see the next two paragraphs) where available. Girard, ‘Memoire sur l’agriculture’: 499–500; Barois, *Les irrigations*: 56–9. The three-crop season and use of wells is also mentioned in John Lewis Burckhardt, *Travels in Nubia*, London: John Murray, 1819: 22–3; and Edward William Lane, *Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians*, London: J. M. Dent, 1954: 334–7. There is a passing reference to waterwheels, used on both wells and <a id="page-310-en"></a>〔原书第310页〕canals, in ʻAbd al-Rahim ʻAbd al-Rahman ʻAbd al-Rahim, *al-Rif al-misri fi al-qarn al-thamin ʻashar*, Cairo: Jamiʻat ʻAyn Shams, Kulliyyat al-Adab, 1974: 179–80.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-026)

<a id="note-ch2-027"></a>

27. 关于 1860 年代之前灌溉变化的大多数论述，都集中在所谓夏季运河的开挖上；这些深渠道使尼罗河水能在春季和初夏、河水开始上涨之前（利用畜力和蒸汽动力）被抽到田中。例外是 Alleaume 的重要研究，〈Les systèmes hydrauliques〉，它说明穆罕默德·阿里及其继任者手下的工程师如何还把十九世纪前埃及各不相同的围堤田区，重组为由平行于河流的运河连接的大型蓄水田区的系统链条，并按不同高度安排，以便蓄存多余的水。这种安排延长了土地在洪水季之外的使用，并且如下文各段所示，与井灌的使用相互配合。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-027)

27. Most accounts of changes to irrigation before the 1860s focus on the digging of so-called summer canals, the deep channels that allowed Nile water to be pumped up into fields (using both animal and steam power) in the spring and early summer, before the river began to rise. The exception is Alleaume’s important study, ‘Les systèmes hydrauliques’, which explains how engineers under Muhammad Ali and his successors also reorganised the diverse flood basins of pre-nineteenth-century Egypt into systematic chains of large basins connected by canals parallel to the river, arranged at different heights to allow the storing of excess water. The arrangement extended the use of lands outside the flood season, and, as we will see in the following paragraphs, worked in conjunction with the use of well irrigation.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-027)

<a id="note-ch2-028"></a>

28. Tignor，〈British Agricultural and Hydraulic Policy in Egypt〉：63。与 Tignor 不同，许多历史学家顺带提到还有第二季作物，一两位提到井的使用。但没有人解释井灌体系如何运作，或它对农民生计的核心意义。Barois，*Les irrigations*：28–9, 58–9, 99，简要提到在田里挖井。Rushdi Said，*The River Nile: Geology, Hydrology, and Utilization*，Oxford: Pergamon Press，1993：188–208，提到井的使用，但认为井主要设在河岸台地，而非围堤田块。Waterbury，*Hydropolitics of the Nile Valley*：29，顺带提及井灌体系。Stanford Shaw，*The Financial and Administrative Organization and Development of Ottoman Egypt, 1517–1798*，Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press，1962：50–1，提到在一些地区“每年可取得三到四次不同的收成”，需要在远离尼罗河的田里进行“人工灌溉”，但没有提到井或水车。Alan Mikhail，*Nature and Empire in Ottoman Egypt*，Cambridge: Cambridge University Press，2011：10，提到第二季作物，并在他详尽丰富的叙述中多次提到水车和拉动水车的牲畜，但没有解释井灌体系或水车所起的作用。Roger Owen 没有提到井，并称夏季作物“只能种在河边，或少数几条深得能在整个夏季蓄水的运河附近，因为它们需要持续灌溉”：*Cotton and the Egyptian Economy*：7–8。Kenneth Cuno，*The Pasha’s Peasants: Land, Society, and Economy in Lower Egypt, 1740–1858*，Cambridge: Cambridge University Press，1992：18，提到井，并更准确地指出“靠近尼罗河、运河或水井的土地……在夏季得到耕种”，但忽略了如下事实：如威尔科克斯所报告，“到处都挖井”，这意味着所有围堤田区的土地都可能靠近一口井。Willcocks 与 Craig，*Egyptian Irrigation*，第 3 版：32。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-028)

28. Tignor, ‘British Agricultural and Hydraulic Policy in Egypt’: 63. Many historians, unlike Tignor, mention in passing that there was a second crop, and one or two mention the use of wells. But none explain how the system of well irrigation worked or its centrality to peasant livelihoods. Barois, *Les irrigations*: 28–9, 58–9, 99, briefly mentions wells dug in the fields. Rushdi Said, *The River Nile: Geology, Hydrology, and Utilization*, Oxford: Pergamon Press, 1993: 188–208, notes the use of wells but suggests they were placed mainly on the berms, not the field basins. Waterbury, *Hydropolitics of the Nile Valley*: 29, mentions the well system in passing. Stanford Shaw, *The Financial and Administrative Organization and Development of Ottoman Egypt, 1517–1798*, Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1962: 50–1, mentions that in some districts ‘three or four different harvests were produced during every year’, requiring ‘artificial irrigation’ in fields distant from the Nile, but does not mention wells or waterwheels. Alan Mikhail, *Nature and Empire in Ottoman Egypt*, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2011: 10, mentions the second crop and refers to waterwheels and the animals that moved them several times in his richly detailed text, but does not explain the well system or the role that waterwheels played. Roger Owen makes no mention of wells and states that summer crops ‘could be grown only near the river or one of the few canals deep enough to hold water throughout the summer, as they required constant irrigation’: *Cotton and the Egyptian Economy*: 7–8. Kenneth Cuno, *The Pasha’s Peasants: Land, Society, and Economy in Lower Egypt, 1740–1858*, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1992: 18, mentions wells, noting more accurately that ‘land . . . near the Nile, a canal or a well, was cultivated during the summer season’, overlooking the fact that, as Willcocks reported, ‘wells are dug everywhere’, meaning that all basin land was potentially near a well. Willcocks and Craig, *Egyptian Irrigation*, 3rd edition: 32.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-028)

49. Alleaume, ‘Les systèmes hydrauliques’: 304–7. An English traveller, observing the Nile flood in 1850–1, wrote that the rise of the river ‘is first felt in the lands at the greatest distance from the river; for these are the lowest. They gradually become moist, then soften into morasses, and in some places glisten for a short time as shallow lakes. There is no rush of water along the surface; but the inundation, as it were, oozes up from the ground. Deep holes, during summer with hard-baked cracked bottoms, change slowly into wells and ponds.’ Bayle St. John, *Village Life in Egypt: With Sketches of the Saïd*, 2 vols, London: Chapman and Hall, 1852: 2: 104–5.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-049)

Dodge 编，*Proceedings of the International Large River Symposium*，Ontario: Canadian Special Publication of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 106，1989：110–27。另参见 Rohan D’Souza，〈Event, Process and Pulse: Resituating Floods in Environmental Histories of South Asia〉，*Environment and History*，26: 1，2020：31–49；以及 Scott，*Against the Grain*：53–4。Scott 在此书写作完成后出版的关于缅甸伊洛瓦底江的更长篇、杰出的研究，说明了洪水脉冲以及河流复杂生命的其他方面，如何使我们能够书写一部较少人类中心主义的涵盖人类及人类之外生命的历史叙述：*In Praise of Floods: The Untamed River and the Life It Brings*，New Haven, CT: Yale University Press，2025。对于尼罗河，我们还没有这样的研究；尼罗河漫长的地下蓄水史为 Scott 所揭示的复杂过程增添了另一个维度。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-059)

59. On this biotic exchange and the concept of the flood pulse, see Wolfgang Junk, Peter Bayley, and R. E. Sparks, ‘The Flood Pulse Concept in River-Floodplain Systems’, in D. P. Dodge, ed., *Proceedings of the International Large River Symposium*, Ontario: Canadian Special Publication of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 106, 1989: 110–27. See also Rohan D’Souza, ‘Event, Process and Pulse: Resituating Floods in Environmental Histories of South Asia’, *Environment and History*, 26: 1, 2020: 31–49; and Scott, *Against the Grain*: 53–4. Scott’s longer, brilliant study of the Ayeyarwady (Irrawaddy) River of Burma, which appeared after this writing, illuminates how the flood pulse and other aspects of the complex life of a river enable us to write a less anthropocentric account of human and more-than-human history: *In Praise of Floods: The Untamed River and the Life It Brings*, New Haven, CT: Yale University Press, 2025. We have no study of this kind for the Nile, where the long history of underground storage adds another dimension to the complex processes that Scott illuminates.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-059)

98. Henry Villiers Stuart 是一位爱尔兰地主兼议会议员，1882 年代表英国政府进行巡视，他报告说：“甚至用水车也能做很多事……因为一架水车由两三对公牛驱动，可灌溉四英亩甘蔗、五六英亩棉花或十三英亩谷类作物……水车的一个重要优势在于，只要把井打到尼罗河水位以下，就能在远离尼罗河的地方使用。由于土壤多孔，在远离河流的内陆，这一深度仍有源源不断的水源。”Henry Villiers Stuart，*Egypt After the War, Being the Narrative of a Tour of Inspection*，London: John Murray，1883：242。Barois，*Les irrigations*：266, 268，给出的数字是每架水车十二至十五英亩（五至六公顷），并指出有时多达四架水车可从同一口井提水。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-098)

98. Henry Villiers Stuart, an Irish landowner and Member of Parliament who conducted a tour of inspection on behalf of the British government in 1882 reported that ‘much might even be done with water-wheels . . . because one water-wheel, worked by two or three pairs of bullocks, can irrigate four acres of cane, five or six acres of cotton, or thirteen acres of cereal crops . . . An important advantage of the water-wheel is that it can be worked at long distances from the Nile by sinking wells below the Nile level. A perpetual supply of water exists far inland at that depth, because the soil is porous.’ Henry Villiers Stuart, *Egypt After the War, Being the Narrative of a Tour of Inspection*, London: John Murray, 1883: 242. Barois, *Les irrigations*: 266, 268, gave figures of twelve to fifteen acres (five to six hectares) per waterwheel, and noted that sometimes up to four wheels could operate one well.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-098)

121. The information on causes of deforestation is sparse, but sources tend to agree that the highlands had been largely deforested by the end of the century. The link between loss of cattle dung and increased use of firewood, and between deforestation and increased runoff, are my own inferences from this literature. <a id="note-ch2-122"></a>

122. 英国主要水利工程师威尔科克斯后来提到废弃的 *saqiya* 井坑时，部分是为了指出它们可用来测量上升的地下水位及相关盐碱化——这是英国人建立的扩展型运河灌溉系统所造成的问题。在从围堤蓄水体系转向常年灌溉的过程中，他们把地下水从一种蓄水方法变成了渍水问题。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-122)

122. When Willcocks, the leading British hydraulic engineer, later mentioned abandoned *saqiya* pits, it was partly to note their use for measuring the rising water table and associated salinity, a problem created by the extended system of canal-based irrigation the British had built. In switching from the basin system to perennial irrigation, they had transformed groundwater from a method of storage into a problem of water logging.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-122)

140. Aḥmad ibn ʻAli al-Maqrizi and Adel Allouche, *Mamluk Economics: A Study and Translation of Al-Maqrizi’s Ighathah*, Salt Lake City, UT: University of Utah Press, 1994, 41. Maqrizi’s source for this dubious information on extreme famine was ‘Abd al-Latif al-Baghdadi, *Kitab al-ifadah wa-l-i‘tibar fi l-umur al-mushahada wa-l-ḥawadith al-mu‘ayana bi-ard Misr*, written in 1204, ed. and trans. as *A Physician on the Nile: A Description of Egypt and Journal of the Famine Years*, New York: New York University Press, 2022: 89–114. ‘The affluent and moderately well-to-do classes got into the habit [of eating one another],’ al-Baghdadi reports, ‘some out of necessity, others for the sake of the novel culinary experience’ (143). <a id="note-ch2-141"></a>

141. Maqrizi 与 Allouche，*Mamluk Economics*。Stuart J. Borsch 提出，Maqrizi 时代以及 1350 年起 150 年间尼罗河的高水位洪水，可以用黑死病（1347–9）导致上埃及围堤蓄水体系衰败来解释。由于南方吸收（并蓄存）的洪水量减少，更多水到达开罗。〈Nile Floods and the Irrigation System in Fifteenth-Century Egypt〉，*Mamluk Studies Review*，4，2000：131–45。关于 Maqrizi 担任 *muhtasib* 的经历及其对其著述的影响，参见 Nasser Rabbat，*Writing Egypt: Al-Maqrizi and his Historical Project*，<a id="page-321"></a>〔原书第321页〕 Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press，2023：80–9。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-141)

141. Maqrizi and Allouche, *Mamluk Economics*. Stuart J. Borsch proposes that high Nile floods in Maqrizi’s time, and across 150 years from 1350, can be explained by a decay of the basin system in Upper Egypt caused by the Black Death (1347–9). With less of the flood absorbed (and stored) in the south, higher volumes of water reached Cairo. ‘Nile Floods and the Irrigation System in Fifteenth-Century Egypt’, *Mamluk Studies Review*, 4, 2000: 131–45. On Maqrizi’s experience as *muhtasib* and its influence on his writings, see Nasser Rabbat, *Writing Egypt: Al-Maqrizi and his Historical Project*, <a id="page-321-en"></a>〔原书第321页〕Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press, 2023: 80–9.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-141)

149. 收割后的甘蔗很快失水，必须在二十四小时内压榨，因此提取汁液并煮沸制成原糖的糖厂必须建在田地附近；但精制糖无法承受长途海运，因为湿气会使晶粒结块；因此供出口的糖，其最后加工——把糖精炼成晶体——必须在消费地区进行，就欧洲而言，这也意味着一个炼糖厂燃料更充足的地区。Galloway，*The Sugar Cane Industry*：17。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-149)

149. Harvested cane loses moisture quickly and must be milled within twenty-four hours, so the mills that extract the juice and boil it to create raw sugar must be built close to the fields; but refined sugar cannot tolerate long sea voyages, as the humidity causes the crystals to coalesce; so for export, the final processing – refining the sugar into crystals – had to take place in the region of consumption, which in the case of Europe also meant a region with more abundant fuel for the refineries. Galloway, *The Sugar Cane Industry*: 17.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-149)

<a id="note-ch2-150"></a>

150. 小麦是例外：在埃及，小麦占据土地六个月，约为其他谷物和豆类耗时两倍。与棉花和甘蔗一样，小麦主要供出口而非本地消费，这反映了它作为一种谷物的价值：其储藏蛋白特别适合制作发酵面包。参见 Colin Wrigley，〈Wheat: An Overview of the Grain That Provides “Our Daily Bread”〉，*Encyclopedia of Food Grains*，第 2 版，第 1 卷，Oxford: Academic Press，2016：105–16。然而与甘蔗和棉花不同，小麦是冬季作物，因此可以大规模种植，而不会干扰围堤田块的洪水漫灌。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-150)

150. The exception is wheat, which in Egypt occupied the ground for six months, or about twice the length of time of other grains and legumes. Like cotton and sugar cane, it was grown mostly for export rather than local consumption, reflecting its value as the cereal whose storage protein is uniquely suited to making leavened bread. See Colin Wrigley, ‘Wheat: An Overview of the Grain That Provides “Our Daily Bread”’, *Encyclopedia of Food Grains*, 2nd edition, vol. 1, Oxford: Academic Press, 2016: 105–16. Unlike cane and cotton, however, wheat was a winter crop, so could be cultivated on a large scale without interfering with the flooding of the field basins.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch2-150)

165. *izba*（庄园）一词本义为“遥远的”或“偏僻的”，最初指建在洪泛平原上的临时住房，用于支持夏季井灌季节和牲畜放牧。后来它成为新地产上固定工人住房的称呼，最终也指这些地产本身。Mitchell，*Rule of Experts*：54–79，以及 Mona Abaza，*The Cotton Plantation Remembered: An Egyptian Family Story*，Cairo: American University in Cairo Press，2013。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch2-165)

165. The ‘*izba*, from a word meaning distant or remote, originally referred to the temporary housing built on the floodplain, to support the summer well-irrigation season and livestock grazing. Udovitch further explains: ‘On the most basic commercial level, sales, both wholesale and retail were normally conducted on a credit basis, i.e. on the basis of deferred payment for a fixed period. The documents make clear that the buyer paid a premium for the deferment of payment. This was expressed either by granting a discount from the stated price in return for an immediate cash payment (discounts varied from 2%–4%), or by the quotation of two prices: one for a cash transaction, and a slightly higher one for a credit transaction’: Abraham L. Udovitch, ‘Reflections on the Institutions of Credits and Banking in the Medieval Islamic Near East’, *Studia Islamica*, 41, 1975: 13.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch3-021)

57. 1833 年，原棉主要从美国进口（还有巴西、印度、西印度群岛和印度；1820 年代短暂从埃及进口）；其中超过 10% 在纺纱中损失，另一部分在织布中损失；余下部分中的 72% 出口，约一半为纱线和线，一半为制成品，留下 28% 供国内消费和库存。数字来自 Edward Baines，*History of the Cotton Manufacture in Great Britain*，London: H. Fisher, R. Fisher, and P. Jackson，1835：367 中的表格。请注意，国内消费的是质量较高的纺织品，而无论是内销还是出口的布匹和纱线，其质量在十九世纪上半叶似乎都迅速下降：（Lars G. Sandberg，〈Movements in the Quality of British Cotton Textile Exports, 1815–1913〉，*The Journal of Economic History*，28: 1，1968：19）。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch3-057)

57. In 1833, raw cotton was imported mostly from the United States (also Brazil, India, the West Indies, and India; briefly from Egypt in 1820s); of this, more than 10 per cent was lost in spinning, and another part in the manufacturing of cloth; of the remainder 72 per cent was exported, about half as yarn and thread and half as manufactured goods, leaving 28 per cent for home consumption and stock. Figures from table in Edward Baines, *History of the Cotton Manufacture in Great Britain*, London: H. Fisher, R. Fisher, and P. Jackson, 1835: 367. Note that domestic consumption was of higher-quality textiles, and that both domestic and exported cloth and yarn appear to have declined rapidly in quality through the first half of the nineteenth century: (Lars G. Sandberg, ‘Movements in the Quality of British Cotton Textile Exports, 1815–1913’, *The Journal of Economic History*, 28: 1, 1968: 19).[↩](#ref-en-note-ch3-057)

For a corrective, see Smail, *Legal* <a id="page-334-en"></a>〔原书第334页〕*Plunder*: 91–2, who argues that the lack of small coins and the wide use of credit for everyday purchases was not a sign of economic weakness.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch3-122)

<a id="note-ch3-123"></a>

123. Kiyotaki 与 Moore，〈Evil Is the Root of All Money〉。1976 年夏天，我有幸在阿尔及利亚南部一个绿洲小定居点遇见 John Moore，当时我正希望从那里穿越撒哈拉前往西非——在那些日子里，这条路线没有道路。他向北回到英格兰剑桥（碰巧我们都在那里求学），后来成为英国最杰出的经济学家之一。我则继续向南穿越撒哈拉。自那以后，我们的道路从未交叉，直到写下这条注释。[↩](#ref-zh-note-ch3-123)

123. Kiyotaki and Moore, ‘Evil Is the Root of All Money’. I was fortunate to meet John Moore in the summer of 1976, in a small oasis settlement in southern Algeria, from where I was hoping to cross the Sahara to West Africa, a route that had no roads in those days. He returned north to Cambridge, England (where, as it happens, we were both students), and went on to become one of Britain’s leading economists. I continued south across the Sahara. Since then, our paths have never crossed, until this note.[↩](#ref-en-note-ch3-123)

Lancashire switched directly to the use of Bank of England banknotes, when the central bank established branch banks in Manchester (1826) and Liverpool (1827), and then to the cheque system.
